Ask the Equipment module to upgrade a unique copy by one level (ADR-039 section 7): par station or boutique, cible the station or merchant. The chance is rolled on the host.

  • Fields: fiche (number), par (text?), cible (id?), joueur (id?)
  • Announced by: —
  • Listened to by: Equipment

items.title: equipement.sertir
items.text:
Ask the Equipment module to set a gem into a unique copy: gemme its kind (a stack of the bag) or gemme_fiche (a unique gem); par station or boutique, cible the station or merchant.

  • Fields: fiche (number), gemme (text?), gemme_fiche (number?), par (text?), cible (id?), joueur (id?)
  • Announced by: —
  • Listened to by: Equipment

items.title: equipement.desertir
items.text:
Ask the Equipment module to remove gem number index (missing: the last) from a unique copy, after the setting retrait_gemme: impossible, the gem destroyed, or returned for a cost.

  • Fields: fiche (number), index (number?), par (text?), cible (id?), joueur (id?)
  • Announced by: —
  • Listened to by: Equipment

items.title: equipement.atelier
items.text:
Open the Equipment workshop (repair, upgrade, set gems) at this station or merchant: the station's Crafting window, or the merchant's Shop window, opened on its workshop tab, for joueur only (without joueur, for the host only).

  • Fields: cible (id), joueur (id?)
  • Announced by: —
  • Listened to by: Equipment

items.title: equipement.casse
items.text:
A unique copy's durability reached zero and it is broken (setting a_zero casse): kept, greyed, without its bonuses until repaired.

  • Fields: joueur (id), fiche (number), objet (text), usure (number), usure_max (number)
  • Announced by: Equipment
  • Listened to by: —

items.title: equipement.detruit
items.text:
A unique copy's durability reached zero and it is destroyed (setting a_zero detruit).

  • Fields: joueur (id), fiche (number), objet (text), usure (number), usure_max (number)
  • Announced by: Equipment
  • Listened to by: —

items.title: equipement.usure_alerte
items.text:
A unique copy's durability went below the warning threshold (seuil_usure, 20% by default).

  • Fields: joueur (id), fiche (number), objet (text), usure (number), usure_max (number)
  • Announced by: Equipment
  • Listened to by: —

items.title: equipement.repare
items.text:
A unique copy was repaired: par station, boutique or kit; usure and usure_max its new durability.

  • Fields: joueur (id), fiche (number), objet (text), par (text), usure (number), usure_max (number)
  • Announced by: Equipment
  • Listened to by: —

items.title: equipement.ameliore
items.text:
An upgrade was tried: reussi says whether the roll succeeded, niveau the copy's level now, echec what a failure did (rien, niveau_perdu, casse).

  • Fields: joueur (id), fiche (number), objet (text), reussi (boolean), niveau (number), echec (text?)
  • Announced by: Equipment
  • Listened to by: —

items.title: equipement.serti
items.text:
A gem was set into a unique copy.

  • Fields: joueur (id), fiche (number), objet (text), gemme (text)
  • Announced by: Equipment
  • Listened to by: —

items.title: equipement.desserti
items.text:
A gem was removed from a unique copy: rendue says whether it went back to the bag.

  • Fields: joueur (id), fiche (number), objet (text), gemme (text), rendue (boolean)
  • Announced by: Equipment
  • Listened to by: —

items.title: inventaire.jeter
items.text:
Ask the inventory to drop a whole slot (version 15 for a unique copy, version 21 for a stack): case is the slot's key ("Wood~2"), otherwise fiche a unique copy, otherwise the first slot of the kind objet. It is put down in front of the player as one object that gives the same quantity back in one pickup (its prompt says "Wood x40"); a unique copy's record follows it and comes back with it. quantite (version 21): only that many from a stack (Shift + drag out of the window drops half); the slot keeps the rest.

  • Fields: objet (text), case (text?), fiche (number?), quantite (number?), joueur (id?)
  • Announced by: Inventory
  • Listened to by: Inventory

items.title: inventaire.diviser
items.text:
Ask the inventory to split a stack (version 21): quantite items of the slot case (missing: half, rounded down) move to a new slot, or with vers onto that stack of the same kind, up to its maximum stack (the rest stays in case). Refused, with a message and the slot lit up, when a new slot is needed and none is free; a stack of 1 or a unique copy does not split.

  • Fields: case (text), quantite (number?), vers (text?), joueur (id?)
  • Announced by: —
  • Listened to by: Inventory

items.title: inventaire.regrouper
items.text:
Ask the inventory to merge two stacks of the same kind (version 21): the slot de pours into the slot vers, up to the kind's maximum stack; the rest stays where it was.

  • Fields: de (text), vers (text), joueur (id?)
  • Announced by: —
  • Listened to by: Inventory

items.title: inventaire.decrire
items.text:
Describe a kind of item during the game (version 29), when « Sortes d'objets » gives it no description: the tooltip and the item's details show it. An empty description removes it.

  • Fields: objet (text), description (text)
  • Announced by: —
  • Listened to by: Inventory

items.title: inventaire.change
items.text:
The quantity of an item changed. total is the new quantity. chargement is true when a saved game gives the items back (game.load): nothing was picked up. For a unique copy (version 15), objet is its kind, fiche its record's number, total how many of that kind. With several stacks of a kind (version 21), total counts all of them; jete is true when a slot was dropped on the ground.

  • Fields: objet (text), quantite (number), total (number), chargement (boolean?), fiche (number?), jete (boolean?)
  • Announced by: Inventory
  • Listened to by: Needs, Shop, Gathering, Building, Dialogue, Equipment, Crafting, Quest log, Knowledge, Healing, Sounds, Ranged weapons

items.title: inventaire.plein
items.text:
An item could not be added: every slot holds another kind of item (or another unique copy), or (version 21) every stack of its kind is full. reste: picked up in part, how many stayed on the ground.

  • Fields: objet (text), fiche (number?), reste (number?)
  • Announced by: Inventory
  • Listened to by: Shop, Loot, Crafting, Knowledge, Sounds

items.title: inventaire.poids
items.text:
With the weight on (inventory setting poids_actif): the weight a player carries, their maximum load (the value charge_max) or their overload step changed. palier is the step's row number in paliers_poids (0: none), seuil its share of the load in %, avant the step before.

  • Fields: poids (number), charge (number), palier (number), seuil (number), avant (number)
  • Announced by: Inventory
  • Listened to by: —

items.title: inventaire.trop_lourd
items.text:
With the weight on: a pickup was refused, the item stays where it is. raison: limite (it would go beyond limite_ramasser, with trop_lourd set to refuser) or palier (the current overload step forbids picking up).

  • Fields: objet (text), poids (number), porte (number), charge (number), raison (text)
  • Announced by: Inventory
  • Listened to by: —

items.title: inventaire.manque
items.text:
Items could not be removed: there are not enough.

  • Fields: objet (text), quantite (number), fiche (number?)
  • Announced by: Inventory
  • Listened to by: Shop, Loot, Building, Equipment, Crafting, Progression, Knowledge

items.title: langue.change
items.text:
Sent by the engine when the player changes the game's language (game.set_language, the Menu options). A module redraws what it already shows: its texts go through game.t and game.language.

  • Fields: langue (text)
  • Announced by: —
  • Listened to by: Status effects, Needs, Loot, Building, Race, Dialogue, Equipment, Inventory, Day and night, Round, Death and respawn, Progression, Knowledge

items.title: ciel.lever
items.text:
Sent by the engine at sunrise, when the scene uses the realistic sky (Game settings, Sky and weather) and its hour moves (day_minutes above 0, or game.set_sky). jour is the day of the year. A jump made by game.set_sky sends nothing.

  • Fields: jour (number)
  • Announced by: —
  • Listened to by: Day and night

items.title: ciel.coucher
items.text:
Sent by the engine at sunset, when the scene uses the realistic sky and its hour moves. jour is the day of the year.

  • Fields: jour (number)
  • Announced by: —
  • Listened to by: Day and night

items.title: ciel.heure
items.text:
Sent by the engine each time the realistic sky's hour reaches a whole hour (heure, 0 to 23), on day jour of the year.

  • Fields: heure (number), jour (number)
  • Announced by: —
  • Listened to by: Day and night

items.title: scene.change
items.text:
Sent by the engine once the player has arrived in another scene of the game (game.go_to, or a passage). Scripts keep running across scenes: this is when a module looks at the objects of the new scene.

  • Fields: depuis (text), vers (text)
  • Announced by: —
  • Listened to by: Companion, Status effects, Map, Enemies, Inventory, Day and night, Menu, Passage, Progression, Health, Healing, Sounds

items.title: joueur.arrivee
items.text:
Sent by the engine, in a game with several players (the game setting Multiplayer), on the computer hosting the game, when a guest joins: joueur is their character (a copy of the player's), numero their place (1 to 7, the host being 0), nom the name they chose. game.players() lists them all. Scripts only run on the host.

  • Fields: joueur (id), numero (number), nom (text)
  • Announced by: —
  • Listened to by: Round, Death and respawn, Progression

items.title: joueur.depart
items.text:
Sent by the engine on the host when a guest leaves the game (they quit, or their connection was lost and they did not come back in time, the game setting Place kept after a drop): their character is removed right after. A module forgets what it kept for them.

  • Fields: joueur (id), numero (number)
  • Announced by: —
  • Listened to by: Gathering, Race, Round, Death and respawn, Passage, Progression

items.title: joueur.reconnecte
items.text:
Sent by the engine on the host when a guest whose connection dropped comes back in time and takes their place again: same character, same bag, the same per-player scripts that kept running (no joueur.depart nor joueur.arrivee was sent). Meanwhile their character stood still. A module can show them a message or resend what is only shown once.

  • Fields: joueur (id), numero (number), nom (text)
  • Announced by: —
  • Listened to by: Progression

items.title: joueur.profil
items.text:
Sent by the engine on the host (ADR-020 § 18) when a player enters with a character: joueur is their character, profil the choices they made on their own PC (game.profile_send) once the game's check accepted them (game.override("profil.verifier")), nouveau true for a character just created, false for one this world's save already had. The script applies only what it understands (hair, colors, name): the profile is plain data and can never give items or progress. Also sent on the host or in solo when the player on this PC calls game.profile_send.

  • Fields: joueur (id), profil (table), nouveau (boolean)
  • Announced by: —
  • Listened to by: Progression

items.title: profil.demande
items.text:
Sent by the engine in the game of a player who is joining (before entering, while their own scripts still run: the title screen, the Menu), when the host wants them to create their character because they have none in this world (game setting Players' characters, ADR-020 § 18). essai is 0 the first time, then the number of refused tries; raison the game's text explaining the last refusal (translate it with game.t); propose the look kept on this PC (setting Same look everywhere), to offer in advance. The creation screen sends the choices with game.profile_send(table).

  • Fields: essai (number), raison (text), propose (table?)
  • Announced by: —
  • Listened to by: Menu

items.title: chat.message
items.text:
Sent by the engine on the host (or the dedicated server) when a player writes in the chat (key T) and the line is accepted (not a command starting with /, not cut by the anti-spam, the game setting Chat on): joueur is their character, nom their name, texte what they wrote (plain text, 200 bytes at most). game.chat_send answers in the chat.

  • Fields: joueur (id), nom (text), texte (text)
  • Announced by: —
  • Listened to by: —

items.title: joueur.occupe
items.text:
The player's hands are taken by something else than fighting (version 23): a building mode where the click places a piece, a tool being aimed. occupe true when it starts, false when it ends; par names who says it ("construction"), so several can overlap. Fighting modules do not strike nor block while any of them keeps the player busy.

  • Fields: occupe (boolean), par (text)
  • Announced by: Building
  • Listened to by: Gathering, Basic combat, Inventory, Ranged weapons

items.title: monde.sommeil
items.text:
Sent by the engine in a large world when objects fall asleep: their 256 m tiles are now beyond the activity radius around the player. objets is the list of their ids (those carrying a system or a tag, characters and moving objects). They still exist, but do not move, walk, animate or detect, and game.with_system, game.with_tag and game.near leave them out unless {asleep = true}. A module sets aside what it was doing with them.

  • Fields: objets (list of ids)
  • Announced by: —
  • Listened to by: —

items.title: monde.reveil
items.text:
Sent by the engine in a large world when objects wake up, as the world kept them: the player came back near them. objets is the list of their ids. A module takes them back; to catch up the time they slept, compare game.time() with the time it noted.

  • Fields: objets (list of ids)
  • Announced by: —
  • Listened to by: —

items.title: timeline.debut
items.text:
Sent by the engine when an animation made by hand or a cutscene starts (game.play_timeline, a trigger, or one that plays from the start). sorte: animation or cutscene.

  • Fields: timeline (text), sorte (text)
  • Announced by: —
  • Listened to by: —

items.title: timeline.fin
items.text:
Sent by the engine when an animation or a cutscene ends: at its end, skipped by the player (passee), or stopped by game.stop_timeline (arretee). An animation that loops never ends on its own. After a cutscene, the player has control again.

  • Fields: timeline (text), sorte (text), passee (boolean), arretee (boolean)
  • Announced by: —
  • Listened to by: —

items.title: collecte.coup
items.text:
The player hit a resource (a use of something carrying collecte). restants is how many hits are left before it is used up.

  • Fields: cible (id), coups (number), restants (number)
  • Announced by: Gathering
  • Listened to by: Sounds

items.title: collecte.recolte
items.text:
A resource was used up and gave what it holds. The inventory, if present, has been asked to add it.

  • Fields: cible (id), ressource (text), quantite (number), joueur (id?), xp (number?), piste (text?)
  • Announced by: Gathering
  • Listened to by: Loot, Equipment, Progression

items.title: collecte.epuise
items.text:
A resource is used up and is about to disappear (destroyed, or hidden until it grows back): it still exists while this is sent.

  • Fields: cible (id)
  • Announced by: Gathering
  • Listened to by: Sounds

items.title: collecte.repousse
items.text:
A used-up resource grew back and can be gathered again.

  • Fields: cible (id)
  • Announced by: Gathering
  • Listened to by: —

items.title: collecte.outil_manquant
items.text:
The player tried to gather a resource without the tool it needs: not held in hand (the default, with attack), or not in the inventory (gathering set to the interaction).

  • Fields: cible (id), outil (text), joueur (id?)
  • Announced by: Gathering
  • Listened to by: —

items.title: ennemi.etat
items.text:
An enemy changed state: patrouille (patrols), poursuite (chases the player), visee (a shooter aims before its first shot: the moment for a warning sound), attaque (hits in reach, or shoots), attente (waits its turn near the player, when enough others are already attacking), retour (goes back to its spot), mort (dead, does nothing more).

  • Fields: cible (id), etat (text)
  • Announced by: Enemies
  • Listened to by: Sounds

items.title: ennemi.tir
items.text:
An enemy fired a shot at a player (its setting tir): sorte is balle, fleche or boule_de_feu. Announced when the shot leaves, hit or miss; a hit is then announced by combat.coup. Listen to it for a sound of your own, a shake of the screen, or to count shots.

  • Fields: source (id), cible (id), sorte (text)
  • Announced by: Enemies
  • Listened to by: —

items.title: combat.attaque
items.text:
Someone struck, whether it hit or not: the stamina module counts it.

  • Fields: source (id)
  • Announced by: Basic combat
  • Listened to by: Stamina, Equipment, Sounds

items.title: endurance.change
items.text:
The player's stamina changed. epuise is true from zero until they regain a share of it: meanwhile they cannot run, jump or strike.

  • Fields: valeur (number), max (number), epuise (boolean)
  • Announced by: Stamina
  • Listened to by: Basic combat, Sounds

items.title: soins.soin
items.text:
The healing module gave health back: a potion drunk, a spring touched. objet is the kind of potion or the name of what healed.

  • Fields: cible (id), montant (number), objet (text)
  • Announced by: Healing
  • Listened to by: Sounds

items.title: alterations.appliquer
items.text:
Ask the Status effects module to put an effect on a carrier (a player, an enemy, an object), as game.status_apply does. duree in seconds (missing: the effect's own; 0: until removed); cumul: a number of stacks, or refaire, cumuler, ignorer.

  • Fields: cible (id), id (text), duree (number?), source (id?), cumul (any?)
  • Announced by: Trigger
  • Listened to by: Status effects

items.title: alterations.retirer
items.text:
Ask the Status effects module to remove an effect from a carrier, or every effect carrying that tag (an antidote removes poison).

  • Fields: cible (id), id (text)
  • Announced by: Trigger
  • Listened to by: Status effects

items.title: alterations.debut
items.text:
A status effect was put on a carrier. encore is true when it was already there (its duration restarted, or it stacked: cumul is its new count).

  • Fields: cible (id), id (text), cumul (number), duree (number), encore (boolean), source (id?)
  • Announced by: Status effects
  • Listened to by: —

items.title: alterations.fin
items.text:
A status effect left a carrier: its time ran out (fin), it was removed (retire) or the carrier died (mort). Its value bonuses are already gone.

  • Fields: cible (id), id (text), raison (text)
  • Announced by: Status effects
  • Listened to by: —

items.title: alterations.tic
items.text:
A status effect hurt (degats) or healed (soins) its carrier at its regular interval; the health module was asked to do it.

  • Fields: cible (id), id (text), sorte (text), montant (number)
  • Announced by: Status effects
  • Listened to by: —

items.title: combat.coup
items.text:
An attack hit something. The health module, if present, has been asked to remove the damage.

  • Fields: cible (id), source (id), montant (number)
  • Announced by: Basic combat, Enemies
  • Listened to by: Equipment, Sounds

items.title: boutique.ouvrir
items.text:
Ask the shop system to open the shop of cible, as if the player had used it: from a dialogue answer, a trigger, a script. onglet opens it on another module's tab (equipement.atelier: the services). It opens for joueur only; without joueur, for the host only (never for every player).

  • Fields: cible (id), onglet (text?), joueur (id?)
  • Announced by: Shops of the city, Dialogue, Equipment
  • Listened to by: Shop

items.title: boutique.acheter
items.text:
Ask the shop system to buy objet at the merchant cible for the player, without the window, exactly as the Buy button (money taken, item given, stock counted): the Commerces system's shared.commerces.acheter sends it. Refused while another merchant's window is open. boutique.achat follows when it is done. For joueur only; without joueur, for the host only.

  • Fields: cible (id), objet (text), joueur (id?)
  • Announced by: Shops of the city
  • Listened to by: Shop

items.title: boutique.onglet
items.text:
The shop window opened another module's tab (onglet, its key; parent, the empty panel to fill; largeur, the window's width), or left it (onglet empty). The module whose tab it is fills the panel.

  • Fields: joueur (id), onglet (text), cible (id?), parent (text?), largeur (number?)
  • Announced by: Shop
  • Listened to by: Equipment

items.title: boutique.achat
items.text:
The player bought an item in a shop: cible is the merchant, quantite how many they received, prix what they paid, in monnaie (a kind of inventory item). The inventory has already changed.

  • Fields: cible (id), objet (text), quantite (number), prix (number), monnaie (text)
  • Announced by: Shop
  • Listened to by: Shops of the city

items.title: boutique.vente
items.text:
The player sold an item to a merchant (cible): quantite how many they gave, prix what they received, in monnaie. The inventory has already changed.

  • Fields: cible (id), objet (text), quantite (number), prix (number), monnaie (text)
  • Announced by: Shop
  • Listened to by: —

items.title: quetes.demarrer
items.text:
Ask the quest log to give a quest to the player, by its title: from a script, a dialogue or a trigger. Nothing happens if it was already given.

  • Fields: quete (text)
  • Announced by: —
  • Listened to by: Quest log

items.title: quetes.creer
items.text:
Ask the quest log to make a real quest from a template (Journal de quêtes 15, events version 34): modele is the template's title (a quest ticked modele). Its holes {name} are filled from valeurs ({lieu = id, n = 3}), or from a field of the event with the hole's name (cible, from a Trigger rule), otherwise by the template's draw rows (an object with a tag at a distance from the player, a number); a value given comes before the draw. titre: its title, holes allowed (empty: the template's title and the next number, "Livraison 3"). graine: the seed of the draw (the same seed gives the same result; empty: drawn from the game). The quest starts at once; quetes.creee follows, or quetes.creation_impossible.

  • Fields: modele (text), valeurs (table?), titre (text?), graine (number?)
  • Announced by: —
  • Listened to by: Quest log

items.title: quetes.creee
items.text:
A quest was made from a template (Journal de quêtes 15, events version 34): quete is its own title, modele the template's, valeurs the value of each hole (an object's id, a number, a text). Sent before its quetes.debut. groupe: true for a quest of the whole group.

  • Fields: modele (text), quete (text), valeurs (table), groupe (boolean?)
  • Announced by: Quest log
  • Listened to by: Population

items.title: quetes.creation_impossible
items.text:
A quest could not be made from a template (Journal de quêtes 15, events version 34); nothing was created. motif: modele_inconnu (no quest of that title), pas_un_modele (the quest is not ticked modele), aucun_candidat (no object with the tag at that distance), valeur_manquante (a hole has no value and no draw), conditions (the template's prerequisites are not met), titre_pris (the title given is already a quest's). raison says it in a sentence, also written in the game log.

  • Fields: modele (text), motif (text), raison (text), groupe (boolean?)
  • Announced by: Quest log
  • Listened to by: —

items.title: quetes.debut
items.text:
A quest started: quete is its title. groupe (Journal de quêtes 8): true for a quest of the whole group (game setting groupe), sent once for the group, joueur being who moved it on.

  • Fields: quete (text), groupe (boolean?)
  • Announced by: Quest log
  • Listened to by: Loot, Map, Population

items.title: quetes.etape_debut
items.text:
A step of a quest starts (Journal de quêtes 11, events version 33): it becomes one to do now, its other ways to end it too. etape is its rank in the quest (from 1), texte what it says. Sent after quetes.debut for the first steps, then after the quetes.etape that opened it, and again when the step starts over (an "Also fails if" row set to recommence) or the quest resumes at it (quetes.reprise); its own annonce_debut event follows. Not sent again when a saved game is loaded. groupe (Journal de quêtes 8): true for a quest of the whole group.

  • Fields: quete (text), etape (number), texte (text), groupe (boolean?)
  • Announced by: Quest log
  • Listened to by: Map, Population

items.title: quetes.etape
items.text:
A step of a quest is done: etape is its rank in the quest (from 1), texte what it said. Sent before quetes.fin when it was the last one. issue (Journal de quêtes 11): the rank (from 1) of the other way to end the step that did it, absent when the step itself did; texte is then that way's text. suite (Journal de quêtes 11): the label the quest goes to next (fin, echec or a step's label), absent when it simply goes on to the next row. groupe (Journal de quêtes 8): true for a quest of the whole group (game setting groupe), sent once for the group, joueur being who moved it on.

  • Fields: quete (text), etape (number), texte (text), issue (number?), suite (text?), groupe (boolean?)
  • Announced by: Quest log
  • Listened to by: Map, Population

items.title: quetes.fin
items.text:
A quest is finished: all its steps are done. Its reward, if any, has been asked to the inventory. xp and piste (version 28): its XP for the Progression module and the track that gets it (empty: the main one). facultatives (Journal de quêtes 11): {faites, total}, how many of its optional steps were done, out of how many; absent when it has none. groupe (Journal de quêtes 8): true for a quest of the whole group (game setting groupe), sent once for the group, joueur being who moved it on.

  • Fields: quete (text), xp (number?), piste (text?), groupe (boolean?), facultatives (table?)
  • Announced by: Quest log
  • Listened to by: Loot, Map, Population, Progression

items.title: quetes.etape_echec
items.text:
A step of a quest failed (Journal de quêtes 11, events version 33): one of its "Also fails if" rows happened. etape is its rank in the quest (from 1), alors what that row does: echoue (the quest fails, quetes.echec follows), recommence (the step starts again from zero) or etiquette (the quest goes to the row's label). Also sent for an "Also fails if" row under the quest itself that does not make it fail (recommence: the quest starts again; etiquette), etape being then the step it was waiting for (0: none). For an optional step, manquee is true: the step is only missed, the quest goes on without it. groupe: true for a quest of the whole group.

  • Fields: quete (text), etape (number), alors (text), manquee (boolean?), groupe (boolean?)
  • Announced by: Quest log
  • Listened to by: Map, Population

items.title: quetes.echouer
items.text:
Ask the quest log to make a quest in progress fail, by its title: from a script or a trigger. Nothing happens if it is not in progress.

  • Fields: quete (text)
  • Announced by: —
  • Listened to by: Quest log

items.title: quetes.abandonner
items.text:
Ask the quest log to abandon a quest in progress, by its title, as the player does from the log. Nothing happens if it is not in progress.

  • Fields: quete (text)
  • Announced by: —
  • Listened to by: Quest log

items.title: quetes.echec
items.text:
A quest failed: an event, a mark, its time ran out, or quetes.echouer. It gives no reward; it may be given again if its settings allow it. groupe (Journal de quêtes 8): true for a quest of the whole group (game setting groupe), sent once for the group, joueur being who moved it on.

  • Fields: quete (text), groupe (boolean?)
  • Announced by: Quest log
  • Listened to by: Loot, Map, Population

items.title: quetes.reessayer
items.text:
Ask the quest log to try a failed quest again, by its title (Journal de quêtes 11, events version 33): the same as its Try again button in the log. It resumes from where its setting reprise says (the start, the failed step or the last checkpoint). Nothing happens if it has not failed or cannot be taken up again (reprendre).

  • Fields: quete (text)
  • Announced by: —
  • Listened to by: Quest log

items.title: quetes.reprise
items.text:
A quest resumes (Journal de quêtes 11, events version 33): tried again after a failure (the log's Try again button, reessayer auto, quetes.reessayer, or given again when it does not start over), or started again by an "Also fails if" row of the quest set to recommence. etape is the step it resumes at (from 1; 0: none). The steps before it stay done; marks stay set and the world is not put back as it was: a Trigger rule on the step's annonce_debut does that. groupe: true for a quest of the whole group.

  • Fields: quete (text), etape (number), groupe (boolean?)
  • Announced by: Quest log
  • Listened to by: Map, Population

items.title: quetes.abandon
items.text:
The player abandoned a quest from the log (or quetes.abandonner asked for it). It gives no reward; it may be given again if its settings allow it. groupe (Journal de quêtes 8): true for a quest of the whole group (game setting groupe), sent once for the group, joueur being who moved it on.

  • Fields: quete (text), groupe (boolean?)
  • Announced by: Quest log
  • Listened to by: Loot, Map, Population

items.title: carte.ouverte
items.text:
The big map opened (ouvert true) or closed (ouvert false). The world is stopped while it is open, unless its setting says otherwise.

  • Fields: ouvert (boolean)
  • Announced by: Map
  • Listened to by: —

items.title: carte.decouvert
items.text:
The player discovered a map marker (cible), one shown only once discovered: they came near enough, or carte.reveler revealed it. It now shows on the map.

  • Fields: cible (id)
  • Announced by: Map
  • Listened to by: —

items.title: carte.reveler
items.text:
Ask the map to reveal the marker of cible, as if the player had come near: a character who tells where a place is, a scroll read, a quest step.

  • Fields: cible (id)
  • Announced by: —
  • Listened to by: Map

items.title: articulation.cassee
items.text:
A joint (an object carrying the articulation system) gave way: pulled harder than its breaking force, or broken by the Trigger or game.joint_break. autre is the object it was attached to, missing when attached to the world. Announced by the engine.

  • Fields: cible (id), autre (id?)
  • Announced by: Joint
  • Listened to by: Trigger

items.title: vehicule.monte
items.text:
A player got into a vehicle (an object carrying the vehicule system) and now drives it: qui and joueur are their character (the host's, or a guest's). Announced by the engine.

  • Fields: cible (id), qui (id), joueur (id?)
  • Announced by: Vehicle
  • Listened to by: Companion, Population, Quest log

items.title: vehicule.descendu
items.text:
A player got out of a vehicle. Announced by the engine.

  • Fields: cible (id), qui (id), joueur (id?)
  • Announced by: Vehicle
  • Listened to by: Companion, Population, Quest log

items.title: vehicule.tombe
items.text:
A motorbike fell over on its side (a crash, a turn too tight, a push). Its rider, if any, is thrown off. Announced by the engine.

  • Fields: cible (id), qui (id?)
  • Announced by: Vehicle
  • Listened to by: —

items.title: chiffon.tombe
items.text:
A character fell limp as a ragdoll: on its death, under a hard hit, or by game.ragdoll. Announced by the engine.

  • Fields: cible (id)
  • Announced by: Ragdoll
  • Listened to by: —

items.title: chiffon.releve
items.text:
A ragdoll got back up: its animation resumes. Announced by the engine.

  • Fields: cible (id)
  • Announced by: Ragdoll
  • Listened to by: —

items.title: besoins.change
items.text:
A need of the player (hunger, thirst, tiredness...) changed by a whole point, or is announced once when the game starts. besoin is its name as written in the needs list (original language).

  • Fields: besoin (text), valeur (number), max (number)
  • Announced by: Needs
  • Listened to by: —

items.title: besoins.bas
items.text:
A need went below the warning level of the besoins system (its bar blinks): a sound, a message, a quest hint.

  • Fields: besoin (text), valeur (number), max (number)
  • Announced by: Needs
  • Listened to by: —

items.title: besoins.vide
items.text:
A need reached zero: from now on the player loses health each second (and maybe walks slower or cannot run), until it goes back up.

  • Fields: besoin (text)
  • Announced by: Needs
  • Listened to by: —

items.title: besoins.consomme
items.text:
The player ate or drank one item of the inventory (its foods list): it has been taken from the inventory and its needs raised.

  • Fields: objet (text)
  • Announced by: Needs
  • Listened to by: —

items.title: besoins.source
items.text:
The player used a source of the world carrying the besoins system (a well, a river, a bed): besoin went up by montant.

  • Fields: cible (id), besoin (text), montant (number)
  • Announced by: Needs
  • Listened to by: —

items.title: besoins.remplir
items.text:
Ask the besoins system to raise a need by its name, without using anything up: a meal at an inn, a Trigger rule, a script.

  • Fields: besoin (text), montant (number)
  • Announced by: Trigger
  • Listened to by: Needs

items.title: besoins.consommer
items.text:
Ask the besoins system to eat or drink one item of the inventory, as a click on its slot would: nothing happens if it is not a food or the player has none.

  • Fields: objet (text)
  • Announced by: —
  • Listened to by: Needs

items.title: fabrication.fabrique
items.text:
The player crafted a recipe: its ingredients left the inventory and objet (quantite of it) came in, at once or at the end of its time in the queue. etabli is the kind of station where it was made (empty bare-handed), cible the station object (missing bare-handed).

  • Fields: objet (text), quantite (number), etabli (text), cible (text?), xp (number?), piste (text?)
  • Announced by: Crafting
  • Listened to by: Progression, Knowledge

items.title: fabrication.manque
items.text:
A recipe could not be crafted: manque lists what is missing, in the player's language ("2 Wood, 1 Stone"), or etabli names the stations it needs (with niveau, the minimum level, when the station is too low), or combustible the fuel a station out of fire needs.

  • Fields: objet (text), manque (text?), etabli (text?), niveau (number?), combustible (text?)
  • Announced by: Crafting
  • Listened to by: —

items.title: fabrication.ouvrir
items.text:
Ask the crafting system to open its window, with the recipes of the station object cible, or of the kind of station named etabli (empty or missing: bare-handed): a Trigger rule, a button of a drawn screen. onglet opens it on another module's tab (equipement.atelier: the workshop). It opens for joueur only; without joueur, for the host only (never for every player).

  • Fields: etabli (text?), cible (text?), onglet (text?), joueur (id?)
  • Announced by: Equipment
  • Listened to by: Crafting

items.title: fabrication.onglet
items.text:
The crafting window opened another module's tab at a station (onglet, its key; parent, the empty panel to fill; largeur, the window's width), or left it (onglet empty). The module whose tab it is fills the panel.

  • Fields: joueur (id), onglet (text), cible (id?), etabli (text?), parent (text?), largeur (number?)
  • Announced by: Crafting
  • Listened to by: Equipment

items.title: fabrication.fabriquer
items.text:
Ask the crafting system to craft the recipe that gives objet, as its button would, at the station object cible, or at the kind of station named etabli (the nearest one of that kind within reach, else as if at a level 1 station), empty or missing: bare-handed. Refused, with fabrication.manque, if something is missing. A recipe with a time joins the queue.

  • Fields: objet (text), etabli (text?), cible (text?)
  • Announced by: —
  • Listened to by: Crafting

items.title: fabrication.commencee
items.text:
A recipe with a time joined the player's queue: its ingredients left the inventory; objet (quantite of it) comes in after temps seconds. etabli is the kind of station, cible the station object (missing bare-handed).

  • Fields: objet (text), quantite (number), temps (number), etabli (text), cible (text?)
  • Announced by: Crafting
  • Listened to by: —

items.title: fabrication.finie
items.text:
A recipe of the queue is done: objet (quantite of it) came into the inventory. fabrication.fabrique is announced too.

  • Fields: objet (text), quantite (number), etabli (text), cible (text?)
  • Announced by: Crafting
  • Listened to by: —

items.title: fabrication.station_amelioree
items.text:
A station (cible, of the kind etabli) was upgraded to the level niveau, named nom (empty if the level has no name); its cost left the inventory. With a model for that level, cible is the new copy, and ancienne the object it replaced.

  • Fields: cible (text), etabli (text), niveau (number), nom (text), ancienne (text?)
  • Announced by: Crafting
  • Listened to by: —

items.title: fabrication.allumee
items.text:
A station that burns fuel (cible, of the kind etabli) starts burning. Its particles effect (the particules system) is switched on with it.

  • Fields: cible (text), etabli (text)
  • Announced by: Crafting
  • Listened to by: —

items.title: fabrication.combustible_vide
items.text:
A station (cible, of the kind etabli) burnt its last fuel (combustible): it stops crafting until fuel is added, and its particles effect is switched off.

  • Fields: cible (text), etabli (text), combustible (text)
  • Announced by: Crafting
  • Listened to by: —

items.title: fabrication.ameliorer
items.text:
Ask the crafting system to upgrade the station cible to its next level, as its Upgrade button would: the player pays the cost. Refused, with a message in the window, if something is missing.

  • Fields: cible (text)
  • Announced by: —
  • Listened to by: Crafting

items.title: fabrication.alimenter
items.text:
Ask the crafting system to put quantite (1 if missing) of the fuel of the station cible into it, taken from the player's inventory, as its fuel button would.

  • Fields: cible (text), quantite (number?)
  • Announced by: —
  • Listened to by: Crafting

items.title: savoir.appris
items.text:
The player learned a knowledge (version 26): connaissance is its name (original language), moyen how (depart, objet, etude, points, plan, evenement, marque, analyse, fabrication, apprendre), categorie its category, etiquettes the tags it unlocks, separated by commas. Each tag is also set as a Dialogue mark of the same word.

  • Fields: connaissance (text), moyen (text), categorie (text), etiquettes (text)
  • Announced by: Knowledge
  • Listened to by: —

items.title: savoir.points
items.text:
The player's knowledge points changed (version 26): points is the new total, gain what was added (negative when spent in the tree).

  • Fields: points (number), gain (number)
  • Announced by: Knowledge
  • Listened to by: —

items.title: savoir.analyse
items.text:
The player analysed an object of the world (version 26): cible, which counts for the knowledge connaissance; compte analyses done, besoin needed.

  • Fields: connaissance (text), compte (number), besoin (number), cible (id)
  • Announced by: Knowledge
  • Listened to by: —

items.title: savoir.refus
items.text:
A knowledge could not be learned (version 26): raison says why, in the player's language (what is needed first, missing points or items, a game script's refusal).

  • Fields: connaissance (text), raison (text)
  • Announced by: Knowledge
  • Listened to by: —

items.title: savoir.apprendre
items.text:
Ask the knowledge system to teach connaissance to the player (version 26), even without what it needs first: a Trigger rule, a master in a Dialogue, a quest's reward. A game script can still refuse it (savoir.permise).

  • Fields: connaissance (text), joueur (id?)
  • Announced by: Trigger, Progression
  • Listened to by: Knowledge

items.title: savoir.donner_points
items.text:
Ask the knowledge system to give points to the player (version 26), to spend in the knowledge window: a level gained, a book read.

  • Fields: points (number), joueur (id?)
  • Announced by: Trigger, Progression
  • Listened to by: Knowledge

items.title: savoir.ouvrir
items.text:
Ask the knowledge system to open its window (version 26); with table, the study of that research table's items.

  • Fields: table (text?)
  • Announced by: —
  • Listened to by: Knowledge

items.title: savoir.etudier
items.text:
Ask the knowledge system to study objet as at the research table named table (empty or missing: any table), as its button would (version 26). Refused, with savoir.refus, if something is missing.

  • Fields: objet (text), table (text?)
  • Announced by: —
  • Listened to by: Knowledge

items.title: construction.pose
items.text:
The player placed a piece (a copy of its model, cible), and its cost left the inventory. piece is its name (original language).

  • Fields: cible (id), piece (text)
  • Announced by: Building
  • Listened to by: —

items.title: construction.detruit
items.text:
A placed piece is gone: torn down by the player, by construction.detruire, or killed (sante.mort). Its place on the grid is free again.

  • Fields: cible (id), piece (text)
  • Announced by: Building
  • Listened to by: —

items.title: construction.mode
items.text:
The building mode opened (actif true: the cursor shows and a preview follows it) or closed.

  • Fields: actif (boolean)
  • Announced by: Building
  • Listened to by: —

items.title: construction.manque
items.text:
The player tried to place a piece without its cost: manque lists what is missing, in the player's language.

  • Fields: piece (text), manque (text)
  • Announced by: Building
  • Listened to by: —

items.title: construction.detruire
items.text:
Ask the building system to remove a placed piece (a storm, an enemy, a script). rendre true gives back part of its cost, as tearing it down would.

  • Fields: cible (id), rendre (boolean?)
  • Announced by: —
  • Listened to by: Building

items.title: jour_nuit.heure
items.text:
A new hour of the world started (0 to 23), on day jour (1 the first day).

  • Fields: heure (number), jour (number)
  • Announced by: Day and night
  • Listened to by: Population

items.title: jour_nuit.lever
items.text:
The sun rose: day jour begins. Lamps tagged for the night went out.

  • Fields: jour (number)
  • Announced by: Day and night
  • Listened to by: Progression, Quest log

items.title: jour_nuit.coucher
items.text:
The sun set: night falls. Lamps tagged for the night lit up.

  • Fields: jour (number)
  • Announced by: Day and night
  • Listened to by: —

items.title: jour_nuit.avancer
items.text:
Ask the day and night system to move the clock on by heures (a night in a bed: 8). Every hour, sunrise and sunset crossed are announced in order.

  • Fields: heures (number)
  • Announced by: Needs
  • Listened to by: Day and night

items.title: jour_nuit.aller_a
items.text:
Ask the day and night system to move the clock on to the next time it is heure (0 to 24): sleep until 7, wait until night.

  • Fields: heure (number)
  • Announced by: —
  • Listened to by: Day and night

items.title: tir.arme
items.text:
The ranged weapon in the player's hand changed (version 25): arme is its name in the tir module's list, "" when no ranged weapon is held (another item, empty hands).

  • Fields: arme (text), joueur (id?)
  • Announced by: Ranged weapons
  • Listened to by: —

items.title: tir.tenir
items.text:
Without the Inventory, give a ranged weapon to the player (if they do not have it yet, with its starting ammunition) and put it in hand (version 25); arme "" puts it away. With the Inventory, use inventaire.ajouter and inventaire.tenir instead.

  • Fields: arme (text), joueur (id?)
  • Announced by: —
  • Listened to by: Ranged weapons

items.title: tir.tir
items.text:
The player fired a ranged weapon (version 25), whether it hits or not: origine is the muzzle, direction the aim before spread. For a sound, a noise that alerts enemies, a counter.

  • Fields: source (id), arme (text), origine (vector), direction (vector)
  • Announced by: Ranged weapons
  • Listened to by: Equipment, Population

items.title: tir.touche
items.text:
A shot of the player hit something carrying Health (version 25); the health module has been asked to remove montant (before armor). partie is tete, torse, bras or jambes (missing for an object or an explosion); tete is true for a head shot. All the pellets of one shotgun shot on the same target make one tir.touche.

  • Fields: cible (id), source (id), arme (text), montant (number), partie (text?), point (vector), tete (boolean)
  • Announced by: Ranged weapons
  • Listened to by: Equipment

items.title: tir.recharge
items.text:
A reload of the weapon in hand (version 25): etat is debut (it starts), fin (the magazine is filled) or annule (the weapon was put away meanwhile). chargeur is what the magazine holds, reserve the ammunition left (-1: endless).

  • Fields: source (id), arme (text), etat (text), chargeur (number), reserve (number)
  • Announced by: Ranged weapons
  • Listened to by: —

items.title: tir.vide
items.text:
The player pulled the trigger with nothing to shoot (version 25): an empty magazine or no ammunition left. For a click sound or a message.

  • Fields: source (id), arme (text)
  • Announced by: Ranged weapons
  • Listened to by: —

items.title: tir.explosion
items.text:
A shot of the player exploded (version 25): a grenade at the end of its fuse or a rocket on impact. Health was removed within rayon metres, with no wall in between.

  • Fields: source (id), arme (text), point (vector), rayon (number)
  • Announced by: Ranged weapons
  • Listened to by: Population

items.title: projectile.touche
items.text:
A projectile launched by game.projectile hit something: cible is the object hit (nil for the terrain and for water), partie the part of a character's body (tete, torse, bras, jambes; missing for an object), os the bone, vitesse its velocity on arrival (m/s), data the table given at launch. eau = true when it entered water (point on the surface): it goes on, strongly slowed, and sinks (put a splash there, game.effect("eclaboussure", e.point), or stop it with game.stop_projectile). Announced by the engine; a projectile that bounces announces each hit.

  • Fields: projectile (number), owner (id?), cible (id?), point (vector), normale (vector), partie (text?), os (text?), vitesse (vector), eau (boolean?), data (table?)
  • Announced by: —
  • Listened to by: Enemies, Population, Ranged weapons

items.title: projectile.fin
items.text:
A projectile launched by game.projectile is gone: raison is touche (it hit and stopped), duree (its life ran out: a grenade explodes here), plantee (stuck, its delay is over), cible_partie (what it was stuck in disappeared), eau (a projectile without gravity stopped by water) or arrete (game.stop_projectile). point is where it ended. Announced by the engine.

  • Fields: projectile (number), owner (id?), raison (text), point (vector), data (table?)
  • Announced by: —
  • Listened to by: Enemies, Ranged weapons

items.title: objet.cree
items.text:
Sent by the engine (ADR-039) when the host created the record of a unique item (game.item_create): numero is its number, sorte its kind.

  • Fields: numero (number), sorte (text)
  • Announced by: —
  • Listened to by: Equipment

items.title: objet.change
items.text:
Sent by the engine when the host changed the record of a unique item (game.item_set): champs lists the fields given.

  • Fields: numero (number), sorte (text), champs (table)
  • Announced by: —
  • Listened to by: Equipment, Inventory

items.title: objet.detruit
items.text:
Sent by the engine when the record of a unique item was destroyed (game.item_destroy), or removed by game.item_collect (ramasse = true, nothing held it any more).

  • Fields: numero (number), sorte (text?), ramasse (boolean?)
  • Announced by: —
  • Listened to by: —

items.title: progression.xp
items.text:
Sent by the engine (ADR-038) when a player gained XP on a track (game.progress_add_xp): gain is what was given after the global multiplier and the cap, xp the track's total, niveau its level, source where it came from, cle the player's key.

  • Fields: joueur (id?), cle (text), piste (text), gain (number), xp (number), niveau (number), source (text)
  • Announced by: —
  • Listened to by: Progression

items.title: progression.niveau
items.text:
Sent by the engine for each level a player reached on a track (several levels at once: several events), also when an admin sets a level. The Progression module gives the rewards of that level; a Trigger rule can play a sound or open a door.

  • Fields: joueur (id?), cle (text), piste (text), niveau (number), ancien (number)
  • Announced by: —
  • Listened to by: Progression, Quest log

items.title: progression.rendu
items.text:
Sent by the engine when spent points were given back (game.progress_refund, or an admin's rendre_points).

  • Fields: joueur (id?), cle (text), sorte (text), points (number)
  • Announced by: —
  • Listened to by: —

items.title: progression.donner
items.text:
Ask the Progression module to give xp to the player (a Trigger rule, a script): it goes through the multipliers and the hook progression.gain, on the host. piste: a track's identifier (empty or missing: the main one); source: a short name for the repetition and the cap.

  • Fields: joueur (id?), xp (number), piste (text?), source (text?)
  • Announced by: Quest log
  • Listened to by: Progression

items.title: progression.depenser
items.text:
Ask the Progression module to spend points on one rank of a characteristic (its name, as in its row) for the player: the host checks the points and the maximum, then answers progression.depense or progression.refus. The Character window sends it.

  • Fields: joueur (id?), caracteristique (text)
  • Announced by: Progression
  • Listened to by: Progression

items.title: progression.depense
items.text:
A rank of a characteristic was bought: rang is its new rank. Its bonuses are already applied.

  • Fields: joueur (id), caracteristique (text), rang (number)
  • Announced by: Progression
  • Listened to by: Progression

items.title: progression.reinitialiser
items.text:
Ask the Progression module to give back the points spent on characteristics (if the game allows it, for its cost). Answers progression.reinitialise or progression.refus.

  • Fields: joueur (id?)
  • Announced by: Progression
  • Listened to by: Progression

items.title: progression.reinitialise
items.text:
The characteristics were reset: points is how many points came back.

  • Fields: joueur (id), points (number)
  • Announced by: Progression
  • Listened to by: Progression

items.title: progression.refus
items.text:
Something was refused to the player by the Progression module: a required level (an item, a door, a zone), points missing, a maximum reached. raison is the text shown, already in the player's language.

  • Fields: joueur (id), raison (text)
  • Announced by: Progression
  • Listened to by: Progression

items.title: progression.recompense
items.text:
A level gave one of its rewards: sorte is points, bonus, connaissance, objet, marque or evenement; nom its kind of points, value, knowledge, item, mark or event; nombre how many.

  • Fields: joueur (id), piste (text), niveau (number), sorte (text), nom (text), nombre (number)
  • Announced by: Progression
  • Listened to by: —

items.title: progression.niveau_ennemi
items.text:
The Progression module gave an enemy its level (fixed, per zone, matched to the players or growing with time): its health and damage grew with it. To show it above its head.

  • Fields: cible (id), niveau (number)
  • Announced by: Progression
  • Listened to by: Loot

items.title: progression.perte
items.text:
The player died and lost xp on a track (never below its level). recuperable: the XP waits where they died.

  • Fields: joueur (id), piste (text), xp (number), recuperable (boolean)
  • Announced by: Progression
  • Listened to by: Progression

items.title: progression.recupere
items.text:
The player came back where they died and recovered the xp lost on a track.

  • Fields: joueur (id), piste (text), xp (number)
  • Announced by: Progression
  • Listened to by: Progression

items.title: progression.ouvrir
items.text:
Ask the Progression module to open the Character window of the player, as its key (P) does.

  • Fields: joueur (id?)
  • Announced by: —
  • Listened to by: Progression

items.title: progression.reputation
items.text:
Ask the Progression module to change the player's reputation with a faction (Progression 9): piste is a track of kind reputation (faction is accepted too); valeur is added (negative: it goes down), or set when fixer is true; it stays within the track's bounds. Sent by a quest, a step or a way to end it (its reputation field), a Trigger rule or a script. groupe: every player present.

  • Fields: joueur (id?), piste (text), faction (text?), valeur (number), fixer (boolean?), groupe (boolean?), source (text?)
  • Announced by: Quest log
  • Listened to by: Progression

items.title: progression.reputation_change
items.text:
A player's reputation with a faction changed (Progression 9): valeur is the new value, avant the old one, ecart the change, palier the name of its tier now. To show it, or for a Trigger rule.

  • Fields: joueur (id), piste (text), valeur (number), avant (number), ecart (number), palier (text), source (text?)
  • Announced by: Progression
  • Listened to by: Progression

items.title: progression.palier
items.text:
A player's reputation reached another tier (Progression 9): palier is the new tier's name, ancien the old one's, rang its rank from 1 (the lowest), monte true if it went up. For the game to react: guards that attack once Hostile, a shop that opens once Friendly.

  • Fields: joueur (id), piste (text), palier (text), ancien (text), rang (number), monte (boolean), valeur (number)
  • Announced by: Progression
  • Listened to by: Progression

items.title: butin.lacher
items.text:
Ask the Loot module to roll a table and drop what it gives (the Trigger, a script). position or cible: where; niveau: the item level; joueur: for whom (the killer, for sharing).

  • Fields: table (text), position (vector?), cible (id?), niveau (number?), joueur (id?)
  • Announced by: Trigger, Quest log
  • Listened to by: Loot

items.title: butin.remplir
items.text:
Ask the Loot module to roll a table into a content (a chest of the Chests module): cle names the content, joueur_seul reserves it for one player.

  • Fields: cle (text), table (text), niveau (number?), joueur (id?), joueur_seul (id?)
  • Announced by: Chests
  • Listened to by: Loot

items.title: butin.tombe
items.text:
Loot was rolled and placed (on the ground, in the inventory or in a content): how many lines dropped.

  • Fields: table (text), nombre (number), cible (text?), joueur (id?)
  • Announced by: Loot
  • Listened to by: —

items.title: butin.ramasse
items.text:
A player took a piece of loot (from the ground or a Take all window). fiche: the unique item's record, if it is one.

  • Fields: objet (text), quantite (number), fiche (number?), joueur (id)
  • Announced by: Loot
  • Listened to by: —

items.title: butin.refus
items.text:
The host refused a player taking loot reserved for someone else (sharing personal, killer or in turn).

  • Fields: cible (text), joueur (id), raison (text)
  • Announced by: Loot
  • Listened to by: Loot

items.title: butin.ouvrir
items.text:
Open the Take all window of a content (a body, a chest) for a player.

  • Fields: cible (text), joueur (id?)
  • Announced by: Loot, Chests
  • Listened to by: Loot, Inventory

items.title: butin.contenu
items.text:
A content (a body, a chest) changed: its Take all windows redraw.

  • Fields: cible (text), nombre (number)
  • Announced by: Loot
  • Listened to by: Loot, Inventory

items.title: butin.sac
items.text:
A dead player dropped their bag (Loot setting mort_sac): cible is the bag left where they fell (nil: each item on the ground), nombre the lines dropped.

  • Fields: joueur (id), cible (id?), nombre (number), position (vector)
  • Announced by: Loot
  • Listened to by: —

items.title: butin.prendre
items.text:
A player asks the host to take from a content: one line (numero) or all they may take.

  • Fields: cible (text), numero (number?), joueur (id)
  • Announced by: Loot, Chests, Inventory
  • Listened to by: Loot

items.title: butin.ranger
items.text:
A player asks the host to put an item of their bag into a chest they may search (the three-part inventory window): a stack (quantite) or a unique copy (fiche). The bag loses it first; nothing enters if the bag no longer has it.

  • Fields: cible (text), objet (text), fiche (number?), quantite (number?), case (text?), joueur (id)
  • Announced by: Inventory
  • Listened to by: Loot

items.title: coffres.ouvert
items.text:
A chest was opened. rempli: a new roll filled it (the first time, or after its delay).

  • Fields: cible (id), joueur (id), rempli (boolean)
  • Announced by: Chests
  • Listened to by: —

items.title: manche.lancer
items.text:
Ask the Round module to start the game now (a menu's Start button, a script), when its setting attente waits for players or for the host. Without effect once started.

  • Fields: —
  • Announced by: —
  • Listened to by: Round

items.title: manche.nouvelle
items.text:
A round is set up (Round module): every player is at their starting place, frozen during the countdown. numero counts from 1; total is the setting manches. The Race resets its laps here.

  • Fields: numero (number), total (number)
  • Announced by: Round
  • Listened to by: Race

items.title: manche.depart
items.text:
The countdown is over: Go! (Round module). The stopwatch of the round starts now.

  • Fields: numero (number), total (number)
  • Announced by: Round
  • Listened to by: Race

items.title: manche.arrivee
items.text:
A player arrived (the Race at the end of the last lap, a zone or a script): the Round module notes their time. Counts once per round.

  • Fields: joueur (id)
  • Announced by: Race
  • Listened to by: Round

items.title: manche.progression
items.text:
How far a player got, a number that grows as they advance (the Race: laps and checkpoints passed, then the share of the way to the next). The Round module ranks those who have not arrived by it.

  • Fields: joueur (id), valeur (number)
  • Announced by: Race
  • Listened to by: Round

items.title: manche.points
items.text:
Give points to a player or a team (Round module, ranking on points): from the Trigger, a script or another system. points may be negative; 1 by default. equipe is a team's name or number.

  • Fields: joueur (id?), equipe (text?), points (number?)
  • Announced by: —
  • Listened to by: Round

items.title: manche.eliminer
items.text:
Put a player out of the round (Round module): they are ranked after those still in, and see Out on screen.

  • Fields: joueur (id)
  • Announced by: —
  • Listened to by: Round

items.title: manche.equipe
items.text:
Put a player in a team (Round module, teams chosen by the game): equipe is the team's name or number. Takes effect at the next round's setup for the starting places.

  • Fields: joueur (id), equipe (text)
  • Announced by: —
  • Listened to by: Round

items.title: manche.resultat
items.text:
A player's round result is known (Round module): they arrived (temps in seconds since Go, rang their place), or they are out (elimine).

  • Fields: joueur (id), temps (number?), rang (number?), elimine (boolean?)
  • Announced by: Round
  • Listened to by: —

items.title: manche.fin
items.text:
A round ended (Round module). classement: the ranking, best first, a list of rows {joueur or equipe, nom, rang, temps?, points, vies, progression, elimine, arrive}; gagnant: the first's player id or team name; raison: arrivee, limite, score or dernier.

  • Fields: numero (number), total (number), classement (table), raison (text), gagnant (text?)
  • Announced by: Round
  • Listened to by: Race

items.title: manche.terminee
items.text:
The whole game ended (Round module), after the last round: classement is the final ranking (with victoires when there were several rounds). Each player's result is shown by game.finish.

  • Fields: classement (table), gagnant (text?)
  • Announced by: Round
  • Listened to by: —

items.title: course.point
items.text:
A player passed the checkpoint they had to pass (Race module): numero its number, tour the lap, cible the object.

  • Fields: joueur (id), numero (number), tour (number), cible (id)
  • Announced by: Race
  • Listened to by: —

items.title: course.tour
items.text:
A player finished a lap (Race module): tour is the lap just finished, total the number of laps.

  • Fields: joueur (id), tour (number), total (number)
  • Announced by: Race
  • Listened to by: —

items.title: course.retour
items.text:
A player (or their vehicle) was put back at their last checkpoint, facing the next (Race module). raison: chute, zone, danger, touche, mort or script.

  • Fields: joueur (id), cible (id?), raison (text)
  • Announced by: Race
  • Listened to by: —

items.title: course.replacer
items.text:
Ask the Race module to put a player back at their last checkpoint, facing the next one (a trap, a button of the game).

  • Fields: joueur (id)
  • Announced by: —
  • Listened to by: Race

items.title: accompagner.suivre
items.text:
Ask a character carrying the Companion system to follow someone (Companion module, version 34): qui, a player or an object (missing: the one it followed last, else the host); lieu, a place where it announces accompagner.arrive once it gets there while following. cible: the character, by id or name; missing, every character carrying the system in the scene. "Follow me" after accompagner.attendre.

  • Fields: cible (id?), qui (id?), lieu (id?)
  • Announced by: —
  • Listened to by: Companion, Population

items.title: accompagner.aller
items.text:
Ask a Companion character to walk to a place (lieu, an object or a point; missing: its setting destination), waiting whenever the player qui is too far; there it announces accompagner.arrive and waits. cible: as for accompagner.suivre.

  • Fields: cible (id?), lieu (id?), qui (id?)
  • Announced by: —
  • Listened to by: Companion, Population

items.title: accompagner.fuir
items.text:
Ask a Companion character to run away from de (an object or a point; missing: qui, else the nearest player) until distance metres (missing: its setting distance_fuite); it announces accompagner.arrive once safe, and runs again if approached. cible: as for accompagner.suivre.

  • Fields: cible (id?), de (id?), distance (number?), qui (id?)
  • Announced by: —
  • Listened to by: Companion, Population

items.title: accompagner.attendre
items.text:
Ask a Companion character to wait where it is ("Wait here"), remembering whom it followed: accompagner.suivre without qui makes it follow them again. cible: as for accompagner.suivre.

  • Fields: cible (id?)
  • Announced by: —
  • Listened to by: Companion, Population

items.title: accompagner.arreter
items.text:
Ask a Companion character to stop whatever it does and forget whom it followed. cible: as for accompagner.suivre.

  • Fields: cible (id?)
  • Announced by: —
  • Listened to by: Companion, Population

items.title: population.apparait
items.text:
A pedestrian appeared around the player, out of sight (Population module): a copy from the pool, tagged population.

  • Fields: cible (id), sorte (text)
  • Announced by: Population
  • Listened to by: —

items.title: population.disparait
items.text:
A pedestrian left (Population module): too far or behind the player, back to the pool. Its id may come back as another pedestrian. important: it had been kept (touched, named by a quest) and nothing names it any more.

  • Fields: cible (id), sorte (text), important (boolean?)
  • Announced by: Population
  • Listened to by: —

items.title: population.touche
items.text:
A pedestrian became important (Population module): a player touched it (comment frappe, tue, parle, monte) or something keeps it (quetes, accompagner, garder, emmene). The director never takes it back while something names it; it stays itself.

  • Fields: cible (id), joueur (id), comment (text), sorte (text)
  • Announced by: Population
  • Listened to by: —

items.title: population.garder
items.text:
Ask the Population module to never take back this object (it puts the tag population.garder on it).

  • Fields: cible (id)
  • Announced by: —
  • Listened to by: Population

items.title: population.liberer
items.text:
Ask the Population module to let this object go again (it removes the tag population.garder).

  • Fields: cible (id)
  • Announced by: —
  • Listened to by: Population

items.title: population.danger
items.text:
Tell the Population module that something dangerous happens here (a shot, an explosion, a fight a game wants to signal): pedestrians within rayon (its setting peur_rayon when missing) flee, cars heading there stop, nobody appears there while the fear lasts. force (1 by default) multiplies the share who flee and how long. Gunshots (tir.tir), explosions (tir.explosion), impacts (projectile.touche) and deaths (sante.mort) do it by themselves. A game script can replace the reaction with game.override("population.reagir", function(default, e) ... end).

  • Fields: lieu (vector), rayon (number?), force (number?), sorte (text?), source (id?)
  • Announced by: —
  • Listened to by: Population

items.title: population.fuite
items.text:
A danger made pedestrians flee (Population module): lieu is where it happened, rayon how far it scared, passants how many fled.

  • Fields: lieu (vector), rayon (number), passants (number)
  • Announced by: Population
  • Listened to by: —

items.title: population.laisser
items.text:
Tell the Population module that a player left this object born of the population (put down, dropped, abandoned): it is kept as it is for its setting garder_laisse (30 minutes of play by default, 0: always), at most laisse_max per player, and saved. Ignored for an object the author placed (the world already remembers it). Getting out of a car born of the population (vehicule.descendu) does it by itself.

  • Fields: cible (id), joueur (id?)
  • Announced by: —
  • Listened to by: Population

items.title: accompagner.arrive
items.text:
A Companion character arrived (Companion module): mode aller (it reached its place, lieu), suivre (it reached its destination lieu while following qui: the end of an escort) or fuir (it is far enough from what it fled, qui).

  • Fields: cible (id), mode (text), lieu (id?), qui (id?)
  • Announced by: Companion
  • Listened to by: —

items.title: accompagner.perdu
items.text:
A Companion character stayed further than its setting perdu_distance from the one it follows or waits for (qui) for perdu_apres seconds: announced once, until it is close again. mode: suivre or aller.

  • Fields: cible (id), qui (id), mode (text), distance (number)
  • Announced by: Companion
  • Listened to by: —

This page is generated automatically from the WorldMint code (modules/events.json, modules/*/module.json): it always matches the editor.

items.title: Every editor control
items.text: Every field, section, button and menu of the editor, area by area, with what it does. It is the text shown as a tooltip when you rest the mouse on it in the editor. The settings of game systems are described on each system's page.

items.title: Adjusting a character's pose
items.text:
Explained in detail: Adjusting a character's pose.

Control What it does Add a joint here Adds a new joint, child of the chosen one, a little beyond it: you name it, then place it with the gizmo. Without skin it is an attach point (a weapon, a held object, particles); with « Take the skin around » it bends the part of the model beyond it. It can then be animated like the others. Adjust the pose Shows the skeleton in the view and the list of its bones. Click a bone, then turn it (E) or move its point (W) with the gizmo, or type its angles: the character changes before your eyes. Adjusted move The move the adjustment is added to: one move, every move, or "Seated on a vehicle", the pose the game gives the driver of a motorbike or a car. Adjustment layer A layer groups turned bones, for one move or for all of them. A model can have several ("Hands on the handlebar", "Hunched back"). The first adjustment creates one. Adjustment strength At 100%, bones turn by their full angle; at 50%, by half; at 0%, the adjustment does nothing. Animal animations For a quadruped (a four-legged skeleton, from the file or created in the editor): its family, then the animal animations shipped with the editor, those of its family first. The + button gives them to the characters (copied into the project with their licence, added to the player's animation files); Ctrl+Z removes them. Attach the skin Works out how every part of the model follows every bone, through its volume: the upper teeth do not follow the lower jaw, a leg does not take the skin of the next one. Run it again after moving joints. Back to the original skeleton Removes every correction of this model's skeleton: moved, turned, removed and added joints. Ctrl+Z brings them back. Bend direction When moving a hand or a foot: which way the elbow or knee bends. Automatic follows the model's rest pose if it is bent there, otherwise the elbow backward and the knee forward. Forward or backward force it, for a limb that is straight at rest or an animal's leg. Bone gizmo What the gizmo does on the chosen bone: Turn (E) rotates it; Move (W) takes its point where you drag it. The hips really move; a hand or a foot bends the two bones above it (the arm, the leg) without stretching them; an elbow, a knee, the head or the back turn the bones that carry them. The Move and Rotate buttons of the toolbar do the same. Bone rotation The angles added to this bone, in degrees, around the standing character's axes: X tilts it forward or back, Y turns it around, Z tilts it sideways. Bones per leg 3 bones per leg (top, middle, bottom) or 4 (with the shoulder in front and the toes behind), for legs that bend more. Calcul de la peau The weights are worked out in the background: you can keep working, the model changes at the end. They are then stored in the project and not worked out again. Copy the left onto the right Gives the right side the left side's adjustments, mirrored. Copy the pose Keeps this layer's angles to paste them elsewhere: in another layer, or on another character. Copy the right onto the left Gives the left side the right side's adjustments, mirrored. Correct the skeleton Correct the skeleton itself, not a move: put a joint back where the limb should bend (a knee behind the leg, an elbow inside the arm, common on an automatically rigged skeleton), turn it, remove it or add one. The model does not move: only its rest pose changes, and all its moves then bend around the new joint. The model file is never changed: the correction is stored in the project, for this model. Create a skeleton Creates the template's skeleton, fitted to this model: front and back, leg height, the head and an open mouth are measured. The model file is not changed; Ctrl+Z removes it. Create the skeleton again Creates the skeleton again with front and back swapped or another up side, if the measure was wrong. Joints moved since are lost; Ctrl+Z brings them back. Delete the layer Removes the layer and all its adjustments. Ctrl+Z brings it back. Ears Adds a bone to each ear, to prick them up or lay them back. Family This animal's family (canines, equines, deer...), guessed from its model's name when possible. The animations of animals of its family come first: they suit it best. A family without shipped animations says so and offers the closest one. The list of families is data (animations/familles.json, next to WorldMint): you add one without changing anything else. Finish adjusting Hides the skeleton and gives back the object's gizmo. The adjustments stay saved. Joint name The new joint's name, as scripts, held objects and the agent will refer to it. It must differ from the skeleton's names. Joint offset How far this joint was moved inside the model at rest, along the character's axes (X to its left, Y up, Z forward), in model units. Drag or type; the Move gizmo (W) does the same in the view. Joint rotation How far this joint was turned on itself at rest, in degrees around the character's axes. Its axes change, the skin does not move: a limb that bent sideways then bends in the right plane. The Turn gizmo (E) does the same in the view. Layer name The layer's name, also used by scripts to switch it on or off (game.pose_layer). Layer on Off, the layer is kept but no longer plays: handy to compare before and after. Mirror On, the bone on the other side follows, as in a mirror: turning the left arm turns the right one too. Model's up The model's up side, for a model lying down or upside down: the template is measured as if this side were up. Moment of the move The moment of the move that is shown. Play it, or stop it where the adjustment shows best. Move the joint alone Off, the joints below the one you correct follow it (moving the shoulder takes the arm and hand along). On, they stay where they were: only this joint moves, and the bone linking it to the next one gets longer or shorter. Number of bones The number of bones in the chain, along the model: the more there are, the more smoothly the tail or tentacle curves. Paste the pose Puts the copied angles in this layer. Bones this model does not have are ignored. Remove the created skeleton Removes the skeleton created in the editor: the model goes back to having no skeleton. Ctrl+Z brings it back. Remove this joint Removes this joint from the skeleton: the skin it moved now follows its parent, and the joints it carried are attached to its parent, at the same place. Its animations and adjustments are ignored. The root of the skeleton cannot be removed. Restore it with « Restore the joint ». Reset everything Removes every adjustment of the layer. The layer stays, empty. Reset the bone Removes this bone's adjustment: it goes back to the original move. Reset this joint This joint goes back to the place and orientation the model file gives it. The other corrections stay. Show the skeleton Draws the bones in the view: one point per bone, clickable. The chosen bone is highlighted, adjusted bones are green. Skeleton bones All the model's bones, as a tree, with a search. In brackets, what the bone is when recognised (Left hand, Back...); a dot marks an adjusted bone. Skeleton pose For an animated model: adjust its pose, bone by bone, on top of its moves. The adjustments apply to every character using this model, wherever the move plays in the game. Skin method How the skin follows the bones at the joints. Preserve volume: a bent knee or neck keeps its thickness, a bone turned on itself does not twist like a candy wrapper. Linear: the classic blend, where the skin pinches at the folds. Automatic preserves volume. Applies to this model everywhere (editor, game, shadows, ray tracing). Skin softness How wide the passage from one bone to the next is: higher, the skin bends smoothly over a longer stretch (fewer folds and creases); 0, sharp passages. The attached skin is worked out again in the background when you release the slider. Swap front and back If the measure took the head for the tail (or the base of a chain for its tip), switch it on and create the skeleton again. Take the skin around The new joint takes from its parent the skin that lies beyond it, with a smooth transition around it: it then bends that part, like the tip of a tail or an ear. Off, it moves nothing: it is an attach point. Template The shape of the skeleton to create: a standing character, a four-legged animal, a chain (tail, tentacle, plant) or a single bone (a door, a chest). It is fitted to the model's shape; you then move its joints. The bone above Only the bone carrying the point turns around its joint (key 2), to bring the point as close to the mouse as it can; its length does not change. The hips and the root never turn this way: a bone they carry then moves alone. The point alone The point moves as it is (key 1): an offset of that bone, whatever it is. What it carries follows; nothing above turns, the bone above stretches or shortens on screen. To touch up a paw without the whole arm moving. The whole limb As before (key 3): a hand or a foot bends the two bones above it without stretching them; an elbow, a knee, the head or the back turn the bones carrying them; the hips move. Weights of the chosen bone Shows on the model the skin the chosen bone holds: from blue (a little) to red (fully), the rest in grey. Follows the bone you choose and the pose shown. To check a skeleton made in the tool as well as an artist's weights. An editor display only: nothing changes in the game or in the project. What moves When moving a point (W): what moves with it. The point alone (key 1): only it moves, with what it carries; nothing above turns, the bone above stretches or shortens. The bone above (key 2): only the bone carrying it turns toward the mouse, keeping its length. The whole limb (key 3): a hand or a foot bends the two bones above it, the back or the neck turn. In a move, each gesture sets a keyframe; Ctrl+Z undoes it at once.

items.title: Creating a move
items.text:
Explained in detail: Creating a move.

Control What it does Attach to a move This adjustment targets a move the model no longer has (a changed animation file, a deleted move): choose the one it should adjust from now on, or all of them. Attach to this model A move or pose adjustments whose model is gone (deleted or moved outside the editor) no longer play: attaching them to this model makes them play again. Ctrl+Z undoes it. Auto keyframe On, turning a bone or moving its point (with the gizmo or its fields) sets a keyframe at the playhead. Off, only a keyframe already set at that moment changes. Bone offset For the hips (or the root): how much it rises, lowers or moves forward, in the model's units. In a move, a keyframe is set at the playhead; in an adjustment layer, the offset is added to the move. The Move gizmo (W) does the same with the mouse. Close the loop Copies the first pose to the end of the move: the loop restarts without a jolt. When looping, a bone with a keyframe at the start already goes back to it at the end. Copy keyframes Keeps the chosen keyframes and their spacing (Ctrl+C, with the mouse over the timeline), to paste them elsewhere in this move or in another one. Create a move Makes a whole move for this model (a walk, a wave, an attack), keyframe by keyframe, in the timeline. It starts from the rest pose, an existing move or the adjustment layer, and then plays like the moves of the files. Delete the move Removes this move from the project (Ctrl+Z brings it back).
