Systems that played it act without it. Feet on the ground On, turning or moving the hips, or leaning the back, leaves the feet where they are: the legs bend by themselves (to crouch, to lean). Finish the move Closes the move's timeline and goes back to pose adjustment. The move stays in the project, saved with it. Interpolation How each bone goes from the chosen keyframes to the next ones: linear (steady), smooth (slow at start and end), stepped (it jumps from one pose to the next). Move length The length of one round of the move, in seconds. It cannot cut keyframes: move them first. Move name The name under which systems, timelines and scripts play it (game.play). The same name as a move of the file replaces it everywhere. Renaming it makes the pose adjustments that target it follow, in a single Ctrl+Z. Moves made in the tool The moves created for this model. Choose one to edit it: the timeline shows its bones and their keyframes. Onion skin Shows the skeleton a little before (in green) and a little after (in the accent colour) the playhead, in pale lines, to tune a smooth gesture. Paste keyframes Pastes the copied keyframes at the playhead (Ctrl+V), with their spacing: the first lands at that moment. Bones this model does not have, and whatever would go past the length, are left out. Paste keyframes here Pastes the copied keyframes at the moment clicked in the timeline, with their spacing: the first lands at that moment. Bones this model does not have, and whatever would go past the length, are left out. Remove keyframes Removes the keyframes chosen in the timeline (Delete, with the mouse over the timeline). A bone left without keyframes leaves the move. Ctrl+Z brings them back. Show all Shows the whole length of the move in the timeline. Ctrl+wheel zooms around the mouse, Shift+wheel (or the bar under the tracks) scrolls. Start from What the move contains at first: nothing (the rest pose), an existing move read as keyframes (to correct it), or the chosen adjustment layer. Starting move The move copied as keyframes, ten per second, to correct it without touching the original file.

items.title: Editor preferences
items.text:
Explained in detail: Preferences.

Control What it does Accent colour With the Plain look: the color of the editor's main buttons, of the selection and of its highlights. Arrow keys step How far the arrow keys nudge the selection (0.1 m by default): Shift for ten times more, Ctrl for ten times less. Page Up and Page Down move it up and down. Each press is undone with one Ctrl+Z. Automatic backup How often, in seconds, the editor keeps a copy of your work (60 by default); 0 turns it off. The copy is kept separately: it doesn't touch the scene file. Changing your mind The Preferences checkbox, at any time: unchecking stops everything and empties the queue; "Erase my measurements" also erases them on the server. Close preferences Goes back to the properties of what is selected. Dark theme With the Plain look: a dark interface; unchecked, a light one. Display How the work views are drawn. Editor look Mint, WorldMint's look, or Plain, the former one. The change applies at once. Erase my measurements Empties the local queue and asks the server to erase everything that came from this installation; the editor then takes a new identifier. Gizmo size The size of the handles that move, rotate and resize the selected object in the view. Grid step The spacing between grid lines, in meters, and the step for moves when snapping is on. Interface size Makes the editor's text and buttons bigger or smaller, from × 0.6 to × 3. The change applies when you release the field. Lines kept How many messages the console keeps; beyond that, the oldest are removed. Mint WorldMint's look: midnight blue and mint green, the green kept for the Play button, the selection and the checked boxes. This is the default look. Navigation How the 3D view moves with the mouse. Orbit speed How fast the view turns when you drag it with the right mouse button, around the point under the mouse (or the selection, with Ctrl). Pan speed How fast the view moves when you drag it with the middle mouse button (the wheel). At the default value, what is under the mouse follows it, near or far. Place on ground when adding An object added to the scene settles on whatever is below it, instead of staying in the air. Placement How objects are placed and moved in the 3D view. Plain The editor's former look, in grey, with a dark or light theme and the accent color of your choice. Rotation step The step for rotations with the gizmo when snapping is on, in degrees. Saving The automatic backup of your work. Scale step The step for size changes with the gizmo when snapping is on. See what is sent Shows the latest waiting measurements in plain text, exactly as they will be sent. Share usage measurements Checked: the editor sends its usage measurements (agent tokens, project milestones, session length, cleaned crash reports). Unchecked, nothing is measured and the local queue is emptied at once. Usage measurements Only with your consent: a few measurements of how the editor is used, sent to the WorldMint server to improve it. Never your messages, your files or your project names. See the "Your data" page of the documentation. View anti-aliasing Smooths the objects' edges in the work views, when their upscaling is off. None, the starting setting, keeps the picture as it is. TAA: sharp when the camera moves, the view is redrawn for a few frames after each gesture. SMAA: sharp, with no trail. FXAA: the lightest. Automatic follows the views' quality. The game has its own setting, in Game window. View indirect lighting Indirect lighting: light bounced by surfaces (a sunlit floor lights the walls, a room is lit through its window), ray traced with a light cache. Medium quality (at half resolution: one ray for four pixels) and High, with ray tracing; costs about 1 to 2 ms in High. On by default; off, the views keep the sky's ambient light. The player chooses their own in the game's menu. View quality How detailed the work views are: shadows, lights, water, glow, distant terrain and plants. Medium, the starting setting, keeps the editor smooth on a large scene, with four views; High shows the picture as the game draws it on a graphics card; Low helps a small computer. The game started with Play keeps its own quality, and the player chooses theirs in the game's menu. A view is only redrawn when something in it changes: at rest, the editor barely uses the graphics card. View ray tracing The work views' shadows and reflections drawn with real rays of light, on a graphics card that has it (NVIDIA RTX, AMD Radeon RX 6000 and later, Intel Arc). Automatic (the default): only on a dedicated graphics card, in Medium or High quality. On: always, even where the picture may slow down (an integrated chip, Low quality). Off: the usual shadows and reflections. The views only use it if the game allows it (Game window); the player chooses their own in the game's menu. View upscaling Draws the scene smaller in the work views, then enlarges it by blending the frames that follow one another: a modest graphics card draws faster, and the objects' edges no longer look like stairs. "Anti-aliasing only" keeps the full size and only smooths the edges. The game has its own setting: click "This game", at the top of the scene list, then Game window. View upscaling method What enlarges the work views' picture when their upscaling is on. None: WorldMint's own. FSR (all cards): AMD FSR, sharper, on every graphics card. DLSS (NVIDIA): on an NVIDIA GeForce RTX card, from the next start of the editor; as for the game, you first read what NVIDIA's license asks and give the folder of its files. What is measured The numbers the agent gives (tokens, stated cost, duration), a project's milestones, session length, added systems, the machine (Windows, graphics card, screen) and cleaned crash reports. What is never measured Your messages to the agent and its replies, your files, your projects' names and contents, your name, your e-mail. The IP address is not kept. Where and for how long On the WorldMint server, hosted by OVH, for 12 months, under a randomly drawn identifier. Zoom step How much one notch of the wheel zooms: at 0.9, the view gets 10% closer. The lower the value, the faster the zoom.

items.title: Game settings (nothing selected)
items.text:
Explained in detail: The properties.

Control What it does Activity radius In a large world, in the game: beyond this distance around the player, in meters (in squares of 256 m), objects fall asleep. They still exist, but no longer move, walk or detect anything, until the player comes back. The same on every computer: the game plays the same everywhere. 300 m by default. Adaptation time The time the eye takes to get used to the dark, in seconds: 1.5 by default. It gets used to light three times faster, like a real eye. 0: at once. Add a character size Adds a size, with its own walkable areas: twice the typical character at first, to adjust afterwards. Each size is computed separately: add one only for characters really smaller or larger. Allow ray tracing Ray tracing draws shadows and reflections by casting real rays of light through the scene: more accurate shadows, sharp at the foot of objects and softer further away, and water, metal or glass reflecting the scenery, even what is off screen. Only some graphics cards have it (NVIDIA RTX, AMD Radeon RX 6000 and later, Intel Arc). Allowed (the default), the player chooses in the game's options: Automatic, On or Off; Automatic only uses it on a dedicated graphics card, in Medium or High quality, and measures what it costs on the player's card in the first seconds of the game: above 2.5 ms per frame in Medium (4 ms in High), it removes effects one by one (reflections, occlusion, indirect light, lights, then the sun, which the usual shadows take over); the player's menu says what is left. On keeps everything. Turned off here, the game is always drawn without it, with the usual shadows and reflections. Also make a .zip file Each export also writes a .zip file next to the folder, named after the title and the version (My game-1.0.4.zip): ready to upload to itch.io or to send. Nothing is sent anywhere. Always active, advised In a large world: how many objects may stay awake everywhere ("Always active") before the editor shows it in red and the agent is warned. Each costs at every moment of the game, wherever it is. Advice, not a limit: the game keeps them all awake. 100 by default. Anti-aliasing Smooths the objects' edges when upscaling is off (upscaling already does it). Automatic (the default) follows the player's quality: TAA in High and Medium (SMAA in a project created before November 2026), FXAA in Low. TAA: the sharpest when the camera moves, but each picture is rebuilt from the previous ones. SMAA: sharp, with no trail behind what moves. FXAA: the lightest, a little softer. None: stair-stepped edges. FSR 2 native: AMD's FSR at full size, sharper than SMAA on thin lines, signs and railings, less good on foliage; a choice, never Automatic's (WorldMint's TAA replaces it where FSR does not run). The player can change it in the game's menu, Display tab. Anticipation How far ahead in time a character sees an encounter coming, in seconds. Longer: it steps aside earlier and more calmly. Shorter: it brushes past the others. Automatic exposure The image slowly brightens when you walk into a dark place (a house, a cave) and comes back when you walk out, without dazzling: like the eye getting used to it. In sunlight, the image does not change. On by default. In the editor, the views show the image once the eye is used to it. Autosave (minutes) How many minutes between two saves of the world (10 by default). 0: only when stopping and when an admin asks ("sauver"). A world asleep with no player is not saved: nothing changes in it. Avoidance quality How many directions each character tries at each step before choosing. High: closer side steps, for more computing. Low: for crowds of several hundred. Back to the original colors Puts the eight colors of the Stylized style back as shipped, in one undoable step. Background The color behind everything else, where there is nothing. In the distance, objects fade into it, as if in a haze. Backups kept Each save leaves a dated backup, to go back in time ("copies", then "restaurer" on the console or the web page). The oldest beyond this number go away. 0: no backup. Ban this address Adds the typed IP address to the banned addresses, for the server's next start (in game, "bannir_ip" acts at once and makes the players from that address leave). Ctrl+Z undoes it. Bandwidth per player The most the host sends each player, in kilobits per second: 128 by default, which works on almost every connection. When there is too much to send, what is near the player goes first, the rest just after. 0: no limit. Banned IP addresses The IP addresses that can no longer come in, whatever the player's key (if they come back with another one). Type an address (203.0.113.7 or 2001:db8::7, without a port) then "Ban this address"; a row's cross removes it. The "bannir_ip" command adds them in game, "debannir_ip" removes them. An IP address is personal data: keep it only as long as needed. An address is often shared (a home, a mobile network): banning it can ban other people. Banned players The keys of the players who can no longer come in, separated by commas. The "bannir" command adds them in game, "debannir" removes them. Blend with the realistic sky How much of the photo is in the sky: at 0%, the realistic sky alone; at 100% (the default), the photo alone. In between, the photo's clouds over the sky of the hour. Brighten up to How many times brighter the image can get in the dark: 1 never, 4 by default (a dark room becomes readable without turning into daylight), 16 and more, you see almost as in daylight in a cellar. The night of a day and night cycle is not brightened: only what is darker than the current daylight. Cancel typing Closes the password line without changing anything; what was typed is wiped. Character height A character's height, in meters: it walks under anything higher (a bridge, a branch), not under anything lower. Character radius Half a character's width, in meters: it keeps this distance from walls, and doesn't go into a passage narrower than twice that. Character walking The typical character for whom the walkable areas are computed: its size, and the slope and step it can climb. Enemies and the other characters that move on their own (game.walk_to) follow these areas, and avoid each other on the way. Other sizes (a small animal, a big monster) each have their own areas. Once the scene is saved, these areas are computed and stored in the project: the game reads them back when it starts. To see them: View menu, Walkable areas. Characters avoid each other Characters that walk on their own (game.walk_to) see each other coming, along with the player and the other characters, and step aside in time instead of bumping into each other or getting stuck in a corridor. Choose the folder Chooses the folder of the NVIDIA files; WorldMint checks they are all there and signed by NVIDIA. Climate The kind of place and season: it sets the latitude, the date and the weather found there. Temperate, summer by default. Color grading Gives the whole image the tint of a look, like grading a film, through a color table: Soft realistic (the one of a new project), a filmic curve for depth, dense but open blacks, darkened corners, sharpening and a fine grain, no tint; Neutral changes nothing (a project made before the looks keeps it); Cinema, marked, with teal shadows and warm highlights; Realistic, a light film contrast; Stylized, bold colors; European city, soft and slightly cool tones; American city, a warm golden light; Seaside, bright with turquoise shadows. A look of the game can also follow a project .cube table (made in a photo or video editor), applied last; a damaged file is reported and ignored. Almost free, at every quality. If the game has a look cycle by the hour (ask the agent), it picks the look by the hour and this choice no longer applies. Corner shading (ambient occlusion) Darkens corners, the foot of walls, the underside of balconies and the inside of windows, where less sky reaches: 0 none, 1 (default) the quality's own, 2 twice as strong. Only the sky's light darkens, never the sun. With ray tracing, its rays look for what hides the sky (3 m around the point, times this setting); without it, it is worked out from what is seen on screen. The setting acts in both cases, on the reach and the strength; 0 turns both off. Off on Low quality. Darken up to How many times darker the image can get under a very strong light: 1 never (default: a sunny scene stays as you set it), 2 to 4 for a glare when walking out of a cave. Dawn, horizon The horizon at dawn, in the Stylized style. Dawn, upper sky The upper sky at dawn, in the Stylized style: the sky goes from the horizon to this color upward. Day of the year The date, from 1 (January 1st) to 366: it sets the season. 182 (early July) by default. Day, horizon The horizon in broad daylight, in the Stylized style; it is also the color of the distant haze. Day, upper sky The upper sky in broad daylight, in the Stylized style. It also tints the ambient light and the reflections. Depth of field Like a camera lens: sharp at the set distance, blurrier and blurrier in front and behind. For a cutscene, a portrait, a close-up view. Off on Low quality. Off by default. Distant detail What gets simplified in the distance so that large maps stay smooth: lighter versions of models, the objects of a district merged into one, distant plants as pictures, what is hidden left out, and the sorting of objects handed to the graphics card. It all happens by itself, for any model; these settings turn it off or adjust it. Distant haze The haze in the air: at 0, pure air where you can see hundreds of kilometers; toward 40, a milky distance. The blue of far mountains comes from the air itself; haze whitens it. 2 by default, an ordinary fine day. District distance From this distance to the camera, in meters, a 256 m square is drawn merged, fading over a short band. 600 m by default, in High quality: three quarters in Medium, half in Low (an integrated graphics chip). Download from NVIDIA Opens NVIDIA's page to download Streamline and DLSS. Draw calls How many times per frame the game asks the graphics card to draw a piece of an object, 95 times out of 100. 1,500 by default: beyond, the processor slows the frame down. Each player's range How far each player receives what happens around them, in meters: 250 by default. Beyond it, they do not see the other players, and what moved far from them is hidden until they come closer. What is near them arrives with every update, what is further a little less often. 0: everything, everywhere (a small map). In a big world, it does not go beyond the activity radius. Edit the terrain Selects the scene's Terrain object, to edit its relief, its regions and its sea. Exposure How much light reaches the image, as on a camera: 1 leaves the light as it is, higher brightens the image, lower darkens it (0.05 to 8). Very strong lights never turn abruptly white. With automatic exposure, it adds to what the eye chose: higher makes the whole game brighter. Film grain A light film grain over the image, moving all the time, mostly in the midtones: 0 (default) none, 0.2 to 0.4 subtle, 1 strong. Off on Low quality. Focus distance The distance from the camera, in metres, where the image is sharp (10 m by default). What is closer or farther blurs. Fog altitude The altitude, in meters, where the fog has the set thickness. With thinning, it is thicker below and lighter above. Fog color The color of what is in the fog, and of the sky behind it: light grey for a mist, bluish for the distance, dark for a night. Fog distance A fog over the whole scene: at this distance, in meters, it hides almost everything in its color. 0: none, only the soft horizon fade remains. A light mist: 300 to 800 m; a thick fog: 40 to 100 m. Folder of the NVIDIA files The folder where you put sl.interposer.dll, sl.common.dll, sl.dlss.dll and nvngx_dlss.dll: each must be there, signed by NVIDIA. FSR sharpness Sharpens the picture when AMD's FSR rebuilds it (the FSR upscaling method, or the FSR 2 native anti-aliasing): the fine detail that blending frames softens (leaves, lettering, railings) gets its sharpness back. From 0 (no sharpening, the default) to 1 (the strongest). No effect without FSR. If the color look has its own sharpness, FSR uses the stronger of the two: never two sharpenings on top of each other. Full light: sun height The sun's height at which lights set to « Switches on at night » are at full strength, in degrees: -6° by default (6° below the horizon, the end of dusk). Between the two heights, they fade in; in the morning, they fade out the same way. Fullscreen The game fills the whole screen, instead of a window. Game password The password players type to come in. Only its fingerprint is kept (the password cannot be found back from it), never the password itself. Without a password, everyone comes in. Game version The game's version number: digits and dots (1.0 by default). Change it each time you put the game online: 1.0, 1.0.1, 1.1…; players see it on the title screen, and other players see it if they don't have the same one. Empty: no version shown. Game window The window the game runs in: its title, its size, fullscreen. Glow of bright lights The soft glow around what shines very brightly: a material giving off light, the sun on water or metal, a lamp close by. 0: none; 1 by default, discreet. Grading strength How much of the color look is applied: 1 (default) all of it, 0.5 half, 0 none (like Neutral). Graphics card memory The graphics card memory of the target computer, in megabytes. 8,192 MB by default (8 GB, an RTX 4060 class card). Graphics card sorting The graphics card picks by itself the objects to draw, instead of the processor. The game can then show many more objects without slowing down, and the image stays the same. Automatic (the default) uses graphics card sorting on a dedicated graphics card, and keeps the old sorting, by the processor, on an integrated graphics chip. On asks for it wherever the card can do it, Off keeps the old sorting. A card that cannot do it always keeps the old sorting. Height of this size The height of the characters of this size, in meters: they walk under anything higher, and wade into water up to half this height. Hero mode Off (the default): each world has its own progress, kept in its save; in another world, you start from zero. On: progress follows the player from one world to another (like Valheim). It stays kept by whoever hosts the game, never on the guest's PC: it cannot be inflated offline. Hide players behind walls Against the cheat that shows through walls: the host does not send a player the other players, nor the moving non-player characters, that a wall hides from them, nor the effects that follow them (their sounds are still heard, without saying who makes them). They come back just before they could be seen, taking the network delay into account: they never pop up. Auto (the default): only when players can hurt each other (a module with "Players can hurt each other" ticked). Yes: always. No: never (a game among friends, or windows that stop objects but let you see through). High definition textures on demand In High quality, the photos of the city's materials (stone, plaster, brick, concrete) switch to 2K: WorldMint downloads them once from Poly Haven, in the background, into a folder shared by all your projects, and the image gets sharper when it is ready. Offline, in Medium or Low, the shipped 1K version stays, without error. Off by default: nothing is downloaded until you turn it on. The exported game carries the resolution the city uses. Highest step What a character steps over without a detour, in meters: a stair, a curb. Higher, it's an obstacle to walk around. Image exposure Makes the photo brighter or darker, in stops (+1: twice as bright). At 0 (the default), it is as bright as the realistic sky at this hour: its light goes down in the evening with the sun's. Image rotation Turns the photo around the vertical, in degrees, to put its clouds, mountains or sun where you want. Added to "Image sun at the hour". Image sun at the hour Turns the photo so its brightest point (its sun) is in the direction of the hour's sun: shadows fall on the same side as in the photo. Checked by default. In the public server list Ticked: the server shows in the List tab of the players' "Join" menu for this game, once the lobby service is in place. Unticked: it is joined by its address or its code. In-game day length How many real minutes 24 hours last in the game. 0: the time stands still. 0 by default. Keep this password Replaces the password with the one typed: only its fingerprint is saved. Large world For a map of several kilometers: the scene is saved in pieces of 256 m, in a folder next to its file (".tuiles"), and only the pieces that changed are rewritten. In the game, what is far from the player falls asleep (see "Activity radius"). The previous file is kept next to it; unticking puts the scene back in a single file. Latitude The distance from the equator, from -90° (South Pole) to 90° (North Pole): it sets how high the sun rises and how long days are. 48° by default. Light from the ground The color of the light bounced back by the ground, which lights the underside of objects. Lights on: sun height Lights set to « Switches on at night » (a street lamp, a shop window) start to switch on when the sun goes below this height, in degrees above the horizon: 2° by default, just before sunset. With the Day and night system, they also switch on as daylight fades. Lights the scene The photo also gives the ambient light and the reflections (metal, glass and water reflect its clouds and colors). Unchecked: the photo is only a background, the light stays the realistic sky's. Checked by default. Loading around the player In a large world, in the game: only the scenery near the player (and the camera showing the game) is loaded, in squares of 256 m. The rest is read in the background as you get closer, and freed as you move away: the game starts faster and takes less memory. What carries a tag or a system stays loaded everywhere. A script that looks for a scenery object by its name only finds it while it is loaded: give it a tag. On by default. Loading budget In a large world, in the game: the most time one frame gives, in milliseconds, to send the models of incoming scenery to the graphics card. Lower means fewer hitches; higher, distant scenery appears sooner. 4 ms by default. Loading margin In a large world, in the game: loaded scenery is only freed this much farther than the loading radius, in meters, so that a player going back and forth over a limit does not reload it over and over. 128 m by default. Loading radius In a large world, in the game: the scenery is loaded within this distance of the player, in meters. Never less than the activity radius plus 64 m. Beyond it, the scenery is drawn as simpler merged districts: a larger radius shows more detail, but takes more memory. The same on every computer. 600 m by default. Lobby service The service that gives players this game's public server list and short codes, helps them connect through their home routers and relays the game when needed. Empty: WorldMint's, shared by every game (each game sees only its own servers): enough for most games. Otherwise, the address of a lobby you host yourself (the kit is in the editor's outils\salon folder): https://lobby.my-game.com, or http://127.0.0.1:port for a test on this PC. The exported game and its dedicated server carry it. If it does not answer, joining a game by its address still works. Location Simple: a ready-made climate gives the latitude and the season. Advanced: you choose the latitude, the day of the year and the year. Simple by default. Log alert above When a player earns more than this XP in one minute, all sources together, a line is written to the server log (once a minute at most): enough to spot cheating or a badly tuned source. 0: never. Main memory The main memory of the target computer, in megabytes. 16,384 MB by default (16 GB). Main track The track whose level the other players see (above heads, in the Group panel) and that the admin commands use when no track is given. "personnage" by default: the name the "Progression" module gives to the character's level. Management web page Ticked: the server opens a web page to manage it from a browser on the same PC (http://127.0.0.1 and its port): state, players, log, backups, settings, message to all. It asks for its own password. Map north Where north is on the map: how many degrees it is turned east from the -Z axis. The sun rises in the east. 0° by default. Max catch-up After a slowdown, the most calculation steps the game catches up on in a single frame (1 to 100). Max physics bodies How many objects the game's physics can handle at once. It applies the next time the game starts. Merged districts In the distance, the fixed objects of a 256 m square (a block of houses, a farm) are drawn as a single simplified object, in the average color of each: this is what lets you see a city's skyline several kilometers away. Done in the background, and redone a few seconds after something changes there. The real objects come back as you get closer. Meshes kept on the graphics card The room taken, at the worst moment, by the scenery shapes (a city) kept on the graphics card, in megabytes. 1,200 MB by default. Most players on the server How many players the server takes at the same time, from 1 to 16. The server itself has no player: 16 means 16 friends. The next one is refused with "the game is full". Motion blur What moves fast in front of the camera blurs along its motion, like on film: 0 (default) none; 0.5 a cinema camera's shutter, good for a driving game (strong at high speed, nothing on what follows the camera: the player's car); 1 very strong. Off on Low quality. Multiplayer Playing with several players: one player hosts the game on their PC, the others join it by its address, and each has their own character. The game is played on the host's computer: the others see and hear what it sends them. Off by default: a single-player game doesn't change. Nearest visible distance Anything closer to the camera than this distance, in meters, isn't drawn. Network port The "door" number through which the other players join the game, on the PC hosting it (48600 by default). Change it only if another program already uses it. On the first start, Windows may ask to allow the game on the network. Night color The color of the sky's light at night (the moon scattered by the air, the city's glow): it lights what the lamps don't reach, facades in shadow, the road far from the streetlights, and colors the night sky. A night blue by default; lamps and windows keep their own color. Night darkness Cinema: a bluish night where you can still see well. Black: a real night, where only the moon and the lamps give light. Cinema by default. Night light The strength of the sky's light at night: 0, only the moon and the lamps give light; 1 by default; higher, a brighter night. Night darkness lowers it further. Night, horizon The horizon at night, in the Stylized style. Night, upper sky The upper sky at night, in the Stylized style: the stars show as small crosses. NVIDIA DLSS What NVIDIA's license asks before using DLSS, and the folder of its files. Objects always active In a large world: the objects carrying this system stay awake even far from the player (a messenger crossing the map). Keep it for few objects: what stays awake far away costs at every moment of the game. Objets toujours actifs dans la scène How many objects of this scene stay awake everywhere: those with "Always active", and those carrying a system ticked "Objects always active". In red beyond the advised number. Out-of-focus blur How much what is far from the sharp distance blurs: 0 none, 0.5 by default, 1 very blurry. Performance targets The computer the game is made for, and what one frame may cost on it. These are not limits: the agent estimates the cost of a large request before making it (a bigger city, denser districts) and, if it goes over these targets, adjusts what lightens the scene, then says what it changed and why. Picture distance How far plants are drawn as pictures, in meters from the camera. 1,500 m by default, in High quality: two thirds in Medium, a third in Low (an integrated graphics chip). Beyond, nothing; they don't go further than the detailed terrain around the camera. Place kept after a drop How many seconds a player whose connection drops keeps their place: their character stays there, still, with their bag and health. If they come back within that time (their game retries by itself), they carry on where they were, with no arrival or departure announced. Beyond it, they leave the game. 60 by default; 0: they leave at once. Plants as pictures Beyond their drawing distance, trees and bushes become pictures of themselves, taken from 64 angles and always facing the camera: a forest stays visible from afar for almost nothing. The change fades in. Play with several players Starts the game twice on this PC: one window hosts the game, the other joins it as a guest. You try the game from both sides this way, without exporting or typing an address. Stopping the game closes both. Players at most How many players in a game, the host included: 2 to 16. The host sends each player up to 128 kbit/s ("Bandwidth per player"): with 16 players, about 2 Mbit/s in all, it needs a good connection (fiber). One more player is refused with a clear message. Players can hurt each other Ticked: a player's hits hurt the other players (the Combat system, in every scene). Unticked: only enemies take hits. Players' characters How each player gets their character in a game with several players. One per world (the default): a player who has no character yet in this world creates it on their own PC before entering (the creation screen runs at their place, with no waiting), then the host checks their choices, applies them and keeps them in this world's save; when they come back, they get their character again without going through the creation. A character never moves from one world to another. Same look everywhere: the same, but the look they chose is kept on the player's PC and offered in advance in a new world; their progress (levels, bag) stays that of each world. Made in game: nothing before entering; the game does its creation during play, at the host's. Preview time The time shown in the editor, and the time a game starts at. Ctrl+click to type it in hours (19.5 for 7:30 pm). 2 pm by default. Progression What the engine itself keeps of the players' progress (experience, levels, points): hero mode, the main track, the XP multiplier and the safeguards against cheating. The tracks, their curves and their rewards are set in the "Progression" module. Publishing What you need to put the game online: its version number, and the .zip file the export writes next to the folder. Radius of this size Half the width of the characters of this size, in meters. A passage narrower than twice that isn't part of their walkable areas: a big monster doesn't go where a small one does. Raise the version Moves to the next version: the last number plus one (1.0.3 becomes 1.0.4). Do it before exporting an update. Rate How many steps the game computes each second: movement, physics. 60 by default. Rays in the air A slightly hazy air that shows the sun's rays even without fog: 0 none; 0.2 by default, mostly when looking toward the sun; 1 very strong, from the side too. In a room, add a little fog (dust) to see the rays from the windows. Read NVIDIA's license Opens the DLSS license on NVIDIA's site. Realistic sky (sun, moon, stars) On, the sky, the sun and the moon follow the location, the date and the time; the sky color, the sun color and its direction are no longer set by hand. Off by default. Remove the game password Removes the password: everyone can come in (except the banned, and those off the whitelist if there is one). Ctrl+Z puts it back. Remove the web page password Removes the web page's password: it then refuses every sign-in. Ctrl+Z puts it back. Scattering toward the sun How much brighter the fog and the air shine when looking toward the sun than with your back to it: 0 the same in every direction, 0.3 by default, 0.6 to 0.9 a strong glow around the sun and very bright rays against the light. Server The settings of the game's dedicated server: a program without a window that keeps the world open day and night, which friends join whenever they like. They make the serveur.json file of "Start a local server" and of the exported server (File, "Export game and its dedicated server..."). They are kept with the project; the game handed out to players does not carry them. Server admins The keys of the players who may type the server's commands in the chat (/kick Léa), separated by commas. A player's key shows with the "joueurs" command. An admin comes in even when not on the whitelist. Server description A few words about the server, for the list of public servers (512 bytes at most). Server name The name players see (64 characters at most). Left at "Mon serveur", the exported server takes the game's name. Server port The "door" number through which players join the server (48600 by default). It must be opened in the Windows firewall and in the router of the PC running the server; LISEZMOI.txt explains how. Server whitelist The keys of the only players let in, separated by commas. Empty: everyone comes in (with the password, if there is one). Server's start scene The scene where the server starts: the game's, or another one of the project. Arriving players join it there. A scene that no longer exists stops the server from starting, with a clear message. Set the game password... Opens a hidden line to type the players' new password (128 bytes at most). Enter or "Keep this password" replaces it; the typing is wiped at once. Set the web page password... Opens a hidden line to type the web page's password (128 bytes at most); the typing is wiped at once. Several players Ticked, the game can be hosted and joined. Each guest arrives with a copy of the player's character, near the starting point; scripts see them arrive ("joueur.arrivee") and leave ("joueur.depart"). The catalog's systems don't all handle several players yet: they take care of the host's player. Shadow distance How far, in meters around the camera, shadows are drawn. Beyond that, they fade out gently. Further away also makes them a little less sharp up close (5 to 2000 m, 150 by default). Shadow quality How fine the shadows are, from the sun and from lights (fires included). Depends on the computer: low on an integrated graphics chip (a laptop), high on a graphics card; the player can also choose it in the game menu. High: sharp all the way. Medium: a little less far, fewer lights with shadows. Low: blurrier up close, lighter to draw. Off: no shadows at all, the lightest. Shadow softness Softens the edge of the sun's shadows, like a real sun: sharp at the foot of an object, softer and softer further from it. It is the size of the sun in the sky, in degrees. 0: sharp; 0.5: the real sun; 2 to 4: a hazy sky; up to 10: very soft. A little costlier on a small computer. Share of lit windows At night, the share of the models' windows, curtains and lit interiors that glow, drawn at random object by object: 0.35 by default (a little over one in three). Signs and neons all light up. Short code Ticked: the lobby service gives the server an easy code to read out, like K7P-2QMX, while it runs; players type it in the Code tab of "Join", with no address. Unticked: no code. Signs and windows lit at night What glows in models (signs, neons, lamps, lit windows of imported buildings) follows the hour like lights set to « Switches on at night »: off by day, on at night. Off: always lit. A project material keeps the glow you set on it. Simplified models From afar, each model is drawn with fewer triangles: half, a quarter, then a tenth, computed once on first load and kept in the project. The version is chosen from the object's size on screen, and changes from one to the next with a fade, without a jump. Size name The name of another character size, the one you read (Small, Large). Each character takes the smallest size it fits in, from the radius and height its script gives it (game.character). Skip what is hidden What buildings hide is not drawn: their solid volumes (a generated city provides them) fill a small depth table each frame, and an object entirely behind them is left out. Nothing visible disappears, nothing shows up late when turning, and shadows stay. Fewer draw calls in a city (close to half fewer at the worst moment, measured). The quality sets its finesse: finer in Medium and High than in Low. Automatic (the default): on in Medium and High, not in Low (not yet measured on a small computer). On forces it at every quality, Off turns it off. The player can change it for themselves in the Menu system's options (Display): their On or Off comes before this choice. Sky The color of the light coming from the sky: it lights the top of objects, even where the sun doesn't reach. Sky and light The scene's lighting: the sun's light, the light coming from the sky and the ground, and the background color. Sky and weather The realistic sky: the sun, the moon and the stars in their place for the location, the date and the time, and the light that follows. Off by default: the scene keeps “Sky and light”. Sky image A photo of the whole sky (an equirectangular .hdr image of the project, for example a Poly Haven HDRI sky added from the online library) drawn as the background, instead of or on top of the realistic sky. The realistic sky's sun stays the direct light and the shadows. None by default. Sky style Realistic: the sky as we see it. Stylized: bold colors chosen for each time of day, for a drawn or low poly game. Realistic by default. Start a local server Starts the game's dedicated server on this PC, without a window (a world that goes on with no player), then a game window that joins it. Its settings come from the Server section (written to serveur.json at each start); its world is kept in the project's work folder, under serveur-local. Stopping the game closes both: the server saves its world before stopping. Steepest slope The steepest slope a character climbs, in degrees. Beyond it, the ground isn't a walkable area. Step of this size What the characters of this size step over without a detour, in meters. A big one often steps over more than a small one. Sun color The color of the sunlight. Sun direction Where the sunlight comes from, -1 to 1 on X, Y and Z: with Y positive, the sun is up high and lights the top of objects. Sun intensity The strength of the sunlight, from 0 (off) to 20. Sun shadows Objects, terrain and plants cast their shadow in the sun, on the ground, the water and each other. Untick for lighter rendering, without shadows. Sunset, horizon The horizon at sunset, in the Stylized style. Sunset, upper sky The upper sky at sunset, in the Stylized style. Synced with the screen The game's frames follow the screen's refresh rate: the image doesn't tear when it moves. Target frames per second How many frames per second the game should hold on the target computer. 60 by default. Target quality The rendering quality the targets are for: Medium by default, that of a mid-range graphics card. Technical settings What you almost never touch: how far you can see, the game's pace, the physics limits and the expected size of models. Terrain The scene's ground: its relief, its regions and its sea. Without a terrain, generate one here; with a terrain, its settings are on the Terrain object. Test the lobby Asks the chosen lobby service (or WorldMint's, when the field is empty) whether it answers, without blocking the editor: "The lobby answers" with the number of servers online, "No answer: check the address", or "This is not a WorldMint lobby" when something else answers at that address. The world sleeps with no player Ticked: when nobody is connected, the world stops (plants no longer grow, enemies no longer move) and the server takes almost nothing from the PC. Unticked: the world goes on. Thins out with height Above its altitude, the fog halves every so many meters: a valley fog, a mist over water or a swamp (5 to 30 m). 0: the same everywhere. Title The title of the game window, and the name of the exported game. Tolerated on-screen gap How far a simplified version may stray from the real model, in screen pixels, before a finer version takes over. 1 by default: the difference doesn't show. Larger, the game is lighter, and distant objects a little less faithful. Triangles in shadows The number of triangles drawn in the sun's shadows, 95 times out of 100. 3 million by default. Triangles in view The number of triangles drawn on screen the game should not exceed, 95 times out of 100 along the streets. 2 million by default. Turn DLSS on Turns DLSS on, once the box is checked and a valid folder chosen. Updates per second How many times per second the host sends each player where the players are and what moves: 20 by default. More is a little more precise and needs more connection; fewer, the opposite. The other players are shown a tenth of a second in the past, so they glide smoothly. Upscaling Draws the game's scene smaller, then enlarges it to the window's size by blending the frames that follow one another. Quality, Balanced, Performance and Ultra performance go from the sharpest to the fastest; "Anti-aliasing only" keeps the full size and only smooths the edges. Works on every graphics card. Off by default. Upscaling method What enlarges the game's picture when upscaling is on. None: WorldMint's own. FSR (all cards): AMD FSR, sharper, on every graphics card, already in WorldMint; with "Anti-aliasing only" it smooths edges without shrinking the picture. DLSS (NVIDIA): NVIDIA DLSS, on GeForce RTX cards; WorldMint doesn't provide it: choosing it shows you what NVIDIA's license asks (its logo when the game starts and in its credits, approved by NVIDIA), then asks for the folder of its files. Where the chosen method doesn't work, WorldMint's replaces it. The player can change it in the Menu (Display). View distance Beyond this distance, in meters, nothing is drawn; what gets close to it fades into the background color. Volumetric fog Sunlight shows in the air and in the fog, with the shadow of whatever hides it: rays of light between trees and through windows, a darker mist in the shade, a brighter one when looking toward the sun. The fog keeps its distance and color. Not on a small computer (Low quality): the usual fog. Off by default. Warning: huge model A model larger than this size, in meters, is flagged when it loads as having an unusual size. Warning: tiny model A model smaller than this size, in meters, is flagged when it loads as having an unusual size. Web page password The password of the management web page, different from the players' one. Without it, the page refuses to open. Only its fingerprint is kept. Web page port The port of the management web page (48680 by default), on this PC only. Welcome message Shown at the top of the screen to each player who arrives, for example the server's rules. Empty: none. Width The width of the game window, in pixels (64 to 16384). Wind direction Where the wind blows to, in degrees: 0 towards +x, 90 towards +z (like the direction of the waves). Plants lean and gusts travel that way. Wind strength The wind in the plants sown by the terrain, from 0 (dead calm) to 1 (strong wind): the base stays fixed, the top bends, and gusts sweep across the field in the wind's direction. Each plant kind follows it by its sway (grass a lot, a tree a little). Their shadows and far versions move with them. Off in Low quality. 0.3 by default: a breeze. World name The name of the world's save: lowercase letters, digits, _ or - (32 at most). Changing the name starts another world; the old one stays on the disk. XP cap per source and per minute A safeguard: a player earns no more than this XP in one minute from the same source (an enemy, a quest, a harvest). What goes over is lost. 0: no cap. XP multiplier All XP earned is multiplied by this number: ×2 for a double XP weekend, ×0.5 for a slower game. A dedicated server has its own on top (xp_multiplicateur in serveur.json, set on its web page). Year The year of the date, from 1900 to 2100: it places the moon and sets its phase. 2027 by default.

items.title: Materials
items.text:
Explained in detail: Materials.

Control What it does Back to the region colors Removes the ground materials, their rules and their painting: the terrain takes back the colors of its regions. Ctrl+Z to return. Cover with materials Gives each region a real material from the library (grass, rock, snow, sand, mud) and three rules: rock on slopes, snow at altitude, sand by the water. DirectX normal (Y flipped) The relief map comes from software that follows the DirectX convention (Unreal, 3ds Max, Substance in DirectX): its green is flipped. If the relief looks dug in instead of raised, change this setting. Emitted light The light the surface gives off by itself: its color, and its strength (0: none). For screens, lamps, lava. Eraser Erases the material painting: the ground takes back the one of its region and of the rules. Glow at night The glow goes out during the day and switches on at dusk, like "Switches on at night" lights: a sign, a street lamp head. Glow image Its colors: the emitted-light image glows with its own colors. Mask (red, green, blue or alpha): only that channel counts, tinted by the emitted-light color. Unreal vehicles store one group of lights per channel (brake, position, indicators). Ground material The material that covers this region, before the automatic rules and the painting. Ground materials The real materials of the terrain: the one of each region, the automatic rules (slope, altitude, water's edge) and what you paint with the Materials brush, which wins. Ground style The look of the ground, chosen for the game. Realistic: photo textures, blended from one material to the next. Stylized · Facets: for a low poly game, small flat facets, one bold color each, crisp transitions. Changing the style offers to match the water (and the lava) to the same style, in a single step. Keep the colour only Leaves the neighboring images aside: the material keeps only the color image. You can add them later in its settings. Material The material put on the object, instead of its model's colors: a file of the project, shared by every object that uses it. In a ground rule: the material it lays. Model materials In the Properties of an object made of a model: each part of the model (its slots: body, windows, lights...) gets a project material, or “The model's own”. The choice is written to “<model>.materials.json”, applies to every object of this model and ships with the exported game. Ctrl+Z undoes it. New material Creates a material of the project and puts it on the selected objects; set it just below, seeing it on the sphere. New rule Adds an automatic rule: a material on steep slopes, at altitude, or by the water. The last rule wins. Open the file Opens the shader file (.wmshader) in your text editor. Each time you save it, WorldMint checks it, recompiles it and shows the result in the view. Opening hours of the glow The glow only switches on between opening and closing, at the hour of the realistic sky: the sign of an open shop. A range can go past midnight (10 pm to 6 am); with "Glow at night", at night and within the range. Without the realistic sky, it stays on. Placement On the model: the image follows its texture coordinates. Without stretching: it is laid by the world, at the same size on every face, even on an enlarged shape. Reset the shader's settings Gives each shader setting back the value its code gives it, for this material. Shader A creator shader changes how the surface looks (a hologram, a dissolve, lava, a glowing rim, cartoon water) or moves its vertices (wind in the leaves). Choose a recipe (in code or in blocks): it is copied into the project's shaders folder. “New shader in blocks” starts one to build with connected blocks, without code. Its settings appear just below, as sliders. While its code is refused, objects keep the last version that worked, or their base material, and the message says on which line. Softness 0: the brush has a sharp edge. 1: a fade from the center to the edge. Transition The width of the transition from one material to the other, in degrees or meters; the edge waves so as not to draw a line. Use them Also adds the proposed neighboring images to the material (normal, roughness, occlusion, height), each in its place. Ctrl+Z to undo. Variation Slightly lighter or darker areas, and the pattern blended with a larger copy of itself: the repetition of the images no longer shows. 0 turns it off.

items.title: Object properties
items.text:
Explained in detail: The properties.

Control What it does Always active In a large world: this object stays awake even far from the player (a messenger crossing the map, a boss on patrol). Otherwise it falls asleep beyond the activity radius. It is the tag "toujours_actif", which a script can also add or remove during the game. Appearance For an object: whether it blocks the player, its color, and whether it shows in the game. In the preferences: the editor's language, theme and interface size. Apply to all copies The changes made to this copy go into the reusable object, and all its copies take them on. Arrival point The spot where the player appears, facing the arrow, when a passage or a script brings them into this scene. It can't be seen in the game. When created, it lands on the ground at the center of the view. Attach to the hand (keep its place) Attaches it to the character's hand bone, found by measuring its skeleton, without moving it: a weapon you placed by hand in the hand is held exactly so in game. Ctrl+Z detaches it. Attached to bone In the game, the object follows this bone as the character animates. Choosing a bone puts it there; then adjust it if needed, on the rest pose. A search filters the bone names; “None” lets it just follow the character. Camera A camera placed in the scene: it shows the game from where it stands, and can't be seen in it. When created, it takes the position and direction of the 3D view; its settings say what it looks at. Center The center of the selected objects, in meters. Changing it moves every object by the same amount. Collision The player and characters cannot pass through it: they bump into the object. With several objects selected, the switch applies to all of them. Color Tints the model or colors the shape: white changes nothing. For a terrain region or a body of water, the color of its ground or its water. Detach from the reusable object Turns it into an ordinary object: it keeps its current look, but no longer follows changes made to the other copies. Details What you rarely need: the object's real size, its model's triangle count, and the tags scripts use to find it. Dimensions The object's real size in meters, scale included: width (X) × height (Y) × depth (Z). Discard my changes This copy goes back to matching the reusable object: what you had changed on it is removed. Ctrl+Z brings it back. Field of view The camera's viewing angle, in degrees (up to 150): larger shows a wider view; smaller narrows the image, like zooming in. Held by the character This object sits inside an animated character: it can follow one of its bones, like a sword in the hand or a bag on the back. It's water This surface of the model becomes real WorldMint water, at its height and with its shape seen from above. Unticked, the added water is removed and the model's surface comes back. Kind of light Bulb: it lights all around it. Spotlight: it lights in a cone, toward the bottom of the object; turn the object to aim. Light A placed light: a bulb lighting all around it, or a spotlight lighting in a cone. Its color is the object's color. The Trigger and scripts switch it on, off or change its color. Thousands can be on at once: the closest to the camera light the scene (512 in Medium quality), the next ones show as a simple halo, a glowing point that costs almost nothing. Light intensity Its strength: the light received 1 m away, falling off with distance. 1 lights at 1 m like a sun of intensity 1. A torch: 2 to 5; a street lamp: 20 to 50. Light off at The hour the light switches off, 0 to 24. Before the opening hour, the range goes past midnight; equal to it, the light is always on. Light on at The hour the light switches on, 0 to 24, to the quarter hour (8.5: 8:30). Light range How far it lights, in meters: beyond, nothing. A room: 5 to 10 m. A short range costs little: many small lights are fine. Light temperature A ready-made tint, that of a real lamp: Sodium (2,000 K), the orange of street lamps; Warm white (3,000 K), a bulb; Neutral (4,000 K); Cold (5,500 K), a bluish light. It changes the object's Color (Appearance), which you can still set by hand. Light's shadows Objects lit by this light cast their shadow. Costlier: only a few lights at a time get them, the closest to the camera (a bulb counts as six spotlights). Keep them for the ones that matter. Look at “Straight ahead”: the camera looks along its rotation. Or an object in the scene: it keeps it in view and turns on its own. Look through this camera The 3D view moves to the camera's place and looks the way it does: you see what it will show in the game. Make this surface real water Proposed for a transparent, flat, horizontal surface whose name evokes water (a pool from a pack): replaces it with real water, in one click. Move to current view The camera takes the position and direction of the 3D view: frame the view first, then click. Multiply size by Grows or shrinks the whole selection around its center: 2 doubles its size, 0.5 halves it. The field then goes back to 1. No longer water The object stays where it is but is no longer water: it is no longer drawn as water and nobody swims in it. Nothing selected Click an object, in the 3D view or in the scene list, or drag a rectangle in the view: its settings show up here. Ctrl adds to the selection. On Off, the light no longer lights but stays in place: the Trigger or a script can switch it back on during the game. Opening hours of the light The light only switches on between the opening hour and the closing hour, at the hour of the realistic sky (World, Sky), which moves on during the game: the ceiling lights of an open shop. A range can go past midnight (10 pm to 6 am). With "Switches on at night", it is on at night and within the range. Without the realistic sky, the hour is unknown: it stays on. Opens the game The game starts on this camera, instead of the one following the player. Place on the bone Puts it back in the bone's place and orientation, on the character's rest pose. Then adjust it if needed. Position Where the object is in the world, in meters: X (red), Y (green, up) and Z (blue). Click to type a value, or drag to adjust it. Position and size Where the object is, how it is turned, and its size. The gizmo in the 3D view does the same with the mouse. Produced by an extension This object is produced by an extension (the city, for example) from its data, and rebuilt on every load. You can look at it and select it, but not change, move or delete it: change it with the extension's tool. Reusable object This object is a copy of a reusable object. If you changed it, you can pass those changes on to every copy, or go back to the original. Ripples The small wind ripples on the surface, from 0 (a mirror) to 1. They make the reflections and the light on the bottom ripple. Rotation Its orientation, in degrees around X, Y and Z. A horizontal half-turn reads “0, 180, 0”. Scale Its size along each axis: 1 is the original size, 2 doubles it, 0.5 halves it. Set as player Makes this model the character you play: it moves with the game's controls, and the player camera follows it. Its settings then come first in the properties. Shadow softness Softens the edge of its shadows: the size of what gives the light, in meters. Sharp at the foot of an object, softer and softer further from it. 0: sharp; 0.05: a bare bulb; 0.3: a lantern, a globe; up to 2. Shallow color The tint of the water where the bottom is close: the light turquoise of a pool. Where it is deep, the water takes the object's color. Spotlight opening The width of its cone, in degrees (1 to 170): narrow for a beam on a stage, wide for a ceiling lamp. Its edge is softened. Spotlight soft edge The part of the cone where the light fades out towards the edge, from 0 (a sharp edge, like a stage spot) to 1 (it fades from the center). 0.2 by default; a street lamp: 0.6 to 0.8, a wide soft pool, no sharp circle on the ground. Switches on at night The light follows the sun: off during the day, it fades in when the sun goes below the horizon, at dusk, and goes out in the morning. For a street lamp, a shop window, a window. The sun is set in World, Environment (its direction); with the realistic sky, it is the real sun at the hour of the sky. System Places a system already turned on in the Systems panel on what is selected. Placed on a folder, it applies to everything the folder holds. Systems Ready-made game rules: health, combat, enemies, passages between scenes… You turn them on for the game in the Systems panel, then place them on objects, each with its own settings. Tags Words scripts use to find the object (“enemy”, “coin”), separated by commas. Triangles The number of triangles in its model: the more there are, the more detailed the model, and the heavier it is to draw. Turn by Turns the whole selection around its center, by these degrees around X, Y and Z. The field then goes back to zero. Visible in game Unchecked, the object doesn't show in the game (a model that scripts copy, for example). It stays visible in the editor. Water clarity How far you can see through the water, in meters: 7 for a clear pool, 1 to 2 for a murky pond. Water depth How far the water goes below its surface, in meters (0.05 to 50). Lower down, you are no longer in the water. The tint follows the real bottom seen below. Water pool Real water placed by hand: a swimming pool, a basin, a fountain. It is drawn like lakes and the sea (tint by depth, ripples, reflections of the sky and surroundings, light patterns on the bottom in High quality) and counts as water in the game: you swim in it, what falls in floats, footsteps splash. Its surface is at the object's height; its scale handles stretch it into a rectangle. Add it with Add, Water pool. Water surfaces The flat, horizontal surfaces of an imported model, material by material. “It's water” replaces the surface with real WorldMint water, at its height and with its shape seen from above (a Water pool stored inside the model). A transparent surface whose name evokes water (water, pool, eau…) is proposed; the words are set in the scene environment.

items.title: Shader blocks
items.text:
Explained in detail: Shaders.

Control What it does Add a block Opens the list of blocks, sorted by family, with a search. The chosen block is placed in the middle of the graph. A right click on the background does the same, where you clicked; so does dropping a link in empty space, and the block arrives already connected. Hide the code Hides the code made by the blocks: the graph takes the whole width again. Open the blocks Opens this shader's blocks window, over the bottom of the view: you add, connect, move and delete blocks there, and the object changes at once above it. It closes when this material is no longer shown. Show the code Shows, next to the blocks, the code the blocks give, read-only: the one that is checked and compiled. To change it, change the blocks.

items.title: Systems
items.text:
Explained in detail: The game's systems and settings.

Control What it does Activate Adds this system to the game, along with the systems it needs. Then place it on objects, if it is a system that goes on objects. Actual size Puts the map back to its normal size, the easiest to read: move around it by dragging. Apply a WorldMint pack… Dresses the whole game with an interface pack in the WorldMint format (a folder with theme.json) found in the library: windows, buttons, tabs, slots, bars, titles, scroll bar and minimap ring, with the right edges, and colors taken from the images. You choose the pack and the ring color, and see what will be replaced before applying. Ctrl+Z goes back. Apply the pack Replaces the interface's image theme and colors with those of the chosen pack, in a single step: its images are copied into the project. Ctrl+Z goes back to the previous theme. Copy into the project Copies into the project the theme images taken from outside it (from a library folder), and the theme rows now cite them by their path in the project: the game, its export and another computer have them without that folder. Deactivate Removes this system from the game. If it is placed on objects or its scripts were changed, the editor asks you to confirm first. Not possible while another system needs it. Deactivate this system? The system leaves the game, and the objects carrying it lose their values. Ctrl+Z brings everything back. Enlarge the preview Opens the image theme preview at a large size, in its own editor window: the window, the buttons in their states, the bars, the slots and the tooltip can be read up close. It follows your settings while it is open; drag its corner to make it larger. Go back to the old version of the systems Puts the systems back in the version they had before they were updated when the game was opened: their scripts, their settings, their screens, and the systems the update had placed on objects. Everything else you did since is kept. Ctrl+Z redoes the update. Keep Gives up and closes the question: nothing is removed or deleted. Esc does the same. Population preview Shows, over the view, the pedestrians and cars the game would bring to life around the camera, in a translucent colour. Nothing is added to the scene or saved. It takes a moment to work out: it is only redone when you click. Remove the preview Removes the preview pedestrians and cars from the view. Show all Adjusts the zoom to see the whole map at once, in width and height. Show the map Opens these rows as a flowchart over the 3D view. A dialogue: Start at the top, one box per line, one diamond per test, a named arrow per answer or exit, an End at the end of each branch. Quests, one at a time: one box per step, one arrow per other way to end it or reason to fail, one diamond per test, an End or a Failure at the bottom, a label that leads nowhere in red; "All quests" shows them together, linked when one starts at the end of another. Both can be edited there: drag the circle at the start of an arrow onto a box to connect it, right-click to add a step or an arrow, or to remove one; everything goes through these rows, and Ctrl+Z undoes it. Drag to move it, Ctrl + wheel to zoom; a click brings you to the row here.

items.title: The agent
items.text:
Explained in detail: The agent.

Control What it does A capture of the 3D view Attaches a picture of what the active 3D view shows to the message, to show the agent what you see. A file from the computer… Attaches an image, a PDF or a text file chosen on the computer to the message. You can also drop it onto the agent panel. Account The agent in use (Claude or Codex) and the account it is connected with. You can change the connection here, or sign out. Agent rules The method the agent follows: a plan, a playable game at every step, and proof. You can customize it for this project, in an AGENT.md file. Allow the agent Opens the editor to an agent started from the terminal. Turned off, the access closes and the current conversation stops. Another agent Lets another agent, started from your terminal, connect to the editor. It keeps its own tools: only do this if you trust it. Back Leaves the settings and goes back to the agent panel. Cancel Gives up what is in progress and goes back, without changing anything. Change connection Goes back to the sign-in choices (subscription, API key...) to connect the agent another way. Check again Looks for the agent's program on the computer again, for example after you installed it yourself. Confirm sign out Really signs the agent out, or forgets its connection. Careful: depending on the agent, signing out applies to the whole computer, not only the editor. Continue without updating Connects the agent with the version already installed. Models that need a newer version will refuse to answer: the panel will offer the update again. Copy the command Copies the command to paste in your terminal to connect the other agent. It contains an access key: don't share it. First steps The first steps to start a scene: drag a model from the library, click an object to open its settings, then describe to the agent what you want to build. Install Runs the official installer of the agent's program, which links the editor to your account. The panel updates when the installation is over. Model The AI model that answers. By default, the one your agent picks. The change applies from the next message. Program Where the agent's program is on the computer. Left empty, the editor finds it by itself. Reasoning effort How much the agent thinks before acting: the higher, the more it thinks, and the slower it is. The change applies from the next message. See the installation page Opens in your browser the page that explains how to install this program. Technical details Shows or hides the exact text of the problem and what the update wrote, for example to copy it into a help request. The copied image Attaches the copied image to the message, for example a screenshot (Ctrl+V in the message box). Greyed out when no image is copied. Try again After an error, checks the agent's connection again. Undo these changes Undoes in one go everything the agent changed in the scene during its last answer. Its changes can also be undone one by one with Ctrl+Z. Update Updates the agent's program without closing the editor (for Claude, this is “claude update”), checks the new version, then reconnects the agent. Use it when a model needs a newer version. Use another agent Opens the agent settings, to choose another agent (Claude or Codex) or set its program. Use this key Connects the agent with the API key pasted just above (Enter does the same). The key stays hidden on screen and is never written to the logs.

items.title: The city
items.text:
Explained in detail: Cities and roads.

Control What it does A model from the library… Replaces the building with a model of the project (a .glb, .gltf or .fbx from the library): a landmark, placed in the middle of the parcel, its +z side facing the street. Access frontage (min) Below this width on the street, a parcel has no access. Access step (max) The largest height difference between the sidewalk and the ground of a parcel that keeps its access. Add a kind Adds a kind of shop: a known kind, or a free name. Add a lane Adds a lane to the profile, like the last one. Add a material Adds to the style a wall material taken from another style of the city. Add a node to this piece Another node of the same file, laid with this one at its place in the file: the window of a pierced wall stored apart. Add a point on this side Adds a point on this side of the district: then drag it to follow a street. Add street lamps… Choose a folder of models (FBX, GLB, OBJ, with their textures, the emissive map included) or a folder that has its lampadaires.json. It is copied into the project (lampadaires/<its name>); each model is measured and its bulbs are found from its emissive map (otherwise under its arms). A file that holds several street lamps (a single-arm one, a double-arm one) is split: one lamp per object; its images are found by their name in its subfolders. A lamp with two opposite arms goes on the medians, a single-arm one along the sidewalks. Ctrl+Z removes the lamps from the catalogue; the copied files stay. All-red time The short time when all the lights of the junction are red between two groups, in seconds (1 to 2 s): the junction clears before the next green. Allowed stretch How much a model without plain wall around its opening may stretch or shrink to fill its cell. A model with plain wall only stretches that wall (in nine cells). American The marking of American streets (MUTCD): a yellow centre line, white broken lines, triangles at give-way lines. An arterial road every N streets One street in how many, each way of the grid, becomes an arterial road; 0: none. Another draw Cuts the parcels of this district another way, with the same style: try until you like it. Arrow length The length of a road arrow, in metres (5 m in town). It stays within the width of its lane. Arrow setback The distance between the stop line and the tip of the first arrow, in metres. As the district says The state of the street is drawn from the style of its district, otherwise from its profile. Back gap The room left between the extended building and the back of the parcel. 0: against the back. Against the back, its wall has no window; with a gap, it keeps some, following the facing distances. Back side The fence at the back of the parcel, opposite the street. Shared with the neighbour: the one chosen here wins. Back to the city's ground Removes the added slabs and changed materials of the parcel: the slab the city lays there comes back. One step, Ctrl+Z undoes it. Back to the district's Removes the material and the tint chosen for this part of the street: it takes those of its district again, or of its profile outside any district. Ctrl+Z brings it back. Back to the generation Removes the change of this parcel: it goes back to what the generation makes (the use and style of its district). Back to the style values Removes this district's zone from the Population system: it takes back the values of its style, at its density. Band The band this piece ends (an end) or turns at a salient corner (a corner): base, string course, cornice. Barrier None, a guardrail (steel, low, along roads) or a railing (higher, at the edge of a drop). Barrier placement On both sides of the road; only where the ground drops at the edge of the road; or Automatic: only where a car can leave the road, along a high embankment and on the outside of a bend too tight for the design speed. Automatic places nothing along a street with sidewalks, in a junction or in front of a district. Bays The number of bays the model takes in width (a garage door over two bays). Blind wall when facing A wall that is not on the street and faces another building closer than this distance has no window there. 0: never. Street fronts do not change. Block plan The ground of each block drawn from its plan: one continuous slope from one street to the next. Block size (max) The largest distance from one street to the next when the city is generated. Block size (min) The smallest distance from one street to the next when the city is generated. Bridge deck The deck of this profile's bridges: flat, or slightly arched (it rises in the middle by a small share of its span, 2 % by default). Bridge railings The railings of this profile's bridges: with bars (a rail and posts on a low wall), solid (a parapet) or none (the deck edge only). Bridge shape The bridge shape of this street only: a flat or slightly arched deck, square or round piers and their spacing, railings with bars, solid or none. "Celle du profil" gives it back to the profile. Its materials (deck, piers, railings) are in "Matières de cette rue…". Broken yellow One broken yellow line in the middle, double solid before junctions. Build This parcel will be built on, even if the built share of its style would have left it open. A parcel without access cannot be. Build to the back of parcels With court buildings: when the back left behind the street building is too small for a courtyard and a court building, the street building reaches the back of the parcel instead of leaving an empty strip. Its walls on the limit, with no neighbour, have no window. Not on corner parcels. Building The building selected with a click in the view, in Buildings mode: its parcel (street, side, frontage, depth, slope) and what can be changed on it. Each change is an adjustment of its parcel, kept when the city is rebuilt; Ctrl+Z undoes it. Buildings What the buildings of this style will have: floors, heights, setbacks, roofs. Built depth (max) Beyond it, the back of the parcel stays a yard, or gets a court building if the style has them. Built share The share of parcels that carry a building; the others stay open (yard, garden, parking). Bulb radius The radius of the roadway of the turnaround bulb, in metres (13 m by default; 12 to 15 m in the United States). The sidewalk is added around it. By junction Wide bars at junctions with traffic lights, two lines elsewhere. By the water The generation places this district by the water when there is some (a harbour). Carrefour fondu Merged junction: two junctions too close to each other, joined into one. The plan keeps its nodes, but the roadway, the terrain and the plots make a single junction of them, halfway between them: a single handle, at that spot. Dragging it moves the joined junctions together; a right click makes it a roundabout. Ctrl+Z undoes. Centrality Where the generation places this district: 0 at the edge of the city, 100 % in the centre. Change the goods… Picks what this piece of furniture shows: tick the goods shipped with WorldMint (breads, pastries, pharmacy boxes…) or add one of your models; they are set at their real size on its shelves or in its baskets. "Those of the kind" goes back to the recipe. Below it, "Colours": the palette of its goods (a garment, a cloth); each product placed takes one, only the fabric is dyed (the wood of a hanger keeps its own, the folds stay); "+" adds a colour, a click on a swatch changes it, "-" removes the last one. Kept when the city regenerates. Change the model… The model of this landmark, chosen among those of the project; « Nothing: I build it myself » leaves the parcel empty for your objects. Character The character who keeps this shop in the game: an object of your project with a model, usually hidden. It is copied behind the counter when the player comes near, facing the room, with its idle clip; used (E), it opens the shop's Shop window. "None": no clerk. The choice is for the kind, or for this shop alone with "For this shop only". Chercher en ligne The words to search, in English as the sources name them (“brick”, “asphalt”, “paving”); the word of the part is suggested. The search runs on this computer. Choose online… Opens a small window of the online library, on the sources already chosen (the asset browser's “Online” folder, Sources button): search a realistic texture (“brick”, “asphalt”, “paving”…), see its licence and real size, then click: it is downloaded into the project as a material, at its real size, and put here.
