Ctrl+Z removes it. City surface Being built: the terrain written from the single surface of the city, under every laid ground. Colour on the plan The colour of this style on the plan view and the game map. Continental Wide white bars along the street, across the whole roadway. Continue… The drawn area goes to the generation window: its name, its mood, its seed and its districts. Enter does the same. Corner building What the style builds at a block corner, on its two corner parcels. Two wings: one L-shaped building, a wing on each street (the dense city). Against the corner: a building set in the corner, a facade with windows on each street, and the other parcel's building behind it; if both do not fit, the corner stays built and the other parcel becomes a garden. Along its own street: each corner parcel keeps its building, aligned on its own street only; when both do not fit together, the corner stays open. None: nothing special at the corner. Corner shape The corner shape of a two-wing corner building: sharp (the two wings meet in an edge), cut corner (a face cuts the corner) or rounded (a curved facade). In a style, the share of each shape, in %, drawn building by building; in the panel of a building, the shape of that building, in one step (Ctrl+Z undoes it). Corner use The use of the corner ground floor of a two-wing corner building: shop, café, hotel, housing, pharmacy, bank or bakery. It chooses the shop fronts, the sign, the blind or the terrace of the corner face. In the panel of a building, the use of that building, in one step (Ctrl+Z undoes it); Back to the generation gives back the one the style draws. In a style, the share of each use, in %, drawn building by building; the shares always add up to 100%: changing one adjusts the others. Court buildings Fills the middle of the blocks: on a deep parcel (not on a corner), a second, lower building stands at the back, aligned on the street building, behind a courtyard. Its walls face the courtyard, with no shop front. Cracked The cracked state (never for markings). In the materials of a profile, the box allows it and the number gives its weight in the draw; in a style, its share (in %) for the streets of the district; in Upkeep, it is forced on the street. Crossing setback The distance between the edge of the junction and the pedestrian crossing, in metres, at every junction of three streets or more. Crossing width The width of the pedestrian crossing along the street, in metres: the length of its stripes. At least 2.5 m in town. Crosswalk style The shape of the crosswalks. By junction: bars (continental) at junctions with traffic lights, two lines elsewhere. Continental: wide bars along the street. Two lines: two white lines across the street. Curb block length The length of a curb block, in metres (about 1 m): a thin joint separates two blocks. 0: a curb in one piece. Curb chamfer The curb edge on the roadway side, cut at an angle over a few centimetres (like a machined curb); 0: a sharp edge. Curb height The height of the curb between the roadway and the sidewalk, in metres. Curb joint The joint between the curb and the sidewalk: a thin strip (1 to 1.5 cm), slightly recessed, along the whole length; 0: no joint. Curb joint color The color of the joint between the curb and the sidewalk (charcoal gray by default). Curb top width The curb is a row of blocks (granite or concrete) that holds the sidewalk. Here, the width of their top, in metres (15 to 30 cm in towns): the sidewalk starts behind it. 0: the sidewalk goes to the edge, with no separate block. Cutting depth (max) The deepest cutting the road digs below the ground, in metres. Beyond it, the road follows the hill (its slope may then exceed the maximum slope: it is reported as too steep), and it does not become a bridge that would go through the hill. Dash length The length of each dash of the give-way line, in metres (0.5 m in France). Dead end The shape of the end of a dead end of this profile. Turnaround bulb (default): the roadway widens into a circle at the end, and the sidewalk and its curb go all around it, like an American cul-de-sac. Straight sidewalk: the sidewalk closes the end in a straight line, with its curb. A bulb without enough room (another street too close, a dead end too short) becomes a straight sidewalk. Delete the change Deletes this change that no longer holds: the parcel goes back to what the generation makes. Ctrl+Z brings it back. Delete the district Removes this district from the plan. Ctrl+Z puts it back. Delete the profile Removes the open profile from the plan. Refused while a street uses it: give that street another profile first. Delete the street Removes this street from the plan, with the nodes no longer used. The roadway disappears, the ground comes back as it was. Ctrl+Z puts it back. Delete the style Removes this style from the city. Refused while a district uses it: give that district another style first. Densité des quartiers The density of every district of the new city: higher gives smaller blocks and tighter buildings; lower gives large plots. You can then set it district by district, in Districts mode. Depth (max) The largest depth of a parcel, from the edge of the sidewalk. Depth (min) The smallest depth of a parcel, from the edge of the sidewalk (less if the block is too narrow). Describe the kit… Opens the panel that describes the kit: the role of each model of the folder, which way its front faces, where its materials go. It writes the kit.json file of the folder. Design speed The speed the road is shaped for along its length, in km/h: at this speed, a car does not take off at the top of a rise nor bottom out at the foot of a dip. The higher it is, the longer and gentler the rises and dips (the road cuts and fills more, within the cutting and embankment limits). 0: the road follows the ground, like a path. Direction The quarter turn of the landmark, in degrees; « Turn by 90° » adds a quarter turn. District density Within the district style, from 0 to 100 %: higher gives smaller blocks, narrower parcels, more, deeper and taller buildings; lower gives large plots and gardens. 50 %: the style as it is set. District population How many people live in this district: pedestrians on the pavements, moving cars, parking spaces taken. By default, the values of its style at its density; dragging a slider sets them for this district only, in the Population system (a zone with its name). District style Changes the style of this district: its parcels and future buildings follow. Ctrl+Z goes back to the previous style. District styles The styles of this city, each with its colour and an outline of its buildings. Click a style to adjust it: all its districts follow. Districts The districts of this city: their colour, name, style and area. A click selects a district. Ditch depth The depth of the ditch in its middle, in metres. Ditch width A ditch on each side, beyond the shoulder, dug into the ground; 0 without a ditch. Double line gap The space between the two yellow lines of a double line, in metres (0.1 m, about 4 in). Double solid yellow Two solid yellow lines in the middle: never crossed. Draw a slab Adds a ground: drag a rectangle in a parcel, it snaps to the edges of the other slabs and of the parcel. It replaces the ground underneath, at the same level, with a single joint between them (half concrete, half asphalt…). Esc stops the drawing. Draw streets Picks the City tool: then click on the ground to place the points of a street, Enter or a double-click ends it. Drawn tint Gives the wall back the tint the generation gives it (one of the variants of the block), instead of the one chosen by hand. Dropped curb height A dropped curb is a lowered curb in front of a driveway or a parking entrance. Here, the height of the curb above the roadway on a dropped curb, in metres (2 to 3 cm). Dropped curb ramp The length of the gentle slope at each end of a dropped curb, in metres; the sidewalk edge slopes down over the same length. Embankment height (max) The highest embankment the road builds above the ground, in metres. Beyond it, the road follows the hollow (its slope may then exceed the maximum slope: it is reported as too steep). European The European marking: white lines, dashes at give-way lines, striped crossings. Facade The facade recipe: the windows, doors, balconies and their rhythm. The list shows those of the content. Facade distance Up to this distance from the camera, in metres, each block shows its full facades; beyond, a light box of the same shape: the walls with their real material and tint, a plate for anything standing out more than 50 cm (balconies, awnings, landings), and the same windows, lit the same at night. The two fade into each other by dithering, without a jump. 160 m by default; Medium quality multiplies it by 0.75 (120 m), Low by 0.5 (80 m). 0: full facades everywhere, no box (slower in a big city). From 30 to 2,000 m. Facade kit The facade modules of the style: « Made modules » (WorldMint's own), or a folder of models of the project. Facades The facade materials of this style, by use (brick, render, stone, tiles…): made, or a project material chosen online; and the grime decal. Faded The faded state, for markings only: the paint has gaps. The box allows it and the number gives its weight in the draw. Few windows when facing Closer than this distance (but beyond the blind wall), a wall facing another building keeps one small window in two or three, never opposite the neighbour's. Fewer floors on the court How many fewer floors the court building has than the street building. 0: as many. Fit to the parcel Scales the model so that it fits in the parcel. Flat roofs (weight) The place of flat roofs among the roofs of this style: the larger the weight, the more there are. Flattening How much of the ground under the way is flattened: 100 % like a street, less for a path that follows the ground. Floor height The height of one floor, in metres. Floors The number of floors the model takes in height (a glass roof over two floors). Floors (max) The largest number of floors above the ground floor. Floors (min) The smallest number of floors above the ground floor. Former ground Paved grounds draped on the relief, joined afterwards (the former model). Front The side of the model that faces the street. Each button shows the model turned as it would be placed: choose the one that shows its front. Furnish from the online library Takes the common furniture of this kind of shop (shelves, till, round tables, chairs, plants, lamps) from Poly Haven (CC0), adds it to the project with its licence and places it in all its shops, at its real size. The gondolas, the fridges and the counter stay made. The floor and the lower walls take real Poly Haven textures (parquet, tiles, wood panels, wall tiles) at their real scale. Poly Haven must be on in the online library. Furniture The furniture of the room, one by one ("rayon#3": its role and rank). "Hide" takes it out (nothing takes its place, and one walks where it was); "Replace with…" places one of your models instead, at its real size. Its front is guessed from its hollows: a counter shows customers its solid side, a shelf or a fridge its open side; if it is wrong, ask the agent to set "front" (+z, -z, +x or -x) on the line of the recipe. "Change the goods…" picks what a piece shows (the goods shipped with WorldMint or your models), "No goods" empties it. Kept when the city regenerates. Furniture height The height of the placed furniture, in metres: the model is scaled to it. 0: the measured size of the model. A pack model is often not to scale: fire hydrant 0.8 m, bin 1 m, bench 0.85 m, pole 9 m. Furniture model The path of a project model (for example modeles/hydrant.glb), placed instead of the made furniture: it is measured, its foot set on the sidewalk, scaled to the furniture height, its longest side along the street. Empty (or unreadable): the furniture made by WorldMint. Confirm with Enter. Furniture per 100 m The number of benches, bins and the like per 100 m of sidewalk. Furniture setback The distance between the furniture and the curb (or the foot of the facades, for trash bags), in metres. The furniture always stays on the sidewalk. Furniture spacing The distance between two spots of this furniture along a sidewalk, in metres. For bins, benches, newspaper boxes and bags, it also follows the district density (Furniture per 100 m). Gap between arrows The distance between the tips of the two arrows of a lane, in metres. Gap between dashes The space between two dashes of the give-way line, in metres (0.5 m in France). Gap between stripes The space between two stripes of the pedestrian crossing, and between the last stripe and the curb, in metres (0.5 m in Europe). Gap between triangles The space between two give-way triangles, in metres (0.2 m). Generate Builds the city in the background (“Generating the city…” in the status line), then places it in one step that Ctrl+Z removes. Generation settings The generation settings of the whole city of this plan, which depend neither on a district nor on a street. Give way The side street gives way: a dashed line across its lanes, and the triangular sign. Go back to the made material Removes the project material of this use: the made material comes back. Graine de la ville The same number gives the same city again; another number gives another one. Grime decal Prepared: a project image with transparency (an ambientCG “Leaking” decal, for instance) that facade placement will use later: real decals are planned. The computed facade grime has been removed: this setting is kept, but has no effect for now. Empty: no grime. Grip in bends The tyre grip allowed in a bend without braking (15%: the usual road value). With the design speed, it gives the safe radius of a bend: V² / (127 × (banking + grip)). A tighter bend gets a guardrail on its outside. Lower: more guardrails. Ground The chosen slab: a flat ground under and around the buildings, at least as high as the sidewalk, a joint all around. Its material and height are changed here; the change stays when the city is regenerated. Ground drop The barrier is placed where the original ground, at the edge, is lower than the road by more than this many metres (an embankment). Ground floor height The height of the ground floor, often taller than the other floors (shops). Ground in front of the buildings The ground of a built parcel between the pavement and the facade, and on its sides: grass (a garden) or a street material (slabs, setts, concrete…). Paved, it extends the pavement, into the gaps between the buildings. Ground left free The ground of the parcels without a building and of the rest of the blocks (their middles, their unbuilt corners). "Like the forecourt or courtyard": the material of the ground in front of the buildings, or that of the courtyards if it is grass; "Car park": asphalt; "Grass": the terrain as it is. The planted share keeps part of it in grass. Paved, it follows the relief, at the height of the pavement, and can be walked on. Ground level The height of the model set at the sidewalk level. « Measured »: the largest flat surface near the bottom of the model (a car park, a lawn, the ground floor), so that a pool or a basement goes below the street instead of lifting the model; within half a metre of the bottom (a plinth, a walkway), the bottom of the model stays at the sidewalk. « Set by hand »: a height in metres above the bottom of the model. Ground model How the city lays its ground and the terrain under it. Former ground (the default): paved grounds draped on the relief, joined afterwards. Block plan: the ground of each block drawn from its plan, in one piece. City surface (being built): the terrain is written from a single surface of the city, always under every laid ground (road, sidewalk, junction, block ground), the grass slightly under that surface; the block grounds are still those of the plan. Ground of the courtyards The ground behind the buildings, in the courtyards: grass (a garden) or a street material. No plant grows on a paved ground. Ground of the parcels without access The ground of a parcel too far below or above its pavement to be entered (a step higher than the allowed step), never built: a bank, the terrain as it is, its slope continuous, with no step and no wall. "Grass" by default, as a slope too steep to build on stays green in a real town; "Like the ground left free": the material and planted share of the ground left free; "Car park": asphalt; or a street material. Guardrail model… A model of the project, repeated along the road at its measured length (stretched by 10% at most to fit), instead of the made guardrail. Gutter width The gutter: a strip of setts or slabs at the foot of the curb, at the level of the roadway, where water runs off (25 to 50 cm). It is taken from the roadway; 0: no gutter. Its material is set like the others, under "Gutter". Height (floors) The number of floors above the ground floor; the height in metres is next to it. The arrows add or remove a floor; a typed number is applied with Enter. Intended dead end A way of this profile can end without joining anything (an alley, a footpath): the check does not report it. Interior The furniture of a visitable shop: that of the interior recipe of its kind (counter, till, shelves, fridges, tables, chairs…), laid out by zones with a free aisle from the door to the back and to the till; or an empty room if the kind has no recipe. The recipe is changed with the agent. Interior depth The depth of the room of a visitable shop, at most, in metres from its window. It always stops before the back of the building. Interior range Up to this distance from the camera, in metres, you see the real room of a visitable shop through its window, with its furniture and goods, lit by its ceiling lights, and you can walk in; farther, the window shows a painted fake shop. The room is only loaded on the graphics card near the shop (this distance plus the loading margin), with no loading screen: far from the doors, interiors cost nothing. 0: always loaded and drawn. Medium and Low shorten it like the facade distance. Lower it if the city is heavy. Junction without lights What this street does where it meets a wider street without lights: it gives way (a dashed line and the triangular sign, the most common in France) or it stops (a solid line and the stop sign). The wider street keeps the right of way; a junction of equal streets keeps its stop signs. Kind's hours The opening and closing of the shops of this kind, in hours of the day (22 then 6: open at night). The same hour twice: open day and night. Closed, the sign, the window and the room go dark; the hour is the sky's (Day and night in Play), nothing is rebuilt as it passes. Kind's shop window The fake shop of every shop of this kind in the city (except those that chose their own). Changes the city's catalogue, not the shipped file. Kind's shutter Ticked: after hours, the shops of this kind lower their metal shutter in front of the window; unticked, the window stays dark. A shop keeps its own "Shutter down after hours" box if it was changed. Kit materials Each material read in the models, and the place it takes: wall, glass, frame, door, metal or trim. A material not chosen is a trim. Lane line dashes The length of each white dash between two lanes going the same way, and of the yellow dashes of a broken line, in metres (3 m, 10 ft). Largeur de la voie The width of this lane, in metres (3.25 m for a common road). Leaf For a door made of two models: the leaf, another model of the folder, placed in the frame. Leave open (yard, garden, parking) This parcel will not be built on: a yard, a garden or a parking lot. The change is kept when the city is rebuilt. Ctrl+Z removes it. Left side The fence on the left boundary of the parcel, seen from the street. Shared with the neighbour: the one chosen here wins. Letter height The height of the letters of the word ONLY, along the street, in metres (2.4 m, 8 ft: long letters to be read while driving). Light amber time How many seconds the lights stay amber after green (3 to 4 s in the US). Light green time How many seconds the lights stay green, for each group of opposite arms of a junction where this street is the widest (25 to 30 s in US towns). Lights cycle in the game and in the editor; every junction has its own offset. Line between the two directions The yellow line between the two directions. Double solid: never crossed (main streets). Broken: passing allowed; it becomes double solid before junctions (small streets). None: nothing in the middle. Make the game map Makes the image of the city plan seen from above (cartes/plan_ville.png in the project, without text) and gives it to the Map system as its drawn map, with the area it covers: the game minimap shows the city. Ctrl+Z brings back the previous map. Without the Map system, the image is only written. Marge de pente des rues A short street between two junctions too far apart in height cannot keep its profile's grade: generation removes it, without digging into the hill. This margin is how far the grade it would need may exceed its profile's maximum grade before it goes (50%: one and a half times). A street that is only steep stays, and a street that part of the city depends on is never removed. Margin before and after a bend The guardrail of a bend that is too tight starts this many metres before it and ends this many metres after it. Marking standard The marking usage. In the generation settings, the standard of the whole city: every profile that follows “The city's” (the default) takes it, roundabouts included. In a profile, it can be forced for its own streets. American (the MUTCD, the default): a yellow line between the two directions, white broken lines between lanes going the same way, triangles at give-way lines and at roundabout entries, a yellow line along the island of a roundabout and arrows at its two-lane entries, the arrows and the word ONLY of American streets. European: the European usage (white lines, dashes at give-way lines). Material The material of this part of the way: one made by the editor (asphalt, cobbles, gravel…), or a material of your project that replaces it. Materials of this street… Opens the materials of this street only: for the roadway, the sidewalk, the curb, the gutter, the shoulder and the markings, a made material or a project material, and a tint. They come before those of the district and the profile. Each change is undone with Ctrl+Z. Maximum ground slope With the « plan » ground model, the ground of a block is one continuous slope, gentle and even from one street to the next, without walls or steps (only the soil sits a few centimetres below the sidewalk). Beyond this slope, under a building, the building is set into the slope: it keeps its level and its plinth goes down to the lowest point of the ground, higher on one side than on the other; below it, a simple footing. 8% by default. From 1 to 50%. Maximum projection For a band: how far it stands out in front of the wall at most. A deeper model is flattened against the wall when laid, its shape kept. « By role »: 5 cm for a base, no limit for a string course or a cornice. Measured The ground level measured on the model: the largest flat surface near its bottom. Median The width of the median between the two directions, in metres; 0 without a median. Minimum courtyard The narrowest courtyard between the street building and the court building. A shallower parcel has no court building. Under 4 m, the walls facing each other have no window. Mode de l'outil Ville Streets: draw and change the streets. Districts: draw areas on the ground and give them a style (old town, houses…). Moving cars How many cars drive on 1 km of lane in this district, at the busiest hour. Name drawn by the city Gives the shop back the name the city draws for its kind, instead of the one chosen by hand. New The new state. In the materials of a profile, the box allows it and the number gives its weight in the draw; in a style, its share (in %) for the streets of the district; in Upkeep, it is forced on the street. New profile Copies the open profile under a new name: adjust the copy without touching the streets that keep the original. Ctrl+Z removes it. New style Creates a style from this one, under a new name: adjust it without changing the other districts. New town… Adds a named town next to the others: draw its area on the terrain (a dragged rectangle, resized by its corners and rotated by its circle, or an outline point by point to follow a coast). The drawing snaps to the edge of a neighbouring town; it turns red if it overlaps it. No goods Empties this piece of furniture: it stays in place with nothing on it (no goods, no boxes). No line Nothing painted between the two directions (a quiet small street). Nodes The nodes of the file that make up this piece, laid together: for example a wall with an opening and its window. The first one gives the frame. Nom de la rue The new name of the street. Enter keeps it. Nom du profil The new name of the profile. Enter keeps it. Nom du quartier The new name of the district. Enter keeps it. Nom du style The new name of the style. Enter keeps it. Nombre de parcelles The parcels of the city, cut along the streets by the style of each district: how many are built, left open (yards, gardens, parking lots) or without access (red on the plan). Nothing: I build it myself The parcel becomes an empty landmark: the generator no longer places anything there, its name shows above it in the view. One floor higher Adds a floor to this building, in one step (Ctrl+Z undoes it). One floor lower Removes a floor from this building, in one step (Ctrl+Z undoes it). Other kind… The kinds of the shop catalogue that the style does not draw (pharmacy, bakery, those added to the project): choosing one gives it to this building. Painted lines Full: the lines between lanes, the edge lines, the crossings and the parking bays. Edge lines only: the lines along the edges. None: no markings. Parcels How the blocks of this style are cut into parcels along the streets. Parcels to the middle (max) When the middle of the block is closer than this to the street, the parcels reach it, beyond the maximum depth: the middle of the block is shared between them and court buildings stand there. A larger block keeps its garden in the middle. 0: never. Parking The width of a parking strip on each side, in metres; 0 without. Parking clearance at a dropped curb No parking space in front of a dropped curb: the marking stops over its width, its ramps and this margin on each side, in metres; a space that would no longer have its full length disappears. Parking spaces taken The share of parking spaces in this district where a car is parked (60%: six in ten). Part du style The share of the city this style takes, compared with the others: the percentage next to it tells what it gives. Patched The patched state, with pieces of new material (never for markings). In the materials of a profile, the box allows it and the number gives its weight; in a style, its share (in %) for the streets of the district; in Upkeep, it is forced on the street. Pedestrian The street becomes a sloped pedestrian street: paving without markings or curbs, without cars; people on foot go through. Pedestrian street A way for people on foot only: no car goes through it. Pedestrians How many pedestrians walk on 100 m of pavement in this district, at the busiest hour. Pier shape Square piers (a wall across the bridge) or round ones (columns under a beam). Pier spacing (0: the generation's) The largest gap between two piers of a bridge of this profile, from 5 to 200 m; 0 keeps the generation setting (30 m). Pitched roofs (weight) The place of pitched roofs among the roofs of this style. Placed Checked: the city places this piece of furniture in the districts where it appears. Unchecked: none, anywhere. Plan view Shows the city from above: the view frames the whole city, each district filled with the colour of its style, the streets as light lines with their names. Turning it off leaves the view where it is. Planted share The share of the ground left free (parcels without a building, middles and corners of the blocks) kept in grass: gardens and squares, by whole parcel or whole block middle, never in scraps. The rest is paved with the ground left free. High for detached houses and housing estates, low in dense districts. Poids de l'état The weight of this state in the draw, from one street to the next: a state of weight 2 comes out twice as often as a state of weight 1. Poids de la sorte The place of this kind among the shops of the style: the larger the weight, the more there are. Population hour The time of day shown by the pavement colours: the crowd follows the hours set in the Population system (busier in the evening than at night, for example). Present Gas station: ticked, a gas station on this parcel (its kiosk, canopy and pumps), even where the style draws none; the parcel must be wide and deep enough. Unticked: no gas station here. Kept when the city is generated again. Price The price of the item to add, in the money of the system Shops of the city (one of its settings, "Or" by default). Profil des nouvelles rues The profile of the streets you are about to draw, chosen from the illustrated list: the cross-section shows the lanes and their direction, the median, the parking and the sidewalks. Profile family Where this profile goes in the gallery: City, Countryside, Mountain or Paths. Profile of its streets The profile of the streets of this district when the city is generated. Profile of the arterial roads The profile of one street in N of the grid of this district when the city is generated (an arterial road with 2 × 3 lanes); the others keep the profile of its streets. Profile of the main axes The profile the main axes crossing the city take in this district when it is generated: a grand boulevard with 2 × 4 lanes for an airy city made for driving. “The city's own”: the avenue of the generation. Pump islands The number of pump islands under the station's canopy (1 to 4), each with its pump; fewer if they do not fit in the parcel. Quartiers voulus The district styles the city must have. The most central ones (business) go in the middle, houses at the edge, the harbour by the water. Radius of the rounded corner The radius, in metres, of the curved facade of a rounded corner; 0: the width of the cut corner. A corner too tight for the curve keeps a cut corner. Random Draws a random seed: another city. Ranger l'outil Puts the tool away (like Esc): a click in the view selects objects again. Reattach to the nearest Reattaches this change to the parcel nearest to where it was: it holds again. Ctrl+Z makes it an orphan again. Regenerate Remakes the selected town in the same area, with the same mood and another seed; its name is kept, the other towns do not move. Ctrl+Z brings back the previous one. Remove the grime decal Removes the grime decal of this style: its facades stay without grime. Remove this kind Removes this kind of shop from the style. Remove this lane Removes this lane from the profile. A profile keeps at least one lane. Remove this material Removes this material from the style (a style keeps at least one). Remove this point Removes this point from the district outline (it keeps at least three). Remove this slab Removes the chosen added slab (also: Delete): the ground from before comes back underneath. One step, Ctrl+Z undoes it. Remove this street lamp from the catalogue Removes it from the catalogue: the profiles and districts that had chosen it go back to Automatic. Its files stay in the project. Remplacer par un matériau du projet… Puts a project material in place of this made material, on every building of the style. Rename the district… Gives this district a name (“The Old Harbour”): it is written in its middle, and the agent uses it to find its way. Rename the profile… Gives the open profile another name. The streets that use it keep it. Rename the shop… Opens the field of the shop name; Enter sets it, in one step (Ctrl+Z undoes it). Rename the street… Gives this street a name (“Harbour Avenue”): it shows when you hover over it, and the agent uses it to find its way. Rename the style… Changes the shown name of this style. Rename… Changes the name of the landmark, written above it in the view; Enter sets it. Replace with… Replaces the building: « Nothing: I build it myself » leaves the parcel empty, as a landmark, for your own objects. Replaces the wall The model carries its own wall: the city does not make a wall behind it. Restore this profile Gives this built-in profile back its original values (widths, materials, wear). Ctrl+Z goes back to your settings. Restore this style Gives this style back its starting values. Retirer ce nœud This node is no longer laid with the piece. Retouches qui ne tiennent plus Parcel changes whose street was removed or cut: they no longer apply, but nothing is lost. Reattach each one to the nearest parcel, or delete it. Right side The fence on the right boundary of the parcel, seen from the street. Shared with the neighbour: the one chosen here wins. Road arrows The arrows painted on the lanes that arrive at a junction (when at least two arrive): straight, left, right, as each lane allows; the left-turn lane carries a left arrow. Roadway The material of the roadway of the city streets of this district, or the one of their profile. Role What this model is in the facade: window, door, shop front, garage, pier… Base, string course, cornice: a band laid along the facade, repeated per bay and mitred at the corners, in place of the made band. Band end, band corner: the piece laid where a band stops short, or at a square salient corner instead of the mitre. « Not in the facade »: the city does not place it (a door leaf, a piece for another use). Roof The shape of the roof: flat (with a low wall), pitched (tiles, the ridge along the street) or a terrace. Roof pitch The pitch of the style's sloped roofs, from 10 to 60 degrees. Roof terraces (weight) The place of roof terraces among the roofs of this style. Room The floor, the lower walls, the walls and the ceiling of the room: each a material of your project (the same list as the other materials of the city) or the city's own, at the size written in the material; the colour of the walls and of the ceiling. "For every shop of this kind" writes the choice into the kind. Kept when the city regenerates. Roundabout Turns this junction into a roundabout, or gives it back its ordinary shape. Save the kit Writes kit.json in the folder of the kit; the old one is kept as kit.json.bak. A file is not a step: Ctrl+Z does not undo it. Second colour The second colour of the storefront: one stripe out of two of the awning. Drawn from the palette of its style, or chosen here; the arrow gives back the drawn colour. Sens de la voie Forward: in the direction the street was drawn. Back: the opposite direction. Set by hand A chosen ground level: it starts from the measured one; set it in metres above the bottom of the model. Set-back top floors The share of buildings whose top floor is set back. Setback from the curb The distance from the pole to the edge of the sidewalk, in metres: 0.5 m keeps it clear of cars that brush the curb. Share of spots kept The share of spots where the furniture is actually placed, from 0 to 1: at 0.15, a work zone (cones) on about one spot in seven. Shop The shop on the ground floor: none, a chosen kind, or drawn by the style like its neighbours. Shop front The shop painted behind the window of this shop when it is not visited (or from afar): shelves, clothes racks, tables, counter or display stands. "From its kind" follows the kind; choosing one sets it for this shop only. It lights up during opening hours and goes dark at closing. Shop logo The project image shown with the name on the sign: the one of the kind, or the one chosen for this shop. Without a logo, the sign carries the name alone. Shop name The name of the shop of this building, drawn by the city from its kind ("Café des Tilleuls"), or chosen: Rename the shop… changes it, the arrow gives back the drawn name. Common names only, never a brand. Shop share The share of ground floors that are shops. Shop weight How many shops along a street of this profile: the shop share of the district, times this weight. 150% on avenues and pedestrian streets, 30% in back lanes: shops line the big streets. Shops The share of shop ground floors and their kinds. Shortest length No short pieces of guardrail: a shorter piece is joined to its neighbour if it is close enough, otherwise removed. Shoulder width A strip at the level of the roadway, on each side, with no curb (gravel, earth or asphalt); 0 without. Show the population On the plan view, colours the pavements by how many pedestrians will walk there at the chosen hour: blue-grey where it is quiet, bright colour where it is busiest. Needs the Population system. Shutter down after hours Ticked: outside the hours of its kind, this shop lowers its metal shutter in front of its window; unticked, its window stays dark. Its kind's choice by default (clothing, pharmacy, bakery: the US custom; never for a shop open day and night, such as the convenience store); changing it sets it for this building. The hour is the sky's (Day and night in Play). Side The side the model is drawn for, seen from the street. An end is mirrored for the other side; a corner is laid only on its side, its return leg going back. Side gap (max) The space left at most between the building and each side of its parcel. Side gap (min) The space left at least between the building and each side of its parcel; 0: buildings touch. Sides Where the street lamps are placed. Automatic: on the median of an avenue if it is 1.5 m or wider, on both sides of an avenue, staggered in a street of 12 m or more or a pedestrian street, on one side otherwise. One, Both, Staggered (one side then the other), Median (in the middle of the roadway). Sidewalk The material of the sidewalk of the city streets of this district, or the one of their profile. Sidewalk width The width of each sidewalk, in metres; 0: no sidewalk, so no curb. Sign after the junction The distance between the junction and the first speed limit sign, in metres (30 m by default). A street shorter than twice this distance has none. Sign height The height of the bottom of the signs above the sidewalk, in metres (2.1 m, 7 feet, in US towns). Sign setback The distance between the curb and the post of the signs and lights, in metres (0.5 m by default). Signs and lights The signs and traffic lights at the ends of this street: a STOP or YIELD sign and a traffic light where the street stops or gives way, on the sidewalk to the right, just before the line. By default the ones WorldMint makes (US standard); a project model can replace them, role by role (signModels, through the agent). Slope (max) The steepest slope along this profile; beyond it, the street is reported as too steep. Soft edge A painted path: the width of its edge that blends into the ground, on each side, in metres. Softened edges The size of the small chamfer laid on the outer edges of generated buildings: the nose of cornices and bands, window sills, surrounds and lintels, steps, balcony slabs, column plinths. It catches the light and breaks the too-sharp line of a box, as in city games. It never takes more than a quarter of the thickness of a part. 2 cm by default; 0: sharp edges. From 0 to 5 cm. The ground of the blocks is not affected. Solid approach line Before the stop or give-way line, the dashed lines between two lanes going the same way become solid over this length, in metres: no more lane changes. 0: dashed to the end. Space between dashes The space between two dashes, in metres (9 m, 30 ft). Spacing (0: from the model) The distance between two street lamps on the same side, in metres. 0: the catalogue model's, otherwise 3.5 times its height (24.5 m for a 7 m street lamp). Speed limit The speed allowed on this street: one SPEED LIMIT sign per direction after every junction (in mph with the US standard, km/h otherwise). 0: no sign. A project model can replace it (signModels, role speed_limit_30 or speed_limit, through the agent). Speed limit sign spacing On a long street, another speed limit sign every this many metres (300 m by default). 0: only one after each junction. Stairs The street becomes stairs in paving slabs, over its whole width: regular steps (17 cm high, 30 cm deep at first), a landing every 12 steps, handrails on both sides. They follow the hill between the two junctions; their edges meet the ground with slopes. In play, you climb without tripping: an invisible ramp runs under the steps. Steep passage What a street drawn between two junctions too far apart in height for the slope of its profile (a street cars cannot climb) becomes. Automatic: a street drawn by hand becomes a sloped pedestrian street up to the plan's pedestrian slope (20% at first), stairs beyond, a street if cars can climb it; a generated street stays a street (the generator removes its own). Street, Stairs or Pedestrian force it, on any street. No cars, no markings; people on foot go through. The hill is not dug and the junctions do not move. Ctrl+Z goes back to the previous passage. Step blocks The length of a stone block across the width of this style's entrance steps (in metres): the steps are cut at the same places from top to bottom, a joint running from tread to riser; each step is also a block of its own, its joint at the back of the tread. 0: each step in one piece. The agent can change it too (stepBlock). Steps The stone of the steps, landing and threshold of this style's entrances: a honed grey granite without joints by default (a shipped ambientCG photo, at its real size, with a softened nosing); its joints are in the geometry, at the back of each tread and at the cuts of the "Step blocks", never the wall's stone. Replace it with a project material or pick one online; the agent can change it too (buildingMaterials, use "marche"). Stock (0: no limit) How many purchases of the item to add each shop can make; 0: it never runs out. The stock stays with the shop when its clerk leaves and comes back, and the saved game keeps it. Stop line setback The distance between the pedestrian crossing and the stop line, in metres. The line is only painted for cars that must stop (a stop sign or a light); the main street keeps the right of way. Stop line width The thickness of the stop line painted across the lanes that arrive at the junction, in metres (0.3 to 0.5 m). Storefront The style of the ground floor of this shop: classic painted shopfront, modern glass front, stone arcade front, café with a covered terrace, bank with columns, simple local shop. Drawn among those of its kind, or chosen here (one step, Ctrl+Z undoes it); None gives back the plain shop front of the facade. The dots show the colours of each style: the shop takes one for its woodwork, its fascia and its awning. Storefront colour The colour of the painted woodwork, the fascia and the awning of this shop. Drawn from the palette of its style, or chosen here (one step when released, Ctrl+Z undoes it); the arrow gives back the drawn colour. Street frontage (max) The largest width of a parcel along the street, in metres. Street frontage (min) The smallest width of a parcel along the street, in metres. Street furniture What the city places on the sidewalks, role by role: fire hydrants (near crossings, the American way), street bins, benches, newspaper boxes, trash bags at the foot of the facades, utility poles and their wires, construction cones and barriers. Never on the roadway, nor in front of an entrance, nor in the crosswalk of a crossing, nor against a tree or a street lamp. Each role comes from contenu/mobilier.json; a change here overrides it for this plan (one step, Ctrl+Z undoes it). Street lamp catalogue The street lamp models of this project, which the city places along the streets: each one with its kind, its wanted height and its number of heads (the bulbs found on the model). Empty: the city places a made street lamp. Street lamps The street lamp placed along the streets of this profile, or in this district. Automatic: the district style's, otherwise a lamp of the catalogue of the right kind (avenue, street, pedestrian street) and the right role (two opposite arms on a median, one arm along the sidewalks and at the corners), otherwise the made street lamp. None: no street lamp (on a profile). A model of the catalogue: that one everywhere. A profile's choice, when it is not Automatic, wins over the district's. Street layout How “Generate a city” lays out the streets of this district: grid, organic (winding streets) or suburban. Street materials of the district The material of the roadway and the sidewalk of the city streets of this district (cobbles in an old town); “The profile's own” keeps the one of each profile. A project material chosen in a profile always wins. Street profile Changes the profile of this street: its roadway, sidewalks and junctions are rebuilt around it. Ctrl+Z goes back to the previous profile. Street profiles The kinds of road of this plan, sorted by family (City, Countryside, Mountain, Paths), each with its cross-section: its lanes and their direction, its median, its parking, its sidewalks or shoulders, its ditches and its barriers. Click a profile to draw the next streets with it and open its settings. Street setback (max) The largest distance between the street and the building front (a front garden). Street setback (min) The smallest distance between the street and the building front. Street side The fence along the street, in front of the house (open on its driveway): "The style's one" follows the street, "None" removes it, or another fence, shipped or from your project. Street wear The share of each state (in %) for the streets of this district, among those their profile allows; the shares always add up to 100%, changing one adjusts the others: plenty of worn and patched in an industrial area, new in a business district. Streets and furniture For “Generate a city”: the street layout, the block size, their profile, where the district sits in the city, the furniture and the planting. Stripe width The width of each white stripe of the pedestrian crossing, in metres (0.5 m in Europe). Structure How the street crosses a dip. Automatic: a bridge where the ground dips more than the generation setting (3 m), or over water. Always on the surface: the street stays on the ground, carried by embankments (fill or cut), never by a wall; over water, which stays intact, the bridge stays. Bridge: a bridge along the whole street between its junctions, even on flat ground. Ctrl+Z gives the previous structure back. Stud diameter The base diameter of the studs of the tactile paving strip, in metres (25 mm by default); they are staggered, 2.4 diameters apart. Stud height The height of the studs of the tactile paving strip, in metres (5 mm by default). Style des nouveaux quartiers The style of the areas you are about to draw, chosen from the gallery: each style shows its colour and a small outline of its buildings. Surface Paved: a raised roadway, with its curbs and sidewalks. Painted in the ground: a dirt track or a footpath, painted into the ground, with no thickness and no sidewalk. Tactile paving color The color of the studded strip at the bottom of the pedestrian crossing ramps (yellow by default). Tactile paving strip At both ends of each pedestrian crossing, the curb is flush over the width of the crossing, with a ramp on each side; at the bottom of the ramp, a studded strip that can be felt with a foot or a cane. Here, its depth into the sidewalk, in metres; 0: no strip. Textured grass The city lawns in real grass: on a terrain that does not have its ground materials yet, the city turns them on (in the same step, Ctrl+Z removes them) and its green spaces show the textured grass of the terrain; a grass strip too narrow between two grounds is covered by the district ground. Unchecked: a terrain without materials keeps the plain colours of its regions. The city's own This profile follows the marking standard of the city, set in the generation settings (American by default). The models Each model of the folder, with its thumbnail and its measures. Nothing is chosen in advance: a model without a role is not in the facade. The whole kit The settings of the whole kit: the allowed stretch, the wall allowed above a piece too low, the wall allowed on the sides of a piece too narrow, and where the materials of the models go. A role a recipe asks for without a piece in the kit is said at the top of the panel: it takes the pieces of a neighbouring role (a French window or a shop front those of a window, an entrance those of a door), otherwise the made module. The "fallbacks" table of kit.json changes these fallbacks. Those of the kind The goods of the recipe of this kind of shop, like the other shops of the same kind. Tie the selected objects Ties the objects selected in the scene to the landmark: they are listed here and follow the parcel if the street moves. An object is tied to one landmark only. Tint A colour that multiplies the one of the material: white leaves it as it is. Tint variation How much the tint and wear change from one building to the next. Top floor step back How far a stepped-back top floor sits back from the street. Towns The named towns of this plan, each in its area, with its mood and its surface. A click selects one: its outline lights up and the view frames it. Tree height The height of the street trees, in metres. Tree spacing The distance between two street trees, in metres; 0 without trees. Triangle base The width of each give-way triangle, in metres (0.6 m, 24 in). The triangles point at the incoming cars. Triangle height The length of each give-way triangle along the street, in metres (0.9 m: one and a half times its base). Turn by 90° Turns the landmark by a quarter turn, in one step: to put its front on the street side. Turn half a turn For a model whose measured front is on the other side: a bench that would turn its back on the street. Two lines Two white lines across the street, at both edges of the crosswalk. Untie Unties the selected tied objects from the landmark (a click in the list selects one). The object stays in the scene. Upkeep The state of this street: as the district says (drawn at random, always the same), or set by hand (new, worn, cracked, patched) for the whole street. Ctrl+Z goes back to the previous upkeep. Visitable Ticked: the interior of this shop is built and can be visited. Drawn by the visitable share of the style; ticking or unticking it sets it for this building. Visitable share The share of the style's shops whose interior is built and can be visited. It is the first setting of the cost of interiors: the higher it is, the more rooms there are to draw. Wall The wall material, among those of the style of its district (brick, render, stone…). Wall allowed above A piece lower than its cell (3 m pieces for a 4 m ground floor) is laid at the foot of the cell, at its own height, unstretched; the wall of the building fills the top, up to this share of the cell. Beyond it, or at 0, the made module is laid. Wall allowed on the sides A piece narrower than its cell (2 m windows for 3 m bays) is laid in the middle of the cell, at its own width, unstretched; the wall of the building fills both sides, up to this share of the cell. A piece that fills the cell comes first. Beyond it, or at 0, the made module is laid. Wall materials The wall materials of the style, drawn building by building; each with its swatch, and replaceable by a project material. Wall tones The tones the walls of the style can take: off-white, cream, pale ochre, grey… Each building draws one, and two neighbours never have the same. The tone multiplies the colour of the wall material. Right-click a swatch to remove it. With no tone, the tint variation chooses. Wall variation Breaks the repetition of the photo textures of the walls: each wall shifts (and turns, if the material allows it) its texture. 0 %: the texture laid as it is. Wanted height The height of the placed street lamp, from the ground to the top, in metres; the model is scaled to it and its bulbs follow. A pack model is often not to scale: avenue 8 to 10 m, street 6 to 7 m, old town and pedestrian street 4 m. Wear The share of each state of the facades (new, worn, cracked), in %, drawn building by building. The shares always add up to 100%: changing one adjusts the others. Wear blend length Where this street meets a newer or more worn street (of the same material), its roadway changes gradually from one to the other over this length, in metres, from the junction (at most half the street). The junction takes a mix of the streets that reach it. 0: the edge stays sharp. Weight Its share among the models of the same role and size: at 2, it comes out twice as often as a model at 1. Width of the cut corner The width, in metres, of the face that cuts the corner of a building with a cut corner; 0: a sharp corner. Width of the two lines The width of each of the two lines of a two-line crosswalk, in metres (0.3 m, 12 in). Worn The worn state. In the materials of a profile, the box allows it and the number gives its weight in the draw; in a style, its share (in %) for the streets of the district; in Upkeep, it is forced on the street. “ONLY” under the arrow Paint the word ONLY under the arrow of the left-turn lane, as in American streets.

items.title: The creation assistant
items.text:
Explained in detail: Getting started.

Control What it does Back Goes back: to the previous question in the assistant, or to the folder opened just before in the library. Launch Sends the request to the agent: it first presents its plan and waits for your approval before building. If the agent isn't connected yet, the request waits, ready, in the conversation. Next Keeps the answers and moves to the next step. Greyed out while a required question has no answer. Rebuild the text from the answers Replaces the request text, which you edited, with a new text built from your current answers. Your edits are lost. Save and close Keeps the answers and the request in the project, and closes the assistant without sending anything to the agent. Skip Skips this step without answering: its default answers stay, and the request will only mention what was chosen. Start from scratch Closes the assistant without answering the questions, to build the game yourself. It can be reopened at any time from Game > Creation assistant. With the assistant Starts the assistant's questions about your game. At the end, it prepares a request for the agent, to read over before launching it.

items.title: The game's controls
items.text:
Explained in detail: Game controls.

Control What it does Add Adds the control to the game. It needs a name not taken yet and a key. Add a control Creates a new control for the game: its name for scripts, its label for the player, and its key. Controls The game's keys: one control per action (jump, attack, use…), with its key and its gamepad button. Scripts read its name, the player sees its label; those of systems are added on their own. Key Click, then press the key, mouse button or wheel you want. Escape cancels. Label for the player The name the player sees, in a key menu for example. Left empty, it's the name for scripts. Name for scripts The name scripts use to read this control, without spaces (for example “parry”). It must not be taken already.

items.title: The game's languages and the Translations window
items.text:
Explained in detail: Translating your game.

Control What it does Add a language Offers one more language to players. The game picks the Windows language if it is offered, and the player can change it in the menu options. Removing a language keeps its table: adding it back finds its translations again. Ask the agent to translate Sends a request to the agent: it reads the texts without a translation and fills in the tables, without touching the original texts. You can then correct each cell. Game languages The language you write your game in, and the other languages you offer to players. Each offered language has its translation table, in the project's translations folder. Only what is missing Shows only the texts that still lack a translation in at least one language. Original language The language you write the game's texts in: lines, messages, title. A text without a translation shows in this language. Translations... Opens the Translations window: every text the player sees, one column per language, what is missing in red.

items.title: The game's scenes
items.text:
Explained in detail: Projects and scenes.

Control What it does An arrival point is missing The player's character isn't in this scene, and it has no arrival point: the player would appear anywhere, maybe in empty space. Create an arrival point Places an arrival point where you are looking. Move and turn it: the player will appear there, facing its direction. Then start the game again. Play anyway Starts the game without an arrival point: the player appears where they are in their other scene. Start the game here Makes this scene the one where the game starts: the exported game will open on it. It then shows the Start tag.

items.title: The game's sound mixer (Game settings panel, Sounds section)
items.text:
Explained in detail: Sound and the sound mixer.

Control What it does Add a ducking rule Adds a ducking rule: then choose the group that plays and the one that gets quieter. Add a group Creates a new sound group (a radio, a boss's voice): its name is enough. Scripts and systems can then put their sounds in it. Automatic ducking Rules such as “while this group plays, that one gets quieter”: the music goes under the voices, the ambience under a cutscene. It comes back on its own once silence returns. Down to How much of its volume it keeps while lowered: 40% keeps it clearly audible, 0% silences it. Fall time The time, in seconds, it takes to get quieter: 0.2 s goes unnoticed, 0 makes it drop at once. Game window in the background What the game's sound does when the player minimizes its window or switches to another window (a browser, a chat): it mutes, gets quieter, or goes on. A game started in the background for a test always stays silent. Group name The name you see, and that the player sees in the Options menu. The name for scripts comes from it, in lowercase and without spaces. Lower this group The group that gets quieter meanwhile: usually the music. Lowered to How much of its volume the sound keeps when the window is not in front: 30% can still be heard without being in the way. Muffled groups A group muffled all the time, as if behind a wall or through a radio: 0 clear, 1 as under water. To muffle while playing, use a Trigger rule or a script instead. Recovery time The time, in seconds, it takes to come back once silence returns: 0.8 s brings it back gently. Remove this ducking rule Deletes this rule: the two groups no longer affect each other. Sound mixer The game's sound groups: music, effects, ambience, voices, interface, and those you add. Each has its volume, can be muted or muffled, and can get quieter on its own while another one plays. The sound Mute the sound: the game is silent while its window is not in front. Lower the sound: it goes on, quieter. Keep the sound: nothing changes. While this group plays The group that makes the other one quieter while one of its sounds is heard: usually the voices. A sound too far away to be heard does not count.

items.title: The home screen (File, Home)
items.text:
Explained in detail: Getting started.

Control What it does Browse… Opens a Windows window to choose where to put the game. Connect an agent Opens the Agent panel settings to connect Claude or Codex. Create the project Creates the game's folder, shown just above, and opens it. Greyed out while the name or the location isn't suitable: the reason is written above. Create with the agent Creates a project (suggested name and folder, which you can change), opens it, and sends your description to the agent, as if you had typed it in the Agent panel. With no agent connected, it waits there, ready to send. Describe your game… What you want to make: the genre, the mood, what the player does. The project's name comes from it; you can change it. Game name Your game's name. It's also the name of the folder created for it. These characters aren't allowed: \ / : * ? " < > | Home Opens the home screen: start a game with the agent, a new game by genre, your recent projects, ways to learn. The cross or Esc closes it on your work. Learn The online documentation, the first steps, what's new and the keyboard shortcuts. Location The folder to put the game in, for example C:\Games. The game's folder is created inside it, with the game's name; the location is created too if it doesn't exist yet. New game A project ready for a genre: its systems are already added, with the genre's starting settings. Hover a card to read its systems. Open a project… Picks a WorldMint project on disk and opens it. Open the folder Opens the project's folder in Windows Explorer. Recent projects The last projects opened, with a picture taken at each save. A click opens it; a right-click opens its folder or removes it from the list. Remove from the list Removes the project from the recent projects. It stays on disk; nothing is deleted. Shortcuts Shows the editor's keyboard shortcuts. Show the home screen at startup Checked: the home screen opens each time WorldMint starts. It never opens in front of a project opened with a double-click. Start with the agent Describe your game in a sentence or more: WorldMint creates the project, then the agent starts building it with you in the Agent panel.

items.title: The interface editor (Interface panel)
items.text:
Explained in detail: The game interface: screens, menus, lists, text fields.

Control What it does Aligned In a column panel: left, centre or right. Anchored to The corner, edge or centre of the screen that holds the element. A score anchored top right stays in that corner on a wide screen as on a narrow one. Changing the anchor does not move it. Announcement The announcements of the systems added to the game. A script can send its own with game.emit: then write its name below. Announcement name The exact name of the announcement listened to, for example sante.change. Apply the game theme Brings the Interface system theme's styles into the game (button, panel, text...). Your own styles are kept; those of the same name you changed are pointed out before being replaced. Automatic height On, the height follows the content: a panel around what it arranges, an image in its proportions, a field according to its text. Automatic width On, the width follows the content: a text on one line, a panel around what it arranges, a button as wide as its panel. Back to the screen Shows the properties of the screen itself, instead of those of the chosen element. Back to the style Forgets what was changed by hand on this shape: it takes back the look of its style. Back to the system's version Puts the screen back the way its system delivered it: your changes to this screen are lost. Ctrl+Z brings them back. Background The background of the shape: none, a color, a gradient, an image from the project or the theme's skin. Background color The shape's background color, with its opacity: type its code (#RRGGBBAA) or click its square to choose it. A chosen color, gradient or image shows on any shape, even with an image theme: the theme no longer dresses it. Bar Places a bar that fills up: health, stamina, ammunition, a loading. Bind it to a value so it moves in the game. Behavior What the shape does: what happens when it is clicked, and whether it is a gauge, a text field or a list. Bottom Puts the shape against the bottom of the screen. With several shapes chosen (Ctrl+click), lines them up on the lowest of them. Bottom margin (pixels) The height of the bottom edge, in pixels of the image. Bring to front Puts the shape in front of all the others in its group. Built-in icon An icon WorldMint draws itself, without a file: a heart, a drop, a star, a sword... Button Places a button: on click, it sends its announcement (for the Trigger or a script) and can close or open a screen. For it to be clicked, the screen must show the cursor. Cells per row The number of cells on each row of the grid, all the same width. Center Puts the shape in the center of the screen, from left to right. With several shapes chosen (Ctrl+click), centers them on one another, in the middle of the box around them all. Center horizontally Puts this element in the middle, from left to right: in the middle of the screen if it stands alone, in the middle of its window if it is placed freely in it. A part arranged in its panel (a column, a slot) does not leave it: it is centered only if its panel allows it (a panel that takes all the room, its content in the middle); otherwise the button is greyed out and says why. Ctrl+Z undoes. Center vertically Puts this element in the middle, from top to bottom: in the middle of the screen if it stands alone, in the middle of its window if it is placed freely in it. A part arranged in its panel (a column, a slot) does not leave it: it is centered only if its panel allows it (a panel that takes all the room, its content in the middle); otherwise the button is greyed out and says why. Ctrl+Z undoes. Choose look-alikes Also chooses the siblings of this element that look like it, in the same panel: the same kind and the same role (all the slots of an inventory grid, all the buttons of a column). Then a width or height you change applies to all of them, in one step that Ctrl+Z removes. Choose what contains it Chooses the window or column that contains the chosen element: to move the whole window at once, or resize a column. Clear the selection Choose nothing in the game screen any more. Esc with the mouse over the screen, or a click on empty space, does the same. Content What the shape shows: an icon or a picture, and a text, each with its own formatting. Control that opens it A control of the game (Game controls panel) that opens it, then closes it: I for an inventory, Tab for a map. Copy formatting Remembers the chosen shape's look, to paste it on another one, like Word's format painter. Copy the look Remembers the chosen element's look as you see it, even if it was never adjusted: its size, font, letter size, color and formatting, background, opacity, and for a panel its margins, spacing and content alignment. Never its text or its place. With several elements chosen, the first one's look. Corner size 1: one pixel of the image is one pixel of a screen 1080 pixels high, and grows with the screen. 2: corners twice as big. Decimal places How many digits after the decimal point for a number: 0 writes 38, 1 writes 37.6. Delete the element Removes the element, and what it contains if it is a panel. Delete does the same, with the mouse over the screen. Ctrl+Z brings it back. Delete the screen Removes the screen from the game. Ctrl+Z brings it back. Disabled (greyed out, cannot be clicked) On, the button is greyed out and reacts neither to clicks nor to the gamepad. A script enables it again with game.hud_set("screen/button", {disabled = false}). Disabled image The image of the disabled button. Empty: the normal image, faded. Display The ribbon tab that sets what the editor shows, without changing anything in the game: the zoom, the screen format being tried, the magnet. Distribute horizontally With three or more shapes chosen (Ctrl+click): the two at the ends stay, the ones in between get equal gaps. Distribute vertically Like horizontally, from top to bottom. Done Closes the style being edited: the Format pane goes back to the screen. Edges and middle Stretch: the edges and the middle get longer. Repeat: they repeat at their size, like tiles (a pattern, a rope). Element The element's name, and what places it. Element name Its name, unique in the screen. A script touches it by "screen/name", for example game.hud_set("jeu/score", {text = "10"}). Elements Everything the screen contains, in the order they are drawn: the first one underneath. A click chooses one. Field Adds a text field: the player types a name, a code, a message in it. Field read The field of the announcement or system that gives the value: vie for sante.change. Fill How the background picture fills the shape. Stretched: it takes the frame's shape (and can become a stretchable frame). Covers the frame: it fills it without distortion, its extra edges cut off (a title screen background). Fits inside: it fits whole inside, centered, without distortion (a logo). Filled (0 to 1) How full the bar is before a bound value changes it: 1 full, 0.5 half. Fills The direction in which the bar fills: left to right, right to left, bottom to top or top to bottom. Fit Puts the whole game screen preview back in its area: zoom at 100 %, no offset. To zoom: "–" and "+", or Ctrl+wheel (50 % to 400 %); to move around the zoomed preview, drag with the middle button, or Space + drag. Fit the screen Goes back to the whole screen, fitted to the space. Format ({valeur}, {max}) The text shown, where {valeur} and {max} are replaced: "Health: {valeur} / {max}", "Score: [b]{valeur}[/b]". Empty: the value alone. From whom (joueur for the player, an object, empty: anyone) joueur to keep only what concerns the player, the name of an object (a boss), or nothing for everyone. Game window Shows the screen with the proportions of the game window (set in Game › Game window), instead of a common format. Gap between elements The space between two elements of the panel, as a share of the screen height. Gauge Adds a gauge, filled by a value: health, stamina, progress. Gradient direction Which way the gradient goes from the start color to the end color. Greyed text of an empty field A hint, greyed, until the player has typed something: "Your name". Hand To rearrange: grab a part of a window (a slot, a title, a column) and drag it. A line shows where it will land: between two neighbours in its panel to change its order, or in another panel to move it there. Dropping outside a panel changes nothing. Ctrl+Z undoes; "Put back as the system places it" returns it to its original place. Height (share of the screen) Its height, as a share of the screen height: 0.05 is a twentieth. Hidden on announcement The announcements that hide it, separated by commas: for example menu.jouer to hide a welcome screen. Home The first tab of the ribbon: undo and redo, the style gallery (a click gives a style to the chosen shape), copy and paste formatting. Horizontal offset The distance to its anchor point, as a share of the screen width: -0.02 moves it a little away from the right edge. Hovered image The image of the button when the mouse is over it. Empty: the normal image, outlined with the accent color. Icon Adds an icon, or chooses the shape's: a project file or an icon drawn by WorldMint. Icon (optional) A small image in the middle of the button (an inventory slot). It can be an icon taken from a sheet. Icon position Where the icon sits next to the text: left, right, above, below, alone, or behind the text. Icon size The size of the icon, as a share of the shape's height. Icon tint A color that tints the icon; off, the icon keeps its own colors. Image Places an image from the project: a logo, an icon, a frame. Choose its file in its properties. Image file An image of the project or the library: drag it from the asset browser onto this field or onto the screen, or use “Choose…” in the list. It is copied into the project. In the middle Puts the shape in the middle of the screen, from top to bottom. With several shapes chosen (Ctrl+click), puts them at the same height, in the middle of the box around them all. Inner margin The space between the edge of the panel and what it contains, as a share of the screen height. Insert The ribbon tab that adds a new shape to the screen: a drawn shape, a text, a button, an image, an icon, a gauge, a field, a panel or a list. Interface screens The screens the game shows on top of the scene: a score, a health bar, a help panel, a menu. They are drawn with the mouse, without code. A click opens one above the 3D view. Layout How the panel arranges what it contains: one under the other (a menu), side by side (a toolbar), or in a grid (an inventory). Layout The ribbon tab that arranges shapes: align them (on the screen, or with each other when several are chosen), bring them forward or send them backward, change their anchor, distribute them or give them the same size. Left Puts the shape against the left edge of the screen. With several shapes chosen (Ctrl+click), lines them up on the leftmost of them. Left margin (pixels) The width of the left edge, in pixels of the image: the cut line shows on the preview. List Adds a list: its first shape is the row model, repeated for each item the game gives it (an inventory, scores). Magnet On (by default), the edges and centre of what you drag or resize snap to the centre and edges of the screen, of its panel and of nearby elements; a thin line shows the guide. Off, you place things pixel-exact. Holding Alt during the gesture does the same, for that gesture. Maximum The value of a full bar, and what {max} shows. Maximum field (empty: a number) The field that gives the maximum (max for sante.change); empty, the maximum is the number below. More Opens "Manage styles": rename, duplicate, delete or edit a style, and apply the game theme. Move back Sends the shape back one step: it goes behind its neighbor. Move down Moves it after the next element: it is drawn on top, and comes lower in its panel. Move forward Brings the shape forward one step: it goes in front of its neighbor. Move up Moves it before the previous element: it is drawn underneath, and comes higher in its panel. My game The screens your game's scripts draw, next to the systems' windows: a round announcement, an end screen, a workshop window… When the agent draws a screen in a script, it declares it here with the way to open it (an event, a key, a click). Choose one: it opens in the game screen, and each of its parts can be adjusted with the mouse, like a system's window. New screen Creates an empty screen and opens it: place shapes on it with the Insert tab of the ribbon. It is shown from the start of the game, unless you change that. New style from this shape Makes a style from the chosen shape's look, and the shape follows it. Other shapes can then take this style from the Home gallery. New style… Makes a style from this shape's look, like "New style" in Word. The shape then follows this style, and other shapes can follow it too: changing the style changes them all. No slicing Removes the margins: the whole image stretches again. Normal image The image of the button at rest, instead of its color. Dropping an image from the asset browser onto the button puts it here. Number of rows How many rows the preview shows in this list. Only to try out the space: in the game, the system gives the real rows. On click What a click on the shape does: open, close or replace a screen, send an event, an action of the screen's system, or a ready-made Trigger action. "Nothing": the shape is not clickable. Opacity 100 %: fully visible; 0 %: transparent. What the shape contains fades with it. Open in the screen editor This element belongs to a screen delivered by a system. It is no longer adjusted here: this button opens its screen, where everything can be formatted. Outline The line around the shape: its color and thickness. Outline and shadow The line around the shape (its color, its thickness), its drop shadow and its opacity. Panel Places a panel: a background that arranges what goes in it, in a column, a row or a grid, without placing each thing by hand. Choose it, then insert a shape (Insert tab of the ribbon): it goes inside. Part shown The part of the image shown: the whole image, or a single icon of a sheet that holds several. Paste formatting Gives the chosen shape the copied look. Paste the look Gives the chosen elements the look copied from another (for example a slot's look on several buttons at once): the letters on those with a text, the background on those with one. Their text and place do not change. One step, Ctrl+Z undoes. Pauses the game While the screen is shown, the world stops: a menu, an inventory. Its control still works, to close it. Pick from the sheet… Opens the whole image: draw the rectangle of the icon you want, or give the size of a cell and click the cell. The chosen part replaces the whole image. Place freely The default tool: drag an element wherever you want, pull its handles to change its size. Its edges and centre snap to the centre and edges of the screen (or of its panel) and of nearby elements, a thin line shows the guide; hold Alt to place without snapping. A part of a window placed this way leaves its column. Placed in The screen itself, where it is placed by its anchor, or a panel, which arranges it with the others. Position and size Where the element is anchored, its offset, and its size. Everything counts as a share of the screen: the interface keeps its shape on every window size. Pressed image The image of the button while it is being clicked. Empty: the normal image, a bit darker. Preview Shows the button in this state here, to see its images. Changes nothing in the game. Put back as the system places it Removes this element's adjustment: it goes back to the place, size, rank and panel its system gives it. Ctrl+Z undoes. Put back as the system places them Removes the adjustments of all chosen elements: each goes back to the place, size, rank and panel its system gives it. A single step, Ctrl+Z undoes. Read from Where the value comes from: an announcement of the game (sante.change tells the health), a value a script gives with game.set_value, or an object's system. Remove the test value The preview goes back to the shape's text, or to three rows for a list. Right Puts the shape against the right edge of the screen. With several shapes chosen (Ctrl+click), lines them up on the rightmost of them. Right margin (pixels) The width of the right edge, in pixels of the image. Same height Gives every chosen shape the height of the first one chosen. Same size Gives every chosen shape the size of the first one chosen. Same width Gives every chosen shape the width of the first one chosen. Screen The screen's name and what it does when it is shown. Screen name Its name in the game. A script shows it with game.screen_show(name), and touches its elements by "name/element". Scrolls with the wheel With a chosen height: what goes beyond scrolls with the wheel, with a thin scroll bar. For a long list. Send to back Puts the shape behind all the others in its group. Shadow The shape's drop shadow: its color, offset and blur. Shape The ribbon tab for the chosen shape: its outline shape, its background, its outline, its shadow, its icon, and a new style made from it. Shape Adds a drawn shape: rectangle, rounded rectangle, circle, pill, diamond, triangle or star. It can hold a text and an icon. Shape The shape itself: its outline shape (rectangle, circle, star…) and, for a rounded rectangle, the radius of its corners.
