Shape outline The shape itself, as in PowerPoint: rectangle, rounded rectangle, circle, pill, diamond, triangle, star, or none for text alone, without a background or an outline. Choosing a background, an outline or a shadow for text alone gives it a rectangle, like filling a text box. Show this background anyway A screen shipped by a system keeps the image theme's dress over its background, which only shows without it. This button shows that background as it is, even with the image theme. Shown at start On, the screen is there from the start: a score, a health bar. Off, it waits for an announcement, a control or a button: a menu, a help window. Shown on announcement The announcements that show it, separated by commas: for example atelier.ouvrir, which a Trigger sends when the player enters the workshop. Shows the cursor While the screen is shown, the mouse cursor appears and the camera no longer turns: its buttons can be clicked. Starting text What the field holds when it appears. Stretchable frame Nine-piece slicing (9-slice): the corners keep their size, the edges and the middle stretch. A frame of any size, without distorted corners. System read The system whose value is read, on the player or on the object named below. Test value What the preview shows in place of the text the system will write (“3”, “Apple x3”). The game never uses it. Text Places a text: a title, a score, an instruction. It can show a value of the game, with [b]bold[/b] and [color=#ffd75a]colors[/color]. Text The ribbon tab for the chosen shape's text: its font, its size, bold, italic or underline, its color, and its place in the shape. Text color On, a chosen color; off, the one of the Interface system. Text field Places a field where the player types: a name, a code. Enter validates it, and the game receives the hud.valider announcement with the text. Text shown What it shows. [b]bold[/b] and [color=#ffd75a]color[/color] change the look of a part. A bound value replaces it in the game. The game screen Everything the player sees at the start, together: your drawn screens and what the systems put on screen (health bar, needs, quick bar, minimap…). Drag a system's element to move it: its settings follow, and Ctrl+Z undoes. The game's windows The windows your systems open during play: the title screen, pause, each tab of the options (Sound, Display, Controls), inventory, shop, dialogue…; in a game set to Multiplayer, also Join a game and character creation. Choose one: it opens in the game screen, filled with examples. Under "My game" come the screens your game's scripts draw (a round announcement, an end screen): the agent adds them there each time it creates one. Click a part (the window, a column, a button, a title), drag it or pull its handles: the adjustment is kept for the game, and Ctrl+Z undoes. The player's health In one click: the player's health, which the Health system announces. A bar fills up, a text writes "75 / 100". The screen The screen the click opens, replaces, or opens and closes. The whole image Shows the whole image again, instead of a part. Top Puts the shape against the top of the screen. With several shapes chosen (Ctrl+click), lines them up on the highest of them. Top margin (pixels) The height of the top edge, in pixels of the image. Use the system's again Removes the color chosen for its text: it takes back the one its system gives it. Value name The name a script gives: game.set_value("score", 12) fills the value "score". Value shown in the game What the element shows during the game, without code: the player's health, a score, a value of a system. In the editor, an example (75 out of 100) shows the room it will take. Vertical offset The distance to its anchor point, as a share of the screen height: 0.03 moves it a little below the top edge. When to show it What shows and hides the screen during the game: announcements of the game, or a key. Width (share of the screen) Its width, as a share of the screen width: 0.25 is a quarter. A text wraps at this width. With the size Ticked (the default): "Paste the look" also gives the copied element's width and height. Unticked: only its look. Zoom in Shows the screen bigger, for small details. The game doesn't change. Zoom out Shows the screen smaller. The game doesn't change.

items.title: The library
items.text:
Explained in detail: The library.

Control What it does Add a folder Adds to the library a folder of your computer that holds models, sounds or videos: pick it with Browse, or paste its path. It applies to all your projects. Add to project Downloads this asset into the project without placing it: its files are checked, then copied into assets/ with a LICENCE.txt file giving its author, source and licence. ambientCG Free materials and decals (leaks, stains, grime) from ambientcg.com, in the public domain (CC0): you can use, change and sell them in your games. A decal arrives as a transparent image, to lay with a Decal. Browse Opens a window to choose the folder to add to the library. Check all Checks every object of the list. Copy path Copies the full location of the file on the computer, to paste it elsewhere. Delete Deletes what is chosen: the selected objects (Del key), a script, a reusable object or a game scene. Ctrl+Z undoes it; a deleted scene is set aside in the project instead. Each piece on its own One object per piece of the file that holds a shape: the case of a pack of simple objects. Give to the characters Copies the animation file chosen in the Animations folder into the project, with its licence, and adds it to the player's animation files. Every character can then play its moves, even those whose bones have other names (borrowing) or whose skeleton was created in the editor. Ctrl+Z removes it. Grouping How the pieces of the file become objects: each on its own, or those of the same parent together. Import a Megascans folder… Imports a Megascans element you downloaded on Fab with your Epic account, then unzipped: choose its folder, or drop it on the editor. It becomes a material ready to apply (and a model for a 3D object or a plant), its images shrunk to 2K. WorldMint downloads nothing from Fab. Check the Fab licence of each element. Keep empty objects Also writes objects with no visible shape (no triangles). Left out otherwise. Keep the file's origin Each object's anchor point stays the file's one, instead of the middle of the object's bottom (which sets it neatly on the ground). Laisser les noms qui contiennent Leaves out objects whose name contains this text, ignoring case. Separate several texts with “;”; “*” stands for any characters (floor*: names that start with floor). Leave out objects larger than Leaves out objects with a side larger than this size, in metres: the studio backdrop of a showcase scene, a huge floor. Library address The address of a library index in the WorldMint format (https://…, or http://127.0.0.1:… for a demo on this computer). Press Enter to add it; the cross removes it. Move to Puts this project model in another project folder (or drag it onto a folder). Whatever uses it follows: the objects of every scene, its moves, its pose adjustments. Ctrl+Z puts it back. A .gltf, .obj or .fbx, which keep files next to them, can only be renamed in place. Objects to leave out The objects the split does not write: too large, with a chosen name, empty, or unchecked in the list. Open Opens what is chosen: a library folder shows its contents, a game scene opens in the editor. Open file location Opens the folder that contains this file in File Explorer. Open in File Explorer Opens this folder in File Explorer. Open the asset's page Opens this asset's page on its source's website in the browser. Pieces of the same parent together Pieces under the same parent make one object: a traffic light head, a piece of furniture made of several parts. A parent that holds the whole file does not count. Place all objects where they were Places every object of the split in the scene, each at its place in the original file, under a group named like the file, where the active view is looking: the scene rebuilt as it was. A single Ctrl+Z removes them all. Place in the scene Adds this model or reusable object to the scene, where the active view is looking. A double-click, or dragging it into the view, does the same. Place in the scene Places the animal chosen in the Animations folder in the scene: a ready model, with its skeleton and its moves (walk, gallop, attack...). It is copied into the project with its licence; the same file serves for the model and its moves. Ctrl+Z removes it from the scene. Poly Haven Free 3D models from polyhaven.com, in the public domain (CC0): you can use, change and sell them in your games. The "Powered by Poly Haven" notice stays shown under their previews, as their site asks. Refresh Reads the catalogues of the online sources again, to see the assets added since. Sources Chooses where the assets of the Online folder come from: the free models and textures of Poly Haven, the materials and decals of ambientCG, or a library address. No source is chosen at first, and nothing is contacted before. Nothing about you is sent: your searches run on this computer. Split Writes one .glb file per checked object into the folder shown, its images once into textures/, and each object's place in objets.json. Each file keeps the model's origin and licence. Split into objects… Splits a model that holds several objects in a single file (a pack of foods, a whole scene, a kit of parts): one model per object, named like it, in a project folder named like the file. A window first shows the objects found. Uncheck all Unchecks every object of the list: then check those to keep. Watch Opens this video in the Windows player, to watch it before putting it in the game. In the game, the Trigger ("Play a video" action) or a script plays it.

items.title: The menus
items.text:
Explained in detail: Menus and shortcuts.

Control What it does Agent The agent is the AI assistant that builds your game in the editor, with your own account. Here: its conversation and its settings. Agent settings Opens the agent settings: account, model, reasoning effort, program, and the rules it follows. Ask the agent Prepares a message about this object in the conversation: "About…". You only have to write what you want. Build tools The build tools' code linked into the editor and the games, with its licence. Bundled animations The animations that come with the editor (characters, animals, weapons): their author, licence and page. Bundled fonts The fonts of the editor's interface: their authors and licence. Bundled models The 3D models that come with the editor (weapons, waterfall rocks…): their author, licence and page. Bundled sounds The sounds that come with the editor (weapons, explosions, magic): their authors, licence and page. Bundled textures The textures of the starter material library: their author, licence and page. Close Closes this window or panel. In a dialog, Esc does the same. Code libraries The open-source software WorldMint is built on: its version, licence and page. The full licence texts are under Full licenses. Console The console lists the editor's messages: what was just done, and errors. It also opens with a click on the status bar, at the very bottom. Console and log The panel with the messages of the editor and of the running game. Conversation Opens the Agent panel on the conversation, ready to type. Copy Keeps a copy of the selected objects, with what they contain, to paste it later (Ctrl+C). Crash reports Opens in File Explorer the folder where the editor and your games keep their crash reports. They stay on this computer: nothing is sent without your consent. Create Adds a new object to the scene: a folder, a camera, an arrival point, a zone, or a basic shape (cube, sphere, cylinder, capsule, plane). Create a project from this scene... For a scene that isn't in any project: turns it into a project, copying the models it uses into it. The original scene isn't changed. Creation assistant... Reopens the assistant that asks a few questions about your game and turns them into a request for the agent. Answers already given are kept. Available in a project. Creator Creator mode: the conversation with the agent on the left, the view in the middle, the drawer of the chosen object on the right, the library at the bottom. The simple gestures, without the advanced tools. Credits Shows the authors of the content that comes with WorldMint (models, textures, animations, sounds, fonts), the online library sources and the code libraries, with their licence and a link to their page. Cut Copies the selected objects, then removes them from the scene, to paste them elsewhere (Ctrl+X). Delete a layout Removes a layout you had saved. The built-in layouts stay. Delete the report Erases the report from this computer. If several are waiting, all of them are erased. Developer Developer mode: all the tools, the full scene, scripts, the timeline, the terrain. The scene, the selection and the conversation stay the same from one mode to the other. Do nothing Closes this question without sending anything. The report stays in the reports folder (Help menu), and the question isn't asked again. Don't recover Sets the automatic backup aside and keeps the scene as it was saved. The backup is put aside, not erased. Don't save Drops the unsaved changes and goes on (opening another scene, quitting...). They won't be offered for recovery. Duplicate Makes a copy of what is chosen, placed right next to it (Ctrl+D for the selected objects). For a game scene, creates a new identical scene. Edit Undo and redo, then cut, copy, paste, duplicate or delete the selected objects. Edit in Developer mode Switches to Developer mode with the terrain still chosen: its relief, region, water and plant tools are there. Export Turns the game into a folder to give to players, like File, Export the game. It first needs a played character. Export game and its dedicated server... Exports the game like "Export game...", and adds a Serveur subfolder to it: the dedicated server (WorldMintServer.exe), which keeps the world open day and night so friends join whenever they like, with its settings (serveur.json) and instructions (LISEZMOI.txt). Only for a multiplayer game. Export game... Turns your game into a standalone folder with its own program, which anyone can run on Windows without WorldMint. Greyed out while the game has no player. File Projects and scenes: create, open, save, export the game. It also holds the preferences, and the way to quit the editor. Fix it Asks the agent to find and fix this script's error. With no agent connected, the request waits in the field. Four views Splits the 3D view into four, each with its own viewpoint, or goes back to a single view (Q). Frame selection Brings the views close to the selection, so you see all of it (F). With nothing selected, shows the whole scene. Free panels in Developer mode On: in Developer mode, every panel can be moved, grouped in tabs or float inside the window. Off: the former fixed layout. Full licenses Opens the Licenses window: the full text of every licence, the same file that goes with every game. Game What applies to the whole game. The menu starts the game, stops it, and reopens the creation assistant. Without free panels, the Game tab, on the left, gathers its controls, its sound mixer, its systems and its screens. Game controls The game controls panel: which key does what, for the player. Game settings The whole game's settings panel: the terrain, the sky and light, the window, and the sound mixing desk. Grid Shows or hides the ground grid in the 3D view. Group Puts the selected objects in a new folder, to move or set them up together (Ctrl+G). Group position The center of the chosen objects. Changing it moves them all together, in a single gesture undone with one Ctrl+Z. Help The list of keyboard shortcuts, the credits and licenses of what comes with WorldMint, and the choice of the editor's language. Ignore Removes this warning. The message stays in the conversation. Interface The game screens panel: the menu, the HUD, the windows the player sees. A click opens a screen next to the view. Invert selection Selects the objects that weren't selected and deselects the others (Ctrl+I). Objects hidden in the view are left out. Keep working Closes this question without doing anything: you stay on the scene, with your changes. Keyboard shortcuts Shows the list of the editor's keyboard shortcuts. Esc closes it. Language Chooses the editor's language, for example Français or English. The interface changes right away. Layout name The name the layout will have in the Windows menu. Layouts The panel layouts: the built-in ones (Default, Animation, World) and the ones you saved. Left panel Shows or hides the left column: the Scene, Game and Scripts tabs. Library Shows or hides the library, below the 3D view: your models and sounds, arranged like in File Explorer. Licenses Shows the licenses of the open-source software inside WorldMint and the exported games. The same file goes with every game. Make a reusable object Turns the chosen object into a reusable object: you can place it as many times as you like, and all its copies change together. It appears in the library, in the Reusable objects folder. New conversation Clears the current conversation and starts an empty one. The work already done in the scene stays. New project... Creates a project, a folder that will hold your whole game, then offers the creation assistant. You first choose where to put it. New scene... Asks where to save a new scene, then opens it empty (Ctrl+N). In a project, the + button of the scene list is simpler. Normal Shows the active 3D view normally, with its colors and lighting. The Z key cycles through Normal, Polygons and Wireframe. Object Create objects, and act on the selected ones: reusable object, groups, placing on the ground, rotation, size and collision. Online library sources The sites the online library downloads assets from into your project, with the credit line they ask for (“Powered by Poly Haven”). Open project folder Opens the project folder in File Explorer, to find its files. Open project... Opens an existing project: pick its .worldmint file, inside the project folder. Open recent scene The scenes you opened last, to go back to one in a click. Hover one to see its path. Open the license file Opens the THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.txt file in Notepad, to read or print it. Open the report Opens the report's folder in File Explorer: the log (journal.txt), the program's state (plantage.dmp) and the version (infos.json). Open... Opens a scene file (.wmscene) chosen in a window (Ctrl+O). If the current scene has changes, the editor first offers to save them. Paste Adds the copied or cut objects to the scene, slightly shifted so they don't stack on the originals (Ctrl+V). The pasted objects are selected. Place on ground Moves the selected objects up or down so they rest on whatever lies beneath, the terrain or another object (End key). Placement Where the object is, and its size. Rotation is done by hand, with the view's Rotate tool; the details are in Developer mode. Play Starts the game in its own window so you can try it (F5). It first needs a player: a character set as the player. Polygons Shows the active view normally, with the polygon edges drawn on top: you see what the models are made of. Preferences The settings of the editor itself, for all your projects: language and appearance, snapping steps, view navigation, automatic backup, console. They appear in the right column. Quit Closes the editor. If there are unsaved changes, it offers to save them first. Recover Reopens the work from the automatic backup. The scene file doesn't change until you save: save to keep it. Recover your work? The editor closed without saving, and an automatic backup holds your work: choose whether to bring it back. Redo Redoes the last change you just undid (Ctrl+Y). Reset rotation to zero Clears any rotation of the selected objects: they go back to their original orientation. Reset scale to 1 Gives the selected objects back their original size, with no enlarging or shrinking. Restore the default layout Puts every panel back in its original place: the scene on the left, the view in the middle, the properties and the agent on the right, the library at the bottom. Right panel Shows or hides the right column: the properties and the agent. Save Saves the open scene, and in a project the game settings too (Ctrl+S). When offered before switching scenes or quitting, it saves and then goes on. Save as... Saves the scene to another file, chosen in a window (Ctrl+Shift+S). The editor then keeps working on that new file. Save layout... Keeps the current place of the panels under a name, in your preferences: it will work in all your projects. Save the layout Keeps the current layout under the chosen name. Save your changes? The scene has unsaved changes: save them, drop them, or keep working without changing anything. Select Select objects in one go: all of them, the opposite of the current selection, or none. Select all Selects every object in the scene, except those hidden in the view (Ctrl+A). Select nothing Deselects every object. Handy to get back to the game settings, shown when nothing is selected. Send the report Opens your email program on a ready message, or the page meant for reports, with the report's folder next to it: you attach the files and send it yourself. Show everything again Brings back into the view every object hidden with the eye in the scene list. Show the whole scene Brings the view back to the whole scene, seen from a little above: its objects, without the terrain they stand on. To find your way back when you went too far (Home key: in every view). Sounds The mixing desk: the volume of each group of game sounds, which the player finds in their options. Stop Stops what is running: the game, whose window closes (F5), or, in the library, the sound being played. Third-party licenses The open-source software WorldMint is built on, with the text of their licenses. Nothing to do: this file already goes with the editor and every exported game. Translations Opens or closes the Translations window: every text the player sees, with its translation in each language the game offers. Turn collision off Removes collision from the selected objects: they can be passed through again. Turn collision on Gives the selected objects a collision box: the player and characters can no longer pass through them. Undo Undoes the last change made to the scene, by you or by the agent (Ctrl+Z). Repeat to go further back. Ungroup Takes the contents out of the selected folder, then removes the now empty folder (Ctrl+Shift+G). The objects don't move. View The viewpoint and display of the active 3D view, the four views, the grid, and the panels to show or hide. Walkable areas Shows in color, over the ground, where the game's characters can walk (game.walk_to): in blue what they reach from the player's place, in orange the isolated spots they can't reach (a roof, a closed room). No color: too steep, too narrow, under water or inside an obstacle. It updates by itself, in the background, when the scene changes. Walkable areas of the size When the game has several character sizes (game settings, Character walking): chooses the one whose walkable areas are shown. A big monster's areas stop where it can't go, even if a small one can. Windows The Developer mode panels: reopen a closed panel, go back to the default layout, pick or save a layout. Wireframe Shows only the edges of the models, without their surfaces, in the active view: you can see through them. The terrain shows like a map: shaded by its slope, tinted by its altitude, with its contour lines seen from above; it hides what is behind it, as in the normal view. WorldMint stopped suddenly The editor closed by itself last time, and left a report on this computer. You choose what to do with it; nothing is sent without you. Your game stopped suddenly A game started from the editor, or exported, closed by itself and left a report on this computer. Your scene isn't affected.

items.title: The player's animations
items.text:
Explained in detail: The properties.

Control What it does Add a sequence Creates a switch from one situation to another, which happens when its conditions are true. At first, it waits for the move to finish. Add a situation Creates a new situation, with a name to change and a move to choose. Sequences then say when the character enters it. Advanced animation settings Fine-tuning: for each situation, its playback speed, whether it loops, and which one comes first; then the sequences, which say when to go from one to another. Animation borrowing On, an animation file made for another character is adapted to this one: to its proportions (taller, stockier), even when it comes from another tool whose bones have other names (Mixamo, Unreal, Blender, Unity…). Bones are found on their own, by their name and then by the shape of the skeleton. Off, moves are read as they are, by bone names: useful if the borrowing goes wrong. Animation files The library files the character's moves come from. An added file is copied into the project; the cross removes it. Animations The move the character plays in each situation: idle, walking, jumping… The eye shows it on the character, in the scene. Bone matching For a file made for a skeleton whose bones have other names: the bone of the file each bone of the character follows, found by name or by shape. A bone marked “to check” rests on a weak clue; choose another bone of the file if it is wrong, or “(none)” so that it keeps its rest pose. By direction The moves used when the character faces the camera instead of turning toward where it goes: backwards, left and right, and the diagonals (forward-left, back-right…) when the file has them. They are blended with the situation's move (forward) according to the direction taken, on 8 directions; a diagonal with no move is shared by its two neighbours (4 directions). Without them, that move is used in every direction. Condition Adds a condition to this sequence: a value of the character (its speed, whether it's on the ground…), a sign and a number. All its conditions must be true for it to happen. Dust on landing A little dust rises under the player when they land from a jump or a fall. Untick it for a game where it does not fit (in space, under water). Feet on the ground On a slope, a step or a terrain, each foot rests on the real ground (moving objects included: a platform, a boat, a vehicle) instead of floating or sinking, and the hips lower as needed, for the foot touching the ground only: the leg the animation lifts follows the body. The engine looks for the legs in the skeleton (a foot, a knee, a hip): without them, nothing changes. File shown The animation file whose bone matching is shown, when several come from another skeleton. Largest feet gap The largest height gap corrected under a foot, in meters: beyond it (a ledge, a hole), the foot follows the animation. Move backwards The move when it walks backwards. Without it, if there is a sideways move, the forward move plays in reverse. Move to the left The move when it steps sideways, to its left. Without it, the forward move. Move to the right The move when it steps sideways, to its right. Without it, the forward move. Preview move The move played in the preview: on the left as the file gives it, on the right replayed on the character. Both should strike the same pose. Show all bones Also shows the bones with no role in the body: fingers, helper bones. By default, only the body bones (hips, spine, head, arms, legs) and those chosen by hand are listed.

items.title: The player: movement, camera and body
items.text:
Explained in detail: The properties.

Control What it does Acceleration How quickly it gets up to speed and stops, in m/s²: the higher it is, the faster it responds to the controls. Character body The invisible shape that stops the character at walls and lets it climb steps: its width, its height, and what it can climb. Distance Its distance from the character, in meters (0.5 to 100). A wall in between brings it closer. Face the camera The character always faces where the camera looks, instead of turning toward where it goes: it then walks sideways or backwards, as in a shooter. Its moves by direction are set in each situation (Advanced animation settings). Fall limit A height, in meters: if the player falls below it, they reappear at their starting point. A movable object (Physics system) that drops below it disappears. Gravity The force pulling the character back to the ground, in m/s²: the stronger it is, the faster it falls and the lower it jumps. Height For the character's body: its height, in meters (at least twice its radius). For the game window: its height, in pixels. Jump strength Its speed as the jump starts, in meters per second: the higher it is, the higher it jumps. Mass How much the character weighs, in kilograms: the heavier it is, the less a thrown crate or a rolling rock knocks it, and the more easily it pushes what it meets. 70 kg for an adult. Max tilt The highest angle the player can give it with the mouse, in degrees (at most 89): near 89, it looks down on the character from straight above. Maximum slope The steepest slope it can walk up, in degrees (1 to 89). It can't walk up anything steeper. Min tilt The lowest angle the player can give it with the mouse, in degrees (at least -89): negative, it dips below the character and looks up. Minimum distance Even when a wall pushes it, it never gets closer to the character than this distance, in meters. More camera settings The limits of its tilt, and how it keeps clear of walls. Mouse sensitivity How many degrees the camera turns for each pixel the mouse moves. At 0, the mouse no longer turns it. Movement How the played character walks, runs, jumps and swims. While the game is running (F5), every change applies right away. Obstacle margin The space it keeps between itself and a wall, in meters, so it doesn't see through it. Player camera The camera that follows the character in the game: its distance, what it aims at, its angle, and how the mouse turns it. Radius The radius of its invisible body, in meters: the larger it is, the harder it is to squeeze between two obstacles. Reset to defaults Puts all the player settings back to their starting values: movement, player camera and body. Its animations don't change. Return after obstacle When a wall has pushed it closer to the character, how fast it returns to its distance, in meters per second. Run speed Its speed when running, while holding the run key, in meters per second (0 to 50). Step height The tallest step it climbs without jumping, in meters. Swim speed Its speed in water deep enough to swim, in meters per second. Target height The height of the point it looks at, in meters above the character's feet. Tilt Its angle when the game starts, in degrees: positive, it looks down at the character from above; negative, from below. It stays between the min and max tilt. Turn speed How quickly it turns to face where it is going, in degrees per second. Walk speed Its speed when walking, in meters per second (0 to 50). While holding the control A game control (Game controls panel): while the player holds it, the character faces where the camera looks, to aim for example. None: it always turns toward where it goes.

items.title: The Scene tab
items.text:
Explained in detail: The Scene tab.

Control What it does Create inside Creates a new object inside this one: a folder, a camera, an arrival point, a zone, a particle effect, a decal or a basic shape. Decal Creates an invisible box that projects an image on the ground or the wall around its base: a footprint, an impact, a stain, a puddle, a sign. It carries the Decal system, turned on if needed; the box's scale sets the image's size. Fog volume Creates an invisible box filled with fog, which stays in its area: the mist of a valley, an undergrowth, a marsh. It carries the Fog volume system, turned on if needed: set its visibility, its colour and its edges in its properties; the box's scale sets its size. With volumetric fog, it catches the sun's rays. Frame in the view Brings the active view onto the whole sector. Double-clicking its name does the same. Game scenes The game's places, one per scene: a house, a cave, a level. A click opens one; the + creates another. Glowing air Creates an invisible box filled with an almost invisible air, which only shows the sun's rays where they cross it, like dust in a forest or a room: a Fog volume of kind Glowing air (rays only). It needs volumetric fog (Sky and light), in High or Medium quality, and a sun low enough to pass between foliage or walls. For a visible mist, choose Fog volume. Lock Freezes the sector: nothing moves, is created or deleted in it, its ground included, neither by you nor by the agent, until you unlock it. Handy for a finished district. New script Creates an empty script and opens it. Scripts give the game its rules; the agent can also write them for you. Particle effect Creates an invisible box giving off particles: a campfire, smoke, sparks, magic, rain or snow. It carries the Particle effect system, turned on if needed: choose the effect, its size and its colour in its properties. The effect already runs in the view. Rename Changes the name in place, as in File Explorer: Enter confirms, Escape cancels. For an object, the shortcut is F2. For a project model in the library (F2 too), the file is renamed and whatever uses it follows: the objects, its moves, its pose adjustments; Ctrl+Z puts it back. Save script Checks the script and saves it in the scene; if it has an error, it shows below the text. Ctrl+S in the text does the same. Sectors The named parts of a large map: the harbour, the old town, the north forest. The + draws a new one by clicking and dragging on the ground, in a view. Clicking a sector lets you work on it alone: the scene list, Ctrl+A and framing only see it, the other objects are hidden, and seen from above the rest of the map darkens. “Whole map” shows everything again. The padlock locks a sector: neither you nor the agent can change anything in it. The number on the right counts its objects (a building counts once). Unlock Reopens the sector: things can be changed in it again. Whole map Works on the whole map again: nothing is hidden. Work on this sector Shows only this sector: the scene list, the views, the selection and Ctrl+A are limited to it, the rest of the map is hidden (nothing is deleted). The agent works on the same sector. Zone Creates an invisible box that reports who enters and leaves it: a pressure plate, a trap, a finish line. It carries the Zone system, turned on if needed; set its size with the scale.

items.title: The script debugger and profiler
items.text:
Explained in detail: The Scripts tab.

Control What it does Calling functions The functions that led here, from the nearest to the farthest, with their line and their local variables. Continue The game resumes until the next breakpoint (F5 key). Its window comes back to the front. Marge des points d'arrêt Click a line number to set a breakpoint (a red dot) or remove it. During a game, the game pauses just before this line, and you see the script's variables. An empty line or a comment stops at the next line. Next line Runs the highlighted line and stops at the next one in the same function (F10 key). A function called on this line runs in one go. Shared variables The shared table, common to all the game's scripts. Step into the function If the highlighted line calls a function of this script, stops at its first line (F11 key). Otherwise, like Next line. Step out of the function Finishes the current function and stops in the one that called it (Shift+F11). If the engine called it (on_update, for example), the game resumes until the next breakpoint. Variables of the function The local variables of the stopped function, as they are before the highlighted line. A table unfolds with a click. Variables of the script This script's global variables (those declared without local), without its functions. Each script has its own. What slows down my game During a game, the time each script takes every frame, the heaviest at the top, in milliseconds and as a share of the frame. The game's systems are scripts: they show up too. A red bar is getting close to a limit. Hover over a row for details, click to open the script. The last game's profile stays shown afterwards.

items.title: The terrain
items.text:
Explained in detail: The terrain.

Control What it does Automatic regions WorldMint places the regions from the relief: sand along the sea and lakes, wide on a gentle coast and absent at the foot of a cliff; rock on steep slopes; snow up high, a little lower on shaded slopes; forests and grasslands in large zones with ragged borders; swamps in flat, damp hollows near water; desert if you want some. Off: the previous rules, which an older world keeps to remake itself exactly. Back to the natural course Removes all your waypoints: from its source, the river goes back to the path water follows by itself. Ctrl+Z brings them back. Greyed out when the river has no waypoint. Beach slope The slope of the ground on both sides of the coastline, from 0.01 to 1: 0.08 at first, a gentle sandy beach; 0.5 and more, a steep coast. The coast is made again when you release the mouse. Beach width The width, in meters, of the beaches that rise gently from the sea (0 to 500 m). Bed depth Multiplies the depth given by the flow, from 0.25 to 4: 1, the default; 2, a bed twice as deep. Bed width Multiplies the width given by the flow, from 0.25 to 4: 1, the default; 2, a bed twice as wide. Black altitude The altitude, in meters, of the image's black points: the lowest possible. Blend between regions The width, in meters, of the color blend from one region to the next. 0: sharp borders. Choppiness The wind on the water, from 0 to 1: 0, round and regular waves; 1, sharp crests, crossing waves, stronger ripples and foam on the crests. Clarity How far one sees through the water, in meters: small, murky water; large, a clear lagoon where the bottom shows far from the shores. Cliff share The share of the coast with cliffs, from 0 (only beaches) to 1 (only cliffs). They sit here and there, from the seed. Coast The sea's coastline: a line with handles laid on the shore. Drag its points, the coast passes where you put them: WorldMint digs below the water on the sea side and builds up above it on the land side, gently sloping, over 40 m on each side; its two ends stay anchored and the rest of the map does not change. The sea level is set further down. Coast detail The coastline: 0, simple and rounded; 1, very indented, with capes, bays and peninsulas. Color near the shores The color of shallow water, where the bottom can still be seen: turquoise over sand, green in a pond. Color steps Stylized water: the number of shades from the shore to the open water, from the color near the shores to the deep water color. 0 or 1: a smooth gradient; 3: three crisp color bands. Crust share Lava, from 0 to 1: the share of the surface covered by a dark, set crust. 0: all molten; 1: almost all set, with a few glowing cracks. Current The strength of the current, from 0 to 5: 1 by default, 0 for water that pushes nothing. The water runs faster on slopes, and carries what floats or swims. Deep water color The color of the water where the bottom can no longer be seen: it is the color of the water object. Deepest cut To pass through a point you placed, the river digs its bed through rising ground (water never flows uphill), but never deeper than this: from 0 to 200 m, 10 m at first. A point that needs more is refused: it turns orange, a sentence says why, and the river keeps its course. Depth The lake's depth at its deepest point, below the surface, from 0.3 to 200 m. The shore keeps its gentle slope; the middle is dug or raised when you release the mouse. Desert share The share of the driest land in desert, from 0 to 1. 0: no desert. Drift direction Lava: where its surface glides to, in degrees, like a compass laid on the terrain. Edit the coast by hand Lays a coastline of 7 points on the shore nearest the centre of the view: then drag its handles in the view. First bring the view close to the shore to edit. Edit the shore by hand For a lake made with the bucket: puts handles on its current shore. You can then drag it, add points or remove some; WorldMint digs and builds up so the water stays inside. Ctrl+Z undoes it. Erosion The strength of the erosion, from 0 to 1: rainwater runs down the slopes, carves gullies that join into V-shaped valleys and leaves fans at the foot of the mountains. 0: the relief as drawn, without erosion. Facet size Stylized water: the side, in meters, of the flat triangles that make the surface. Large, very low poly water; small, more detail. Waves shorter than three facets do not show. Facet strength Stylized water, from 0 to 1: at 1, each facet has its own crisp shade, from its slope facing the sun; toward 0, the surface smooths out, with the same waves. Floating things follow the facets in any case. Flow The river's flow, from 0.02 to 1: 0.15 a stream, 0.4 a river, 0.85 a wide river. It gives the width and depth of the bed, narrow at the source and wider and wider downstream. The river is made again when you release the mouse. Foam The white foam, from 0 to 1: on wave crests, along the shores and around whatever touches the water. 0: none. Foam width Stylized water: the width, in meters, of the white foam band along the shores and around whatever touches the water. In High quality, a second thinner band comes and goes beyond the first. The foam is also set with Foam (0: none). Forest share The share of the land in forest, from 0 to 1: the wettest, in large zones with ragged borders. Hills The height of the hills at the foot of the mountains and on the lowlands, from 0 to 1: never a vast flat plain. Hot color Lava: the color of the molten lava, in the cracks and pools. The hotter core turns yellow; the crust stays dark. Import Lays the heightmap as the terrain's relief, with the regions and sea set for “Generate a world”. Ctrl+Z to go back. Import a relief Makes the map from a heightmap: a grayscale image where white is the highest (preferably a 16-bit PNG, or a raw .raw or .r16 file), like World Machine, Gaea or real-data converters make. You then choose its scale and altitudes. Up to 4 km per side. Kind of water A ready-made kind of water: sea, stormy sea, lagoon, lake, pond, low poly sea or low poly lake. Choosing one sets the swell, the colors, the clarity and the foam at once; the two low poly kinds also switch the water to the Stylized style. Everything stays adjustable afterwards. lac:profondeur The depth of the lake at its deepest, in meters, below the water surface. Lake The chosen lake: its depth at the deepest point. In the view its shore shows its handles: a round handle per point, to drag, and a plus in the middle of each side to add one. WorldMint digs the bottom and builds up the banks so the water stays inside the shore. Its level and the look of its water are set just below. Lake depth The depth of the generator's lakes at their deepest, in meters, below the water surface. Lake size The mean radius of the generator's lakes, in meters; each varies a little around it. Lakes The number of natural lakes the generator places by itself, in the hollows of the relief, away from steep slopes and never in the sea. Each has an irregular outline, gently sloping shores and an uneven bottom. 0: none; the same seed places them at the same spots. Land centre Where the land is on the map, from 0.1 to 0.9 on each axis: 0.5 and 0.5 in the middle. Land share For an island, continents or an archipelago: the share of the map that is land, from 0.05 to 0.95. The rest is sea. Land span The size of the island or continent, as a share of the map side (0.1 to 1). With several lands: the area they spread over. Lava drift Lava: the speed, in meters per second, at which its crust (or its bands, when Stylized) slowly glides. 0: still. Lava light Lava, from 0 to 4: the strength of the light it gives off, which the bloom makes shine. 1: the starting one; 0: off, a cooled lava. Level The height of the water surface, in meters. Higher, the water covers more land: the sea rises, a lake overflows its hollow. Liquid What fills the body: water, or lava. Water can be swum and carries what floats. Lava glows by itself (the bloom makes it shine, day and night), is opaque, without waves or reflections; nobody swims in it, what falls in sinks and vanishes, and what touches it gets burned with the Health system. Its style (Realistic or Stylized) follows the same setting as water. Meters per point The distance between two points of the image, in meters: a 1,025-point image at 1 m makes a 1,024 m map. A map is at most 4 km per side. Mountain ranges The number of mountain ranges, 0 to 8. 0: one to three per land, from the seed. Their highest peaks reach the max altitude. Natural relief The island and mountain generator: coasts with a natural outline, gently sloping beaches and a few cliffs, a sea floor that slopes down to the open sea, mountain ranges with their ridges, valleys and foothills, and small relief down to a few meters. Off: the old generator; an older world keeps it to remake itself exactly with its seed. New region A region of your own, to paint wherever you want: name it and give it its color and systems. No-sand slope The coast slope, from 2 to 45°, from which there is no more sand. Paint this region Takes the Paint tool with this region: click and drag on the ground, in the view, to spread it. Pool at the foot How many metres deeper than the bed the pool at the foot of a waterfall is dug (1.2 m by default; 0: no pool). Put the coastline here Replaces the coastline with a new one, of 7 points, laid on the shore nearest the centre of the view. Ctrl+Z undoes it. Ragged borders From 0 to 1: 0, smooth borders between regions; 1, very ragged. Range direction The direction of the ranges, in degrees: 0 towards the east (+x), 90 towards the south (+z). -1: each seed picks its own. Range length The length of a range, as a share of its land's size (0.05 to 1.5). Range width The half width of a range, as a share of its land's size (0.02 to 1): narrow, steep slopes; wide, a massif. Regions The large areas of the ground: snow, rock, forest, grassland, desert, swamp, beach. Each one is an object with its color, plants and systems. When generating, untick those you do not want: their areas take the most fitting neighboring region. Regions from the terrain Redoes only the regions, from the current relief (sculpting included) and the settings above, without touching the relief. The vegetation follows the regions. Regions you added keep their areas; default regions painted by hand are redone. Ctrl+Z to go back. Remove the terrain Deletes the terrain from the scene, with everything stored in it: its regions, its water, its plants. Ctrl+Z brings it back. Rim width Stylized lava: the width, in meters, of the bright band along the shores and around whatever touches the lava. River The settings of the chosen river: its flow, the width and depth of its bed, its current, and how deep it may dig to pass through your points. In the view it shows its handles: the drop of its source, a round handle per waypoint, a plus to add one. The look of its water is set just below. River flow The flow of the generator's rivers: 0.15 a stream, 0.4 a river, 0.85 a wide river. It gives their width and depth. Rivers The number of rivers the generator places by itself: sources high up, far from each other, whose water follows the slope down to the sea, a lake or another river (they then join at a confluence). A river that would end anywhere else is not kept. Each can then be tuned like a source placed by hand. Rock slope Beyond this slope, from 15 to 80°, the ground is rock. Sand width The width of the sand along the water on a flat coast, from 0 to 200 m. It narrows as the coast gets steeper and is nil at the foot of a cliff. 0: no beach. Scree angle The angle of repose, from 20 to 60°: beyond it, the ground slides and piles up as scree at the foot of slopes. Cliff faces stay standing. Sea A sea at the coast level: it covers everything lower. It is always there around continents or islands. Sea shelf The width, in meters, of the shallow floor along the coasts before it drops to the deep sea (0 to 5,000 m). Seamless edges The left edge continues the right edge, and the top continues the bottom: a map that can wrap around the world. The game does not cross from one edge to the other yet. Shape The shape of the land: up to the edge of the map, one continent, several continents or an archipelago. Except with land up to the edge, a sea surrounds it up to the horizon. Size For the map: its side (256 m, 512 m, 1,024 m, 2 km or 4 km), used at the next generation. Beyond 1,024 m, a large map: the ground is drawn in detail around the camera and simplified in the distance. For a plant: its size compared with its model (× 1: as is, × 2: twice as big). Snow altitude Snow above this share of the altitude: 0 at the water's edge, 1 at the highest peak. It comes a little lower on shaded slopes (facing north). 1: no snow. source:courant The strength of the current, from 0 to 5 (1 by default): the water runs faster on slopes, its ripples and foam move downstream with it, and it carries along what floats or swims. 0: water that pushes nothing. source:debit The river's flow, from 0.02 to 1: 0.15 a stream, 0.4 a river, 0.85 a wide river. It sets the width and depth of the bed, narrow at the source and wider and wider downstream. Steepest lake ground The generator places no lake where the ground around is steeper than this slope, in degrees: on a slope, the upper shore would be a steep cut. Style The look of the water, chosen for the game. Realistic: fine waves, reflections of the sky and the scenery, see-through water where the bottom shows. Stylized: for a low poly game, a surface of flat facets, gentle readable waves, bold color steps and crisp foam bands; it costs less. Floating and swimming things follow the drawn waves in both cases. The render quality (Low, Medium, High) only sets the cost: stylized water stays stylized on a powerful computer. Swallows objects Lava: ticked, a moving object (Physics system) that falls in sinks slowly, then leaves the game. Unticked, it falls to the bottom and stays there. Swamps near water Swamps in flat, damp hollows within this distance of the water, from 0 to 1,000 m. 0: no swamp. Swell direction Where the waves go, in degrees, like a compass laid on the terrain. The smaller waves stray from it a little. Tree line No forest above this share of the altitude (0 at the water's edge, 1 at the highest peak). Variant The number that sets how the world is drawn: the same number, with the same settings, gives the same map again. The button next to it picks another one at random. Vegetation The plant kinds growing on this region, with their count. Drag a model from the explorer into the frame (a tree, a bush, grass, a rock): it grows over the whole region. Wakes The wakes and ripples around whatever moves in the water, from 0 to 1: the V opening behind a boat, the churned water in its wake, the rings around a swimmer or a floating crate. They are only drawn: floating things do not feel them. 0: none. Waterfall height The smallest drop, in metres, that makes a waterfall (2 m by default). A lower step stays a steep stretch, with a little foam. Waterfalls from The slope, in degrees, beyond which a drop of the river becomes a waterfall: the water leaves the lip and falls as an opaque white sheet in front of the rock instead of a softened channel, full foam on it fading at its foot, where a pool is dug. Waterfalls are in preparation: off by default (90°); 50° shows them, as a preview. Wave length The distance from one crest to the next, for the biggest waves, in meters. Short: a chop; long: an ocean swell. Shorter waves are always added on top. Waves The height of the biggest waves, in meters. 0: calm water, like a mirror. White altitude The altitude, in meters, of the image's white points: the highest possible. Zone size The size of the large forest and grassland zones, from 50 to 5,000 m.

items.title: The timeline: animations and cutscenes
items.text:
Explained in detail: Animate and make cutscenes.

Control What it does Add here Adds a moment where you clicked: a camera, a character (the selected one), a sound, a subtitle or an event, to set in the row above. Animation Creates an animation of the selected objects (a door that opens, a platform that rises) and opens it in the timeline, with a first keyframe of each as it is. Animation timeline Shows or hides the timeline, at the bottom of the view: there you animate objects frame by frame and put cutscenes together. Can be skipped The player can skip the cutscene with Esc (or Start): everything is set as at its end, and its events are sent. Cutscene Creates a cutscene and opens it in the timeline: cameras, characters, sounds, subtitles and events, while the player watches. Delete the timeline Removes this animation or cutscene from the scene. Ctrl+Z brings it back. Fade to black A fade to black of this length, centred on the camera change. From the start of the game Plays the timeline as soon as the game starts: a platform that comes and goes, an intro cutscene. Otherwise a Trigger rule or a script starts it. Glide The camera glides from the previous one during this time, instead of cutting at once. Keyframe Sets a keyframe of the selected objects, as they show, at the playhead. An object that already has its row also gets one as soon as you move, turn or scale it. Keyframe here Sets a keyframe of the object, as it shows, where you clicked. Lecture de l'animation Once: it stops at its end. Loop: it starts again. There and back: it goes back in reverse, forever (a platform that comes and goes). Length The length of the timeline, in seconds. It cannot cut keyframes off: move them first. Looping The character's animation repeats forever, instead of playing once. Music A music: it loops, and replaces the one that was playing. Otherwise, a sound played once. Name The name you see in the lists. The id does not change: the rules and scripts that play it still find it. New animation A new animation, with the selected objects as they are as its first keyframe. New cutscene A new ten-second cutscene: add its moments by right-clicking its rows. Remove the keyframe Removes this keyframe: the object goes straight from the previous one to the next. Remove this object from the timeline Removes this object's row and all its keyframes: it stays where it is in the scene. Règle de la frise The seconds of the timeline. Click or drag to move the playhead: the view shows the objects at that moment. Vers l'image clé suivante How the object goes from this keyframe to the next: linear (at a steady pace), smooth (it starts and stops gently), in steps (it waits, then jumps). Visible Shows or hides the object from this moment on: a blinking light, a bridge that appears. World stopped During the cutscene, the rest of the world stops: enemies, physics, scripts. Only it goes on, with its characters. Otherwise the world lives around it. Événement envoyé The name of the event sent at this moment: a Trigger rule ("When an event happens") or a script can wait for it.

items.title: Vegetation
items.text:
Explained in detail: The terrain.

Control What it does Density The number of plants per 100 m², up to 2,000 (20 per m²). Changing the density redoes the sowing: hand edits may no longer land on the same plants. Above 100, the plant kind becomes a carpet, for thick grass: its plants are only made around the camera, up to its draw distance (60 m suggested, 40 to 80 m advised), and fade out smoothly at the edge. A carpet does not stop the player, is not selected plant by plant, and its plant count is an estimate for the whole map. Erase Removes the selected plant (Delete key). It will not grow back, even if the terrain changes. Far ground tint For a grass carpet: beyond the distance where its blades fade out, the ground takes the colour of the grass as it is seen, computed from the model, so that the edge of the grass does not show when driving fast. Auto: the strength comes from the density and size of the blades; otherwise from 0 (the ground keeps its colour) to 1. Grounds On which ground materials its plants grow. By default, on the terrain's natural grounds (those of its regions, its rules, and the shipped grounds); never on a hard ground painted by hand, a square of tiles or paving. "Grows here": where it is painted, only on the ticked grounds. "Never": on none of these grounds, painted or not. In game How its plants behave during the game. Match the ground For a carpet only (density above 100): how much of the colour of the ground under the grass the whole carpet takes, from 0 (the grass keeps its model's colour) to 1 (it takes the ground's). 0.25 by default: a pack's grass matches the chosen ground. At the carpet's edge, the grass always takes the full ground colour as it shrinks: you cannot see where it stops. Max. size The largest size of a plant, compared with its model (× 2: twice as big). Each plant takes a random size between the min. size and the max. size. Max. slope The steepest slope it grows on, in degrees: nothing grows on steeper ground. Lower it to keep cliffs bare. Min. size The smallest size of a plant, compared with its model (× 1: as is). Each plant takes a random size between the min. size and the max. size. Put all plants back Forgets all hand edits of this kind: each plant goes back to the place, rotation and size it was sown with, and erased ones grow back. Put back in place As sown: the plant goes back to its original place, rotation and size. Reseed New random places for all its plants. Hand edits are forgotten. Select all its plants Selects all the plants of this kind, to edit them or place a system on them together. A system placed on the plant kind already applies to all of them. Select its plant kind Selects the plant kind that sowed this plant: its sowing settings and systems apply to all its plants. Sink into the ground Each plant is set at the lowest point of the ground under its foot, then sunk by this much, in meters: the foot seems to come out of the earth. Sowing How this plant kind spreads over its region: how many, what size, on which slopes. Stop growing it Removes this plant kind from its region: all its plants disappear. Ctrl+Z brings it back. Sway in the wind How much its plants bend in the wind, from 0 (stiff) to 1 (the most supple grass). Auto: from the model's height, grass very supple, a big tree a little, and slower. The wind's strength and direction are set in Sky and light. Tint noise Slightly lighter or darker patches in the tinted ground in the distance, so it does not look flat. From 0 (none) to 1. Trunk The diameter, in meters, that stops the player in the game. 0: you walk through (grass, flowers, bushes). Visible up to The distance, in meters, beyond which its plants are no longer drawn (60 % of this distance in Low quality, on an integrated chip). Closer, the game runs faster: grass can stop early, trees further away.

This page is generated automatically from the WorldMint code (help/*.json, locales/*.json): it always matches the editor.

items.title: Game scripts (Luau)
items.text:
Scripts give the game its own rules. They are written in Luau, in the editor's Scripts tab, and the agent writes them for you. Here is the full reference, exactly as the agent reads it (tool scripts_reference).

Game scripts are Luau, stored in the scene. They run on every simulation step, with the same result for the same inputs: there is no clock (only the date, game.today()), no file or network access, and math.random is seeded.

A script may define on_start() and on_update(dt), and on_save() and on_load(state) to keep its state in a saved game (see Saving). Each script has its own global variables; the table shared is common to all scripts. An error stops that script and is listed by game_run.

Objects are designated by id (a string). Positions are vectors: vec(x, y, z), with .x .y .z, arithmetic, and vector.magnitude(v), vector.normalize(v). Y is up, metres. A rotation is a yaw in radians; 0 faces +Z.

items.title: Finding objects
items.text:
game.player() -> id                    game.find(name_or_id) -> id or nil
game.players() -> {ids}. The character of every player: the one playing on this computer first, then, in a game with several players (the game setting Multiplayer), each guest who joined. The engine sends "joueur.arrivee" {joueur, numero, nom} when a guest joins and "joueur.depart" {joueur, numero} when they leave. A guest whose connection drops keeps their place (the game setting, 60 s by default): their character stands still, their per-player scripts keep running; back in time, the engine sends "joueur.reconnecte" {joueur, numero, nom} and neither depart nor arrivee. Particles (game.effect with a preset, game.stop_effect, game.object_effect) and full-screen videos (game.video) started by scripts on the host reach the guests like sounds: from a per-player copy or with {joueur = id}, that player only (the host does not show them); otherwise everyone, except one-shot particles too far from a guest.
Several players: game.player() is the player whose action is being handled. A script whose first lines hold the line "-- multijoueur: par_joueur" runs once per player (the host's copy, then one for each guest who joins, with its own variables, its own HUD and its own saved state): inside it, game.player() is always its player. A listener of an event that carries a field joueur handles that player; game.each_player(function(id) ... end) runs the function once per player, as that player. Elsewhere game.player() is the host's own player: in a game with several players, say which player. An event emitted while handling a player gets joueur = that player if it has none; the per-player copies of a script only receive the events of their player, and those that name no player.
game.player_name(id?) -> the player's name, the same everywhere (chat, "joined"/"left" lines, above heads, the server console): their character's name (the "nom" of the profile sent with game.profile_send and accepted by the host), else the name they typed to join or host, else "Joueur N" (N = game.player_number); nil if id is not a player. In a guest's game it comes from the host.    game.set_player_name(id, name) -> true, or false and why. A game with its own character creation gives the player's name (1 to 32 bytes of text): the host's or the server's game only (a guest's game is refused: "only the host (or the server) names players"); the new name reaches every player.    game.player_number(id?) -> 1 for the host, then 2, 3...; 0 if id is not a player (game.player_number(id) > 0 asks "is it a player?").
The controls, the mouse and the body of a player take an optional last argument, the player: game.pressed("attack", id), game.action, game.released, game.player_forward(id), game.set_player_speed(scale, id), game.set_player_can_run(on, id), game.set_player_can_jump(on, id), game.player_running(id), game.player_jumped(id), game.player_landed(id), game.player_swimming(id), game.set_player_dead(dead, id), game.player_dead(id), game.show_cursor(on, id), game.cursor_shown(id), game.drive(vehicle, id), game.leave_vehicle(id), game.driving(id), game.active_camera(id), game.camera_view(id), game.using_pad(id), game.pause(on, reason, {actions}, id), game.paused(id). game.use_camera and game.use_player_camera take {joueur = id}. Without it: the player whose action is being handled.
game.with_tag(tag, {asleep=false}?) -> {ids}     game.near(pos_or_id, radius, tag?, {asleep=false}?) -> {ids}, nearest first
game.exists(id) -> bool                game.name(id) -> string
game.awake(id) -> bool. In a large world, objects in 256 m tiles beyond the activity radius around the player (300 m by default) are asleep: they still exist and can be read, but do not move, walk, animate or detect, and game.with_tag, game.with_system and game.near leave them out unless {asleep = true}. The engine sends "monde.sommeil" {objets} and "monde.reveil" {objets} when they fall asleep and wake up; compare game.time() on waking to catch up the time they slept. The tag "toujours_actif" (or a system listed in the game setting alwaysActiveSystems) keeps an object awake everywhere. Without "Large world", everything is awake.
game.has_tag(id, tag)   game.add_tag(id, tag)   game.remove_tag(id, tag)
game.data(id) -> table or nil. The data an extension gave an object it made: a shop of a generated city (see Shops of the city), a traffic light or a speed limit sign (see Traffic lights of the city); nil for other objects.
game.distance(a, b)                    game.line_of_sight(a, b) -> bool, blocked by colliders. a and b: id or vector.

items.title: Moving and changing objects
items.text:
game.position(id) -> vector            game.set_position(id, v). Moves its collider too; teleports a character.
game.rotation(id) -> yaw               game.set_rotation(id, yaw)      game.face(id, pos_or_id)
game.bounds(id) -> low, high or nil. The box it fills in the world, what it contains included, measured on its models (hidden ones too): low.y is its foot, high - low its size. nil if it has no model. Never guess a model's size: measure it.
game.scale(id) -> vector               game.set_scale(id, number_or_vector). What it contains follows, along its own axes, as in the editor: their place, size and collider; the player put inside it moves with it, at their own size.
game.go_to(scene, arrival?). Goes to another scene of the game (a building's inside, a cave, the next level), after a fade to black, at the object named arrival (an empty marker placed there), or where the player stands in that scene. Scripts keep running and keep their variables; the scene left stays as it was. Sends "scene.change" {depuis, vers} once there. game.bring_along(id, true|false): that object (a companion) enters with the player, with its children, the next scene it is not in yet; place it near the player on "scene.change".
game.scene() -> name of the current scene    game.scenes() -> {names}. A scene's name is its file name, without folder or extension.
game.start_scene() -> the scene where the game starts for the player (the project's start scene), even when a test run starts from another scene; "" for a game of a single scene.
game.visible(id) -> bool               game.set_visible(id, bool)            game.set_solid(id, bool). false: it stops nobody any more, but stays visible (a tree falling).
game.set_color(id, vec(r, g, b)): its color (sRGB, 0 to 1): tints its model, and colors an engine shape ("builtin:cube"). Online, guests see it on objects made with game.spawn (and their copies), not on objects placed in the scene.
game.effect(id, kind, {duration=1, away_from=pos_or_id, after="destroy" or "hide"}?). The engine animates it around its base, whatever the model: "fall" (tips over, away from away_from), "collapse" (breaks into pieces of its own model that fall in a heap), "shrink", "burst" (breaks into pieces that fly out, bounce and fade), "shake" (trembles, then comes back). after="destroy" removes it at the end; after="hide" hides it and puts it back as it was, so it reappears upright when shown again. What it contains (its children) follows it, as with game.set_scale, and comes back with it.
game.effect(preset, pos_or_id, {size=1, color=vec, amount=1, duration, loop=false, direction=vec, light=true, light_intensity=1, light_shadows=true}?) -> handle. "feu", "explosion", "magie", "etincelles" and "impact" also give their own light (it follows the effect, flickers with a fire, grows with size, casts shadows for "feu", "explosion" and "magie"): light=false removes it, light_intensity multiplies it, light_shadows=false keeps it without shadows. It changes nothing in the game. Particles, simulated by the game (the same game gives the same particles) and drawn by the renderer. preset: "eclats" (chips; on an object they take its colour), "eclats_bois", "eclats_pierre", "poussiere" (dust spreading on the ground), "feu" (flames with a little smoke and sparks: a campfire at size 1, a torch at 0.4), "fumee", "explosion", "etincelles", "impact" (a hit: a flash, sparks, dust), "pluie", "neige" (falling from a disc around the place: size widens it), "magie", "faisceau" (a column of light rising straight from a point, on a soft glowing foot: marks loot from afar, by day and night; what passes in front hides it). On an object, a looping effect follows it. size scales the whole effect; amount the number of particles; duration in seconds (loop: 0 runs until game.stop_effect). direction: where chips or sparks fly (on an object, chips jump from the spot nearest the player, in its colour, toward the player). The report counts them under particles.
game.stop_effect(handle). It stops emitting; its particles end their life.
game.object_effect(id, on). Starts again (true) or stops (false) the effect an object carries with the "particules" system (a campfire lit or put out), and stops the looping effects scripts put on it.
game.decal(image, pos_or_id, {size=1, normal=vec(0,1,0), angle=0, opacity=1, color=vec(1,1,1), life=0}?) -> handle. Projects an image on the surfaces under it: a footprint, an impact, a stain, a puddle, a sign. image: "tache", "impact", "brulure", "flaque", "pas", "trace", or an image file of the project (PNG, JPEG). normal: the surface it lies on (up for the ground, a wall's outward direction). angle: radians around the normal. life: seconds before it fades, 0 to keep it. A game keeps a limited number of decals: the oldest disappears to make room. game.remove_decal(handle) removes one. The report counts them under decals.
game.instance_layer(name, model, {shadows=true, distance=400}?). Creates (or changes) a named instance layer: one model drawn in series at many places, without one object per copy (parked cars, street furniture, a distant crowd). Thousands of copies cost a few draws: the renderer groups them in 64 m squares and only redraws the squares that changed. Copies are drawn, not simulated: no collider, no script, not saved. distance: beyond it (m), a square is not drawn; the model's LOD versions are used if it has them.
game.set_instance(name, number, pos, {angle=0, scale=1, color=vec(1,1,1)}?). Puts or moves the copy with this number (a whole number of your choice, to change or remove it later). The model's lowest point sits on pos; angle: radians around the vertical. color multiplies the parts whose material name contains "carrosserie", "peinture", "teinte", "paint", "body" or "tint" (the car body, not its windows and tyres; color is sRGB, 0 to 1, like game.set_color), or the whole model if no part has such a name. game.remove_instance(name, number) -> removed? game.remove_instance_layer(name) -> removed?
game.parent(id) -> id or nil             game.children(id) -> {id}. Moving, turning, scaling, hiding, cloning or destroying a parent carries its children along.
game.clone(id, pos, {tags={...}, systems={module = {values}}}?) -> new id. Clones a template (usually hidden, with visible: false), which keeps tags, collider, animations and systems; the clone is visible. systems gives the copy alone systems of the game on top of the template's, with these values over each object's defaults (and what they require: a boutique brings interaction): a clerk copied from the pool becomes a merchant one uses. A system that is not in the game is an error. A vehicle (car, motorbike, boat) clones into another vehicle you can drive, with its wheels.
game.destroy(id). Removes it and its collider: a door or a wall can open that way. Not the player.
game.attach(id, holder, {bone=, offset=vec(0,0,0), rotation=vec(0,0,0), like=}?). Holds an object on a bone of an animated character (the player, another player, a character): an axe in the hand, a torch, a bag on the back. It follows the bone as the character walks, runs, strikes or chops, and no longer blocks anything. bone: a bone of the holder (read them with asset_info); without it, the bone that holds things, found by measuring the skeleton (game.hand_bone). The object is placed on the bone at rest, offset (metres) and rotation (degrees) counted along the bone's axes. like: an object already placed on a bone in the editor (a hidden axe set in the hand by hand): its exact place on its bone is reused. A copy held this way is not kept by game.save: put it back in the hand after game.load (the inventaire system does it for the item held).
game.detach(id). Lets go of it: it stays where it is, free.
game.hand_bone(id) -> bone name or nil. The bone of a character that holds things: a bone made for it under the right hand if the model has one (its name says slot, grip, weapon, prop...), else the right hand, found by its name (hand_r, RightHand, mixamorig:RightHand...) or by the shape of the skeleton. Nothing is assumed of a pack.
game.body_bone(id, part) -> bone name or nil. The bone of a part of a character's body, found by measuring its skeleton (names and shape, any pack): tete, cou, poitrine, bassin, epaule_gauche, epaule_droite, bras_gauche, bras_droit, avant_bras_gauche, avant_bras_droit, main_gauche, main_droite, cuisse_gauche, cuisse_droite, jambe_gauche, jambe_droite, pied_gauche, pied_droit. Never write a bone name of a pack: ask for the part.
game.attach(id, holder, {weapon=true, front="auto", upright=false, hand="right", hold="auto"}). Holds it like a weapon, measured on its model, nothing assumed of the file: the barrel is its longest side, its front (the muzzle) the thinnest end (front "+x"..."-z" forces it), its top the side away from the grip; the grip goes into the palm of the hand (found by the bone roles), the barrel along the fingers, the top on the thumb side. upright: held across the fist like a bow. melee=true: a melee weapon or tool (sword, dagger, axe, hammer, mace, pickaxe, spear, staff), measured on its profile along its longest side: the handle is the longest run of round, narrow sections; the hand grips it from its end away from the head, at three times its thickness (the middle of a sword grip, low on a long haft); the front is the side with the most material outside the handle (the head, the blade and its guard; a uniform staff: its thicker end, else +), front "+x"..."-z" forces it; the handle goes across the palm, the head or blade on the thumb side, the edge along the fingers; grip_at: the hand from the back (0) to the front (1). hand "left": the left hand. length: its real length in metres for a 1.8 m holder (along the barrel; a bow's height), scaled to the holder's measured height (reference lengths: pistol 0.20, revolver 0.28, submachine gun 0.6, assault rifle 0.9, shotgun 1.0, sniper rifle 1.15, crossbow 0.8, bow 1.45, sword 0.95, dagger 0.3); 0 keeps the object's size. The weapon is also fitted to the holder's hand: its measured grip at most a tenth taller than the palm is wide (measured on the finger bones), its magazine no longer than the hand; the smaller scale wins (low-poly models are stocky). size: a multiplier applied after that (1.5 for a cartoon weapon). grip_at, guard_at: where the hand and the other hand hold, as a fraction of the length from the back (0, the stock) to the muzzle (1), for a model the measure gets wrong (default: measured on the side silhouette: the rear-most part hanging under the weapon that slants back, behind the magazine; a stock is skipped). hold: "auto" (default: "bow" if upright, "two_hands" if the weapon is longer than 60 % of the holder's arm or has a stock, else "one_hand"), "one_hand", "two_hands", "bow"; the arms follow the animation clips played (no hold pose is built by the engine). pose = a clip name (such as "Pistol_Aim_Neutral"): the weapon is fitted on that clip's pose, its grip in the fist measured on the finger bones (middle, ring and little finger curled around it), its barrel toward the character's front, then turned by a few degrees around the fist if it would go through the trunk, head or arms, and slid against the palm; the pose is taken at the middle of the clip; hands = another clip giving the fingers (a pack whose hands have no finger bones, such as KayKit: "Pistol_Aim_Neutral" or "Idle_Torch_Loop" closes the fist). It stays fixed to the hand bone, so it follows the fist in every clip (play the holding clips with game.play_upper). offset and rotation apply on top. Given only weapon (and front, upright, hand), an object already held keeps its bone, offset, rotation and like: the inventaire system's model in hand stays as the user set it. A like placed by hand in the editor wins.
game.weapon(id, {front=, upright=}?) -> {muzzle, direction, up, grip, length, front, grip_height, grip_at, guard_at} or nil. The weapon of an object, measured on its model, in the world, as it is held now: the muzzle where a shot starts, the barrel's direction, its length in metres, the height of its grip (metres), where the grip and the handguard are (fractions of the length from the back). front: "fin" (the thinnest end), "mesure", "debout" or "reglage" (with "+prise", "+garde" when grip_at, guard_at are given).
game.hold_check(holder) -> {penetration, arms, palm, support, palm_width, wrist, support_wrist, support_twist, correction, correction_wanted, hold, penetration_bone, penetration_at, arms_bone, arms_at} or nil. Checks the weapon held by a character in its pose of the moment, in metres: how deep the weapon's vertices go into its trunk and head capsules (penetration: aim at 0.01 or less) and into its arm and forearm capsules (arms, hands excluded), the distance from the palm of the holding hand and of the support hand to the weapon's surface (-1: that hand does not hold it; aim at 0.015 or less), the width of its palm. wrist and support_wrist: how far each wrist bends, in degrees, between the forearm and the hand (aim at 35 or less; -1: no support hand). support_twist: the roll of the support forearm against the upper arm, in degrees (aim at 60 or less: more shows as a twisted elbow). correction: how far the engine moved the support hand or slid the weapon after the clip, in metres (never more than 0.02: the clip of the weapon's family makes the pose); correction_wanted: how far it would have needed (more than 0.02: the clip is wrong for this weapon). penetration_bone and arms_bone: the bone of the deepest capsule; penetration_at and arms_at: where the deepest vertex is along the weapon, 0 at the butt, 1 at the muzzle (-1: no contact).
game.hold_support(holder, target?, weight?) -> boolean. The support hand of a weapon held two-handed with game.attach {support = true}: after the clip, only that hand moves (two-bone arm IK) onto the real weapon in hand. target "handguard" (default: the measured handguard; out of reach, the most forward point under the weapon the arm reaches, in front of the magazine, never the magazine nor empty air), "magazine" (the bottom of the measured magazine, during a reload) or "none" (the clip's hand); weight from 0 (the clip's hand) to 1 (on the weapon). false if the holder holds no weapon that way.
game.spawn(file, position?) -> id.
