While it plays it takes the keyboard, mouse and gamepad: with skip, Escape, Enter, Space, a click, A or Start skip it. pause=true stops the world meanwhile. Starting another one replaces it.
When it ends (finished, skipped or stopped), the engine announces "video.fin" {video=handle, fichier=file, passee=true if skipped}, and also your event if given: game.on("intro_done", function(e) game.go_to("Village") end). This is how you chain what comes next.
game.hud_video(key, file, {x, y, w=0.3, h=0, loop=true, volume=1, group="effects", event=nil, alpha, align, parent}?) -> handle. A video inside the HUD (a screen in a menu, an animated portrait), like game.hud_image: h=0 keeps the video's real proportions. Calling it again with the same key and file keeps it playing; game.hud_remove(key) stops it. volume=0 for a silent one.
game.video_stop(handle)    game.video_playing(handle) -> bool    game.video_time(handle) -> seconds into the video, or nil once it ended (to time subtitles).
A video on an object of the world (a television) is not available yet.

items.title: Saving the player's progress
items.text:
game.save(slot, table) -> true, or false and a reason. slot: lowercase letters, digits, _ and -, such as "game1". The table holds text, numbers, booleans, vectors, lists and tables with text keys: the state of the game (level, position, items), not the whole world. 1 MB at most.
game.load(slot) -> table, or nil if there is none.     game.has_save(slot) -> bool     game.delete_save(slot)
Saves are kept between plays of the player's game. In game_run they stay in memory: your tries never touch the player's saves.
The systems keep their own state: game.save asks every script that defines on_save() for a table (its state: the inventory's items, the quests' progress, the shops' stocks, the dialogues' marks), and game.load gives each one back to its on_load(state). game.load called in on_start waits until every script has started. Do not save or re-add what a system keeps. The engine keeps the world too, in every scene visited: objects shown or hidden, solid or not, moved, turned, resized or pushed, destroyed (game.destroy) or copied (game.clone, game.pool), tags, lights, looping effects, decals, the active camera, timelines playing, joints, ragdolls, the vehicle driven, the player's speed and abilities. game.load puts each scene back as it was when saved; the player's own position is the game's to keep. Copies tagged population or population.<kind> (passers-by and cars of the dynamic population, with what they contain) are not saved: they are born again from the seed; a copy whose group carries population.garder (added by a script or a Trigger rule with game.add_tag) is saved and comes back. {systems = false} as the last argument of game.save or game.load leaves them out (to read a save without resuming it).
A script of your own can do the same: function on_save() return {opened = opened} end   function on_load(state) opened = state.opened end. The state follows the rules of game.save; it is stored under the script's name.

items.title: Ranged weapons
items.text:
Rays and projectiles (guns, bows, crossbows, grenades). The engine does the hard part; a script decides what a hit does (damage through sante.blesser). Melee stays with combat.basique: do not use these for a sword.

game.raycast(from, direction, distance=1000, {ignore=id or {ids}, tag=nil, water=false}?) -> hit or nil. The first thing on the line: a collider (fixed or moving), the terrain, or a character (the player, other players, enemies, any animated model). hit = {id (nil for the terrain), point, normal (facing the shooter; on the terrain, that of the very triangle hit), distance, part, bone, water}.
  water = true: the surface of water (seas, lakes, rivers of the terrain) stops the ray too: hit.water = true, id nil, point on the surface. Without it, a shot goes through water to the bottom. A ray that starts under water does not see the surface.
  A character is hit by its real body, bone by bone, measured on its model: a shot between the legs or above a shoulder misses. part is "tete" (head), "torse" (torso), "bras" (arms) or "jambes" (legs), found by measuring the skeleton (any model: Mixamo, Quaternius, Meshy...); bone is the bone's name. A character without a skeleton is hit by its capsule: part and bone are nil.
  Always ignore the shooter: {ignore = game.player()} (or the enemy that shoots). With tag, only objects carrying it count, and everything else is passed through (walls too): to find a target, not to shoot.
  Cheap: hundreds of rays per second are fine. A hitscan gun is one ray per shot from the muzzle (or the camera) along the aim.
game.projectile({from=, velocity=, gravity=1, radius=0.02, life=5, ignore=, model=nil, stick=false, stick_time=10, bounce=0, owner=nil, data=nil}) -> handle. A projectile the engine moves on every step under gravity (a factor of the scene's: 0 flies straight, 1 falls like a stone). Each step it sweeps its whole path: nothing goes through a thin wall, even at 900 m/s. It never hits its owner. life in seconds.
  model: a hidden object of the scene (an arrow, a rocket, a grenade); a copy of it follows the path, turned along its velocity (its longest side is its length, as placed in the scene), and goes back to a pool at the end. The projectile's point is the model's tip (its end furthest forward, measured on the model, wherever its pivot is): from is where the tip starts. Without model nothing is seen: an effect can follow it. Players who joined see the copies.
  stick=true: it stays planted in what it hits by its tip (a sixth of its length goes in, at most 12 cm; the rest sticks out) and follows it (a moving enemy, the bone of an arm), then disappears after stick_time seconds. bounce (0 to 1): it bounces off what it hits keeping that share of its speed, then rests on the ground until its life ends (a grenade: life is its fuse).
  Water: a projectile entering water announces "projectile.touche" with cible nil and eau = true (point on the surface: put game.effect("eclaboussure", e.point) there). It goes on, strongly slowed (a bullet stops within 2 m, an arrow within 1 m) and lighter: an arrow or a grenade sinks slowly to the bottom. A projectile without gravity stopped by water ends with raison "eau". To stop it at the surface instead: game.stop_projectile(e.projectile).
  data: a table given back with its events (the weapon, the damage). Events: "projectile.touche" {projectile, owner, cible (nil for the terrain and water), point, normale, partie, os, vitesse, eau, data} at each hit; "projectile.fin" {projectile, owner, raison, point, data} when it is gone: raison is "touche", "duree" (life over: explode the grenade here), "plantee", "cible_partie", "eau" or "arrete".
game.stop_projectile(handle) -> true if it was still flying. Its "projectile.fin" (raison "arrete") is announced on the next step.
Example: local hit = game.raycast(muzzle, aim, 200, {ignore = game.player()}) if hit and hit.id then game.emit("sante.blesser", {cible = hit.id, montant = hit.part == "tete" and 50 or 20, source = game.player()}) end

items.title: Ending and debugging
items.text:
game.finish("won" or "lost", message?, players?). Stops the simulation; the game shows the message and offers to play again. Only for a game that has an ending.
players (optional): each player's own end, { [player] = { outcome = "won" or "lost", titre = "1st", texte = "..." } }, a player being one of game.players(). Each player sees their own end screen: their titre (empty: Victory or Defeat from their outcome) and their texte (empty: message). Players left out see the game's end. Online, each guest receives their own.
game.log(...). Shown in the report of game_run.
game.time() -> seconds                 game.dt() -> seconds per step           game.step() -> step number

items.title: Example of the syntax, not a model for your game
items.text:
A dog that follows the player, and coins to collect.

local gold = 0
function on_start()
  for _, id in game.with_tag("dog") do
    game.character(id, {idle="Idle", walk="Walking_A"})
  end
end
function on_update(dt)
  local player = game.player()
  for _, id in game.with_tag("dog") do
    local to = game.position(player) - game.position(id)
    if vector.magnitude(to) > 3 then game.walk(id, vector.normalize(to) * 2) end
  end
  for _, id in game.near(player, 1.2, "coin") do
    game.destroy(id)
    gold += 1
  end
  game.hud_text("gold", "Gold: " .. gold, {x=0.02, y=0.07, align="left"})
end

items.title: Game systems
items.text:
Systems are ready-made game rules that ship with the editor. You activate them in the Developer mode's Systems panel, then place them on objects or folders: see The game's systems and settings. The agent can activate, place and set them for you.

System What it does Basic combat The player strikes ahead with a key, with the damage, reach and cooldown set on them. It hits what carries Health. For enemies that attack, add "Enemies". Building The player places pieces in the world: walls, floors, a campfire, any model. In building mode (B), a preview goes where they aim, on a grid or freely: with the view (the centre of the screen) when they play a character, with the cursor from above. A click places the piece and takes its cost from the inventory. The catalog (Tab) shows the pieces by category, with their picture and their cost; while placing, a panel tells the piece chosen, a sentence tells why it cannot go there, and a bar recalls the keys. A placed piece can be torn down, and gives back part of its cost. Chat The chat of games with several players: the T key (can be changed) opens a line, Enter sends it to everyone with the player's name, Escape cancels. Arrivals, departures and server messages are written in it. Admins type the server's commands in it (/kick Léa). This system sets all of it: the key, the commands' names and who may use them, the command sign, the anti-spam, the display and the texts. Without it, the chat works with its default settings. Chests What carries this system is a chest: used, it rolls its loot table (Loot module) and shows what it holds in a "Take all" window. Opened once for everyone, once per player, or once for the group straight into the bag, and refilled after a delay, or never. Companion The character carrying this system follows the player (or an object) at the set distance, runs to catch up, goes to a place while waiting for the player, flees, or waits where it is. A companion, a pet, a team member, a quest escort, a hostage, a runaway. It walks around walls with its own animations. Crafting Recipes that turn what the player carries into something else: three wood and two stones make an axe. One crafts bare-handed (C) or at a station: an object of the world, an imported model included, given a function the game defines (Workbench, Campfire, Oven, Forge...), with its levels to upgrade, its fuel and its queue. Day and night Time goes by: the sun rises, crosses the sky and sets, then night falls, darker and bluish, and the day comes back. Broad daylight is the scene's light as you set it. The chosen lamps light up at night, and a clock can show. With the scene's realistic sky, it follows the sky's time, which then gives all the light. Death and respawn What happens to the player at zero health: they fall (an animation of their character, if chosen), control nothing, see a death screen, then respawn (at the start, at the last respawn point or where they fell) or the game ends. Placed on an object, it makes it a respawn point. Needs Health. Decal An image projected on what lies under the object: a footprint, an impact, a stain, a puddle, a scorch mark, a sign painted on a wall. Create > Decal places an invisible box that carries it: the image covers its width and depth, and lies on the ground or the wall around its base. Dialogue A character who talks when used: their lines show one by one, with the player's answers as buttons. An answer leads to another line and can send an event, to which the Trigger system or a script reacts. Tests (an item carried, a mark, the talks already had, how far a quest is) choose what they say. Enemies What carries this system patrols, chases the player when it sees them, and hits them in reach, or shoots at them from afar (bullet, arrow, fireball), with its own values: an early skeleton and a boss have neither the same speed nor the same damage. They walk around walls. Equipment The player wears items in slots (head, chest, weapon, rings...) that you invent: their bonuses add to their characteristics, and they can show on the character. They wear an item by double-clicking it in the inventory or dragging it onto a slot. Fog volume A local fog, limited to an area: the mist of a valley, an undergrowth, a marsh, the smoke of a cave. Create > Fog volume places an invisible box that carries it: it fills the box (or the sphere inside it) and fades out towards its edges. With volumetric fog (High or Medium quality), it catches the sun's rays and shadows. Its kind "Glowing air (rays only)" (Create > Glowing air) is an almost invisible air that only shows the sun's rays, like the dust of a forest. Gathering What carries this system is a resource to gather: a tree to chop, a rock to mine, a bush to pick. Each use is a hit; at the last one, the resource gives what it holds to the inventory, disappears, and grows back if wanted. Healing What carries this system gives health back to the player: a spring to touch, or a potion picked up into the inventory and drunk with a key, each with what it gives. Health Health and armor for the objects that carry it: the player, a group of skeletons, a boss, each with its own values. Shows nothing: add "Health bar" to see it. Health bar Shows the player's health on screen, as a bar and in numbers. Interaction The player uses with a key what carries this system: a door, a merchant, a lever. Shows the prompt, and leaves the effect to the game. Interface The look of the game's menus, buttons, lists and text fields: the colors of backgrounds, text and what is selected, the text size, the rounding of corners, and an image theme (an interface pack) laid on each kind of element. Everything the game shows uses them, except what a script chooses itself. Inventory What carries this system can be picked up, and the player keeps it, grouped by kind. The game can give some, take some, and react to each change. Optionally, a weight: each item weighs, the player has a maximum load, and carrying too much slows them. Joint Links this object to another one, or to the world: a door on its hinges, a drawbridge, a wheel, a drawer, an elevator, a chandelier, a plank that gives way under a weight, a rope, a spring. With stops, a motor that opens and closes it, a breaking force. The object also carries Physics. Knowledge What the player knows how to do, and how they learn it: knowledges that unlock Crafting recipes, Building pieces or whatever the game wants. Each is learned in one or several ways: known from the start, by obtaining an item, by studying an item at a research table, with points in a tree, by reading a plan, from a character or a quest, by analysing objects of the world, or by crafting again and again. A window (K) shows what is known, what can be learned and how. Loot Loot tables, rolled when an enemy dies, a chest opens, on harvest, at the end of a quest or by the Trigger: what drops, with its rarity (color, glow), its random bonuses and its generated name for unique copies. On the ground, in the inventory, or in a "Take all" window. Map A minimap in a corner of the screen, the player in the middle, and a big map of the whole scene with the M key, zoomed and moved with the mouse or the gamepad (triggers and stick). What carries this system shows on it as a marker: a shape and a color, or an image, and its name; always, once discovered up close, or only as a quest objective. Merchants, characters who talk, the objectives of quests in progress and, with several players, the other players with their names are marked by themselves. The player places their own markers, ticks what they want to see, and can follow a compass at the top of the screen. Menu The title screen when the game starts, and the pause with Escape: Resume, Options (in sections: sound, display with the graphics and, for a translated game, the language, controls), Quit. The game stops while the menu is open, and it takes the look of the Interface system. A game with the Multiplayer setting also has Host and Join there. Needs What the player needs to live: hunger, thirst, tiredness, or whatever the game wants. Each need goes down over time; at zero, the player loses health. It goes back up by eating or drinking what the inventory holds, at a source in the world (a well, a bed) carrying this system, or through a Trigger rule. Each need can be switched off without losing its settings. Particle effect Particles coming out of the object: a campfire, a torch, smoke, sparks, magic, rain or snow around the player. Choose the effect, its size, its colour and its amount; it loops or plays once. For an effect on its own, Create > Particle effect places an invisible box that carries it. Passage What carries this system leads to another scene of the game: a door into a house, a cave entrance, a level's exit. One arrives at the chosen object of that scene, after a fade to black. Physics The objects that carry it fall, roll, slide, and the player pushes them by walking into them: crates, barrels, a ball, rocks. Those that come at the player push back, by their mass: a rock knocks them aside, a ball bounces off. In water, they float, sink or stay in between, and drift with the water. Their shape wraps the model, or follows its outline. Placed on a folder, it applies to everything inside. Population Pedestrians who appear on the pavements around the player, out of sight, walk along the streets and leave behind them. Nothing is written in the scene: only these settings. Pedestrians are copies of your model characters (hidden), reused over and over. Those who matter are never taken back: what a quest names until it ends, a companion, a pedestrian the player touched. They remember: a pedestrian who left comes back the same for a minute, a damaged car stays damaged, and what the player leaves waits for them. A gunshot or an explosion empties the street around: pedestrians flee, cars heading there stop. Progression Experience, levels, points and characteristics (ADR-038). Tracks (the character, cooking, woodcutting...) each with its curve; XP for defeated enemies, quests, what is crafted or gathered and any free rule; rewards at each level (points, bonuses, knowledges, items); characteristics to spend points on; required levels; the reputation with each faction of the game (a track that can go down, with its tiers: Hostile, Neutral, Friendly); an XP bar, "Level 5!" and the Character window (P). The host keeps everyone's progression. Quest log The game's quests and their steps, which move on by themselves: on an event (a Trigger rule, a Dialogue answer, an enemy defeated), a Dialogue mark, items carried or handed over, a place reached, a time held. A step can have other ways to end that lead elsewhere (branches), be optional, or fail for several reasons. A finished quest can give a reward; a quest can also fail (an event, a mark, time running out, an item lost, the player too far) or be abandoned from the log, then be taken up again from the start, at the failed step or at the last checkpoint. A quest can also be a template, with holes such as {lieu}: during the game, quetes.creer makes a real quest from it ("Delivery 3"), its holes filled by a script, a Trigger rule or a draw (a shop at random, at such a distance). A log opens with J, and a notification announces each new quest, each step and each end. Race A race without code, on top of the Round: numbered checkpoints (the system placed on objects), passed in order (a skipped checkpoint does not count), a finish line that only counts after the last one, laps, and the return to the last checkpoint passed (a fall, a "return" zone, a hazard, or a key for an overturned vehicle). Everyone sees their lap, their checkpoint and their place. Ragdoll An animated character that falls limp, like a rag doll: when it dies, under a hard hit, or when the Trigger asks. Its body is built on its own, from its skeleton. It can get back up, and its animation resumes smoothly. Ranged weapons Pistols, rifles, bows, crossbows and grenades: the player aims (right click), shoots (left click) and reloads (R). Each weapon is a row of settings: damage, head, fire rate, spread, recoil, magazine, ammunition. It hits what carries Health. Round How a game with several players unfolds, without code: everyone at their starting place, frozen during "3, 2, 1, Go!", a stopwatch or a time limit, an end (everyone arrived, a score reached, only one left standing), a ranking, and each player sees their own result. On time, on points or last one standing, alone or in teams, in one or several rounds. Placed on an object, it makes it a starting place. Shop A merchant who sells when used: a window with their items and prices, the player's money, and Buy and Sell buttons. The money is a kind of inventory item, such as "Gold". Shops of the city The city's shops become merchants: a clerk, taken from your characters by kind, stands behind the counter of each visitable shop near the player, and sells their kind's items through the Shop. Without a character set, no clerk. Sounds The game's noises, placed on what makes them: footsteps of characters (timed by their animation, and by the ground), hits given and taken, deaths, doors and chests being used, ambience of a fire or a river, an enemy's alert cry. Plus, for the whole game: music, fight music, pickups. Several files separated by commas: a random one each time. Stamina Placed on the player: running, jumping and striking tire them. Exhausted, they can only walk until they recover. Shows its bar under the health bar. Status effects Buffs and debuffs that last a while: poison, regeneration, haste, slowness, strength, weakness… Each one is set here, without code: its duration, its stacking, what it changes to values, its regular damage or healing. A row of icons shows the player those they carry. Trigger "When… then…" rules without writing code: when the player enters a zone, uses a lever, when a boss dies… then a door opens, a chest appears, the game is won. With ready-made actions, and those written for this game. Vehicle Turns a model into a car, a motorbike or a boat you drive. A car: its wheels (chosen among its children, found by their name, or taken out of a one-piece model) spin, steer and follow the suspension. A motorbike: it stays upright, leans into turns and can fall over. A boat: its hull floats, measured on its model, an engine pushes it and a rudder turns it; it runs aground on land. The player gets in and out with the Use control, drives with the game's controls, on the keyboard or the gamepad, and the camera follows. Zone A zone that announces who enters and who leaves it: a pressure plate, a trap, a finish line, a goal. Place it on an invisible box, of the size you want. The game decides what happens.

items.title: Companion
items.text:
The character carrying this system follows the player (or an object) at the set distance, runs to catch up, goes to a place while waiting for the player, flees, or waits where it is. A companion, a pet, a team member, a quest escort, a hostage, a runaway. It walks around walls with its own animations.

Identifier accompagner Version 2 Placed on objects yes

items.title: Settings for the whole game
items.text:
In the Systems panel (Developer mode), by opening the system's card.

None.

items.title: Settings on each object
items.text:
In the Properties of an object or folder that carries the system, Systems section. A folder passes its values on to what it contains; an object can change a value for itself only.

Setting What it does Name in code Type Default Limits or choices Follows the player from the start Ticked: it follows the player as soon as the game starts, without any event (a pet, a team member). Unticked: it waits for an order (accompagner.suivre, sent by a quest step, a Trigger rule or a script). suit_des_le_debut Yes or no no Distance kept (m) How many meters from the one it follows it stops. It does not stick to them or get under their feet. distance Number 2.5 from 0.5 to 50 Place near the one it follows Where it stands near the one it follows: behind them, or beside them (on their right, the next one on their left). items.title: What it announces
items.text: Event Fields Description accompagner.arrive cible (id), mode (text), lieu (id?), qui (id?) A Companion character arrived (Companion module): mode aller (it reached its place, lieu), suivre (it reached its destination lieu while following qui: the end of an escort) or fuir (it is far enough from what it fled, qui). accompagner.perdu cible (id), qui (id), mode (text), distance (number) A Companion character stayed further than its setting perdu_distance from the one it follows or waits for (qui) for perdu_apres seconds: announced once, until it is close again. mode: suivre or aller.

items.title: What it listens to
items.text: Event Fields Description accompagner.suivre cible (id?), qui (id?), lieu (id?) Ask a character carrying the Companion system to follow someone (Companion module, version 34): qui, a player or an object (missing: the one it followed last, else the host); lieu, a place where it announces accompagner.arrive once it gets there while following. cible: the character, by id or name; missing, every character carrying the system in the scene. "Follow me" after accompagner.attendre. accompagner.aller cible (id?), lieu (id?), qui (id?) Ask a Companion character to walk to a place (lieu, an object or a point; missing: its setting destination), waiting whenever the player qui is too far; there it announces accompagner.arrive and waits. cible: as for accompagner.suivre. accompagner.fuir cible (id?), de (id?), distance (number?), qui (id?) Ask a Companion character to run away from de (an object or a point; missing: qui, else the nearest player) until distance metres (missing: its setting distance_fuite); it announces accompagner.arrive once safe, and runs again if approached. cible: as for accompagner.suivre. accompagner.attendre cible (id?) Ask a Companion character to wait where it is ("Wait here"), remembering whom it followed: accompagner.suivre without qui makes it follow them again. cible: as for accompagner.suivre. accompagner.arreter cible (id?) Ask a Companion character to stop whatever it does and forget whom it followed. cible: as for accompagner.suivre. sante.mort cible (id), source (id?) An object's health reached zero. What happens next belongs to the game: the health module does nothing else, unless its setting says to destroy the object. sante.change cible (id), vie (number), max (number) An object's health changed, or is announced once when the game starts. vehicule.monte cible (id), qui (id), joueur (id?) A player got into a vehicle (an object carrying the vehicule system) and now drives it: qui and joueur are their character (the host's, or a guest's). Announced by the engine. vehicule.descendu cible (id), qui (id), joueur (id?) A player got out of a vehicle. Announced by the engine. scene.change depuis (text), vers (text) Sent by the engine once the player has arrived in another scene of the game (game.go_to, or a passage). Scripts keep running across scenes: this is when a module looks at the objects of the new scene.

items.title: Points a script can replace (game.override)
items.text:
The descriptions come from the code.

  • accompagner.place: function(default, infos) -> the point (a vector) where a following character stands near the one it follows. infos: cible (the character), chef (the one followed), rang (its rank among the characters following that one, from 1), nombre (how many follow it), reglages (its settings). The default places them behind the leader at their distance, spread by the setting ecart, or beside them with placement cote.

items.title: What the agent knows about this system
items.text: The text the agent reads before using this system.

items.title: Companion (accompagner)
items.text: Placed on a character (systems_attach): it follows the player or an object, walks to a place while waiting for the player, flees, or waits where it is. One system for every character who goes along: a pet, a team member, an escorted merchant, a hostage, a runaway. Use it whenever a character must follow, be escorted, lead the way or run away: never write that walking in a script. Never edit the system: set its values (systems_set), send its events, or override its hook with game.override.

items.title: How it walks
items.text:
• It walks with game.walk_to (the walkable areas, around walls, stepping aside from the other walkers) and plays its own idle, walk and run animations: animation_repos, animation_marche, animation_course (clip names of its model, read with animation_clips); empty, the clip whose name says idle, walk or run, if the model has one. Set them when the names say nothing. Never make up a pose.
  • Following: it stays at distance (2.5 m) behind the one it follows, walks at vitesse_marche, runs at vitesse_course when it is further than distance + rattrapage or when the leader runs, and stops close by. Several companions of the same player share the places without walking into each other: placement derriere (spread by ecart degrees) or cote (right, then left, then further back). A game rule of your own: override accompagner.place (returns the point; infos: cible, chef, rang, nombre, reglages).
  • Very far (teleport_distance, 50 m) or stuck with no way (teleport_bloque, 6 s), it reappears at its place near the leader (teleportation, on by default; untick it for an escort the player can abandon).
  • Vehicles: with vehicule monter (default) it gets in with the player it follows when they drive off, and gets out next to them. It sits at a free passenger seat of the car or motorbike (game.seat), visible, playing animation_assis (a clip of its model; empty: the looping clip whose name says sit or seat, not the one where it sits down or stands up). With no sitting clip, in a boat, with the vehicle's « conducteur » off or no free seat, it rides hidden: never a made-up pose. The seats are the vehicle's settings (passagers, passager_avant, passager_hauteur, passager_cote): move them there when it sinks in or floats, after a screenshot. a_pied: it stays outside and runs after them, or reappears near them.
  • Other scenes: autres_scenes compagnon (default: when suit_des_le_debut is on), oui (whenever it follows the player) or non. When the player it follows goes to another scene (game.go_to), it enters with them (game.bring_along) and reappears at its place near them, still following, with its orders. One it does not take along stays in its scene with its state, and is found there on coming back; its copy in a scene it has left is hidden. A scene already visited without it gets it too, with its children and its state; it is never there twice.
  • Dead (sante.mort on it), it does nothing until its health comes back.

items.title: Orders (events)
items.text:
Send them from a quest step's annonce_debut, a declencheur rule (action envoyer: the rule's object is the cible, the player who triggered it the qui), a dialogue answer's annonce, or a script. cible is the character (id or name); without cible, every character carrying the system in the scene obeys (a step's annonce_debut sends none: fine with one companion in the scene; with several, put a declencheur rule on the character, quand evenement, action envoyer accompagner.suivre).

  • accompagner.suivre {cible, qui, lieu?}: follow qui (a player or an object; missing: the one it followed last, else the host). With lieu (or its setting destination), it announces accompagner.arrive (mode suivre) once it gets there.
  • accompagner.attendre {cible}: "Wait here"; accompagner.suivre without qui is "Follow me" again. Bind them to a key (a control and a script line if game.pressed("wait") then game.emit("accompagner.attendre", {cible = ...}) end) or to dialogue answers (annonce).
  • accompagner.aller {cible, lieu?, qui?}: walk to lieu (an object, its name or a point; missing: destination), stopping to wait, facing the player, while qui is further than attente (10 m); within rayon_arrivee it announces accompagner.arrive (mode aller) and waits there.
  • accompagner.fuir {cible, de?, distance?}: run away from de (missing: qui, else the nearest player) until distance (missing: distance_fuite); safe, it announces accompagner.arrive (mode fuir), and runs again if approached.
  • accompagner.arreter {cible}: stop and forget the leader.
  • suit_des_le_debut on: it follows the host from the start, with no event (a pet, a team member).
  • accompagner.perdu {cible, qui, mode, distance}: further than perdu_distance (30 m) from the one it follows or waits for during perdu_apres seconds (10; 0 never). Once, until it is close again.

items.title: Recipes
items.text:
• An escort quest: on the merchant, the system with teleportation off and destination the village. The step {"sorte": "etape", "texte": "Escort the merchant to the village", "fin": "evenement", "fin_evenement": "accompagner.arrive", "fin_cible": "Merchant", "annonce_debut": "accompagner.suivre"} (or fin lieu on the village: then only the player needs to get there), under it {"sorte": "echec", "echec": "eloigne", "echec_lieu": "<merchant id>", "echec_rayon": 25} (abandoned) and {"sorte": "echec", "echec": "evenement", "echec_evenement": "sante.mort", "echec_cible": "Merchant"} (killed); the merchant carries sante. Keep echec_rayon below teleport_distance if teleportation stays on. Everything else is the Quest log's (resume, try again).
  • A guide who leads the way: annonce_debut accompagner.aller, the step fin evenement accompagner.arrive with fin_cible the guide.
  • A pet: suit_des_le_debut on, placement cote, its own clips; "Sit" and "Come" as accompagner.attendre and accompagner.suivre on two controls or dialogue answers.
  • A runaway thief: a declencheur rule quand entree on a zone around him, action envoyer accompagner.fuir; a quest step sante.mort or dialogue.fin on him.
  • Fighting at the player's side is not part of this system: a companion does not attack. (Planned: the ennemis system as an ally.)

items.title: Several players, saves, tests
items.text:
• One copy for the whole game: each character follows the player it is told (qui: the Trigger and quests give the player who caused it), the host otherwise.
  • Saves keep who follows whom, who waits, where it goes or what it flees, and in which scene it is; the engine keeps its position. Nothing to write.
  • Test with game_run: move the player, then read the character's position (game.position) and log accompagner.arrive, accompagner.perdu and the quetes.* events.

This page is generated automatically from the WorldMint code (modules/accompagner/module.json, modules/accompagner/AGENT.md, modules/events.json): it always matches the editor.

Called before an effect is put on a carrier (a player, an enemy, an object). options: {duree, source, cumul, genre, etiquettes = {tag = true}}. items.title: Status effects (alterations), shown as « Effets temporaires »
items.text:
Buffs and debuffs that last a while: poison, regeneration, haste, slowness, strength, weakness. Not to be confused with game.effect (visual particles and death effects): this module is game rules. Use it whenever something should help or hinder for a time: a potion of speed, a poisonous wolf, a poison zone, a blessing at an altar.

  • Every effect is data, in the game setting effets (modules_configure): an « effet » row (id, nom, description, icone an image of the project or empty, forme the icon the engine draws without any file when there is no image: auto (the preset's own, otherwise a disc with the name's initials), goutte, coeur, fleche_haut, fleche_bas, sablier, epee, epee_bas, etoile, losange, triangle, carre, or empty for the disc, genre bonus or malus, etiquettes comma separated tags, duree in seconds or 0 until removed, cumul refaire / cumuler (up to cumul_max) / ignorer, tic aucun / degats / soins with tic_montant every tic_intervalle s through the Health module, particule and teinte on the carrier), followed by its « valeur » rows (the editor indents them under their effect and names it: « Valeur modifiée de : Poison »): valeur (any value: vitesse_deplacement, degats, sante_max, charge_max, endurance_max, or one a script declares), ajout (+n) and pourcent (+%). Six presets come with it (poison, regeneration, rapidite, lenteur, force, faiblesse): change them rather than writing code.
  • Value bonuses go through game.stat_bonus with the source alteration:<id> and are removed exactly at the end. A value nobody declared is declared by the module (vitesse_deplacement acts on the player's speed, predicted the same on a guest). Enemies read degats and vitesse_deplacement too.
  • Where effects come from, without code: a Healing potion's effets (ids, comma separated; such a potion can be drunk at full health); an enemy's effet and effet_chance (%) on each hit or shot that lands; the Trigger actions appliquer_alteration and retirer_alteration (alteration: an id, or a tag to remove; porteur: joueur, the player who triggered it, or cible; alteration_duree, 0 for the effect's own).
  • From a script: game.status_apply(target, id, {duree, source, cumul}), game.status_remove(target, id or tag), game.status_has, game.status_list. Events: alterations.debut, alterations.fin (raison fin, retire, mort), alterations.tic. Death removes the carrier's effects.
  • Hook alterations.avant (game.override): refuse (return false) or change an effect before it applies: an immunity (options.etiquettes.poison), a shorter duration. alterations.texte changes the HUD's texts.
  • What the player sees: a row of slots (settings afficher, ancrage, x, y, taille; by default centered at the top, under the clock, couleur_bonus, couleur_malus) with the icon (the creator's image first, otherwise the drawn shape: a drop for poison, a heart for regeneration, an arrow for haste, an hourglass for slowness, a sword for strength, a sword pointing down for weakness; an effect without image or shape gets a disc with two initials), the time left and the stack (x2) under it; hovering shows a tooltip with the name and description. Both are screens delivered by the system, which the user restyles in the screen editor: « Effets en cours » (the list Rangée, one Case per effect in the order they were applied: Effets en cours/Case#1...; installed from the model of its ancrage) and « Infobulle d'effet » (Bulle, Nom, Description). Never draw effect icons yourself, and do not name another screen like these. Theme roles: panneau.effets, case.effet.bonus, case.effet.malus, infobulle.effet.

items.title: Several players
items.text:
The rule runs once, on the host, for every carrier. The row of icons is drawn by one copy per player and reaches that player. A player's effects and their time left are kept in their save and come back when it is loaded.

items.title: Joint
items.text:
Links this object to another one, or to the world: a door on its hinges, a drawbridge, a wheel, a drawer, an elevator, a chandelier, a plank that gives way under a weight, a rope, a spring. With stops, a motor that opens and closes it, a breaking force. The object also carries Physics.

Identifier articulation Version 1 Placed on objects yes Also activates Physics Also needs, on the same object Physics Run by the engine yes: the engine runs it itself, without a script

items.title: Settings for the whole game
items.text:
In the Systems panel (Developer mode), by opening the system's card.

None.

items.title: Settings on each object
items.text:
In the Properties of an object or folder that carries the system, Systems section. A folder passes its values on to what it contains; an object can change a value for itself only.

Setting What it does Name in code Type Default Limits or choices Kind of joint How the object moves relative to what holds it: it turns around an axis (hinge), slides along an axis (slider), turns every way around a point (ball), stays in place until it breaks (fixed), or hangs at the end of a rope or a spring. type Choice in a list Hinge: turns around an axis (door, drawbridge, wheel) charniere: Hinge: turns around an axis (door, drawbridge, wheel)glissiere: Slider: slides along an axis (drawer, elevator)boule: Ball: turns every way (chandelier, pendulum)fixe: Fixed: holds in place until it breaks (plank, beam)corde: Rope: never goes further than a lengthressort: Spring: comes back to its length Attached to (empty: the world) The object that holds it: the cart of a wheel, the furniture of a drawer. Empty, it is attached to the world, where it stands: a door in a wall, a chandelier on a ceiling. autre Object of the scene (empty) Attachment point Where it is held, on its model's box: a door on one side, a drawbridge at the bottom, a chandelier at the top, a wheel in the middle. The point and the axis show in the 3D view when the object is selected. pivot Choice in a list In the middle centre: In the middlegauche: On the left side (−X)droite: On the right side (+X)bas: At the bottomhaut: At the toparriere: At the back (−Z)avant: At the front (+Z) Axisshown only if Kind of joint is “Hinge: turns around an axis (door, drawbridge, wheel)” or “Slider: slides along an axis (drawer, elevator)” The object's axis it turns around (hinge) or slides along (slider). Vertical for a door or an elevator, sideways for a drawbridge or a wheel, front to back for a drawer. axe Choice in a list Vertical (Y): a door, an elevator vertical: Vertical (Y): a door, an elevatorcote: Sideways (X): a drawbridge, a wheelavant: Front to back (Z): a drawer Stop on one side (degrees, 0 or less)shown only if Kind of joint is “Hinge: turns around an axis (door, drawbridge, wheel)” How far it turns one way, from where it starts: 0 for a door that opens one way only, −90 for a swing door. −180 and 180: it turns endlessly, like a wheel. angle_min Number 0 from -180 to 0 Stop on the other side (degrees)shown only if Kind of joint is “Hinge: turns around an axis (door, drawbridge, wheel)” or “Ball: turns every way (chandelier, pendulum)” Hinge: how far it turns the other way, 90 for a door. Ball: how far it swings from where it starts, in every direction; 180: no limit. angle_max Number 90 from 0 to 180 Travel backwards (m, 0 or less)shown only if Kind of joint is “Slider: slides along an axis (drawer, elevator)” How far it slides towards the back of the axis, in meters, from where it starts: 0 for a drawer closed at the start. course_min Number 0 from -100 to 0 Travel forwards (m)shown only if Kind of joint is “Slider: slides along an axis (drawer, elevator)” How far it slides towards the front of the axis, in meters: 0.5 for a drawer, 5 for a one-floor elevator. course_max Number 1 from 0 to 100 Length (m, 0: the starting one)shown only if Kind of joint is “Rope: never goes further than a length” or “Spring: comes back to its length” The length of the rope or spring, in meters. 0: the distance between the object and what holds it at the start. Attached to the world, the rope hangs from a point above the attachment point. longueur Number 0 from 0 to 100 Springiness (0: rigid)shown only if Kind of joint is “Hinge: turns around an axis (door, drawbridge, wheel)”, “Slider: slides along an axis (drawer, elevator)” or “Spring: comes back to its length” 0: the stops are hard. Above, they cushion like a spring: 1 bounces softly, 5 is firm. For a spring, its stiffness: 2 by default. rigidite Number 0 from 0 to 20 Motorshown only if Kind of joint is “Hinge: turns around an axis (door, drawbridge, wheel)” or “Slider: slides along an axis (drawer, elevator)” What makes it move on its own. To a position: it goes to its stop (open) or back to the other (closed), and the Trigger opens and closes it. At a steady speed: it turns or slides without stopping. Without a motor, the Trigger can still open and close it. moteur Choice in a list None: it moves when pushed aucun: None: it moves when pushedposition: To a position: open or closedvitesse: At a steady speed: a wheel, a mill Speed (degrees or meters per second)shown only if Kind of joint is “Hinge: turns around an axis (door, drawbridge, wheel)” or “Slider: slides along an axis (drawer, elevator)” ; shown only if Motor is “At a steady speed: a wheel, a mill” The motor's speed: in degrees per second for a hinge (360: one turn per second), in meters per second for a slider. Negative, the other way. vitesse Number 90 from -3600 to 3600 Motor strengthshown only if Kind of joint is “Hinge: turns around an axis (door, drawbridge, wheel)” or “Slider: slides along an axis (drawer, elevator)” The motor's strength (in newtons, or newton-meters for a hinge). The higher, the heavier the object it moves, and the more it resists a push: 500 for a door, 20,000 for an elevator carrying the player. force Number 500 from 0 to 1 000 000 Open at the start (motor to a position) With a motor to a position: it starts open (at its stop) instead of closed. The Trigger then opens and closes it. ouvert Yes or no no Breaking force (N, 0: unbreakable) Beyond this force, in newtons, the joint gives way and the object falls: a rotten plank 800 (the player breaks it by jumping on it), a footbridge 5,000. 0: it never breaks, except through the Trigger. rupture Number 0 from 0 to 10 000 000

A joint (an object carrying the articulation system) gave way: pulled harder than its breaking force, or broken by the Trigger or game.joint_break. autre is the object it was attached to, missing when attached to the world. items.title: Joint (articulation)
items.text:
Links an object to another one, or to the world, with a real physics joint: a door on its hinges, a drawbridge, a wheel on a cart, a drawer, an elevator, a chandelier, a pendulum, a plank that gives way, a rope, a spring. The engine runs it, without a script. The object also carries physique (added with it): give it a masse.

  • systems_attach it on the moving part (the door, not the wall), then systems_set:
  • type: charniere (turns around an axis), glissiere (slides along an axis), boule (turns every way around a point), fixe (holds until it breaks), corde (never further than a length), ressort (comes back to its length).
  • autre: the object that holds it (the cart of a wheel, the furniture of a drawer); empty: the world, where it stands.
  • pivot: where it is held on its model's box: centre, gauche (−X), droite (+X), bas, haut, arriere (−Z), avant (+Z). No coordinates: a door is held on one side, a drawbridge at the bottom, a chandelier at the top, a wheel in the middle.
  • axe (charniere, glissiere): vertical (a door, an elevator), cote (X: a drawbridge, a wheel), avant (Z: a drawer).
  • Stops: angle_min (−180 to 0) and angle_max (0 to 180) in degrees for a hinge, from where it starts (−180 and 180: it turns endlessly); angle_max is the swing cone of a boule (180: free); course_min / course_max in meters for a slider. longueur for a rope or spring (0: the starting distance; attached to the world, it hangs from that far above the pivot). rigidite: 0 hard stops, above: springy (a spring's stiffness).
  • Motor (charniere, glissiere): moteur aucun (moves when pushed), position (holds closed, goes to its far stop when opened), vitesse (turns or slides all the time at vitesse, degrees or meters per second); force its strength (500 for a door, 20000 for an elevator that carries the player); ouvert starts it open.
  • rupture: the force in newtons beyond which it breaks (800: a rotten plank the player breaks by landing on it; 0: never).
  • Open and close without code: a declencheur rule with action ouvrir or fermer and cible the door (a lever with interaction, a zone in front of the door). Action casser breaks it. A rule quand: casse reacts when it breaks.
  • Scripts: game.joint_open(id), game.joint_close(id), game.joint_break(id), game.joint(id) (kind, position: degrees or meters, broken). The engine announces articulation.cassee (cible, autre).
  • Examples: a door {"type": "charniere", "pivot": "gauche", "axe": "vertical", "angle_max": 100, "moteur": "position", "force": 800} with masse 30; a drawbridge {"type": "charniere", "pivot": "bas", "axe": "cote", "angle_min": -90, "angle_max": 0, "moteur": "position", "ouvert": true}; a chandelier {"type": "boule", "pivot": "haut", "angle_max": 30}; an elevator {"type": "glissiere", "axe": "vertical", "course_max": 5, "moteur": "position", "force": 20000} with masse 200.
  • Check with game_run: joints gives each one's angle or position now and the range it reached, and whether and when it broke.

items.text:
The engine runs it once for the whole game: joints are shared.

items.title: Health bar
items.text:
Shows the player's health on screen, as a bar and in numbers.

Identifier barre_de_vie Version 4 Placed on objects no Also activates Health

items.title: Settings for the whole game
items.text:
In the Systems panel (Developer mode), by opening the system's card.

Setting What it does Name in code Type Default Limits or choices Horizontal position (0 to 1) Where the bar starts, from left to right: 0 at the left edge of the screen, 1 at the right edge. 0.02 puts it almost against the left edge. x Number 0.02 from 0 to 1 Vertical position (0 to 1) Where the bar sits, from top to bottom: 0 at the top of the screen, 1 at the bottom. 0.03 puts it at the very top. y Number 0.03 from 0 to 1 Width (share of the screen) The length of the full bar, as a share of the screen width: 0.25 is a quarter of the screen. largeur Number 0.25 from 0.02 to 1 Height (share of the screen) The thickness of the bar, as a share of the screen height: 0.025 gives a thin bar, 0.05 a thick one. The numbers grow with it. hauteur Number 0.025 from 0.005 to 0.2 Color (#RRGGBB) The color of the remaining health, written #RRGGBB (red, green, blue in hexadecimal), for example #d94848 for a soft red. A badly written color gives red. couleur Text #d94848 Show the numbers Writes the remaining and maximum health to the right of the bar, for example "75 / 100". chiffres Yes or no yes

items.title: Events
items.text: The descriptions come from the code.

items.title: What it listens to
items.text: Event Fields Description sante.change cible (id), vie (number), max (number) An object's health changed, or is announced once when the game starts.

items.title: What the agent knows about this system
items.text: The text the agent reads before using this system.

items.title: Health bar (barre_de_vie)
items.text:
Shows the player's health on screen, from the health module (sante), which it activates if missing. The player must carry sante (systems_attach on the player): otherwise the bar never shows. It does nothing else, and is not placed on objects.

  • It delivers the screen « Barre de vie » (shapes Fond, Barre, Chiffres; HUD keys Barre de vie/Barre...), which the user restyles in the screen editor; the script shows it and fills it. Never draw a health bar yourself, and do not name another screen « Barre de vie ».
  • Settings: position, width and height as fractions of the screen (they move and size the screen's shapes), color as #RRGGBB, and whether the numbers show (off: the shape Chiffres is hidden).
  • It shows the player only. For a bar above enemies, say it is not available yet.
  • A full bar that never moves usually means nothing in the game sends sante.blesser to the player.

items.title: Several players
items.text:
One copy per player: each player sees their own health bar (the health of their own character, sante.change with cible = that player).

This page is generated automatically from the WorldMint code (modules/barre_de_vie/module.json, modules/barre_de_vie/AGENT.md, modules/events.json): it always matches the editor.

items.title: Needs
items.text:
What the player needs to live: hunger, thirst, tiredness, or whatever the game wants. Each need goes down over time; at zero, the player loses health. It goes back up by eating or drinking what the inventory holds, at a source in the world (a well, a bed) carrying this system, or through a Trigger rule. Each need can be switched off without losing its settings.

Identifier besoins Version 6 Placed on objects yes Also activates Health Also needs, on the same object Interaction

items.title: Settings for the whole game
items.text:
In the Systems panel (Developer mode), by opening the system's card.

Setting What it does Name in code Type Default Limits or choices The player's needs One row per need, with its name, its reserve, what it loses per minute and what happens at zero. Hunger and thirst by default; add tiredness, cold, or remove what your game does not want. Untick "On" to switch a need off without losing its settings. besoins List of “Need” [{'nom': 'Faim', 'actif': True, 'max': 100, 'baisse': 2, 'course': 0, 'degats': 1, 'vide': 'rien', 'couleur': '#d9893b'}, {'nom': 'Soif', 'actif': True, 'max': 100, 'baisse': 3, 'course': 1, 'degats': 1, 'vide': 'rien', 'couleur': '#3b9ad9'}] one line per “Need”: its fields What can be eaten and drunk The inventory items that raise a need when the player uses them up: a click on their slot in the inventory window. One item can have several rows: a watermelon feeds and quenches. aliments List of “Food” (empty) one line per “Food”: its fields A click in the inventory uses up a food Ticked: in the inventory window (I), a click on a food's slot eats or drinks it. Unticked: only through the event besoins.consommer, from a script or a Trigger rule. manger_fenetre Yes or no yes Use nothing up when the need is full Ticked: a food whose needs are all full is not eaten, and does not disappear for nothing. rien_si_plein Yes or no yes Warning level (%) Below this share of the reserve, the bar blinks and the need is announced (besoins.bas): a sound, a message. 0: never a warning. alerte Number 25 from 0 to 100 Health regained per second, when satisfied The health points the player regains each second while all their needs are above the level below: well fed, they heal. 0: never. soin_rassasie Number 0 from 0 to 100 000 Satisfied above (%) The share of their reserve that every need must be above for the player to regain health. seuil_rassasie Number 80 from 0 to 100 Player speed when a need slows them down The share of their usual speed the player keeps while a need set to "walks slower" is at zero: 0.6 keeps 60 %. lenteur Number 0.6 from 0.1 to 1 Show the bars Shows one bar per need on screen, with its name, under the health bar. Untick it if your game shows them its own way (a drawn screen, with besoins.change). afficher Yes or no yes Horizontal position (0 to 1) Where the bars start, from left to right: 0 at the left edge of the screen, 1 at the right edge. 0.02 lines them up with the health bar. x Number 0.02 from 0 to 1 Vertical position of the first (0 to 1) Where the first bar sits, from top to bottom: 0 at the top of the screen, 1 at the bottom. The next ones line up under it. y Number 0.1 from 0 to 1 Width (share of the screen) The length of a full bar, as a share of the screen width. largeur Number 0.18 from 0.02 to 1 Height (share of the screen) The thickness of a bar, as a share of the screen height. hauteur Number 0.014 from 0.005 to 0.2 Gap between two bars The distance from one bar to the next, as a share of the screen height. ecart Number 0.03 from 0.005 to 0.3

items.title: The fields of each “Need”
items.text:
In the Properties, each “Need” has its own numbered frame; Add: Need adds one, the cross removes it. A field only appears when it is useful: under its name, the table says when.

Setting What it does Name in code Type Default Limits or choices Name The name the player sees next to its bar, such as "Hunger", "Thirst" or "Tiredness". Foods and sources name it exactly as written here. nom Text (empty) On Ticked: the need counts in the game. Unticked: it is switched off, without losing its settings: no bar, it does not go down and never hurts; the foods and sources that raise it do nothing (the prompt says so, the food stays in the inventory). To try the game without tiredness, for example. actif Yes or no yes Full reserve The value of the need when the player is satisfied, at the start of the game. Losses and what foods give are compared with it: with 100 and a loss of 2 per minute, it takes 50 minutes to reach zero. max Number 100 from 1 to 100 000 Loss per minute What the need loses per minute of play, standing still or walking. 0: it never goes down by itself (tiredness that only comes from running). baisse Number 2 from 0 to 100 000 Extra loss while running (per minute) What the need loses on top per minute of running: running makes one thirsty and tired. 0: running changes nothing. course Number 0 from 0 to 100 000 Health lost per second at zero The health points the player loses each second while this need is at zero. 0: it does not kill, only the effect chosen below. degats Number 1 from 0 to 100 000 At zero, also What also happens while the need is at zero, until it goes back up: nothing, a slower walk (hunger), or no more running or jumping (tiredness). vide Choice in a list Nothing more rien: Nothing morelent: The player walks slowersans_course: The player can no longer run or jump Color of its bar The color of this need's bar on screen: orange for hunger, blue for thirst, purple for tiredness. couleur Color #d9893b

items.title: The fields of each “Food”
items.text:
In the Properties, each “Food” has its own numbered frame; Add: Food adds one, the cross removes it. A field only appears when it is useful: under its name, the table says when.

Setting What it does Name in code Type Default Limits or choices Item (kind of inventory item) The kind of item used up, as the inventory stores it, such as "Apple", "Flask" or "Cooked meat". One goes each time. objet Text (empty) Need raised (its name) The name of the need it raises, written as in the list of needs: "Hunger" or "Thirst". besoin Text (empty) By how much What it gives back to the need, without going past the full reserve: 30 out of 100 for an apple, 60 for a meal. montant Number 30 from 0 to 100 000 Health given too The health points it also gives back, like a hot meal. 0: only the need. vie Number 0 from 0 to 100 000

items.title: Settings on each object
items.text:
In the Properties of an object or folder that carries the system, Systems section. A folder passes its values on to what it contains; an object can change a value for itself only.

Setting What it does Name in code Type Default Limits or choices Need raised when used (its name) An object of the world carrying this system raises this need when the player uses it (E): "Thirst" for a well or a river, "Tiredness" for a bed. Written as in the list of needs. source_besoin Text (empty) By how much, each use What one use gives back to the need, without going past the full reserve: 100 fills it all. source_montant Number 100 from 0 to 100 000 Prompt text (Drink, Sleep… empty: Interaction's) The word of the prompt in front of the source, such as "Drink" or "Sleep". Empty: the usual text of the Interaction system. source_verbe Text (empty) Wait between two uses (s) The time, in seconds of play, before the source works again: a well that fills up, a bed one cannot use again at once. 0: always ready. source_recharge Number 0 from 0 to 86 400 Hours that pass when used (Day and night system) With the Day and night system, using it moves the clock on that much: 8 for a night in a bed. 0: time does not jump. source_heures Number 0 from 0 to 24

items.title: Events
items.text: The descriptions come from the code.

items.title: What it announces
items.text: Event Fields Description besoins.change besoin (text), valeur (number), max (number) A need of the player (hunger, thirst, tiredness...) changed by a whole point, or is announced once when the game starts. besoin is its name as written in the needs list (original language). besoins.bas besoin (text), valeur (number), max (number) A need went below the warning level of the besoins system (its bar blinks): a sound, a message, a quest hint. besoins.vide besoin (text) A need reached zero: from now on the player loses health each second (and maybe walks slower or cannot run), until it goes back up. besoins.consomme objet (text) The player ate or drank one item of the inventory (its foods list): it has been taken from the inventory and its needs raised. besoins.source cible (id), besoin (text), montant (number) The player used a source of the world carrying the besoins system (a well, a river, a bed): besoin went up by montant. sante.blesser cible (id), montant (number), source (id?) Ask the health module to remove health from an object. sante.soigner cible (id), montant (number) Ask the health module to give health back, up to its maximum. inventaire.retirer objet (text), quantite (number), fiche (number?) Ask the inventory to remove items, such as a payment. Answered by inventaire.change, or inventaire.manque if there are not enough. For a kind with unique copies (version 15): fiche removes that copy, otherwise the first ones; their records are destroyed. jour_nuit.avancer heures (number) Ask the day and night system to move the clock on by heures (a night in a bed: 8). Every hour, sunrise and sunset crossed are announced in order.

items.title: What it listens to
items.text: Event Fields Description besoins.remplir besoin (text), montant (number) Ask the besoins system to raise a need by its name, without using anything up: a meal at an inn, a Trigger rule, a script. besoins.consommer objet (text) Ask the besoins system to eat or drink one item of the inventory, as a click on its slot would: nothing happens if it is not a food or the player has none. inventaire.change objet (text), quantite (number), total (number), chargement (boolean?), fiche (number?), jete (boolean?) The quantity of an item changed. total is the new quantity. chargement is true when a saved game gives the items back (game.load): nothing was picked up. For a unique copy (version 15), objet is its kind, fiche its record's number, total how many of that kind. With several stacks of a kind (version 21), total counts all of them; jete is true when a slot was dropped on the ground. inventaire.choisi objet (text), total (number), fiche (number?), double (boolean?), case (text?) The player clicked a slot of the inventory window: objet is the kind of item, total how many they carry. What it does belongs to the game: eat, equip, read. case (version 21) is the slot's key ("Wood~2" for a second stack). interaction.utiliser cible (id), joueur (id) The player used the object in reach: a door, a merchant, an item to pick up. Whoever owns that object decides what it does. sante.change cible (id), vie (number), max (number) An object's health changed, or is announced once when the game starts. langue.change langue (text) Sent by the engine when the player changes the game's language (game.set_language, the Menu options). A module redraws what it already shows: its texts go through game.t and game.language.

items.title: Points a script can replace (game.override)
items.text:
The descriptions come from the code.

  • besoins.baisse: function(default, besoin, par_minute) -> how much this need goes down per minute right now (number). The default is its baisse setting, plus its course setting while the player runs. To make thirst fall faster in the desert or at noon, hunger slower while sleeping.

items.title: What the agent knows about this system
items.text: The text the agent reads before using this system.

items.title: Needs (besoins)
items.text:
Hunger, thirst, tiredness, or any need the game wants: each one goes down with the time of play, and at zero the player loses health. Add it once with modules_add (it needs sante: put sante on the player, and barre_de_vie to show the health). Use it whenever the user talks about eating, drinking, starving, sleeping or survival: never write a hunger script.

  • The needs (game setting besoins, modules_set): a list, one row per need, in the user's language. Hunger and thirst by default; add « Fatigue » or anything else, remove what the user did not ask for. Each row: nom (shown next to its bar, and how foods and sources name it), actif (true by default; false switches the need off without losing its settings: no bar, it does not fall, never hurts, and its foods and sources do nothing, saying so; a row without it is on), max (the full reserve, the value at the start), baisse (lost per minute of play), course (lost on top per minute of running), degats (health lost per second at zero; 0: it never kills), vide (also at zero: rien, lent (the player walks at lenteur of their speed), sans_course (no running nor jumping: tiredness)), couleur (its bar).
  • Tiredness (« Fatigue ») is a row of its own, like hunger: add it only when the user wants sleep to matter (baisse low or 0, course for running, vide sans_course, degats 0 so it never kills), and set actif false when they want to try the game without it, rather than deleting the row. Ask, or offer, how energy comes back; any mix works: sleep in a bed (a source: source_besoin « Fatigue », source_verbe « Dormir », source_heures 8 with jour_nuit), a food or drink (an aliments row: « Café », besoin « Fatigue »), or anything else through a declencheur rule with the action remplir_besoin (besoin « Fatigue », montant): resting by a campfire (a zone around it, quand entree, fois chaque), sitting on a bench (quand utilise), a prayer at an altar. Never a script for that.
  • Foods (game setting aliments): which inventory items raise which need, by how much (objet, besoin written as the need's nom, montant), and vie (health given too). One row per need an item raises: a watermelon feeds and quenches. The player eats with a click on its slot in the inventory window (I), as long as manger_fenetre is on; rien_si_plein keeps a food when its needs are full. The items themselves come from inventaire (picked up), collecte (gathered: berries from a bush), fabrication (cooked at a campfire) or boutique.
  • Sources in the world: place besoins on an object (systems_attach; interaction comes with it) and set source_besoin (the need's nom), source_montant, source_verbe (the prompt: « Boire », « Dormir »), source_recharge (seconds before it works again), source_heures (hours that pass, with jour_nuit: 8 for a bed). A well, a river bank, a bed, a spring.
  • Dosage: with baisse 2 per minute and max 100, hunger reaches zero after 50 minutes of play. Say the numbers to the user and check them with game_run (a long segment doing nothing): the player must have time to find food, and doing nothing must end badly if the user asked for a survival game.
  • Game settings: alerte (% under which the bar blinks and besoins.bas is sent), soin_rassasie and seuil_rassasie (health regained per second while every need is above that %), afficher and the bars' place (x, y, largeur, hauteur, ecart: they line up under the health bar by default).
  • Events announced: besoins.change (besoin, valeur, max), besoins.bas, besoins.vide (besoin), besoins.consomme (objet), besoins.source (cible, besoin, montant). Send besoins.remplir (besoin, montant) to raise a need without using anything (a meal at an inn; from a declencheur rule, use its action remplir_besoin, which sends it with these fields), besoins.consommer (objet) to eat an item from a script or a declencheur rule.
  • Change how fast a need falls from your own script, never the module's: game.override("besoins.baisse", function(default, besoin, par_minute) if besoin == "Soif" and game.has_tag(game.ground(game.player()) or "", "desert") then return par_minute * 2 end return default(besoin, par_minute) end).
  • Saved games: game.save keeps every need and the sources' waiting time; game.load gives them back. Nothing to write.
  • What it shows is delivered as screens, which the user restyles in the screen editor: « Besoins » (the list Barres, one row per need that is on: Fond, Barre and Nom; rows are numbered among the needs that are on: Besoins/Barre#1 is the first bar shown) and « Message des besoins » (Message: a need switched off). Never draw need bars yourself, and do not name another screen like these.
  • Testing: in game_run, read the report's hud (Besoins/Barre#1, Besoins/Nom#1...) and the besoins.* events; a script listening to sante.change shows the health lost at zero.

items.title: Several players
items.text:
One copy per player: each player has their own needs, bars, food and penalties; a source (a well, a bed) refills the player who uses it. A bed that moves the clock on (jour_nuit.avancer) moves it on for everyone: the day is shared.
