items.title: Shop
items.text:
A merchant who sells when used: a window with their items and prices, the player's money, and Buy and Sell buttons. The money is a kind of inventory item, such as "Gold".

Identifier boutique Version 10 Placed on objects yes Also activates Interaction, Inventory Also needs, on the same object Interaction

items.title: Settings for the whole game
items.text:
In the Systems panel (Developer mode), by opening the system's card.

Setting What it does Name in code Type Default Limits or choices Stop the game while shopping Ticked: the world stops while the shop window is open, enemies included. Unticked: the game goes on behind it. pause Yes or no yes Width of the window (old) No longer used: the window is now the screen "Boutique". To widen it, drag the handle of its shape "Fenêtre" (and of the columns of "Article") in the screen editor. Kept for the games that had set it; the tab of another system (the Equipment's services) still receives it. largeur Number 0.55 from 0.3 to 1

items.title: Settings on each object
items.text:
In the Properties of an object or folder that carries the system, Systems section. A folder passes its values on to what it contains; an object can change a value for itself only.

Setting What it does Name in code Type Default Limits or choices Name of the shop (empty: the object's name) The title of the window, such as "Bram's forge". Empty: the object's name in the scene. nom Text (empty) Money (a kind of inventory item) The kind of item used to pay, as the inventory stores it, such as "Gold" or "Coin". The player picks it up or receives it like any item. monnaie Text Or Opens when the player uses it (E) Ticked: the shop opens when the player uses the merchant. If they also carry a Dialogue, they talk first, and their last line offers "Show me your goods". Unticked: only through the event boutique.ouvrir, from a zone or a script. a_l_usage Yes or no yes What they sell The shop's items, in the order they show: the kind of item, how many one purchase gives, the price, the stock, and what the merchant pays if the player sells one to them. articles List of “Item” (empty) one line per “Item”: its fields

items.title: The fields of each “Item”
items.text:
In the Properties, each “Item” has its own numbered frame; Add: Item adds one, the cross removes it. A field only appears when it is useful: under its name, the table says when.

Setting What it does Name in code Type Default Limits or choices Item (kind of inventory item) The kind of item sold, as the inventory stores it, such as "Sword" or "Apple". Items of the same kind add up in the inventory. objet Text (empty) They sell it Ticked: the item can be bought, with a Buy button. Unticked: the merchant only buys it back (then set the buy-back), like wolf pelts they collect. a_vendre Yes or no yes How many per purchase How many one purchase gives: 10 for a quiver of 10 arrows. quantite Number 1 from 1 to 1 000 000, as a whole number Price How much money one purchase costs. 0: it is free. prix Number 10 from 0 to 1 000 000, as a whole number Stock at the start (0: no limit) How many purchases of this item the merchant can make before running out: 1 for a unique sword. 0: they never run out. What the player sells back to them adds to it. stock Number 0 from 0 to 1 000 000, as a whole number Buy-back: what they pay for one (0: they buy none) The price the merchant pays when the player sells them one of this item: a Sell button appears. 0: they buy none, and nothing shows. rachat Number 0 from 0 to 1 000 000, as a whole number

items.title: Events
items.text: The descriptions come from the code.

items.title: What it announces
items.text: Event Fields Description boutique.achat cible (id), objet (text), quantite (number), prix (number), monnaie (text) The player bought an item in a shop: cible is the merchant, quantite how many they received, prix what they paid, in monnaie (a kind of inventory item). The inventory has already changed. boutique.vente cible (id), objet (text), quantite (number), prix (number), monnaie (text) The player sold an item to a merchant (cible): quantite how many they gave, prix what they received, in monnaie. The inventory has already changed. boutique.onglet joueur (id), onglet (text), cible (id?), parent (text?), largeur (number?) The shop window opened another module's tab (onglet, its key; parent, the empty panel to fill; largeur, the window's width), or left it (onglet empty). The module whose tab it is fills the panel. inventaire.ajouter objet (text), quantite (number), joueur (id?), fiche (number?) Ask the inventory to add items, such as a reward. Answered by inventaire.change, or inventaire.plein. With several players, joueur says whose bag; without it, the player whose action is being handled, or every player. inventaire.retirer objet (text), quantite (number), fiche (number?) Ask the inventory to remove items, such as a payment. Answered by inventaire.change, or inventaire.manque if there are not enough. For a kind with unique copies (version 15): fiche removes that copy, otherwise the first ones; their records are destroyed.

items.title: What it listens to
items.text: Event Fields Description interaction.utiliser cible (id), joueur (id) The player used the object in reach: a door, a merchant, an item to pick up. Whoever owns that object decides what it does. boutique.ouvrir cible (id), onglet (text?), joueur (id?) Ask the shop system to open the shop of cible, as if the player had used it: from a dialogue answer, a trigger, a script. onglet opens it on another module's tab (equipement.atelier: the services). It opens for joueur only; without joueur, for the host only (never for every player). boutique.acheter cible (id), objet (text), joueur (id?) Ask the shop system to buy objet at the merchant cible for the player, without the window, exactly as the Buy button (money taken, item given, stock counted): the Commerces system's shared.commerces.acheter sends it. Refused while another merchant's window is open. boutique.achat follows when it is done. For joueur only; without joueur, for the host only. inventaire.change objet (text), quantite (number), total (number), chargement (boolean?), fiche (number?), jete (boolean?) The quantity of an item changed. total is the new quantity. chargement is true when a saved game gives the items back (game.load): nothing was picked up. For a unique copy (version 15), objet is its kind, fiche its record's number, total how many of that kind. With several stacks of a kind (version 21), total counts all of them; jete is true when a slot was dropped on the ground. inventaire.plein objet (text), fiche (number?), reste (number?) An item could not be added: every slot holds another kind of item (or another unique copy), or (version 21) every stack of its kind is full. reste: picked up in part, how many stayed on the ground. inventaire.manque objet (text), quantite (number), fiche (number?) Items could not be removed: there are not enough.

items.title: Points a script can replace (game.override)
items.text:
The descriptions come from the code.

  • boutique.onglets: function(default, infos) -> a list of {cle, libelle}: the tabs other modules add to this merchant's window (infos: cible, the merchant; joueur). The default is an empty list: the window shows its goods alone. With a tab, the window shows a row of tabs (its goods first, labelled by the text onglet); the open tab of another module is an empty panel the module fills when boutique.onglet announces it. Equipment adds « Services » (repair, upgrade, set gems) at a merchant with a service ticked. Call default(infos) and add yours to its list.
  • boutique.texte: function(default, key) -> the text the shop shows for that key: titre_vide, bourse, acheter, vendre, prix, reste, epuise, plus_en_stock, fermer, achete, vendu, manque, place, sans_objet, onglet (the label of the goods tab, shown when another module adds a tab). It may hold {objet}, {n} and {monnaie}, replaced afterwards (the item and the money in the player's language). The default is the game's translation of the text in the original language (translations_get lists them as built-in texts of the shop); without one, French or English, after the player's language.

items.title: What the agent knows about this system
items.text: The text the agent reads before using this system.

items.title: Shop (boutique)
items.text:
A merchant who sells: when the player uses them (E), a window lists their items with prices, the player's money, and Buy and Sell buttons. The money is a kind of inventory item, such as "Or". Activating it activates interaction and inventaire; placing it on an object places interaction there too. Use it for every shop the user asks for (a merchant, a blacksmith, a vending machine) rather than a script.

Place it on the merchant with systems_attach, then set its values with systems_set:

  • articles: the list of what they sell, one row each: objet (the kind of item, as the inventory stores it: "Épée"), a_vendre (on: it can be bought; off: the merchant only buys it back), quantite (how many one purchase gives: 10 arrows), prix, stock (purchases before running out; 0: no limit), rachat (what the merchant pays when the player sells one back; 0: they buy none, and no Sell button shows).
  • monnaie: the kind of item used to pay ("Or" by default). Name it, and the items, in the user's language, exactly as the inventory stores them. The player gets money like any item: coins to pick up (inventaire with quantite 50), a quest reward, inventaire.ajouter.
  • nom: the window's title (empty: the object's name). Set the interaction prompt texte to "Shop" or "Trade" in the user's language.
  • a_l_usage (on by default): the shop opens when the merchant is used. A merchant who also carries dialogue talks first, and nothing has to be turned off: the shop waits, and the dialogue's last line offers a "Show me your goods" button ("Voir la marchandise" in French) that closes the conversation and opens the shop. To offer it elsewhere in the conversation, give an answer annonce: "boutique.ouvrir" and suite: "fin" (the answer's event carries the merchant as cible): the dialogue then adds no button of its own. Turn a_l_usage off only for a shop opened by a zone or a script.

Buying takes the price (inventaire.retirer), then gives the item (inventaire.ajouter). The window says it clearly when the player lacks money ("You need 5 more Gold"), when the inventory is full (they get their money back), or when an item is sold out. Selling does the reverse, one item at a time, and refills a limited stock.

Example, a blacksmith who sells a unique sword and potions, and buys back wolf pelts:

{"monnaie": "Or", "articles": [{"objet": "Épée", "prix": 30, "stock": 1}, {"objet": "Potion", "quantite": 2, "prix": 5}, {"objet": "Peau de loup", "a_vendre": false, "rachat": 4}]}.

Other details:

  • Events: boutique.achat and boutique.vente (cible the merchant, objet, quantite, prix, monnaie), after the inventory changed: for a sound, a quest step ("buy a sword": a quetes step on boutique.achat), a declencheur rule. game.emit("boutique.ouvrir", {cible = id}) opens a merchant's shop from a zone or a script.
  • Game settings: pause (the world stops while shopping, on by default). largeur is no longer used (kept for old games): the window is the screen « Boutique »; resize its shape Fenêtre (and the columns of the row Article) with screens_set, never by redrawing it.
  • Texts follow the player's language. The shop's own texts (Buy, Close...) are built-in texts of the system, listed by translations_get with the game's texts: translate them there for every language the game offers (French and English are built in). The shop's name (nom), the money and the items are translated with the game's tables too; events keep their original names. To change a word, override boutique.texte from a game script: game.override("boutique.texte", function(default, key) if key == "acheter" then return "Prendre" end return default(key) end). Keys and their {n}, {objet}, {monnaie} placeholders are in modules_info.
  • Services (hook boutique.onglets): another module may add a tab to the shop window; the Equipment adds « Services » (repair, upgrade, set gems) at a merchant when one of its boutique_* services is ticked. The window then shows « Marchandise » and « Services » under the purse (Boutique/Onglet#1, Boutique/Onglet#2, rows of the list Onglets); the other system shows its tab inside the shape Boutique/Onglet ouvert (the Equipment: its screen « Atelier de l'équipement », with game.screen_show(name, {inside = "Boutique/Onglet ouvert"})). A merchant who sells nothing opens on « Services ». boutique.ouvrir {cible, onglet = "equipement.atelier"} opens that tab. With several players, boutique.ouvrir opens for its joueur only; without joueur, for the host only.
  • The window is a screen delivered by the system, « Boutique » (modules/boutique/ecrans/boutique.json): Fenêtre, Titre, Bourse, the list Onglets (row Onglet), Onglet ouvert, Vide, the list Articles (row Article: Image, Nom, Prix, Acheter or Sans achat, Vendre), Message, Fermer. Its buttons send the system's actions acheter, vendre, onglet, fermer. Change its look, places and sizes with screens_set (styles, not hand-made values); never draw a shop with game.hud_*, and never edit the system.
  • Saved games: game.save keeps what each merchant has left of a limited stock, and game.load gives it back. Nothing to write.
  • Buying from a script, without the window: game.emit("boutique.acheter", {cible = merchant, objet = "Épée"}) makes the same purchase as the Buy button (refused while another merchant's window is open); boutique.achat follows when it is done. A merchant given stock_cle (a text) keeps its limited stocks under that key instead of its id: the Commerces system (commerces) gives one per shop to the clerks it copies, so a shop's stock stays when its clerk leaves and comes back. The clerks of a city's shops are set in commerces, not here.
  • Gamepad and keyboard: the first Buy button has the focus; the d-pad or the arrows move it, A or Enter buys, B or Escape closes (Boutique/Fermer is the window's back button).
  • Testing: in game_run, give money first (inventaire.ajouter), walk to the merchant, press interact, then click Boutique/Acheter#<row> (or Boutique/Vendre#<row>, Boutique/Fermer; the row counts the items shown); the report's hud gives each button's area and Boutique/Message what the shop answered. With a gamepad: segments with pad (["pad_down"], then ["pad_a"], each followed by a segment without); the report marks the button with the focus (focused).

items.title: Several players
items.text:
One copy per player: each player has their own window and money (their own inventory). A merchant's limited stocks are shared: what one buys is gone for the others. The host's saved game keeps the stocks.

items.title: Fog volume
items.text:
A local fog, limited to an area: the mist of a valley, an undergrowth, a marsh, the smoke of a cave. Create > Fog volume places an invisible box that carries it: it fills the box (or the sphere inside it) and fades out towards its edges. With volumetric fog (High or Medium quality), it catches the sun's rays and shadows. Its kind "Glowing air (rays only)" (Create > Glowing air) is an almost invisible air that only shows the sun's rays, like the dust of a forest.

Identifier brouillard Version 1 Placed on objects yes Run by the engine yes: the engine runs it itself, without a script

items.title: Settings for the whole game
items.text:
In the Systems panel (Developer mode), by opening the system's card.

None.

items.title: Settings on each object
items.text:
In the Properties of an object or folder that carries the system, Systems section. A folder passes its values on to what it contains; an object can change a value for itself only.

Setting What it does Name in code Type Default Limits or choices Kind Fog: a visible mist, of its colour (a valley, a marsh, smoke). Glowing air: an almost invisible air that only shows the sun's rays where they cross it, like dust in a forest or a room. It needs volumetric fog (Sky and light), in High or Medium quality, and a sun that passes between foliage or walls. sorte Choice in a list Fog brouillard: Fogair_lumineux: Glowing air (rays only) Shape Box: the fog fills the object's whole box (a valley, a room). Sphere: the ball inside it, oval if the box is stretched (a round patch, a cloud). forme Choice in a list Box boite: Boxsphere: Sphere Visibility (m)shown only if Kind is “Fog” At this distance inside the fog, you can hardly see anything (95% hidden). Small: a pea-souper; large: a light haze. The box must be larger than this distance for it to hide everything. distance Number 20 from 0.5 to 2000 Colorshown only if Kind is “Fog” The color of the fog in full light: bluish white for a mist, pale green for a marsh, dark grey for smoke. In the shade, it is darker. couleur Color #dfe4e8 Air visibility (m)shown only if Kind is “Glowing air (rays only)” The air's visibility, in metres: smaller gives stronger rays; larger, subtler ones. 200 by default; 100 for strong rays (a dusty room), 400 for a light trace. Outside the rays, the air hardly veils anything. distance_air Number 200 from 20 to 2000 Soft edgesshown only if Kind is “Glowing air (rays only)” The part of the box, from its edges, where the air fades out: 1 by default, the rays appear and fade gently, without showing the box's faces. bords_air Number 1 from 0 to 1 Soft edgesshown only if Kind is “Fog” The part of the box, from its edges, where the fog fades out: 0 cuts sharply at the faces, 1 leaves only the core thick. bords Number 0.3 from 0 to 1 Thicker at the bottom 0: the same over the whole height. 1: thick at the bottom of the box, nothing at the top, like a mist that stays on the ground. degrade Number 0 from 0 to 1

items.title: What the agent knows about this system
items.text: The text the agent reads before using this system.

items.title: Fog volume (brouillard)
items.text:
An object carrying this system fills its box with a local fog: the mist of a valley or an undergrowth, a marsh, the smoke of a cave, a cloud of dust. The scene fog (world_set fogDistance) covers the whole map; a fog volume stays where you put it. The system has no script: the renderer draws it. Several volumes can overlap: their fog adds up.

  • Make one: create a box (builtin:cube) with visible: false and no collider, then systems_attach this system on it. Scale the box to the area (20 × 6 × 30 for a valley floor, 4 × 3 × 4 for a room): the fog fills it, or the ball inside it (forme "sphere"). Place it so that its bottom is a little under the ground.
  • Per object (systems_set): forme (boite, sphere), distance (m: at this distance inside the fog, 95% is hidden; 5 to 15 for a thick mist, 40 to 100 for a haze; the box must be larger than this distance to hide everything behind it), couleur ("#rrggbb", its color in full light), bords (0 to 1: how much of the box, from its edges, fades out), degrade (0 to 1: 1 is thick at the bottom and nothing at the top, a mist that stays on the ground).
  • With volumetric fog on (world_set volumetricFog true, and High or Medium quality), the volume catches the sun's rays and the shadows of the trees: a fog volume in a forest shows sun shafts there only, without fogging the rest of the map. Raise volumetricAir for brighter shafts.
  • Two kinds (sorte): brouillard (the default, a visible fog) and air_lumineux ("Glowing air (rays only)"), an almost invisible air that only shows the sun's rays where they cross it, like dust in a forest. Pick by what the user describes: "sun rays in the forest", "light shafts", "god rays through the trees or a window", "dust in the light" -> air_lumineux; "mist in the valley", "a foggy marsh", "smoke in a cave", "the forest is misty" -> brouillard. The air has its own settings: distance_air (m, 200 by default; 100 for strong rays, 400 for a light trace) and bords_air (1 by default, keep it); distance, couleur and bords do not apply to it (it has no colour: it takes the sun's). It needs volumetric fog on (world_set volumetricFog true; turn it on if it is off) and a sun low enough to pass between trees or walls; on Low quality it does not show at all. Make its box large and tall enough to hold the rays from the treetops to the ground (30 × 12 × 30 for a clearing). Keep fogDistance 0 if the user wants no mist.
  • In Low quality (and on a small graphics card), it is still drawn, without shadows or rays. Far from the camera it is also drawn without shadows: it never stops at a distance.
  • Do not make its box visible: that would show the box. It moves with its object (a cloud that drifts, smoke that follows a fire).

items.title: Several players
items.text:
The engine draws it once for the whole game: every player sees it.

This page is generated automatically from the WorldMint code (modules/brouillard/module.json, modules/brouillard/AGENT.md, modules/events.json): it always matches the editor.

items.title: Loot
items.text:
Loot tables, rolled when an enemy dies, a chest opens, on harvest, at the end of a quest or by the Trigger: what drops, with its rarity (color, glow), its random bonuses and its generated name for unique copies. On the ground, in the inventory, or in a "Take all" window.

Identifier butin Version 6 Placed on objects yes Also activates Inventory

items.title: Settings for the whole game
items.text:
In the Systems panel (Developer mode), by opening the system's card.

Setting What it does Name in code Type Default Limits or choices Loot tables Each table has a name, how many rolls it makes and its chance of giving nothing. Its rows (what may drop) are in the "Table rows" list. An enemy, a chest, a harvest or a quest names a table. tables List of “Table” (empty) one line per “Table”: its fields Table rows What each table may drop: a kind of item or another table, its weight (or a percentage tried apart), its quantity, its conditions, and "guaranteed". lignes List of “Row” (empty) one line per “Row”: its fields Rarities Your game's rarities, from the most common to the rarest: name, color (the item's name, its glow on the ground), chance, number of random bonuses, multiplier of their strength, chance of gem sockets, sound and glow when dropped. Only unique copies (Inventory) get one. raretes List of “Rarity” [{'nom': 'Commun', 'couleur': '#c8c8c8', 'chance': 60, 'bonus': 0, 'multiplicateur': 1, 'chance_gemmes': 0, 'son': '', 'lueur': False}, {'nom': 'Peu commun', 'couleur': '#3fbf4a', 'chance': 25, 'bonus': 1, 'multiplicateur': 1, 'chance_gemmes': 0, 'son': '', 'lueur': True}, {'nom': 'Rare', 'couleur': '#3f7fff', 'chance': 10, 'bonus': 2, 'multiplicateur': 1.2, 'chance_gemmes': 0.1, 'son': '', 'lueur': True}, {'nom': 'Épique', 'couleur': '#a03fff', 'chance': 4, 'bonus': 3, 'multiplicateur': 1.5, 'chance_gemmes': 0.3, 'son': '', 'lueur': True}, {'nom': 'Légendaire', 'couleur': '#ff9f1f', 'chance': 1, 'bonus': 4, 'multiplicateur': 2, 'chance_gemmes': 0.6, 'son': '', 'lueur': True}] one line per “Rarity”: its fields Random bonuses The bonuses a unique copy may get: the modifiable value it changes, its range, the categories of items that may get it, the lowest rarity, and a piece of name ("sharp", "of the Wolf"). bonus_hasard List of “Bonus” (empty) one line per “Bonus”: its fields Bonus growth with item level How ranges grow with the item level (the enemy's or the zone's): in a straight line, or faster and faster. The same curve as enemy growth (Progression). croissance_forme Choice in a list In a straight line lineaire: In a straight lineexponentielle: Faster and faster Rise per item level 0.1: +10% of the range per level above the first. 0: ranges do not move. croissance_taux Number 0.1 from -1 to 100 Most gem sockets How many sockets an item may get, each tried with its rarity's chance. gemmes_max Number 3 from 0 to 32, as a whole number How loot appears On the ground, to pick up; straight into the inventory; or in a "Take all" window when using the body (or chest). apparition Choice in a list On the ground, to pick up sol: On the ground, to pick upinventaire: Straight into the inventoryfenetre: In a "Take all" window Rarity glow on the ground Ticked: an item on the ground glows with its rarity's color, in the world (if its rarity has "Glow on the ground"): what passes in front hides it, and it shows by day as by night. lueur Yes or no yes Glow style A beam: a column of light rising from the item, on a glowing foot, which marks it from afar. Sparkles: stars turning around it, with a small light. style_lueur Choice in a list A rising beam faisceau: A rising beametincelles: Sparkles around Glow size 1: a beam about 1.5 m high. 2 twice that, 0.5 half. taille_lueur Number 1 from 0.1 to 5 Floating name above loot Ticked: the item's name, in its rarity's color, floats above it when the player is near. nom_flottant Yes or no yes Floating name distance (m) The name only shows within this distance. distance_nom Number 8 from 1 to 100 Ground loot disappears after (s, 0: never) Loot not picked up disappears after this many seconds. disparition Number 300 from 0 to 86 400 Keep ground loot in the save Ticked: loot still on the ground comes back when the game loads, with its time left. garder_au_sol Yes or no yes Models on the ground For each kind of item, the scene object (usually hidden) a copy of which is placed on the ground. A missing kind takes the default model. modeles List of “Model” (empty) one line per “Model”: its fields Default model on the ground The scene object (usually hidden, a small bag of your game) copied for a kind without a model (neither in "Models on the ground" nor in the Inventory's "Models in hand"). Empty: the engine shape below. modele_defaut Object of the scene (empty) Without any model set What is placed on the ground for a kind without a model, when no default model is chosen: a small engine shape (no file, no pack), in its rarity's color, with its floating name and glow; or straight into the inventory. forme_sans_modele Choice in a list A small cube cube: A small cubesphere: A small sphereinventaire: Straight into the inventory Shape size (m)shown only if Without any model set is “A small cube” or “A small sphere” The width of the small cube or sphere placed on the ground without a model, in metres. taille_forme Number 0.15 from 0.02 to 2 Loot sharing (several players) Free: whoever picks it up first. Personal: each their own roll, that only they can take. Reserved for the killer a few seconds, then free. Each in turn: each item is reserved for one player, in turn. partage Choice in a list Free libre: Freepersonnel: Personaltueur: Reserved for the killer, then freetour: Each in turn Reserved for the killer for (s) With "Reserved for the killer": the time before anyone may take it. delai_tueur Number 30 from 0 to 3600 On death, the player drops With the "Death and respawn" module (joueur.mort): what the player loses from their bag when they die, left where they fall. Nothing by default. Unique items keep their record. mort_sac Choice in a list Nothing rien: Nothingtout: The whole bagpart: A share of the bag Share of the bag dropped (%)shown only if On death, the player drops is “A share of the bag” Of each stack, this share (rounded); of unique items, this share too, the first in the bag. mort_part Number 50 from 1 to 100 What is dropped goesshown only if On death, the player drops is “The whole bag” or “A share of the bag” A bag where they fell, which opens (the "Take all" window) and disappears when empty; or each item on the ground, like loot. mort_forme Choice in a list In a bag to pick up sac: In a bag to pick upsol: Each item on the ground Model of the dropped bagshown only if On death, the player drops is “The whole bag” or “A share of the bag” The scene object (usually hidden) copied for the bag. None: a small engine cube, twice the "Shape size". mort_modele_sac Object of the scene (empty) Reserved for the dead player for (s)shown only if On death, the player drops is “The whole bag” or “A share of the bag” During this time, only they can take back what they dropped; then anyone. 0: anyone at once. mort_reserve Number 60 from 0 to 86 400 Starting loot luck The modifiable value chance_butin (equipment, effects and levels raise it): it multiplies the chances of rarities above the most common and divides the chance of nothing. chance_base Number 1 from 0 to 1000 Bad-luck protection Ticked: after each roll without a rare item, the chance of a rare item rises, until one drops. protection_active Yes or no no Rarity aimed at by the protection The name of a rarity: it and rarer ones count as "rare". protection_rang Text Rare Rise per miss 0.1: +10% chance for rare after each missed roll. protection_hausse Number 0.1 from 0 to 100 Rare bonuses from Gathering For a resource gathered, a table rolled on top, with a chance (a nugget in a rock). collecte List of “Resource” (empty) one line per “Resource”: its fields Rewards rolled from Quests For a finished quest, a table rolled as a reward, on top of its own. quetes List of “Quest” (empty) one line per “Quest”: its fields

items.title: The fields of each “Table”
items.text:
In the Properties, each “Table” has its own numbered frame; Add: Table adds one, the cross removes it. A field only appears when it is useful: under its name, the table says when.

Setting What it does Name in code Type Default Limits or choices Name The table's name, such as "Wolf" or "Cave chest". nom Text (empty) Rolls How many times the table picks a row (by weight) each time it is used. tirages Number 1 from 0 to 100, as a whole number Most rolls (0: always the number above) Above "Rolls": a random number between the two. tirages_max Number 0 from 0 to 100, as a whole number Chance of nothing (0 to 1) On each roll, the chance that nothing drops: 0.3 for 30%. Loot luck lowers it. rien Number 0 from 0 to 1

items.title: The fields of each “Row”
items.text:
In the Properties, each “Row” has its own numbered frame; Add: Row adds one, the cross removes it. A field only appears when it is useful: under its name, the table says when.

Setting What it does Name in code Type Default Limits or choices Table The table this row belongs to (its name). table Text (empty) Kind of item The kind of item that drops, as the Inventory stores it. Empty if the row rolls another table. objet Text (empty) Or another table The name of another table, rolled "quantity" times (a gem table inside a boss's). A loop (A rolls B which rolls A) is refused. sous_table Text (empty) Weight The larger, the more often the row is chosen against the other rows of the table: 3 against 1 drops three times as often. poids Number 1 from 0 to 1 000 000 000 Or a percentage, tried apart (0: by weight) Above 0: the row is tried on each roll with this chance (5 for 5%), on top of the row chosen by weight. pourcentage Number 0 from 0 to 100 Quantity How many drop. quantite Number 1 from 0 to 100 000, as a whole number Most quantity (0: always the same) Above "Quantity": a random number between the two (1 to 3). quantite_max Number 0 from 0 to 100 000, as a whole number Guaranteed Ticked: always drops, once, whatever happens (a boss's key). garanti Yes or no no Source level at least The row only counts if the enemy (or zone) is at least this level. 0: no condition. niveau_min Number 0 from 0 to 100 000, as a whole number Source level at most The row only counts up to this enemy level. 0: no condition. niveau_max Number 0 from 0 to 100 000, as a whole number Player level at least The row only counts if the player is at least this level (Progression). 0: no condition. joueur_min Number 0 from 0 to 100 000, as a whole number Player level at most 0: no condition. joueur_max Number 0 from 0 to 100 000, as a whole number Only in the zone The name of a zone (Zone module): the row only counts while the player is in it. Empty: everywhere. zone Text (empty) Only during the quest The title of a quest in progress: the row only counts during it. Empty: always. quete Text (empty)

Empty: none. son Text (empty) Glow on the ground Ticked: the item on the ground glows with its rarity's color. lueur Yes or no yes

In the Properties of an object or folder that carries the system, Systems section. A folder passes its values on to what it contains; an object can change a value for itself only.
