Empty: nothing. table Text (empty) Item level (0: the enemy's) The level of the items rolled here. 0: the level Progression gave the enemy, else 1. niveau Number 0 from 0 to 100 000, as a whole number

items.title: Events
items.text: The descriptions come from the code.

items.title: What it announces
items.text: Event Fields Description butin.tombe table (text), nombre (number), cible (text?), joueur (id?) Loot was rolled and placed (on the ground, in the inventory or in a content): how many lines dropped. butin.ramasse objet (text), quantite (number), fiche (number?), joueur (id) A player took a piece of loot (from the ground or a Take all window). fiche: the unique item's record, if it is one. butin.refus cible (text), joueur (id), raison (text) The host refused a player taking loot reserved for someone else (sharing personal, killer or in turn). butin.ouvrir cible (text), joueur (id?) Open the Take all window of a content (a body, a chest) for a player. butin.contenu cible (text), nombre (number) A content (a body, a chest) changed: its Take all windows redraw. butin.prendre cible (text), numero (number?), joueur (id) A player asks the host to take from a content: one line (numero) or all they may take. inventaire.ajouter objet (text), quantite (number), joueur (id?), fiche (number?) Ask the inventory to add items, such as a reward. Answered by inventaire.change, or inventaire.plein. With several players, joueur says whose bag; without it, the player whose action is being handled, or every player. inventaire.retirer objet (text), quantite (number), fiche (number?) Ask the inventory to remove items, such as a payment. Answered by inventaire.change, or inventaire.manque if there are not enough. For a kind with unique copies (version 15): fiche removes that copy, otherwise the first ones; their records are destroyed. inventaire.sortir objet (text), fiche (number?), case (text?), joueur (id?) Ask the inventory to take one item out of the bag without destroying it (version 16): objet is its kind, fiche a unique copy (it keeps its record; whoever takes it says its new holder). The Equipment module takes what it makes the player wear. A stack gives one from its smallest stack, or from case (version 21), a slot's key. butin.sac joueur (id), cible (id?), nombre (number), position (vector) A dead player dropped their bag (Loot setting mort_sac): cible is the bag left where they fell (nil: each item on the ground), nombre the lines dropped.

items.title: What it listens to
items.text: Event Fields Description sante.mort cible (id), source (id?) An object's health reached zero. What happens next belongs to the game: the health module does nothing else, unless its setting says to destroy the object. progression.niveau_ennemi cible (id), niveau (number) The Progression module gave an enemy its level (fixed, per zone, matched to the players or growing with time): its health and damage grew with it. To show it above its head. collecte.recolte cible (id), ressource (text), quantite (number), joueur (id?), xp (number?), piste (text?) A resource was used up and gave what it holds. The inventory, if present, has been asked to add it. quetes.debut quete (text), groupe (boolean?) A quest started: quete is its title. groupe (Journal de quêtes 8): true for a quest of the whole group (game setting groupe), sent once for the group, joueur being who moved it on. quetes.fin quete (text), xp (number?), piste (text?), groupe (boolean?), facultatives (table?) A quest is finished: all its steps are done. Its reward, if any, has been asked to the inventory. xp and piste (version 28): its XP for the Progression module and the track that gets it (empty: the main one). facultatives (Journal de quêtes 11): {faites, total}, how many of its optional steps were done, out of how many; absent when it has none. groupe (Journal de quêtes 8): true for a quest of the whole group (game setting groupe), sent once for the group, joueur being who moved it on. quetes.abandon quete (text), groupe (boolean?) The player abandoned a quest from the log (or quetes.abandonner asked for it). It gives no reward; it may be given again if its settings allow it. groupe (Journal de quêtes 8): true for a quest of the whole group (game setting groupe), sent once for the group, joueur being who moved it on. quetes.echec quete (text), groupe (boolean?) A quest failed: an event, a mark, its time ran out, or quetes.echouer. It gives no reward; it may be given again if its settings allow it. groupe (Journal de quêtes 8): true for a quest of the whole group (game setting groupe), sent once for the group, joueur being who moved it on. zone.entree cible (id), qui (id), joueur (id?) Something entered a zone (an object carrying the zone system): a player, a character or a moving object, depending on what the zone detects (joueur: every player). joueur is set when qui is a player. Announced by the engine. zone.sortie cible (id), qui (id), joueur (id?) Something left a zone. Not announced for an object removed from the game while inside. inventaire.plein objet (text), fiche (number?), reste (number?) An item could not be added: every slot holds another kind of item (or another unique copy), or (version 21) every stack of its kind is full. reste: picked up in part, how many stayed on the ground. butin.lacher table (text), position (vector?), cible (id?), niveau (number?), joueur (id?) Ask the Loot module to roll a table and drop what it gives (the Trigger, a script). position or cible: where; niveau: the item level; joueur: for whom (the killer, for sharing). butin.remplir cle (text), table (text), niveau (number?), joueur (id?), joueur_seul (id?) Ask the Loot module to roll a table into a content (a chest of the Chests module): cle names the content, joueur_seul reserves it for one player. butin.prendre cible (text), numero (number?), joueur (id) A player asks the host to take from a content: one line (numero) or all they may take. butin.refus cible (text), joueur (id), raison (text) The host refused a player taking loot reserved for someone else (sharing personal, killer or in turn). butin.ouvrir cible (text), joueur (id?) Open the Take all window of a content (a body, a chest) for a player. butin.contenu cible (text), nombre (number) A content (a body, a chest) changed: its Take all windows redraw. interaction.utiliser cible (id), joueur (id) The player used the object in reach: a door, a merchant, an item to pick up. Whoever owns that object decides what it does. langue.change langue (text) Sent by the engine when the player changes the game's language (game.set_language, the Menu options). A module redraws what it already shows: its texts go through game.t and game.language. joueur.mort joueur (id), cible (id), source (id?), position (vector) A player died (death and respawn module): they control nothing until they respawn. Other systems hook here: drop the bag, a grave, a counter. fenetres.fermer joueur (id?), raison (text?) Close every window a player has open (loot, inventory, equipment, workshop...), sent by the Death module when they die; any script may send it (a cutscene). joueur: that player (missing: everyone). Each module with a window closes its own. butin.ranger cible (text), objet (text), fiche (number?), quantite (number?), case (text?), joueur (id) A player asks the host to put an item of their bag into a chest they may search (the three-part inventory window): a stack (quantite) or a unique copy (fiche). The bag loses it first; nothing enters if the bag no longer has it. inventaire.manque objet (text), quantite (number), fiche (number?) Items could not be removed: there are not enough.

items.title: What the agent knows about this system
items.text: The text the agent reads before using this system.

items.title: Loot (butin)
items.text:
Loot tables rolled by the host (ADR-039 § 8 to § 10). It needs the inventory. Never edit its scripts: change its settings, listen to its events, or use game.override from a script of the game.

  • Tables (tables: nom, tirages, tirages_max, rien from 0 to 1) and their rows (lignes: table, objet or sous_table, poids, or pourcentage tried apart on each roll, quantite, quantite_max, garanti once per table, conditions niveau_min, niveau_max, joueur_min, joueur_max, zone, quete). A loop between tables (a -> b -> a) is refused: nothing drops and the reason goes to the log.
  • Rarities (raretes, from the most common to the rarest; five by default, Commun to Légendaire): nom, couleur (the item's name, its glow on the ground), chance (a weight), bonus (how many random bonuses), multiplicateur, chance_gemmes (tried gemmes_max times), son, lueur. Only kinds with uniques ticked in the inventory's sortes_objets get a rarity, bonuses and a generated name; a stack stays a stack.
  • Random bonuses (bonus_hasard): valeur (a Progression value: degats, sante_max...), min, max (at item level 1), pourcent, categories (comma separated, the kind's categorie), rarete_min, nom (a piece of name) and place (apres, avant). The item level is the enemy's (event progression.niveau_ennemi) or the object setting niveau; ranges grow with it along croissance_forme and croissance_taux (the Progression's growth curve).
  • Sources: an object carrying this system with table (an enemy) drops it on sante.mort; collecte rows (a resource, a table, a chance); quetes rows (a quest, a table); butin.lacher {table, cible or position, niveau, joueur} (the Trigger's action « Lâcher un butin », a script); chests (module coffres, through butin.remplir).
  • Appearance (apparition): sol: a copy of the kind's model (modeles, else the inventory's en_main model of that kind, else modele_defaut, all set by the creator; nothing is assumed of a pack; with none, forme_sans_modele: a small engine cube or sphere in its rarity color, taille_forme metres wide (0.15, measured on the shape), set on the ground; or into the inventory), glowing in its rarity color in the world, hidden by what passes in front, by day and night, with no asset (lueur; style_lueur: faisceau, a column of light rising from it, or etincelles, sparkles around it; taille_lueur, 1 for a beam about 1.5 m high; light enough for 50 items on the ground), a floating name (nom_flottant, distance_nom), gone after disparition seconds (once empty, it shows « Plus rien. » for 1.5 s and closes by itself; fenetres.fermer closes it); a model must not carry the « inventaire » system itself; inventaire; fenetre: the body becomes usable and opens the « Tout prendre » window, delivered as a screen the user restyles in the screen editor: « Butin » (Fenêtre, Titre, Vide, the list Objets: one row per item, Image and the button Objet, Objet#2 the second; Tout prendre, Fermer; actions prendre, tout, fermer); a refusal shows « Message du butin » (Message). Never draw these windows yourself, and do not name another screen like these. The floating names follow the world and stay HUD (butin.nom.<object>). With the Inventory's disposition_fenetre trois_parties (version 3), that window stays closed: the content shows in the inventory's right column, and a bag slot dragged onto a chest's content is put in it with butin.ranger {cible, objet, fiche?, quantite, joueur?} (chests only, coffre/..., with their sharing rules; checked by the host; without joueur, the host's player).
  • Dropping the bag on death (mort_sac, off by default: rien): with the module mort (its event joueur.mort), tout or part (mort_part %, of each stack and of the unique items, the first in the bag) of the dead player's bag leaves it (inventaire.retirer, inventaire.sortir: a unique item keeps its record), left where they fell: mort_forme sac (a bag to open with « Tout prendre », a copy of mort_modele_sac, an object chosen by the creator, else a small engine cube; it disappears when empty) or sol (each item on the ground, like loot). Reserved for them mort_reserve seconds (0: anyone), then anyone. Announced by butin.sac {joueur, cible, nombre, position}. Nothing is dropped when the Inventory's bag is shared by the group. Saved with the game (the bag comes back where it was).
  • Luck: the value chance_butin (base chance_base) multiplies the chance of every rarity but the first and divides the chance of nothing. protection_active, protection_rang, protection_hausse: the bad-luck protection, counted per player on the host.
  • Online: an item set on the ground is seen by every guest, a copy of its model or the engine shape in its rarity color, at the same place and size (protocol 25), and leaves when picked up.
  • Several players (partage): libre, personnel (one roll per player, never on the ground where others would see it: in that player's own « Tout prendre » window on the body, or straight into their bag; the records of one player's share are never sent to the others' machines), tueur (delai_tueur seconds), tour. Only the host rolls and checks each pickup; a refusal sends butin.refus (raison reserve) and shows a message to that player.
  • A full bag never loses an item: what does not fit stays on the ground or in the window (butin.refus with raison plein, and a message); given straight to the bag, it drops at the player's feet.
  • Conditions receive the player's zone (zone.entree: the zone's name without its number), their quests in progress (quetes.debut until quetes.fin, quetes.abandon, quetes.echec) and their level; a zone object carrying this system with niveau gives the item level of what drops while the player is in it (when the source has no level).
  • Save: loot on the ground (when garder_au_sol, with its time left; a unique item keeps its record), the contents of bodies and chests (a body opens its window again after a load; identical stacks are merged), and each player's bad-luck count.
  • Events: emits butin.tombe, butin.ramasse, butin.refus, butin.ouvrir, butin.contenu, butin.sac, inventaire.ajouter, inventaire.retirer, inventaire.sortir; listens to butin.lacher, butin.remplir, butin.prendre, sante.mort, joueur.mort, collecte.recolte, quetes.fin, progression.niveau_ennemi, interaction.utiliser.
  • Scripts: game.loot_roll(table, {niveau, niveau_joueur, zone, quetes, chance, joueur}) returns the list rolled without creating anything; game.loot_simulate(table, n) rolls n times (the editor's simulator). Under the module's settings, the editor offers the genre presets (Survie, Jeu de rôle, Tir) and « Tirer cette table N fois ».

This page is generated automatically from the WorldMint code (modules/butin/module.json, modules/butin/AGENT.md, modules/events.json): it always matches the editor.

items.title: Map
items.text:
A minimap in a corner of the screen, the player in the middle, and a big map of the whole scene with the M key, zoomed and moved with the mouse or the gamepad (triggers and stick). What carries this system shows on it as a marker: a shape and a color, or an image, and its name; always, once discovered up close, or only as a quest objective. Merchants, characters who talk, the objectives of quests in progress and, with several players, the other players with their names are marked by themselves. The player places their own markers, ticks what they want to see, and can follow a compass at the top of the screen.

Identifier carte Version 15 Placed on objects yes

items.title: Settings for the whole game
items.text:
In the Systems panel (Developer mode), by opening the system's card.

Setting What it does Name in code Type Default Limits or choices Minimap in a corner of the screen Ticked: a small piece of the map, around the player, stays on screen in a corner, with the markers nearby. It hides during a pause (a menu, a dialogue). mini_carte Yes or no yes Corner of the minimap The corner of the screen where the minimap sits. At the top right, it may get in the way of the inventory and the current quest step, shown there. mini_coin Choice in a list Bottom right bas_droite: Bottom rightbas_gauche: Bottom lefthaut_droite: Top righthaut_gauche: Top left Size of the minimap (share of the screen height) The height of the minimap: 0.26 takes a little more than a quarter. It stays square, or round, whatever the shape of the screen. mini_taille Number 0.26 from 0.1 to 0.6 Shape of the minimap A rectangle with rounded corners and a thin border (the default), round or square. The big map is always square. mini_forme Choice in a list Rounded rectangle arrondie: Rounded rectangleronde: Roundcarree: Square Corner roundness of the minimap (share of its size)shown only if Shape of the minimap is “Rounded rectangle” 0: square corners; 0.5: fully round sides. mini_arrondi Number 0.12 from 0 to 0.5 Thickness of the minimap border (pixels for 1080)shown only if Shape of the minimap is “Rounded rectangle” A thin line around the rounded rectangle; 0: no border. mini_bordure Number 1.5 from 0 to 12 Color of the minimap bordershown only if Shape of the minimap is “Rounded rectangle” Also the outline of the destination panel of the big map. mini_bordure_couleur Color #ffffff Opacity of the minimap bordershown only if Shape of the minimap is “Rounded rectangle” 0: invisible; 1: solid. mini_bordure_opacite Number 0.35 from 0 to 1 Distance to go under the minimap With the GPS: the distance along the route to the destination ("480 m"), under the minimap (above it when it is at the bottom of the screen). mini_distance Yes or no yes District names on the minimap The names of the plan (districts, towns) that fall inside the minimap. mini_noms Yes or no yes What the minimap shows, from edge to edge (m) The zoom of the minimap: how many meters of the world it shows from edge to edge. Less shows the details; more shows far away. mini_etendue Number 80 from 10 to 5000 The minimap turns with the player Ticked: the minimap turns so that the player always faces up. Unticked: north stays at the top, and the player's arrow turns. mini_tourne Yes or no no Map tucked inside its frame (share of its size) For a frame of the image theme laid over the map (a ring from an interface pack, role cadre.minicarte or cadre.carte): the map is tucked in by this share of its size, on each side, so it does not spill under a thick frame. 0.08 for a ring a twelfth of the size. 0: the map takes the whole place. cadre_marge Number 0 from 0 to 0.3 Big map with a key (M) Ticked: the Open the map control (M, or ↓ on a gamepad) opens the map of the whole scene, and closes it. The wheel zooms, holding the mouse moves it. On a gamepad, the right trigger zooms in, the left trigger zooms out and the left stick moves it; on a keyboard, Page Up and Page Down zoom, the walking keys move it. grande_carte Yes or no yes Stop the game while the big map is open Ticked: the world stops while the big map is open. Unticked: the game goes on behind it, enemies included. pause_fenetre Yes or no yes Marker names on the big map Ticked: each marker of the big map has its name written under it, such as "Forge" or "Village". noms Yes or no yes Mark the merchants (Shop) Ticked: each object carrying the Shop system has a golden diamond marker, without placing anything. A Map system placed on it chooses its look. marchands Yes or no yes Mark the characters who talk (Dialogue) Ticked: each object carrying the Dialogue system has a light blue marker, without placing anything. A Map system placed on it chooses its look. personnages Yes or no yes Show the other players With several players, each other player has their arrow, in a color of their own, turned where they look, and their name (their character's name, or their nickname). Nowhere: for a game where people hide, nobody sees the others on the map. joueurs Choice in a list On the minimap and the big map partout: On the minimap and the big mapgrande: Only on the big mapaucun: Nowhere (hide and seek) Show the objective of quests in progress Ticked: a marker whose object is aimed at by the current step of a quest ("Defeat the wolves", for objects named Wolf) becomes an objective, ringed with its color; outside the minimap, it stays at its edge, in its direction. objectifs Yes or no yes Color of the objectives The color of the ring around a marker which is the objective of a quest in progress. couleur_objectif Color #ffcc33 GPS to the objective A line on the minimap and the big map, from the player to the objective of the current quest (or their last marker), following the way. In a generated city, it follows the streets: by vehicle, in the driving direction, through roundabouts and left-turn lanes; on foot, both ways. Elsewhere, the walkable areas. It is redone when the player strays from it. Off by default. gps Choice in a list Off aucun: Offauto: Automatic: by vehicle while the player drives, on foot otherwisea_pied: Always on footvehicule: Always by vehicle Where the GPS leadsshown only if GPS to the objective is “Automatic: by vehicle while the player drives, on foot otherwise”, “Always on foot” or “Always by vehicle” The objective: that of the quest highest in the log, the nearest if there are several. A marker: the last one the player placed on the big map (if they can place some). gps_cible Choice in a list The last marker placed, otherwise the objective auto: The last marker placed, otherwise the objectiveobjectif: Only the quest objectiverepere: Only the last marker placed The GPS redoes the route at this distance (m)shown only if GPS to the objective is “Automatic: by vehicle while the player drives, on foot otherwise”, “Always on foot” or “Always by vehicle” When the player moves farther than this from the line (another street, a shortcut), the route is redone from where they are. gps_ecart Number 15 from 2 to 500 Color of the GPS lineshown only if GPS to the objective is “Automatic: by vehicle while the player drives, on foot otherwise”, “Always on foot” or “Always by vehicle” The color of the line that leads to the objective. gps_couleur Color #3d8bff Thickness of the GPS line (pixels for 1080)shown only if GPS to the objective is “Automatic: by vehicle while the player drives, on foot otherwise”, “Always on foot” or “Always by vehicle” A single smooth line, with round ends, along the middle of the streets. 5: thin; 7: easy to see; 12: very thick. gps_epaisseur Number 7 from 1 to 40 GPS: price of a lane change (m)shown only if GPS to the objective is “Automatic: by vehicle while the player drives, on foot otherwise”, “Always on foot” or “Always by vehicle” By vehicle, moving to the next lane of the same direction counts as this many extra metres: small, the GPS changes lanes readily to take the shortest way; large, it prefers to stay in its lane. gps_changement_voie Number 15 from 0 to 1000 GPS: price of a U-turn (m)shown only if GPS to the objective is “Automatic: by vehicle while the player drives, on foot otherwise”, “Always on foot” or “Always by vehicle” By vehicle, the GPS turns back only at the end of a dead end, and that U-turn counts as this many extra metres: large, it avoids it as long as another way exists. gps_demi_tour Number 300 from 0 to 10 000 Glow of the GPS line (pixels for 1080)shown only if GPS to the objective is “Automatic: by vehicle while the player drives, on foot otherwise”, “Always on foot” or “Always by vehicle” The glow on each side of the line; 0: no glow. gps_halo Number 5 from 0 to 30 Color of the glow (empty: that of the line)shown only if GPS to the objective is “Automatic: by vehicle while the player drives, on foot otherwise”, “Always on foot” or “Always by vehicle” A color "#rrggbb"; empty: the color of the line. gps_halo_couleur Text (empty) Opacity of the glowshown only if GPS to the objective is “Automatic: by vehicle while the player drives, on foot otherwise”, “Always on foot” or “Always by vehicle” 0: invisible; 1: solid. gps_halo_opacite Number 0.3 from 0 to 1 Image of the destination (empty: a diamond)shown only if GPS to the objective is “Automatic: by vehicle while the player drives, on foot otherwise”, “Always on foot” or “Always by vehicle” At the end of the GPS line, on both maps: an icon of your own, preferably square on a transparent background. image_destination Image from the library (empty) Destination panel on the big mapshown only if GPS to the objective is “Automatic: by vehicle while the player drives, on foot otherwise”, “Always on foot” or “Always by vehicle” With the GPS: at the top left of the big map, the name of the destination, its district and the distance along the route. panneau_destination Yes or no yes Ring the area of a place to reach Ticked: around the place of a "reach a place" or "hold on" step of the Quest log (an objective, even if it does not carry this system), the minimap and the big map show the area of its radius, in the color of the objectives. objectif_zone Yes or no yes Announce a place discovered Ticked: when the player discovers a marker up close ("Once discovered up close"), a small message announces it at the top of the screen. annoncer Yes or no yes Map background Plan: a plan drawn from the scene's data (the streets by importance, water, parks, squares, relief, district names), in the colors chosen here. View: the scene seen from above, like a photo. A drawn map (below) comes before both. fond_carte Choice in a list Plan plan: Planvue: View from above Plan: background colorshown only if Map background is “Plan” The ground, between the streets (the blocks, the countryside). plan_fond Color #1b1e24 Plan: main roadsshown only if Map background is “Plan” Avenues and boulevards (four lanes and more). plan_grandes_rues Color #b4b9c1 Plan: streetsshown only if Map background is “Plan” Ordinary streets. plan_rues Color #8a909a Plan: small streetsshown only if Map background is “Plan” Alleys, one-way streets and pedestrian streets. plan_petites_rues Color #646a74 Plan: pathsshown only if Map background is “Plan” Trails and dirt tracks (hidden on the map seen from far away). plan_chemins Color #454a53 Plan: street width (times their real width)shown only if Map background is “Plan” 0.5 (the default): thin lines, like a street map; 1: the width of the roadway; more: thicker lines, easier to read from afar. plan_largeur_rues Number 0.5 from 0.2 to 4 Plan: watershown only if Map background is “Plan” The sea, lakes and rivers. plan_eau Color #1d3047 Plan: parksshown only if Map background is “Plan” The parks and gardens the plan knows. plan_parcs Color #1f2e25 Plan: squaresshown only if Map background is “Plan” Squares and esplanades. plan_places Color #252931 Plan: buildingsshown only if Map background is “Plan” Ticked: the footprint of each building, in a color of its own. plan_batiments Yes or no no Plan: buildings colorshown only if Plan: buildings is ticked The footprint of the buildings, a little lighter or darker than the background to stay discreet. plan_couleur_batiments Color #262a32 Plan: relief shadingshown only if Map background is “Plan” 0: a flat ground; 1: well marked hills. plan_relief Number 0.25 from 0 to 1 Plan: district namesshown only if Map background is “Plan” The names of districts and towns, in capitals, on both maps. plan_noms Yes or no yes Plan: names colorshown only if Plan: district names is ticked The color of the district and town names. plan_couleur_noms Color #c9ced6 Plan: letter spacing of the namesshown only if Plan: district names is ticked The names in capitals, their letters tight (the default), spaced by a thin space (if the font has it; otherwise "?"), or by a full space. plan_noms_espacement Choice in a list None fin: Thinlarge: Wideaucun: None Plan: font of the names (empty: the game's)shown only if Plan: district names is ticked A font shipped with WorldMint ("inter", "manrope"...) or a font added to the project ("projet:<id>"). plan_police Text (empty) Plan: background under the names (opacity)shown only if Plan: district names is ticked A dark rounded background under each name, so that it reads over the GPS line and the streets; 0: no background. plan_noms_fond Number 0.55 from 0 to 1 A single marker at the destination With the GPS: the diamond at the end of the line replaces the objective's marker on the maps (its name stays on the big map). destination_seule Yes or no yes Scale on the big map A scale bar at the bottom left ("200 m"), which follows the zoom. echelle Yes or no yes Image of the player on the maps (empty: an arrow) Turned where they look: an arrow of your own, pointing up, on a transparent background. image_joueur Image from the library (empty) Image of the minimap frame Laid over the whole minimap (a ring, a decorated frame); its middle transparent. image_cadre Image from the library (empty) Merchants icon An image of your own, in its colors, for each merchant without its own. picto_marchands Image from the library (empty) Characters icon Likewise, for the characters who talk. picto_personnages Image from the library (empty) Objectives icon Likewise, for quest objectives. picto_objectifs Image from the library (empty) Places icon Likewise, for the places that carry this system. picto_lieux Image from the library (empty) My markers icon Likewise, for the markers placed by the player. picto_mes_reperes Image from the library (empty) Drawn map (empty: the view from above taken by the game) An image of the map, drawn by hand or taken elsewhere. Empty: the game takes a picture of the scene from above by itself, when the game starts. dessin Image from the library (empty) What the drawn map covers The part of the world the drawn map shows, so that the player and the markers fall in the right place. By default, the same square as the view from above taken by the game: draw over a capture of it. dessin_zone Choice in a list The whole scene, like the view from above auto: The whole scene, like the view from abovemanuelle: A square I give West edge of the drawn map (x, in m)shown only if What the drawn map covers is “A square I give” The x position of the left edge of the image, in the world. North is at the top of the image. dessin_x Number 0 from -100 000 to 100 000 North edge of the drawn map (z, in m)shown only if What the drawn map covers is “A square I give” The z position of the top edge of the image, in the world: the smallest, as north is towards -z. dessin_z Number 0 from -100 000 to 100 000 Side of the drawn map (m)shown only if What the drawn map covers is “A square I give” How many meters of the world the image covers, from edge to edge. A square image works best. dessin_cote Number 100 from 1 to 100 000 Compass at the top of the screen Ticked: a band at the top of the screen scrolls when the player turns the camera, with N, NE, E… and the degrees. Quest objectives, their markers and the places nearby sit at their direction, with the distance of the nearest objective. With it, a game can do without the minimap, like a survival game. boussole Yes or no no Place of the compass At the top in the middle, as in most games; or at the bottom in the middle, if the top is already taken. boussole_position Choice in a list At the top, in the middle haut: At the top, in the middlebas: At the bottom, in the middle Places shown on the compass up to (m) The places visible on the map show on the compass when the player is closer than this distance. Quest objectives and the player's markers are always on it. boussole_portee Number 150 from 10 to 5000 The player places their own markers Ticked: on the big map, a right click (or Y on a gamepad, at the crosshair in the middle) places a marker, "Marker 1", "Marker 2"…; clicking it removes it. They are also on the minimap and the compass, and the saved game keeps them. reperes_joueur Yes or no yes Markers shared with the other players With several players, ticked: a marker placed by one player shows for everyone, and anyone can remove it. Unticked: each has their own. reperes_groupe Yes or no no Most markers at once How many markers the player (or the group, if they are shared) can place at the same time. They remove one to place another. reperes_max Number 10 from 1 to 50, as a whole number Color of the player's markers The color of the triangle that marks a marker placed by the player. couleur_reperes Color #ff6fb5 Legend to tick on the big map Ticked: on the right of the big map, one line per kind of marker (merchants, characters, objectives, players, my markers, places). A click shows or hides it, on the big map and the minimap; the choice is kept for the player. legende Yes or no yes List of quests beside the big map If the game has the Quest log, ticked: on the left of the big map, the quests in progress. A click on one centers the map on its objective. liste_quetes Yes or no yes Hide what is not explored yet Ticked: on the big map and the minimap, the places the player has not been to yet stay covered by a shadow. They uncover them by walking around. Places under the shadow do not show, except quest objectives and the player's markers. The saved game keeps what is uncovered. Good for an exploration or survival game. brouillard Yes or no no Distance uncovered around the player (m) Everything closer than this distance to the player is uncovered on the map as they go by. The map is cut into 32 × 32 squares: on a very large scene, the edges are wider. brouillard_rayon Number 25 from 2 to 500 Color of what is hidden The color that covers the places not explored yet. brouillard_couleur Color #14161c What one player uncovers is uncovered for all With several players, ticked: the players explore the same map, what one uncovers shows for everyone. Unticked: each uncovers their own. brouillard_groupe Yes or no no Objective marker on screen Ticked: the objective of the tracked quest shows in the world, above its target, with its distance ("120 m"). When the target is out of view or behind the camera, the marker sticks to the edge of the screen, with an arrow towards it. It gets smaller and paler as it gets farther. repere_ecran Yes or no yes Markers on screen forshown only if Objective marker on screen is ticked The tracked quest: the one shown on the right of the screen (the last one started). All: the objectives of every quest in progress, the six nearest. repere_ecran_quetes Choice in a list The tracked quest only suivie: The tracked quest onlytoutes: All the quests in progress Look of the marker on screenshown only if Objective marker on screen is ticked With the distance written under the icon, or the icon alone, more discreet. repere_ecran_style Choice in a list Icon and distance icone_distance: Icon and distanceicone: Icon only Hide the marker closer than (m)shown only if Objective marker on screen is ticked Right next to the objective, the marker fades away so as not to hide it. Inside the area of a place to reach, it fades away too. repere_ecran_masquer Number 10 from 0 to 1000 Color of the marker on screenshown only if Objective marker on screen is ticked The color of the icon, its arrow and the distance. repere_ecran_couleur Color #ffcc33 Image of the marker on screen (empty: a diamond)shown only if Objective marker on screen is ticked An icon of your own, preferably square on a transparent background; the color tints it (white leaves it as it is). repere_ecran_image Image from the library (empty) Size of the marker on screen (share of the screen height)shown only if Objective marker on screen is ticked Its size up close; it gets smaller as it gets farther. repere_ecran_taille Number 0.034 from 0.015 to 0.1 "!" and "?" above the characters Ticked: a "!" above a character who can give a quest (their Dialogue gives it, or they are the quest's giver), which goes away when it starts; a "?" above the one to talk to or hand something to for the current step. Grey when the quest is not available yet. On screen and on the maps. icones_donneurs Yes or no yes "!" and "?" visible on screen up to (m)shown only if "!" and "?" above the characters is ticked Farther away, the icon no longer shows above the character (it stays on the maps). icones_portee Number 50 from 5 to 1000 Color of the "!"shown only if "!" and "?" above the characters is ticked The color of the "!" of a quest to take. icone_donneur_couleur Color #ffd23f Color of the "?"shown only if "!" and "?" above the characters is ticked The color of the "?" above the one to talk to or hand something to. icone_rendre_couleur Color #ffd23f Color of a quest not available yetshown only if "!" and "?" above the characters is ticked The "!" of a quest still missing a condition (a level, an item) takes this color. icone_indisponible_couleur Color #9aa0a6 Image of the "!" (empty: the sign)shown only if "!" and "?" above the characters is ticked An icon of your own instead of the "!", preferably square on a transparent background. Grey when the quest is not available yet. icone_donneur_image Image from the library (empty) Image of the "?" (empty: the sign)shown only if "!" and "?" above the characters is ticked An icon of your own instead of the "?", preferably square on a transparent background. icone_rendre_image Image from the library (empty)

items.title: Settings on each object
items.text:
In the Properties of an object or folder that carries the system, Systems section. A folder passes its values on to what it contains; an object can change a value for itself only.

Setting What it does Name in code Type Default Limits or choices Name on the map (empty: its name, without number) The name written under the marker, such as "Village" or "Forge". Empty: the object's name without number ("Tower 2" is written "Tower"). nom Text (empty) Shape of the marker The shape of the marker on the map, in its color; or an image, such as a sword icon for the forge. forme Choice in a list Circle rond: Circlelosange: Diamondtriangle: Trianglecarre: Squareetoile: Starimage: An image Color of the marker The color of the shape. For an image, it tints it: white leaves it as it is. couleur Color #4da3ff Image of the markershown only if Shape of the marker is “An image” The icon shown on the map, preferably square, on a transparent background. image Image from the library (empty) Size of the marker 1 for the usual size, 2 for a marker twice as big: a town, a dungeon. taille Number 1 from 0.5 to 3 When it shows on the map Always: from the start. Once discovered up close: when the player has come near enough, or a carte.reveler event reveals it; it stays so in a saved and loaded game. Hidden: only while it is the objective of a quest in progress. visible Choice in a list Always toujours: Alwaysdecouvert: Once discovered up closecache: Hidden, except as a quest objective Discovery distance (m)shown only if When it shows on the map is “Once discovered up close” How many meters away the player must come to discover this marker. distance Number 15 from 1 to 1000 Objective of the quest (its title, optional) The exact title of a quest of the Quest log: while it is in progress, this marker is its objective, ringed. Useful when the step does not name the object, such as "Go back to the miller". quete Text (empty) Only during step no. (0: the whole quest) The number of the step, from 1, during which this marker is the objective: 2 for the second step. 0: during the whole quest. quete_etape Number 0 from 0 to 100, as a whole number

items.title: Controls added to the game
items.text:
They appear in the Game controls panel (Developer mode), where you can change their key.

Control Name for scripts Key Gamepad Open the map carte M ↓ Zoom the big map in carte_rapprocher Page Up RT Zoom the big map out carte_eloigner Page Down LT Place or remove a marker on the big map carte_repere Right-click Y

items.title: Events
items.text: The descriptions come from the code.

items.title: What it announces
items.text: Event Fields Description carte.ouverte ouvert (boolean) The big map opened (ouvert true) or closed (ouvert false). The world is stopped while it is open, unless its setting says otherwise. carte.decouvert cible (id) The player discovered a map marker (cible), one shown only once discovered: they came near enough, or carte.reveler revealed it. It now shows on the map.

items.title: What it listens to
items.text: Event Fields Description carte.reveler cible (id) Ask the map to reveal the marker of cible, as if the player had come near: a character who tells where a place is, a scroll read, a quest step. quetes.debut quete (text), groupe (boolean?) A quest started: quete is its title. groupe (Journal de quêtes 8): true for a quest of the whole group (game setting groupe), sent once for the group, joueur being who moved it on. quetes.etape_debut quete (text), etape (number), texte (text), groupe (boolean?) A step of a quest starts (Journal de quêtes 11, events version 33): it becomes one to do now, its other ways to end it too. etape is its rank in the quest (from 1), texte what it says. Sent after quetes.debut for the first steps, then after the quetes.etape that opened it, and again when the step starts over (an "Also fails if" row set to recommence) or the quest resumes at it (quetes.reprise); its own annonce_debut event follows. Not sent again when a saved game is loaded. groupe (Journal de quêtes 8): true for a quest of the whole group. quetes.etape quete (text), etape (number), texte (text), issue (number?), suite (text?), groupe (boolean?) A step of a quest is done: etape is its rank in the quest (from 1), texte what it said. Sent before quetes.fin when it was the last one. issue (Journal de quêtes 11): the rank (from 1) of the other way to end the step that did it, absent when the step itself did; texte is then that way's text. suite (Journal de quêtes 11): the label the quest goes to next (fin, echec or a step's label), absent when it simply goes on to the next row. groupe (Journal de quêtes 8): true for a quest of the whole group (game setting groupe), sent once for the group, joueur being who moved it on. quetes.etape_echec quete (text), etape (number), alors (text), manquee (boolean?), groupe (boolean?) A step of a quest failed (Journal de quêtes 11, events version 33): one of its "Also fails if" rows happened. etape is its rank in the quest (from 1), alors what that row does: echoue (the quest fails, quetes.echec follows), recommence (the step starts again from zero) or etiquette (the quest goes to the row's label). Also sent for an "Also fails if" row under the quest itself that does not make it fail (recommence: the quest starts again; etiquette), etape being then the step it was waiting for (0: none). For an optional step, manquee is true: the step is only missed, the quest goes on without it. groupe: true for a quest of the whole group. quetes.reprise quete (text), etape (number), groupe (boolean?) A quest resumes (Journal de quêtes 11, events version 33): tried again after a failure (the log's Try again button, reessayer auto, quetes.reessayer, or given again when it does not start over), or started again by an "Also fails if" row of the quest set to recommence. etape is the step it resumes at (from 1; 0: none). The steps before it stay done; marks stay set and the world is not put back as it was: a Trigger rule on the step's annonce_debut does that. groupe: true for a quest of the whole group. quetes.fin quete (text), xp (number?), piste (text?), groupe (boolean?), facultatives (table?) A quest is finished: all its steps are done. Its reward, if any, has been asked to the inventory. xp and piste (version 28): its XP for the Progression module and the track that gets it (empty: the main one). facultatives (Journal de quêtes 11): {faites, total}, how many of its optional steps were done, out of how many; absent when it has none. groupe (Journal de quêtes 8): true for a quest of the whole group (game setting groupe), sent once for the group, joueur being who moved it on. quetes.echec quete (text), groupe (boolean?) A quest failed: an event, a mark, its time ran out, or quetes.echouer. It gives no reward; it may be given again if its settings allow it. groupe (Journal de quêtes 8): true for a quest of the whole group (game setting groupe), sent once for the group, joueur being who moved it on. quetes.abandon quete (text), groupe (boolean?) The player abandoned a quest from the log (or quetes.abandonner asked for it). It gives no reward; it may be given again if its settings allow it. groupe (Journal de quêtes 8): true for a quest of the whole group (game setting groupe), sent once for the group, joueur being who moved it on. scene.change depuis (text), vers (text) Sent by the engine once the player has arrived in another scene of the game (game.go_to, or a passage). Scripts keep running across scenes: this is when a module looks at the objects of the new scene. menu.pause ouvert (boolean) The pause menu opened (ouvert true) or closed (ouvert false). The world is stopped while it is open.

items.title: Points a script can replace (game.override)
items.text:
The descriptions come from the code.

  • carte.texte: function(default, key) -> the text the map shows for that key: titre, fermer, aide, decouvert, vous. It may hold {nom}, replaced afterwards. The default is the game's translation of the text in the original language (a built-in text of the map in translations_get); without one, French or English, after the player's language.
  • carte.couleur_joueur: function(default, joueur) -> the color ("#rrggbb") of that other player's arrow and name on the map, such as their team's color. The default is a color of their player number (game.player_number), the same for everyone.

items.title: What the agent knows about this system
items.text: The text the agent reads before using this system.

items.title: Map (carte)
items.text:
A minimap in a corner of the screen, the player in the middle as an arrow, and a big map of the whole scene opened with the control carte (M, or ↓ on a gamepad), zoomed with the mouse wheel or with the controls carte_rapprocher (Page Up, or the right trigger RT on a gamepad) and carte_eloigner (Page Down, or the left trigger LT), held, and moved by dragging with the mouse, with the gamepad's left stick or with the walking keys. While the map has the gamepad's focus the player does not move, so LT (also run) does not make them run. Add it with modules_add when the user asks for a map, a minimap, markers or places to discover: do not build a map yourself.

The picture is the scene seen from above, taken by the engine when the scene starts (north, -Z, at the top), without the player and characters. The game setting dessin can give a drawn map instead (an image file): by default it covers the same square as the engine's view (dessin_zone "auto"); with dessin_zone "manuelle", dessin_x, dessin_z (its north-west corner) and dessin_cote (its side, in metres) say where it lies.

Markers, without code: place the system on an object (systems_attach), at its position, or on a group or folder: one marker for everything inside, sub-folders included, in the middle of the box enclosing its pieces (the folder's own position does not matter), discovered when the player comes within distance of that box. A piece inside with its own values for carte (systems_set on it) becomes its own marker. Its object settings:

  • nom: the name shown under it on the big map; empty, the name of the object or group without a trailing number. Write it in the user's language.
  • forme: rond, losange, triangle, carre, etoile, or image with image (an icon file, find one with assets_search and kind "image"); couleur ("#rrggbb", tints an image); taille (1 usual, up to 3).
  • visible: toujours; decouvert, shown once the player came within distance metres, or when your script or a declencheur rule sends carte.reveler {cible = id} (the object or group, or any piece of the group); cache, shown only while it is a quest objective.
  • quete and quete_etape: the exact title of a quetes quest (and a step number, 0 for the whole quest) for which this marker is the objective, such as the miller for "Go back to the miller".

What marks itself (game settings marchands and personnages, on by default): objects carrying boutique (a golden diamond) and dialogue (a light blue circle), named after the shop or the character, one marker per object or group they are placed on. Placing carte on one of them chooses its look instead.

Quest objectives (game setting objectifs, couleur_objectif): while a quetes step is active, the markers it names are ringed in that color, and on the minimap they stay at its edge, pointing the way. A step names objects through fin_cible (the "Loup" of "Vaincre 3 loups": every marker on an object or group named "Loup", "Loup 2"...) or its fin_lieu (a lieu or tenir step), and so do the other ways to end it (issue rows: both doors of a branch are objectives until one is taken); or a marker names its quest with quete. The quest log is not changed: the map reads what it publishes at each quetes.* event (version 13, below).

Other game settings: mini_carte (shown or not), mini_coin (bas_droite by default, bas_gauche, haut_droite, haut_gauche; the inventory and the current quest step are at the top right), mini_taille (share of the screen height), mini_forme (ronde or carree), mini_etendue (metres shown from edge to edge), mini_tourne (turns with the player, otherwise north up), cadre_marge (the map tucked inside a theme frame), grande_carte (the M window), pause_fenetre (the world stops while it is open, and the big map is a screen of its own: the rest of the HUD, such as the hotbar, health or the quest tracker, is hidden with game.hud_only({"carte.", "Grande carte/"}) until it closes; a pause menu opened over it (menu.pause) still shows), noms (names on the big map), annoncer (a message when a marker is discovered).

  • Events announced: carte.ouverte (ouvert), carte.decouvert (cible: the object or group the system is placed on, once for all its pieces). Listened: carte.reveler (cible).
  • The minimap hides during a pause (a menu, a dialogue, a shop) and while the big map is open.
  • Saved games keep the places already discovered, in every scene (on_save, on_load): a loaded game shows them again without announcing them.
  • Texts follow the player's language: the map's own texts are built-in texts of the system, listed by translations_get (French and English are built in). To change a word, override carte.texte from a game script: game.override("carte.texte", function(default, key) if key == "titre" then return "Atlas" end return default(key) end). Keys: titre, fermer, aide, decouvert (with {nom}), vous; version 10: aide_repere (with {touche}), repere (with {n}), distance (with {d}), legende, quetes, s_objectifs, s_lieux, s_marchands, s_personnages, s_joueurs, s_mes_reperes, and the compass points n, ne, e, se, s, so, o, no; version 14: donne ("!") and rendre ("?").
  • When the world changes a lot (a bridge built, a forest burnt), game.map_refresh() from a script takes the picture again.
  • A frame from an interface pack (a ring around the minimap): not a script. Set the interface theme row {"sorte": "cadre", "role": "cadre.minicarte", "image": "<the ring>"} (cadre.carte for the big map): the engine draws it over the map, its markers and the north, under the player's arrow, and drops the dark outline of the minimap's disc. Then the game setting cadre_marge (a share of the map's size, 0 by default; 0.06 to 0.12 for a thick ring) tucks the map inside the frame so it does not show under the ring. Check it with capture_steps.
  • Its windows are screens delivered by the system (modules/carte/ecrans/, version 12), which its script shows and fills:
  • « Grande carte » (the big map): Fenêtre, Titre, Place (where the map picture goes: its height in the file is the map's height, the map stays square), Aide, Aide repère (hidden without reperes_joueur), Fermer (action fermer); on its right Légende with Titre de la légende and the list Sortes (row Sorte, a button, action legende), on its left Quêtes with Titre des quêtes and the list Liste des quêtes (row Quête, action quete). The two side panels are placed against the window by the script and hidden when empty.
  • « Lieux découverts » (top centre): Fond, the list Lignes (row Annonce, the last three).
  • « Mini-carte ronde » or « Mini-carte carrée » (after mini_forme): Fond, the dark disc or square under the map; its place and size follow mini_coin, mini_taille and cadre_marge.
  • « Boussole » or « Boussole en bas » (after boussole_position): Bande, the band; the letters, ticks and markers are drawn on it at its place and size. Change their look with screens_set (styles, not hand-made values); never draw them again with game.hud_*, and never edit the system. What follows the world at every step stays drawn by the script over them, with keys starting with carte. (no shape can carry it: the engine's picture of the map with a moving, turning part, the fog mask, the turned arrows and markers, the north, the theme frame, the scrolling graduations): do not use that prefix in a game script.
  • Testing: in game_run, read the report's hud: carte.mini.r.<n> are the minimap markers, carte.mini.o.<n> the rings of objectives, carte.mini.joueur the arrow; press carte and read Grande carte/Fenêtre, carte.g.n.<n> (the names on the big map) and carte.grande.image (its uv, the part of the map shown). A discovered place is announced in Lieux découverts/Annonce#1. wheel and mouse in a segment zoom and drag it, stick ([x, y], y down) moves it, actions carte_rapprocher or carte_eloigner held zoom it in or out. A discovery sends carte.decouvert, counted in the report's events.
  • After a saved game is loaded, the map reads the quests in progress from the quest log (shared.quetes_en_cours, version 11): the objective is back on the map, the compass and the quest list at once, for each player, guests included. A failed or abandoned quest (quetes.echec, quetes.abandon) loses its objective.
  • Version 13: the map no longer works out the active step itself; it reads what the quest log publishes (shared.quetes_en_cours: active steps and other ways to end them, their targets and places) at each quetes.* event (quetes.reprise included: a quest tried again after a failure gets its objective back). The objective follows the branch taken; an optional step's target is an objective while it is doable. The fin_lieu of an active lieu or tenir step is an objective even without this system on it, and with objectif_zone (on by default) the minimap and the big map show the area of its fin_rayon around it (carte.mini.z.<n>, carte.g.z.<n> in the report's hud).

items.title: Objective marker on screen and quest-giver icons (version 14)
items.text:
• repere_ecran (on by default): the objective of the tracked quest (the one in the quest tracker, the last started; repere_ecran_quetes toutes: every quest in progress, the six nearest) shows in the world above its target, with its distance ("120 m"; repere_ecran_style icone for the icon alone). Out of view or behind the camera, it sticks to the screen's edge with an arrow towards the target (behind: at the bottom). It gets smaller and paler with distance, and hides closer than repere_ecran_masquer metres (10) or inside the area of a place to reach. repere_ecran_couleur, repere_ecran_taille (share of the screen height), repere_ecran_image (an icon of the user's, tinted; empty: a diamond). Its objectives are the map's own (a fin_cible, a fin_lieu, a marker naming its quest): nothing to add. Turn it off for a game that wants the player to look (exploration, survival) or a race.
  • icones_donneurs (on by default): a "!" above a character who can give a quest not started yet (or to take up again): the quest's donneur (quetes), or else every character whose dialogue sends the quest's depart_evenement (an annonce) or sets its depart_marque (a marque). It goes away when the quest starts. A "?" above the one to talk to or hand something to for an active step: the fin_cible of a remettre step or of a dialogue.* event step ("Revenir voir le meunier" with dialogue.fin and "Meunier"). Grey (icone_indisponible_couleur) while the quest is not available yet (conditions to come). On screen within icones_portee metres (50), and on the minimap and the big map above the character's marker. icone_donneur_couleur, icone_rendre_couleur, icone_donneur_image, icone_rendre_image (the user's own icons; empty: the sign). The signs are texts donne and rendre of carte.texte.
  • Nothing is worked out here: the map reads shared.quetes_en_cours (suivie, rendre) and shared.quetes_donneurs from the quest log.
  • Testing: the report's hud has carte.e.r.<n> (the marker), carte.e.d.<n> (its distance, "40 m"), carte.e.a.<n> (its arrow, at the edge only), carte.e.i.<n> (a "!" or "?" on screen, text [b]![/b]), and carte.mini.i.<n> / carte.g.i.<n> on the maps. They hide during a pause and while the big map is open.

items.title: Fog of war (version 11)
items.text:
• brouillard (off by default): on the big map and the minimap, what the player has not approached yet stays covered in brouillard_couleur (dark by default). Walking uncovers everything within brouillard_rayon metres (25 by default) around the player. Places under the fog do not show (on the map, the minimap and the compass), except quest objectives and the player's own markers. Saved games keep it, for each player, in each scene. brouillard_groupe: what one player uncovers is uncovered for everyone; otherwise each has their own.
  • When to turn it on: exploration, survival, an adventure where discovering the world is part of the fun (Valheim, Enshrouded, Zelda style). Leave it off for a shooter, a race, a town or farm game, a small arena, or when the player must read the whole map at once.
  • The map area is cut into 32 × 32 squares: the edges are smooth curves, about one square wide; on a very large scene (more than about 1 km), the uncovered area grows by bigger steps. It costs one HUD element per map (an image @mask: the engine computes), whatever is uncovered: sent to guests like any image.
  • Testing: the report's hud has carte.mini.brouillard (minimap) and, map open, carte.g.brouillard (big map); their text is the mask.

items.title: Compass, the player's markers, legend and quest list (version 10)
items.text:
• Compass (game setting boussole, off by default; boussole_position haut or bas, in the middle): a band that scrolls as the camera turns, with N, NE, E… every 45°, degrees every 30° and ticks every 15°, a fixed mark in the middle. On it, at their heading: quest objectives (held at the band's edge when behind), the player's markers, and the places visible on the map within boussole_portee metres; the distance of the nearest objective is written under it. Style panneau.boussole for its background (the shape Bande). It hides during a pause and while the big map is open. Only what fits in the band is created (about 20 HUD elements).
  • Compass or minimap? A survival game in the manner of Rust (find your way by the sun and landmarks) sets boussole on and mini_carte off: the big map (M) stays for planning. An adventure or RPG game with towns, merchants and quests keeps the minimap, and may add the compass for the quest objective's direction (Valheim, WoW style). With both, put the minimap in a bottom corner (mini_coin) so the top stays clear.
  • The player's markers (reperes_joueur, on by default): on the big map, the control carte_repere (right click, or Y on a gamepad at the crosshair in the middle of the view) places "Marker 1", "Marker 2"… at that spot, or removes the one there; a left click without dragging on one removes it too. They show on the big map, the minimap and the compass, in couleur_reperes, at most reperes_max. Saved games keep them, for each player, in each scene. reperes_groupe: shared with all the players (anyone can remove one); otherwise each has their own.
  • Legend (legende, on by default): on the right of the big map, one button per kind of marker present (objectives, places, merchants, characters, players, my markers); a click hides or shows that kind on the big map and the minimap, kept for the player by saved games. Its rows (Grande carte/Sorte#<row>) have the style coche.carte, selected while shown.
  • Quest list (liste_quetes, on by default, only with the quetes system): on the left of the big map, the quests in progress; a click centers the map on its objective. It does not change the quest log.
  • Testing: with boussole, the report's hud has Boussole/Bande (the band; Boussole en bas/Bande at the bottom), carte.b.l.<n> (its letters and degrees), carte.b.r.<n> (markers, carte.b.o.<n> rings of objectives) and carte.b.d (the distance). Map open: Grande carte/Sorte#<row> (legend rows, in the order objectives, places, merchants, characters, players, my markers; selected while shown), Grande carte/Quête#<row> (quests), and the player's markers named carte.g.n.<n> "Marker 1"... A guest in game_run « players » sees their own.

items.title: Several players
items.text:
One copy per player: each player has their own minimap, map window, discovered places, compass, legend choices and markers (unless reperes_groupe shares the markers).

The other players show by themselves (game setting joueurs: partout by default, on the minimap and the big map; grande, only on the big map; aucun, nowhere, for hide and seek): an arrow turned where they look, in a color of their player number (the same for everyone; a game script gives another one, such as a team's, with game.override("carte.couleur_joueur", function(default, joueur) ... end)), and their name (game.player_name: their character's name or nickname), on the guests' maps as on the host's. Do not place carte on the player's character for that: the markers would all carry the copied character's look. Placed there anyway, it chooses the look of the others' markers, which are named after each player (never after the object), and nobody sees one on themselves. Testing: with game_run « players », a guest's hud has carte.mini.j.<n> (the arrows), carte.mini.jn.<n> and, map open, carte.g.jn.<n> (the names).

items.title: GPS (version 15)
items.text:
• gps (aucun by default, so a game without it is unchanged; auto: by vehicle while the player drives (game.driving()), on foot otherwise; a_pied; vehicule): a line on the minimap and the big map from the player to the objective of the quest highest in the quest log (the nearest of its objectives), or to the player's last marker (gps_cible: auto the last marker placed, otherwise the objective; objectif; repere). The way comes from game.route: in a generated city it follows the streets (by vehicle in the driving direction, through roundabouts by their ring and the left-turn lanes; on foot both ways), elsewhere the walkable areas (game.path). The map never computes a way itself.
  • By vehicle the route may change to the next lane of the same direction (gps_changement_voie, 15 m added) and turns back only at the end of a dead end (gps_demi_tour, 300 m added).
  • It is redone when the target changes or moves more than gps_ecart metres (15), when the player strays more than gps_ecart from the line, or gets in or out of a vehicle (auto); checked a few times a second. It is one smooth thick line (a curve through the points of game.route with axe = true: the middle of the streets, not the shifted lane), round ends, a glow: gps_couleur (#3d8bff), gps_epaisseur (pixels for a 1080 high screen, 7), gps_halo (pixels, 5), gps_halo_couleur (empty: the line's), gps_halo_opacite (0.3). The destination is a diamond of the line's color (image_destination: an image of the user's). mini_distance writes the distance along the route under the minimap; panneau_destination shows on the big map the destination's name, district and distance.
  • When to turn it on: a town or open-world game with quests or deliveries (GTA, a taxi or delivery game), or a large world where the way is not obvious. Leave it off for a small level, an arena, or an exploration game where finding the way is the point.
  • Testing: the report's hud has carte.mini.gps (an image @trace:..., laid like the map image), carte.mini.destination, carte.mini.distance and, map open, carte.g.gps, carte.g.destination, carte.g.dest.nom, carte.g.dest.lieu, carte.g.echelle.texte.

items.title: The map's look (version 15)
items.text:
• fond_carte (plan by default): the map is a vector plan made once from the scene's data (game.map_plan: the streets of a generated city by importance, water, parks, squares, buildings, the relief and water of the terrain) and drawn in the game's colors, with the district and town names in capitals (plan_noms, mini_noms). vue: the photo of the scene seen from above, as before. A drawn map (dessin) comes before both.
  • Theme, by hand in the system's settings or with modules_configure: plan_fond, plan_grandes_rues, plan_rues, plan_petites_rues, plan_chemins, plan_largeur_rues (times the real width, 0.5), plan_eau, plan_parcs, plan_places, plan_batiments + plan_couleur_batiments, plan_relief, plan_couleur_noms. To match a reference image (a dark slate plan with light streets and a bright route): set the background, the four street colors, water and parks from it, then gps_couleur, gps_halo.
  • Minimap: mini_forme arrondie by default (a rounded rectangle, mini_arrondi, with a thin border mini_bordure, mini_bordure_couleur, mini_bordure_opacite), ronde or carree; mini_coin, mini_taille, mini_tourne (turns with the player, or north fixed), a "N" badge. image_cadre lays an image over it (a decorated ring).
  • Images of the user's: image_joueur (the player's arrow, pointing up), image_destination, image_cadre, and one icon per kind of marker: picto_marchands, picto_personnages, picto_objectifs, picto_lieux, picto_mes_reperes (in their own colors; a marker's own image wins).
  • Names: in capitals with spaced letters (plan_noms_espacement: aucun by default, fin a thin space if the font has one, large a full space), in plan_police (a shipped font such as manrope, or projet:<id>; empty: the game's), on a dark rounded background (plan_noms_fond, its opacity). A name never covers the route, the player or the destination: it moves to the nearest free place, or hides (game.map_labels, recomputed when the route or the zoom changes).
  • Plan content from a generated city: the street axes (cut at a roundabout's island), the ring and island of each roundabout, parks (free ground in grass) and squares (paved free ground), building footprints, district and town names; the terrain adds its sea and lakes.
  • Destination: destination_seule (on): the diamond at the end of the line replaces the objective's marker on the maps. The line starts and ends on the street: the walk from the street to an off-street target is not drawn.
  • Big map: zoom and drag as before, the destination panel, a scale bar (echelle, "200 m"), the legend with the icon of each kind (its picto_*, or its shape and color), placing a marker.
  • Never copy a game's name, sprites or texts into another: the user gives their own images in these settings.

This page is generated automatically from the WorldMint code (modules/carte/module.json, modules/carte/AGENT.md, modules/events.json): it always matches the editor.

items.title: Chat
items.text:
The chat of games with several players: the T key (can be changed) opens a line, Enter sends it to everyone with the player's name, Escape cancels. Arrivals, departures and server messages are written in it. Admins type the server's commands in it (/kick Léa). This system sets all of it: the key, the commands' names and who may use them, the command sign, the anti-spam, the display and the texts. Without it, the chat works with its default settings.

Identifier chat Version 1 Placed on objects no

items.title: Settings for the whole game
items.text:
In the Systems panel (Developer mode), by opening the system's card.

Setting What it does Name in code Type Default Limits or choices Players talk to each other Ticked: each player opens the chat with its key (T by default) and writes a line everyone sees, with their name. Unticked: only the game's messages and the commands go through. joueurs_parlent Yes or no yes Arrivals and departures in the chat Ticked: "Léa joined the game", "Léa left the game" are written in the chat. messages_systeme Yes or no yes Lines shown How many lines the chat box shows, the newest at the bottom. lignes Number 8 from 1 to 30 Display time (seconds) A line fades out that many seconds after it arrived. While the chat is open, every line shows. duree Number 10 from 1 to 600 Length of a message (characters) At most that many bytes per message (an accented letter counts as two); the rest is cut. longueur_max Number 200 from 10 to 200 Messages in a row (anti-spam) How many messages a player can send at once; then one more every "Wait between two messages". rafale Number 5 from 1 to 50 Wait between two messages (seconds) Once their messages in a row are sent, the player gets one back every that many seconds. Beyond: "Slow down". recharge Number 1.5 from 0.1 to 120 Command sign What starts a command in the chat, like /kick Léa: 1 to 3 signs (no letter or digit). The server console accepts it too, without needing it. prefixe Text / The commands and their names Each server command, the names typed for it (the first is its name, the others aliases, separated by commas) and who may use it. The names work in the chat and in the server console. With no name it is off. The web management page does not depend on them. commandes List of “Command” [{'commande': 'aide', 'noms': 'aide, help', 'niveau': 'tous'}, {'commande': 'joueurs', 'noms': 'joueurs, players', 'niveau': 'admin'}, {'commande': 'dire', 'noms': 'dire, say', 'niveau': 'admin'}, {'commande': 'expulser', 'noms': 'expulser, kick', 'niveau': 'admin'}, {'commande': 'bannir', 'noms': 'bannir, ban', 'niveau': 'admin'}, {'commande': 'debannir', 'noms': 'debannir, unban', 'niveau': 'admin'}, {'commande': 'blanche', 'noms': 'blanche, whitelist', 'niveau': 'admin'}, {'commande': 'admin', 'noms': 'admin', 'niveau': 'admin'}, {'commande': 'sauver', 'noms': 'sauver, save', 'niveau': 'admin'}, {'commande': 'copies', 'noms': 'copies, backups', 'niveau': 'admin'}, {'commande': 'restaurer', 'noms': 'restaurer, restore', 'niveau': 'admin'}, {'commande': 'regler', 'noms': 'regler, set', 'niveau': 'admin'}, {'commande': 'arreter', 'noms': 'arreter, stop', 'niveau': 'admin'}, {'commande': 'motdepasse', 'noms': 'motdepasse, password', 'niveau': 'admin'}, {'commande': 'motdepasse_web', 'noms': 'motdepasse_web, webpassword', 'niveau': 'admin'}, {'commande': 'recharger', 'noms': 'recharger, reload', 'niveau': 'admin'}, {'commande': 'personnage', 'noms': 'personnage, character', 'niveau': 'admin'}, {'commande': 'xp', 'noms': 'xp, givexp', 'niveau': 'admin'}, {'commande': 'niveau', 'noms': 'niveau, setlevel', 'niveau': 'admin'}, {'commande': 'rendre_points', 'noms': 'rendre_points, refund', 'niveau': 'admin'}] one line per “Command”: its fields

items.title: The fields of each “Command”
items.text:
In the Properties, each “Command” has its own numbered frame; Add: Command adds one, the cross removes it. A field only appears when it is useful: under its name, the table says when.

Setting What it does Name in code Type Default Limits or choices Command What the command does; it keeps this identifier whatever its name. commande Choice in a list Help (the list of commands) aide: Help (the list of commands)joueurs: Players (who is here)dire: Say (a message to everyone)expulser: Kick (make a player leave (they can come back))bannir: Ban (make a player leave for good)debannir: Unban (lift a ban)blanche: Whitelist (who may come in)admin: Admins (add or remove an admin)sauver: Save (save the world now)copies: Backups (the backups of the save)restaurer: Restore (bring the world back from a backup)regler: Set (change a server setting)arreter: Stop (save and stop the server)motdepasse: Password (the server's password)motdepasse_web: Web password (the web page's password)recharger: Reload (read serveur.json again)personnage: Character (redo or erase a player's character in this world)xp: XP (give a player experience)niveau: Level (set a player's level)rendre_points: Refund points (a player gets back the points they spent) Names typed The names to type, separated by commas: "kick, expulser, boot". Empty: off. noms Text (empty) Who may use it In the chat: admins (their key is in the server's admins list; in a hosted game, the one hosting), everyone, or nobody. Off, it no longer exists on the console either. niveau Choice in a list Admins admin: Adminstous: Everyonedesactivee: Nobody (off)

items.title: Controls added to the game
items.text:
They appear in the Game controls panel (Developer mode), where you can change their key.

Control Name for scripts Key Gamepad Open the chat chat T —

items.title: Points a script can replace (game.override)
items.text:
The descriptions come from the code.

  • chat.texte: function(default, key) -> the text the chat shows for that key: arrivee, depart, expulse, banni ({nom}), reserve_admins, inconnue ({commande}, {aide}), trop_vite, chat_coupe, sans_commandes, serveur, hote ({texte}), saisie (the input line's hint), aide_titre ({prefixe}); and every reply of the server commands: aide_<command> (what each command does in the help), aide_console, joueurs_compte ({nombre}, {max}), joueurs_ligne, sauve, arret_dans ({duree}), expulse_fait ({nom}), banni_fait ({qui}), usage ({commande}, {arguments}), relu, copies_titre, restaure ({copie}), reglage_fait ({reglage}, {valeur})... (the full list is the TEXTES table of chat.luau). The fields are replaced afterwards by the engine. The help a player asks for in the chat is put together on that player's PC, in their language. The default is the game's translation of the text in the original language (a built-in text of the chat in translations_get); without one, French or English, after the player's language. On a dedicated server, the game's original language.

items.title: What the agent knows about this system
items.text: The text the agent reads before using this system.

items.title: Chat (chat)
items.text:
The chat of games with several players (hosted by a player, or a dedicated server). The chat itself is in the engine and works in every multiplayer game, with or without this system: the control chat (T by default) opens a one-line input at the bottom left, Enter sends it, Escape cancels; the host checks the line (plain text, length bounded, anti-spam), then everyone sees it with the sender's name. Arrivals, departures and the server's messages (dire) are written in it. Add this system with modules_add when the user wants to change how the chat works: everything is a game setting, no code.

Game settings:

  • joueurs_parlent (players talk; off: only the game's messages and commands), messages_systeme (arrivals and departures), lignes (lines shown), duree (seconds before a line fades; the open chat shows them all), longueur_max (bytes per message, 200 at most), rafale and recharge (anti-spam: that many messages at once, then one more every recharge seconds).
  • prefixe: what starts a command (/ by default; 1 to 3 signs, no letter or digit).
  • commandes: one row per server command: commande (its fixed identifier: aide, joueurs, dire, expulser, bannir, debannir, bannir_ip, debannir_ip, blanche, admin, sauver, copies, restaurer, regler, arreter, motdepasse, motdepasse_web, recharger), noms (the names typed, comma separated: the first is its name, the others aliases, such as "expulser, kick, virer"; empty: off) and niveau (admin, tous, desactivee). The names work in the chat (after the prefix) and in the dedicated server's console; aide lists them as the game set them. An off command does not exist in the chat nor on the console. The web management page and the code use the identifiers, whatever the names.
  • Who is admin: on a dedicated server, a player whose verified key is in admins of serveur.json; in a game hosted by a player, the one hosting. A command at level tous can be typed by anyone.
  • The key: the control chat (Controls of the game settings, or the game's key menu). There is no gamepad button: typing needs a keyboard.

Scripts: game.chat_send(text, {joueur = id}?) writes a message of the game in the chat (to everyone or one player); the host hears chat.message (joueur, nom, texte) for each accepted line of a player (not the commands).

  • Texts follow the game's translations: the chat's own texts are built-in texts of the system, listed by translations_get (French and English are built in). Override chat.texte from a game script to change one: game.override("chat.texte", function(default, key) if key == "reserve_admins" then return "Réservé à l'équipe." end return default(key) end). Keys: arrivee, depart, expulse, banni ({nom}), reserve_admins, inconnue ({commande}, {aide}), trop_vite, chat_coupe, sans_commandes, serveur, hote ({texte}), saisie, aide_titre ({prefixe}). The answers of the commands themselves come from the server and are in French.
  • Testing: game_run with several players is not available yet; the engine tests cover the chat (test_dedicated_server).

items.title: Ragdoll
items.text:
An animated character that falls limp, like a rag doll: when it dies, under a hard hit, or when the Trigger asks. Its body is built on its own, from its skeleton. It can get back up, and its animation resumes smoothly.

Identifier chiffon Version 2 Placed on objects yes

items.text:
In the Systems panel (Developer mode), by opening the system's card.

None.

items.text:
In the Properties of an object or folder that carries the system, Systems section. A folder passes its values on to what it contains; an object can change a value for itself only.

Setting What it does Name in code Type Default Limits or choices Falls limp when it dies (Health system) When its health reaches zero, it collapses like a rag doll, and does not get back up. a_la_mort Yes or no yes Falls under a hit harder than (m/s, 0: never) An object that hits it and gives it more than this speed, in meters per second, knocks it down: a rolling rock, a thrown barrel. 6: a clear hit. 0: never. choc Number 6 from 0 to 100 Gets back up after a hit Knocked down by a hit (not by dying), it gets back up after a while, and its animation resumes smoothly. se_relever Yes or no yes Gets up after (s) How many seconds it stays down before getting up, once still. delai Number 3 from 0.2 to 60 Mass (kg) The weight of the falling body, in kilograms, shared among its limbs by their size: 70 for an adult, 25 for a child, 300 for an ogre. masse Number 70 from 1 to 10 000 Limb looseness (degrees) How far each limb can bend relative to the one carrying it, in degrees: 45 is natural, 20 falls stiff like a statue, 90 is very floppy. raideur Number 45 from 5 to 120 Floats in water Fallen into water, the body floats, the head and shoulders just above the water, and drifts with it. Otherwise, it sinks slowly to the bottom, like a knight in armor. flotte Yes or no yes
