items.title: Ragdoll (chiffon)
items.text:
An animated character falls limp like a rag doll, then can get back up and its animation resumes smoothly. Its body is built by the engine from its skeleton (capsules measured on its bones, joints with reasonable limits): nothing to set per model, any skeleton works.

  • systems_attach it on the characters (the player, enemies, villagers) or their folder. Per object: a_la_mort (falls when its sante reaches zero, and stays down), choc (a hit from a moving object faster than this, in m/s, knocks it down; 0 never), se_relever and delai (after a hit, it gets back up once still for that many seconds), masse (kg), raideur (how far each limb bends, in degrees: 45 natural, 20 stiff).
  • In water, the fallen body floats, head and shoulders just above the surface, and drifts; set « flotte » to false to make it sink (a knight in armor). The game_run « water » part lists it.
  • The character must be animated (a model with bones and animations): a static model cannot fall as a ragdoll.
  • Without code: a declencheur rule with action chiffon (falls) or relever (gets up), cible the character.
  • Scripts: game.ragdoll(id, true) makes it fall (an optional third argument, a vec, throws it), game.ragdoll(id, false) gets it back up, game.ragdolled(id) tells if it is down. Events chiffon.tombe and chiffon.releve (cible).
  • While down, the player does not move and the camera follows the body; a character is not walked by its scripts.
  • Check with game_run: ragdolls gives each one's falls, get_ups, and whether it is down at the end.

items.title: Several players
items.text:
One for the whole game: any character carrying it falls on death, guests' characters included (on the host; guests see their place, not the limp pose).

items.title: Chests
items.text:
What carries this system is a chest: used, it rolls its loot table (Loot module) and shows what it holds in a "Take all" window. Opened once for everyone, once per player, or once for the group straight into the bag, and refilled after a delay, or never.

Identifier coffres Version 2 Placed on objects yes Also activates Loot, Interaction Also needs, on the same object Interaction

In the Systems panel (Developer mode), by opening the system's card.

In the Properties of an object or folder that carries the system, Systems section. A folder passes its values on to what it contains; an object can change a value for itself only.

Setting What it does Name in code Type Default Limits or choices Loot table The table of the Loot module rolled when opening. table Text (empty) Opened Once for everyone: the first to open it rolls what it holds, shared by all in its window. Once per player: each has their own roll (with four players, four times the contents). Once for the group: rolled once, everything goes into the bag of the player who opens it (the Inventory's shared bag if it is ticked), and the chest stays empty for the others; for a cooperative game. mode Choice in a list Once for everyone tous: Once for everyonejoueur: Once per playergroupe: Once for the group, straight to the bag Refilled after (s, 0: never) The time after opening before a new roll fills it. Kept by the save. delai Number 0 from 0 to 31 536 000 Item level The level of the items rolled in this chest (bonus ranges grow with it). niveau Number 1 from 1 to 100 000, as a whole number

Open the Take all window of a content (a body, a chest) for a player. butin.prendre cible (text), numero (number?), joueur (id) A player asks the host to take from a content: one line (numero) or all they may take.

items.title: Chests (coffres)
items.text:
What carries this system is a chest (ADR-039 § 8). It needs the Loot module (butin) and interaction. Never edit its script.

  • Object settings: table (a loot table of the butin module), mode (tous: opened once for everyone, one content shared by all, taken from its window; joueur: once per player, each their own roll that only they can take, so four players get four times the contents; groupe: once for the group, rolled once and everything goes straight into the bag of the player who opens it, the Inventory's shared bag when sac_commun is ticked, no window, the chest stays empty for the others: use it for a cooperative game instead of a script), delai (seconds before a new roll refills it; 0: never), niveau (the item level of what it rolls).
  • Used (E), it asks the Loot module to roll (butin.remplir) the first time, then each time its delay has passed, and opens the « Tout prendre » window for the player who used it (butin.ouvrir; in groupe mode it takes everything for them, butin.prendre, and the window only shows what a full bag left). What is left stays inside; a refill replaces it.
  • Events: coffres.ouvert {cible, joueur, rempli}.
  • Save: which chests were opened and the time left before a refill; their contents are kept by the Loot module.

items.title: Gathering
items.text:
What carries this system is a resource to gather: a tree to chop, a rock to mine, a bush to pick. Each use is a hit; at the last one, the resource gives what it holds to the inventory, disappears, and grows back if wanted.

Identifier collecte Version 10 Placed on objects yes Also activates Interaction Also needs, on the same object Interaction

items.title: Settings for the whole game
items.text:
In the Systems panel (Developer mode), by opening the system's card.

Setting What it does Name in code Type Default Limits or choices Show what is gathered on screen Briefly writes on screen what the player has just gathered ("+3 Wood"), and the message when the tool is missing. Untick it if your game shows this its own way. afficher Yes or no yes Chips at each hit At each hit, a few chips jump from the spot hit, in its colour: wood for a tree's trunk, stone for a rock. Untick it for a game without particles. eclats Yes or no yes Gather what needs a tool with The attack (the default), as in survival games: the player holds the axe in hand (the inventory's bar) and strikes the tree with the left click. The interaction: the E key gathers, having the tool in the bag is enough, as before. What is gathered bare-handed (berries) stays on the interaction. recolte_outil Choice in a list The attack, with the tool held in hand attaque: The attack, with the tool held in handinteraction: The interaction (E), with the tool in the bag Attack action that gathers The game's control action that strikes a resource with the tool in hand ("attack": the left click by default, X on a gamepad). action_attaque Text attack Message when the tool is in the bag, not in hand The text shown when the player strikes a resource without holding the tool they do have in the bag. {outil} is replaced by its name: "Take in hand: Axe". message_en_main Text Prenez en main : {outil} Message when the tool is missing ({outil}: its name) The text shown when the player tries to gather without the tool needed. {outil} is replaced by the tool's name: "You need: {outil}" becomes "You need: Axe". message_outil Text Il faut : {outil}

items.title: Settings on each object
items.text:
In the Properties of an object or folder that carries the system, Systems section. A folder passes its values on to what it contains; an object can change a value for itself only.

Setting What it does Name in code Type Default Limits or choices Resource given (empty: its name, without number) The name of what the resource puts in the inventory once used up, for example "Wood" for a tree. Empty: the object's name without its number ("Oak 12" gives "Oak"). ressource Text (empty) Quantity given How many of the resource the player receives when it is used up. 0: nothing goes to the inventory. quantite Number 1 from 0 to 1 000 000, as a whole number Hits before it is used up The number of uses before the resource is used up: 1 gathers it in one hit, 5 takes five axe blows. The prompt shows the progress ("Chop 2/5"). coups Number 1 from 1 to 1000, as a whole number XP given when gathered (Progression system) The XP gained by whoever uses it up, if the game has the Progression system. Their gathering speed (a Progression value) divides the hits they need. 0: none. xp Number 0 from 0 to 1 000 000 Track that gets the XP (empty: the main one) The identifier of a track of the Progression system, such as "woodcutting". piste_xp Text (empty) Grows back after (seconds, 0: never) The time, in seconds, before the resource comes back after being used up, ready to be gathered again. 0: it never comes back; 60: a minute later. repousse Number 0 from 0 to 86 400 Tool needed, held in hand (empty: none) The name of an item the player must hold in hand to gather, for example "Axe", written exactly as in the inventory: they then strike with the attack. Empty: bare hands, with the interaction (E). outil Text (empty) Prompt text (Chop, Mine, Pick… empty: Interaction's) The word of the prompt in front of the resource, for example "Chop" for a tree or "Mine" for a rock. Empty: the usual text of the Interaction system. verbe Text (empty) Its end, when used up What happens to the resource when it is used up: it vanishes at once, falls, collapses, shrinks or bursts. From the last hit on, it no longer blocks the player. fin Choice in a list Vanishes at once disparait: Vanishes at oncetombe: Falls, away from the playerseffondre: Collapses where it standsretrecit: Shrinkseclate: Bursts Length of its end (s) How many seconds the chosen end lasts: 1 to 2 seconds for a falling tree. No effect if it vanishes at once. duree_fin Number 1.2 from 0.1 to 10 Its own end animation, if its model has one (replaces the chosen end) An animation of the resource's own model, if its file contains one (a tree falling down, for example). It plays instead of the chosen end. animation_ressource Animation of the object's model (empty) Shakes at each hit The resource shakes a little at each hit that does not use it up yet, to show the hit landed. secousse Yes or no yes Player animation (optional) An animation of the player's character, played at each hit: they turn to the resource and play it in place, and holding the key chains the hits. Empty, or missing from their model: the hit is instant. animation Player animation (empty) Moment of the hit in the animation (%) At what moment of the player's animation the hit counts, as a percentage of its length: 50 in the middle, 70 a bit later, when the axe meets the trunk. moment Number 50 from 0 to 100 Animation speed Speeds up or slows down the player's animation: 1 at its original speed, 2 twice as fast (hits closer together), 0.5 twice as slow. vitesse_animation Number 1 from 0.1 to 5

items.title: Events
items.text: The descriptions come from the code.

items.title: What it announces
items.text: Event Fields Description collecte.coup cible (id), coups (number), restants (number) The player hit a resource (a use of something carrying collecte). restants is how many hits are left before it is used up. collecte.recolte cible (id), ressource (text), quantite (number), joueur (id?), xp (number?), piste (text?) A resource was used up and gave what it holds. The inventory, if present, has been asked to add it. collecte.epuise cible (id) A resource is used up and is about to disappear (destroyed, or hidden until it grows back): it still exists while this is sent. collecte.repousse cible (id) A used-up resource grew back and can be gathered again. collecte.outil_manquant cible (id), outil (text), joueur (id?) The player tried to gather a resource without the tool it needs: not held in hand (the default, with attack), or not in the inventory (gathering set to the interaction). inventaire.ajouter objet (text), quantite (number), joueur (id?), fiche (number?) Ask the inventory to add items, such as a reward. Answered by inventaire.change, or inventaire.plein. With several players, joueur says whose bag; without it, the player whose action is being handled, or every player. action.prise action (text), prise (boolean), par (text), joueur (id?) A system takes a control action for itself, or gives it back (prise false) (version 24): gathering takes attack while the player aims at a resource that needs a tool, so the press chops instead of swinging a weapon. par names who says it ("collecte"). Fighting modules do not strike (nor block) with that action while any system holds it; tir takes attack, block and heal while a ranged weapon is held, so the right button aims and R reloads without drinking.

items.title: What it listens to
items.text: Event Fields Description interaction.utiliser cible (id), joueur (id) The player used the object in reach: a door, a merchant, an item to pick up. Whoever owns that object decides what it does. inventaire.change objet (text), quantite (number), total (number), chargement (boolean?), fiche (number?), jete (boolean?) The quantity of an item changed. total is the new quantity. chargement is true when a saved game gives the items back (game.load): nothing was picked up. For a unique copy (version 15), objet is its kind, fiche its record's number, total how many of that kind. With several stacks of a kind (version 21), total counts all of them; jete is true when a slot was dropped on the ground. inventaire.en_main objet (text), avant (text), place (number), chargement (boolean?), joueur (id?), fiche (number?), source (text?) What the player holds in hand changed (version 24): the slot chosen in the inventory's bar (keys 1 to 9, wheel), an item used up, a load (chargement true). objet is the kind held, "" for empty hands; avant the one held before; place the bar slot (0: nothing). Gathering checks the tool held; a game script equips a sword with it. joueur.occupe occupe (boolean), par (text) The player's hands are taken by something else than fighting (version 23): a building mode where the click places a piece, a tool being aimed. occupe true when it starts, false when it ends; par names who says it ("construction"), so several can overlap. Fighting modules do not strike nor block while any of them keeps the player busy. joueur.depart joueur (id), numero (number) Sent by the engine on the host when a guest leaves the game (they quit, or their connection was lost and they did not come back in time, the game setting Place kept after a drop): their character is removed right after. A module forgets what it kept for them.

items.title: Points a script can replace (game.override)
items.text:
The descriptions come from the code.

  • collecte.don: function(default, id) -> resource name (text), quantity (number): what this resource gives when it is used up. The default is its ressource and quantite settings.

items.title: What the agent knows about this system
items.text: The text the agent reads before using this system.

items.title: Gathering (collecte)
items.text:
Makes what the user calls a resource gatherable: a tree to chop, a rock to mine, a bush to pick, any model. Activating it activates the interaction module; placing it on an object places interaction there too.

  • A resource: an object carrying this system (systems_attach), every child of a group carrying it, or every plant of a plant kind object carrying it (a whole forest at once, see the terrain rules). Set per object or group (systems_set): ressource (what it gives, in the user's language; empty: its name without a trailing number), quantite, coups (uses before it is used up), repousse (seconds before it grows back; 0: never), outil (an item the player must hold in hand, such as "Axe"; empty: bare hands), verbe (the prompt word: Chop, Mine, Pick).
  • A resource with an outil is struck with the attack (left click, X on a gamepad), the tool held in hand: the inventory's bar (keys 1 to 9, the wheel) chooses what is held, announced by inventaire.en_main. This is the user's decision for every game (ADR-029, 11 November 2026). The player aims like the game is seen: the centre of the screen with a character, else what is in front of them, within the interaction reach measured at the trunk or the foot. With the tool only in the bag the message says to take it in hand (message_en_main); without it, message_outil; no hit either way. While the player aims at such a resource, gathering takes the attack (action.prise): combat.basique does not swing too. Holding the attack chains the hits. The game setting recolte_outil = interaction brings back the old way (E, the tool in the bag); do not change it unless the user asks.
  • A resource without outil (berries, a bush) is gathered with the interaction (E by default): each use is one hit. At the last one, what it gives goes to the inventory (inventaire.ajouter: activate inventaire too, or listen to collecte.recolte yourself), and the resource disappears: destroyed, or hidden until it grows back.
  • The prompt shows the key, the verb, the tool to hold in brackets, and the hits so far ("Click: Chop 2/3").
  • On screen, the system delivers two screens, which the user restyles in the screen editor: « Message de la collecte » (shape Message, HUD key Message de la collecte/Message: "+3 Wood", the missing tool) and « Invite de la collecte » (shape Invite, HUD key Invite de la collecte/Invite: the attack prompt in front of a resource). Each player sees their own. Never draw these yourself, and do not name another screen like them.
  • animation: a clip of the player's model, read with animation_clips (names differ from one model to another: never guess). The player then turns to the resource and plays it in place; the hit counts at moment (% of the clip, 50 by default), and the gesture lasts the clip's length divided by vitesse_animation. Holding the key chains the hits. Without it, or if the player lacks the clip, each use is an instant hit.
  • Its end, when used up (fin): disparait (vanishes at once, the default), tombe (falls away from the player), seffondre, retrecit, eclate, over duree_fin seconds; it stops blocking at once. If the resource's own model has an end animation, set animation_ressource to it (read its clips with animation_clips on its own file): it replaces the end. secousse (on by default) shakes it at each hit. Its sounds belong to the resource, not to the end: the sons module's recolte_coup and recolte_fin on the resource or its plant kind.
  • React with game.on: collecte.coup (cible, coups, restants) for a hit sound or wood chips, collecte.recolte (cible, ressource, quantite), collecte.epuise (cible, sent before it disappears: read its position to drop logs there), collecte.repousse (cible), collecte.outil_manquant (cible, outil).
  • Give the tool with game.emit("inventaire.ajouter", {objet = "Axe", quantite = 1}), or make an axe an item to pick up with inventaire: it goes into the bar, and into the hand if its slot is the chosen one (game.emit("inventaire.tenir", {objet = "Axe"}) puts it in hand). Its model shows in the hand by itself (see inventaire). Never write your own hotbar, held item or attack-to-gather script: these systems do it.
  • Do not put inventaire on a resource: it would be picked up whole at the first use.
  • Change what a resource gives from your script with game.override("collecte.don", function(default, id) ... end): it returns the resource name and the quantity.
  • Saved games: game.save keeps the hits already struck and the time left before each regrowth (the engine keeps the resource hidden or destroyed); game.load gives them back. Nothing to write.
  • In a large world, resources stay loaded (they carry a system) and asleep when far; one gathered far away still grows back on time.
  • A survival game: collecte gives the materials, fabrication turns them into tools and food, construction spends them on a shelter, besoins makes food matter, jour_nuit gives days and nights. The resource names must match the recipes' and pieces' items exactly.

items.title: Several players
items.text:
One for the whole game: resources are shared (a tree cut down is cut for everyone, its regrowth too), but each player has their own gesture, tools, message, and what they harvest goes into their own bag (inventaire.ajouter with joueur).

This page is generated automatically from the WorldMint code (modules/collecte/module.json, modules/collecte/AGENT.md, modules/events.json): it always matches the editor.

items.title: Basic combat
items.text:
The player strikes ahead with a key, with the damage, reach and cooldown set on them. It hits what carries Health. For enemies that attack, add "Enemies".

Identifier combat.basique Version 13 Placed on objects yes Also activates Health

items.title: Settings for the whole game
items.text:
In the Systems panel (Developer mode), by opening the system's card.

Setting What it does Name in code Type Default Limits or choices Player action The game's control action that makes the player strike ("attack": the left mouse button by default). action Text attack Several players: players can hurt each other In a game with several players: ticked, a hit also lands on the other players. Unticked (the default), friends do not hurt each other. No effect with a single player. blesser_joueurs Yes or no no A flash and sparks when a hit lands Each hit that lands makes a brief flash, a few sparks and a little dust on the target. Untick it for a game without particles. impact Yes or no yes Action to block The control action to hold to block ("block": the right mouse button by default, LB on a gamepad). It only matters if the player can block. action_parade Text block

items.title: Settings on each object
items.text:
In the Properties of an object or folder that carries the system, Systems section. A folder passes its values on to what it contains; an object can change a value for itself only.

Setting What it does Name in code Type Default Limits or choices Damage of a hit The health points a hit takes from the target, before its armor. With 25 against an enemy with 100 health points, it takes four hits. degats Number 25 from 0 to 1 000 000 Reach (m) How far, in meters, the hit reaches a target in front of the player: 2 m for a sword, more for a spear. It strikes the nearest one. portee Number 2 from 0.2 to 50 Strike angle ahead (°) The width of the area hit in front of the player, in degrees: 100 covers the front, 360 also hits behind them. Smaller, aiming must be more precise. angle Number 100 from 10 to 360 Time between two hits (s) The minimum time, in seconds, between two hits: 0.5 allows two hits per second at most. With an animation, the next hit also waits for the end of the gesture. recharge Number 0.5 from 0 to 30 Knockback of the target How hard the target hit is pushed back. 0: it does not move. Only characters are knocked back, not still objects. recul Number 4 from 0 to 100 Hit animation (optional) An animation of the player's character, played at each hit; the hit lands at its moment of impact. Empty, or missing from their model: the hit lands at once. animation Player animation (empty) Moment of the hit in the animation (%) At what moment of the animation the hit lands, as a percentage of its length: 50 in the middle, later for a big wind-up swing. moment Number 50 from 0 to 100 Animation speed Speeds up or slows down the hit animation: 1 at its original speed, 2 twice as fast. The next hit waits for the end of the gesture: faster, the player strikes more often. vitesse_animation Number 1 from 0.1 to 5 Share of a hit stopped when blocking (%, 0: cannot block) The share of damage stopped when the player blocks a hit from the front, as a percentage: 70 lets 30 % through, 100 stops everything. 0: the player cannot block. parade Number 0 from 0 to 100 Protected angle ahead (°) The width of the area protected in front of the player while blocking, in degrees: 120 covers the front, 360 also protects the back. angle_parade Number 120 from 10 to 360 Walking speed while blocking (1: normal) The player's walking speed while blocking, compared with normal: 0.5 half, 1 just as fast, 0 standing still. They cannot strike meanwhile. vitesse_parade Number 0.5 from 0 to 1 Block animation (optional) An animation of the player's character, replayed while they block. items.title: Basic combat (combat.basique)
items.text:
The player strikes the nearest object carrying Health in front of them with a key (attack, the left mouse button by default). Activating it activates the health module.

  • Place it on the player with systems_attach: the player's damage, reach, strike angle, cooldown, knockback and hit animation are their values (systems_set). Without it on the player, the key does nothing. The animation is a clip of the player's model, read with animation_clips (never guess names): the hit lands at moment (% of the clip, 50 by default), and the next strike waits for the end of the gesture, whose length is the clip's divided by vitesse_animation. Without an animation, the hit is instant.
  • What can be hit: objects carrying sante. The damage sent is raw: the target's armor is applied by the health module.
  • It handles the player's hits only. Enemies that move and attack are the module ennemis: add it only if the user asked for enemies that fight.
  • Blocking: set parade on the player (the share of a hit stopped, in %, such as 70 or 100; 0 by default: no blocking). While the action block is held (right mouse button by default, LB on a gamepad), hits from in front within angle_parade lose that share before armor, the player walks at vitesse_parade and cannot strike. animation_parade is a clip of the player's model, replayed while blocking. A blocked hit is announced by sante.pare (cible, source, montant stopped).
  • With the stamina module (endurance), each strike costs stamina, and an exhausted player cannot strike or block.
  • While the game shows the cursor (game.show_cursor(true): an inventory, a menu), or while something keeps the player busy (the event joueur.occupe: construction's building mode, where the click places a piece), the player neither strikes nor blocks. A script of yours that takes the player's hands (aiming a fishing rod) sends joueur.occupe with occupe true, then false, and its own par.
  • While another system takes the attack action for itself (the event action.prise: collecte while the player aims at a resource that needs a tool, so the click chops), the player does not strike with it: one press, one gesture. The same for the block action: while a ranged weapon of tir is held, the right button aims instead of blocking.
  • React to hits: listen to combat.coup (cible, source, montant), for a sound or an effect. Deaths come from the health module: sante.mort.
  • Knockback moves characters only. A dead object stays unless its health values say to remove it.
  • The weapon in the hand belongs to the inventory (inventaire, list en_main): an example the creator placed in the character's hand gives the grip (prise placee), else the measured grip (prise arme). Never delete that example. Check it on a capture standing and during a hit: the fist closed on the handle, no hand through the handle or the blade.

items.title: Several players
items.text:
One copy per player: each player has their own cooldown, block and hits. Players do not hurt each other unless the game setting blesser_joueurs ("Players can hurt each other") is ticked.

items.title: Shops of the city (commerces)
items.text:
The shops of a generated city become merchants without code: near the player, each visitable shop gets a clerk standing behind its counter (the place its interior recipe left for them, facing the room), who sells the items of its kind through the Shop (boutique). Activating it activates boutique (and so interaction and inventaire). Use it for every "the grocery sells sodas", "a clerk in each café"; never write a script that clones clerks or a shop window yourself, and never edit the system: set it, listen to its events, override its hooks.

Set it with modules_set (game-wide settings; nothing is placed on objects):

  • vendeurs: who keeps each kind, one row each: sorte (the kind as the city names it: superette, cafe, banque, vetements, pharmacie… city_get lists the shops and their kinds), commerce (empty: the whole kind; a shop's name, building id or place id: that shop only, instead of its kind's rows), personnage (a character of the scene, usually hidden: it is copied, with its animations), animation (a clip of that character, looped; empty or missing: its first clip whose name holds "idle", else its usual animation; never invent a pose). Several rows for a kind: each shop takes one of them, always the same. No row, or a character missing from the scene: no clerk, without error. Never pick a model of a pack by default: ask the user which characters keep the shops.
  • articles: what each kind sells, in the window's order: sorte, commerce (a named shop's rows replace its kind's rows for it), objet (the inventory kind, in the user's language), quantite, prix, stock (per shop; 0: no limit).
  • monnaie (the inventory kind that pays, "Or" by default: set the game's money, such as "Dollar"), texte (the prompt near the clerk, "Acheter"), distance (m, 40: clerks appear closer than this to the player and go back to the pool beyond it; lower it if the game slows down).

Example: {"vendeurs": [{"sorte": "superette", "personnage": "Vendeuse"}], "articles": [{"sorte": "superette", "objet": "Soda", "prix": 2, "stock": 12}, {"sorte": "superette", "objet": "Sandwich", "prix": 5}], "monnaie": "Dollar"}.

How it plays: the player walks in (commerce.entree), the clerk faces them; using the clerk (E) opens the Shop window titled with the shop's name. Buying is the Shop's (money taken, item given, clear messages); the stock belongs to the shop, not to the clerk: it is kept when the clerk leaves and comes back, and by the saved game.

Ports for scripts (shared.commerces, from any game script):

  • shared.commerces.articles(lieu) -> the list of what the shop sells (objet, quantite, prix, stock, and reste when the stock is limited).
  • shared.commerces.vendeur(lieu) -> its clerk now (tagged commerce.vendeur), or nil (far away, closed, no character set); shared.commerces.lieu(clerk) -> the shop of a clerk.
  • shared.commerces.ouvrir(lieu) opens its shop window; shared.commerces.acheter(lieu, objet) buys one purchase of objet without the window (the Shop's own purchase, through the event boutique.acheter). Both need the clerk there (false otherwise).
  • Event commerce.achat {lieu, vendeur, objet, quantite, prix, monnaie, joueur}: after a purchase from a clerk; a quest step, a declencheur rule, a sound. boutique.achat still comes first, with the clerk as cible.
  • The place of a shop: game.near(game.player(), 2000, "commerce:superette", {asleep = true})[1]; game.data(lieu) has sorte, nom, porte, vendeur {position, regard} and arrets (customer stops).

Hooks (game.override from a game script, never an edit of the system):

  • commerces.vendeur function(default, infos) -> {personnage, animation} or nil (infos.lieu, infos.donnees): a special clerk for one shop, none at night.
  • commerces.articles function(default, infos) -> a list of Shop rows: prices that change with the story, a sold-out shop.
  • commerces.ouvert function(default, infos) -> false to have no clerk now (after a robbery; or by infos.donnees.horaires with the game's own clock). The default is always open.

Cost: one animated character per visitable shop within distance (2 to 10 at once in a dense street), copied from the pool. Testing: in game_run, give money (inventaire.ajouter), walk into the shop, press interact near the clerk, click Boutique/Acheter#1; or call shared.commerces.acheter from the test script and read commerce.achat in the logs.

items.title: Several players
items.text:
One copy, on the host: the clerks are the same for everyone. Each player buys through their own Shop window and inventory; a shop's limited stock is shared.

items.title: Building
items.text:
The player places pieces in the world: walls, floors, a campfire, any model. In building mode (B), a preview goes where they aim, on a grid or freely: with the view (the centre of the screen) when they play a character, with the cursor from above. A click places the piece and takes its cost from the inventory. The catalog (Tab) shows the pieces by category, with their picture and their cost; while placing, a panel tells the piece chosen, a sentence tells why it cannot go there, and a bar recalls the keys. A placed piece can be torn down, and gives back part of its cost.

items.title: Building (construction)
items.text:
The player places pieces in the world (walls, floors, a fence, a campfire: any model of the library), pays them from the inventory, and can tear them down. Add it once with modules_add (with inventaire). Use it whenever the user talks about building a shelter, a base, a camp: never write a building script.

Its game setting pieces (modules_set) is a list of rows, in order. A piece row is a piece; the cout rows under it are its cost.

  • piece: nom (shown, in the user's language; it names the piece in events), categorie (the catalog tab, such as « Murs », « Sols », « Meubles »; empty: « Autres », last; a single category shows no tabs), icone (optional picture of the piece in the catalog and the placing panel: an image of the project, square on a transparent background; without it the name is written), modele (the id of an object of the scene copied at each placement: create it once, standing on the ground where nothing walks, with visible: false, a collider if it should stop the player, and the systems each copy should have), decalage (on a grid, metres pushed forward along its facing: half a cell for a wall that edges the cell).
  • cout: objet (an inventory kind, as collecte gives it), nombre. A piece without cost is free.
  • Example: [{"sorte": "piece", "nom": "Mur en bois", "modele": "mur_modele", "decalage": 1}, {"sorte": "cout", "objet": "Bois", "nombre": 4}, {"sorte": "piece", "nom": "Feu de camp", "modele": "feu_modele"}, {"sorte": "cout", "objet": "Pierre", "nombre": 3}].
  • Never guess a model's size: measure it (the model's bounds in scene_get, or game.bounds in a script) to choose grille and decalage. The module itself puts each piece's foot on the surface aimed at, from the model's own bounds.
  • A piece that does something: its model's systems go to every copy. A campfire model carrying fabrication (nom_etabli « Feu de camp ») and particules becomes a cooking station with flames, wherever it is built (a workbench is its own model, nom_etabli « Établi »); a bed model carrying besoins (source_besoin « Fatigue », source_heures 8) lets the player sleep.
  • Playing: the control build (B, or RB on a gamepad) opens the building mode: a preview of the piece goes where the player aims (it blinks where it cannot go, beyond portee too). build_place (click, or X) places it and takes its cost; build_rotate (wheel, or right stick pressed) turns it by rotation degrees; build_next (Q, or ←) or the keys 1 to 9 choose the piece; build_remove (X key, or B) tears down the piece aimed at and gives back rendu % of its cost. build again leaves the mode. build_catalog (Tab, or LB: the block button of combat.basique, which does not block during the building mode) opens the catalog: a window (role fenetre.construction, title titre.construction) with a tab per category (bouton.onglet), a grid with one slot per piece (case.construction: its picture or its name, and its cost « 4 / 4 Bois », what the player has / what it takes, in the alert color when short), and below the card of the piece hovered (name, cost, what is missing). A click (A on a gamepad) chooses the piece and closes it; Close, B or Escape close it; the cursor shows while it is open. While placing (aide): a panel at the bottom left (panneau.construction) tells the piece chosen and its cost, and a bar at the bottom (panneau.touches) recalls the real keys of the controls (the gamepad's buttons when the player uses one). Always, when the preview cannot be placed, a short sentence above the centre tells why: too far, aim at the ground, not on yourself, already built here, what is missing, or the reason a construction.permise override gives. While the mode is open the module sends joueur.occupe (occupe true, par « construction »), so combat.basique neither strikes nor blocks: the click places.
  • Aiming (game setting visee): auto (default) follows the game's camera (game.camera_view()): a character in first or third person aims with the view, the centre of the screen, and the camera keeps turning with the mouse, like the building mode of every survival game; a top-down view (the player camera's lowest tilt is 45° or more) or a placed camera aims with the cursor, which shows during the mode. centre or curseur force one. With a gamepad, the view aims (from above: the ground just in front of the player). Leave auto unless the user asks.
  • Game settings: grille (cell size in metres; 0: free placement exactly where the player aims), visee, rotation, portee (metres from the player), rendu, demolir (the player may tear down), aide.
  • Events announced: construction.pose (cible: the new piece, piece: its name), construction.detruit (cible, piece), construction.mode (actif), construction.manque (piece, manque). Send construction.detruire (cible, rendre?) to remove a piece (a storm, an enemy). Placed pieces carry the tag « construction.piece »; the preview carries « construction.apercu ».
  • Forbid building somewhere from your own script, never the module's: game.override("construction.permise", function(default, piece, position) if game.distance(position, game.find("Village")) < 30 then return false, game.t("Pas dans le village.") end return default(piece, position) end).
  • Saved games: game.save keeps the pieces (the engine keeps the copies, the module which piece each one is); game.load gives them back. In a large world, placed pieces stay loaded and asleep when far, like everything a system follows.
  • What it shows is made of screens delivered by the system (version 5), filled by its script; to dress them, set the interface theme with these styles; never lay images over them. « Mode construction » (modules/construction/ecrans/mode.json): Panneau (panneau.construction, the placing panel at the bottom left: Titre « Pièce choisie », Image, Nom, Coût, and Rien when there is no piece), Raison (the refusal, above the centre), Barre des touches (panneau.touches, its text Touches). « Catalogue de construction » (ecrans/catalogue.json): Fenêtre (fenetre.construction), Titre (titre.construction), the list Onglets (row Onglet, bouton.onglet), Cases (it scrolls past three rows) holding the grid list Grille (row Case, case.construction), Fiche (Nom, Aide, Coût, Manque), Fermer. Their buttons send the system's actions onglet, case, fermer. Keys: Mode construction/Nom, Mode construction/Raison, Mode construction/Touches, Catalogue de construction/Onglet#N, Catalogue de construction/Case#N (N counts the pieces shown in the open tab), Catalogue de construction/Fermer (B, Escape). The script sets a few sizes from what it shows, as before the screens: the columns of Grille (as many as pieces in the tab, 5 at most, slots of 0.105 × 0.13) and the width of Cases; the window keeps the width of its shape Fenêtre (widen it in the screen editor), wider only when its grid or its tabs need it. Change their look, places and sizes with screens_set (styles, not hand-made values); never draw them with game.hud_*, and never edit the system. The preview of the piece is an object of the world, not a screen.
  • Testing: in game_run, give the cost with inventaire.ajouter in a test script, press build, then aim: with the view (third person), turn the camera with pitch/yaw until the centre of the screen is on the ground in front of the player (the default tilt already looks about 4 m ahead); with the cursor (top-down, visee « curseur »), use mouse ([x, y] of the screen). Press build_place; read construction.pose in the report's events, then build_remove on the same spot. The catalog: press build_catalog, read Catalogue de construction/Case#N in the report's hud, click one (its rect), and capture_steps to look at it.

items.title: Several players
items.text:
One copy per player: each player has their own build mode, piece, preview, catalog window and cost (their own inventory), aiming with their own camera (and cursor, from above). What is built is shared: every player sees it (the pieces are shared copies), and the host's saved game keeps it.

This page is generated automatically from the WorldMint code (modules/construction/module.json, modules/construction/AGENT.md, modules/events.json): it always matches the editor.

items.title: Race
items.text:
A race without code, on top of the Round: numbered checkpoints (the system placed on objects), passed in order (a skipped checkpoint does not count), a finish line that only counts after the last one, laps, and the return to the last checkpoint passed (a fall, a "return" zone, a hazard, or a key for an overturned vehicle). Everyone sees their lap, their checkpoint and their place.

Identifier course Version 3 Placed on objects yes Also activates Round

items.title: Settings for the whole game
items.text:
In the Systems panel (Developer mode), by opening the system's card.

Setting What it does Name in code Type Default Limits or choices Number of laps How many times to go round. The finish line (or, without one, the last checkpoint) closes each lap; once the last lap is done, the player has arrived. tours Number 1 from 1 to 99, as a whole number Back to the last checkpoint on a fall The player (or their vehicle) who falls below the height below goes back to the last checkpoint passed, facing the next one. chute Yes or no yes Fall height (m) Below this height (Y, in metres), the player is put back. Set it a little below the lowest part of the track. hauteur_chute Number -20 from -100 000 to 100 000 Event that puts back The name of an event that sends the player it names (its field joueur or cible) back to the last checkpoint: "lave.contact" for lava, or one of your game's traps. Empty: none. A death (Death system) also puts back at the last checkpoint. evenement_retour Text lave.contact "Put back" key The player can go back to the last checkpoint themselves (the control "course_replacer", Backspace by default): an overturned vehicle, a stuck player. touche Yes or no yes Lap and checkpoint on screen Under the Round's stopwatch, each player sees their lap (x/N) and their checkpoint (x/N). Their place is the Round's. afficher Yes or no yes

items.text:
They appear in the Game controls panel (Developer mode), where you can change their key.

Control Name for scripts Key Gamepad Back to the last checkpoint (race) course_replacer Backspace —

items.title: Events
items.text: The descriptions come from the code.

items.title: What it announces
items.text: Event Fields Description course.point joueur (id), numero (number), tour (number), cible (id) A player passed the checkpoint they had to pass (Race module): numero its number, tour the lap, cible the object. course.tour joueur (id), tour (number), total (number) A player finished a lap (Race module): tour is the lap just finished, total the number of laps. course.retour joueur (id), cible (id?), raison (text) A player (or their vehicle) was put back at their last checkpoint, facing the next (Race module). raison: chute, zone, danger, touche, mort or script. manche.arrivee joueur (id) A player arrived (the Race at the end of the last lap, a zone or a script): the Round module notes their time. Counts once per round. manche.progression joueur (id), valeur (number) How far a player got, a number that grows as they advance (the Race: laps and checkpoints passed, then the share of the way to the next). The Round module ranks those who have not arrived by it.

items.title: What it listens to
items.text: Event Fields Description manche.nouvelle numero (number), total (number) A round is set up (Round module): every player is at their starting place, frozen during the countdown. numero counts from 1; total is the setting manches. The Race resets its laps here. manche.depart numero (number), total (number) The countdown is over: Go! (Round module). The stopwatch of the round starts now. manche.fin numero (number), total (number), classement (table), raison (text), gagnant (text?) A round ended (Round module). classement: the ranking, best first, a list of rows {joueur or equipe, nom, rang, temps?, points, vies, progression, elimine, arrive}; gagnant: the first's player id or team name; raison: arrivee, limite, score or dernier. course.replacer joueur (id) Ask the Race module to put a player back at their last checkpoint, facing the next one (a trap, a button of the game). joueur.reapparu joueur (id), cible (id), position (vector) A dead player stands up again (death and respawn module): respawned, or brought back by sante.ranimer. joueur.depart joueur (id), numero (number) Sent by the engine on the host when a guest leaves the game (they quit, or their connection was lost and they did not come back in time, the game setting Place kept after a drop): their character is removed right after. A module forgets what it kept for them. langue.change langue (text) Sent by the engine when the player changes the game's language (game.set_language, the Menu options). A module redraws what it already shows: its texts go through game.t and game.language.

items.title: Points a script can replace (game.override)
items.text:
The descriptions come from the code.

  • course.texte: function(default, key, joueur) -> the text shown for that key: tour (Lap {n}/{total}), point (Checkpoint {n}/{total}), rate (a checkpoint was missed). The default is the built-in text in the game's language.

items.title: What the agent knows about this system
items.text: The text the agent reads before using this system.

items.title: Race (course)
items.text:
Checkpoints, laps and the return to the last checkpoint, on top of the Round (manche, added with it, mode temps) which does the countdown, the stopwatch, the ranking and the end (ADR-045). For any race (on foot, by car, by boat, an obstacle course), use this instead of scripting checkpoints, laps or respawns.

  • Checkpoints: objects carrying this system, sorte point with numero 1, 2, 3... in the order of passage: an arch, a ring, or an invisible box (builtin:cube, visible: false, no collider) the size of the passage, 1 m deep or more. Passed by entering the object's box (rayon 0), or within rayon metres of its centre. Only the expected checkpoint counts: a skipped one does not, and the player must go back for it. Two objects with the same number are two ways through the same checkpoint.
  • The start and finish line: one object sorte arrivee. It closes each lap, only after the last checkpoint. Without it, the last checkpoint closes the lap. Put the Round's starting places (manche on markers) just behind it.
  • Laps (tours, 1). After the last lap, the player has arrived: the Round notes their time and place.
  • Back to the last checkpoint (facing the next one; their vehicle too if they drive): falling below hauteur_chute (chute), entering an object sorte retour (a pit, the sea, off track), the event named in evenement_retour (lave.contact by default, with joueur or cible: a lava or a trap of your game), a respawn of the mort module, the control course_replacer (Backspace; touche) for an overturned car or a stuck player, or game.emit("course.replacer", {joueur = id}). Before any checkpoint, back at their start.
  • Progress: sent to the Round (manche.progression): laps and checkpoints passed, then the share of the way to the next. That is the place each player sees while racing, and the ranking of those who did not finish at the time limit.
  • On screen (each player their own, afficher): "Lap 1/3 Checkpoint 2/5" inside the Round's top banner, under its stopwatch (the optional shape Course of its screen "Bandeau de la partie", filled with game.screen_set; deleted from the screen, the line is not shown) (when the Round's afficher is off: its own screen « Avancée dans la course », Fond and Ligne, which the user restyles in the screen editor; never draw it yourself, and do not name another screen like it); the place is the Round's. Texts: override course.texte.
  • Events: course.point {joueur, numero, tour, cible}, course.tour {joueur, tour, total}, course.retour {joueur, cible, raison}. A sound or an effect at each checkpoint: listen to course.point.
  • Check it with game_run « players » and the report's HUD of each guest; measure the track (game.bounds) for hauteur_chute, never guess.

items.title: Several players
items.text:
One for the whole game, on the host: it watches every player's position; each sees their own lap, checkpoint and place.

items.title: Decal
items.text:
An image projected on what lies under the object: a footprint, an impact, a stain, a puddle, a scorch mark, a sign painted on a wall. Create > Decal places an invisible box that carries it: the image covers its width and depth, and lies on the ground or the wall around its base.

Identifier decalcomanie Version 1 Placed on objects yes Run by the engine yes: the engine runs it itself, without a script

items.text:
In the Systems panel (Developer mode), by opening the system's card.

None.

Its transparency is kept: the transparent parts let the surface show through. fichier Image from the library (empty) Opacity From 0 (invisible) to 1 (the whole image): 0.5 for a faint mark. opacite Number 1 from 0 to 1 Tint A tint applied to the image: white leaves it as it is, dark red makes a blood stain, green a puddle of poison. couleur Color #ffffff

items.title: Decal (decalcomanie)
items.text:
An object carrying this system projects an image on what lies around its base: the ground, a wall, a floor of cubes. A footprint, an impact, a stain, a puddle, a scorch mark, a sign. The system has no script: the renderer projects it. The game report counts decals under decals.

  • Make a decal: create a box (builtin:cube) with visible: false and no collider, then systems_attach this system on it. The image covers the box's width (x) and depth (z), and lies on the surface around the box's base, within half its height above and below (y). Scale the box to size the image: 1 × 0.5 × 1 for a puddle of one metre, 0.3 × 0.3 × 0.5 for a footprint. Turn the box around its height to turn the image.
  • On a wall: tip the box so that its height points out of the wall (rotate 90 degrees around x or z), and place its base on the wall.
  • Per object (systems_set): image (tache, impact, brulure, flaque, pas, trace, trou (a bullet hole), or fichier with fichier: an image of the project, from assets_search kind "image"; its transparency is kept), opacite (0 to 1), couleur ("#rrggbb", a tint: dark red for blood, green for poison; white leaves the image as it is).
  • A decal shows as long as its object is in the game: game.destroy removes it. Do not make its box visible: that would show the box.
  • From a script, during the game: game.decal("impact", pos, {size = 0.6, normal = vec(0, 1, 0)}) (a crater where a fireball lands, footprints that follow the player). The game keeps a limited number of them (fewer on a small graphics card): the oldest fades out to make room. See the script reference.
  • It projects on everything inside its box, characters walking through included: keep the box thin over a ground where characters walk.

items.title: Several players
items.text:
The engine runs it once for the whole game: decals are seen by the host.

This page is generated automatically from the WorldMint code (modules/decalcomanie/module.json, modules/decalcomanie/AGENT.md, modules/events.json): it always matches the editor.

items.text:
"When… then…" rules without writing code: when the player enters a zone, uses a lever, when a boss dies… then a door opens, a chest appears, the game is won. With ready-made actions, and those written for this game.
