The background music (Sounds module) fades down without stopping, then resumes where it is when this one comes back. musique Sound from the library (empty) Looping (unticked: the background music comes back when the piece ends)shown only if Then is “Music: play one over the background music” Ticked: it loops until a rule "Music: back to the background music" (the end of a step, the boss's death). Unticked: it plays once, and the background music comes back by itself at the end. boucle_musique Yes or no yes Volume (1: that of the background music)shown only if Then is “Music: play one over the background music” Its volume, compared with the background music volume set in the Sounds module: 1 just as loud, 0.5 half as loud. The sound mixer (Music group) then sets both. volume_musique Number 1 from 0 to 1 Fade (seconds)shown only if Then is “Music: play one over the background music” or “Music: back to the background music” The time, in seconds, the music takes to rise while the background one lowers, and the reverse on the way back. 0: at once; 1.5: a smooth change; 0.3: a chase that starts sharply. fondu_musique Number 1.5 from 0 to 10 Videoshown only if Then is “Play a video” The video played full screen, with its sound: an intro, an ending, a story moment. The world stops meanwhile. MP4 files. video Video from the library (empty) The player can skip itshown only if Then is “Play a video” Checked: Escape, Enter, Space, a click or A on the gamepad skip the video. Unchecked: it is watched to the end. passer Yes or no yes Event sent at the end (optional)shown only if Then is “Play a video” An event name sent when the video ends or is skipped ("intro_done"): another rule ("When an event happens") chains what comes next, such as changing scene. fin Text (empty) Video sound (sound mixer group)shown only if Then is “Play a video” The sound mixer group the video's sound goes to. Voice by default: a cutscene talks, and the game's music lowers meanwhile. Music for a clip without words. groupe_video Group of the sound mixer voice Strength, away from the player (m/s)shown only if Then is “Push a moving object (Physics system)” The speed given to the pushed object, horizontally and away from the player, in meters per second: 6, a good kick in a ball. The object must carry the Physics system. force Number 6 from 0 to 100 Upwards (m/s)shown only if Then is “Push a moving object (Physics system)” The speed given upwards, in meters per second: 0 sends it skimming along the ground, 5 makes it jump. hauteur Number 2 from 0 to 100 Event to send (a name of the game, or of a system)shown only if Then is “Send an event” The name of the event sent: a name chosen for your game ("door_opened") or a system's. Other rules ("When an event happens") and scripts can wait for it. nom Text (empty) Need to raise (its name)shown only if Then is “Raise a need (Needs system: hunger, tiredness…)” The name of the need, written as in the list of the Needs system: "Tiredness", "Hunger". The player who triggered the rule gets it back: resting by the fire, a meal at the inn, a prayer at the altar. besoin Text (empty) By how muchshown only if Then is “Raise a need (Needs system: hunger, tiredness…)” What the need gets back, without going past its full reserve: 100 out of 100 fills it. A need switched off in the Needs system does not change. montant Number 50 from 0 to 100 000 Effect (its identifier or a tag)shown only if Then is “Apply a status effect (poison, haste…)” or “Remove a status effect” The identifier of an effect of the Status effects system, such as "poison" or "rapidite". To remove, a tag removes every effect carrying it: "poison" for an antidote. alteration Text (empty) On whomshown only if Then is “Apply a status effect (poison, haste…)” or “Remove a status effect” The player who entered the zone or used the object (a poison zone), or the object chosen below: an enemy, a character. porteur Choice in a list The player who triggered the rule joueur: The player who triggered the rulecible: The chosen object (or the one carrying the rule) Duration (s, 0: the effect's own)shown only if Then is “Apply a status effect (poison, haste…)” How many seconds it lasts, for this rule. 0: the duration set in the Status effects system. alteration_duree Number 0 from 0 to 1 000 000 Knowledge to learn (its name)shown only if Then is “Learn a knowledge (Knowledge system)” The name of the knowledge, written as in the list of the Knowledge system: "Ironworking". The player who triggered the rule learns it, even if they lack what is needed first: a master who teaches, an altar, a reward. connaissance Text (empty) How many pointsshown only if Then is “Give knowledge points (Knowledge system)” The knowledge points the player who triggered the rule receives, to spend in the knowledge window (K): a book read, a level gained, a boss defeated. points Number 1 from 1 to 100 000, as a whole number Loot tableshown only if Then is “Drop loot (Loot system)” The name of a table of the Loot module: what it gives drops on the target object (else near the player), as set in the Loot module. table_butin Text (empty) Item levelshown only if Then is “Drop loot (Loot system)” The level of the items rolled: the ranges of their random bonuses grow with it. niveau_butin Number 1 from 1 to 100 000, as a whole number Action settingsshown only if Then is a reusable action that has settings The settings of the chosen action when it is an action written for this game: a distance, a speed… They change with the action. parametres Settings of the chosen action (empty) the settings declared by the reusable action chosen in Then Effectshown only if Then is “Play an effect (fire, chips, explosion…)” The effect played on the target: the one the target carries (its Particle effect system, lit again), or a ready-made effect, played once: chips, dust, an explosion, magic, what a shot shows (a muzzle flash, a bullet impact, a splash)… effet Choice in a list The one placed on the target (Particle effect system) objet: The one placed on the target (Particle effect system)eclats: Chips (the target's colour)eclats_bois: Wood chipseclats_pierre: Stone chipspoussiere: Dustfeu: Firefumee: Smokeexplosion: Explosionetincelles: Sparksimpact: Hit impactmagie: Magicfaisceau: Light beampluie: Rainneige: Snowbouche: Muzzle flash (a shot)impact_balle: Bullet impact (the target's colour)eclaboussure: Splashimpact_chair: Hit on a character Size of the effectshown only if Then is “Play an effect (fire, chips, explosion…)” The size of the ready-made effect: 1 its usual size, 0.5 half as big, 3 for a big explosion. No effect on the one the target carries: it keeps its settings. taille_effet Number 1 from 0.05 to 20 Animationshown only if Then is “Play an animation” or “Stop an animation” The animation made in the editor's timeline (a door that opens, a platform that rises). Playing it again restarts it. frise Animation or cutscene of the scene (empty) Cutsceneshown only if Then is “Play a cutscene” The cutscene made in the editor's timeline. While it plays, the player watches; at the end, they get control back. cinematique Animation or cutscene of the scene (empty) At the end, send the event (optional)shown only if Then is “Play an animation” or “Play a cutscene” A name chosen for your game ("bridge_down"), sent when the animation or cutscene ends: another rule ("When an event happens") can then follow on. Empty: nothing. fin Text (empty)

items.title: Events
items.text: The descriptions come from the code.

items.title: What it announces
items.text: Event Fields Description besoins.remplir besoin (text), montant (number) Ask the besoins system to raise a need by its name, without using anything up: a meal at an inn, a Trigger rule, a script. savoir.apprendre connaissance (text), joueur (id?) Ask the knowledge system to teach connaissance to the player (version 26), even without what it needs first: a Trigger rule, a master in a Dialogue, a quest's reward. A game script can still refuse it (savoir.permise). savoir.donner_points points (number), joueur (id?) Ask the knowledge system to give points to the player (version 26), to spend in the knowledge window: a level gained, a book read. alterations.appliquer cible (id), id (text), duree (number?), source (id?), cumul (any?) Ask the Status effects module to put an effect on a carrier (a player, an enemy, an object), as game.status_apply does. duree in seconds (missing: the effect's own; 0: until removed); cumul: a number of stacks, or refaire, cumuler, ignorer. alterations.retirer cible (id), id (text) Ask the Status effects module to remove an effect from a carrier, or every effect carrying that tag (an antidote removes poison). butin.lacher table (text), position (vector?), cible (id?), niveau (number?), joueur (id?) Ask the Loot module to roll a table and drop what it gives (the Trigger, a script). position or cible: where; niveau: the item level; joueur: for whom (the killer, for sharing).

items.title: What it listens to
items.text: Event Fields Description zone.entree cible (id), qui (id), joueur (id?) Something entered a zone (an object carrying the zone system): a player, a character or a moving object, depending on what the zone detects (joueur: every player). joueur is set when qui is a player. Announced by the engine. zone.sortie cible (id), qui (id), joueur (id?) Something left a zone. Not announced for an object removed from the game while inside. interaction.utiliser cible (id), joueur (id) The player used the object in reach: a door, a merchant, an item to pick up. Whoever owns that object decides what it does. sante.mort cible (id), source (id?) An object's health reached zero. What happens next belongs to the game: the health module does nothing else, unless its setting says to destroy the object. articulation.cassee cible (id), autre (id?) A joint (an object carrying the articulation system) gave way: pulled harder than its breaking force, or broken by the Trigger or game.joint_break. autre is the object it was attached to, missing when attached to the world. Announced by the engine.

items.title: Points a script can replace (game.override)
items.text:
The descriptions come from the code.

  • declencheur.condition: function(default, condition, valeur, regle) -> true or false: whether a rule's condition holds for the player who triggered it. condition is the rule's choice (connait: the player knows the knowledge or tag valeur; ignore: they do not; quete: the quest condition_quete is at condition_etat, and at the step condition_etape for etape), valeur its text, regle all the rule's fields (for a condition that needs more than one). The default, without a system that answers: nobody knows anything and no quest is started (connait is false, ignore is true, quete is true only for pas_commencee). The Savoir system answers connait and ignore, the Quest log (quetes) answers quete; a game script can add its own conditions.

items.title: What the agent knows about this system
items.text: The text the agent reads before using this system.

items.title: Trigger (declencheur)
items.text:
"When… then…" rules placed on objects, so the user gets a game reaction without code: when the player enters a zone, uses a lever, when a boss dies, at the start, after a time, or when an event happens… then show, hide or destroy an object, make a copy appear, teleport the player, go to a scene, end the game, play a sound, play a full-screen video, muffle or mute the sound, show a message, push a moving object, send an event — or run a reusable action written for this game.

  • Place it on the object the rule is about (systems_attach), with its rules in regles: a list, one object per rule. Prefer it to a script for these reactions: the user sees and changes the rules in the object's properties.
  • Each rule: quand (entree, sortie: the object carries zone; utilise: it carries interaction; mort: it carries sante; debut; delai with secondes; evenement with evenement, an event name), fois (une or chaque), attente (seconds before acting), action, and the fields of that action:
  • cible (an object id; empty: the object carrying the rule) for montrer, cacher, basculer, detruire, copier, teleporter (the player goes to it), solide, traversable (on a zone: switches it on or off), son, pousser.
  • copier: lieu (an object where the copy appears; empty: where the copied object is). Usually the copied object is a hidden template.
  • animation: frise (an animation's id, made with timeline_set) and fin (optional: an event sent when it ends, for another rule). cinematique: cinematique (a cutscene's id) and fin. arreter_animation: frise.
  • scene: scene and arrivee. finir: resultat (won or lost) and texte. message: texte, duree; shown on the screen « Message du Déclencheur » (its shape Message), which the user restyles in the screen editor: never draw it yourself, and do not name another screen like it. son: son (a sound file, from assets_search kind "sound"). musique (version 17): musique (a music file, from assets_search kind "sound"), boucle_musique (true by default; false: it plays once and the background music comes back by itself at the end), volume_musique (0 to 1, compared with the sons module's volume_musique: 1 just as loud), fondu_musique (seconds of the fade both ways, 1.5 by default): it plays over the background music (the sons module's), which fades down without stopping, on the mixer group music. musique_revenir: fondu_musique; the background music fades back in where it is. A new musique replaces the previous one (crossfade). assourdir: groupe (a sound mixer group, or master for all the sound), assourdi (0 clear again, 1 under water), fondu (seconds). couper_son: groupe, coupe (true mutes, false brings it back). video: video (an MP4 file, from assets_search kind "video"), passer (true: the player can skip it), fin (an event sent when it ends or is skipped, to chain the next rule; a video file that cannot be read still sends it), groupe_video (the mixer group of its sound, voice by default: the music lowers under it). pousser: force, hauteur. envoyer: nom (sends that event with cible, source and qui). remplir_besoin: besoin (a need's name, as in the besoins list: « Fatigue ») and montant: the player who triggered the rule gets it back (resting by a fire, a meal at an inn); a need switched off does not change.
  • apprendre: connaissance (a knowledge's name, as in the savoir list): the player who triggered the rule learns it, even without what it needs first (a master who teaches, an altar). donner_points: points, knowledge points to spend in the savoir window.
  • lacher_butin (version 12, needs the butin module): table_butin (a loot table) and niveau_butin (the item level); what it gives drops on cible (else near the player who set it off), shown as the Loot module shows loot.
  • cible also for ouvrir, fermer (a hinge or slider of the articulation system: a door, a drawbridge, an elevator; its motor drives it to its open or closed stop), casser (its joint gives way and it falls), chiffon (a character falls limp as a ragdoll) and relever (it gets back up).
  • effet: effet (objet: lights again the effect the target carries with the particules system; or a ready-made effect played once on the target: eclats, eclats_bois, eclats_pierre, poussiere, feu, fumee, explosion, etincelles, impact, magie, faisceau, pluie, neige, and those of a shot: bouche, impact_balle (in the target's colour), eclaboussure, impact_chair) and taille_effet (its size, 1 by default). arreter_effet: puts out the effect the target carries (a campfire), and the looping effects scripts put on it.
  • quand casse: the object's joint broke (it carries articulation): a bridge gives way, then a message.
  • cible (a placed light, created with a light field) for allumer (switch on), eteindre (switch off), basculer_lumiere (on or off in turn) and couleur_lumiere, with couleur ("#rrggbb"): a lamp lit by a lever, an alarm turning red.
  • Example, a pressure plate that opens a door: a zone box named Plaque, and on it {"regles": [{"quand": "entree", "action": "cacher", "cible": "<door id>"}]}.
  • Under water: a zone box over the water with {"regles": [{"quand": "entree", "fois": "chaque", "action": "assourdir", "groupe": "master", "assourdi": 1}, {"quand": "sortie", "fois": "chaque", "action": "assourdir", "groupe": "master", "assourdi": 0}]}.
  • A brazier lit by a lever: the particules system on the brazier with boucle true, and on the lever {"quand": "utilise", "fois": "chaque", "action": "effet", "effet": "objet", "cible": "<brazier id>"}; another rule with arreter_effet puts it out. A barrel that explodes when hit: {"quand": "mort", "action": "effet", "effet": "explosion", "taille_effet": 2} then a rule that destroys it.
  • A lever: interaction on the lever and a rule {"quand": "utilise", "fois": "chaque", "action": "basculer", "cible": "<door id>"}.
  • Something that comes back every few seconds (a rock launcher, falling crates, a wave of barrels): one rule, no script. {"quand": "delai", "secondes": 4, "fois": "chaque", "action": "copier", "cible": "<hidden template id>", "lieu": "<spawn point id>"} makes a copy of the template at the spawn point every 4 s. Give the template the physique system: each copy falls and rolls by itself (put the spawn point at the top of a slope, or above the course). pousser pushes its cible away from the player who triggered the rule (a placed object, the template), not the copy just made: to throw each copy in a direction, write a reusable action once (below). Never write a timer script for what this rule does.
  • Chase music at the start of a quest step, back at its end (also a boss, an area): on the step, "annonce_debut": "poursuite.debut" and "annonce": "poursuite.fin" (sent when it ends); on any object {"regles": [{"quand": "evenement", "evenement": "poursuite.debut", "fois": "chaque", "action": "musique", "musique": "<music file>", "fondu_musique": 0.5}, {"quand": "evenement", "evenement": "poursuite.fin", "fois": "chaque", "action": "musique_revenir"}]}. Add the same musique_revenir rule on the quest's annonce_echec so a failed or abandoned chase does not keep its music. A boss: musique on entree of its arena zone, musique_revenir on its mort. Never write a script, never use game.music for this: the background music would restart from the beginning.
  • A lamp switched by a lever: {"quand": "utilise", "fois": "chaque", "action": "basculer_lumiere", "cible": "<light id>"}.
  • A drawbridge that lowers when the lever is used, then a chest appears: {"quand": "utilise", "action": "animation", "frise": "pont_baisse", "fin": "pont_en_bas"} on the lever, and {"quand": "evenement", "evenement": "pont_en_bas", "action": "montrer", "cible": "<chest id>"}. A door that moves (slides, swings) is an animation, not a reusable action.

Conditions: every rule has condition (aucune by default; connait: only if the player who triggered it knows condition_valeur, a knowledge or a tag of the savoir system; ignore: only if they do not; quete: only while the quest condition_quete (its original title in the quetes log) is at condition_etat for that player: pas_commencee, en_cours, etape (in progress and the step condition_etape, its number from 1 or its label, is the one to do), finie, echouee, abandonnee, disponible: it can be given now, its prerequisites met and not already done today); reputation (version 17): only if that player's reputation with the faction condition_piste (a reputation track of the progression system) is at least the tier condition_palier (its name, such as « Amical », or a number); the Progression answers it, and without it the rule never acts. A "once" rule whose condition is not met waits for the next time. Example, a bridge that only opens during a quest: {"quand": "utilise", "condition": "quete", "condition_quete": "The mill bridge", "condition_etat": "en_cours", "action": "cacher"}. The quest log answers it itself: never write a script or a mark that copies a quest's state for a rule. Example, a door only a lockpicker opens: {"quand": "utilise", "condition": "connait", "condition_valeur": "Lockpicking", "action": "cacher"}, and a second rule ignore with a message "Locked". A game script can answer its own conditions with game.override « declencheur.condition » (function(default, condition, valeur, regle): regle holds all the rule's fields).

Reusable actions: when the user wants an effect no ready-made action does and that is not a set movement (a set movement such as a door that slides, a bridge that rises or a light that blinks is an animation: timeline_set, then the action animation), write it ONCE as a reusable action, never as a one-off script tied to one object: - A game script named action.<id> (scripts_set; id: lowercase letters, digits, _), which starts with its description in JSON between --[[action and ]]: label and description in fr and en, and fields (settings like a module's: key, type number/text/boolean/choice/object/sound/video/scene, default, label in fr and en, min/max, options; a number takes decimals unless it has "integer": true, for a count). - Its code listens to action.<id>: game.on("action.porte_glissante", function(e) ... end). e.cible is the rule's target (or the object carrying the rule), e.source the object carrying the rule, e.qui who triggered it, and each of its fields by key. - It then appears in the "Then" list of every Trigger, with its fields, next to the ready-made actions; a rule uses it with "action": "<id>" and its values in parametres. The user can reuse it on other objects without asking you again: tell them so. - Example: --[[action {"label": {"fr": "Porte qui glisse", "en": "Sliding door"}, "description": {"fr": "La cible glisse sur le côté.", "en": "The target slides aside."}, "fields": [{"key": "distance", "type": "number", "default": 2, "min": 0, "max": 50, "label": {"fr": "Distance (m)", "en": "Distance (m)"}}]} ]], then the code.

items.title: Several players
items.text:
One for the whole game: "the player" of a rule is the one who triggered it (who entered the zone, who used the object); its message is shown to that player only, and teleporter moves that player. Rules at the start or after a delay concern no one in particular: their message is shown to everyone.

This page is generated automatically from the WorldMint code (modules/declencheur/module.json, modules/declencheur/AGENT.md, modules/events.json): it always matches the editor.

items.title: Dialogue
items.text:
A character who talks when used: their lines show one by one, with the player's answers as buttons. An answer leads to another line and can send an event, to which the Trigger system or a script reacts. Tests (an item carried, a mark, the talks already had, how far a quest is) choose what they say.

Identifier dialogue Version 11 Placed on objects yes Also activates Interaction Also needs, on the same object Interaction

items.title: Settings for the whole game
items.text:
In the Systems panel (Developer mode), by opening the system's card.

Setting What it does Name in code Type Default Limits or choices Stop the game during a dialogue Ticked: the world stops while the dialogue window is open, enemies included. Unticked: the game goes on behind it. pause Yes or no yes Bottom of the window (share of the screen height) Where the dialogue window ends, from the top of the screen: 0.96 puts it at the very bottom, 0.5 in the middle. It grows upwards with the text and the choices. bas Number 0.96 from 0.2 to 1 Width of the window (old) No longer used: the window is now the screen "Dialogue". To widen it, drag the handle of its shape "Bulle" (and of "Texte" and "Réponses") in the screen editor. Kept for the games that had set it. largeur Number 0.6 from 0.2 to 1

items.title: Settings on each object
items.text:
In the Properties of an object or folder that carries the system, Systems section. A folder passes its values on to what it contains; an object can change a value for itself only.

Setting What it does Name in code Type Default Limits or choices Name shown (empty: the object's name) The name written at the top of the window, above what they say. Empty: the object's name in the scene. nom Text (empty) The dialogue What the character says, what the player can answer, and the tests that choose what comes next, in order. The dialogue starts at the first row; "Show the map" shows it at a glance. lignes List of “Row” (empty) one line per “Row”: its fields

items.title: The fields of each “Row”
items.text:
In the Properties, each “Row” has its own numbered frame; Add: Row adds one, the cross removes it. A field only appears when it is useful: under its name, the table says when.

Setting What it does Name in code Type Default Limits or choices Kind of row What this row does: the character says a line; the player answers (an answer belongs to the line above it); a test chooses what comes next according to the game; a test's exit says where to go from a number on. sorte Choice in a list The character says replique: The character sayschoix: The player answerstest: Testsortie: Test exit Label (to lead here)shown only if Kind of row is “The character says” or “Test” A word naming this row, such as "friend". A next step that is this word leads here. A labelled row starts a branch: the row above does not continue into it. etiquette Text (empty) Textshown only if Kind of row is “The character says” or “The player answers” What the character says, or the text of the answer's button. It wraps by itself; [b]bold[/b] and [color=#ff8800]color[/color] change the look of a word. texte Text (empty) Questionshown only if Kind of row is “Test” What the test looks at. Yes or no: does the player carry an item, is a mark set, is a quest at that point (not started, in progress, at a step, finished…). By a number: the talks already finished with this character, or how many of an item they carry; the "Test exit" rows that follow say where to go. test Choice in a list Do they carry an item? objet: Do they carry an item?marque: Is a mark set?visites: By the talks already finishedquantite: By how many of an item they carryquete: How far is a quest? Itemshown only if Kind of row is “Test” ; shown only if Question is “Do they carry an item?” or “By how many of an item they carry” The kind of item, as the inventory stores it, such as "Key" or "Gold". test_objet Text (empty) How many at leastshown only if Kind of row is “Test” ; shown only if Question is “Do they carry an item?” The number to carry for a yes, such as 10 gold coins. test_quantite Number 1 from 1 to 1 000 000, as a whole number Markshown only if Kind of row is “Test” ; shown only if Question is “Is a mark set?” The mark's word, such as "met_the_king". test_marque Text (empty) Quest (its title)shown only if Kind of row is “Test” ; shown only if Question is “How far is a quest?” The quest's title, as written in the Quest log (its original language), such as "The mill bridge". test_quete Text (empty) How far it isshown only if Kind of row is “Test” ; shown only if Question is “How far is a quest?” Not started, in progress, at a given step (in progress, and that step to do now), finished, failed, abandoned, or can be given (its prerequisites met, not already done today: the yellow "!"). The Quest log tells it: nothing to copy here. test_etat Choice in a list In progress pas_commencee: Not starteden_cours: In progressetape: At a stepfinie: Finishedechouee: Failedabandonnee: Abandoneddisponible: Can be given Step (its number or its label)shown only if Kind of row is “Test” ; shown only if Question is “How far is a quest?” ; shown only if How far it is is “At a step” The quest's step: its number (1 for the first step) or its label, such as "bridge". Yes while it is the one to do. test_etape Text (empty) If yes: label (empty: the next row; fin: ends)shown only if Kind of row is “Test” ; shown only if Question is “Do they carry an item?”, “Is a mark set?” or “How far is a quest?” Where the dialogue goes on a yes: a row's label, "fin", or empty for the next row, if it has no label. si_oui Text (empty) If no: label (empty: the next row; fin: ends)shown only if Kind of row is “Test” ; shown only if Question is “Do they carry an item?”, “Is a mark set?” or “How far is a quest?” Where the dialogue goes on a no: a row's label, "fin", or empty for the next row, if it has no label. si_non Text (empty) Fromshown only if Kind of row is “Test exit” The number from which this exit is taken, up to the next exit's. 0, 1, 2, 3 then 4: the last one counts for 4 and more. a_partir_de Number 0 from 0 to 1 000 000, as a whole number Offeredshown only if Kind of row is “The player answers” When the player sees this answer. items.text: Event Fields Description dialogue.debut cible (id) A dialogue window opened: cible is the character who talks. dialogue.choix cible (id), choix (number), texte (text), etiquette (text) The player chose an answer in a dialogue: choix is its rank among the answers shown (from 1), texte its text, etiquette the label of the line it answered (empty if none). Sent before the answer's own event, if it has one. dialogue.marque marque (text) A dialogue set a mark: a word the game remembers (a line shown, an answer chosen). Every dialogue's conditions can use it. dialogue.fin cible (id) A dialogue window closed: after its last line, or a choice leading to fin. boutique.ouvrir cible (id), onglet (text?), joueur (id?) Ask the shop system to open the shop of cible, as if the player had used it: from a dialogue answer, a trigger, a script. onglet opens it on another module's tab (equipement.atelier: the services). It opens for joueur only; without joueur, for the host only (never for every player).

items.title: What it listens to
items.text: Event Fields Description interaction.utiliser cible (id), joueur (id) The player used the object in reach: a door, a merchant, an item to pick up. Whoever owns that object decides what it does. dialogue.ouvrir cible (id) Ask the dialogue system to start the dialogue of cible, as if the player had used it: from a zone, a trigger, a script. dialogue.marquer marque (text), retirer (boolean?) Ask the dialogue system to set a mark, from a script or another system; with retirer true, to remove it. Dialogue conditions then see it. inventaire.change objet (text), quantite (number), total (number), chargement (boolean?), fiche (number?), jete (boolean?) The quantity of an item changed. total is the new quantity. chargement is true when a saved game gives the items back (game.load): nothing was picked up. For a unique copy (version 15), objet is its kind, fiche its record's number, total how many of that kind. With several stacks of a kind (version 21), total counts all of them; jete is true when a slot was dropped on the ground. langue.change langue (text) Sent by the engine when the player changes the game's language (game.set_language, the Menu options). A module redraws what it already shows: its texts go through game.t and game.language.

items.title: Dialogue (dialogue)
items.text:
A character who talks when the player uses them: their lines show one by one in a window at the bottom of the screen, with the player's answers as buttons. Activating it activates interaction; placing it on an object places interaction there too. Use it for every talk the user asks for (a merchant, a guard, a quest giver) rather than a script.

Place it on the character with systems_attach, then fill lignes with systems_set: a list of rows, in order, read like a flowchart. Each row has a sorte:

  • replique: the character says texte. The choix rows right under it are its answers.
  • choix: an answer the player can click (texte is its button). As many as needed. condition hides it unless it is met: objet / sans_objet (condition_objet, condition_quantite), marque / sans_marque (condition_marque), visites (condition_visites: talks with this character already finished), quete (condition_quete, condition_etat, condition_etape: as the quete test below), reputation (version 11: the player's reputation with the faction condition_piste, a reputation track of the progression system, is at least the tier condition_palier, its name such as « Amical », or at least that number; without progression, never offered).
  • test: a question to the game, which chooses where to go.
  • Yes or no: test: "objet" (test_objet, test_quantite), test: "marque" (test_marque) or test: "quete" (test_quete: the quest's original title in the quetes log; test_etat: pas_commencee, en_cours, etape, finie, echouee, abandonnee, disponible (it can be given now: its prerequisites met, not already done today; the yellow "!"); test_etape for etape: the step to do now, its number from 1 or its label), with si_oui and si_non.
  • By a number: test: "visites" (talks already finished) or test: "quantite" (how many test_objet the player carries), followed by sortie rows.
  • sortie: an exit of the number test above it: a_partir_de (from this number on, up to the next exit's; the last one counts for "and more") and suite.

How it flows:

  • The dialogue starts at the first row. Tests are crossed until a line to show.
  • suite, si_oui, si_non say where to go next: a row's etiquette (replique and test rows have one), fin to close, or empty for the row after the group.
  • An empty suite goes on to the row after only if that row has no etiquette: a labelled row starts another branch, so the talk ends before it. Give a label to every row a branch leads to, and none to the rows that simply follow.
  • marque (on a line or an answer) sets a word the game remembers, for every dialogue's tests and answers. annonce sends an event at the same moment, for a declencheur rule or a script.

A character who says something else before a quest, during its step 2 and after it (the quest log tells where the quest is; never copy it with marks):

  1. test quete « The bridge » test_etat: "finie", si_oui: "after"
  2. test quete « The bridge » test_etat: "etape", test_etape: "2", si_oui: "during"
  3. test quete « The bridge » test_etat: "pas_commencee", si_oui: "before", si_non: "started"
  4. one labelled replique per branch; under before, the answer that gives the quest (annonce = its depart_evenement)

A guard who loses patience, then lets in who has the key:

  1. test objet Clé, si_oui: "entre", si_non empty (the next row)
  2. test visites
  3. its exits: sortie 0 → cle, 1 → encore, 2 → rien, 3 → assez, 4 → cachot
  4. one labelled replique per branch (cle, encore, rien, assez, cachot with annonce: "cachot", entre)

Other details:

  • Answers: a line with no answer shown has a Next button, or End when nothing follows.
  • A merchant: on a character who also carries boutique (opening on use), the dialogue comes first, and its last line (the one with End) also offers "Show me your goods" ("Voir la marchandise"), which closes the conversation and opens the shop (boutique.ouvrir). If a line of the dialogue already sends boutique.ouvrir, that button is not added.
  • Gamepad and keyboard: each new line gives the focus to its first button; A or Enter clicks it, the d-pad or the arrows choose another answer. End is the window's back button (B, Escape); a line with Next or answers has none, so Escape still opens the pause there.
  • Saved games: game.save keeps the marks and the conversations already had with each character, and game.load gives them back.
  • Inventory: objet tests and conditions read the inventaire system (the kind of item, as it stores it), so add it to the game.
  • Marks from scripts: a script sets one with game.emit("dialogue.marquer", {marque = "..."}) (retirer = true removes it) and hears them with dialogue.marque.
  • Language: write every line in the user's language, and keep each line short (two or three sentences). For a game offered in other languages, the lines, answers and name go through the game's translation tables (translations_set): never write a dialogue per language.
  • Name and prompt: the name at the top is nom (empty: the object's name). Set the interaction prompt texte to "Talk" in the user's language.
  • Events: dialogue.choix (cible, choix, texte, etiquette), dialogue.debut and dialogue.fin (cible). game.emit("dialogue.ouvrir", {cible = id}) starts a character's dialogue from a zone or a script.
  • Game settings: pause (the world stops during a dialogue, on by default), and bas, a share of the screen height (where the window ends at the bottom; it grows upwards). largeur is no longer used (kept for old games): resize the shape Bulle (and Texte, Réponses) with screens_set.
  • The window is a screen delivered by the system, « Dialogue » (modules/dialogue/ecrans/dialogue.json): Bulle, Nom, Texte, the list Réponses (row Choix), Boutique ("Show me your goods"), Suivant (Next or End). Its buttons send the system's actions choix, suivant, boutique. Change its look, places and sizes with screens_set (styles, not hand-made values); never draw a dialogue with game.hud_*, and never edit the system.
  • The map: the user sees the dialogue as a map in the editor (the character's properties, "Show the map"). It is a flowchart from Start to an End per branch, with boxes for lines, diamonds for tests, and named arrows (an answer, yes, no, "4 and more"). Labels that lead nowhere show in red there: check yours. The user can also edit the dialogue in that map (reconnect an arrow by dragging it, add or remove steps): read lignes again before changing a dialogue they may have touched.
  • Testing: in game_run, walk to the character, press interact, then click the buttons. The report's hud gives each button's area (Dialogue/Suivant, Dialogue/Choix#1, Dialogue/Boutique...).

items.title: Stamina
items.text:
Placed on the player: running, jumping and striking tire them. Exhausted, they can only walk until they recover. Shows its bar under the health bar.

items.text: Event Fields Description endurance.change valeur (number), max (number), epuise (boolean) The player's stamina changed. epuise is true from zero until they regain a share of it: meanwhile they cannot run, jump or strike.

items.title: Stamina (endurance)
items.text:
Place it on the player (systems_attach): running, jumping and striking (with combat.basique) cost stamina; resting gives it back after a short delay. At zero, the player is exhausted: they can still walk, but not run, jump or strike until they regain a share of it (reprise). Placed on anything else, it does nothing.

  • The player's values (systems_set): maximum, costs, recovery, delay, share to regain.
  • For the whole game (modules_set): the bar under the health bar, dimmed while exhausted, its place, size and color. It is the screen « Barre d'endurance » delivered by the system (shapes Fond and Barre; HUD key Barre d'endurance/Barre), which the user restyles in the screen editor; the settings move and size its shapes. Never draw a stamina bar yourself, and do not name another screen « Barre d'endurance ».
  • Know the value: listen to endurance.change (valeur, max, epuise), announced on the first step, then when it changes.
  • Costs are multiplied by the value endurance_cout when it is declared (1 by default): the inventory's weight raises it at an overload step (its endurance field). A script may give it a bonus too (game.stat_bonus(player, "endurance_cout", "potion", {pct = -0.5})).
  • Only running, jumping and the strikes of combat.basique cost stamina. If the user wants another action to tire the player, say it is not available yet.
  • It uses game.set_player_can_run and game.set_player_can_jump: do not call them yourself while this module is in the game.

items.title: Enemies
items.text:
What carries this system patrols, chases the player when it sees them, and hits them in reach, or shoots at them from afar (bullet, arrow, fireball), with its own values: an early skeleton and a boss have neither the same speed nor the same damage. They walk around walls.

Identifier ennemis Version 10 Placed on objects yes Also activates Health Also needs, on the same object Health

items.text:
In the Systems panel (Developer mode), by opening the system's card.

Setting What it does Name in code Type Default Limits or choices Enemies striking at once (0: all) How many enemies can strike the player at the same time; the others circle around them waiting their turn. 1 or 2 keeps a fight against several playable. 0: all strike together. attaquants_max Number 0 from 0 to 100, as a whole number Distance where the others wait their turn (m) How far from the player, in meters, the enemies waiting their turn circle around them. distance_attente Number 3.5 from 1 to 50

items.title: Events
items.text: The descriptions come from the code.

items.title: What it announces
items.text: Event Fields Description ennemi.etat cible (id), etat (text) An enemy changed state: patrouille (patrols), poursuite (chases the player), visee (a shooter aims before its first shot: the moment for a warning sound), attaque (hits in reach, or shoots), attente (waits its turn near the player, when enough others are already attacking), retour (goes back to its spot), mort (dead, does nothing more). ennemi.tir source (id), cible (id), sorte (text) An enemy fired a shot at a player (its setting tir): sorte is balle, fleche or boule_de_feu. Announced when the shot leaves, hit or miss; a hit is then announced by combat.coup. Listen to it for a sound of your own, a shake of the screen, or to count shots. combat.coup cible (id), source (id), montant (number) An attack hit something. The health module, if present, has been asked to remove the damage. sante.blesser cible (id), montant (number), source (id?) Ask the health module to remove health from an object.

items.title: What it listens to
items.text: Event Fields Description scene.change depuis (text), vers (text) Sent by the engine once the player has arrived in another scene of the game (game.go_to, or a passage). Scripts keep running across scenes: this is when a module looks at the objects of the new scene. sante.mort cible (id), source (id?) An object's health reached zero. What happens next belongs to the game: the health module does nothing else, unless its setting says to destroy the object. sante.change cible (id), vie (number), max (number) An object's health changed, or is announced once when the game starts. projectile.touche projectile (number), owner (id?), cible (id?), point (vector), normale (vector), partie (text?), os (text?), vitesse (vector), eau (boolean?), data (table?) A projectile launched by game.projectile hit something: cible is the object hit (nil for the terrain and for water), partie the part of a character's body (tete, torse, bras, jambes; missing for an object), os the bone, vitesse its velocity on arrival (m/s), data the table given at launch. eau = true when it entered water (point on the surface): it goes on, strongly slowed, and sinks (put a splash there, game.effect("eclaboussure", e.point), or stop it with game.stop_projectile). Announced by the engine; a projectile that bounces announces each hit. projectile.fin projectile (number), owner (id?), raison (text), point (vector), data (table?) A projectile launched by game.projectile is gone: raison is touche (it hit and stopped), duree (its life ran out: a grenade explodes here), plantee (stuck, its delay is over), cible_partie (what it was stuck in disappeared), eau (a projectile without gravity stopped by water) or arrete (game.stop_projectile). point is where it ended. Announced by the engine.

items.title: What the agent knows about this system
items.text: The text the agent reads before using this system.

items.title: Enemies (ennemis)
items.text:
Objects carrying this system become characters with a state machine: they patrol around their spot, chase the player once they see them, hit them in reach, and go back home when they lose them. Placing it on an object places Health there too. Add it only if the user asked for enemies that attack.

  • Place it on each kind of enemy, best on a group: "Early skeletons" with low damage and speed, "Late skeletons" with high values, the boss alone with its own. Set them with systems_set, and the Health values (health, armor) the same way. A child can change one value for itself.
  • Several enemies at once: set the game setting attaquants_max (modules_set), usually 1 or 2. Only that many strike at the same time; the others wait their turn at distance_attente, circling the player, and step in when a place is free. With the default 0, all strike together: five skeletons in reach kill the player in seconds.
  • States: patrouille, poursuite, visee (a shooter aims before its first shot), attaque, attente (waits its turn), retour, mort. Each change is announced by ennemi.etat (cible, etat): listen to it for a growl, an alert icon, a music change.
  • They walk around obstacles (objects with a collider) to reach the player or go back home. A closed room keeps them out. With vue on, they still have to see the player first.
  • With vue on, walls with a collider hide the player; they give up after recherche seconds without seeing them (3 by default), or beyond abandon.
  • Their hits go through the health module, like the player's: the player's armor applies. They are announced by combat.coup. When the player dies, they all go back home.
  • Death: a dead enemy never moves nor strikes again. animation_mort (empty by default) is a clip of its own model, picked from its clips (animation_clips), never guessed: it plays once and the body stays on its last frame, seen the same by guests. Empty: it just stops where it stands; say so to the user and offer to pick a clip. corps: reste (default; Loot can still open its window on it), apres (stays duree_corps seconds, then goes), aussitot; it goes with effet_corps (retrecir, effondrer, eclater, tomber, or aucun) in duree_effet_corps seconds. Health's « remove at death » still removes it at once.
  • Animations: give the clip names of their model (read them with animation_clips); without them, nothing plays. Never guess a clip name.
  • Enemies cloned during the game from one carrying the system join in within half a second, with its values.

items.title: Enemies that shoot
items.text:
Only if the user asked for enemies that shoot, throw or cast (soldiers, archers, a mage). Set tir on that group: balle (an instant shot, a firearm), fleche (flies, drops, sticks) or boule_de_feu (slow, straight, explodes). The other values appear once tir is set; everything is per object or group, nothing is in a script.

  • What the player sees: before its first shot the enemy aims for temps_visee seconds: it turns, leans its upper body toward the player (game.aim_at), a small glint shines (eclat_visee), and son_visee / animation_visee play if given. It aims again each time it lost sight. Never set temps_visee to 0 for ordinary enemies: the player needs that moment to take cover.
  • Walls: it never shoots through a collider. Hidden, it walks around the wall to find the player again (state poursuite); give shooters a longer recherche (6 to 10 s) than melee guards, or they give up quickly.
  • Distance: it shoots within portee_tir and keeps distance_gardee (steps back when the player comes closer, moves in when they back off, shooting as it walks; 0: it stays put). With frappe_de_pres (default), right next to the player it strikes with its melee values (portee, degats, recharge) instead.
  • Accuracy: imprecision degrees at first, going down to imprecision_min after temps_ajustement seconds of steady aim, plus imprecision_mouvement degrees per m/s of the player's speed. So: far shots often miss, a player who stays in the open gets hit more and more, running helps.
  • Rhythm: bursts of rafale shots at cadence shots per second, then pause_rafales; chargeur shots before a reload of temps_rechargement s (0: never reloads). degats_tir per shot, times multiplicateur_tete on the head (the part is measured on the player's skeleton).
  • Several at once: attaquants_max counts shooters too: aiming or shooting takes a place; the others keep their distance and wait. With 3 or more shooters, set it to 1 or 2.
  • Allies: by default its shots pass through other enemies and never hurt them (blesse_allies off). On, an enemy in the way blocks the shot, so it moves to clear its line.
  • Projectiles (fleche, boule_de_feu): vitesse_projectile (an arrow 30-50 m/s, a fireball 10-15: dodgeable), gravite_projectile (0 for a fireball, 0.3-1 for an arrow; it aims higher to make up for it), anticipation (0: aims where the player is, 1: where they will be). modele_projectile: a hidden object of the scene (an arrow, a ball), copied for each shot; without it, a bright trail shows the projectile.
  • Effects: effets_tir (default on) shows the muzzle flash, the trail, impacts and bullet holes on scenery, a puff on a body, a small explosion for a fireball. Sounds (son_tir, son_rechargement) and animations (animation_tir, animation_rechargement) are optional: clip names read on the model with animation_clips (a pistol pack has clips such as Pistol_Idle_Loop, Pistol_Shoot, Pistol_Reload: use what the model really has; for the idle clip while armed, set animation_repos to its armed idle).
  • Shipped sounds (cite "sons/<pack>/<file>", copied into the project with their licence; several separated by commas: one at random at each shot): son_tir of a gunman the family of its weapon (sons/armes-a-feu/pistolet_1.wav, sons/armes-a-feu/pistolet_2.wav, fusil_assaut_, mitraillette_, fusil_pompe_, fusil_precision_, revolver_), or its _loin file for an enemy that shoots from afar (a sniper); son_rechargement sons/rechargements/chargeur_fusil.wav (or chargeur_pistolet, pompe_armer). An archer (tir fleche): son_tir sons/arc-arbalete/arc_tir_1.wav, sons/arc-arbalete/arc_tir_2.wav (a crossbowman arbalete_tir_1..3), son_visee sons/arc-arbalete/arc_bander_1.wav. A mage (tir boule_de_feu): son_tir sons/explosions-magie/boule_de_feu_lancer_1.wav, sons/explosions-magie/boule_de_feu_lancer_2.wav. The impact of an enemy's projectile has no sound setting yet.
  • Each shot announces ennemi.tir (source, cible, sorte), hit or miss; a hit is announced by combat.coup and goes through sante.blesser (the player's armor and invulnerability apply).

Starting values by kind of game (the player has 100 health points; defaults are the first line):

Game tir degats_tir rafale / cadence / pause_rafales imprecision / imprecision_min temps_visee portee_tir / distance_gardee Action, third person (default) balle 8 3 / 4 / 1.5 7 / 3 0.8 25 / 10 Arcade, many enemies balle 5 2 / 3 / 2 9 / 5 1.2 20 / 8 Tactical, few deadly enemies balle 25 1 / 1 / 2.5 3 / 0.5 1.5 60 / 25 Medieval archer fleche 12 1 / 1 / 2 4 / 1.5 1 35 / 18 Mage boule_de_feu 15 1 / 1 / 2.5 3 / 1 1 20 / 10 (vitesse_projectile 12, gravite_projectile 0) Sniper (one, far) balle 40 1 / 1 / 4 2 / 0 2.5 120 / 60

Measured with the default values: a player standing still in the open, two pistol shooters 17-19 m away, survives about 22 s; about a third of the shots hit. Tell the user these are starting points to tune by playing.

items.title: Several players
items.text:
One for the whole game: each enemy chases the nearest living player it sees and keeps them while it sees them; when that player falls or is lost, it looks for another, or goes home.

This page is generated automatically from the WorldMint code (modules/ennemis/module.json, modules/ennemis/AGENT.md, modules/events.json): it always matches the editor.

items.title: Equipment
items.text:
The player wears items in slots (head, chest, weapon, rings...) that you invent: their bonuses add to their characteristics, and they can show on the character. They wear an item by double-clicking it in the inventory or dragging it onto a slot.

Identifier equipement Version 8 Placed on objects no Also activates Inventory

Progression's required levels apply too. niveau_requis Number 0 from 0 to 100 000, as a whole number Level track (empty: the highest) The key of the Progression track, such as "personnage". piste Text (empty) Characteristic required A value, such as "force": at least the minimum below is needed. carac_requise Text (empty) Characteristic minimum The total to reach. carac_min Number 0 from -1 000 000 to 1 000 000 Temporary effect while worn With the Temporary effects module: the effect set while the item is worn (with no duration), removed when taken off. effet Text (empty) What shows A model attached to a bone, pieces of the character shown or hidden, both, or nothing. visible Choice in a list Nothing rien: Nothingmodele: A model attachedpieces: Pieces of the characterles_deux: Both Model attached (an object of the scene, usually hidden) The object a copy of which shows on the character. Empty: the bone of the slot's body part (the head...), found by measuring the skeleton; otherwise the place of the object set in the editor. os Text (empty) Offset X (m) Moves the model along the bone's first axis, in metres. decalage_x Number 0 from -2 to 2 Offset Y (m) Moves the model along the bone's second axis, in metres. decalage_y Number 0 from -2 to 2 Offset Z (m) Moves the model along the bone's third axis, in metres. decalage_z Number 0 from -2 to 2 Rotation X (°) Turns the model around the bone's first axis, in degrees. rotation_x Number 0 from -180 to 180 Rotation Y (°) Turns the model around the bone's second axis, in degrees. rotation_y Number 0 from -180 to 180 Rotation Z (°) Turns the model around the bone's third axis, in degrees. rotation_z Number 0 from -180 to 180 Size X (× the model's) Enlarges or shrinks the attached model along its X axis, to fit the measured head or body: 1 keeps its size. echelle_x Number 1 from 0.01 to 100 Size Y (× the model's) Enlarges or shrinks the attached model along its Y (height) axis, to fit the measured head or body: 1 keeps its size. echelle_y Number 1 from 0.01 to 100 Size Z (× the model's) Enlarges or shrinks the attached model along its Z (depth) axis, to fit the measured head or body: 1 keeps its size. echelle_z Number 1 from 0.01 to 100 Character pieces to show The names of the pieces (objects of the character) shown while it is worn, separated by commas: chosen in the model, such as "Armor_chest". pieces_montrer Text (empty) Character pieces to hide The names of the pieces hidden while it is worn, separated by commas (the hair under a helmet). pieces_cacher Text (empty) Maximum durability (0: does not wear) The durability of a new copy. Each use lowers it; at zero the item is broken or destroyed (setting "Durability: at zero"). usure_max Number 0 from 0 to 1 000 000, as a whole number What wears it Weapon: each hit (Combat) or shot (Shooting) while in hand. Armour: each hit taken while worn (Health). Tool: each harvest while in hand (Gathering). usee_par Choice in a list Nothing aucun: Nothingattaque: A hit or a shot (weapon)coup_recu: A hit taken (armour)recolte: A harvest (tool) Durability lost each time How much durability goes with each hit, shot, hit taken or harvest. perte Number 1 from 0 to 1 000 000 Maximum upgrade level (0: none) How far the item can be upgraded at a station or a merchant; its name shows the level ("Iron sword +2"). niveau_max Number 0 from 0 to 100, as a whole number Each level: % of the bonuses Each level adds this percentage of the item's bonuses (10: +2 gives 20% more). 0: only the "Bonuses per level". amelioration_pct Number 0 from 0 to 1000 Gem sockets How many gems a copy of this kind can take (Loot can also roll them). emplacements_gemmes Number 0 from 0 to 8, as a whole number
