items.title: Events
items.text: The descriptions come from the code.

items.title: What it announces
items.text: Event Fields Description equipement.porte joueur (id), emplacement (text), objet (text), fiche (number?) The player now wears an item: emplacement is the slot key, objet its kind, fiche its record (a unique copy). Its bonuses have the source equipement:<emplacement>. equipement.retire joueur (id), emplacement (text), objet (text), fiche (number?) The player took off an item: it is back in the bag, and its bonuses are gone. equipement.refus joueur (id), raison (text) Wearing was refused: raison is the text shown (a condition, the game's equipement.avant hook, a record that is not the player's, no slot). inventaire.sortir objet (text), fiche (number?), case (text?), joueur (id?) Ask the inventory to take one item out of the bag without destroying it (version 16): objet is its kind, fiche a unique copy (it keeps its record; whoever takes it says its new holder). The Equipment module takes what it makes the player wear. A stack gives one from its smallest stack, or from case (version 21), a slot's key. inventaire.ajouter objet (text), quantite (number), joueur (id?), fiche (number?) Ask the inventory to add items, such as a reward. Answered by inventaire.change, or inventaire.plein. With several players, joueur says whose bag; without it, the player whose action is being handled, or every player. inventaire.tenir_porte objet (text), fiche (number?), prioritaire (boolean?), joueur (id?) Ask the inventory to hold in hand an item worn (version 17): the Equipment module hands it the weapon of its slot, so it is held, shown (its row of the list Models in hand, measured hold included) and announced (inventaire.en_main) exactly like the bar's. objet "" : nothing worn in hand any more. prioritaire: it comes before the bar; otherwise only when the bar holds nothing. equipement.casse joueur (id), fiche (number), objet (text), usure (number), usure_max (number) A unique copy's durability reached zero and it is broken (setting a_zero casse): kept, greyed, without its bonuses until repaired. equipement.detruit joueur (id), fiche (number), objet (text), usure (number), usure_max (number) A unique copy's durability reached zero and it is destroyed (setting a_zero detruit). equipement.usure_alerte joueur (id), fiche (number), objet (text), usure (number), usure_max (number) A unique copy's durability went below the warning threshold (seuil_usure, 20% by default). equipement.repare joueur (id), fiche (number), objet (text), par (text), usure (number), usure_max (number) A unique copy was repaired: par station, boutique or kit; usure and usure_max its new durability. equipement.ameliore joueur (id), fiche (number), objet (text), reussi (boolean), niveau (number), echec (text?) An upgrade was tried: reussi says whether the roll succeeded, niveau the copy's level now, echec what a failure did (rien, niveau_perdu, casse). equipement.serti joueur (id), fiche (number), objet (text), gemme (text) A gem was set into a unique copy. equipement.desserti joueur (id), fiche (number), objet (text), gemme (text), rendue (boolean) A gem was removed from a unique copy: rendue says whether it went back to the bag. equipement.retirer emplacement (text), joueur (id?) Ask the Equipment module to take off what is worn at a slot (its key, such as tete, or its name): it goes back to the bag. equipement.reparer fiche (number?), par (text?), cible (id?), joueur (id?) Ask the Equipment module to repair a unique copy (ADR-039 section 6): par is station (at the station named by station_reparation, cible that station), boutique (cible a merchant, with boutique_reparation), or kit (one repair kit taken from the bag; without fiche, the most worn of what is worn or held). On the host, the record must be the player's (game.item_citable). inventaire.retirer objet (text), quantite (number), fiche (number?) Ask the inventory to remove items, such as a payment. Answered by inventaire.change, or inventaire.manque if there are not enough. For a kind with unique copies (version 15): fiche removes that copy, otherwise the first ones; their records are destroyed. fabrication.ouvrir etabli (text?), cible (text?), onglet (text?), joueur (id?) Ask the crafting system to open its window, with the recipes of the station object cible, or of the kind of station named etabli (empty or missing: bare-handed): a Trigger rule, a button of a drawn screen. onglet opens it on another module's tab (equipement.atelier: the workshop). It opens for joueur only; without joueur, for the host only (never for every player). boutique.ouvrir cible (id), onglet (text?), joueur (id?) Ask the shop system to open the shop of cible, as if the player had used it: from a dialogue answer, a trigger, a script. onglet opens it on another module's tab (equipement.atelier: the services). It opens for joueur only; without joueur, for the host only (never for every player).

items.title: What it listens to
items.text: Event Fields Description equipement.porter objet (text?), fiche (number?), emplacement (text?), joueur (id?) Ask the Equipment module to make the player wear an item of their bag: objet its kind, fiche a unique copy (it must be in this player's bag), emplacement a slot key or name (missing: the first free slot accepting it). equipement.retirer emplacement (text), joueur (id?) Ask the Equipment module to take off what is worn at a slot (its key, such as tete, or its name): it goes back to the bag. inventaire.choisi objet (text), total (number), fiche (number?), double (boolean?), case (text?) The player clicked a slot of the inventory window: objet is the kind of item, total how many they carry. What it does belongs to the game: eat, equip, read. case (version 21) is the slot's key ("Wood~2" for a second stack). inventaire.glisse objet (text), fiche (number?), cible (text), joueur (id?), case (text?) The player dragged a slot of the inventory window (mouse button pressed on it, released elsewhere, version 16): cible is the key of the HUD element under the cursor. The Equipment module wears an item dragged onto a slot. case (version 21): the dragged slot's key. inventaire.fenetre ouverte (boolean), joueur (id?) The inventory window opened or closed (version 16): ouverte. The Equipment window opens beside it. objet.change numero (number), sorte (text), champs (table) Sent by the engine when the host changed the record of a unique item (game.item_set): champs lists the fields given. langue.change langue (text) Sent by the engine when the player changes the game's language (game.set_language, the Menu options). A module redraws what it already shows: its texts go through game.t and game.language. equipement.reparer fiche (number?), par (text?), cible (id?), joueur (id?) Ask the Equipment module to repair a unique copy (ADR-039 section 6): par is station (at the station named by station_reparation, cible that station), boutique (cible a merchant, with boutique_reparation), or kit (one repair kit taken from the bag; without fiche, the most worn of what is worn or held). On the host, the record must be the player's (game.item_citable). equipement.ameliorer fiche (number), par (text?), cible (id?), joueur (id?) Ask the Equipment module to upgrade a unique copy by one level (ADR-039 section 7): par station or boutique, cible the station or merchant. The chance is rolled on the host. equipement.sertir fiche (number), gemme (text?), gemme_fiche (number?), par (text?), cible (id?), joueur (id?) Ask the Equipment module to set a gem into a unique copy: gemme its kind (a stack of the bag) or gemme_fiche (a unique gem); par station or boutique, cible the station or merchant. equipement.desertir fiche (number), index (number?), par (text?), cible (id?), joueur (id?) Ask the Equipment module to remove gem number index (missing: the last) from a unique copy, after the setting retrait_gemme: impossible, the gem destroyed, or returned for a cost. equipement.atelier cible (id), joueur (id?) Open the Equipment workshop (repair, upgrade, set gems) at this station or merchant: the station's Crafting window, or the merchant's Shop window, opened on its workshop tab, for joueur only (without joueur, for the host only). equipement.porte joueur (id), emplacement (text), objet (text), fiche (number?) The player now wears an item: emplacement is the slot key, objet its kind, fiche its record (a unique copy). Its bonuses have the source equipement:<emplacement>. equipement.retire joueur (id), emplacement (text), objet (text), fiche (number?) The player took off an item: it is back in the bag, and its bonuses are gone. objet.cree numero (number), sorte (text) Sent by the engine (ADR-039) when the host created the record of a unique item (game.item_create): numero is its number, sorte its kind. inventaire.en_main objet (text), avant (text), place (number), chargement (boolean?), joueur (id?), fiche (number?), source (text?) What the player holds in hand changed (version 24): the slot chosen in the inventory's bar (keys 1 to 9, wheel), an item used up, a load (chargement true). objet is the kind held, "" for empty hands; avant the one held before; place the bar slot (0: nothing). Gathering checks the tool held; a game script equips a sword with it. inventaire.manque objet (text), quantite (number), fiche (number?) Items could not be removed: there are not enough. inventaire.change objet (text), quantite (number), total (number), chargement (boolean?), fiche (number?), jete (boolean?) The quantity of an item changed. total is the new quantity. chargement is true when a saved game gives the items back (game.load): nothing was picked up. For a unique copy (version 15), objet is its kind, fiche its record's number, total how many of that kind. With several stacks of a kind (version 21), total counts all of them; jete is true when a slot was dropped on the ground. combat.attaque source (id) Someone struck, whether it hit or not: the stamina module counts it. combat.coup cible (id), source (id), montant (number) An attack hit something. The health module, if present, has been asked to remove the damage. tir.tir source (id), arme (text), origine (vector), direction (vector) The player fired a ranged weapon (version 25), whether it hits or not: origine is the muzzle, direction the aim before spread. For a sound, a noise that alerts enemies, a counter. tir.touche cible (id), source (id), arme (text), montant (number), partie (text?), point (vector), tete (boolean) A shot of the player hit something carrying Health (version 25); the health module has been asked to remove montant (before armor). partie is tete, torse, bras or jambes (missing for an object or an explosion); tete is true for a head shot. All the pellets of one shotgun shot on the same target make one tir.touche. collecte.recolte cible (id), ressource (text), quantite (number), joueur (id?), xp (number?), piste (text?) A resource was used up and gave what it holds. The inventory, if present, has been asked to add it. fenetres.fermer joueur (id?), raison (text?) Close every window a player has open (loot, inventory, equipment, workshop...), sent by the Death module when they die; any script may send it (a cutscene). joueur: that player (missing: everyone). Each module with a window closes its own. fabrication.onglet joueur (id), onglet (text), cible (id?), etabli (text?), parent (text?), largeur (number?) The crafting window opened another module's tab at a station (onglet, its key; parent, the empty panel to fill; largeur, the window's width), or left it (onglet empty). The module whose tab it is fills the panel. boutique.onglet joueur (id), onglet (text), cible (id?), parent (text?), largeur (number?) The shop window opened another module's tab (onglet, its key; parent, the empty panel to fill; largeur, the window's width), or left it (onglet empty). The module whose tab it is fills the panel.

items.title: Points a script can replace (game.override)
items.text:
The descriptions come from the code.

  • equipement.corps: function(default, joueur) -> the object that shows what the player wears, and its kind of body (a text matched against the rows of visible_corps). The default is the player's character and its profile field champ_corps. For a game whose other body is another object following the player. The Inventory's item in hand follows it too (its hook inventaire.porteur).
  • equipement.avant: function(default, infos) -> true, or false and the reason shown: whether the player may wear this item. infos is {joueur, emplacement, objet, fiche, second}. The default is true. For "no heavy armour for a mage".

items.title: What the agent knows about this system
items.text: The text the agent reads before using this system.

items.title: Equipment (equipement)
items.text:
The player wears items in slots (head, chest, weapon, two rings...): their bonuses add to the player's values, and they can show on the character. It requires the Inventory: the items worn come from the bag and go back to it. Prefer it to your own script; adapt it through its settings, its events and game.override, never by editing it.

  • Slots: the list emplacements (a row per slot: nom, icone, categories (the Inventory's categories it accepts, separated by commas), nombre (2 for two rings), visible, partie (the body part where what shows is attached: its bone is found by measuring the character's skeleton, game.body_bone), arme (holds the weapon in hand)). Empty: the preset prereglage (jeu_de_role: head, chest, hands, legs, feet, weapon, off hand, two rings, amulet, back; survie: head, chest, legs, feet, bag, tool; tir: helmet, vest, main weapon, secondary weapon). A slot's key in scripts is its name in lowercase without accents (« Main secondaire » -> main_secondaire, two rings -> anneau_1, anneau_2).
  • Wearable kinds: give the kind a categorie in the Inventory's sortes_objets (« casque »): it then goes to a slot accepting it. A row in sortes_equipables adds: emplacement (a precise slot), deux_emplacements with autre_emplacement (a two-handed weapon takes « Arme » and « Main secondaire »), conditions (niveau_requis on piste, carac_requise with carac_min; the Progression's required levels apply too), effet (with the Temporary effects module: set while worn, source equipement), and what shows (below). Fixed bonuses: bonus_sortes (a row per kind and value: valeur, add, pct in %), added to the record's bonuses of a unique copy.
  • Wearing: a double click on an inventory slot (A twice on a gamepad), or dragging it onto a slot of the equipment window (control equipment, O; it also opens beside the inventory, avec_inventaire; with the Inventory's disposition_fenetre trois_parties, the slots are drawn in the inventory's left column instead, through shared.equipement.places() and shared.equipement.placesPour(kind), version 6). A click on a worn slot takes it off. Scripts: game.emit("equipement.porter", {objet = "Casque", fiche = 12, emplacement = "tete", joueur = id}) (fiche for a unique copy, emplacement optional) and game.emit("equipement.retirer", {emplacement = "tete", joueur = id}). Read what is worn: shared.equipement.porte(player); what shows for a kind on the player's body: shared.equipement.apparence(kind) -> {[slot key] = {objet, fiche, nom, double?}} (double: the second slot of a two-slot item, naming the main one).
  • What happens: the item leaves the bag (inventaire.sortir); a unique copy's record gets the holder equipement:<player entity>, and inventaire:<player entity> again when taken off. Bonuses go through game.stat_bonus, source equipement:<slot key>, and are removed exactly. Events equipement.porte and equipement.retire {joueur, emplacement, objet, fiche}; equipement.refus {joueur, raison}. The hook equipement.avant refuses: game.override("equipement.avant", function(default, infos) if infos.objet == "Armure lourde" then return false, "Pas pour un mage" end return default(infos) end) (infos: joueur, emplacement, objet, fiche, second).
  • Effective bonuses: one function, shared.equipement.bonusEffectifs(record, kind) -> {{valeur, add, pct}}: the record's bonuses plus the kind's, raised by its upgrade level, plus its gems; a broken record (usure_max > 0 and usure == 0) gives nothing. When a worn record changes (objet.change), its bonuses are computed again.
  • What shows (visible on the kind's row): modele (a copy of an object attached to a bone: best, set the model on the character in the editor — the helmet on the head —, check it with a capture, hide it, and choose it in modele: its exact place is reused; os (a bone chosen in the character's skeleton; empty: the slot's measured body part), the offsets and echelle_x/y/z (sizes fitted to the measured head or body) override it), pieces (objects of the character shown or hidden while worn: pieces_montrer, pieces_cacher, names separated by commas, chosen in the model), les_deux, or rien. By body: a row in visible_corps (objet, corps, then another model, bone, offset, size or pieces) is used when the player's profile field champ_corps (« corps ») has that value. Never assume a bone, a model, a clip or a size, and never write a pack's bone name: use the slot's body part (measured), or a bone chosen in the character's skeleton, and measure the head before setting sizes. The equipment's models are the creator's, kind by kind: there is no default model.
  • The weapon in hand (arme_en_main): barre (the Inventory's hotbar, as before), emplacement (the weapon worn in the slot that holds the weapon is handed to the Inventory, inventaire.tenir_porte: held, shown and announced exactly like the bar's, with its row of en_main, whose prise can be the measured weapon hold), or lies (both: the weapon worn comes back in hand when the bar holds nothing). Equipment never attaches the weapon in hand itself. With the hook equipement.corps (another body following the player), the Inventory holds the weapon in that body's hand too (its hook inventaire.porteur, whose default follows equipement.corps).
  • The window: one line per slot (its name, then what is worn; a slot in use takes the theme's selected state) and the totals of the values worn and of the list valeurs; control equipment (O, Y on a gamepad); styles fenetre.equipement, titre.equipement, case.equipement (case.rare for a rare item worn), texte.equipement, bouton.fermer. The tooltip of an inventory item compares it with what is worn at the same place (comparer): green what goes up, red what goes down. One piece of information per bonus: an upgraded or set item shows its effective total (« +9 Dégâts », green) instead of the record's raw bonus; a broken item shows its raw bonuses greyed, followed by « (sans effet) ». Tier and comparison colors are made readable on the theme's image by the engine (hudReadableTint).
  • Durability (ADR-039 § 6), only when the user asks for wear: give the kind's row in sortes_equipables a usure_max (0: never wears; a new copy's record gets it), usee_par (attaque: each hit, combat.attaque, or shot, tir.tir, while held; coup_recu: each hit taken while worn, combat.coup or tir.touche on the player; recolte: each harvest while held, collecte.recolte) and perte (lost each time). At zero, a_zero: casse (kept, greyed, « Cassé » in the tooltip, no bonuses until repaired: bonusEffectifs gives nothing) or detruit (taken off and destroyed). Below seuil_usure % (20), a message and the slot turns red (equipement.usure_alerte). Events equipement.casse, equipement.detruit.
  • Repair, each path optional: at a station whose name is station_reparation (Crafting's station kind, « Établi »: its Crafting window gets a workshop tab, « Atelier », costs in couts_station rows with action reparer), at a merchant if boutique_reparation (the Shop window gets a « Services » tab) (price prix_reparation for an item at zero, in proportion to what is lost; money monnaie, else the merchant's), or a kit (kit_reparation, an Inventory kind: a double click on it repairs the most worn item worn or held; kit_montant 0: all). baisse_reparation lowers the maximum at each repair. Script: game.emit("equipement.reparer", {fiche = n, par = "station"|"boutique"|"kit", cible = station or merchant}); announces equipement.repare.
  • Sets (§ 7): ensembles (nom, pieces: kinds separated by commas) and ensembles_paliers (ensemble, nombre of pieces worn, valeur, add, pct in %): set and removed by themselves, source ensemble:<name key>; a broken piece does not count. The tooltip shows « Loup (2/4) » and each tier, green with « (actif) » when reached, grey with « (encore 2) » (the pieces still missing) otherwise: a written mark, not only a color (texts palier_atteint, palier_manque).
  • Upgrade (§ 7): the kind's row niveau_max (0: none) and amelioration_pct (each level adds that % of the item's bonuses), plus fixed bonuses per level in amelioration_bonus. Where: station_amelioration (« Forge »; costs couts_station with action ameliorer, niveau the level aimed for or 0) or merchants (boutique_amelioration, price per level in amelioration_niveaux). amelioration_niveaux (niveau, chance %, prix): 100 % without a row; the roll is made on the host. On failure, echec_amelioration: rien, niveau_perdu or casse. The name shows « Épée de fer +2 ». Script: equipement.ameliorer {fiche, par, cible}; announces equipement.ameliore {reussi, niveau, echec}.
  • Gems (§ 7): a kind whose Inventory categorie is categorie_gemme (« gemme »); its bonuses in gemmes_bonus (gemme, categorie of the item receiving it, empty for any other, valeur, add, pct). Sockets: the kind's row emplacements_gemmes, or rolled by Loot. Set at station_sertissage or merchants (boutique_sertissage, prix_sertissage); retrait_gemme: impossible, detruite, or rendue (for prix_retrait, or couts_station retirer_gemme). Scripts: equipement.sertir {fiche, gemme or gemme_fiche, par, cible}, equipement.desertir {fiche, index, par, cible}; announce equipement.serti, equipement.desserti.
  • The workshop: one window at a station or a merchant, never two. At a station named in station_reparation, station_amelioration or station_sertissage, the Crafting window has two tabs, « Fabrication » (its recipes) and « Atelier »; at a merchant with a service ticked, the Shop window has « Marchandise » and « Services » (hooks fabrication.onglets, boutique.onglets). The workshop tab lists the player's unique items with Repair, Upgrade, Set and Remove buttons and their cost. A station without recipes, fuel or level to gain, or a merchant selling nothing, opens on the workshop tab at once. equipement.atelier {cible, joueur} opens the station's or merchant's window on that tab from a script, for that player only (without joueur: the host). atelier_x is no longer used (version 5). Refusals go through equipement.refus with the reason shown. All this changes only the record (usure, usure_max, amelioration, gemmes): the bonuses follow through bonusEffectifs and objet.change, and the save keeps them with the records.
  • The screens (version 8), delivered by the system and filled by its scripts: never draw an equipment window with game.hud_*, and never edit the system; change their look, places and sizes with screens_set (styles, not hand-made values). « Équipement » (modules/equipement/ecrans/fenetre.json): Fenêtre, Titre, the list Emplacements (row Ligne: Image of the item worn, hidden without one; Case, a button with the action retirer), Caractéristiques, the list Valeurs (row Valeur, hidden when empty), Fermer (action fermer, B or Escape). Keys of a row: Équipement/Case#N, N in the order of the slots (Équipement/Case#1: the first, « Tête » in jeu_de_role); dragging an inventory slot onto it wears the item there. The script sets each Case to the width of its row (minus the image), read on screen. fenetre_x left at 0.115: the window stays where its shape Fenêtre is (move it in the screen); another value puts it there, as before. « Atelier de l'équipement » (ecrans/atelier.json): shown inside the host window's tab shape (Fabrication/Onglet ouvert, Boutique/Onglet ouvert) with game.screen_show(name, {inside = key}): Atelier, Rien, the list Objets (row Ligne: Objet, Action 1 to Action 6, buttons with the action service; an item with more services goes on to the next row; up to two services each button keeps its width in the screen, more share the width of two). « Message de l'équipement » (ecrans/message.json): its Message, at the top, red for a refusal, gone after a few seconds. With several players, each player has their own screens.
  • Displayed names of values: the list valeurs (valeur, libelle, translated) names values everywhere (game.stat_name, which also works in a guest's game: the names go with the progression); the Progression names its own.
  • Several players: one copy per player, on the host. A guest's request (to wear, repair, upgrade, set a gem) only cites their own records (game.item_citable), and the upgrade roll is made on the host; what shows is an attached copy that guests receive. What is worn is saved per player and per world.

This page is generated automatically from the WorldMint code (modules/equipement/module.json, modules/equipement/AGENT.md, modules/events.json): it always matches the editor.

items.title: Crafting
items.text:
Recipes that turn what the player carries into something else: three wood and two stones make an axe. One crafts bare-handed (C) or at a station: an object of the world, an imported model included, given a function the game defines (Workbench, Campfire, Oven, Forge...), with its levels to upgrade, its fuel and its queue.

Identifier fabrication Version 12 Placed on objects yes Also activates Inventory, Interaction Also needs, on the same object Interaction

items.title: The fields of each “Row”
items.text:
In the Properties, each “Row” has its own numbered frame; Add: Row adds one, the cross removes it. A field only appears when it is useful: under its name, the table says when.

Setting What it does Name in code Type Default Limits or choices Kind of row A recipe, with what it gives and where; or an ingredient, which belongs to the recipe above it. sorte Choice in a list Recipe recette: Recipeingredient: Ingredient What it gives (kind of inventory item)shown only if Kind of row is “Recipe” The kind of item crafted, as the inventory stores it, such as "Axe" or "Torch". It also names the recipe in events. objet Text (empty) Category (empty: Other)shown only if Kind of row is “Recipe” The group where the detailed window puts this recipe, such as "Tools", "Weapons" or "Food". Empty: "Other", last. categorie Text (empty) How many it givesshown only if Kind of row is “Recipe” How many one crafting gives: 4 for four planks from one log. quantite Number 1 from 1 to 100 000, as a whole number Stations where it is made (empty: bare-handed, anywhere)shown only if Kind of row is “Recipe” The name of a kind of station, such as "Campfire", or several separated by commas: "Campfire, Oven". Empty: anywhere, from the crafting window (C). etabli Text (empty) Minimum station levelshown only if Kind of row is “Recipe” The level the station must have reached: 2 for a recipe asking for a workbench upgraded once. niveau_min Number 1 from 1 to 100, as a whole number Crafting time (s)shown only if Kind of row is “Recipe” 0: at once. Otherwise the recipe joins the queue and the item arrives at the end (at a station that takes the time, or bare-handed). temps Number 0 from 0 to 86 400 XP given (Progression system)shown only if Kind of row is “Recipe” The XP gained by whoever crafts it, if the game has the Progression system. Their crafting speed (a Progression value) divides the time. 0: none. xp Number 0 from 0 to 1 000 000 Track that gets the XP (empty: the main one)shown only if Kind of row is “Recipe” The identifier of a track of the Progression system, such as "cooking" or "smithing". piste_xp Text (empty) Knowledge needed (empty: none)shown only if Kind of row is “Recipe” The name of a knowledge the player must have learnt, such as "Metalwork". This system does not check it itself: a knowledge system, or a game script, reads it and reserves the recipe. connaissance Text (empty) Ingredient (kind of inventory item)shown only if Kind of row is “Ingredient” A kind of item the recipe uses up, as the inventory stores it, such as "Wood". ingredient Text (empty) How manyshown only if Kind of row is “Ingredient” How many of this ingredient the recipe uses up: 3 wood. nombre Number 1 from 1 to 100 000, as a whole number Needed but not used up (a tool)shown only if Kind of row is “Ingredient” Ticked: the player must have it to craft, but keeps it, like a hammer or a knife. Unticked: it is used up. garde Yes or no no

items.text:
In the Properties, each “Row” has its own numbered frame; Add: Row adds one, the cross removes it. A field only appears when it is useful: under its name, the table says when.

Setting What it does Name in code Type Default Limits or choices Kind of row A kind of station (its name, how it is used, its fuel); a level of the station above; or what the level above costs, one row per ingredient. sorte Choice in a list Kind of station station: Kind of stationniveau: Levelcout: Cost of the level Name of the stationshown only if Kind of row is “Kind of station” Such as "Workbench", "Campfire", "Oven" or "Forge". Recipes ask for it by this name, and an object of the world becomes one through its "Function". nom Text (empty) How it is usedshown only if Kind of row is “Kind of station” By using it: one must stand in front of it and press E (or C right next to it). Within a radius: its recipes are allowed anywhere around it, in the window (C), like Valheim's workbench. usage Choice in a list By using it (E), right next to it interaction: By using it (E), right next to itrayon: Within a radius around it Radius (m)shown only if Kind of row is “Kind of station” ; shown only if How it is used is “Within a radius around it” How far around it its recipes are allowed. rayon Number 6 from 1 to 100 Recipes take their time there (queue)shown only if Kind of row is “Kind of station” Ticked: a recipe with a time joins a queue, shown in the window, and the item reaches the inventory at the end. Unticked: everything is crafted there at once. file Yes or no yes Fuel (empty: none)shown only if Kind of row is “Kind of station” The kind of item it burns, such as "Wood" or "Coal". items.title: Settings on each object
items.text:
In the Properties of an object or folder that carries the system, Systems section. A folder passes its values on to what it contains; an object can change a value for itself only.

Setting What it does Name in code Type Default Limits or choices Function of this object The kind of station this object becomes, an imported model included: an Oven, a Workbench, or any kind the game defines in the stations. "From its name": its name without number, a "Campfire 3" is a Campfire. nom_etabli Choice in a list (empty) a name from this system's list stations, or empty Starting level The level of this station at the start of the game. The player then upgrades it from its window (Upgrade), and the saved game keeps its level. niveau Number 1 from 1 to 100, as a whole number Fuel at the start (units) How many units of fuel this station has at the start: 2 logs for a campfire already lit. 0: out. combustible_depart Number 0 from 0 to 100 000, as a whole number

items.title: Events
items.text: The descriptions come from the code.

items.title: What it announces
items.text: Event Fields Description fabrication.fabrique objet (text), quantite (number), etabli (text), cible (text?), xp (number?), piste (text?) The player crafted a recipe: its ingredients left the inventory and objet (quantite of it) came in, at once or at the end of its time in the queue. etabli is the kind of station where it was made (empty bare-handed), cible the station object (missing bare-handed). fabrication.manque objet (text), manque (text?), etabli (text?), niveau (number?), combustible (text?) A recipe could not be crafted: manque lists what is missing, in the player's language ("2 Wood, 1 Stone"), or etabli names the stations it needs (with niveau, the minimum level, when the station is too low), or combustible the fuel a station out of fire needs. fabrication.commencee objet (text), quantite (number), temps (number), etabli (text), cible (text?) A recipe with a time joined the player's queue: its ingredients left the inventory; objet (quantite of it) comes in after temps seconds. etabli is the kind of station, cible the station object (missing bare-handed). fabrication.finie objet (text), quantite (number), etabli (text), cible (text?) A recipe of the queue is done: objet (quantite of it) came into the inventory. fabrication.fabrique is announced too. fabrication.station_amelioree cible (text), etabli (text), niveau (number), nom (text), ancienne (text?) A station (cible, of the kind etabli) was upgraded to the level niveau, named nom (empty if the level has no name); its cost left the inventory. With a model for that level, cible is the new copy, and ancienne the object it replaced. fabrication.allumee cible (text), etabli (text) A station that burns fuel (cible, of the kind etabli) starts burning. Its particles effect (the particules system) is switched on with it. fabrication.combustible_vide cible (text), etabli (text), combustible (text) A station (cible, of the kind etabli) burnt its last fuel (combustible): it stops crafting until fuel is added, and its particles effect is switched off. fabrication.onglet joueur (id), onglet (text), cible (id?), etabli (text?), parent (text?), largeur (number?) The crafting window opened another module's tab at a station (onglet, its key; parent, the empty panel to fill; largeur, the window's width), or left it (onglet empty). The module whose tab it is fills the panel. inventaire.ajouter objet (text), quantite (number), joueur (id?), fiche (number?) Ask the inventory to add items, such as a reward. Answered by inventaire.change, or inventaire.plein. With several players, joueur says whose bag; without it, the player whose action is being handled, or every player. inventaire.retirer objet (text), quantite (number), fiche (number?) Ask the inventory to remove items, such as a payment. Answered by inventaire.change, or inventaire.manque if there are not enough. For a kind with unique copies (version 15): fiche removes that copy, otherwise the first ones; their records are destroyed.

items.title: What it listens to
items.text: Event Fields Description fabrication.ouvrir etabli (text?), cible (text?), onglet (text?), joueur (id?) Ask the crafting system to open its window, with the recipes of the station object cible, or of the kind of station named etabli (empty or missing: bare-handed): a Trigger rule, a button of a drawn screen. onglet opens it on another module's tab (equipement.atelier: the workshop). It opens for joueur only; without joueur, for the host only (never for every player). fabrication.fabriquer objet (text), etabli (text?), cible (text?) Ask the crafting system to craft the recipe that gives objet, as its button would, at the station object cible, or at the kind of station named etabli (the nearest one of that kind within reach, else as if at a level 1 station), empty or missing: bare-handed. Refused, with fabrication.manque, if something is missing. A recipe with a time joins the queue. fabrication.ameliorer cible (text) Ask the crafting system to upgrade the station cible to its next level, as its Upgrade button would: the player pays the cost. Refused, with a message in the window, if something is missing. fabrication.alimenter cible (text), quantite (number?) Ask the crafting system to put quantite (1 if missing) of the fuel of the station cible into it, taken from the player's inventory, as its fuel button would. interaction.utiliser cible (id), joueur (id) The player used the object in reach: a door, a merchant, an item to pick up. Whoever owns that object decides what it does. inventaire.change objet (text), quantite (number), total (number), chargement (boolean?), fiche (number?), jete (boolean?) The quantity of an item changed. total is the new quantity. chargement is true when a saved game gives the items back (game.load): nothing was picked up. For a unique copy (version 15), objet is its kind, fiche its record's number, total how many of that kind. With several stacks of a kind (version 21), total counts all of them; jete is true when a slot was dropped on the ground. inventaire.plein objet (text), fiche (number?), reste (number?) An item could not be added: every slot holds another kind of item (or another unique copy), or (version 21) every stack of its kind is full. reste: picked up in part, how many stayed on the ground. inventaire.manque objet (text), quantite (number), fiche (number?) Items could not be removed: there are not enough.

items.title: Points a script can replace (game.override)
items.text:
The descriptions come from the code.

  • fabrication.onglets: function(default, infos) -> a list of {cle, libelle}: the tabs other modules add to this station's window (infos: cible, the station; etabli, its kind; joueur). The default is an empty list: the window shows its recipes alone. With a tab, the window shows a row of tabs (the recipes first, labelled by the text onglet); the open tab of another module is the shape "Fabrication/Onglet ouvert" of the screen "Fabrication", which the module fills when fabrication.onglet announces it (its parent field). A station without recipes, fuel or level to gain opens on the first other tab. Equipment adds « Atelier » (repair, upgrade, set gems) at the stations its settings name. Call default(infos) and add yours to its list.
  • fabrication.permise: function(default, recette, infos) -> true, or false and the reason shown (text): whether this recipe can be crafted now. recette is its title (the product's original name). infos (version 3) is a table: objet, quantite, etabli (the stations it asks for, as written), niveau (the minimum station level), temps (seconds), connaissance (the knowledge it asks for, as written; empty: none). The default is true. To unlock a recipe with a quest, a book read, a level, a knowledge learnt (the connaissance field). Call default(recette, infos) for the other cases.
  • fabrication.texte: function(default, key) -> the text the crafting window shows for that key: titre, titre_etabli, aucune, fabriquer, fabriquer_n, tout, autres, categorie, recherche, temps, ingredient, garde, plus, moins, tout_max, choisir, introuvable, fermer, fabrique, manque, place, il_faut, il_faut_niveau, refus, niveau, feu, eteint, alimenter, ameliorer, ameliore, max, en_cours, attente_feu, trop_loin, annuler, commence, sans_combustible, disparue, onglet (the label of the recipes tab, shown when another module adds a tab). It may hold {objet}, {n}, {etabli}, {liste}, {secondes}, {combustible}, {nom}, {part}, {a} (how many the player has) and {raison}, replaced afterwards (in the player's language). The default is the game's translation of the text in the original language (translations_get lists them as built-in texts of the crafting window); without one, French or English, after the player's language.

items.title: What the agent knows about this system
items.text: The text the agent reads before using this system.

items.title: Crafting (fabrication)
items.text:
Recipes that turn items of the inventory into another item: three wood and two stones make an axe; raw meat cooked at a campfire. Add it once with modules_add (with inventaire and interaction). Use it whenever the user talks about crafting, making, cooking, smelting, forging, a workbench, an oven, a forge or a kitchen: never write a crafting script. Version 3 (ADR-035): stations defined by the game, with levels, fuel and a queue. Version 4: a station's window shows only its own recipes. Version 8: a detailed window (disposition_fenetre), with categories, slots and a details panel.

It has two game settings (modules_set), each a list of rows, in order, and two values per object.

items.title: The kinds of stations (stations)
items.text:
A station row starts a kind of station; the niveau rows under it are its levels, in order; the cout rows under a level are what upgrading to that level costs. Nothing is hard-coded: the default rows (Établi with 3 levels, Feu de camp burning wood, Four, Forge) are examples the user changes or deletes. Any game logic fits: Valheim (workbench radius, levels), Rust (furnace with fuel), Enshrouded, ARK...

The default survival progression (the rows of a new game, matching the default knowledges of savoir): bare-handed, a stone axe (« Hache »: 3 Bois, 2 Pierre); at the Établi level 1, « Pioche » and « Lance »; at level 2 (10 Bois, 4 Pierre), « Arc », « Hache de fer » and « Pioche de fer » (2 Bois, 3 Fer); level 3 costs 20 Bois and 5 Fer. The Feu de camp (burns Bois, 30 s a log) cooks « Viande cuite », « Poisson grillé », « Baies grillées »; the Four (burns Bois only while cooking) also does « Pain » and « Ragoût »; the Forge smelts « Fer » from 2 « Minerai de fer ». A campfire is a cooking station, not a workbench: never put tools on it. Rename everything in the user's words, and drop what their game does not have.

  • station: nom (the name recipes ask for, in the user's language: « Établi », « Forge », « Table d'alchimie »), usage (interaction: the player stands at it and presses E, or C right next to it; rayon: its recipes are allowed anywhere within rayon metres, in the window C), file (on: a recipe with a time joins a queue; off: everything is instant there), combustible (the item it burns, an inventory kind; empty: no fuel), duree_combustible (seconds of fire per unit), allumage (toujours: burns while fuel remains, a campfire; fabrication: burns only while crafting, an oven).
  • niveau: nom_niveau (« Établi simple »), modele (optional: a hidden object of the scene carrying fabrication, used as a mould: at this level a copy replaces the station, same place and turn, keeping its level and fire). The first level is the starting one; its cost is not used. A station without niveau rows has one level.
  • cout: objet, nombre: the price of the level above.
  • Example, a forge that burns coal and has two levels: {"sorte": "station", "nom": "Forge", "usage": "interaction", "combustible": "Charbon", "duree_combustible": 90, "allumage": "fabrication"}, {"sorte": "niveau", "nom_niveau": "Forge en pierre"}, {"sorte": "niveau", "nom_niveau": "Forge en fer"}, {"sorte": "cout", "objet": "Fer", "nombre": 10}.

items.title: The recipes (recettes)
items.text:
A recette row starts a recipe; the ingredient rows under it are what it needs.

  • recette: objet (the item it gives, an inventory kind, in the user's language; it also names the recipe), categorie (version 8: its group in the detailed window, « Outils », « Nourriture »; empty: « Autres »), quantite, etabli (the kinds of stations where it is made, by their nom, several separated by commas: « Feu de camp, Four »; empty: bare-handed, anywhere), niveau_min (minimum station level), temps (seconds; 0: at once), connaissance (a knowledge name the player must have learnt; this module does not check it: a knowledge system or a game script does, through fabrication.permise; empty: none).
  • ingredient: ingredient (an inventory kind), nombre, garde (on: the player must have it but keeps it, a tool such as a hammer).
  • Cooking is only stations: a campfire, an oven, a kitchen are kinds of stations; any food is a recipe: {"sorte": "recette", "objet": "Poisson grillé", "etabli": "Feu de camp, Four", "temps": 5}, {"sorte": "ingredient", "ingredient": "Poisson cru", "nombre": 1}. Bread and stew at the oven only.
  • A recipe at a level too low shows in grey with « Il faut : Établi niveau 2 »; a recipe of another station does not show.

items.title: Giving an object a station function (values per object)
items.text:
Attach the system to the object (systems_attach; interaction comes with it) and set nom_etabli, shown as « Fonction de cet objet »: one of the station names (a list in the inspector). Any object works, an imported model included: an imported oven model with nom_etabli « Four » is an oven. Empty: its name without trailing number (a « Feu de camp 3 » is a Feu de camp). niveau: its starting level. combustible_depart: units of fuel at the start (0: out).

  • A station with fuel crafts only while it has fire; the window shows « Feu : 45 s (Bois) » or « Éteint » and a button « Ajouter : Bois » that takes one unit from the inventory. The queue stops when the fire dies and resumes when fed. If the object carries particules (flames, smoke), its effect is switched on and off with the fire.
  • Upgrade: the window of a station with a next level has « Améliorer (10 Bois, 4 Pierre) »; it takes the cost, raises the level (kept per object, in the save, the same for all players).
  • A piece the player builds with construction keeps its model's systems: an oven model carrying fabrication becomes an oven wherever it is built.
  • A kind of station used by an object but missing from stations behaves like version 2: one level, no fuel, used with E.

items.title: The window and the queue
items.text:
• The control craft (C, or the left stick pressed) opens the window with the bare-handed recipes, plus those of the nearest station in reach (its radius, or the hand's reach); using a station (E) opens it with only that station's recipes (version 4: the campfire does not show the axe; the bare-handed ones stay in the window C), unless mains_nues_station is ticked (off by default; a game made before version 4 keeps it on, as it was). Close with C again or Close (B / Escape). montrer_impossibles shows what cannot be made yet, in grey. pause_fenetre (off by default) stops the world while it is open, and the queue with it.
  • A recipe with a time takes its ingredients at once and joins the player's queue, shown in the window with its progress and a Cancel button (the ingredients come back); window closed, the current one shows at the right of the screen. The item reaches the inventory at the end; if it does not fit, it waits for room. rester_pres on: the queue waits while the player is away from the station.
  • Two looks (version 8, disposition_fenetre): liste (default, and kept by older games): one row per recipe with its Craft button. detaillee: the wider window of survival games (Rust, Valheim, Enshrouded): at the top the station, its level, its fire (Add) and Upgrade, and a Search field; on the left the categories (« Tout » first, each with how many of its recipes can be made now; a recipe without categorie goes in « Autres », last; one category only: no column); in the middle the items as slots (the icon of the item kind of the inventory if it has one, else its name; impossible ones in grey); on the right the chosen recipe: its name, the item's description, the ingredients as « 2 / 3 Bois » (missing ones in the alert colour), the time, « Il faut : Établi niveau 2 », a quantity (− 1 +, Max: as many as the ingredients allow) and Craft (greyed when impossible); the queue at the bottom. Choose detaillee when the game has many recipes (more than about eight), for survival and role-playing games; give each recipe a categorie in the user's words (« Outils », « Armes », « Nourriture »). Keep liste for a handful of recipes. It is the screen « Fabrication détaillée » (see below); its keys: Fabrication détaillée/Recherche (the field), Fabrication détaillée/Catégorie#N (1: Tout), Fabrication détaillée/Case#N (Case rare#N for a rare item kind), Fabrication détaillée/Nom, Ingrédients, Il faut, Nombre, Moins / Plus / Max, Fabriquer. The Atelier tab of Equipment keeps its place in both looks (it opens in the screen « Fabrication »).
  • Spell every item exactly as the inventory stores it: the same kind as what collecte gives (ressource) and what the player picks up.

items.title: Events and hooks
items.text:
• Announced: fabrication.fabrique (objet, quantite, etabli, cible?; at once or at the end of the queue), fabrication.manque (objet, manque or etabli with niveau or combustible), fabrication.commencee (objet, quantite, temps, etabli, cible?), fabrication.finie, fabrication.station_amelioree (cible, etabli, niveau, nom, ancienne?), fabrication.allumee and fabrication.combustible_vide (cible, etabli).
  • Listened: fabrication.ouvrir (cible? or etabli?), fabrication.fabriquer (objet, cible? or etabli?), fabrication.ameliorer (cible), fabrication.alimenter (cible, quantite?): from a declencheur rule (« envoyer »), a drawn screen's button or a script. A Trigger rule « quand l'événement fabrication.station_amelioree » can play a sound or show a message.
  • Reserve a recipe from your own script, never the module's: game.override("fabrication.permise", function(default, recette, infos) if infos.connaissance == "Métallurgie" and not appris then return false, game.t("Il faut d'abord apprendre la métallurgie.") end return default(recette, infos) end). infos holds objet, quantite, etabli, niveau, temps, connaissance. A refused recipe is not shown.
  • Texts follow the player's language; its own texts are built-in texts listed by translations_get. Change one with game.override("fabrication.texte", ...).
  • Saved games: the player's queue, and each station's level and fire (the host keeps them). An upgraded station replaced by its level's model is kept by the engine (copied objects).
  • Tabs from other modules (hook fabrication.onglets): at a station, another module may add a tab to this window instead of opening its own; the Equipment adds « Atelier » (repair, upgrade, set gems) at the stations its settings name. The window then shows « Fabrication » and « Atelier » under its title (Fabrication/Onglet#1, Fabrication/Onglet#2..., rows of the list Onglets); the other tab is the shape Fabrication/Onglet ouvert, which its module fills when the event fabrication.onglet announces it (its parent field). A station without recipes, fuel or level to gain opens on that tab. fabrication.ouvrir {cible, onglet} opens a precise tab. With several players, fabrication.ouvrir opens for its joueur only; without joueur (a rule, a script of the game), for the host only.
  • The window is made of screens delivered by the system: « Fabrication » (modules/fabrication/ecrans/fenetre.json, the look liste, and another module's tab in both looks): Fenêtre, Titre, the list Onglets (row Onglet), Onglet ouvert, Station, Actions de la station (Alimenter, Améliorer), Vide, the list Recettes (row Recette: Image, Nom, Fabriquer), the list File (row Ligne de la file: En cours, Annuler), Message, Fermer. « Fabrication détaillée » (ecrans/detaillee.json): Voile, Fenêtre, Entête (Titre, Recherche), Onglets, Ligne de la station, Corps with the list Catégories, Cases (Vide, the grid list Grille, row Place: Case, Case rare) and Fiche (Image, Nom, Choisir, Description, Ingrédients, Temps, Il faut, Quantité, Fabriquer), the list File (with the gauge Progression), Message, Fermer. Their buttons send the system's actions (onglet, alimenter, ameliorer, fabriquer, annuler, fermer, and in the detailed one categorie, case, moins, plus, max). The script sets a few sizes from what it shows, as before the screens: the name beside an image, the list Recettes five rows high with more than five recipes, and in the detailed screen the height of Corps (0.36 with a queue, else 0.44), the width of Cases, the columns of Grille and the width of each Place (wider without categories). It reads the sizes the shapes have on screen (Fenêtre, Message, Fiche, Catégories): widen Fenêtre (or narrow Fiche) in the screen and the slots take the room left. Change their look, places and sizes with screens_set (styles, not hand-made values); never draw a crafting window with game.hud_*, and never edit the system. largeur is no longer used (kept for old games): resize the shape Fenêtre.
  • Gamepad and keyboard: the window's buttons get the focus like every window (the detailed one starts on its first slot); B or Escape closes it (Fabrication/Fermer). Keys of a row: Fabrication/Fabriquer#N, Fabrication/Annuler#N, Fabrication/En cours#N (N counts the rows shown). The line of the crafting under way, window closed, is the screen « Fabrication en cours » delivered by the system (modules/fabrication/ecrans/encours.json, its shape Ligne, key Fabrication en cours/Ligne): move it or change its look with screens_set, never by drawing it again.
  • Testing: in game_run, give the ingredients with inventaire.ajouter in a test script, then send fabrication.fabriquer with cible (the station's id), fabrication.alimenter, fabrication.ameliorer, or click Fabrication/Fabriquer#N; read the events and the inventory, and Fabrication/Message, in the report's hud.

items.title: Several players
items.text:
One copy per player: each player has their own window, queue and ingredients (their own inventory). The stations are common: their level and fire are the same for everyone, burnt once per step.

This page is generated automatically from the WorldMint code (modules/fabrication/module.json, modules/fabrication/AGENT.md, modules/events.json): it always matches the editor.

items.title: Points a script can replace (game.override)
items.text:
The descriptions come from the code.

  • interaction.texte: function(default, id) -> the prompt text for this object, after the key. The default is its texte setting, or its name. For a door that says Open or Close.
  • interaction.permise: function(default, cible) -> true, or false: whether the player may use this object now (version 7). Refused, interaction.utiliser is not announced. The default is true. The Progression module uses it for required levels (a door at level 10); say why yourself (a message).

items.title: What the agent knows about this system
items.text: The text the agent reads before using this system.

items.title: Interaction (interaction)
items.text:
Lets the player use the nearest object carrying this system with a key (interact, E by default), and shows a prompt such as "E : Door". It never decides what using does.

  • Make an object usable: place the system on it with systems_attach, or on a group so that all its children are usable. Its prompt shows texte if set (systems_set, such as "Open" or "Talk"), otherwise the object's name: name it in the user's language.
  • React when it is used: game.on("interaction.utiliser", function(e) if e.cible == door then ... end end). Doors, merchants, levers and talks are scripts of the game that listen to this event.
  • interaction.proche tells which object is in reach, or none (cible missing): use it to highlight something.
  • Items to pick up carry the system inventaire, which places this one with it: do not handle them yourself.
  • For the whole game: the reach, the action, and whether the prompt shows. The prompt is the screen « Invite d'interaction » delivered by the system (shape Invite, HUD key Invite d'interaction/Invite), which the user restyles in the screen editor. Never draw a prompt yourself, and do not name another screen « Invite d'interaction ».

items.title: Several players
items.text:
One copy per player: each player has their own prompt, and interaction.utiliser carries joueur, the player who used the object.

This page is generated automatically from the WorldMint code (modules/interaction/module.json, modules/interaction/AGENT.md, modules/events.json): it always matches the editor.

items.title: Interface
items.text:
The look of the game's menus, buttons, lists and text fields: the colors of backgrounds, text and what is selected, the text size, the rounding of corners, and an image theme (an interface pack) laid on each kind of element. Everything the game shows uses them, except what a script chooses itself.

Identifier interface Version 5 Placed on objects no Run by the engine yes: the engine runs it itself, without a script
