items.title: Interface (interface)
items.text:
The look of everything the game shows on screen: panels, buttons, text fields, texts. The system has no script: the engine applies it to the HUD. Add it once with modules_add; it is for the whole game, not placed on objects.

Before any interface work, read the method: guide_get with id interface (see AGENT.md).

  • Its settings (modules_set) are the default look of every HUD element: fond_panneaux (panel background), fond_boutons (button and field background), accent (hovered button, selected field, scroll bar), texte (text color) as #rrggbb colors; taille_texte (text height, a share of the screen height, 0.03 by default); arrondi (corner rounding, a share of the screen height, 0 for square corners); opacite (background opacity, 0 to 1).
  • A value a script gives (color, alpha, size, text_color) wins over the theme. To let the user restyle the whole interface from one place, do not give colors in scripts: use the theme.
  • When the user asks for a style ("dark and gold", "like a parchment", "bigger text"), change these settings instead of every script.
  • Without the system, the HUD keeps its former look (texts slightly bigger than buttons).
  • Build menus with game.hud_panel and parent (see scripts_reference): the engine places the elements, wraps texts, scrolls long lists, and announces hud.clic and hud.valider.
  • Check a menu in game_run: the report's hud gives each element's rect as the engine placed it, hidden for what is outside a scrolled panel's frame, lines for wrapped texts, and role (the theme row that dresses it). Then look at it with capture_steps.

items.title: Dressing the interface with a UI pack: the image theme
items.text:
Rule: to dress the interface with a pack, set the theme (habillage); never lay images over the elements. No script that puts a game.hud_image on every button, bar or window: it breaks when a window moves, and those images fill the HUD sent to each guest until it is cut. The engine lays the theme itself when it draws, on every player's screen (guests included: their game has the same settings; only each element's role travels).

habillage is a list of rows (modules_set interface habillage). Each row dresses one kind of element (sorte), or one role of it (role):

sorte What it dresses Its images panneau panels and windows image (the frame) bouton buttons image (normal), survol (hovered), appui (pressed), grise (disabled), choisi (selected: the open tab), alerte (a refusal, for a moment) champ text fields image (normal), actif (being typed in) barre bars (health, XP, stamina, needs) image (the background), remplissage (the fill: laid over the whole bar then cut to the value, never stretched), cadre (a frame drawn on top) case slots (inventory grid, hotbar) image (normal), survol, appui, grise, choisi (the chosen hotbar slot), alerte (the slot of an item refused as too heavy) infobulle tooltips image titre window titles image (a banner behind the title text) defilement scroll bars image (the track), curseur (the thumb) cadre frames laid on top of what they surround, with no background of their own: the minimap (cadre.minicarte) and the big map (cadre.carte) image (a ring or an ornate border, drawn over the map and its markers, under the player's arrow; without an image, nothing) coche the box of a yes/no button (role coche…, such as coche.option for the yes/no choices of the menu Options screen): a small square left of the label, never stretched over the button; the button's background stays the bouton row's image (unticked), choisi (ticked), grise (disabled)

Each row also has: marge_gauche, marge_haut, marge_droite, marge_bas (the 9-slice margins, in pixels of the image: the corners keep their size, the edges stretch one way, the middle both; 0 everywhere stretches the whole image), echelle (corner size on screen, 1: one image pixel per pixel of a 1080-high screen), teinte (#rrggbb, multiplied), opacite (0 to 1), couleur_element (true: the image also takes the color the game gives the element, for a grey image made to be tinted, such as a fill tinted red for health and blue for XP), texte and texte_inactif (#rrggbb, or empty: automatic): the color of the text laid on the image (button and slot labels, titles, tooltips, the lines of a dressed window) and of greyed text. Left empty, the engine picks dark text on a light image and light text on a dark one, from the image's average brightness; text a script colors keeps its color. With a light pack (parchment, cream buttons), check the captures: set texte if the automatic choice does not suit the pack.

  • A state without its image takes the normal image, shaded by the engine (darker pressed, greyed disabled, outlined in the accent color when hovered or selected, veiled and outlined in the alerte color (#rrggbb setting, red by default) when it signals a refusal). In your scripts, alert = true on a button or panel (game.hud_set(key, {alert = false}) to end it) signals a refusal the same way. A kind without any image keeps the color drawing (the color settings above).
  • Roles. The systems tag their elements: barre.vie (health bar), barre.xp (the progression bar), barre.endurance, barre.besoin (needs), barre.volume (menu), case.inventaire (inventory grid), case.barre_rapide (hotbar slots), panneau.barre_rapide, fenetre.inventaire, fenetre.fabrication, fenetre.savoir, fenetre.quetes, fenetre.boutique, fenetre.dialogue, fenetre.personnage (progression), fenetre.construction (the building catalog), case.construction (its slots), panneau.construction (the placing panel), panneau.touches (the key bar of the building mode and of the title screen), fenetre.menu, fenetre.carte, cadre.minicarte and cadre.carte (the map frames, kind cadre), panneau.suivi_quete, panneau.annonce, panneau.file (crafting queue), titre.inventaire, titre.fabrication, titre.savoir, titre.quetes, titre.boutique, titre.dialogue, titre.personnage, titre.construction, titre.menu, titre.carte, bouton.fermer, bouton.onglet, bouton.choix (dialogue answers); champ.chat is the chat line.
  • Roles by meaning. The systems also tag their buttons by what they do, so a pack's « primary », « danger » or « reward » buttons and its « rare » slots find their place:
  • bouton.principal: the main action of a window: Buy and Sell (boutique), Make and the station's Upgrade (fabrication), Learn or Study (savoir), Spend a point (progression), Take all (butin), Upgrade at the workshop (equipement), and bouton.principal.lancer (Start, manche).
  • bouton.danger: what destroys or gives up: Abandon a quest (quetes), Reset the spent points (progression), Remove a gem when it is destroyed (equipement), and bouton.danger.jeter (Drop, inventaire; it was bouton.jeter).
  • bouton.recompense: collecting a reward. No system has such a button yet: give it to yours (role = "bouton.recompense").
  • case.rare: the slot of an item rare or better: the inventory grid, the hotbar, the equipment slots and the « Take all » window. It wins over the slot's role (a rare hotbar slot is case.rare, not case.barre_rapide). « Rare or better »: the item's rarity is at least the rank of the rarity the game counts as rare (the butin setting protection_rang, « Rare » by default); if no rarity has that name (renamed rarities), the 3rd rarity of the list and the rarer ones. Only unique copies have a rarity.
  • coche.option: a yes/no choice of the menu Options screen (ticked when yes: selected = true). In your scripts, give role = "coche.<something>" and selected = <the value> to a yes/no button: with a coche row, its box is that row's image, drawn left of the label; without one, the engine draws a plain box there (filled with the accent colour and ticked when selected); the button's background stays a button's.
  • A role without its own row takes its parent, then its kind: bouton.danger.jeter takes bouton.danger, then bouton; without any theme row, nothing changes on screen. A case.rare row without a « selected » or « hovered » image shades its own image for those states; give it those images if the pack has them. Buttons whose meaning is not one of these keep bouton or their role (bouton.fermer, bouton.onglet, bouton.choix). A row with a role is a variant: it wins for those elements; what it has no image for comes from its kind's row, with that row's margins. A role without a row takes its kind; barre.vie.boss takes barre.vie first.
  • The first word of a role is the kind: fenetre or panneau, bouton, champ, barre, case (a button or a panel), titre (a text or a panel), infobulle. In your own scripts, give role = "..." to game.hud_* (and selected = true to the open tab or the chosen slot). role = "fond.barre.vie" marks a colored backing (the dark band under a bar) that is not drawn once the theme dresses barre.vie.

  • An element whose script gives its own images (background, fill_image in a drawn screen) keeps them: the theme dresses the rest.

  • The minimap's ring. A row {"sorte": "cadre", "role": "cadre.minicarte", "image": "<the ring>"} lays it over the minimap; the dark outline the map draws by default disappears (its dark disc stays where the map does not reach). Set the carte setting cadre_marge (a share of the map's size, 0.06 to 0.12 for a thick ring) so the map stays inside the ring. A row panneau never dresses a frame; the former role panneau.minicarte no longer exists (it was drawn under the map).

  • Images go into the project. An image chosen from the library (by modules_set, or in the editor) is copied into the project and kept by its path there: the game and its export do not depend on the library folder. A theme whose images still point outside the project shows a warning in the editor, with « Copier dans le projet ».

items.title: A pack in the WorldMint format: interface_pack_apply first
items.text: A pack in the WorldMint format is a folder with theme.json (palette, sprites with their nineSlice margins), PNG/Default and PNG/Double, and the same base image names in every pack (panel_window, button_primary_normal, slot_square_empty, progress_track_horizontal, banner_title, minimap_frame_mint...). For such a pack, never build the rows by hand: call interface_pack_apply {"pack": "<the pack folder, or its folder name in the library>"} ("cadre": "gold" or "pond" for another minimap ring, "dry_run": true to see the reply without changing anything). In one undoable step it adds the interface system if missing, replaces habillage with every kind and role (2× images, margins doubled, echelle 0.5; banner and ring margins measured on the images), sets the colors measured on the images (the palette names do not say the color), and sets the carte system's cadre_marge to the ring's thickness. Its reply lists the rows, the colors, the base images the pack lacks (those elements keep their look) and the pack's extensions (name, size, pivot, path): lay those yourself in drawn screens (screens_set) when the game needs them. Then check the result in game_run and capture_steps as below. A pack without the WorldMint base (its own names) is refused: dress it by hand with the method below.

items.title: Finding the right images in a pack
items.text: Never guess a file name or a size. assets_search with kind image and the pack's name gives every image with its size in pixels; then search by what each piece is: assets_search {"query": "UI_Modern button", "kind": "image"}, then panel, window, frame, bar, fill, slot, input, tooltip, scroll, title or header, and words like hover, pressed, disabled, selected for the states. Check a candidate with asset_info (and look at it in a capture) before choosing: a frame has a border all around and a plain middle; measure its border in pixels for the margins (a 64 × 64 panel with a 12-pixel rim: 12 on each side). Prefer images of the same pack and style for every kind.

items.title: Example: « habille l'interface avec mon pack UI_Modern »
items.text:
1. modules_add interface if the game does not have it.
  2. assets_search {"query": "UI_Modern", "kind": "image"}: list the pack, then search each kind (UI_Modern panel, UI_Modern button, UI_Modern bar...). Look at the candidates; note each size and the thickness of its border.
  3. modules_set interface habillage with one row per kind found, and variants where the pack has them: 
    [
  {"sorte": "panneau", "image": "UI_Modern/panel_window.png", "marge_gauche": 24, "marge_haut": 24, "marge_droite": 24, "marge_bas": 24},
  {"sorte": "titre", "image": "UI_Modern/header.png", "marge_gauche": 16, "marge_haut": 8, "marge_droite": 16, "marge_bas": 8},
  {"sorte": "bouton", "image": "UI_Modern/button_normal.png", "survol": "UI_Modern/button_hover.png", "appui": "UI_Modern/button_pressed.png", "grise": "UI_Modern/button_disabled.png", "marge_gauche": 12, "marge_haut": 12, "marge_droite": 12, "marge_bas": 12},
  {"sorte": "champ", "image": "UI_Modern/input.png", "actif": "UI_Modern/input_focus.png", "marge_gauche": 10, "marge_haut": 10, "marge_droite": 10, "marge_bas": 10},
  {"sorte": "barre", "image": "UI_Modern/bar_back.png", "remplissage": "UI_Modern/bar_fill_grey.png", "couleur_element": true, "marge_gauche": 8, "marge_droite": 8},
  {"sorte": "barre", "role": "barre.vie", "remplissage": "UI_Modern/bar_fill_red.png"},
  {"sorte": "case", "image": "UI_Modern/slot.png", "choisi": "UI_Modern/slot_selected.png", "marge_gauche": 8, "marge_haut": 8, "marge_droite": 8, "marge_bas": 8},
  {"sorte": "infobulle", "image": "UI_Modern/tooltip.png", "marge_gauche": 10, "marge_haut": 10, "marge_droite": 10, "marge_bas": 10},
  {"sorte": "defilement", "image": "UI_Modern/scroll_track.png", "curseur": "UI_Modern/scroll_thumb.png", "marge_haut": 6, "marge_bas": 6}
]
    (These file names are an example: use the ones assets_search returned.)
  4. Check: game_run opening a window (the inventory with I), then capture_steps: corners sharp, borders not stretched, text readable on the images, nothing spilling out. Adjust the margins or echelle if the corners look blurred or too thick. Say to the user which image went where; they change any of it in the editor (Systems tab, Interface, « Thème en images »), which shows the cut lines and a preview.

items.title: Several players
items.text:
The interface theme is the same for every player: each one's game draws it, guests included.

This page is generated automatically from the WorldMint code (modules/interface/module.json, modules/interface/AGENT.md, modules/events.json): it always matches the editor.

items.title: Inventory
items.text:
What carries this system can be picked up, and the player keeps it, grouped by kind. The game can give some, take some, and react to each change. Optionally, a weight: each item weighs, the player has a maximum load, and carrying too much slows them.

Identifier inventaire Version 32 Placed on objects yes Also activates Interaction Also needs, on the same object Interaction

items.title: Settings for the whole game
items.text:
In the Systems panel (Developer mode), by opening the system's card.

Setting What it does Name in code Type Default Limits or choices Most kinds of items How many different kinds of items the player can carry. Once full, they no longer pick up a new kind, but still more of the kinds they have. places Number 20 from 1 to 1000, as a whole number Pick up by walking over, without a key Ticked: the player picks up an item just by walking over it. Unticked: they have to use it (E by default). au_contact Yes or no no Reach to pick up by walking over (m) The distance, in meters, at which an item is picked up by walking over it, when picking up by contact is ticked. distance_contact Number 1.2 from 0.1 to 10 One bag for the whole group (several players) In a game with several players: ticked, all players share the same bag; what one picks up, the others can use. Unticked, each has their own. No effect in a single-player game. sac_commun Yes or no no Show the content on screen Shows at the top right of the screen what the player carries, such as "Apple x3". afficher Yes or no yes Inventory window with a key (I) Ticked: the Open the inventory control (I, or Back on a gamepad) opens a window with one slot per kind of item, and closes it. A click on a slot tells the game (inventaire.choisi). fenetre Yes or no yes Slots per row in the window How many slots the window lines up before starting the next row. Beyond four rows, the grid scrolls with the mouse wheel. colonnes Number 5 from 1 to 8, as a whole number Look of the inventory window A grid only: the small window from before, with one slot per item. Three parts: as in survival games, a window that fills the screen, with the character and what they wear on the left (if the game has Equipment), the bag and the hotbar in the middle, and on the right what is being searched (a chest, a body) or the details of the chosen item. disposition_fenetre Choice in a list A grid only grille: A grid onlytrois_parties: Three parts: character, bag, search Width left for the character (three parts) In the three-part window, the empty space between the two columns of slots, as a share of the screen width (0.14: a little more than a seventh). Set 0 to bring the slots together. espace_personnage Number 0.14 from 0 to 0.4 Show the character between the slots (three parts) Ticked: when the three-part window opens, the game camera turns toward the player's character, who appears in the empty space between their equipment slots, as in role-playing games. It goes back behind them when the window closes. The framing follows the character's size. No effect with the grid only, or without Equipment. montrer_personnage Yes or no yes A "Drop" button in the window (key G) Ticked: the whole slot can be dropped on the ground from the window, with "Drop" in the small window a click on the slot opens, the G key (the one hovered) or by dragging it out of the window. A stack falls as one object ("Wood x40") picked up in one go; a unique copy keeps its record. bouton_jeter Yes or no yes Size of a dropped item (metres) A dropped slot takes its kind's model (the one in hand, the one kept on pickup, or an object of that kind in the world). With no model at all, a small engine shape, measured then set to this size. taille_jete Number 0.3 from 0.05 to 5 Stop the game while the window is open Ticked: the world stops while the inventory window is open. Unticked: the game goes on behind it, enemies included. pause_fenetre Yes or no yes A bar of items to hold in hand (keys 1 to 9, wheel) Ticked: as in survival games, a bar of slots chooses what the player holds in hand, with keys 1 to 9 (then 0, - and = beyond 9 slots), the mouse wheel or the gamepad's d-pad left (it goes round the slots). Untick it if the player never holds anything. What they pick up goes into it by itself, and the key of the slot already chosen puts the item away. The tool held is used to gather (Gathering); a game script can use it too (inventaire.en_main). barre Yes or no yes Slots in the bar How many slots the bar of items in hand has, from 1 to 12: keys 1 to 9, then 0, - and = (the top row of the keyboard) choose them. Set the number of things the player really holds: 2 for an axe and a pickaxe, 3 to 5 in a shooter, 6 to 8 in a survival game, 10 to 12 in a role-playing game. cases_barre Number 5 from 1 to 12, as a whole number Rows in the bar 1 or 2. With 2, a second row with as many slots shows above the first one (or beside it, in a column), as in online role-playing games. Shift + a slot's key chooses the slot of the second row (the key can be changed in the Options). What is picked up fills the first row first; the wheel goes round both. rangees_barre Number 1 from 1 to 2, as a whole number Show the bar on screen Shows the slots of the bar, their number, what they hold and the chosen slot. Untick it if your game draws its own bar (an editor screen, for example): the keys still work. afficher_barre Yes or no yes Place of the bar Where the bar of items in hand is drawn on screen: at the bottom in the middle, as in most games, at the top, or in a column on one side. place_barre Choice in a list At the bottom, in the middle bas: At the bottom, in the middlehaut: At the top, in the middlegauche: On the left, in a columndroite: On the right, in a column Show the item held in the character's hand Ticked: the model of the item held appears in the character's hand and follows their moves. Its model comes from the "Models in hand" list, otherwise from the item picked up. The hand is found by measuring the character's skeleton. montrer_en_main Yes or no yes Bone that holds the item (empty: found by itself) The name of a bone of the character where the item held goes. Empty: the bone made for holding under the right hand if the model has one, otherwise the right hand, recognised by its name or the shape of the skeleton. os_main Text (empty) Models in hand For each kind of item held, the model shown in the hand and its place. Best: put the model in the character's hand in the editor, hide it, and choose it here; its exact place is reused. A kind missing from the list shows the model of the item picked up. en_main List of “Item” (empty) one line per “Item”: its fields Kinds of items One row per kind of item that needs more than a name: its description (shown in the tooltip), its category, its default rarity, its picture in the slots, and "Unique copies". A kind missing from the list stacks as before. sortes_objets List of “Kind” (empty) one line per “Kind”: its fields Weight: each item weighs, the player has a maximum load Ticked: each item has a weight, the player carries at most a load, and carrying too much slows them, stops them running or picking up, after the steps below. Unticked (default): nothing weighs. Slots and weight can be used together. poids_actif Yes or no no Starting maximum load What the player carries without trouble, in the game's unit. It is the base of the value charge_max: Strength from Progression, a level or a backpack raise it. charge_base Number 50 from 0 to 1 000 000 Weight unit shown Written after each weight, such as "kg", "lb" or "stones". It is translated like the game's other texts. unite Text kg Weight of an item with no weight set The weight of one item of a kind that has neither a weight on the item picked up nor a row in the list below. poids_defaut Number 1 from 0 to 1 000 000 Weight of each kind of item One row per kind: its weight for one item. Useful for what scripts give (a reward, a purchase), which no item picked up describes. The weight set on an item picked up comes before its row; a kind with neither weighs the default weight. poids_objets List of “Kind” (empty) one line per “Kind”: its fields Overload steps What carrying too much costs. Each step starts beyond a share of the maximum load (100 %: the full load); the highest reached applies. By default: beyond 100 %, 30 % slower and no running; beyond 150 %, not a step nor a pickup. paliers_poids List of “Step” [{'seuil': 100, 'ralentir': 30, 'sans_course': True, 'sans_saut': False, 'sans_ramasser': False, 'immobile': False, 'endurance': 0, 'message': '', 'libelle': 'Surchargé', 'couleur': '#f08c33'}, {'seuil': 150, 'ralentir': 0, 'sans_course': True, 'sans_saut': True, 'sans_ramasser': True, 'immobile': True, 'endurance': 0, 'message': '', 'libelle': 'Écrasé', 'couleur': '#e8473a'}] one line per “Step”: its fields Color of "Loaded" (before the first step) The color of the "Loaded" indicator when the player nears the maximum load, before any step. Each step has its own. couleur_charge Color #f2bf4d Show "loaded" from (% of the load) The small weight indicator appears from this share of the maximum load, before the first step. 0: always visible. alerte_charge Number 80 from 0 to 10 000 An item that would go over the limit What happens when the player picks up an item that would take them over the limit below: they take it and the steps apply, or the item stays on the ground with a message. trop_lourd Choice in a list Pick it up anyway (the steps apply) permettre: Pick it up anyway (the steps apply)refuser: Refuse it, with a message Limit to pick up (% of the load) With "Refuse it": an item that would go beyond this share of the maximum load stays on the ground. 100: never more than the full load. limite_ramasser Number 100 from 1 to 10 000 Refusal: the slot lights up (seconds, 0: never) When an item is refused because it is too heavy, its slot lights up for a moment to say why: the slot of its kind in the hotbar and in the window, otherwise the hotbar slot it would have gone to. The color, or the "alert" image, comes from the Interface system's theme. 0: only the message. signal_refus Number 1.5 from 0 to 30 Who carries the shared bag? With one bag for the whole group: its weight is split equally between the players present (default), weighs fully on each, or on nobody. poids_sac_commun Choice in a list Shared: each carries their share partage: Shared: each carries their sharechacun: Each carries all of itaucun: It weighs on nobody Show the weight carried on screen A small indicator, "Loaded" or "Overloaded" with the weight and the load, when the player nears or goes over their load. The inventory window always shows the weight. afficher_poids Yes or no yes Weight indicator: horizontal position (0 to 1) 0 at the left edge of the screen, 1 at the right edge. On the right half, the indicator lines up to the right of this point. poids_x Number 0.98 from 0 to 1 Weight indicator: vertical position (0 to 1) 0 at the top of the screen, 1 at the bottom. 0.08 puts it under the list of what the player carries. poids_y Number 0.08 from 0 to 1

items.title: The fields of each “Item”
items.text:
In the Properties, each “Item” has its own numbered frame; Add: Item adds one, the cross removes it. A field only appears when it is useful: under its name, the table says when.

Setting What it does Name in code Type Default Limits or choices Kind of item The kind as the inventory stores it, such as "Axe". objet Text (empty) Model (an object of the scene, usually hidden) The object a copy of which shows in the hand. If it is already set on a bone of the character in the editor, its exact place is reused; otherwise it goes on the bone that holds, with the offset and rotation below. modele Object of the scene (empty) Model (a file, if no object is chosen) The file of the model shown in the hand when no object of the scene is chosen above: a weapon shipped with WorldMint (armes/...), copied into the project with its licence. With several players, each guest loads the same file from their copy of the game and sees it held the same way. modele_fichier model (empty) Way to hold Placed: the exact place of the object set in the hand in the editor, otherwise the offset. Measured: the handle found by measuring the model (its longest round, narrow part) and gripped in the fist, the head or blade forward; "upright", its length across the fist, like a sword. prise Choice in a list Placed (the object's place, or the offset below) placee: Placed (the object's place, or the offset below)arme: Measured, a melee weapon or a tool (the handle in the fist)debout: Measured, upright in the fist (a sword, a bow) Real length (m, 0: the model's) With a measured hold: the real length of the item for a 1.8 m character, scaled to the character's size (0.95 for a sword, 0.3 for a dagger). longueur Number 0 from 0 to 5 Front of the model (measured hold) The tip of the item (the point of a blade, the head of an axe): found by itself, the side of its longest axis with the most material outside the handle. avant Choice in a list Found by itself auto: Found by itself+x: +X-x: −X+y: +Y-y: −Y+z: +Z-z: −Z Offset X (m) Moves the model in the hand, along the bone's first axis, in metres. decalage_x Number 0 from -2 to 2 Offset Y (m) Moves the model in the hand, along the bone's second axis (often along the fingers), in metres. decalage_y Number 0 from -2 to 2 Offset Z (m) Moves the model in the hand, along the bone's third axis, in metres. decalage_z Number 0 from -2 to 2 Rotation X (°) Turns the model in the hand around the bone's first axis, in degrees: 90 to lay a handle down. rotation_x Number 0 from -180 to 180 Rotation Y (°) Turns the model in the hand around the bone's second axis, in degrees. rotation_y Number 0 from -180 to 180 Rotation Z (°) Turns the model in the hand around the bone's third axis, in degrees. rotation_z Number 0 from -180 to 180

items.title: The fields of each “Kind”
items.text:
In the Properties, each “Kind” has its own numbered frame; Add: Kind adds one, the cross removes it. A field only appears when it is useful: under its name, the table says when.

Setting What it does Name in code Type Default Limits or choices Kind of item The kind as the inventory stores it, such as "Iron sword". objet Text (empty) Unique copies No: items of this kind stack, all alike. Yes: each copy has its own record (its name, its bonuses, its wear...), kept with the world; it takes a slot of its own and does not stack. uniques Yes or no no Description The text shown in the item's tooltip, translated like the game's other texts. description Text (empty) Category Free: weapon, armour, tool, gem... The Equipment and Loot modules will use it to know where the item goes. categorie Text (empty) Default rarity The rarity written on a new copy's record (common, rare...). Empty: none. rarete Text (empty) Max. stack How many items of this kind fit in one slot, such as 100 for Wood. Beyond it, a new slot opens; totals stay those of the kind. 0: no limit, a single slot, as before. pile_max Number 0 from 0 to 1 000 000, as a whole number Picture The item's picture in the slots (bag, quick bar, equipment, chest, crafting, shop): drag it from the Library, preferably square on a transparent background. The quantity is written small in a corner, the name stays in the tooltip. Empty: its name. icone Image from the library (empty)

items.title: The fields of each “Kind”
items.text:
In the Properties, each “Kind” has its own numbered frame; Add: Kind adds one, the cross removes it. A field only appears when it is useful: under its name, the table says when.

Setting What it does Name in code Type Default Limits or choices Kind of item The kind as the inventory stores it, such as "Stone". objet Text (empty) Weight of one item In the game's unit: 0.01 for a coin, 5 for a log. poids Number 1 from 0 to 1 000 000

items.title: The fields of each “Step”
items.text:
In the Properties, each “Step” has its own numbered frame; Add: Step adds one, the cross removes it. A field only appears when it is useful: under its name, the table says when.

Setting What it does Name in code Type Default Limits or choices Beyond (% of the maximum load) The step applies when the weight carried goes beyond this share of the maximum load: 100 for the full load, 150 for half as much again. seuil Number 100 from 0 to 10 000 Slow down by (%) How much slower the player walks, runs and swims: 30 for 30 % less. It is a negative bonus from the source "poids" on the value vitesse_deplacement. ralentir Number 30 from 0 to 95 No running Ticked: the player can only walk. sans_course Yes or no yes No jumping Ticked: the player can no longer jump. sans_saut Yes or no no No picking up Ticked: the player picks up nothing while at this step; a message tells them. What scripts give still goes in. sans_ramasser Yes or no no Stop all moving Ticked: the player cannot take a step until their load gets lighter. immobile Yes or no no Extra stamina spent (%) With the Stamina system: running, jumping and striking cost this much more. 50: one and a half times. Without it, nothing. endurance Number 0 from 0 to 1000 Label on screen The word the weight indicator shows at this step, followed by the weight carried: "Overloaded: 52 / 40 kg", "Crushed: 70 / 40 kg". libelle Text Surchargé Color on screen The color of the indicator and of the window's "Weight" line at this step: orange, then red for the heaviest. couleur Color #f08c33 Message on entering this step Shown to the player when they reach this step. Empty: "Too heavy" with their weight, or "Far too heavy" if they can no longer move. message Text (empty)

items.title: Settings on each object
items.text:
In the Properties of an object or folder that carries the system, Systems section. A folder passes its values on to what it contains; an object can change a value for itself only.

Setting What it does Name in code Type Default Limits or choices Kind of item (empty: its name, without number) The kind of item it is stored under, such as "Apple": items of the same kind add up. Empty: its name without number ("Apple 3" is an "Apple"). nom Text (empty) Quantity picked up How many one pickup gives: 50 for a bag of 50 coins. quantite Number 1 from 1 to 1 000 000, as a whole number Weight of one item (-1: its kind's) With weight ticked in the game settings: what one item weighs, in the game's unit. -1: its kind's weight in the game's list, otherwise the default weight. poids Number -1 from -1 to 1 000 000

items.title: Controls added to the game
items.text:
They appear in the Game controls panel (Developer mode), where you can change their key.

Control Name for scripts Key Gamepad Open the inventory inventory I Back Next item in hand item_next Wheel down ← Previous item in hand item_previous Wheel up — Drop the hovered slot (inventory window) item_drop G — Split while dragging (hold) item_split Left Shift — Second row of the bar (hold with a number) item_second_row Left Shift —

items.title: Events
items.text: The descriptions come from the code.

items.title: What it announces
items.text: Event Fields Description inventaire.change objet (text), quantite (number), total (number), chargement (boolean?), fiche (number?), jete (boolean?) The quantity of an item changed. total is the new quantity. chargement is true when a saved game gives the items back (game.load): nothing was picked up. For a unique copy (version 15), objet is its kind, fiche its record's number, total how many of that kind. With several stacks of a kind (version 21), total counts all of them; jete is true when a slot was dropped on the ground. inventaire.plein objet (text), fiche (number?), reste (number?) An item could not be added: every slot holds another kind of item (or another unique copy), or (version 21) every stack of its kind is full. reste: picked up in part, how many stayed on the ground. inventaire.manque objet (text), quantite (number), fiche (number?) Items could not be removed: there are not enough. inventaire.choisi objet (text), total (number), fiche (number?), double (boolean?), case (text?) The player clicked a slot of the inventory window: objet is the kind of item, total how many they carry. What it does belongs to the game: eat, equip, read. case (version 21) is the slot's key ("Wood~2" for a second stack). inventaire.en_main objet (text), avant (text), place (number), chargement (boolean?), joueur (id?), fiche (number?), source (text?) What the player holds in hand changed (version 24): the slot chosen in the inventory's bar (keys 1 to 9, wheel), an item used up, a load (chargement true). objet is the kind held, "" for empty hands; avant the one held before; place the bar slot (0: nothing). Gathering checks the tool held; a game script equips a sword with it. inventaire.poids poids (number), charge (number), palier (number), seuil (number), avant (number) With the weight on (inventory setting poids_actif): the weight a player carries, their maximum load (the value charge_max) or their overload step changed. palier is the step's row number in paliers_poids (0: none), seuil its share of the load in %, avant the step before. inventaire.trop_lourd objet (text), poids (number), porte (number), charge (number), raison (text) With the weight on: a pickup was refused, the item stays where it is. raison: limite (it would go beyond limite_ramasser, with trop_lourd set to refuser) or palier (the current overload step forbids picking up). inventaire.glisse objet (text), fiche (number?), cible (text), joueur (id?), case (text?) The player dragged a slot of the inventory window (mouse button pressed on it, released elsewhere, version 16): cible is the key of the HUD element under the cursor. The Equipment module wears an item dragged onto a slot. case (version 21): the dragged slot's key. inventaire.fenetre ouverte (boolean), joueur (id?) The inventory window opened or closed (version 16): ouverte. The Equipment window opens beside it. inventaire.jeter objet (text), case (text?), fiche (number?), quantite (number?), joueur (id?) Ask the inventory to drop a whole slot (version 15 for a unique copy, version 21 for a stack): case is the slot's key ("Wood~2"), otherwise fiche a unique copy, otherwise the first slot of the kind objet. It is put down in front of the player as one object that gives the same quantity back in one pickup (its prompt says "Wood x40"); a unique copy's record follows it and comes back with it. quantite (version 21): only that many from a stack (Shift + drag out of the window drops half); the slot keeps the rest. equipement.porter objet (text?), fiche (number?), emplacement (text?), joueur (id?) Ask the Equipment module to make the player wear an item of their bag: objet its kind, fiche a unique copy (it must be in this player's bag), emplacement a slot key or name (missing: the first free slot accepting it). equipement.retirer emplacement (text), joueur (id?) Ask the Equipment module to take off what is worn at a slot (its key, such as tete, or its name): it goes back to the bag. butin.prendre cible (text), numero (number?), joueur (id) A player asks the host to take from a content: one line (numero) or all they may take. butin.ranger cible (text), objet (text), fiche (number?), quantite (number?), case (text?), joueur (id) A player asks the host to put an item of their bag into a chest they may search (the three-part inventory window): a stack (quantite) or a unique copy (fiche). The bag loses it first; nothing enters if the bag no longer has it.

items.title: What it listens to
items.text: Event Fields Description interaction.utiliser cible (id), joueur (id) The player used the object in reach: a door, a merchant, an item to pick up. Whoever owns that object decides what it does. inventaire.ajouter objet (text), quantite (number), joueur (id?), fiche (number?) Ask the inventory to add items, such as a reward. Answered by inventaire.change, or inventaire.plein. With several players, joueur says whose bag; without it, the player whose action is being handled, or every player. inventaire.retirer objet (text), quantite (number), fiche (number?) Ask the inventory to remove items, such as a payment. Answered by inventaire.change, or inventaire.manque if there are not enough. For a kind with unique copies (version 15): fiche removes that copy, otherwise the first ones; their records are destroyed. inventaire.tenir objet (text?), place (number?), joueur (id?) Ask the inventory to hold something in hand (version 24): a bar slot (place), or a kind of item (objet; one outside the bar takes the chosen slot). objet "" puts the item away: empty hands. joueur.occupe occupe (boolean), par (text) The player's hands are taken by something else than fighting (version 23): a building mode where the click places a piece, a tool being aimed. occupe true when it starts, false when it ends; par names who says it ("construction"), so several can overlap. Fighting modules do not strike nor block while any of them keeps the player busy. hud.clic cible (text), joueur (id?) A button of the HUD was clicked: pressed, then released on it; or chosen with A (Enter) while it has the gamepad or keyboard focus; or the window's back button (back = true), with B (Escape). cible is the button's key (game.hud_button), joueur the player who clicked (a guest clicks on their own computer; the host plays the click). Announced by the engine, before the scripts' on_update of that step. langue.change langue (text) Sent by the engine when the player changes the game's language (game.set_language, the Menu options). A module redraws what it already shows: its texts go through game.t and game.language. inventaire.jeter objet (text), case (text?), fiche (number?), quantite (number?), joueur (id?) Ask the inventory to drop a whole slot (version 15 for a unique copy, version 21 for a stack): case is the slot's key ("Wood~2"), otherwise fiche a unique copy, otherwise the first slot of the kind objet. It is put down in front of the player as one object that gives the same quantity back in one pickup (its prompt says "Wood x40"); a unique copy's record follows it and comes back with it. quantite (version 21): only that many from a stack (Shift + drag out of the window drops half); the slot keeps the rest. inventaire.sortir objet (text), fiche (number?), case (text?), joueur (id?) Ask the inventory to take one item out of the bag without destroying it (version 16): objet is its kind, fiche a unique copy (it keeps its record; whoever takes it says its new holder). The Equipment module takes what it makes the player wear. A stack gives one from its smallest stack, or from case (version 21), a slot's key. inventaire.tenir_porte objet (text), fiche (number?), prioritaire (boolean?), joueur (id?) Ask the inventory to hold in hand an item worn (version 17): the Equipment module hands it the weapon of its slot, so it is held, shown (its row of the list Models in hand, measured hold included) and announced (inventaire.en_main) exactly like the bar's. objet "" : nothing worn in hand any more. prioritaire: it comes before the bar; otherwise only when the bar holds nothing. objet.change numero (number), sorte (text), champs (table) Sent by the engine when the host changed the record of a unique item (game.item_set): champs lists the fields given. fenetres.fermer joueur (id?), raison (text?) Close every window a player has open (loot, inventory, equipment, workshop...), sent by the Death module when they die; any script may send it (a cutscene). joueur: that player (missing: everyone). Each module with a window closes its own. inventaire.diviser case (text), quantite (number?), vers (text?), joueur (id?) Ask the inventory to split a stack (version 21): quantite items of the slot case (missing: half, rounded down) move to a new slot, or with vers onto that stack of the same kind, up to its maximum stack (the rest stays in case). Refused, with a message and the slot lit up, when a new slot is needed and none is free; a stack of 1 or a unique copy does not split. inventaire.regrouper de (text), vers (text), joueur (id?) Ask the inventory to merge two stacks of the same kind (version 21): the slot de pours into the slot vers, up to the kind's maximum stack; the rest stays where it was. inventaire.decrire objet (text), description (text) Describe a kind of item during the game (version 29), when « Sortes d'objets » gives it no description: the tooltip and the item's details show it. An empty description removes it. butin.ouvrir cible (text), joueur (id?) Open the Take all window of a content (a body, a chest) for a player. butin.contenu cible (text), nombre (number) A content (a body, a chest) changed: its Take all windows redraw. equipement.porte joueur (id), emplacement (text), objet (text), fiche (number?) The player now wears an item: emplacement is the slot key, objet its kind, fiche its record (a unique copy). Its bonuses have the source equipement:<emplacement>. equipement.retire joueur (id), emplacement (text), objet (text), fiche (number?) The player took off an item: it is back in the bag, and its bonuses are gone. scene.change depuis (text), vers (text) Sent by the engine once the player has arrived in another scene of the game (game.go_to, or a passage). Scripts keep running across scenes: this is when a module looks at the objects of the new scene.

items.title: Points a script can replace (game.override)
items.text:
The descriptions come from the code.

  • inventaire.porteur: function(default, joueur) -> the object that holds the item in hand (its model is attached to that object's hand bone). The default is the object given by the hook equipement.corps when a game overrides it, otherwise the player's character. For a game whose visible body is another object following the player.
  • inventaire.sorte: function(default, id) -> the kind of item this object gives when picked up (text). The default is its nom setting, or its name without a trailing number.
  • inventaire.permise: function(default, objet, usage) -> true, or false: whether the player may hold (usage tenir: chosen in the bar) or use (usage utiliser: a click on its slot) that kind of item (version 10). The default is true. The Progression module uses it for required levels; say why yourself (a message), the inventory only refuses.
  • inventaire.infobulle: function(default, lignes, infos) -> the lines of an item's tooltip (version 16): lignes is the list of texts shown ([b], [color=#rrggbb] allowed), infos is {objet, fiche, joueur}. Return the lines, with yours added: the Equipment module adds the comparison with what is worn at the same place.
  • inventaire.poids: function(default, objet) -> the weight of one item of that kind (a number), when the weight is on (version 11). The default is the weight set on the item picked up, else its row in the list Weight of each kind, else the default weight. For a weight that changes (a full or empty water skin), or one computed by the game.

items.title: What the agent knows about this system
items.text: The text the agent reads before using this system.

items.title: Inventory (inventaire)
items.text:
Keeps what the player carries, grouped by kind. Activating it activates the interaction module; placing it on an object places interaction there too, so the player can use it.

  • An item to pick up: an object carrying this system (systems_attach), or every child of a group carrying it. Its kind is nom if set (systems_set), otherwise its name without a trailing number: "Apple 3" is an "Apple". quantite is how many one pickup gives: a bag of 50 coins. Name items in the user's language.
  • Picking up: the player uses the item (E by default), or walks over it if the game setting au_contact is on. The item leaves the world.
  • Give or take items from your scripts, such as a reward or a payment: game.emit("inventaire.ajouter", {objet = "Apple", quantite = 2}), game.emit("inventaire.retirer", {objet = "Gold", quantite = 10}).
  • Know what the player has: listen to inventaire.change (objet, quantite, total). A shop checks total before selling, or listens to inventaire.manque, sent when there are not enough.
  • inventaire.plein is sent when every slot holds another kind of item (game setting places).
  • The content shows at the top right with the HUD key inventaire.
  • The window: the control inventory (I, or Back on a gamepad) opens a grid of every place of the bag (places slots, empty ones included, colonnes per row), and closes it (game setting fenetre). Rows that do not fit scroll with the wheel; pause_fenetre stops the world while it is open. With disposition_fenetre grille (default) it is the system's screen « Inventaire » (version 30, modules/inventaire/ecrans/inventaire.json): Inventaire/Fenêtre, Inventaire/Titre, Inventaire/Poids, the list Inventaire/Cases whose rows are the places, Inventaire/Case#N (full or empty, the empty one fainter; same theme role case.inventaire), N being the slot's number in the grid, and Inventaire/Bouton Fermer. Change its look in the screen editor (styles, theme), never in the script. The three-part window is still drawn by the script, with keys starting with inventaire. (inventaire.case.N, inventaire.place.N). Beyond 200 places (a weight-only game with places 1000), the grid shows the rows up to the last item and one empty row more.
  • Each item keeps its slot (version 28): dragged onto an empty slot it goes there (with Shift, half of a stack starts a new stack there); dragged onto another kind (or a full stack, or a unique copy) the two slots swap; onto a stack of the same kind they merge as before. What is picked up or given goes into the first free slot; « Trier » (three-part window) packs everything at the start, in sorted order; emptying a slot leaves it empty (nothing shifts). Saved games keep each item's slot (case in the save, written only when it is not the next one, so a bag never rearranged saves exactly as before); an older save fills the first slots in order. Each player, guests included, has their own (the host keeps a guest's bag with its slots).
  • Gamepad and keyboard: the first slot has the focus, the d-pad or the arrows move it, A or Enter chooses it, B or Escape closes the window (Inventaire/Bouton Fermer is its back button; inventaire.fermer in three parts).
  • Saved games: game.save keeps what the player carries, and game.load gives it back; then the inventory announces each kind again with inventaire.change and chargement = true (nothing was picked up), so that every system knows the totals. Do not re-add items after a load.
  • The item in hand (game setting barre, on by default): a bar of cases_barre slots (5) at the bottom of the screen (place_barre; afficher_barre off if the game draws its own). It is the system's screen « Barre rapide » (version 30): Barre rapide/Fond, the lists Barre rapide/Rangée (keys 1 to 9...) and Barre rapide/Seconde rangée (Shift), each slot Barre rapide/Case#N with Icône#N (the kind's image) and Texte#N (Case 2#N, Icône 2#N, Texte 2#N in the second row); the script places it and lays its rows out for place_barre. What is picked up fills the first free slot; keys 1 to 9 (then 0, - and =, up to 12 slots; a second row with rangees_barre: see version 27 below), the wheel (item_next, item_previous) and the d-pad left (item_next: it goes round the slots; every other gamepad button already belongs to a system) choose the slot, and its key again puts the item away. What is held is announced by inventaire.en_main (objet, "" for empty hands, avant, place): collecte gathers with the tool held, a game script equips a sword with it. Choose it from a script with game.emit("inventaire.tenir", {objet = "Axe"}) (or place, or objet = ""); objet and place together put that item at that slot of the bar and hold it (what the slot held takes the slot it left): a game window that drags an item onto the bar sends just that, without taking the item out of the bag. In the window, a number key puts the hovered slot at that place of the bar. The bar, the chosen slot and what is held are saved; each player has their own.
  • Its model in the hand (montrer_en_main, on): a copy of its model follows the character's hand bone, found by measuring the skeleton (game.hand_bone: a bone made for holding under the right hand, else the right hand; os_main overrides it). The model comes from the list en_main (a row per kind: objet, modele, an object of the scene, usually hidden, and an offset and rotation along the bone), else from the first item of that kind picked up. An item the game gives (at the start, a reward, crafted) was never picked up: without its en_main row, nothing shows in the hand (the game log says inventaire: « Hache » est tenu sans modèle). Give every tool and weapon its row: modele_fichier (the model file) and prise arme are enough. Best: set the model in the character's hand in the editor (entities_create with attach_bone), check it with a capture, hide it, and name it in en_main: its exact place is reused. Do not leave a visible model in the hand, nor write a script that shows or hides one.
  • Holding a melee weapon right (prise placee): the copy takes the exact place of its model RELATIVE TO THE HAND BONE. An example the creator put in (or right next to) the character's hand in the editor is enough as modele, even if it is not attached to a bone: its place relative to the measured hand bone, in the scene (the rest pose the editor shows), is copied. Too far from the hand (more than 15 % of the character's height), nothing is copied and the game log says attach: ... from the hand: read it after game_run. To make the example follow the hand in the editor too, attach it without moving it: entities_update with parent (the character), then a second entities_update with attach_bone (from game.hand_bone or asset_info bones) and keep_place: true (the editor's button "Attach to the hand (keep its place)" does the same); never retype its numbers.
  • Never delete, move or "clean up" an example object the creator placed (a weapon put in the hand to show the grip, even if it looks like it floats or counts as a spawn point): it is the reference. Hide it, or ask; do not remove it. Then hide it and name it in modele. Without an example, use prise arme (the grip measured on the model). Every pack differs (pivot at the pommel or the guard, long axis x, y or z, centimetres): measure or copy, never guess an axis.
  • Check every melee weapon on a capture in game, standing and during a hit (the clip of the combat module): the fist closes on the handle, no finger nor hand goes through the handle or the blade, the blade is not inside the arm or the body. One weapon held right does not mean the others are: check each row of en_main.
  • A click on a slot sends inventaire.choisi (objet, total). What it does belongs to the game: eat an apple (inventaire.retirer, then sante.soigner), equip a sword, read a letter. Write that in a game script, or a declencheur rule on the event.

items.title: A bigger bar, and two rows (version 27)
items.text:
• cases_barre goes from 1 to 12: keys 1 to 9, then 0, - and = for slots 10, 11 and 12 (the top row of the keyboard, as in World of Warcraft). Keys are read by their place on the keyboard, not the character they type: on an AZERTY keyboard, the two keys right of 0 () and =) are the - and = of the bar.
  • rangees_barre = 1 (default) or 2. With 2, a second row of cases_barre slots shows above the first one at the bottom (bas), below it at the top (haut), and beside it on the screen side in a column (gauche, droite). The control item_second_row (« Deuxième rangée de la barre », left Shift by default, changeable in the Options) held with a slot's key chooses the slot of the second row: Shift+2 is its second slot (it shows « Maj+2 »). The second row's slots are numbered 13 to 24 whatever cases_barre is (place of inventaire.en_main and inventaire.tenir): 13 is its first slot.
  • What is picked up fills the first row first, then the second. The wheel and the d-pad go round every slot of both rows. The three-part window shows both rows under the bag. Saved games keep both rows; each player, guests included, has their own.
  • Too many slots for the screen (12 slots on a 4:3 screen, a long column): every slot shrinks the same way, nothing goes past the screen's edge. The Progression's XP bar sits above the whole bar, both rows.
  • Fit the bar to the game. cases_barre = the number of things the player really holds: 2 for an axe and a pickaxe, 3 to 5 in a shooter, 6 to 8 in a survival game, 10 to 12 and rangees_barre 2 for an action RPG or an online RPG. Untick barre when the player never holds anything (a puzzle game, a racing game).

items.title: Kinds of items and unique copies (version 15, off by default)
items.text:
The list sortes_objets (« Sortes d'objets ») gives a kind more than a name: a row per kind with objet (the kind), description (shown in the item's tooltip, translated like the game's texts), categorie (free: arme, armure, outil, gemme... the coming Equipment and Loot modules read it), rarete (the default rarity written on a new copy's record), icone (« Image », version 25: see below) and uniques (« Exemplaires uniques », off). A kind missing from the list, or with uniques off, stacks exactly as before, saved games included.

The item's picture (version 25): the column icone (an image file; an image given to modules_set is copied into the project, like every image setting). Every slot that shows the item then shows its picture filling the slot (proportions kept, a small margin) with the quantity small in a corner (« x4 »), the name staying in the tooltip and the card: the bag (grille and trois_parties), the hotbar at the bottom of the screen and in the window, the worn equipment slots, the card (a bigger picture at its top), the searched chest or body, the Loot window, Crafting (liste and detaillee), shops (a small picture left of the name) and the Equipment window. Empty, or a file that cannot be found: the name is written as before, without any error. Give a picture to every kind of item: the game's own item pictures, or the generic icons of a UI pack (icon_*) only when one really matches the item. Other systems and a game's own windows read it with shared.inventaire_icone(kind) (the file, or nil), or game.module_settings("inventaire").sortes_objets. The hud report of game_run gives a slot button's image. In a game with several players, the picture is a game setting: each guest sees it in their own slots (one image per slot).

  • Unique copies (uniques on): each copy picked up or given gets its own record (game.item_create, kept with the world's save, written by the host only): its number, kind, rarity, displayed name, bonuses, wear, upgrade level, gem slots and gems, item level and free data (see the script reference, game.item_*). Each copy takes a slot of its own and never stacks; it weighs like one item of its kind.
  • What the inventory says: inventaire.change, inventaire.en_main, inventaire.choisi and inventaire.plein give objet = the kind and, for a unique copy, fiche = its record's number (total counts the copies of that kind). Read a copy with game.item_get(e.fiche).
  • Give a copy already made (a reward with chosen bonuses): local n = game.item_create("Épée de fer", {bonus = {{valeur = "degats", add = 4}}}), then game.emit("inventaire.ajouter", {objet = "Épée de fer", fiche = n}). Without fiche, the inventory makes a new record with the kind's default rarity.
  • Take one: game.emit("inventaire.retirer", {objet = "Épée de fer", fiche = n}) (without fiche: the first copies of that kind); their records are destroyed. Drop one: game.emit("inventaire.jeter", {objet = "Épée de fer", fiche = n}) puts it in front of the player with its record (its porteur becomes objet:<scene>/<id>); picked up again, the same record comes back.
  • The tooltip: hovering a slot of the window (or giving it the focus) shows the record's name, the kind's description and the record's bonuses (HUD key inventaire.infobulle, theme role infobulle.objet). The hook inventaire.infobulle receives {objet, fiche, joueur, bonus = {debut, fin}}: bonus says which lines are the record's bonuses, so Equipment replaces them by their total or greys them instead of adding lines. A stack without description shows no tooltip. Rarity colours come with the Loot module.
  • Several players: the records stay on the host; each guest receives the records of their own items and of those on the ground (protocol 21), so their tooltips show the same thing.

items.title: Weight (off by default)
items.text:
In the editor, every weight setting is in the folding group « Poids » of the Inventory's card.

Ticking the game setting poids_actif (modules_set) gives every item a weight and the player a maximum load; off, nothing weighs and nothing changes. Slots (places, the value inventaire_places) and weight work together or apart: a game uses slots, weight, or both.

  • The weight of one item, in the game's unit (unite, « kg » by default, translated like the game's texts): the poids set on the item picked up (systems_set; -1: its kind's), else its kind's row in poids_objets (objet, poids: use it for what scripts give, such as gold at 0.01), else poids_defaut (1). A script can compute it with the hook inventaire.poids: game.override("inventaire.poids", function(default, objet) if objet == "Water skin" then return 0.2 + 0.8 * full end return default(objet) end).
  • The maximum load is the value charge_max (game.stat(player, "charge_max")), whose base is charge_base (50). It grows like any value: a Progression characteristic (« Force: +2 kg of load per point » is the row effet, valeur charge_max, ajout 2), a level reward (bonus on charge_max), later equipment (game.stat_bonus(player, "charge_max", "sac_a_dos", {add = 20})).
  • Overload steps (paliers_poids): each row starts beyond seuil % of the load; the highest reached applies. Its effects: ralentir (% slower: a negative bonus from the source « poids » on vitesse_deplacement, which the engine applies on the host and in a guest's prediction), sans_course, sans_saut, sans_ramasser, immobile (no step at all), endurance (% more stamina spent running, jumping and striking, with the endurance system: the value endurance_cout), message (shown on entering it; empty: « Trop chargé : 12 / 10 kg. », or « Bien trop chargé » when immobile). Leaving every step says « Vous n'êtes plus surchargé. ». Defaults: beyond 100 %, 30 % slower and no running; beyond 150 %, no step and no pickup.
  • Picking up: trop_lourd = permettre (default: picked up, the steps apply) or refuser (an item that would go beyond limite_ramasser % of the load stays on the ground, with « Enclume est trop lourd (7 kg). »). A step with sans_ramasser refuses every pickup. Both send inventaire.trop_lourd (objet, poids, porte, charge, raison limite or palier). The refused item's slot lights up for signal_refus seconds (1.5 by default, 0: never): its kind's slot in the hotbar and the window, otherwise the hotbar slot it would have gone to; the color, or the alerte image, comes from the interface theme. While the window is open, the weight message sits under it. What scripts give (inventaire.ajouter: a reward) always goes in: the steps then apply.
  • On screen: the window shows « Poids : 7 / 10 kg » under its title (Inventaire/Poids; inventaire.poids.total in three parts) and each slot the weight of its stack; a small indicator (inventaire.poids, at poids_x, poids_y; afficher_poids) says « Chargé : 8 / 10 kg » in amber (couleur_charge) from alerte_charge % (80), then each step's own libelle and couleur (by default « Surchargé : 12 / 10 kg » in orange, then « Écrasé : 16 / 10 kg » in red; the window's « Poids » line takes the step's color too); the step's message is inventaire.poids.message, on the discreet backing of announcements (inventaire.poids.message.fond, role panneau.annonce.poids), for 3 seconds, even while the window pauses the game. Restyle them by those keys like the rest of the HUD.
  • Events: inventaire.poids (poids, charge, palier the row number, 0 for none, seuil, avant) when the weight, the load or the step changes. A Trigger rule or a script reacts to it (a panting sound, a tip).
  • Several players: computed on the host, one copy per player: each guest has their own weight, load and steps, sees their own indicator and window, and their prediction walks at the slowed speed and without running, as the host makes them walk. With sac_commun, poids_sac_commun says who carries the shared bag: partage (default: its weight split equally between the players present), chacun (each carries all of it) or aucun.
  • Running and jumping are also taken by endurance (exhausted) and besoins (an empty need): each system asks again every step while it needs it, so none gives them back to a player another one still holds.

Examples: - Survival: poids_actif on, charge_base 40, unite « kg »; poids_objets Wood 2, Stone 3, Iron ore 4, Berries 0.1, Gold 0.01; steps 100 % (ralentir 25, sans_course, endurance 50) and 130 % (immobile, sans_ramasser); trop_lourd permettre; with Progression, Force +2 charge_max per point, and a backpack (a script on inventaire.choisi) adding +20. - RPG: poids_actif on, charge_base 100, unite « lb », places 1000 (weight only); swords 8, armour 25, potions 0.5, scrolls 0.1; one step at 100 % (ralentir 50, sans_course, sans_saut); trop_lourd refuser with limite_ramasser 120; Force +5 charge_max per point.

items.title: Rarity in the tooltip and « Jeter » (version 16)
items.text:
• The tooltip of a unique copy shows its name in its rarity's color and the rarity written under it, when the butin module sets that rarity (raretes); without it, the theme's color.
  • bouton_jeter (on): « Jeter » in the small window of a clicked slot drops it, and the control item_drop (G) drops the one hovered, with inventaire.jeter. Since version 21, stacks are dropped too (see below).

items.title: Stacks, split, merge and drop (version 21, ADR-042)
items.text:
• Maximum stack: the column pile_max (« Pile max. ») of sortes_objets, an integer; 0 or missing: no limit, one slot per kind, exactly as before (saved games included). With it, a kind can take several slots: the first stack keeps the kind as its key ("Bois"), the next ones are "Bois~2", "Bois~3"... A unique copy keeps "kind#record".
  • Adding fills the kind's stacks that are not full (in slot order), then opens new slots. A pickup from the world takes what fits and the object keeps the rest (inventaire.plein with reste); what scripts give (inventaire.ajouter: Loot, Crafting, a shop) is all or nothing, as before.
  • Totals never change meaning: inventaire.change.total, what Crafting, Gathering, Needs and Quests count, inventaire.retirer and inventaire.sortir all work on the kind, all its slots together. Removing takes from the smallest stack first; an empty stack frees its slot and leaves the bar. The bar holds a slot (a precise stack).
  • Events (from any script or a game's own window):
  • inventaire.jeter {objet, case?, fiche?}: drops the slot case (its key), otherwise the unique copy fiche, otherwise the first slot of kind objet. The whole slot falls in front of the player as ONE object (the kind's model in hand, the one kept at pickup, or an object of that kind in the world; with none, a builtin:cube measured then scaled to taille_jete metres), set on the measured ground, never on a body. Its prompt says « Bois x40 »; E picks the same quantity back in one go. A unique copy keeps its record. The dropped object is kept by the saved game.
  • inventaire.diviser {case, quantite?, vers?}: quantite items of that slot (missing: half, rounded down) go to a new slot right after it, or with vers onto that stack of the same kind, up to pile_max (the rest stays in case). Refused when a new slot is needed and none is free (« Plus de place dans le sac. », the slot lights up like other refusals); a stack of 1 or a unique copy does not split.
  • inventaire.jeter {case, quantite}: only quantite items of a stack fall (one object « Bois x5 »); the slot keeps the rest.
  • inventaire.regrouper {de, vers}: two stacks of the same kind merge, up to pile_max; the rest stays where it was.
  • inventaire.decrire {objet, description} (version 29): describes a kind during the game when its row of sortes_objets gives no description (that row wins); the tooltip and the three-part details show it. An empty description removes it.
  • Reading the slots one by one: shared.inventaire_contenu[player]() returns the list of slots in order, each {cle, objet, quantite, fiche} (cle is the slot key to send to the events above), and whether the bag is shared.
  • The module's window: a click on a slot (A on a gamepad) opens its small window next to it (HUD key inventaire.menu, theme role panneau.menu.inventaire): the name and quantity, « Jeter », « Diviser en deux » and a quantity (« − », « 5 sur 10 », « + », « Valider »); a unique copy or a stack of 1 only has « Jeter ». It closes with Escape or B (its « Fermer » button), a click elsewhere, or once the action is done; near the right edge it opens on the slot's left. The single click still sends inventaire.choisi (eating an apple by a click keeps working); the double click keeps its role (use, equip) and closes the small window. Right click splits a slot in two in place. Dragging a stack onto another of the same kind merges them; dragging a slot out of every window drops it. Shift + drag (the control item_split, « Diviser en glissant (tenir) », left Shift by default, read when the drag starts or when it is released) moves only half: onto an empty place of the window, a new stack; onto a stack of the same kind, up to pile_max, the rest goes back; out of the window, half falls on the ground. A stack of 1 or a unique copy drags as usual. item_split shares left Shift with run: both are held together, which is harmless (the window pauses the world, or the player is not moving). While the window pauses the game, item_drop and item_split still reach it. inventaire.choisi and inventaire.glisse also give case.
  • A game's own window (a survival game's bag): draw each slot from shared.inventaire_contenu[game.player()](), keep its cle, and add your buttons: Drop sends game.emit("inventaire.jeter", {objet = c.objet, case = c.cle}), Split sends game.emit("inventaire.diviser", {case = c.cle}) (or with quantite), dropping a stack on another sends game.emit("inventaire.regrouper", {de = a.cle, vers = b.cle}). For Shift + drag, read game.action("item_split") when the drag starts or ends and send inventaire.diviser {case, quantite = half, vers = the target stack} (or without vers onto an empty place), or inventaire.jeter {case, quantite = half} out of the window. Redraw on inventaire.change. Never edit the module.
  • Several players: each player drops and splits in their own bag; what is dropped is a world object everyone sees and can pick up.

items.title: Several players
items.text: One copy per player: each player has their own bag by default. The game setting sac_commun ("One bag for the whole group") gives everyone the same bag; with the weight on, poids_sac_commun says who carries it (split by default). The host's saved game keeps each guest's bag under their player key: they find it again when they come back.

items.title: For the Equipment module (version 16)
items.text:
• inventaire.sortir {objet, fiche?}: takes one item out of the bag without destroying it (a unique copy keeps its record).
  • A double click on a slot (or A twice on a gamepad) sends inventaire.choisi with double = true; dragging a slot onto another element of the HUD sends inventaire.glisse {objet, fiche, cible, joueur}; opening or closing the window sends inventaire.fenetre {ouverte, joueur}.
  • The hook inventaire.infobulle (lines, {objet, fiche, joueur}) -> lines: other systems add lines to an item's tooltip ([b] and [color=#rrggbb] allowed). Bonuses show their value's displayed name (game.stat_name).
  • inventaire.tenir {objet = kind} also finds a unique copy of that kind (or fiche for a precise one). With place too (version 20), that copy goes to that slot.

items.title: Version 17
items.text:
• The hook inventaire.porteur (default, player) -> the object that holds the item in hand (the model is attached to its hand bone). The default is the object the hook equipement.corps gives when the game overrides it (one hook for a game whose visible body is another object following the player: what is worn and the weapon in hand follow it), otherwise the player's character.
  • inventaire.tenir_porte {objet, fiche?, prioritaire?}: the Equipment module hands the weapon worn in its slot to the inventory, which holds, shows and announces it like the bar's (prioritaire: before the bar; otherwise when the bar holds nothing; objet "": none).
  • The list en_main gains modele_fichier (a model file, such as a weapon shipped in armes/), prise (placee as before; arme or debout: the measured weapon hold of ADR-034, the grip found on the model), longueur (its real length for a 1.8 m character) and avant. Online, guests load the same modele_fichier from their copy of the game and see it held the same way (protocol 23).

items.title: Version 22
items.text:
• prise arme is the measured hold of a melee weapon or a tool (game.attach melee): the handle is the longest round, narrow part of the model, measured slice by slice along its longest side; the fist grips it from its end away from the head (the middle of a sword grip, low on an axe haft), the head or blade forward, on the thumb side. avant forces the side of the head. A model whose handle is flat, or whose round blade is longer than its grip, is measured wrong: use placee with an example in the hand. A firearm stays held by the Shooting module (tir).
  • os_main also applies to a measured hold. A bone the character does not have (hand_r on a KayKit, which has handslot.r): the bone found by measuring the skeleton holds the item, and the game log says it once (attach: ... has no bone named ...).

items.title: The window in three parts (version 24, disposition_fenetre)
items.text:
• disposition_fenetre = grille (default, the window above, unchanged) or trois_parties: one window that fills the screen, as in Rust (Tab), Valheim or Enshrouded. Choose trois_parties for a survival game or an RPG (equipment, chests, bodies to search); keep grille for a small game with a few items.
  • Left (only with the equipement system): the slots the game defined in Equipment, as slots (not a list), in two columns on each side of an empty space for the character (espace_personnage, a share of the screen width, 0.14; 0 brings them together), the weapon slots at the bottom of each column (version 26: the slots spread over the whole height of the column, and the space goes from the top of the first slot to the bottom of the last one, with no slot in it). Dragging an item of the bag onto a slot wears it (equipement.porter), a click on a worn slot takes it off (equipement.retirer): the Equipment module does the rest, as always. Its own window (O) still works; it no longer opens beside the inventory (avec_inventaire) in this layout.
  • Centre: the bag (title with the slots used out of places, the weight if on), the grid (colonnes), the hotbar under it, separate (drag a bag slot onto it, drag it back onto the bag to empty that place; two bar slots swap), « Trier » (sorts by the categorie of sortes_objets, then kind, then name) and « Fermer ».
  • Right: what is searched when the player opens a chest or a body (everything that sends butin.ouvrir; the Loot module's own window then stays closed), with « Tout prendre » (role bouton.principal): dragging an item to the bag takes it (butin.prendre), dragging a bag slot onto it puts it in a chest (butin.ranger, chests only, with the chest's sharing rules). Otherwise the details of the chosen item: its name in its rarity's colour, description, bonuses (the inventaire.infobulle hook, so Equipment's comparison too), quantity, weight, and « Équiper » (bouton.principal, if equipable), « Diviser en deux », « Jeter » (bouton.danger). In this layout, a click on a slot shows its details instead of the small window, and the hover tooltip is not shown.
  • HUD keys: inventaire.fenetre, inventaire.gauche, inventaire.centre, inventaire.droite, inventaire.grille, inventaire.case.N, inventaire.fbarre.N, inventaire.equip.<slot>, inventaire.fouille.N, inventaire.fouille.tout, inventaire.trier, inventaire.equiper. Roles: fenetre.inventaire, titre.inventaire, case.inventaire, case.barre_rapide, case.equipement, case.rare, case.butin, fenetre.butin (the right column while searching), bouton.principal, bouton.danger.
  • Everything else stays: drop and split (Shift + drag), weight, stacks, unique copies, keys 1 to 9 (and 0, - and =; with two rows, inventaire.fbarre.13 to .24 under the first), gamepad (focus, A, B on « Fermer »), several players (each their own window; a guest's take or put goes through the host).
  • Behind the window, a dark veil over the whole screen (inventaire.voile, role fond.voile); dropping a dragged slot on it drops the item on the ground. A slot holding a rare-or-better copy (bag, hotbar of the window, searched content, worn slot) gets a thin frame in its rarity's colour (the one set in Loot's raretes), the panel <slot key>.cadre with role fond.case.rare: an interface pack with a case.rare row replaces it with its own image.
  • The character in the empty space (version 26, montrer_personnage, on): while the three-part window is open, the game camera turns toward the player's character, who stands in the empty space between the equipment slots, as in Baldur's Gate 3 or Diablo. The camera is made for it (game.spawn_camera), faces the character at the height of its centre, and its distance comes from the character's measured size (game.bounds) and the place of inventaire.personnage on screen: a 1 m or a 2.5 m character fills the space the same way. The character fills about 85 % of the space's height (of at most three times its width, on a narrow 4:3 screen, so that its shoulders do not go behind the slots) (framed on its height: a rest pose that is a T or an A pose makes its bounds wide, so its arms may go a little past the space rather than the character shrinking). On opening, the character is put at once in the rest state of its animation graph (its entry state, game.rest_pose), so it is never frozen mid-step, and its idle clip keeps playing while the window pauses the world. It glides there in 0.25 s and comes back to the player's camera (or to the placed camera that was active before) when the window closes, on death, on fenetres.fermer and on a scene change; the camera made is destroyed. The dark veil goes round that space, which stays clear; the window then has no background of a single block: each column has its own, and the left column's is drawn in pieces round the space (inventaire.fond.haut, .bas, .gauche, .droite). With an interface pack, they keep the window's look: their roles (fenetre.inventaire.equipement, fenetre.inventaire.sac, fenetre.inventaire.fiche) take the theme's fenetre.inventaire row. Online, each player sees their own character through their own camera, at home; nobody else sees a camera nor an object. Off, or with grille, or without Equipment: nothing changes. A wall right in front of the character can hide it: nothing moves the camera around it. Never write your own camera script for this: tick or untick the setting.
