items.title: Day and night
items.text:
Time goes by: the sun rises, crosses the sky and sets, then night falls, darker and bluish, and the day comes back. Broad daylight is the scene's light as you set it. The chosen lamps light up at night, and a clock can show. With the scene's realistic sky, it follows the sky's time, which then gives all the light.

Identifier jour_nuit Version 4 Placed on objects no

items.title: Settings for the whole game
items.text:
In the Systems panel (Developer mode), by opening the system's card.

Setting What it does Name in code Type Default Limits or choices Length of a whole day (minutes of play) How many minutes of play 24 hours of the world last, night included: 20 gives about 13 minutes of day and 7 of night with the default hours. 1440 follows real time. duree Number 20 from 1 to 1440 Time when the game starts The world's time when the game starts, from 0 to 24: 8 for the morning, 12 for noon, 22 to start at night. heure_depart Number 8 from 0 to 24 Sunrise (hour) The hour the sun appears on the horizon. The light rises during the first hour. With the realistic sky, sunrise and sunset pick the climate whose day length is the closest (except 6 and 20: the scene's climate). lever Number 6 from 0 to 24 Sunset (hour) The hour the sun disappears below the horizon. Night is the time between sunset and sunrise. coucher Number 20 from 0 to 24 Moonlight (share of the sun) The strength of the light in the middle of the night, as a share of the sun's at noon: 0.15 lets one see the way, 0 gives a pitch-black night where only lamps give light. With the realistic sky, it is the night darkness of Sky and weather. nuit_lumiere Number 0.15 from 0 to 1 Moonlight color The tint of the light at night: a pale blue by default. couleur_nuit Color #8ea6e0 Night sky The color of the sky and the horizon in the middle of the night, toward which the scene's sky darkens at dusk. ciel_nuit Color #0b1020 Rising and setting sun color The warm tint of the sun near the horizon, in the morning and the evening. It blends into the scene's sun color as it rises. couleur_aube Color #ff9a5c Tag of the lamps lit at night (empty: none) The placed lights carrying this tag, such as "lamp", light up at sunset and go out at sunrise: street lamps, torches, windows. lumieres Text (empty) Scenes without the cycle, separated by commas (interiors) The scenes where the light does not change, such as "Cave, Inn": an interior keeps its own. Time still goes by there. scenes_exclues Text (empty) Show the day and the time Shows at the top of the screen the world's day and time, such as "Day 2 — 07:30". horloge Yes or no no

items.title: Events
items.text: The descriptions come from the code.

items.title: What it announces
items.text: Event Fields Description jour_nuit.heure heure (number), jour (number) A new hour of the world started (0 to 23), on day jour (1 the first day). jour_nuit.lever jour (number) The sun rose: day jour begins. Lamps tagged for the night went out. jour_nuit.coucher jour (number) The sun set: night falls. Lamps tagged for the night lit up.

items.title: What it listens to
items.text: Event Fields Description jour_nuit.avancer heures (number) Ask the day and night system to move the clock on by heures (a night in a bed: 8). Every hour, sunrise and sunset crossed are announced in order. jour_nuit.aller_a heure (number) Ask the day and night system to move the clock on to the next time it is heure (0 to 24): sleep until 7, wait until night. scene.change depuis (text), vers (text) Sent by the engine once the player has arrived in another scene of the game (game.go_to, or a passage). Scripts keep running across scenes: this is when a module looks at the objects of the new scene. langue.change langue (text) Sent by the engine when the player changes the game's language (game.set_language, the Menu options). A module redraws what it already shows: its texts go through game.t and game.language. ciel.lever jour (number) Sent by the engine at sunrise, when the scene uses the realistic sky (Game settings, Sky and weather) and its hour moves (day_minutes above 0, or game.set_sky). jour is the day of the year. A jump made by game.set_sky sends nothing. ciel.coucher jour (number) Sent by the engine at sunset, when the scene uses the realistic sky and its hour moves. jour is the day of the year. ciel.heure heure (number), jour (number) Sent by the engine each time the realistic sky's hour reaches a whole hour (heure, 0 to 23), on day jour of the year.

items.title: What the agent knows about this system
items.text: The text the agent reads before using this system.

items.title: Day and night (jour_nuit)
items.text:
Time goes by in the world: the sun rises, crosses the sky and sets, night falls, darker and bluish, then the day comes back. Add it once with modules_add. Use it whenever the user asks for days and nights, a clock, nights that are dangerous: never write a sun script.

  • Broad daylight is the scene's own light (world_set: sun direction, color, intensity, sky): set the scene as it should look at noon, and the module only tilts and darkens it. The sun rises a quarter turn before its noon place and sets a quarter turn after.
  • With the realistic sky (sky_set enabled): set the hour and the length of a day here (heure_depart, duree), the rest in Sky and weather (sky_set: climate or place and date, night darkness, haze). There is then one clock, the sky's: the module gives it the start hour and the day length, and no longer sets the light (the sky gives the sun, the moon and the ambient light; nuit_lumiere, couleur_nuit, ciel_nuit and couleur_aube are not used). The clock, the lumieres lamps and the jour_nuit.* events follow game.sky() (the sky's sunrise and sunset). lever and coucher other than 6 and 20 pick the shipped climate whose day length, at its date, is the closest (a short winter day, a long summer one); with a place and date chosen in the advanced mode, they change nothing.
  • Game settings (modules_set): duree (minutes of play for 24 hours of the world, 20 by default), heure_depart (0 to 24: match the time of day the user chose; 12 at noon, 7 in the morning, 19 at sunset, 22 at night), lever and coucher (hours), nuit_lumiere (the moon's strength, a share of the sun: 0.15 lets one see, 0 is pitch black), couleur_nuit (moonlight), ciel_nuit (the night sky), couleur_aube (the warm sun at dawn and dusk), lumieres (a tag: the placed lights carrying it light up at sunset and go out at sunrise), scenes_exclues (scene names, separated by commas, where the light stays as set: interiors, caves; the title scene of the menu system (scene_titre) always keeps its own light, without being listed), horloge (shows « Day 2 — 07:30 » at the top).
  • Events announced: jour_nuit.heure (heure, jour), jour_nuit.lever (jour), jour_nuit.coucher (jour). React with a declencheur rule or a script: wolves come out at night, a shop closes. Send jour_nuit.avancer (heures) to move the clock on (a night in a bed: the besoins system's source does it with source_heures), jour_nuit.aller_a (heure) to skip to a time.
  • A script can read and change the light itself with game.environment() and game.set_environment({...}) (a storm); with this module and without the realistic sky, change the scene's light with world_set instead, or the module overrides it on the next step. With the realistic sky, the module never sets the light: change the sky with sky_set, or game.set_sky in a script.
  • Saved games: game.save keeps the day and the time, and the engine keeps the light; game.load gives them back. Nothing to write.
  • In a large world, time goes by the same everywhere; lights tagged for the night switch even far away.
  • The clock is the screen « Horloge » delivered by the system (shape Heure, HUD key Horloge/Heure), which the user restyles in the screen editor. Never draw a clock yourself, and do not name another screen « Horloge ».
  • Testing: check the events in game_run (jour_nuit.coucher after the right number of steps: with duree 20, one hour of the world is 50 seconds of play), or log game.environment().sun_intensity from a test script; capture_steps shows the light at those steps (start the game at the hour to see with heure_depart).

items.title: Several players
items.text:
One for the whole game: the time of day, the sun and the clock are the same for everyone.

This page is generated automatically from the WorldMint code (modules/jour_nuit/module.json, modules/jour_nuit/AGENT.md, modules/events.json): it always matches the editor.

items.title: Round
items.text:
How a game with several players unfolds, without code: everyone at their starting place, frozen during "3, 2, 1, Go!", a stopwatch or a time limit, an end (everyone arrived, a score reached, only one left standing), a ranking, and each player sees their own result. On time, on points or last one standing, alone or in teams, in one or several rounds. Placed on an object, it makes it a starting place.

Identifier manche Version 4 Placed on objects yes

items.title: Settings for the whole game
items.text:
In the Systems panel (Developer mode), by opening the system's card.

Setting What it does Name in code Type Default Limits or choices Ranking On time: the first to arrive wins (the arrival comes from the Race, a zone or a script); the round ends when everyone has arrived or at the time limit, those who did not finish are ranked by how far they got. On points: the first to reach the target score wins, or whoever has the most points at the time limit. Last one standing: a player with no life left is out; the round ends when only one is left. mode Choice in a list On time (first to arrive) temps: On time (first to arrive)points: On points (a score to reach)dernier: Last one standing Time limit (s) How long a round lasts, in seconds, shown to everyone as the time left. At the limit, the round stops and everyone is ranked where they are. 0: no limit, a stopwatch counts the time spent. limite Number 0 from 0 to 36 000 Countdown (s) The seconds of "3, 2, 1, Go!" at the start of each round; players cannot move during it. 0: immediate start. compte Number 3 from 0 to 30, as a whole number Before the first round At once: the countdown starts as soon as the game starts. A number of players: wait until they are there. The host: they see a "Start the game" button, the others wait. A script can also start the game with the event manche.lancer. attente Choice in a list Start at once aucune: Start at oncejoueurs: Wait for a number of playershote: The host starts the game (a button) Players to wait forshown only if Before the first round is “Wait for a number of players” The game starts as soon as this many players are in the game. joueurs_min Number 2 from 1 to 64, as a whole number Score to reachshown only if Ranking is “On points (a score to reach)” The first player (or team) to reach this score wins the round. Points come from the event manche.points: the Trigger, a script or another system gives them. score_cible Number 10 from 1 to 1 000 000 Lives per roundshown only if Ranking is “Last one standing” Each death (the Health system) costs a life; with no life left, the player is out and watches the end. Between lives, they respawn as the Death system says if it is there, else at their starting place. The event manche.eliminer also puts a player out. vies Number 1 from 1 to 99, as a whole number Teams In teams: the ranking and the victory count per team (on time, the best place of its players; on points, the sum; last one standing, the last team with a player left). Shared out: each arriving player joins the smallest team. Chosen: a menu or a script sends manche.equipe; whoever chose nothing is shared out at the start. equipes_mode Choice in a list Every player for themselves seul: Every player for themselvesequilibrees: In teams, shared out on arrivalchoix: In teams, chosen by the game The teamsshown only if Teams is “In teams, shared out on arrival” or “In teams, chosen by the game” Two teams or more, each with its name and color. equipes List of “Team” [{'nom': 'Rouges', 'couleur': '#e0574f'}, {'nom': 'Bleus', 'couleur': '#4f86e0'}] one line per “Team”: its fields Number of rounds 1: a single round. More: the game is played in this many rounds, or until this many wins (the next setting). manches Number 1 from 1 to 99, as a whole number End of the game In N rounds: every round is played, the most wins wins (on a tie, the best places). First to N wins: the game stops as soon as a player or a team has won N rounds. manches_mode Choice in a list In N rounds (most wins wins) nombre: In N rounds (most wins wins)victoires: First to N wins Board between rounds (s) How many seconds the score board stays on screen before everyone goes back to their starting place for a new countdown. tableau_duree Number 5 from 1 to 60 Stopwatch, rank and score on screen At the top of each player's screen: their stopwatch or the time left, their place, their points or lives, their team. The countdown and the board are always shown. afficher Yes or no yes Height of the banner (old) No longer used: the banner is now the screen "Bandeau de la partie". To move it down (when the row of the Temporary effects system already uses the top), move its shape "Fond" in the screen editor. Kept for the games that had set it. hud_y Number 0.015 from 0 to 0.9

items.title: The fields of each “Team”
items.text:
In the Properties, each “Team” has its own numbered frame; Add: Team adds one, the cross removes it. A field only appears when it is useful: under its name, the table says when.

Setting What it does Name in code Type Default Limits or choices Name The team's name, shown on screen and in the ranking. nom Text (empty) Color The team's color on screen. couleur Color #ffffff

items.title: Settings on each object
items.text:
In the Properties of an object or folder that carries the system, Systems section. A folder passes its values on to what it contains; an object can change a value for itself only.

Setting What it does Name in code Type Default Limits or choices Starting place: number The order of the starting places: the first player takes 1, the second 2... 0: after the numbered ones, in scene order. The player is set there, facing like the object. place Number 0 from 0 to 64, as a whole number Starting place: team A team's name: the place goes to its players first. Empty: for anyone. equipe Text (empty)

items.title: Events
items.text: The descriptions come from the code.

items.title: What it announces
items.text: Event Fields Description manche.nouvelle numero (number), total (number) A round is set up (Round module): every player is at their starting place, frozen during the countdown. numero counts from 1; total is the setting manches. The Race resets its laps here. manche.depart numero (number), total (number) The countdown is over: Go! (Round module). The stopwatch of the round starts now. manche.resultat joueur (id), temps (number?), rang (number?), elimine (boolean?) A player's round result is known (Round module): they arrived (temps in seconds since Go, rang their place), or they are out (elimine). manche.fin numero (number), total (number), classement (table), raison (text), gagnant (text?) A round ended (Round module). classement: the ranking, best first, a list of rows {joueur or equipe, nom, rang, temps?, points, vies, progression, elimine, arrive}; gagnant: the first's player id or team name; raison: arrivee, limite, score or dernier. manche.terminee classement (table), gagnant (text?) The whole game ended (Round module), after the last round: classement is the final ranking (with victoires when there were several rounds). Each player's result is shown by game.finish. sante.ranimer cible (id), part (number?), montant (number?), invulnerabilite (number?) Ask the health module to bring an object back to life, even dead: part (0 to 1 of its maximum, all by default) or montant (points), then invulnerabilite seconds without losing health. Sent by the death and respawn module.

items.title: What it listens to
items.text: Event Fields Description manche.lancer — Ask the Round module to start the game now (a menu's Start button, a script), when its setting attente waits for players or for the host. Without effect once started. manche.arrivee joueur (id) A player arrived (the Race at the end of the last lap, a zone or a script): the Round module notes their time. Counts once per round. manche.progression joueur (id), valeur (number) How far a player got, a number that grows as they advance (the Race: laps and checkpoints passed, then the share of the way to the next). The Round module ranks those who have not arrived by it. manche.points joueur (id?), equipe (text?), points (number?) Give points to a player or a team (Round module, ranking on points): from the Trigger, a script or another system. points may be negative; 1 by default. equipe is a team's name or number. manche.eliminer joueur (id) Put a player out of the round (Round module): they are ranked after those still in, and see Out on screen. manche.equipe joueur (id), equipe (text) Put a player in a team (Round module, teams chosen by the game): equipe is the team's name or number. Takes effect at the next round's setup for the starting places. sante.mort cible (id), source (id?) An object's health reached zero. What happens next belongs to the game: the health module does nothing else, unless its setting says to destroy the object. joueur.reapparu joueur (id), cible (id), position (vector) A dead player stands up again (death and respawn module): respawned, or brought back by sante.ranimer. joueur.arrivee joueur (id), numero (number), nom (text) Sent by the engine, in a game with several players (the game setting Multiplayer), on the computer hosting the game, when a guest joins: joueur is their character (a copy of the player's), numero their place (1 to 7, the host being 0), nom the name they chose. game.players() lists them all. Scripts only run on the host. joueur.depart joueur (id), numero (number) Sent by the engine on the host when a guest leaves the game (they quit, or their connection was lost and they did not come back in time, the game setting Place kept after a drop): their character is removed right after. A module forgets what it kept for them. langue.change langue (text) Sent by the engine when the player changes the game's language (game.set_language, the Menu options). A module redraws what it already shows: its texts go through game.t and game.language. menu.jouer — The player left the title screen with Play: the game really starts. For an intro message, a music, a timer that should not run behind the title.

items.title: Points a script can replace (game.override)
items.text:
The descriptions come from the code.

  • manche.texte: function(default, key, joueur) -> the text shown for that key: attente, attente_hote, lancer, partez, arrive, elimine, reste, points, vies, rang, manche, classement, victoire, place, defaite, temps, gagne, gagnent, victoires, pas_arrive (some hold {n}, {total}, {nom}...). joueur is the player who will read it (nil: everyone). The default is the built-in text in the game's language.
  • manche.points: function(default, qui, points) -> the points really given (a number; 0: none). qui is a player id, or a team's name. For double points in the last minute, or points refused to a player.
  • manche.classement: function(default, classement) -> the ranking, a list of rows {joueur or equipe, nom, temps?, points, vies, progression, elimine, arrive}, best first. Called each time the ranking is made (on screen, at the end of a round). Reorder it for a rule of your own.

items.title: What the agent knows about this system
items.text: The text the agent reads before using this system.

items.title: Round (manche)
items.text:
How a game with several players unfolds (ADR-045): starting places, a frozen countdown "3, 2, 1, Go!", a stopwatch or a time limit, an end, a ranking, and each player sees their own result. For a race, an arena, a party game, a team match or any "first to..." game, add this module instead of scripting a countdown, a timer, an end or a ranking yourself. For checkpoints and laps add course too (it requires this one).

  • Starting places: objects carrying this system (systems_attach manche on an invisible marker or a pad at ground level, values place: 1, 2, 3... and equipe: a team's name, empty for anyone). Each player is set there, facing like the object (entities_update its rotation). Without any, players start where they are. More players than places: next to them.
  • Before the first round (attente): aucune (the countdown starts at once), joueurs (wait for joueurs_min players), hote (the host sees a "Start the game" button, the others "The host will start the game"). A script or a menu can start it: game.emit("manche.lancer", {}).
  • With the menu title screen (ecran_titre): the round follows the menu. Title screen → Play (or Host a game) → the waiting room of this system (the waiting text, and « Start the game » for the host) → the countdown. Nothing of the round shows and nothing starts while the title screen is open (menu.jouer ends it). While the pause menu is open, the Start button goes away and comes back when it closes. Never add another start button.
  • Countdown (compte, 3 s): players cannot move (speed 0, no jump; one pushed or sliding is put back at their place). Then "Go!" and manche.depart.
  • Ranking (mode):
  • temps: the first to arrive wins. The arrival is game.emit("manche.arrivee", {joueur = id}): from the course module, or from your own script on a finish zone (zone.entree with e.joueur). The round ends when everyone arrived or at limite; those who did not arrive are ranked by manche.progression {joueur, valeur} (any growing number: the race sends it).
  • points: game.emit("manche.points", {joueur = id, points = 1}) (or equipe = "Rouges"), from the Trigger (declencheur, action "event") or a script; the first at score_cible wins, else the most points at limite.
  • dernier: last one standing. Each death (the sante system on the player) costs one of vies; with no life left the player is out (lying down until the next round) and sees "Out". game.emit("manche.eliminer", {joueur = id}) puts one out directly (fell off the arena). With the mort module, it respawns players between lives; without it, the round raises them at their starting place.
  • Teams (equipes_mode): seul, equilibrees (each arriving player joins the smallest team) or choix (a menu sends manche.equipe {joueur, equipe}; those who chose nothing are shared out at the start). equipes: list of {nom, couleur}. The ranking and the win count per team: on time the best place of its players, on points the sum, last one standing the last team with someone left. All the winning team sees "Victory".
  • Time limit (limite, seconds, 0: none): each player sees the time left, else their own stopwatch (it stops at their arrival).
  • Several rounds (manches, manches_mode): nombre (in N rounds, most wins wins) or victoires (first to N wins). Between rounds the board (tableau_duree s), then everyone back to their starting place and a new countdown (manche.nouvelle).
  • Its screens (delivered as data, modules/manche/ecrans, one screen per moment, no shape shared; each player sees their own): "Lancer la partie" (the host's button Bouton Lancer, action lancer), "Attente des joueurs" (Message: the wait, or "The host will start the game" for a guest), "Compte à rebours" (Chiffre), "Départ" (Partez), "Annonces" (Éliminé, Arrivé), "Bandeau de la partie" (Chrono, Place in gold, Info: points, lives or team, optional; Course: the Race's line, optional), "Tableau entre deux manches" (Titre, the list Lignes with its row Ligne, Suite) and "Classement final" (Titre, Lignes/Ligne; drawn above the end screen's veil). Change their look with styles and the theme in the screen editor, never by editing the system or its script; the script fills their texts (game.screen_set, game.screen_list).
  • On screen (each player their own, afficher): the banner at the top centre on a dark translucent background: the stopwatch or time left and the place "2nd / 4" in gold, then the points or lives (in teams on points: every team's score in its color, "Rouges 6 · Bleus 4 / 10"), and the race's lap and checkpoint; in the middle, each on its own screen, the countdown, "Go!", "Finished! 1st" or "Out"; the board between rounds. hud_y no longer moves the banner: move the shape "Fond" of "Bandeau de la partie" in the screen editor (when something else uses the top, such as the row of alterations at y 0.07).
  • The end: each player gets their own result through game.finish (Victory, their place, their time or points); the full ranking stays on everyone's screen, under the end title and above its darkening (an element whose role ends with .fin, or inside a panel that has one, is drawn over the engine's end screen: a game's own end board can do the same). manche.terminee {classement, gagnant}.
  • Events for the game: manche.nouvelle {numero, total}, manche.depart {numero}, manche.resultat {joueur, temps?, rang?, elimine?}, manche.fin {numero, classement, raison, gagnant} (each round), manche.terminee. React to them in your scripts (a sound at Go, fireworks for the winner).
  • Change a rule without touching the module (game.override): manche.texte (any text: function(default, cle, joueur) if cle == "partez" then return "Allez !" end return default(cle, joueur) end), manche.points (double points at the end, points refused), manche.classement (reorder the ranking for your own rule).
  • It sets players' speed and jump during the countdown and back to normal at Go: do not fight it with game.set_player_speed in the same moments.

items.title: Several players
items.text:
One for the whole game, on the host: it decides arrivals, points, eliminations and the end; each player (guests included) sees their own stopwatch, place, score and result. A guest who joins during the countdown gets a place and is frozen like the others; one who joins later plays from there. Prove it with game_run « players »: the report shows each guest's HUD (Bandeau de la partie/Chrono, Bandeau de la partie/Place).

This page is generated automatically from the WorldMint code (modules/manche/module.json, modules/manche/AGENT.md, modules/events.json): it always matches the editor.

items.title: Menu
items.text:
The title screen when the game starts, and the pause with Escape: Resume, Options (in sections: sound, display with the graphics and, for a translated game, the language, controls), Quit. The game stops while the menu is open, and it takes the look of the Interface system. A game with the Multiplayer setting also has Host and Join there.

Identifier menu Version 19 Placed on objects no

items.title: Settings for the whole game
items.text:
In the Systems panel (Developer mode), by opening the system's card.

Setting What it does Name in code Type Default Limits or choices Title screen at start Ticked: the game opens on a screen with its title and a Play button, the world stopped behind it. Unticked: play starts at once. ecran_titre Yes or no yes Title screen scene (none: the game's scene behind) A scene of your game is the backdrop of the title screen: a garage with the car, a campfire, the character in the spotlight. The player does not move there and nothing of the game runs there. Play leads to the game's start scene. None: the title screen shows over the start scene, stopped. scene_titre Game scene (empty) Camera of the title screen scene (optional) The name of a camera placed in the title screen scene: the backdrop is seen through it. Empty: that scene's start camera, otherwise its first placed camera. camera_titre Text (empty) Title shown (empty: the game's) The big title of the title screen. Empty: the game's title, set in the game settings, Window section. titre Text (empty) Subtitle (optional) A smaller line under the title of the title screen: a tagline, "Chapter 1", the studio's name. Empty: no subtitle. sous_titre Text (empty) Logo (empty: the title as text) An image of the project shown instead of the title text, on the title screen. It keeps its proportions: it is never stretched. An image with a transparent background (PNG) works best. logo Image from the library (empty) Background image (empty: the game world behind) A picture that covers the whole title screen. It is never distorted: if the screen does not have its proportions, its edges are cut off. Empty: the game world shows, stopped, behind the menu. Use a wide picture (1920 × 1080 or more) and keep the subject in the middle. fond Image from the library (empty) Layout of the title screen and the pause Where the title and the buttons go. Centered: for farming, party games. On the left: for shooters, racing, strategy, survival, role-playing games; the scene stays visible on the right, the menu side is darker. At the bottom: for a story or a puzzle game; the middle of the picture stays clear. disposition Choice in a list Centered: title at the top, buttons in the middle centre: Centered: title at the top, buttons in the middlegauche: On the left: title and buttons on the left, the scene on the rightbas: At the bottom: title at the top, buttons at the bottom Controls bar at the bottom of the screen Ticked: a strip at the bottom of the title screen and the pause recalls the menu's keys ("Enter Select · Esc Back" on the keyboard, "A Select · B Back" on a gamepad). It follows the device the player uses. barre_touches Yes or no yes Pause with Escape Ticked: the Pause control (Escape, or Start on a gamepad) stops the game and opens the Resume, Options, Quit menu. It closes it too. pause Yes or no yes Options button: volumes, graphics and controls Adds an Options button: the player sets the master volume and that of each sound mixer group there (music, effects, ambience, voice, interface…), chooses the graphics (the quality, Low, Medium or High, particles included; the upscaling and its method, None, FSR (all cards) or DLSS if you provided it; ray tracing, Automatic, On or Off, if their card has it and the game allows it, and its indirect lighting, the light bounced by surfaces in Medium and High quality), changes the key of each control and, if the game is translated, chooses their language. The player finds these choices again the next time the game starts; the game's own settings do not change. options Yes or no yes Quit button Adds a Quit button, which closes the game. quitter Yes or no yes Host and Join buttons (multiplayer game) In a game with the Multiplayer setting (game settings): the title screen and the pause have Host a game and Join a game (you type the host's address, and your name, seen by the other players and kept for the next time). The host's pause then says how many guests are there, and lets them stop the online game. Without the Multiplayer setting, these buttons do not show. en_ligne Yes or no yes Short code for the hosted game When a player hosts a game, WorldMint's game service gives it a short code ("K7P-2QMX") to give to friends: they type it in Join, Code tab, instead of the address. The code goes away when the game stops. Without the service, the game still works, by address. salon_code Yes or no yes Hosted game in the public list When a player hosts a game, it shows in the list of this game's games (Join, List tab), seen by every player of the game. Left off, only those with the code or the address find it. salon_public Yes or no no Connection path and ping (guests) In the pause of a player who joined a game: a discreet line says how they are linked to the host ("Direct connection", "Connection through the relay", slower, or "Connection by address") and their ping in milliseconds. Unticked, the line does not show. connexion Yes or no yes Simple character creation screen (multiplayer game) When a player joins a world where they have no character yet (game setting "Players' characters"), the menu shows them a simple screen before they enter: their character's name, then Enter. Their choices go to the host, who checks them; if refused, the reason shows and they fix it. Untick it if your game has its own creation screen (it listens to "profil.demande" and sends the choices with game.profile_send). creation_personnage Yes or no yes Darkening of the game behind the menu (0: none, 1: black) How much the stopped game darkens behind the menu: 0 leaves it as it is, 1 hides it completely. voile Number 0.55 from 0 to 1

items.title: What it announces
items.text: Event Fields Description menu.jouer — The player left the title screen with Play: the game really starts. For an intro message, a music, a timer that should not run behind the title. menu.pause ouvert (boolean) The pause menu opened (ouvert true) or closed (ouvert false). The world is stopped while it is open.

items.title: What it listens to
items.text: Event Fields Description hud.clic cible (text), joueur (id?) A button of the HUD was clicked: pressed, then released on it; or chosen with A (Enter) while it has the gamepad or keyboard focus; or the window's back button (back = true), with B (Escape). cible is the button's key (game.hud_button), joueur the player who clicked (a guest clicks on their own computer; the host plays the click). Announced by the engine, before the scripts' on_update of that step. profil.demande essai (number), raison (text), propose (table?) Sent by the engine in the game of a player who is joining (before entering, while their own scripts still run: the title screen, the Menu), when the host wants them to create their character because they have none in this world (game setting Players' characters, ADR-020 § 18). essai is 0 the first time, then the number of refused tries; raison the game's text explaining the last refusal (translate it with game.t); propose the look kept on this PC (setting Same look everywhere), to offer in advance. The creation screen sends the choices with game.profile_send(table). scene.change depuis (text), vers (text) Sent by the engine once the player has arrived in another scene of the game (game.go_to, or a passage). Scripts keep running across scenes: this is when a module looks at the objects of the new scene.

items.title: What the agent knows about this system
items.text: The text the agent reads before using this system.

items.title: Menu (menu)
items.text:
The title screen when the game starts, and the pause menu with Escape: Resume, Options (the master volume and one volume per group of the sound mixer: music, effects, ambience, voice, ui and the game's own groups; the graphics; a new key for every control), Quit. Add it once with modules_add; it is for the whole game, not placed on objects. Use it whenever the user wants a title screen, a pause or an options menu: do not write one in a script.

  • The world stops while the menu is open (game.pause): the player, enemies, physics, animations and game.time. The menu takes the look of the interface system: change the style there, not here.
  • Game settings (modules_set): ecran_titre (title screen at start), titre (the title shown; empty: the game's title from the game settings, Window), pause (Escape opens the pause menu), options and quitter (show those buttons), voile (how dark the stopped game gets behind the menu, 0 to 1).
  • Look of the title screen and the pause (settings disposition, fond, logo, sous_titre, barre_touches); the Options screen keeps its own window:
  • disposition follows the family of the game, like the games players know. gauche (title at the top left, the buttons in a column under it, the scene alive on the right, the menu side darker): shooters, racing, strategy, survival, role-playing games. centre (the default: title and buttons in a window in the middle, the world behind): farming, party games. bas (title at the top, the buttons in a row at the bottom, the middle of the picture left clear; a short column at the bottom when there are Host and Join): a story, a puzzle game. For a role-playing game played online, the simple character creation screen (creation_personnage) is already there.
  • fond: a picture that covers the whole title screen (and the screens opened from it), cropped to the screen, never stretched: it keeps its middle on 4:3 and very wide screens. Empty: the stopped game world shows behind (the usual choice when the scene is worth seeing). Pick a wide image (1920 × 1080 or more) with its subject in the middle. logo: an image shown instead of the title text, with its proportions (a transparent PNG). sous_titre: a smaller line under the title (translated with the game's tables). Find images with assets_search and kind image, then modules_set menu with the path; never guess a file name. A missing file falls back to the world and the title text.
  • barre_touches (on by default): a strip at the bottom recalls the menu's keys on the device the player uses: « Entrée Choisir · Échap Retour » on the keyboard, « A Choisir · B Retour » on a gamepad (Retour only where a button goes back: the pause, Join). These are the engine's menu keys (Enter or A clicks, Escape or B goes back); they cannot be rebound. Its words are texts of the menu: choisir, retour, touche_entree, touche_echap, touche_a, touche_b (hook « menu.texte »).
  • The title screen and the pause are screens the system delivers (screens_get): « Écran titre » and « Pause », one of each in the game. Their shapes: Fenêtre (the window), Voile, Titre, Logo, Sous-titre, Version (the title screen), Bouton Jouer or Bouton Reprendre, Bouton Options, Groupe en ligne (Libellé du nom, Nom du joueur, Bouton Héberger, Bouton Rejoindre), Partie en ligne, Code de la partie, Bouton Arrêter en ligne, Connexion (a guest's pause), Erreur, Bouton Quitter, Barre des touches (Touches); En-tête and Bande (gauche), Bas de l'écran and Rangée des boutons (bas). Their HUD keys are « Écran titre/Bouton Jouer », « Pause/Bouton Reprendre »… (click Play in game_run with {"frames": 3, "click": "Écran titre/Bouton Jouer"}). The menu's script shows them, fills their texts and hides what the settings remove (Options, Quit, the online group…): change their look with screens_set like any screen (a style, a place, a size), never their names. disposition installs the screen's model for that layout (centre, gauche, bas): changing the setting replaces the screen, unless the user modified it; then it keeps its own layout and modules_set says so (screens_kept).
  • Styles for a UI pack (interface system, habillage): Play and Resume are bouton.principal, Quit is bouton.danger, the window fenetre.menu, the title titre.menu, the key strip panneau.touches, the veil fond.voile, the band fond.bande, the version texte.version (« Version 1.0.4 », small at the bottom right of the title screen; only when the game has a version: game settings, Publication, world_set window.version; text « version » of the menu). A style without a row of the theme takes its kind (bouton, panneau): nothing changes without a pack.
  • « Rejoindre » and « Personnage » are delivered screens too. « Rejoindre »: Titre, Onglets (Onglet Liste, Onglet Code, Onglet Adresse), Ligne de recherche (Recherche, Bouton Actualiser), Salon (what the game service says), Serveurs (a list: one Serveur row per server, keys « Rejoindre/Serveur#1 »…), Code, Adresse, Mot de passe requis, Mot de passe, Nom du joueur, Connexion, Erreur, Bouton Rejoindre, Bouton Retour. « Personnage »: Titre, Refus, Nom du personnage, Attente, Bouton Entrer, Erreur. Both have Voile and Barre des touches.
  • « Options » is a delivered screen too: Titre, Onglets (Onglet Son, Onglet Affichage, Onglet Touches), Contenu (it takes the height of the open section up to half the screen, then scrolls) with three lists: Volumes (rows Nom du volume, Moins, Volume, Plus: « Options/Moins#1 » is the master volume, then each mixer group), Choix (rows Nom du choix, Valeur: the graphics, Quality first) and Commandes (rows Nom de la commande, Touche), plus Ligne de langue (Langue), Graphismes, Ray tracing lourd, Ray tracing coupé, Ligne de lumière (Lumière), Aide de la lumière, Aide de l'occlusion, Aide and Bouton Retour. The menu's script draws nothing with game.hud_* any more: all its screens are delivered.
  • Texts follow the player's language: the menu's own texts (Play, Options, Graphics...) are built-in texts of the system, listed by translations_get like the game's texts. Translate them there for every language the game offers; without a translation, the menu shows its French or English text. For a translated game (world_set languages), Options shows a Language row: each click moves to the next offered language, and the game remembers it. The titre setting is translated with the game's tables. To change a word, override menu.texte from a game script: game.override("menu.texte", function(default, key) if key == "jouer" then return "Commencer" end return default(key) end).
  • Options are arranged in sections, one tab each (Options/Onglet Son, Options/Onglet Affichage, Options/Onglet Touches): Sound (the volumes), Display (the language of a translated game and the graphics; only when there is something to choose) and Controls (the keys). A section taller than half the screen scrolls inside the window, which never overflows, however many sound groups or controls the game has. In game_run, click a tab before the rows of its section: only the open section is in the report's hud.
  • Graphics, in Options (Display section), for a game on screen: Quality (Low, Medium, High or Ultra: shadows, lights, water, glow, terrain and plant distances, and the particles budget; the machine chooses at first, Low on an integrated chip, High on a graphics card), Upscaling (Off, anti-aliasing only, Quality 67 %, Balanced 58 %, Performance 50 %, Ultra performance 33 %; the game's own window.upscaling at first), Shadows (As quality at first, then High, Medium, Low, Off: for the sun and every light, effects' lights included; Off removes every shadow, the lightest; over the scene's shadowQuality), the upscaling method (None, FSR on every card, and DLSS (NVIDIA) only when the user provided NVIDIA's files and turned DLSS on in the game settings (Game window), on an RTX card; shown only when FSR or DLSS works there); Ray tracing (Automatic, On, Off) only on a graphics card that has it, when the game allows it (« ray_tracing » in world_set window, allowed by default). Automatic draws shadows and reflections with rays only on a dedicated graphics card in Medium and High quality; On forces it, with a short warning under the line where it is heavy (an integrated chip, Low quality); when the graphics card's memory is full, the game turns rays off by itself (classic shadows) and a short line under it says so, until the player picks another value. Under it, Indirect lighting (On at first, or Off; shape Options/Lumière, with a short line saying what it does): the light bounced by surfaces, ray traced, only in High quality (about 1 to 2 ms). Don't draw what is hidden (Automatic, On, Off; a row of Choix, with a short line Aide de l'occlusion saying what it does): objects fully behind buildings are not drawn; Automatic follows the game's own choice (world_set detail.occlusion), whose Automatic is on in Medium and High quality and off in Low; On or Off wins over the game's choice. Each click moves to the next value, at once. The menu uses game.graphics and game.set_graphics: a game script can call them too, but never alongside the menu's options. Not shown in game_run without capture: nothing is drawn there.
  • The player's choices in Options (the volume of each sound group, the graphics and the keys and gamepad buttons they changed) are kept from one launch of the game to the next, in the save slot menu-options: the exported game keeps it with the player's saves, the editor with the saves of its test runs. The game settings and the project are never changed by it. Do not use that slot name in a game script; game.delete_save("menu-options") gives the player the game's own volumes, graphics and keys back at the next launch. A control the game no longer has is forgotten. In game_run, saves start empty: every run begins with the game's own volumes, graphics and keys.
  • A title scene (setting scene_titre, a scene of the game; camera_titre, the name of a placed camera of that scene, optional): the title screen shows over its own backdrop, as many games do (the car in a garage, a campfire at night, the character in the light), with a very light veil. The game opens there from its start scene, through that scene's camera (camera_titre, else the scene's start camera, else its first placed camera); the player is hidden there and controls nothing, the game's HUD is hidden. Play (and Host a game) leads to the game's start scene through the usual scene change, with its fade, and menu.jouer is sent once arrived there. Host a game opens the game to guests only once the host is in the start scene: a guest who joins arrives there, never in the title scene. A test run started in the editor from another scene goes straight to that level; started from the title scene, it shows it. A scene_titre that is not a scene of the game: the title screen shows over the start scene as without it, and the game's log says why. Make it with the recipe of scenes.md (Title screen scene). The game's systems started in the start scene: in the title scene, nothing starts before Play (the hotbar and timers are hidden, manche waits for menu.jouer); jour_nuit leaves the title scene with its own light, and the game's music (sons) plays over it. The pause stays the pause: there is no way back to the title scene during a game.
  • The title screen shows only the menu, over the world: the engine hides the rest of the HUD (the hotbar, a timer, the game's drawn screens) while it is open (game.hud_only("menu."); the report marks those elements hidden), and shows it again on Play. The pause leaves the game's HUD visible behind its veil.
  • With manche: title screen → Play (or Host a game) → the round's waiting room (« Start the game » for the host) → the countdown. Never add a start button of your own.
  • menu.jouer is sent when the player leaves the title screen: start an intro, a timer or a music on it rather than in on_start, which runs behind the title. A declencheur rule can use it too ("when the event menu.jouer"). menu.pause (ouvert) is sent when the pause menu opens or closes.
  • In game_run, the title screen waits for a click on Play: show nothing else first. The report's hud gives the area of menu.jouer; click its centre with mouse and buttons (a short segment with left, then one without). Turn ecran_titre off only if the user does not want a title screen.
  • A segment {"frames": 3, "click": "menu.jouer"} clicks Play by its key, without reading its area. With « players » (several players), only the host has the title screen: click Play in the host's inputs; the simulated players are guests and play their own inputs at once.
  • Gamepad and keyboard: with a gamepad, Play (or Resume) has the focus at once; the d-pad or the arrows move it, A or Enter clicks, B or Escape goes back from the options and closes the pause (Resume and Back are the window's back buttons). While a key is being changed in the options, the menu turns the engine's navigation off (game.hud_navigation(false)), so that A, B and the arrows can be bound too.
  • The screens « Écran titre », « Pause », « Options », « Rejoindre » and « Personnage » are the menu's: do not use these screen names, nor the HUD prefix menu., in a game script.

items.title: Several players
items.text: One copy per player: in a game hosted online, a menu does not stop the game. A guest has no title screen (they join a game already running) and no options (their sound, display and keys belong to their own computer): only Resume and Quit, and Quit makes them leave the game.

items.title: Host and Join (several players)
items.text:
In a game with the « Multiplayer » setting, the title screen and the pause have « Host a game » and « Join a game » (setting « en_ligne », on by default). Join opens a screen with three tabs: List (the public servers of this game and version, from WorldMint's lobby service: name, players n/max, « [password] » when locked; a search field and Refresh), Code (the short code a host gives, such as K7P-2QMX) and Address (the host's address). A password field shows when the chosen server is locked, or after a server refused with « mot de passe manquant ou faux ». While the lobby service is not set up or does not answer, List and Code say so and Address still works. A refusal shows there; a player with another version of the game than the host reads both numbers (« L'hôte a la version 1.0.4, vous avez la 1.0.3 : mettez votre jeu à jour », texts erreur_update_needed and erreur_host_outdated). While hosting, the pause says how many guests are there, the game's short code if it has one, and has « Stop the online game ». Settings « salon_code » (on: a hosted game gets a short code) and « salon_public » (off: a hosted game is not in the public list). On the title screen and the pause the buttons go Play (or Resume), Options, then the online group (the label « Your name (seen by the other players) », the name field, « Host a game », « Join a game »), then Quit. The « Your name » field (pseudo) sits right above « Host a game » and on the Join screen: the same field and the same name kept on this PC (game.network().player_name prefills it). A player's name everywhere (chat, « X joined », game.player_name) is their character's name (the « nom » sent by the character screen), else this name, else « Joueur N ». They call game.host({public, code, name}), game.join(address, password?, name?), game.join_code(code, password?), game.find_servers(text?) and game.leave_online; only the game on screen does it (in game_run, game.network() says available=false and the buttons do not show). Texts: heberger, rejoindre, adresse, rejoindre_ok, connexion, en_ligne, hors_ligne, echec, onglet_liste, onglet_code, onglet_adresse, code, mot_de_passe, recherche, actualiser, recherche_en_cours, aucun_serveur, joueurs, cadenas, salon_absent, salon_injoignable, mot_de_passe_requis, recherche_code, code_partie (hook « menu.texte »).

This page is generated automatically from the WorldMint code (modules/menu/module.json, modules/menu/AGENT.md, modules/events.json): it always matches the editor.

items.title: Death and respawn
items.text:
What happens to the player at zero health: they fall (an animation of their character, if chosen), control nothing, see a death screen, then respawn (at the start, at the last respawn point or where they fell) or the game ends. Placed on an object, it makes it a respawn point. Needs Health.

Identifier mort Version 2 Placed on objects yes Also activates Health

items.title: Settings for the whole game
items.text:
In the Systems panel (Developer mode), by opening the system's card.

Setting What it does Name in code Type Default Limits or choices Death animation (a clip of your character) The clip the player plays when dying, chosen among their character's clips, whatever the pack. It plays once, and the body stays on its last frame until respawn. Empty: the player stops, standing, with no animation of its own. animation Player animation (empty) After death Button: the player chooses when to respawn. Automatic: they respawn after the delay. Game over: the "Game over" screen; the game stops when no player is left alive. apres Choice in a list A "Respawn" button bouton: A "Respawn" buttonauto: Automatic respawnfin: Game over (no respawn) Delay before respawn (s) Automatic: the seconds before respawning, counted on screen. Button: the seconds before the button shows (0: at once). Game over: the seconds before the game stops. delai Number 5 from 0 to 600 Where to respawn A respawn point is an object carrying this system (a sleeping bag, a campfire): it counts as soon as the player comes near. With no point reached, the player respawns where they entered the game. lieu Choice in a list At the last respawn point (else at the start) point: At the last respawn point (else at the start)depart: At the starting pointsur_place: Where they fell Health given back How to count the health the player respawns with. vie_mode Choice in a list A share of maximum health (%) part: A share of maximum health (%)nombre: A number of health points Health given back (% or points) 100 as a share: all their health. 50 as a number: 50 points, never more than their maximum. vie Number 100 from 1 to 1 000 000 Invulnerability on respawn (s) During these seconds, the respawned player loses no health: time to get away from danger. 0: none. invulnerabilite Number 3 from 0 to 600 Death screen text The big text of the death screen. Empty: "You died", in the player's language. texte_mort Text (empty) Game over textshown only if After death is “Game over (no respawn)” The text of the end screen. Empty: "Game over", in the player's language. texte_fin Text (empty) Screen darkening (0 to 1) The veil laid over the game during the death screen: 0 darkens nothing, 1 hides everything. voile Number 0.55 from 0 to 1

items.title: Settings on each object
items.text:
In the Properties of an object or folder that carries the system, Systems section. A folder passes its values on to what it contains; an object can change a value for itself only.

Setting What it does Name in code Type Default Limits or choices Respawn point: distance to activate it (m) The player who comes this close to the object makes it their respawn point. rayon Number 3 from 0.5 to 100

items.title: Events
items.text: The descriptions come from the code.

items.title: What it announces
items.text: Event Fields Description joueur.mort joueur (id), cible (id), source (id?), position (vector) A player died (death and respawn module): they control nothing until they respawn. Other systems hook here: drop the bag, a grave, a counter. joueur.reapparu joueur (id), cible (id), position (vector) A dead player stands up again (death and respawn module): respawned, or brought back by sante.ranimer. mort.point joueur (id), cible (id) A player reached a respawn point (an object carrying the death and respawn system): they will respawn there. sante.ranimer cible (id), part (number?), montant (number?), invulnerabilite (number?) Ask the health module to bring an object back to life, even dead: part (0 to 1 of its maximum, all by default) or montant (points), then invulnerabilite seconds without losing health. Sent by the death and respawn module. fenetres.fermer joueur (id?), raison (text?) Close every window a player has open (loot, inventory, equipment, workshop...), sent by the Death module when they die; any script may send it (a cutscene). joueur: that player (missing: everyone). Each module with a window closes its own.

items.title: What it listens to
items.text: Event Fields Description sante.mort cible (id), source (id?) An object's health reached zero. What happens next belongs to the game: the health module does nothing else, unless its setting says to destroy the object. sante.change cible (id), vie (number), max (number) An object's health changed, or is announced once when the game starts. mort.reapparaitre joueur (id) Ask the death and respawn module to respawn this dead player now (a button of the game's own, a teammate). joueur.arrivee joueur (id), numero (number), nom (text) Sent by the engine, in a game with several players (the game setting Multiplayer), on the computer hosting the game, when a guest joins: joueur is their character (a copy of the player's), numero their place (1 to 7, the host being 0), nom the name they chose. game.players() lists them all. Scripts only run on the host. joueur.depart joueur (id), numero (number) Sent by the engine on the host when a guest leaves the game (they quit, or their connection was lost and they did not come back in time, the game setting Place kept after a drop): their character is removed right after. A module forgets what it kept for them. langue.change langue (text) Sent by the engine when the player changes the game's language (game.set_language, the Menu options). A module redraws what it already shows: its texts go through game.t and game.language.

items.title: Points a script can replace (game.override)
items.text:
The descriptions come from the code.

  • mort.texte: function(default, key) -> the text shown for that key: mort, fin, reapparaitre, dans (it may hold {n}, the seconds left). The default is the game's text setting if filled, else the built-in text in the player's language.

items.title: What the agent knows about this system
items.text: The text the agent reads before using this system.

items.title: Death and respawn (mort)
items.text:
What happens to a player at zero health (sante.mort), chosen by the creator: they fall, control nothing, see a death screen, then respawn or the game ends. Needs sante on the player. Only add it if the user wants deaths handled (a game where the player can die). Never script a death or a respawn yourself when this module fits.

  • The fall: animation is a clip of the player's own character, picked from its clips (player_get lists them), whatever the pack; never assume a name. It plays once and the body stays on its last frame until respawn (the engine adds it to the player's animation graph as the state mort; a graph that already has a state mort keeps it). Empty (the default): the player just stops where they stand, standing; say so to the user and offer to pick a clip.
  • Controls: a dead player does not move, jump or act (only pause still reaches the scripts), whatever their machine sends: game.set_player_dead. The host decides; every player sees them dead.
  • After death (apres): bouton (a "Respawn" button after delai seconds), auto (respawn after delai seconds, counted on screen), or fin (a "Game over" screen; the game stops delai seconds after no player is left alive, with game.finish("lost")).
  • Where (lieu): point (the last respawn point reached, else where the player entered the game), depart, or sur_place. A respawn point is an object carrying this system (systems_attach, value rayon: how close the player must come); objects cloned from it during the game (a sleeping bag the player builds) are points too. Announced by mort.point (joueur, cible).
  • Health back: vie_mode part (vie in % of the maximum) or nombre (vie points), then invulnerabilite seconds without losing health. Done by sante.ranimer (cible, part or montant, invulnerabilite), which a script can also send to bring someone back where they are.
  • Screen: texte_mort, texte_fin (empty: "You died", "Game over" in the player's language), voile (how dark). What it shows is delivered as screens, which the user restyles in the screen editor: « Écran de mort » (Voile, Fenêtre, Titre, Compte: the seconds before an automatic respawn, Réapparaître: the button, action reapparaitre) and « Fin de partie » (Voile, Fenêtre, Titre). Never draw a death screen yourself, and do not name another screen like these. Other texts: override mort.texte.
  • Events: joueur.mort (joueur, cible, source, position) when a player dies, joueur.reapparu (joueur, cible, position) when they stand up again. Hook other systems on them: dropping the bag (loot), a grave, a death counter. Ask for a respawn from a script: game.emit("mort.reapparaitre", {joueur = id}). At death it also sends fenetres.fermer (joueur, raison mort): the windows of the modules (loot, inventory, equipment, workshop) close, so the death screen covers none; a game's own window script should listen to it too.
  • Save: a game saved while a player is dead comes back with them dead (lying, no controls, their screen), for the time left, then they respawn as set.
  • Dropping the bag: the butin module's setting mort_sac (off by default): all or part of the bag, in a bag left where they fell or on the ground, reserved for them for a while. Never script it yourself.
  • Losses: the XP lost at death is the progression module's (each track's mort, mort_part): it already listens to sante.mort, nothing to add here.
  • Enemies and other characters: unchanged; this module only handles players.

items.title: Several players
items.text:
One for the whole game, on the host. A dead guest is seen dead and lying on every machine, then respawns everywhere; they cannot move by cheating, since the host moves their body. Each player sees their own death screen and button.

This page is generated automatically from the WorldMint code (modules/mort/module.json, modules/mort/AGENT.md, modules/events.json): it always matches the editor.

items.title: Particle effect
items.text:
Particles coming out of the object: a campfire, a torch, smoke, sparks, magic, rain or snow around the player. Choose the effect, its size, its colour and its amount; it loops or plays once. For an effect on its own, Create > Particle effect places an invisible box that carries it.

Identifier particules Version 1 Placed on objects yes Run by the engine yes: the engine runs it itself, without a script

items.title: Settings for the whole game
items.text:
In the Systems panel (Developer mode), by opening the system's card.

None.

items.title: Settings on each object
items.text:
In the Properties of an object or folder that carries the system, Systems section. A folder passes its values on to what it contains; an object can change a value for itself only.

Setting What it does Name in code Type Default Limits or choices Effect What the object gives off: fire (a campfire; a torch with a size of 0.4), smoke, sparks, magic, rain or snow (placed on the player, they follow them), dust, chips, an explosion, or what a shot shows: the flash at the end of a barrel, a bullet impact, a splash, a hit on a character. effet Choice in a list Fire (with a little smoke) feu: Fire (with a little smoke)fumee: Smokeetincelles: Sparksmagie: Magicfaisceau: Light beampluie: Rainneige: Snowpoussiere: Dusteclats: Chips (the object's colour)eclats_bois: Wood chipseclats_pierre: Stone chipsexplosion: Explosionimpact: Hit impactbouche: Muzzle flash (a shot)impact_balle: Bullet impacteclaboussure: Splashimpact_chair: Hit on a character Size The size of the whole effect: 1 for a campfire, 0.4 for a torch, 3 for a big blaze. For rain and snow, the width of the area where they fall. taille Number 1 from 0.05 to 20 Colour The effect's colour: its own (a yellow and red fire, grey smoke), or a chosen colour (a blue fire, green magic). teinte Choice in a list The effect's own effet: The effect's ownchoisie: A chosen colour Chosen colourshown only if Colour is “A chosen colour” The particles' starting colour; they darken as they age, like the original effect. couleur Color #4da6ff Amount The number of particles, multiplied: 0.5 for a lighter effect, 2 for a fuller one. A small graphics card keeps fewer at a time. quantite Number 1 from 0 to 10 Looping (unticked: only once, when the game starts) Ticked: the effect runs as long as the object is there (a campfire). Unticked: it plays once when the game starts; the Trigger can play it again ("Play an effect"). boucle Yes or no yes Duration (seconds, 0: endless, or the effect's own) How many seconds the effect lasts. 0: endless if it loops, its usual length otherwise (a fire of a second and a half). duree Number 0 from 0 to 3600 Height above the object's base (m) Where the effect starts: at the object's base (0), or higher. For a torch's flame, the height of its tip; for rain, 0 is enough: it falls from high up. hauteur Number 0 from -50 to 50 Effect lightshown only if Effect is “Fire (with a little smoke)”, “Explosion”, “Magic”, “Sparks” or “Hit impact” A fire, an explosion, magic or sparks light up what is around them: a light that follows the effect, flickers with the fire and grows with its size. With its shadows, what stands next to it (a cube, a wall, a character) casts its shadow; fire, explosions and magic have them, sparks and hits, too brief, never. Without shadows: the light alone, lighter to draw. None: the effect is only drawn. lumiere Choice in a list With its shadows effet: With its shadowssans_ombres: Without shadowsaucune: None Light strengthshown only if Effect is “Fire (with a little smoke)”, “Explosion”, “Magic”, “Sparks” or “Hit impact” ; shown only if Effect light is “With its shadows” or “Without shadows” The strength of the effect's light, multiplied: 0.5 for a discreet glow, 2 for a blaze that lights the whole camp. It already grows with the size of the effect. force_lumiere Number 1 from 0 to 10

items.title: What the agent knows about this system
items.text: The text the agent reads before using this system.

items.title: Particle effect (particules)
items.text:
An object carrying this system gives off particles, simulated by the game and drawn by the renderer: a campfire, a torch, smoke, sparks, magic, rain or snow. The system has no script: the engine runs it. The same game gives the same particles, and the game report counts them under particles.

  • Place it on the object the effect comes from (systems_attach): a campfire model, a torch, a cauldron. For an effect on its own (a fire in the middle of a camp, snow over a valley), create a box (builtin:cube) with visible: false, no collider, then attach the system on it: a hidden box still gives off its effect.
  • Per object (systems_set): effet (feu, fumee, etincelles, magie, faisceau (a column of light rising from a point, like loot), pluie, neige, poussiere, eclats, eclats_bois, eclats_pierre, explosion, impact, and those of a shot: bouche, impact_balle, eclaboussure, impact_chair), taille (1 a campfire, 0.4 a torch; for rain and snow, the width of the area), teinte (effet, or choisie with couleur "#rrggbb": a blue fire), quantite (the number of particles, multiplied), boucle (true: runs while the object is there; false: plays once at the start), duree (seconds; 0 endless when looping), hauteur (metres above the object's base: the tip of a torch).
  • Fire, explosion, magic, sparks and hit give their own light: it follows the effect, flickers with a fire, grows with taille, and goes out with the effect. Fire, explosion and magic cast shadows from it (a crate next to a campfire casts its shadow); the object carrying the effect does not. « lumiere »: effet (default: its light, with its shadows), sans_ombres (the light alone, lighter to draw), aucune (no light). « force_lumiere »: multiplied (0.5 a discreet glow, 2 a blaze). Never add a placed light next to a fire made with this system: it already lights. These lights count with the placed lights (the closest first) and follow the shadow quality (world_set environment shadowQuality); they change nothing in the game, only the image.
  • On a visible object, the effect stops while the object is hidden and comes back when it is shown; destroyed, it stops. game.object_effect(id, false) puts it out, game.object_effect(id, true) lights it again; the Trigger does the same with « Jouer un effet » (effet « objet ») and « Arrêter un effet ».
  • Rain or snow over the whole game: place the system on the player, effet pluie or neige, taille 1 to 2: it follows them.
  • A one-off effect from a script, at a place or on an object: game.effect("explosion", pos), game.effect("eclats", rock) (chips take the rock's colour). See the script reference.
  • What the engine already does: a little dust when the player lands (landingDust of the player), chips and dust when an object bursts or collapses (game.effect(id, "burst")), dust where a falling object lands. The Gathering system sends chips at each hit, and the Combat system a hit impact; each has a setting to turn them off.
  • Effects follow the graphics quality, on three levels (High, Medium, Low: 6,000, 3,000 and 1,500 particles at once; fewer and slightly larger particles given off, simpler light on smoke at lower levels). An effect never breaks the game, it only looks lighter. A game run by the agent keeps High, so its report does not depend on the machine; the report gives the level under particles.quality and particles.budget.
  • The fire preset already has its flames, a bright core, a warm glow, embers and smoke: do not stack several fire effects to make one campfire, raise taille or quantite instead. In the editor, a visible effect animates on its own (30 frames per second in the active view, 10 in the others).

items.title: Passage (passage)
items.text:
Leads to another scene of the game: a door into a house, a cave entrance, the exit of a level. Activating it activates the interaction module; placing it on an object places interaction there too.

  • A game with several places has one scene per place, in the project's scenes folder. A scene's name is its file name, without folder or extension.
  • Place it on the door, the entrance or a zone (systems_attach), and set (systems_set): scene (where it leads, a name from scenes_list), arrivee (the name of an arrival point of that scene, where the player appears turned like it: entities_create with arrival: true, just inside the door), en_marchant (true: taken by walking into it within distance, without a key; false: with the interaction key).
  • Make the way back too: a passage in the other scene, leading to an arrival point just outside the first door. An arrival on a passage taken by walking does not send the player back at once (they must step out first), but keep them apart: the player would be standing in a doorway.
  • scene_validate lists passages that lead to a missing scene or arrival.
  • The player keeps everything (inventory, health, quests): scripts keep running. A scene left stays as it was.
  • From a script: game.go_to(scene, arrival?), and game.on("scene.change", function(e) ... end) with e.depuis and e.vers.

items.title: Several players
items.text:
One for the whole game: the whole group changes scene together. By default the passage waits until every player has taken it (groupe = attendre, showing "Waiting for the group: 2 of 3"); emmener takes everyone as soon as one takes it. - The waiting message is the screen « Attente du groupe » delivered by the system (shape Message, HUD key Attente du groupe/Message), shown to the waiting players only, which the user restyles in the screen editor. Never draw it yourself, and do not name another screen « Attente du groupe ».

items.title: Physics
items.text:
The objects that carry it fall, roll, slide, and the player pushes them by walking into them: crates, barrels, a ball, rocks. Those that come at the player push back, by their mass: a rock knocks them aside, a ball bounces off. In water, they float, sink or stay in between, and drift with the water. Their shape wraps the model, or follows its outline. Placed on a folder, it applies to everything inside.

Identifier physique Version 3 Placed on objects yes Run by the engine yes: the engine runs it itself, without a script

Higher, they move heavier objects; 0: they push nothing. force_du_joueur Number 300 from 0 to 100 000

items.text:
In the Properties of an object or folder that carries the system, Systems section. A folder passes its values on to what it contains; an object can change a value for itself only.

Setting What it does Name in code Type Default Limits or choices Shape The shape used to compute movement. The first four are simple, at the model's size: a box slides and tips over, a ball rolls in every direction, a cylinder rolls on its side like a barrel, a capsule (a cylinder with rounded ends) rolls too, and tips over gently. The hull follows the model's outline, without its hollows: a rock rolls and catches on its edges, a statue stands on its base. It takes a little more computing: keep it for objects whose shape matters. forme Choice in a list Box: a crate, furniture boite: Box: a crate, furnitureboule: Ball: a ball, a round rockcylindre: Cylinder: a barrel, a columncapsule: Capsule: a bottle, a log, a dummyenveloppe: Model hull: its real outline (a rock, a statue) Mass (kg): the heavier, the harder to push Its weight, in kilograms: a crate 10 to 30, a barrel 40, a rock 200. The heavier, the harder to push. masse Number 10 from 0.1 to 100 000 Friction: 0 slides as on ice How much it grips the ground: 0 slides as on ice, 0.6 is ordinary friction, 1 and above grips hard. frottement Number 0.6 from 0 to 2 Bounce: 0 does not bounce, 1 bounces without losing anything How much it bounces when falling or hitting something: 0 does not bounce, like a crate; 0.8 bounces a lot, like a ball. rebond Number 0.1 from 0 to 1 In water What it does in the water of a lake or the sea. It floats half sunk, sinks slowly to the bottom, or stays in between. In every case, the water slows it down, rocks it with the waves and carries it along when it moves. Its pieces, if it breaks, do the same. eau Choice in a list Floats: a crate, a barrel, a ball flotte: Floats: a crate, a barrel, a ballentre_deux: In between: stays where it is let gocoule: Sinks: a stone, an anchor, an iron chestdensite: By its density, chosen below Density (kg per m³; water: 1,000)shown only if In water is “By its density, chosen below” How much one cubic meter of its material weighs, in kilograms. Less than water (1,000), it floats, the higher the lighter it is: wood 500, cork 200, ice 900. More, it sinks: stone 2,500, iron 7,800. densite Number 500 from 10 to 20 000 Drag in water (1 ordinary) How much the water slows it down and carries it: 1 is ordinary, 0 glides on the water without being held, 3 sticks to the water like a dead leaf. freinage_eau Number 1 from 0 to 10

items.title: Physics (physique)
items.text:
The objects carrying this system are simulated by the engine: they fall, roll, slide, bounce, and the player and characters push them by walking into them. Crates, barrels, balls, rocks, a cart. The system has no script: the engine does it all.

  • Make objects movable: modules_add it once, then systems_attach on each object, or on a group so that all its children move. An object carrying it does not need a collider: it collides by itself.
  • Per object (systems_set): forme, masse in kg (a crate 10 to 30, a barrel 40, a rock 200: the heavier, the harder to push), frottement (0 slides as on ice, 0.6 by default), rebond (0 to 1).
  • forme: boite (a crate, furniture: slides and tips over), boule (a ball, a round rock: rolls every way), cylindre (a barrel, a column: rolls on its side), capsule (a cylinder with rounded ends: a bottle, a log, a dummy; rolls on its side and tips over gently), all four at the size of the model; or enveloppe, the model's own outline without its hollows (a jagged rock that rolls and catches on its edges, a statue standing on its base, an L-shaped piece of furniture). enveloppe costs a little more: use it when the shape changes how the object moves, not for crates and balls. A flat model (a sign, a sheet) has no outline and becomes a boite.
  • A moving object hits the player and the characters as two bodies do, by their masses (a character weighs 70 kg): a 200 kg rock rolling down a slope knocks the player back, a 40 kg barrel shoves them a little, a light ball bounces off them. It never goes through them. To make a rolling trap dangerous, give it mass and speed (game.push); add damage with a zone on its path or a script, not by expecting the shove to hurt.
  • In water (a lake, the sea): « eau » says what it does. « flotte » (the default: half sunk, a crate, a barrel, a ball), « entre_deux » (stays at the depth where it is let go), « coule » (sinks slowly to the bottom: a stone, an anchor), or « densite » with densite in kg per m³ (below 1000 it floats, higher the lighter: cork 200, wood 500, ice 900; above, it sinks: stone 2500). « freinage_eau » (1 ordinary, 0 glides, 3 sticks to the water). The water slows it, rocks it with the waves and carries it when it moves; its pieces, if it breaks, float or sink like it.
  • For the whole game: force_du_joueur, the force in newtons with which the player and characters push (300 by default; 0: they never push anything).
  • Place them resting on the ground or on each other (entities_ground): one placed in the air falls when the game starts.
  • Scripts move them with the physics: game.push(id, vec(...)) throws one (a change of speed in m/s), game.velocity(id) reads its speed, game.set_position puts one back at rest. One that falls out of the world disappears.
  • To know when something reaches a place (a ball in a goal, a crate on a plate), use the zone system.
  • game_run reports moving_objects: how far each one travelled, and whether it fell out of the world. Check there that what should move did. Its « water » part lists each object that touched the water: « state » at the end (« floating », « underwater », « out_of_water »), « submerged_pct », « below_surface_m », « in_water_s » and « drift_m » (how far the water carried it); « floating_debris » counts broken pieces that floated.

items.title: Population
items.text:
Pedestrians who appear on the pavements around the player, out of sight, walk along the streets and leave behind them. Nothing is written in the scene: only these settings. Pedestrians are copies of your model characters (hidden), reused over and over. Those who matter are never taken back: what a quest names until it ends, a companion, a pedestrian the player touched. They remember: a pedestrian who left comes back the same for a minute, a damaged car stays damaged, and what the player leaves waits for them. A gunshot or an explosion empties the street around: pedestrians flee, cars heading there stop.

Identifier population Version 6 Placed on objects no
