items.text:
In the Systems panel (Developer mode), by opening the system's card.

Setting What it does Name in code Type Default Limits or choices Bring the streets to life Ticked: pedestrians appear around the player on the city pavements. Unticked: nobody. actif Yes or no yes People in the streets (× the density) The overall slider: 0 nobody, 1 the set density, 2 twice as many. Always capped by the most pedestrians at once. curseur Number 1 from 0 to 4 Pedestrians per 100 m of pavement How many pedestrians walk on 100 m of pavement around the player. passants_100m Number 6 from 0 to 200 Density by zone One row per place that does not have the overall density: a city district (its name), a map sector (its name), or "partout" (everywhere). A city district already has the density of its style; a row naming it replaces it. zones List of “Zone” (empty) one line per “Zone”: its fields Who you see in the street Your model characters, usually hidden in the scene (an animated mannequin, for example animations/quaternius-ual1/UAL1_Standard.glb shipped with the editor). Each pedestrian is a copy of one of them, with its own walk clip. No row: the objects tagged population.passant. modeles List of “Model” (empty) one line per “Model”: its fields Most pedestrians at once The number of pedestrians alive at once, whatever the density: the machine never runs more. budget Number 250 from 0 to 5000 Nobody appears within (m) A pedestrian always appears further than this from the player, and out of sight. rayon_min Number 35 from 0 to 1000 Hidden, appears from (m) Behind a wall or a building, where the camera cannot see, a pedestrian can appear closer, down to this distance from the player. rayon_cache Number 15 from 15 to 1000 Margin around the view (degrees) Nobody appears in the camera image, nor in this margin around it: a player who turns their head a little never sees someone appear. marge_vue Number 15 from 0 to 60 Appear up to (m) The edge of the ring where pedestrians appear. rayon_max Number 100 from 1 to 1000 Leave beyond (m) Further than this from the player, a pedestrian leaves (it goes back to the pool). rayon_depart Number 120 from 1 to 2000 Most appearances per step The pace: at most this many pedestrians appear at each game step, to avoid hitches. par_pas Number 4 from 0 to 100 Parked cars Your model cars, hidden in the scene. Each parked car is a copy of one of them, shown within reach, solid within 15 m of the player. No row: the objects tagged population.voiture. garees_modeles List of “Model” (empty) one line per “Model”: its fields Parked cars visible up to (m) Further than this from the player, parked cars are not shown. garees_portee Number 150 from 1 to 5000 Parked cars lightening A factor applied on top of the share of parking spaces taken of each zone and of the overall setting (0.5: half as many parked cars everywhere, districts included). The agent lowers it when the aimed machine is too loaded; 1: nothing is lightened. garees_allegement Number 1 from 0 to 1 The same come back for (s) A pedestrian who leaves out of sight is remembered this long: if the player comes back, the same one comes back (same character, same pavement, same direction), moved on by the time spent. 0: never remembered. memoire_courte Number 60 from 0 to 3600 Traces last (s) A damaged car, an emptied bay, a touched pedestrian stay as they are for this game time (600: 10 minutes), then the street becomes ordinary again. They go into the save. traces_duree Number 600 from 0 to 86 400 Most traces The number of traces kept at once: beyond it, the oldest goes first. What the player leaves does not count. traces_max Number 64 from 0 to 4096 Keep what the player leaves (s) A car parked, an object dropped by the player waits for them this game time (1,800: 30 minutes), even if they go far: they can change their mind and come back. 0: always. Their last car is always kept. Goes into the save. garder_laisse Number 1800 from 0 to 864 000 Most things a player leaves How many objects left behind are kept per player: beyond it, the oldest goes first. The player's last car never goes. laisse_max Number 32 from 0 to 1024 Walking speed (m/s) The average speed of pedestrians; each walks a little faster or slower. vitesse Number 1.3 from 0.1 to 20 Cars driving around Ticked: cars appear on the lanes around the player, out of sight, follow their lane, stop at red lights, give way and turn at junctions. voitures Yes or no yes Cars per 100 m of lane How many cars drive on 100 m of lane around the player (× the slider). voitures_100m Number 1.5 from 0 to 100 Parking spaces taken The share of parking bays where a car is parked (0.6: six in ten). Each bay is drawn from the game seed: the same bay always has the same car. Nothing is written in the scene. garees Number 0.6 from 0 to 1 By the hour How the number of pedestrians changes from one hour to the next, wherever a zone does not give its own hours. "City": almost nobody at 4 am, crowds at 8 am and 6 pm. heures Hours of the day City (low at 4 am, peaks at 8 am and 6 pm) ville: City (low at 4 am, peaks at 8 am and 6 pm)ville_nuit: City that never sleepsvillage: Village (empty at night)constant: Always the sameor 24 numbers of your own (midnight to 11 pm), from 0 to 4 Follow the time of day Ticked: the time of the sky or of the Day and night module changes the number of pedestrians. Unticked: the same number at any time. selon_heure Yes or no yes The cars you see Your model cars, hidden in the scene, with their wheels as children (for example the free CC0 cars of Quaternius' Realistic Car Pack). Each car is a copy of one of them; its length is read from its bounds. No row: the objects tagged population.voiture. modeles_voitures List of “Model” (empty) one line per “Model”: its fields Most cars at once The number of cars driving at once, whatever the density. budget_voitures Number 80 from 0 to 2000 No car appears within (m) A car always appears further than this from the player, and out of sight. rayon_min_voitures Number 60 from 0 to 2000 Cars appear up to (m) The edge of the ring where cars appear. rayon_max_voitures Number 200 from 1 to 2000 Cars leave beyond (m) Further than this from the player, a car leaves (it goes back to the pool). rayon_depart_voitures Number 240 from 1 to 4000 Speed without a sign (m/s) The speed of cars on a street without a speed limit sign (13.9 m/s: 50 km/h). With a sign, they follow its limit. vitesse_voiture Number 13.9 from 0.5 to 80 Gap between two stopped cars (m) The distance from one bumper to the other when a car stops behind another. ecart_voitures Number 2.5 from 2 to 30 Simulation levels Ticked: near the player, a pedestrian has a real body (steps aside, can be bumped) and so does a car (it can be hit, it brakes); further away, they follow their line; out of sight, they are only data. Unticked: all of them follow their line. niveaux Yes or no yes Pedestrians are near within (m) Closer than this to the player, a pedestrian has a real body: it avoids others and can be bumped. It loses it 5 m further away. rayon_proche Number 25 from 0 to 500 Cars are near within (m) Closer than this to the player, a driving car has a body: it can be hit, and it brakes in front of the player. It loses it 5 m further away. rayon_proche_voitures Number 25 from 0 to 500 Fear around a gunshot (m) A gunshot, an impact or a death (population.danger too) makes pedestrians within this distance flee, and stops the cars heading there. For an explosion, its radius is added. 0: nobody reacts. peur_rayon Number 30 from 0 to 1000 Fear lasts (s) How long they flee, cars stay stopped and nobody appears around; then the street becomes ordinary again. peur_duree Number 20 from 0 to 3600 Share of pedestrians who flee 0.9: nine pedestrians in ten flee, the others go on their way. items.title: What it announces
items.text: Event Fields Description population.apparait cible (id), sorte (text) A pedestrian appeared around the player, out of sight (Population module): a copy from the pool, tagged population. population.disparait cible (id), sorte (text), important (boolean?) A pedestrian left (Population module): too far or behind the player, back to the pool. Its id may come back as another pedestrian. important: it had been kept (touched, named by a quest) and nothing names it any more. population.touche cible (id), joueur (id), comment (text), sorte (text) A pedestrian became important (Population module): a player touched it (comment frappe, tue, parle, monte) or something keeps it (quetes, accompagner, garder, emmene). The director never takes it back while something names it; it stays itself. population.fuite lieu (vector), rayon (number), passants (number) A danger made pedestrians flee (Population module): lieu is where it happened, rayon how far it scared, passants how many fled.

items.title: What it listens to
items.text: Event Fields Description population.garder cible (id) Ask the Population module to never take back this object (it puts the tag population.garder on it). population.liberer cible (id) Ask the Population module to let this object go again (it removes the tag population.garder). quetes.debut quete (text), groupe (boolean?) A quest started: quete is its title. groupe (Journal de quêtes 8): true for a quest of the whole group (game setting groupe), sent once for the group, joueur being who moved it on. quetes.creee modele (text), quete (text), valeurs (table), groupe (boolean?) A quest was made from a template (Journal de quêtes 15, events version 34): quete is its own title, modele the template's, valeurs the value of each hole (an object's id, a number, a text). Sent before its quetes.debut. groupe: true for a quest of the whole group. quetes.etape quete (text), etape (number), texte (text), issue (number?), suite (text?), groupe (boolean?) A step of a quest is done: etape is its rank in the quest (from 1), texte what it said. Sent before quetes.fin when it was the last one. issue (Journal de quêtes 11): the rank (from 1) of the other way to end the step that did it, absent when the step itself did; texte is then that way's text. suite (Journal de quêtes 11): the label the quest goes to next (fin, echec or a step's label), absent when it simply goes on to the next row. groupe (Journal de quêtes 8): true for a quest of the whole group (game setting groupe), sent once for the group, joueur being who moved it on. quetes.etape_debut quete (text), etape (number), texte (text), groupe (boolean?) A step of a quest starts (Journal de quêtes 11, events version 33): it becomes one to do now, its other ways to end it too. etape is its rank in the quest (from 1), texte what it says. Sent after quetes.debut for the first steps, then after the quetes.etape that opened it, and again when the step starts over (an "Also fails if" row set to recommence) or the quest resumes at it (quetes.reprise); its own annonce_debut event follows. Not sent again when a saved game is loaded. groupe (Journal de quêtes 8): true for a quest of the whole group. quetes.etape_echec quete (text), etape (number), alors (text), manquee (boolean?), groupe (boolean?) A step of a quest failed (Journal de quêtes 11, events version 33): one of its "Also fails if" rows happened. etape is its rank in the quest (from 1), alors what that row does: echoue (the quest fails, quetes.echec follows), recommence (the step starts again from zero) or etiquette (the quest goes to the row's label). Also sent for an "Also fails if" row under the quest itself that does not make it fail (recommence: the quest starts again; etiquette), etape being then the step it was waiting for (0: none). For an optional step, manquee is true: the step is only missed, the quest goes on without it. groupe: true for a quest of the whole group. quetes.reprise quete (text), etape (number), groupe (boolean?) A quest resumes (Journal de quêtes 11, events version 33): tried again after a failure (the log's Try again button, reessayer auto, quetes.reessayer, or given again when it does not start over), or started again by an "Also fails if" row of the quest set to recommence. etape is the step it resumes at (from 1; 0: none). The steps before it stay done; marks stay set and the world is not put back as it was: a Trigger rule on the step's annonce_debut does that. groupe: true for a quest of the whole group. quetes.fin quete (text), xp (number?), piste (text?), groupe (boolean?), facultatives (table?) A quest is finished: all its steps are done. Its reward, if any, has been asked to the inventory. xp and piste (version 28): its XP for the Progression module and the track that gets it (empty: the main one). facultatives (Journal de quêtes 11): {faites, total}, how many of its optional steps were done, out of how many; absent when it has none. groupe (Journal de quêtes 8): true for a quest of the whole group (game setting groupe), sent once for the group, joueur being who moved it on. quetes.echec quete (text), groupe (boolean?) A quest failed: an event, a mark, its time ran out, or quetes.echouer. It gives no reward; it may be given again if its settings allow it. groupe (Journal de quêtes 8): true for a quest of the whole group (game setting groupe), sent once for the group, joueur being who moved it on. quetes.abandon quete (text), groupe (boolean?) The player abandoned a quest from the log (or quetes.abandonner asked for it). It gives no reward; it may be given again if its settings allow it. groupe (Journal de quêtes 8): true for a quest of the whole group (game setting groupe), sent once for the group, joueur being who moved it on. accompagner.suivre cible (id?), qui (id?), lieu (id?) Ask a character carrying the Companion system to follow someone (Companion module, version 34): qui, a player or an object (missing: the one it followed last, else the host); lieu, a place where it announces accompagner.arrive once it gets there while following. cible: the character, by id or name; missing, every character carrying the system in the scene. "Follow me" after accompagner.attendre. accompagner.aller cible (id?), lieu (id?), qui (id?) Ask a Companion character to walk to a place (lieu, an object or a point; missing: its setting destination), waiting whenever the player qui is too far; there it announces accompagner.arrive and waits. cible: as for accompagner.suivre. accompagner.fuir cible (id?), de (id?), distance (number?), qui (id?) Ask a Companion character to run away from de (an object or a point; missing: qui, else the nearest player) until distance metres (missing: its setting distance_fuite); it announces accompagner.arrive once safe, and runs again if approached. cible: as for accompagner.suivre. accompagner.attendre cible (id?) Ask a Companion character to wait where it is ("Wait here"), remembering whom it followed: accompagner.suivre without qui makes it follow them again. cible: as for accompagner.suivre. accompagner.arreter cible (id?) Ask a Companion character to stop whatever it does and forget whom it followed. cible: as for accompagner.suivre. sante.blesser cible (id), montant (number), source (id?) Ask the health module to remove health from an object. sante.mort cible (id), source (id?) An object's health reached zero. What happens next belongs to the game: the health module does nothing else, unless its setting says to destroy the object. dialogue.fin cible (id) A dialogue window closed: after its last line, or a choice leading to fin. vehicule.monte cible (id), qui (id), joueur (id?) A player got into a vehicle (an object carrying the vehicule system) and now drives it: qui and joueur are their character (the host's, or a guest's). Announced by the engine. vehicule.descendu cible (id), qui (id), joueur (id?) A player got out of a vehicle. Announced by the engine. population.laisser cible (id), joueur (id?) Tell the Population module that a player left this object born of the population (put down, dropped, abandoned): it is kept as it is for its setting garder_laisse (30 minutes of play by default, 0: always), at most laisse_max per player, and saved. Ignored for an object the author placed (the world already remembers it). Getting out of a car born of the population (vehicule.descendu) does it by itself. jour_nuit.heure heure (number), jour (number) A new hour of the world started (0 to 23), on day jour (1 the first day). population.danger lieu (vector), rayon (number?), force (number?), sorte (text?), source (id?) Tell the Population module that something dangerous happens here (a shot, an explosion, a fight a game wants to signal): pedestrians within rayon (its setting peur_rayon when missing) flee, cars heading there stop, nobody appears there while the fear lasts. force (1 by default) multiplies the share who flee and how long. Gunshots (tir.tir), explosions (tir.explosion), impacts (projectile.touche) and deaths (sante.mort) do it by themselves. A game script can replace the reaction with game.override("population.reagir", function(default, e) ... end). tir.tir source (id), arme (text), origine (vector), direction (vector) The player fired a ranged weapon (version 25), whether it hits or not: origine is the muzzle, direction the aim before spread. For a sound, a noise that alerts enemies, a counter. tir.explosion source (id), arme (text), point (vector), rayon (number) A shot of the player exploded (version 25): a grenade at the end of its fuse or a rocket on impact. Health was removed within rayon metres, with no wall in between. projectile.touche projectile (number), owner (id?), cible (id?), point (vector), normale (vector), partie (text?), os (text?), vitesse (vector), eau (boolean?), data (table?) A projectile launched by game.projectile hit something: cible is the object hit (nil for the terrain and for water), partie the part of a character's body (tete, torse, bras, jambes; missing for an object), os the bone, vitesse its velocity on arrival (m/s), data the table given at launch. eau = true when it entered water (point on the surface): it goes on, strongly slowed, and sinks (put a splash there, game.effect("eclaboussure", e.point), or stop it with game.stop_projectile). Announced by the engine; a projectile that bounces announces each hit.

items.title: Points a script can replace (game.override)
items.text:
The descriptions come from the code.

  • population.reagir: function(default, e) -> anything. Called for every danger the Population module hears: a gunshot (tir.tir), an explosion (tir.explosion), an impact (projectile.touche), a death (sante.mort) or population.danger. e: lieu (a vector), rayon (metres, or nil: the setting peur_rayon), force (or nil: 1), sorte (tir, explosion, impact, mort or danger), source (who caused it, or nil). The default makes the pedestrians around flee and stops the cars heading there (game.population_danger). Return without calling default to replace it; call default(e) with changed fields to adjust it.

items.title: What the agent knows about this system
items.text: The text the agent reads before using this system.

items.title: Population (population)
items.text: Pedestrians who appear on the city pavements around the player, out of sight, walk along the streets and leave behind them. Use it whenever a city must feel alive: never write pedestrians in the scene, never animate them with timelines or scripts. The scene holds only these settings; the engine (engine/game/game_population.cpp) does the work at the start of each step. Never edit the module: set its values (modules_set).

items.title: Filling a city, step by step
items.text:
1. The city needs its lanes: a generated city writes its pavements, lanes and parking bays in voies.json. With none, the report's probleme says so and nobody appears: generate or regenerate the city first, never write pedestrians in the scene.
  2. Add the module if the game has none (modules_add population), then set it with modules_set. Never edit the module, its script or its module.json.
  3. The models: place hidden model objects in the scene and list them in modeles (pedestrians), modeles_voitures (driving cars, wheels as children) and garees_modeles (parked cars). Only models whose licence lets the game ship them: the mannequin shipped with the editor, CC0 or CC-BY models (with their credit), the free cars and passers-by of a pack. Never a paid pack's model in a shipped game, and never change a model (its mesh, size or materials): measure its bounds, the director reads them.
  4. How many, overall: curseur (0 nobody, 1 the set density, 2 twice) for everything at once; passants_100m for pedestrians, voitures_100m for driving cars, garees for the share of parking bays taken. voitures (unticked) removes the driving cars.
  5. Where (zones): zones, one row per place (lieu: a city district name, a map sector name or id, or partout; passants, voitures, garees, heures). A generated city already gives each district its values; write a row only to change one district (empty a park, fill a market street).
  6. When (hours): heures (ville, ville_nuit, village, constant, or 24 numbers of your own) with selon_heure ticked to follow the hour of the sky or of the Day and night module.
  7. Keep a character (a quest giver met in the street, a witness): name it in a quest (it is kept until the quest ends), or send population.garder {cible} (and population.liberer to give it back); see "Who is never taken back".
  8. Change how the street reacts to a danger: game.override("population.reagir", ...), or send population.danger from a script or a Trigger rule; to empty a place, set its zones row; see "Reactions".
  9. Before raising a density, estimate it (city_perf with {"population": {...}}, see "Lightening on your own"); after, prove it with game_run (see "Proving it").

items.title: How it works
items.text:
• Where: the pavements (trottoirs) of the city lanes (voies.json of each tile, the graph of game.route). A game with no generated city has no pavement yet: nobody appears.
  • Who: copies of the model characters in modeles (hidden objects of the scene; usually the animated mannequin animations/quaternius-ual1/UAL1_Standard.glb shipped with the editor, placed hidden). No row: every object tagged population.passant. Each copy plays its model's own walk clip (the clip whose name says walk, a loop first). Never make up a pose.
  • On arrival (the scene loads, or the player jumps further than rayon_min in one step): the whole disc up to rayon_max fills at once, in view too, before the first image. The pool of copies is prepared when the scene loads, not during play.
  • How many: passants_100m (6) per 100 m of pavement within rayon_max of the player, times curseur (1), at most budget (250) at once.
  • Where and when (zones and hours): each piece of pavement takes the density of the zone it lies in, times the coefficient of the hour, times curseur. heures is the overall hour model (ville: low at 4 am, peaks at 8 am and 6 pm; ville_nuit: the city that never sleeps; village: empty at night; constant); selon_heure (ticked) follows the hour of the realistic sky, or the jour_nuit.heure event of the Day and night module; no hour known: coefficient 1. zones (under Advanced) has one row per place: lieu (a city district name, a map sector name or id, or partout), passants (per 100 m of pavement), voitures (moving cars per km of lane: births and the director's target follow the zone where the car appears, 0 for none; hours do not change it) and garees (share of parking spaces taken, 0 to 1: each bay of the zone is drawn from the seed with it, 0 for none), both -1 for like elsewhere (version 6), heures (empty: like elsewhere). Any heures is a model name or 24 numbers of your own (0 h to 23 h, 0 to 4): the editor draws it as a 24 h curve whose points the user drags. A generated city writes its districts with the population block of their style (pedestrians, cars, parked share, hour model, varying with the district density) in its lanes: those are the defaults. A zones row naming a district replaces its values (one value shown in two places: the district panel writes the same row). To empty or fill a district, set its row; never write pedestrians.
  • The rings (Medium quality): nobody appears in sight. In sight means inside the camera's cone (its horizontal and vertical openings, each widened by marge_vue, 15 degrees) and not hidden: three rays from the camera to the pedestrian's head, waist and knees all hit a wall or a building to hide it. Further than rayon_min (35 m), out of the cone or hidden is enough; between rayon_cache (15 m) and rayon_min, only hidden behind the scenery; never within rayon_cache. They appear up to rayon_max (100 m), at most par_pas (4) per step; they leave beyond rayon_depart (120 m), or when out of sight for 4 s, further than 60 m and behind the player.
  • They walk along their pavement at vitesse (1.3 m/s, each a little faster or slower); at the end of a pavement they take another one that touches it, or turn back.
  • The copies come from a pool prepared once at the start (game.pool): no object is created during play. They carry the tags population and population.passant, and saves leave them out.

items.title: Cars (driving)
items.text:
• Where: the lanes of the city (voies and liaisons of voies.json), never a pavement. Each car follows its lane at the street's speed limit (the limite_vitesse signs of the city, in km/h or mph; vitesse_voiture, 13.9 m/s, on a street without a sign), keeps ecart_voitures (2.5 m) behind the car in front, stops at a red light of its junction (the feu lights: game.data(light).feu, the same cycle as their lamps), stops at amber when it can, gives way when it enters a roundabout (cede links) or turns left, never enters a junction while a car is on a crossing path or its exit is full, and picks one of its lane's links at each junction (straight, right, left, the left-turn lanes). No physics, except near the player (see Simulation levels).
  • Who: copies of modeles_voitures (hidden cars of the scene, with their wheels as children: the pool copies the whole group), or every object tagged population.voiture. Only redistributable cars (CC0, such as the free cars of Quaternius' Realistic Car Pack); never a paid pack model. Their length and width are read from their bounds.
  • How many: voitures_100m (1.5) per 100 m of lane within rayon_max_voitures, times curseur, at most budget_voitures (80). They appear between rayon_min_voitures (60 m; hidden behind a building, from 30 m) and rayon_max_voitures (200 m), out of sight, never on a junction nor within 12 m of another car on their lane; they leave beyond rayon_depart_voitures (240 m), or out of sight and behind the player. They carry the tags population and population.voiture.

items.title: Simulation levels (niveaux)
items.text:
• Near (closer than rayon_proche, 25 m; lost 5 m further): a pedestrian gets a capsule (game.character), walks to its place on its pavement by physics, steps aside from the player and the others (avoidance) and can be bumped; a driving car gets its model's collider (it can be hit) and brakes in front of the player or a near pedestrian (rayon_proche_voitures, 25 m).
  • On its line (further): as above, no physics. Out of sight (donnees, unticked by default; ticked): only its place moves on; the object is hidden and no longer placed, and it is placed before it shows again. Level changes never jump: the capsule starts where the pedestrian is shown, and one leaving the near level gives back its gap to the line slowly.
  • niveaux = false: everyone stays on its line (the behaviour before). The report gives niveaux {passants_proches, passants_en_donnees, voitures_proches, voitures_en_donnees, montees, descentes, bouscules, freinages, pire_saut_m}.

items.title: Who is never taken back (the important ones)
items.text:
• The director only ever takes back its own copies: anything the author placed in the scene (a quest giver, a guard, a shop keeper) is never touched.
  • A pedestrian leaves the director, stays itself and stops walking its pavement (an object like any other) as soon as: it carries the tag population.garder (game.add_tag, or the events population.garder / population.liberer {cible}); it goes with the player to the next scene (game.bring_along); a quest that has started names it (its donneur, or the fin_cible, fin_lieu, echec_cible, echec_lieu, reprise_lieu of any of its rows, and the values of a quest created from a template), until the quest ends, completed, failed or abandoned; Accompagner makes it follow, go, flee or wait (until accompagner.arreter); a player touches it: hurts it or kills it (sante.blesser, sante.mort with a player as source), talks to it (dialogue.fin), gets in it (vehicule.monte). Another one is born to keep the density.
  • When nothing names it any more, it goes back to the pool once the player is further than twice rayon_depart and it is out of sight. A quest object therefore persists until the end of its quest, then becomes ordinary again.
  • A script or a Trigger rule never writes these lists: set tags, send events. Name a pedestrian by its id (copies share their model's name). Engine calls behind the module: game.population_garder(reason, list), game.population_touche(target, player, how) and game.population_laisse(target, player, how).

items.title: What it remembers (the memory)
items.text:
• The short memory: a pedestrian who leaves out of sight is remembered memoire_courte (60) s. If the player comes back and the place is in the ring again, the same one comes back first (same model, same pavement, same direction), moved on by the time spent. After that, the next one there is another. The density still decides: a remembered pedestrian comes back only as the zone and the hour allow (always the same draw for the same one), and only while fewer are alive than the density asks for.
  • Traces: a parked car the game changed (colour, tags, size: dented, painted), a parked car pushed or taken from its bay (the bay stays empty, the bay reads its trace before its seed), a touched pedestrian, stay as they are when the player comes back, for traces_duree (600) s of play, at most traces_max (64), the oldest goes first.
  • What the player leaves (a car they got out of, vehicule.descendu; any object born of the population sent with population.laisser {cible, joueur?}) waits for them garder_laisse (1800) s of play, 0 = always, at most laisse_max (32) per player, never pushed out by other traces: they can change their mind and come back. Their last car is always kept.
  • Traces and what the player leaves go into the save with their age (game.save / game.load); the short memory does not.
  • Objects the author placed are not concerned: the world already remembers them.

items.title: Reactions (version 5)
items.text:
• A danger empties the street around it: a gunshot (tir.tir, at the muzzle), an explosion (tir.explosion: its radius is added to peur_rayon), a projectile impact (projectile.touche), a death (sante.mort), or population.danger {lieu, rayon?, force?, sorte?, source?} sent by any script or Trigger rule (a fight, a siren, a fire: anything a game wants to signal).
  • Within peur_rayon (30 m): a share peur_part (0.9, drawn from the seed) of the pedestrians flee along their pavement, away from the danger, peur_vitesse (2.5) times faster, with their own run clip if they have one (a clip named run, sprint, jog, course), otherwise their walk clip played faster; for peur_duree (20) s, then they walk on their line again, or leave out of sight like the others. Cars within the radius heading towards the danger stop where they are while the fear lasts; those driving away go on. Nobody appears within the radius while the fear lasts (the density drops there for a while). force multiplies the share and the duration; several dangers at the same place (under 2 m) extend the fear.
  • The important ones do not flee: a quest giver kept by its quest, a companion, a pedestrian touched by a player or tagged population.garder is no longer a pedestrian of the director. A game that wants them to flee sends accompagner.fuir.
  • To change the reaction, never edit the module: game.override("population.reagir", function(default, e) ... end) receives every danger e {lieu, rayon?, force?, sorte = tir, explosion, impact, mort or danger, source?}. Return without calling default to replace it (nobody flees: the game does its own thing), or call default(e) with changed fields (a larger rayon, a smaller force). Engine call behind it: game.population_danger(lieu, rayon?, force?).

items.title: Events
items.text:
• population.apparait {cible, sorte = passant or voiture}: a pedestrian or a car appears.
  • population.disparait {cible, sorte = passant or voiture}: it leaves (back to the pool). Never keep its id after this.
  • population.touche {cible, joueur, comment, sorte = passant}: a pedestrian becomes important (comment: frappe, tue, parle, monte, or what keeps it: quetes, accompagner, garder, emmene).
  • population.fuite {lieu, rayon, passants}: a danger made pedestrians flee (how many).
  • Listens to population.garder and population.liberer {cible}: put or remove the tag population.garder; to population.laisser {cible, joueur?} and vehicule.descendu: what the player leaves (above); to population.danger, tir.tir, tir.explosion, projectile.touche and sante.mort: the reactions (above).

items.title: Proving it (game_run)
items.text:
After any change, run game_run with a walk through the city (the player moving and turning the camera) and read the report's population part. A proof says, with the numbers: naissances_vues = 0 and voitures.naissances_vues = 0 (nothing appeared in sight), plus_vivants within budget, and the cost (cout.mesure_ms next to cout.estime_ms, under cout.budget_ms). If the part has an alerte list, a rule is broken: say it to the user as it is, fix it (an alerte on cost: see "Lightening on your own"), and run again.

The report has a population part: heure (the hour used, -1 when unknown), zones (zones in use, city districts included), vivants (alive now), plus_vivants, cible (what the density asks for), naissances, departs, departs_derriere, refus_trop_pres and refus_dans_la_vue (places drawn then refused: too close, or in view), naissances_cachees (born closer or in the cone because hidden by the scenery), naissances_vues (births checked again in the exact camera image with free rays: it must stay 0), remplis and remplissages (pedestrians placed on arrival, and how many arrivals), reserve_ms and remplissage_ms (the pool and the arrival fill, outside the steps), naissance_la_plus_proche_m, importants (kept now), importants_touches, importants_devenus, importants_rendus, memoire_courte (pedestrians remembered now), revenus (came back the same), traces (ordinary traces now), traces_faites, laisses (what players left, kept now), trottoirs_m, modeles, reactions {dangers (received), dangers_vifs (still scaring now), fuyards (fleeing now), ont_fui (fled in all), voitures_arretees_pas (car steps held by fear), and the four peur_* values}, ms_par_pas, pire_ms, budget (the setting), niveaux (see Simulation levels), garees (the parked cars: part, cases, tirees, montrees, solides, plus_montrees, ms_par_pas, budget; also at the report's root as population_garees), cout {mesure_ms (the measured population step, parked cars included), estime_ms, estime_cpu_ms and estime_gpu_ms (the estimate of what lived at the busiest, same rates as city_perf), budget_ms (what the aimed machine allows, see below), qualite, images_s, and allegement when the cost is over the budget}, alerte (only when a rule is broken: a pedestrian or a car born in sight, more alive than a budget, a cost over the aimed machine's budget; one line each), and probleme when no model or no pavement was found. Its voitures part says the same for cars (vivantes, naissances, departs, naissances_vues...) plus arrets_au_feu (stops at a red light), arretees_au_feu (waiting at a red light now), attentes_carrefour (steps spent waiting to give way or for a free junction), ecart_min_m (the smallest bumper-to-bumper gap to the car in front: never under 2 m), ecart_gabarits_min_m (the smallest gap between the outlines of any two cars: above 0, no car goes through another), voies_m, feux (junctions with lights), its budget (the budget_voitures setting) and its own ms_par_pas and pire_ms.

items.title: Lightening on your own (the aimed machine)
items.text:
You estimate the cost of a request and lighten it yourself; the user does not have to ask. Never touch the models (no simpler mesh, no smaller texture) and never edit the module: only its settings.

  • The aimed machine is the game's performance targets (world_set performanceTargets: quality and fps; by default Medium at 60 fps). The population may take a share of each frame: 4% in low (a weak machine), 9% in medium (1.5 ms at 60 fps), 12% in high, 15% in ultra. That is budget_ms in city_perf's population part and in game_run's cout. Change the targets only when the user names another machine or frame rate.
  • Before raising a density (or filling a new city), call city_perf with {"population": {...}} and the values you want. Its population part gives cout_estime_ms, budget_ms and au_dessus_du_budget; when it is over, allegement gives modules_set values (budget, budget_voitures, garees_allegement: a factor on top of every zone's and the overall garees, so it also thins districts that set their own) and their cout_estime_ms, under the budget (sous_le_budget). Write them with modules_set (keeping the user's density: the streets look as full near the player, fewer live at the busiest point), and tell the user what you lowered, the cost before and after, and why.
  • game_run does the same from what really lived: when cout.mesure_ms plus the drawing, or cout.estime_ms, is over budget_ms, its cout.allegement proposes the same settings.
  • If it is still too high, in this order: shorten the reach (rayon_max, rayon_max_voitures, garees_portee), keep niveaux ticked (only the near ones get physics) and tick donnees (out of sight, only the place moves on), then lower curseur last (it thins the whole city). Run city_perf, then game_run again, and give the numbers.

items.title: Not yet
items.text:
Spinning wheels, real physics near the player, the fine view cone and walls, richer reactions (hiding, calling the police, cars swerving), being shoved hard, several players: later missions of the population design (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-26-population-dynamique-design.md).

This page is generated automatically from the WorldMint code (modules/population/module.json, modules/population/AGENT.md, modules/events.json): it always matches the editor.

items.title: Progression
items.text:
Experience, levels, points and characteristics (ADR-038). Tracks (the character, cooking, woodcutting...) each with its curve; XP for defeated enemies, quests, what is crafted or gathered and any free rule; rewards at each level (points, bonuses, knowledges, items); characteristics to spend points on; required levels; the reputation with each faction of the game (a track that can go down, with its tiers: Hostile, Neutral, Friendly); an XP bar, "Level 5!" and the Character window (P). The host keeps everyone's progression.

Identifier progression Version 9 Placed on objects no

items.title: Settings for the whole game
items.text:
In the Systems panel (Developer mode), by opening the system's card.

Setting What it does Name in code Type Default Limits or choices The progression tracks Each track has its XP, its levels and its curve: the character's level is one, "Cooking" or "Woodcutting" others. The main track (the level other players see) is chosen in the game settings, Progression section. pistes List of “Track” [{'cle': 'personnage', 'nom': 'Personnage', 'icone': '', 'cachee': False, 'courbe': {'forme': 'progressive', 'base': 100, 'hausse': 75, 'niveau_max': 50, 'paliers': [{'niveau': 20, 'facteur': 1.25}, {'niveau': 40, 'facteur': 1.25}], 'arrondi': 5, 'ecart': {'forme': 'lineaire', 'tolerance': 2, 'hausse': 0.1, 'plafond': 1.5, 'baisse': 0.2, 'plancher': 0.05}}, 'mort': 'aucune', 'mort_part': 10}] one line per “Track”: its fields Defeated enemies give their XP Each enemy's XP and level are set on it, in the Enemies system ("XP given", "Level"). An enemy stronger than the player gives more, after the curve's "gap". xp_ennemis Yes or no yes Finished quests give their XP The "XP" field of each quest, in the Quests system. xp_quetes Yes or no yes What is crafted gives its XP The "XP" field of each recipe, in the Crafting system. xp_fabrication Yes or no yes What is gathered gives its XP The "XP" field of each resource, in the Gathering system. xp_collecte Yes or no yes The reputation tiers The names a reputation takes after its value, each from its threshold: Hostile from -1000, Neutral from -100, Friendly from 100. Without a track, a tier applies to every reputation; a track with its own tiers only takes its own. The Character window shows the tier, the event progression.palier announces each change, and a Dialogue or a Trigger rule can ask for "at least Friendly". paliers List of “Tier” [{'piste': '', 'nom': 'Hostile', 'seuil': -1000}, {'piste': '', 'nom': 'Inamical', 'seuil': -300}, {'piste': '', 'nom': 'Neutre', 'seuil': -100}, {'piste': '', 'nom': 'Amical', 'seuil': 100}, {'piste': '', 'nom': 'Vénéré', 'seuil': 500}] one line per “Tier”: its fields Free rules: when this event happens, this much XP For everything else: "dialogue.fin" 20 XP, "zone.entree" on "Cave" 50 XP, "savoir.appris" 30 XP to the track "research". regles List of “Rule” (empty) one line per “Rule”: its fields XP for a place discovered (a zone, the first time) Each zone (an object carrying the Zone system) the player enters for the first time gives this XP to the main track. 0: nothing. xp_decouverte Number 0 from 0 to 1 000 000 The level gap counts Ticked: a stronger enemy gives more, a much weaker one almost nothing, after the "gap" of the track's curve. ecart_actif Yes or no yes Repetition gives less Ticked: the same action repeated often in a short time gives less and less. repetition_actif Yes or no no Repetition: how many times before it drops The number of gains from the same source, within the time window, before it drops. repetition_seuil Number 10 from 0 to 100 000, as a whole number Repetition: drop for each extra time (0 to 1) 0.1: each extra time gives 10 % less than the one before. repetition_baisse Number 0.1 from 0 to 1 Repetition: never less than (0 to 1) 0.1: even very repeated, the action keeps 10 % of its XP. repetition_plancher Number 0.1 from 0 to 1 Repetition: time window (s) Older gains no longer count. repetition_fenetre Number 300 from 1 to 86 400 First-time bonus (0.5: +50 %) The first enemy of a kind, the first resource, the first recipe give this bonus on top. 0: none. premiere_bonus Number 0.5 from 0 to 100 Multipliers per zone "×1.5 in the Burnt Lands": a zone (an object carrying the Zone system) by its name without number, or by a tag. zones List of “Zone” (empty) one line per “Zone”: its fields In a group: who gets an enemy's XP When several players fight. Nearby: within the radius below of the enemy, or who hit it. In proportion to the damage: the hits of Combat, Shooting and Enemies say who hit; without them, everything goes to the last hit. groupe Choice in a list Everyone gets it all (nearby players) tous: Everyone gets it all (nearby players)partage: Shared between nearby playersdegats: In proportion to the damagedernier: Only the last hit In a group: radius of nearby players (m) Players closer than this to the defeated enemy count. 0: only those who hit it. rayon_groupe Number 30 from 0 to 10 000 Death: radius to recover the lost XP (m) For tracks whose lost XP is recoverable: coming this close to where the player died returns it. rayon_recuperation Number 2.5 from 0.5 to 100 Death: what marks the XP to recover (optional) A hidden object of the scene, copied where the player died while the XP waits there (a grave, a glow). Empty: nothing shows. modele_recuperation Object of the scene (empty) The kinds of points The points levels give. A kind "for Knowledge" goes to the tree of the Knowledge system (its knowledges bought with points). points List of “Kind of points” [{'sorte': 'caracteristique', 'nom': 'Points de caractéristique', 'savoir': False}, {'sorte': 'talent', 'nom': 'Points de talent', 'savoir': True}] one line per “Kind of points”: its fields What a level gives Each row: at which levels, and what. No name is imposed. caracteristiques List of “Row” [{'sorte': 'caracteristique', 'nom': 'Force', 'description': 'Des coups plus forts, et plus de charge.', 'max': 20, 'cout': 1, 'points_sorte': 'caracteristique'}, {'sorte': 'effet', 'valeur': 'degats', 'ajout': 0, 'pourcent': 5}, {'sorte': 'effet', 'valeur': 'charge_max', 'ajout': 2, 'pourcent': 0}, {'sorte': 'caracteristique', 'nom': 'Vigueur', 'description': 'Plus de vie et de souffle.', 'max': 20, 'cout': 1, 'points_sorte': 'caracteristique'}, {'sorte': 'effet', 'valeur': 'sante_max', 'ajout': 10, 'pourcent': 0}, {'sorte': 'effet', 'valeur': 'endurance_max', 'ajout': 5, 'pourcent': 0}, {'sorte': 'caracteristique', 'nom': 'Agilité', 'description': 'Courir plus vite.', 'max': 10, 'cout': 1, 'points_sorte': 'caracteristique'}, {'sorte': 'effet', 'valeur': 'vitesse_deplacement', 'ajout': 0, 'pourcent': 2}] one line per “Row”: its fields The player can reset their characteristics A "Reset" button in the Character window gives the spent points back. reinitialiser Yes or no yes Reset cost: item (empty: free) A kind of inventory item, such as "Gold". reinit_objet Text (empty) Reset cost: how many How many of that item. reinit_nombre Number 1 from 1 to 1 000 000, as a whole number Extra values (for scripts) The module already declares sante_max, degats, endurance_max, endurance_recuperation, inventaire_places, charge_max, vitesse_recolte, vitesse_fabrication and vitesse_deplacement. Add more (a defence, a critical chance): a script reads them with game.stat(player, name). valeurs List of “Value” (empty) one line per “Value”: its fields The required levels "Level 10" for a sword, "Cooking 5" for a recipe. Checked on the host; the refusal says what is needed. requis List of “Required level” (empty) one line per “Required level”: its fields Enemies: how they grow with their level An enemy's health, damage and XP grow for each level above the first. croissance_forme Choice in a list Linear: the same addition at each level lineaire: Linear: the same addition at each levelexponentielle: Exponential: faster and faster Enemies: extra health per level (0.08: +8 %) Per level above the first. croissance_sante Number 0.08 from 0 to 10 Enemies: extra damage per level Per level above the first. croissance_degats Number 0.05 from 0 to 10 Enemies: extra XP per level Per level above the first. croissance_xp Number 0.1 from 0 to 10 Enemies growing with time: minutes of a game day Without the Day and night system: the length of a day that counts. In the Properties, each “Track” has its own numbered frame; Add: Track adds one, the cross removes it. A field only appears when it is useful: under its name, the table says when.

Setting What it does Name in code Type Default Limits or choices Kind of track XP, which only goes up, and levels after its curve; or a reputation with a faction of your game (the bandits, the guard, a village): a value that goes up and down, even below zero, between two bounds, with its tiers (Hostile, Neutral, Friendly...) set below. A quest, a Trigger rule or a script changes it with the event progression.reputation. sorte Choice in a list XP and levels xp: XP and levelsreputation: A reputation with a faction Identifier (lowercase, no space) The track's short name in events, sources and required levels, such as "personnage" or "cooking". Do not change it once the game is out: the save keeps it. cle Text (empty) Name the player sees Such as "Character" or "Cooking", translated into the player's language. nom Text (empty) Icon (optional) A small image before its name in the Character window. icone Image from the library (empty) Hidden until it has started Ticked: the window only shows it after the first XP earned on it, like a discovery. cachee Yes or no no Starting reputationshown only if Kind of track is “A reputation with a faction” Where each player stands the first time: 0 (neutral), -200 for a faction that is wary at first. depart Number 0 from -1 000 000 000 to 1 000 000 000 Lowest reputationshown only if Kind of track is “A reputation with a faction” The reputation never goes lower: -1000, the bottom of the lowest tier. min Number -1000 from -1 000 000 000 to 1 000 000 000 Highest reputationshown only if Kind of track is “A reputation with a faction” The reputation never goes higher: 1000. max Number 1000 from -1 000 000 000 to 1 000 000 000 Curve: the XP of each levelshown only if Kind of track is “XP and levels” How much XP each level costs: a formula, a table pasted from a spreadsheet, steps. The editor draws it, offers presets and simulates the play time. Its "gap" sets what a stronger or weaker enemy gives. courbe Progression curve {'forme': 'progressive', 'base': 100, 'hausse': 50, 'niveau_max': 50} When the player diesshown only if Kind of track is “XP and levels” What death costs on this track. One never goes down a level. Recoverable: the XP waits where the player died; going back there returns it (dying again before erases the old one). mort Choice in a list No loss on death aucune: No loss on deathpart: A share of the current level's XP is lostrecuperable: A share lost, recoverable where the player died Share lost (% of the current level's XP)shown only if Kind of track is “XP and levels” ; shown only if When the player dies is “A share of the current level's XP is lost” or “A share lost, recoverable where the player died” 10: a tenth of what was earned since the last level. mort_part Number 10 from 0 to 100

items.title: Events
items.text: The descriptions come from the code.

items.title: What it announces
items.text: Event Fields Description progression.depenser joueur (id?), caracteristique (text) Ask the Progression module to spend points on one rank of a characteristic (its name, as in its row) for the player: the host checks the points and the maximum, then answers progression.depense or progression.refus. The Character window sends it. progression.reinitialiser joueur (id?) Ask the Progression module to give back the points spent on characteristics (if the game allows it, for its cost). Answers progression.reinitialise or progression.refus. progression.depense joueur (id), caracteristique (text), rang (number) A rank of a characteristic was bought: rang is its new rank. Its bonuses are already applied. progression.refus joueur (id), raison (text) Something was refused to the player by the Progression module: a required level (an item, a door, a zone), points missing, a maximum reached. raison is the text shown, already in the player's language. progression.recompense joueur (id), piste (text), niveau (number), sorte (text), nom (text), nombre (number) A level gave one of its rewards: sorte is points, bonus, connaissance, objet, marque or evenement; nom its kind of points, value, knowledge, item, mark or event; nombre how many. progression.niveau_ennemi cible (id), niveau (number) The Progression module gave an enemy its level (fixed, per zone, matched to the players or growing with time): its health and damage grew with it. To show it above its head. progression.perte joueur (id), piste (text), xp (number), recuperable (boolean) The player died and lost xp on a track (never below its level). recuperable: the XP waits where they died. progression.recupere joueur (id), piste (text), xp (number) The player came back where they died and recovered the xp lost on a track. progression.reinitialise joueur (id), points (number) The characteristics were reset: points is how many points came back. progression.reputation_change joueur (id), piste (text), valeur (number), avant (number), ecart (number), palier (text), source (text?) A player's reputation with a faction changed (Progression 9): valeur is the new value, avant the old one, ecart the change, palier the name of its tier now. To show it, or for a Trigger rule. progression.palier joueur (id), piste (text), palier (text), ancien (text), rang (number), monte (boolean), valeur (number) A player's reputation reached another tier (Progression 9): palier is the new tier's name, ancien the old one's, rang its rank from 1 (the lowest), monte true if it went up. For the game to react: guards that attack once Hostile, a shop that opens once Friendly. savoir.donner_points points (number), joueur (id?) Ask the knowledge system to give points to the player (version 26), to spend in the knowledge window: a level gained, a book read. savoir.apprendre connaissance (text), joueur (id?) Ask the knowledge system to teach connaissance to the player (version 26), even without what it needs first: a Trigger rule, a master in a Dialogue, a quest's reward. A game script can still refuse it (savoir.permise). inventaire.ajouter objet (text), quantite (number), joueur (id?), fiche (number?) Ask the inventory to add items, such as a reward. Answered by inventaire.change, or inventaire.plein. With several players, joueur says whose bag; without it, the player whose action is being handled, or every player. inventaire.retirer objet (text), quantite (number), fiche (number?) Ask the inventory to remove items, such as a payment. Answered by inventaire.change, or inventaire.manque if there are not enough. For a kind with unique copies (version 15): fiche removes that copy, otherwise the first ones; their records are destroyed. dialogue.marquer marque (text), retirer (boolean?) Ask the dialogue system to set a mark, from a script or another system; with retirer true, to remove it. Dialogue conditions then see it.

items.title: What it listens to
items.text: Event Fields Description progression.xp joueur (id?), cle (text), piste (text), gain (number), xp (number), niveau (number), source (text) Sent by the engine (ADR-038) when a player gained XP on a track (game.progress_add_xp): gain is what was given after the global multiplier and the cap, xp the track's total, niveau its level, source where it came from, cle the player's key. progression.niveau joueur (id?), cle (text), piste (text), niveau (number), ancien (number) Sent by the engine for each level a player reached on a track (several levels at once: several events), also when an admin sets a level. The Progression module gives the rewards of that level; a Trigger rule can play a sound or open a door. progression.depenser joueur (id?), caracteristique (text) Ask the Progression module to spend points on one rank of a characteristic (its name, as in its row) for the player: the host checks the points and the maximum, then answers progression.depense or progression.refus. The Character window sends it. progression.depense joueur (id), caracteristique (text), rang (number) A rank of a characteristic was bought: rang is its new rank. Its bonuses are already applied. progression.reinitialiser joueur (id?) Ask the Progression module to give back the points spent on characteristics (if the game allows it, for its cost). Answers progression.reinitialise or progression.refus. progression.reinitialise joueur (id), points (number) The characteristics were reset: points is how many points came back. progression.refus joueur (id), raison (text) Something was refused to the player by the Progression module: a required level (an item, a door, a zone), points missing, a maximum reached. raison is the text shown, already in the player's language. progression.perte joueur (id), piste (text), xp (number), recuperable (boolean) The player died and lost xp on a track (never below its level). recuperable: the XP waits where they died. progression.recupere joueur (id), piste (text), xp (number) The player came back where they died and recovered the xp lost on a track. progression.donner joueur (id?), xp (number), piste (text?), source (text?) Ask the Progression module to give xp to the player (a Trigger rule, a script): it goes through the multipliers and the hook progression.gain, on the host. piste: a track's identifier (empty or missing: the main one); source: a short name for the repetition and the cap. progression.reputation joueur (id?), piste (text), faction (text?), valeur (number), fixer (boolean?), groupe (boolean?), source (text?) Ask the Progression module to change the player's reputation with a faction (Progression 9): piste is a track of kind reputation (faction is accepted too); valeur is added (negative: it goes down), or set when fixer is true; it stays within the track's bounds. Sent by a quest, a step or a way to end it (its reputation field), a Trigger rule or a script. groupe: every player present. progression.reputation_change joueur (id), piste (text), valeur (number), avant (number), ecart (number), palier (text), source (text?) A player's reputation with a faction changed (Progression 9): valeur is the new value, avant the old one, ecart the change, palier the name of its tier now. To show it, or for a Trigger rule. progression.palier joueur (id), piste (text), palier (text), ancien (text), rang (number), monte (boolean), valeur (number) A player's reputation reached another tier (Progression 9): palier is the new tier's name, ancien the old one's, rang its rank from 1 (the lowest), monte true if it went up. For the game to react: guards that attack once Hostile, a shop that opens once Friendly. progression.ouvrir joueur (id?) Ask the Progression module to open the Character window of the player, as its key (P) does. sante.mort cible (id), source (id?) An object's health reached zero. What happens next belongs to the game: the health module does nothing else, unless its setting says to destroy the object. sante.blesser cible (id), montant (number), source (id?) Ask the health module to remove health from an object. quetes.fin quete (text), xp (number?), piste (text?), groupe (boolean?), facultatives (table?) A quest is finished: all its steps are done. Its reward, if any, has been asked to the inventory. xp and piste (version 28): its XP for the Progression module and the track that gets it (empty: the main one). facultatives (Journal de quêtes 11): {faites, total}, how many of its optional steps were done, out of how many; absent when it has none. groupe (Journal de quêtes 8): true for a quest of the whole group (game setting groupe), sent once for the group, joueur being who moved it on. fabrication.fabrique objet (text), quantite (number), etabli (text), cible (text?), xp (number?), piste (text?) The player crafted a recipe: its ingredients left the inventory and objet (quantite of it) came in, at once or at the end of its time in the queue. etabli is the kind of station where it was made (empty bare-handed), cible the station object (missing bare-handed). collecte.recolte cible (id), ressource (text), quantite (number), joueur (id?), xp (number?), piste (text?) A resource was used up and gave what it holds. The inventory, if present, has been asked to add it. zone.entree cible (id), qui (id), joueur (id?) Something entered a zone (an object carrying the zone system): a player, a character or a moving object, depending on what the zone detects (joueur: every player). joueur is set when qui is a player. Announced by the engine. zone.sortie cible (id), qui (id), joueur (id?) Something left a zone. Not announced for an object removed from the game while inside. jour_nuit.lever jour (number) The sun rose: day jour begins. Lamps tagged for the night went out. joueur.arrivee joueur (id), numero (number), nom (text) Sent by the engine, in a game with several players (the game setting Multiplayer), on the computer hosting the game, when a guest joins: joueur is their character (a copy of the player's), numero their place (1 to 7, the host being 0), nom the name they chose. game.players() lists them all. Scripts only run on the host. joueur.profil joueur (id), profil (table), nouveau (boolean) Sent by the engine on the host (ADR-020 § 18) when a player enters with a character: joueur is their character, profil the choices they made on their own PC (game.profile_send) once the game's check accepted them (game.override("profil.verifier")), nouveau true for a character just created, false for one this world's save already had. The script applies only what it understands (hair, colors, name): the profile is plain data and can never give items or progress. Also sent on the host or in solo when the player on this PC calls game.profile_send. joueur.reconnecte joueur (id), numero (number), nom (text) Sent by the engine on the host when a guest whose connection dropped comes back in time and takes their place again: same character, same bag, the same per-player scripts that kept running (no joueur.depart nor joueur.arrivee was sent). Meanwhile their character stood still. A module can show them a message or resend what is only shown once. joueur.depart joueur (id), numero (number) Sent by the engine on the host when a guest leaves the game (they quit, or their connection was lost and they did not come back in time, the game setting Place kept after a drop): their character is removed right after. A module forgets what it kept for them. inventaire.manque objet (text), quantite (number), fiche (number?) Items could not be removed: there are not enough. scene.change depuis (text), vers (text) Sent by the engine once the player has arrived in another scene of the game (game.go_to, or a passage). Scripts keep running across scenes: this is when a module looks at the objects of the new scene. langue.change langue (text) Sent by the engine when the player changes the game's language (game.set_language, the Menu options). A module redraws what it already shows: its texts go through game.t and game.language.

items.title: Points a script can replace (game.override)
items.text:
The descriptions come from the code.

  • progression.gain: function(default, joueur, piste, xp, source) -> the XP given (a number; 0: nothing). Called before each gain, after the multipliers (level gap, repetition, first time, zone; the global multiplier comes after, in the engine). piste is the track's key, source names where it comes from (ennemi:Loup, quete:Titre, fabrication:Hache, collecte:Bois, regle:event, recuperation). For double XP at night, a bonus with a ring, nothing for a track in a place.
  • progression.requis: function(default, joueur, sorte, nom, piste, niveau) -> true, or false and the text shown: whether the player may use what asks for a level. sorte: objet (hold or use an item), recette, connaissance, objet_monde (use an object of the world: a door), zone (enter a zone). The default compares the player's level on piste with niveau. To ask for a quest done, a knowledge, two tracks at once.
  • progression.texte: function(default, key) -> the text shown for that key: titre, niveau, niveau_court, gain, monte, points, caracteristiques, depenser, reinitialiser, reinit_cout, fermer, pas_de_points, max_atteint, refus_requis, perdu, recupere, rien, xp, reputation (a reputation's value in the window: {n}, {min}, {max}), palier (a tier reached: {piste}, {nom}). It may hold {n}, {piste}, {xp}, {requis}, {nom}, {niveau}, {objet}, replaced afterwards (in the player's language). The default is the game's translation of the text in the original language; without one, French or English, after the player's language.

items.title: What the agent knows about this system
items.text: The text the agent reads before using this system.

items.title: Progression (progression)
items.text: Experience, levels, points to spend and characteristics (ADR-038): the « level up » of RPGs, survival and action games, as user data. Add it once with modules_add when the user asks for levels, XP, skills that rise with use, characteristics (strength, agility...) or talent points; never write an XP script. The engine keeps the progress of each player (in the world's save, under their key; only the host writes); this module decides where XP comes from, how much, and what a level gives. Change what it does through its settings, its events and its hooks (game.override), never by editing it.

items.title: Tracks (pistes)
items.text: Each row is a track: cle (identifier, lowercase: personnage, cuisine, bucheronnage), nom (shown, translated), icone, cachee (hidden in the window until its first XP), courbe (type curve: the XP of each level; the editor draws it, offers the presets « RPG classique », « Survie lente », « Arcade rapide », « Hardcore » and simulates the play time; its ecart sets what a stronger or weaker enemy gives), mort (aucune by default, part: lose mort_part % of the XP earned since the last level, never a level; recuperable: the same, but the XP waits where the player died, and coming back there returns it). The main track (the level others see) is the game setting progression.mainTrack (« personnage » by default). Tune a curve with progression_simulate, then modules_set.

items.title: Reputation (tracks of sorte reputation, version 9)
items.text:
The reputation with each faction of the game is a track too: sorte reputation (default xp), one row per faction the user names (bandits, garde, village; the module ships none, never invent one), with depart (each player's value the first time, 0 by default), min and max (bounds, -1000 and 1000 by default). It goes up and down, below zero too (the engine keeps it like XP, game.progress_define(cle, courbe, {sous_zero = true}), in the save and for guests); its level stays 1 and it gets no XP (progression.donner, quests, rules: refused, game log). Its tiers are the list paliers: nom (shown, translated), seuil (the tier starts there), piste (empty: for every reputation; a track with its own rows takes only its own). Defaults: Hostile -1000, Inamical -300, Neutre -100, Amical 100, Vénéré 500; tune them with modules_set.

  • Change it: emit progression.reputation {piste (or faction), valeur (added; negative lowers it), fixer? (true: set it), joueur?, groupe? (every player present)}; it stays within min..max. A quest, a step or an issue (a branch) does it with its fields reputation and reputation_valeur (system quetes); a declencheur rule with envoyer; a dialogue answer with its annonce event and a rule. Never write a reputation script.
  • Its events: progression.reputation_change {joueur, piste, valeur, avant, ecart, palier}, and progression.palier {joueur, piste, palier, ancien, rang, monte, valeur} when the tier changes (guards that attack once Hostile: a declencheur rule on it). The player sees « Bandits : Hostile » for a moment.
  • Read it: a dialogue answer's or a declencheur rule's condition reputation (condition_piste, condition_palier: a tier's name, at least that tier, or a number, at least that value). A game script: shared.progression_reputation(joueur, piste, palier?) -> {valeur, min, max, palier, rang, nombre, atteint}, or the raw value game.progress(joueur).pistes[piste].xp.
  • The Character window shows each reputation with its tier in place of the level, its value and its bounds (« -250 (-1000 à 1000) »), its bar from min to max.

items.title: Where XP comes from
items.text:
• Enemies: on each enemy group, in the ennemis system: xp (at its first level; 0: none), piste_xp (empty: the main track), its level niveau_mode = fixe (niveau), zone (random between niveau_min and niveau_max), joueurs (the players' average level + niveau_ecart, within niveau_min..niveau_max) or temps (+1 level every jours_par_niveau game days from niveau, up to niveau_plafond; a day is a sunrise of jour_nuit, or minutes_par_jour). Its level grows its health (croissance_sante, +8 % per level), damage (croissance_degats) and XP (croissance_xp), croissance_forme linear or exponential. Switch off with xp_ennemis.
  • Quests (quetes, on the quest row: xp, piste_xp), recipes (fabrication, on the recipe row: xp, piste_xp), resources (collecte, per object: xp, piste_xp); switches xp_quetes, xp_fabrication, xp_collecte. A quest of the whole group (quetes game setting groupe, its quetes.fin carries groupe: true) gives its XP to every player present, each on their own track with their own « +XP »; any other quest, to the player who finishes it.
  • Places discovered: xp_decouverte for the first entry in each zone (zone system).
  • Free rules (regles): evenement, cible (only for the object named), piste, xp, fois (toujours or une: once per player). E.g. dialogue.fin 20, savoir.appris 30 to recherche, boutique.achat 2 to commerce.
  • Anything else: emit progression.donner {xp, piste?, source?} from a script or a Trigger rule (envoyer).

items.title: How much
items.text:
The amount is multiplied by: the level gap (ecart_actif, the curve's ecart); repetition (repetition_actif, repetition_seuil gains of the same source within repetition_fenetre seconds, then −repetition_baisse each, never below repetition_plancher); the first time (premiere_bonus, 0.5 = +50 % for the first enemy of a kind, first resource, first recipe); zones (zones: a zone's name without number, or a tag, and its multiplicateur); then the hook progression.gain; the engine applies the global multiplier (progression.xpMultiplier × a dedicated server's xp_multiplicateur) and the per-minute cap.

In a group (groupe): tous (default: each nearby player gets it all), partage (split between nearby players), degats (in proportion to the damage each dealt: Combat, Shooting and Enemies say who hit; with no damage known, the last hit gets it all), dernier (the last hit only). Nearby: within rayon_groupe metres of the enemy, or who hit it.

items.title: What a level gives (recompenses)
items.text: Rows: piste (empty: the main one), quand (tous, liste with niveaux « 5, 10, 20 », chaque every chaque levels from a_partir), sorte: points (points_sorte, nombre), bonus (valeur, ajout +n and/or pourcent +%, added for each such level: « +10 sante_max per level »), connaissance (nom: learnt in savoir), objet (nom, nombre: into the inventory), marque (nom: a Dialogue / quest mark), evenement (nom: an event with joueur, piste, niveau, for a Trigger rule: a sound, a door). Kinds of points: points rows (sorte, nom shown, savoir: those points go to the Knowledge system's tree, as savoir.donner_points). progression.niveau is also announced by the engine for each level.

items.title: Characteristics (caracteristiques)
items.text: A caracteristique row (nom, description, max rank, cout points per rank, points_sorte) followed by its effet rows (valeur, ajout per rank, pourcent per rank). No name is imposed (Force, Vigueur, Agilité are examples). The player spends in the Character window; reinitialiser allows a reset, for reinit_nombre × reinit_objet (empty: free).

items.title: Values
items.text: The module declares the values it drives, read by the other systems with their own setting as base: sante_max (Santé: max health; health follows when it rises), degats (Combat: the player's hits; Ennemis: an enemy's hits and shots), endurance_max, endurance_recuperation (Endurance), inventaire_places (Inventaire: slots), charge_max (Inventaire: the maximum load, when its weight poids_actif is on; « Force: +2 kg of load per point » is an effet row charge_max ajout 2, in the default characteristics), vitesse_recolte (Collecte: divides the hits a resource needs), vitesse_fabrication (Fabrication: divides a recipe's time), vitesse_deplacement (the engine: walk, run, swim; the inventory's weight adds a negative bonus from the source « poids », down to 0 when it stops the player). valeurs adds more for scripts (game.stat(player, name)). Without this module, those systems behave as before. Bonuses are given again from the saved progress at the start, when a player arrives and after a load.

items.title: Required levels (requis)
items.text: Rows: sorte (objet: holding or using an inventory item; recette; connaissance; objet_monde: using an object, a door, by its name without number; zone: entering a zone, the player is pushed back), nom, piste, niveau, message (with {niveau} and {piste}; empty: « Il faut le niveau 5 (Personnage). »). Checked on the host. The hook progression.requis can ask for more (a quest done, two tracks).

items.title: What the player sees
items.text:
Above heads (noms_tetes, off by default since the engine shows no name above heads; distance_noms, 30 m): the name and main level of each other player nearby, « Léa · Niv. 5 », on every player's screen (theme role nom.joueur; the head is measured on the body). Turn it on when the user wants players to see each other's level.

A Group panel made by a game script: game.players() lists the players, game.player_name(id) their names and game.progress_level(id) their main level; both work in a guest's game too, for every player (the host sends them, protocol 17 and 24). E.g. one game.hud_text line per player, game.player_name(p) .. " · " .. game.progress_level(p), redrawn on progression.niveau and joueur.arrivee/joueur.depart. A Group panel already written by the game (Naufragés' « Groupe ») is a script of the game: to show the level there, edit that script (not a module), adding game.progress_level(p) after each player's name on the line it draws.

An XP bar of the main track with its level (barre, barre_x, barre_y, barre_largeur, barre_hauteur, barre_couleur); when the Inventory's quick bar is where the XP bar is set (at the bottom, by default), the XP bar sits just above it, as wide as it. « +45 XP » for a moment, above the bar on the right (afficher_gain, duree_gain; another track says its name: « +30 XP (Récolte) »); « Niveau 5 ! » (annoncer_niveau, son_niveau, effet_niveau, duree_niveau); the Character window (action character, key P; fenetre, pause_fenetre, largeur): one row per track (level, bar, XP), the points, the characteristics with their « Améliorer » buttons (« Maximum » at the top rank), the reset. A guest's clicks are checked by the host. Texts: hook progression.texte.

Its screens (version 8). These are screens the system delivers as data, each player seeing their own: « Barre d'expérience » (Fond, Barre, the level label Étiquette with Niveau; its place follows barre_x/barre_y/barre_largeur/barre_hauteur, or sits above the Inventory's « Barre rapide »), « Gain d'expérience » (Fond, Gain: « +45 XP », at the bar's right end), « Passage de niveau » (Annonce: « Niveau 5 ! »), « Messages de la progression » (Message, and Refus for a refusal, at the top while the window is closed) and « Fiche du personnage » (the Character window: Fenêtre, Titre, the list Pistes whose rows hold Piste with Nom, Niveau, Barre, XP, or Rien; Caractéristiques, Points, the list Liste des caractéristiques whose rows Rangée hold Caractéristique and the button Améliorer (action ameliorer), Réinitialiser (action reinitialiser), Message, Refus, Fermer (action fermer, B or Escape)). Their keys in game_run are screen/shape (Fiche du personnage/Améliorer#2, Gain d'expérience/Gain). To change their look, size, colours or texts' style, the user edits them in the screen editor (Game tab, Interface screens), or you change them with screens_set; never edit the module. largeur scales the window and its rows from the sizes of its file. Only the name above heads (progression.tete.<player>) is still drawn by the script.

items.title: Hooks
items.text:
• progression.gain: function(default, joueur, piste, xp, source) return xp * 2 end (double XP at night).
  • progression.requis: function(default, joueur, sorte, nom, piste, niveau) ... return false, "Finish the Old Mine first." end.
  • progression.texte: function(default, cle) if cle == "monte" then return "LEVEL {n}!" end return default(cle) end.

items.title: Presets by genre
items.text:
• RPG classique: one track personnage, curve « RPG classique », enemies fixe or zone, groupe tous, rewards 1 characteristic point per level, +10 sante_max per level, a talent point every 5 levels (savoir), quests 100 to 500 XP; Force +5 % degats and +2 charge_max (kg of load) per point.
  • Survie lente: tracks personnage plus recolte/fabrication (curve « Survie lente »), XP mostly from collecte and fabrication (5 to 20 each), enemies temps (+1 level every 2 days), repetition_actif, rewards vitesse_recolte +3 % per level of recolte; with the inventory's weight, +5 charge_max every 5 levels of personnage.
  • Arcade rapide: curve « Arcade rapide » (20 levels), enemies joueurs (the group's level), ecart_actif off, groupe partage, big « Niveau ! » announcements, +5 % degats per level.
  • Hardcore: curve « Hardcore », mort recuperable with mort_part 50, enemies zone, groupe dernier, repetition_actif, no reset (reinitialiser off).

This page is generated automatically from the WorldMint code (modules/progression/module.json, modules/progression/AGENT.md, modules/events.json): it always matches the editor.

items.title: Quest log
items.text:
The game's quests and their steps, which move on by themselves: on an event (a Trigger rule, a Dialogue answer, an enemy defeated), a Dialogue mark, items carried or handed over, a place reached, a time held. A step can have other ways to end that lead elsewhere (branches), be optional, or fail for several reasons. A finished quest can give a reward; a quest can also fail (an event, a mark, time running out, an item lost, the player too far) or be abandoned from the log, then be taken up again from the start, at the failed step or at the last checkpoint. A quest can also be a template, with holes such as {lieu}: during the game, quetes.creer makes a real quest from it ("Delivery 3"), its holes filled by a script, a Trigger rule or a draw (a shop at random, at such a distance). A log opens with J, and a notification announces each new quest, each step and each end.

Identifier quetes Version 18 Placed on objects no

items.title: Settings for the whole game
items.text:
In the Systems panel (Developer mode), by opening the system's card.

Setting What it does Name in code Type Default Limits or choices The quests and their steps Each quest is a "Quest" row, followed by its steps, in order. A quest starts when the game starts, on an event, a mark or the end of another; it ends when all its steps are done. It can also fail, or be abandoned by the player. Under a step, an "Other way to end the step" row gives another way to finish it; under a quest or a step, an "Also fails if" row adds a reason to fail; a "Test" row chooses what comes next by a mark or an item carried. quetes List of “Row” (empty) one line per “Row”: its fields Log with a key (J) Ticked: the Open the quest log control (J, or → on a gamepad) opens a window with the quests in progress, their steps, and the finished ones. The same key closes it. fenetre Yes or no yes Stop the game while the log is open Ticked: the world stops while the log is open. Unticked: the game goes on behind it, enemies included. pause_fenetre Yes or no yes Announce quests and steps on screen Ticked: a small message at the top of the screen announces a new quest, a step done and a finished quest, with its reward. notifications Yes or no yes Duration of an announcement (s) How many seconds of play each announcement stays on screen.
