It waits during a pause. duree_notification Number 4 from 1 to 30 Show the current step on screen Ticked: on the right of the screen, the title of the latest quest started and what is left to do, with the progress (2/5). suivi Yes or no yes Group quests (several players) In a game with several players: ticked, the quests belong to the whole group. Any player moves a step on, everyone sees the same step and the same tracker, and the quest ends for everyone; a player who arrives during the game finds where the group is. Unticked, each player has their own quests. No effect with one player. groupe Yes or no no Reward of a group quest With "Group quests": to the group, once, the reward goes into the Inventory's shared bag if it is ticked, otherwise into the bag of the player who finishes the quest; to each player, every player present gets it in their bag. recompense_groupe Choice in a list To the group, once groupe: To the group, oncechacun: To each player Day of a quest to do again For "Once a day" quests: a day of the game starts at sunrise of the Day and night system (without it, the day does not change); a real day, at midnight, by the computer's date (the host's). jour_repetition Choice in a list A day of the game (Day and night) jeu: A day of the game (Day and night)reel: A real day (the date)

items.title: The fields of each “Row”
items.text:
In the Properties, each “Row” has its own numbered frame; Add: Row adds one, the cross removes it. A field only appears when it is useful: under its name, the table says when.

Setting What it does Name in code Type Default Limits or choices Kind of row A quest, with its title, its start and its reward; a step, which belongs to the quest above it; another way to end the step above; a test, which chooses what comes next; one more reason to fail, for the quest or the step above; a prerequisite of the quest above, without which it is not given; under a template, a random draw that fills one of its holes; or one more reward (an item, XP, loot, a mark), given at the end of the quest, the step or the way to end it above. sorte Choice in a list Quest quete: Questetape: Stepissue: Other way to end the steptest: Testechec: Also fails ifcondition: Only if (prerequisite)tirage: Random draw (template)recompense: Reward Titleshown only if Kind of row is “Quest” The quest's name, such as "The mill's wolves": the log and the notifications show it, and events name it by it. titre Text (empty) Descriptionshown only if Kind of row is “Quest” One or two sentences under the title, in the log: who asks for it, and why. description Text (empty) Template (quests made during the game)shown only if Kind of row is “Quest” Ticked: this quest never starts by itself and is not in the log. Its texts and places have holes, such as "Deliver the parcel to {lieu}"; the event quetes.creer, or its starting event, makes a real quest from it, "Delivery 1", "Delivery 2"… with the holes filled: by the script or the Trigger rule that sends it, otherwise by its "Random draw" rows. {n} in a step's text is also the number to reach. modele Yes or no no Startsshown only if Kind of row is “Quest” What gives the quest to the player: the start of the game, an event (a Dialogue answer, a Trigger rule), a Dialogue mark, or the end of another quest. The event quetes.demarrer gives it too. depart Choice in a list When the game starts debut: When the game startsevenement: When an event happensmarque: When a mark is setquete: When another quest ends Event nameshown only if Kind of row is “Quest” ; shown only if Starts is “When an event happens” The exact name of the event that gives the quest, such as "wolves.accepted", sent by a Dialogue answer or a Trigger rule. depart_evenement Text (empty) Markshown only if Kind of row is “Quest” ; shown only if Starts is “When a mark is set” The mark's word, set by a Dialogue, such as "met_the_miller". If it is already set, the quest starts at once. depart_marque Text (empty) Title of the quest beforeshown only if Kind of row is “Quest” ; shown only if Starts is “When another quest ends” The exact title of the quest that must be finished for this one to start: a chain of quests. depart_quete Text (empty) Character who gives it (optional)shown only if Kind of row is “Quest” The character above whom the Map shows a "!" while the quest can be given. Empty: each character whose Dialogue sends the starting event or sets the starting mark. Useful when a Trigger rule gives it near them. donneur Object of the scene (empty) Steps one after the othershown only if Kind of row is “Quest” Ticked: a step only starts once the previous one is done, and the log does not show the next ones yet. Unticked: all the steps are to do at the same time, in any order. dans_l_ordre Yes or no yes Givesshown only if Kind of row is “Reward” What this reward gives, once, at the end of the quest, the step or the way to end it above it: an item and how many (the inventory), XP (the Progression system), a table of the Loot system (rolled and dropped near the player), or a mark (like the Dialogue's). Add one row per reward. The quest log shows the item and the XP to come, the end announcement names them. donne Choice in a list An item objet: An itemxp: XPbutin: A loot tablemarque: A mark Reward: kind of item (empty: none)shown only if Kind of row is “Quest” or “Reward” ; shown only if Gives is “” or “An item” The item the inventory receives when the quest ends (or, on a "Reward" row, what is above it), such as "Gold" or "Sword". Empty: no reward. More rewards: "Reward" rows under the quest. recompense Text (empty) How many as a rewardshown only if Kind of row is “Quest” or “Reward” ; shown only if Gives is “” or “An item” How many of the reward: 50 for 50 gold coins. recompense_quantite Number 1 from 1 to 1 000 000, as a whole number XP givenshown only if Kind of row is “Reward” ; shown only if Gives is “XP” The XP earned, if the game has the Progression system (it goes through its multipliers). With several players, each player present gets it for a quest of the group. donne_xp Number 0 from 0 to 1 000 000 Track that gets the XP (empty: the main one)shown only if Kind of row is “Reward” ; shown only if Gives is “XP” The identifier of a track of the Progression system, such as "smithing". donne_piste Text (empty) Loot tableshown only if Kind of row is “Reward” ; shown only if Gives is “A loot table” The name of a table of the Loot system: it is rolled and what it gives drops near the player (or in their bag, depending on the Loot settings). donne_table Text (empty) Mark setshown only if Kind of row is “Reward” ; shown only if Gives is “A mark” The word of a mark, such as "bridge_repaired": the Dialogues, tests and other quests see it. The player does not see it. donne_marque Text (empty) XP reward (Progression system)shown only if Kind of row is “Quest” The XP gained when the quest is done, if the game has the Progression system. 0: none. xp Number 0 from 0 to 1 000 000 Track that gets the XP (empty: the main one)shown only if Kind of row is “Quest” The identifier of a track of the Progression system. piste_xp Text (empty) Failsshown only if Kind of row is “Quest” or “Also fails if” What makes the quest in progress fail: an event (the merchant to escort dies), a Dialogue mark (the guard was betrayed), a time limit, a lost item (the parcel to deliver) or the player too far from a place. A failed quest stops, without a reward. The event quetes.echouer makes it fail too. On an "Also fails if" row: one more reason, for the quest or the step above; "Never" does nothing. echec Choice in a list Never aucun: Neverevenement: When an event happensmarque: When a mark is settemps: When time runs outobjet: When the player loses an itemeloigne: When the player goes too far Event nameshown only if Kind of row is “Quest” or “Also fails if” ; shown only if Fails is “When an event happens” The exact name of the event that makes the quest fail, such as "sante.mort". It only counts during the quest. echec_evenement Text (empty) Only for the object named (empty: any)shown only if Kind of row is “Quest” or “Also fails if” ; shown only if Fails is “When an event happens” The name of the object the event must be about, without number: with sante.mort and "Merchant", the quest fails if the merchant dies. echec_cible Text (empty) Markshown only if Kind of row is “Quest” or “Also fails if” ; shown only if Fails is “When a mark is set” The word of the mark that makes the quest fail, set by a Dialogue or another quest, such as "guard_betrayed". If it is already set, the quest fails at once (only with "The quest fails": starting again or going to a label waits for it to be set during the quest). echec_marque Text (empty) Time to finish it (s)shown only if Kind of row is “Quest” or “Also fails if” ; shown only if Fails is “When time runs out” How many seconds of play the player has to finish the quest, from its start (on an "Also fails if" row under a step: from the start of the step). Time waits during a pause; the tracker and the log show what is left. echec_delai Number 60 from 1 to 86 400 Only if the player did itshown only if Kind of row is “Quest” or “Also fails if” ; shown only if Fails is “When an event happens” Ticked: the event only counts if the player caused it (its source), or the vehicle they drive: with sante.mort and "Passer-by", the quest fails if the player kills a passer-by, not if someone else does. echec_par_joueur Yes or no no Item (kind of inventory item)shown only if Kind of row is “Quest” or “Also fails if” ; shown only if Fails is “When the player loses an item” The kind of item the player must not lose, such as "Parcel". The reason only counts once the player has carried enough of it: the quest does not fail before they took it. Handing it over with a "When the player hands items over" step is not losing it. echec_objet Text (empty) How many at leastshown only if Kind of row is “Quest” or “Also fails if” ; shown only if Fails is “When the player loses an item” Fails when the player carries fewer than this number. echec_quantite Number 1 from 1 to 1 000 000, as a whole number Place: a scene objectshown only if Kind of row is “Quest” or “Also fails if” ; shown only if Fails is “When the player goes too far” The object the player must not go far from: a character to escort, a district. It can move: the distance follows its position. The reason only counts once the player has been close enough: it does not fail before they joined it. echec_lieu Object of the scene (empty) Distance beyond which it fails (m)shown only if Kind of row is “Quest” or “Also fails if” ; shown only if Fails is “When the player goes too far” Measured flat, as on the map. With several players, group quests: when all the players are too far. echec_rayon Number 30 from 0.5 to 5000 What happensshown only if Kind of row is “Also fails if” The quest fails (under an optional step, the step is only missed); the step above starts again (under the quest: it resumes as "After a failure, resume" says, without failing); or the quest goes to a label, a plan B. alors Choice in a list The quest fails echoue: The quest failsrecommence: The step starts againetiquette: It leads to a label Label to go toshown only if Kind of row is “Also fails if” ; shown only if What happens is “It leads to a label” The label of the step where the quest goes on, such as "flee". alors_suite Text (empty) The player can abandon itshown only if Kind of row is “Quest” Ticked: the log shows an Abandon button under the quest in progress (a second press confirms). Unticked: an important quest cannot be abandoned. The event quetes.abandonner abandons it in any case. abandon Yes or no yes Can be taken up again after failing or abandoningshown only if Kind of row is “Quest” Ticked: what gives the quest (its event, quetes.demarrer) gives it again: from the start, or, after a failure, from where "After a failure, resume" says. Unticked: a failed or abandoned quest stays so for good. reprendre Yes or no yes After a failure, resumeshown only if Kind of row is “Quest” Where the quest starts again when it is taken up after a failure: from the start, at the failed step, or at the last step ticked "Checkpoint". The steps before stay done; marks set stay, and the world is not put back as it was. reprise Choice in a list From the start debut: From the startetape: At the failed steppoint: At the last checkpoint Try again after a failureshown only if Kind of row is “Quest” After a failure: wait for what gives the quest to give it again, show a Try again button in the log, or take it up by itself. Only used if "Can be taken up again" is ticked. reessayer Choice in a list No: it must be given again non: No: it must be given againbouton: With a Try again button in the logauto: By itself After how many secondsshown only if Kind of row is “Quest” ; shown only if Try again after a failure is “By itself” How many seconds of play after the failure the quest is taken up by itself. reessai_delai Number 3 from 0 to 600 Can be done againshown only if Kind of row is “Quest” No: a finished quest is done for good. Yes: what gives it (its event, quetes.demarrer) gives it again as soon as it is done. Once a day: given again on another day than the one it was done, a day of the game (sunrise of the Day and night system) or a real day, as the setting "Day of a quest to do again" says; a quest given at the start of the game, by a mark or by another quest then comes back by itself. The log shows it "available" or "again tomorrow". repetable Choice in a list No: only once non: No: only oncetoujours: Yes, as soon as it is donechaque_jour: Once a day How many a dayshown only if Kind of row is “Quest” ; shown only if Template (quests made during the game) is ticked ; shown only if Can be done again is “Once a day” A "Once a day" template: how many quests it makes each day, each from a new draw (a different mission). Given at the start of the game, by a mark or by another quest: all of them at the start of each day. Given by an event (a quest giver, a Trigger rule): one each time, up to this number; then nothing before the next day and the giver's "!" is grey. Saves keep the day and the count: loading on the same day makes nothing again. par_jour Number 1 from 1 to 20, as a whole number Yesterday's unfinished questshown only if Kind of row is “Quest” ; shown only if Template (quests made during the game) is ticked ; shown only if Can be done again is “Once a day” A "Once a day" template: on a new day, a quest it made on another day and not finished yet. Kept: the player can still finish it. Removed: it is abandoned, without counting as a failure ("Quest abandoned", the event quetes.abandon). hier Choice in a list Kept garder: Keptretirer: Removed (abandoned, not failed) Sets the mark if it fails or is abandoned (optional)shown only if Kind of row is “Quest” A word the game remembers when the quest fails or is abandoned, such as "wolves_failed": the miller can complain about it in his Dialogue. marque_echec Text (empty) Sends the event if it fails or is abandoned (optional)shown only if Kind of row is “Quest” An event name, such as "bridge.collapse", sent when the quest fails or is abandoned. A Trigger rule "When the event" reacts to it. annonce_echec Text (empty) Only ifshown only if Kind of row is “Only if (prerequisite)” What is needed for the quest above to be given: a level of the Progression system, items carried, a mark set or not, another quest done. While a condition is missing, what gives it is ignored and its giver's "!" is grey; a quest given at the start of the game, by a mark or by another quest is given as soon as everything is there. condition Choice in a list A level reached niveau: A level reachedobjet: They carry an itemsans_objet: They do not carry an itemmarque: A mark is setsans_marque: A mark is not setquete: Another quest Level at leastshown only if Kind of row is “Only if (prerequisite)” ; shown only if Only if is “A level reached” The level to have reached, such as 5. With several players, group quests: that of one of the players. condition_niveau Number 1 from 1 to 100 000, as a whole number Track (empty: the main one)shown only if Kind of row is “Only if (prerequisite)” ; shown only if Only if is “A level reached” The identifier of a track of the Progression system, such as "woodcutting". Empty: the player's main level. condition_piste Text (empty) Item (kind of inventory item)shown only if Kind of row is “Only if (prerequisite)” ; shown only if Only if is “They carry an item” or “They do not carry an item” The kind of item, as the inventory stores it, such as "Key". condition_objet Text (empty) How many at leastshown only if Kind of row is “Only if (prerequisite)” ; shown only if Only if is “They carry an item” or “They do not carry an item” The number to carry (or, for "does not carry", from which it is a no). condition_quantite Number 1 from 1 to 1 000 000, as a whole number Markshown only if Kind of row is “Only if (prerequisite)” ; shown only if Only if is “A mark is set” or “A mark is not set” The mark's word, set by a Dialogue or a quest, such as "met_the_miller". condition_marque Text (empty) Title of the other questshown only if Kind of row is “Only if (prerequisite)” ; shown only if Only if is “Another quest” The exact title of the other quest, in the game's original language. condition_quete Text (empty) How far it isshown only if Kind of row is “Only if (prerequisite)” ; shown only if Only if is “Another quest” Finished (the most common), in progress, not started, failed or abandoned: what the log already keeps. condition_etat Choice in a list Finished finie: Finisheden_cours: In progresspas_commencee: Not startedechouee: Failedabandonnee: Abandoned Hole to fill (its name, without braces)shown only if Kind of row is “Random draw (template)” The name of the hole this draw fills, such as "lieu" for {lieu}. A value given by the script or the rule that creates the quest comes before the draw. tirage_trou Text (empty) Drawshown only if Kind of row is “Random draw (template)” A scene object at random, among those that carry the tag and are at the right distance from the player; or a whole number at random between two bounds. The same draw, with the same seed, gives the same result. Two holes drawn in one quest never get the same object. tirage Choice in a list An object with a tag objet: An object with a tagnombre: A number Tagshown only if Kind of row is “Random draw (template)” ; shown only if Draw is “An object with a tag” The tag the object must carry. A town's shops carry "commerce" and "commerce:<kind>", such as "commerce:superette": they are places with nothing more to do. tirage_etiquette Text (empty) At least (m from the player)shown only if Kind of row is “Random draw (template)” ; shown only if Draw is “An object with a tag” The shortest distance between the player and the object drawn, measured flat as on the map: 100 not to deliver next door. tirage_distance_min Number 0 from 0 to 100 000 At most (m from the player)shown only if Kind of row is “Random draw (template)” ; shown only if Draw is “An object with a tag” The longest distance. No object between the two: the quest is not created, and the event quetes.creation_impossible says why. tirage_distance_max Number 300 from 1 to 100 000 Fromshown only if Kind of row is “Random draw (template)” ; shown only if Draw is “A number” The smallest number drawn, included. tirage_nombre_min Number 1 from 0 to 1 000 000, as a whole number Toshown only if Kind of row is “Random draw (template)” ; shown only if Draw is “A number” The largest number drawn, included. With {n} in a step's text, it is also the number to reach: "Bring {n} apples". tirage_nombre_max Number 5 from 0 to 1 000 000, as a whole number What to doshown only if Kind of row is “Step” or “Other way to end the step” The step as the log writes it, such as "Defeat the wolves" or "Talk to the miller". texte Text (empty) Label (to lead here)shown only if Kind of row is “Step” or “Test” A word naming this row, such as "alarm". A next step that is this word leads here. etiquette Text (empty) Then: label (empty: the next step; fin: the quest succeeds; echec: it fails)shown only if Kind of row is “Step” or “Other way to end the step” Where the quest goes once this row is done: a step's label (backwards too: the steps it goes back to are to do again), "fin", "echec", or empty for the next step. suite Text (empty) Optional (the quest can end without it)shown only if Kind of row is “Step” Ticked: the quest moves on to the next step at once, and this one stays doable until the end of the quest. Failing it does not fail the quest: it is only missed. facultative Yes or no no Checkpointshown only if Kind of row is “Step” Ticked: a quest taken up after a failure "at the last checkpoint" starts again from this step. point_de_reprise Yes or no no Where the player starts again (optional)shown only if Kind of row is “Step” ; shown only if Checkpoint is ticked A scene object where the player is put back when the quest resumes here (with several players, group quests: every player). A dead player is put there when they respawn. Empty: they stay where they are. reprise_lieu Object of the scene (empty) Sends the event at the start (optional)shown only if Kind of row is “Step” An event name, such as "wolves.appear", sent when the step starts. A Trigger rule "When the event" makes what the step needs appear. annonce_debut Text (empty) Doneshown only if Kind of row is “Step” or “Other way to end the step” What ends the step: an event (a Trigger rule, a Dialogue answer, an enemy defeated), a Dialogue mark, a number of items in the inventory, or items handed over: on the event (a talk finished, for example), the inventory takes them back. Or the player reaches a place, or holds on for a time (near a place, if one is given). fin Choice in a list When an event happens evenement: When an event happensmarque: When a mark is setobjet: When the player carries enough of an itemremettre: When the player hands items overlieu: When the player reaches a placetenir: When they held on long enough Event nameshown only if Kind of row is “Step” or “Other way to end the step” ; shown only if Done is “When an event happens” or “When the player hands items over” The exact name of the event, such as "door.open", "sante.mort" (something dies) or "dialogue.fin" (a talk finished). It only counts during the step. fin_evenement Text (empty) Only for the object named (empty: any)shown only if Kind of row is “Step” or “Other way to end the step” ; shown only if Done is “When an event happens” or “When the player hands items over” The name of the object the event must be about, without number: "Wolf" counts "Wolf 1" and "Wolf 2". With sante.mort, only defeated wolves count; with dialogue.fin, only the talk with that character. fin_cible Text (empty) How many timesshown only if Kind of row is “Step” or “Other way to end the step” ; shown only if Done is “When an event happens” How many times the event must happen: 5 to defeat five wolves. The log shows how far the player is, such as 2/5. fin_fois Number 1 from 1 to 100 000, as a whole number Markshown only if Kind of row is “Step” or “Other way to end the step” ; shown only if Done is “When a mark is set” The mark's word, set by a Dialogue or another quest, such as "guard_convinced". If it is already set, the step is done at once. fin_marque Text (empty) Item (kind of inventory item)shown only if Kind of row is “Step” or “Other way to end the step” ; shown only if Done is “When the player carries enough of an item”, “When the player hands items over” or “When an event happens” The kind of item to carry or to hand over, as the inventory stores it, such as "Wolf pelt". With an event: only if it is about that kind of item (boutique.achat and "Apple", butin.ramasse and "Key"); empty: any. fin_objet Text (empty) How many at leastshown only if Kind of row is “Step” or “Other way to end the step” ; shown only if Done is “When the player carries enough of an item” or “When the player hands items over” The number to carry at the same time, or to hand over: 3 pelts. The log shows how far the player is, such as 1/3. If they do not have enough when handing them over, an announcement says how many are missing. fin_quantite Number 1 from 1 to 1 000 000, as a whole number Count the quantitiesshown only if Kind of row is “Step” or “Other way to end the step” ; shown only if Done is “When an event happens” Ticked: an event counts its quantity, and "How many times" becomes the total: buying 6 apples at once does "Buy 6 apples". Unticked: each event counts 1. fin_compter Yes or no no Only if the player did itshown only if Kind of row is “Step” or “Other way to end the step” ; shown only if Done is “When an event happens” Ticked: the event only counts if the player caused it (its source), or the vehicle they drive: a wolf killed by someone else does not count. fin_par_joueur Yes or no no Place: a scene objectshown only if Kind of row is “Step” or “Other way to end the step” ; shown only if Done is “When the player reaches a place” or “When they held on long enough” Where to go: an object with the Zone system counts when entering it; another object, within the radius (it can move). To hold on: optional; if given, time only passes within the radius. fin_lieu Object of the scene (empty) Radius around the place (m)shown only if Kind of row is “Step” or “Other way to end the step” ; shown only if Done is “When the player reaches a place” or “When they held on long enough” How close to the place the player must be, measured flat, as on the map. fin_rayon Number 5 from 0.5 to 5000 How long to hold on (s)shown only if Kind of row is “Step” or “Other way to end the step” ; shown only if Done is “When they held on long enough” The seconds of play to hold on while the step is active. Time waits during a pause; the tracker shows what is left. fin_duree Number 30 from 1 to 86 400 Questionshown only if Kind of row is “Test” What the test looks at, when the quest reaches it: does the player carry an item, is a mark set. test Choice in a list Do they carry an item? objet: Do they carry an item?marque: Is a mark set? Itemshown only if Kind of row is “Test” ; shown only if Question is “Do they carry an item?” The kind of item, as the inventory stores it, such as "Key" or "Gold". test_objet Text (empty) How many at leastshown only if Kind of row is “Test” ; shown only if Question is “Do they carry an item?” The number to carry for a yes, such as 10 gold coins. test_quantite Number 1 from 1 to 1 000 000, as a whole number Markshown only if Kind of row is “Test” ; shown only if Question is “Is a mark set?” The mark's word, such as "king_betrayed". test_marque Text (empty) If yes: label (empty: the next row; fin: the quest succeeds; echec: it fails)shown only if Kind of row is “Test” Where the quest goes on a yes: the label of a step or a test, "fin", "echec", or empty for the next row. si_oui Text (empty) If no: label (empty: the next row; fin: the quest succeeds; echec: it fails)shown only if Kind of row is “Test” Where the quest goes on a no: the label of a step or a test, "fin", "echec", or empty for the next row. si_non Text (empty) Sets the mark at the end (optional)shown only if Kind of row is “Quest”, “Step” or “Other way to end the step” A word the game remembers when this quest or step ends (or ends this way), such as "wolves_hunted". Dialogue tests and answers can use it: the miller thanks the player. marque Text (empty) Changes the reputation with (optional)shown only if Kind of row is “Quest”, “Step” or “Other way to end the step” The identifier of a reputation track of the Progression system, such as "bandits": at the end of this quest, this step or this way to end it (a branch), the player's reputation with that faction changes by the value below. Empty: none. reputation Text (empty) By how much (negative: it goes down)shown only if Kind of row is “Quest”, “Step” or “Other way to end the step” +50: the faction likes it; -100: it likes the player less, for instance after a branch where they betrayed its people. Bounded by the track. reputation_valeur Number 0 from -1 000 000 to 1 000 000 Sends the event at the end (optional)shown only if Kind of row is “Quest”, “Step” or “Other way to end the step” An event name, such as "bridge.repair", sent when this quest or step ends (or ends this way). A Trigger rule "When the event" or a script reacts to it. annonce Text (empty)

items.title: Controls added to the game
items.text:
They appear in the Game controls panel (Developer mode), where you can change their key.

Control Name for scripts Key Gamepad Open the quest log journal J →

items.title: Events
items.text: The descriptions come from the code.

items.title: What it announces
items.text: Event Fields Description progression.reputation joueur (id?), piste (text), faction (text?), valeur (number), fixer (boolean?), groupe (boolean?), source (text?) Ask the Progression module to change the player's reputation with a faction (Progression 9): piste is a track of kind reputation (faction is accepted too); valeur is added (negative: it goes down), or set when fixer is true; it stays within the track's bounds. Sent by a quest, a step or a way to end it (its reputation field), a Trigger rule or a script. groupe: every player present. progression.donner joueur (id?), xp (number), piste (text?), source (text?) Ask the Progression module to give xp to the player (a Trigger rule, a script): it goes through the multipliers and the hook progression.gain, on the host. piste: a track's identifier (empty or missing: the main one); source: a short name for the repetition and the cap. butin.lacher table (text), position (vector?), cible (id?), niveau (number?), joueur (id?) Ask the Loot module to roll a table and drop what it gives (the Trigger, a script). position or cible: where; niveau: the item level; joueur: for whom (the killer, for sharing). quetes.debut quete (text), groupe (boolean?) A quest started: quete is its title. groupe (Journal de quêtes 8): true for a quest of the whole group (game setting groupe), sent once for the group, joueur being who moved it on. quetes.creee modele (text), quete (text), valeurs (table), groupe (boolean?) A quest was made from a template (Journal de quêtes 15, events version 34): quete is its own title, modele the template's, valeurs the value of each hole (an object's id, a number, a text). Sent before its quetes.debut. groupe: true for a quest of the whole group. quetes.creation_impossible modele (text), motif (text), raison (text), groupe (boolean?) A quest could not be made from a template (Journal de quêtes 15, events version 34); nothing was created. motif: modele_inconnu (no quest of that title), pas_un_modele (the quest is not ticked modele), aucun_candidat (no object with the tag at that distance), valeur_manquante (a hole has no value and no draw), conditions (the template's prerequisites are not met), titre_pris (the title given is already a quest's). raison says it in a sentence, also written in the game log. quetes.etape_debut quete (text), etape (number), texte (text), groupe (boolean?) A step of a quest starts (Journal de quêtes 11, events version 33): it becomes one to do now, its other ways to end it too. etape is its rank in the quest (from 1), texte what it says. Sent after quetes.debut for the first steps, then after the quetes.etape that opened it, and again when the step starts over (an "Also fails if" row set to recommence) or the quest resumes at it (quetes.reprise); its own annonce_debut event follows. Not sent again when a saved game is loaded. groupe (Journal de quêtes 8): true for a quest of the whole group. quetes.etape quete (text), etape (number), texte (text), issue (number?), suite (text?), groupe (boolean?) A step of a quest is done: etape is its rank in the quest (from 1), texte what it said. Sent before quetes.fin when it was the last one. issue (Journal de quêtes 11): the rank (from 1) of the other way to end the step that did it, absent when the step itself did; texte is then that way's text. suite (Journal de quêtes 11): the label the quest goes to next (fin, echec or a step's label), absent when it simply goes on to the next row. groupe (Journal de quêtes 8): true for a quest of the whole group (game setting groupe), sent once for the group, joueur being who moved it on. quetes.etape_echec quete (text), etape (number), alors (text), manquee (boolean?), groupe (boolean?) A step of a quest failed (Journal de quêtes 11, events version 33): one of its "Also fails if" rows happened. etape is its rank in the quest (from 1), alors what that row does: echoue (the quest fails, quetes.echec follows), recommence (the step starts again from zero) or etiquette (the quest goes to the row's label). Also sent for an "Also fails if" row under the quest itself that does not make it fail (recommence: the quest starts again; etiquette), etape being then the step it was waiting for (0: none). For an optional step, manquee is true: the step is only missed, the quest goes on without it. groupe: true for a quest of the whole group. quetes.fin quete (text), xp (number?), piste (text?), groupe (boolean?), facultatives (table?) A quest is finished: all its steps are done. Its reward, if any, has been asked to the inventory. xp and piste (version 28): its XP for the Progression module and the track that gets it (empty: the main one). facultatives (Journal de quêtes 11): {faites, total}, how many of its optional steps were done, out of how many; absent when it has none. groupe (Journal de quêtes 8): true for a quest of the whole group (game setting groupe), sent once for the group, joueur being who moved it on. quetes.echec quete (text), groupe (boolean?) A quest failed: an event, a mark, its time ran out, or quetes.echouer. It gives no reward; it may be given again if its settings allow it. groupe (Journal de quêtes 8): true for a quest of the whole group (game setting groupe), sent once for the group, joueur being who moved it on. quetes.abandon quete (text), groupe (boolean?) The player abandoned a quest from the log (or quetes.abandonner asked for it). It gives no reward; it may be given again if its settings allow it. groupe (Journal de quêtes 8): true for a quest of the whole group (game setting groupe), sent once for the group, joueur being who moved it on. quetes.reprise quete (text), etape (number), groupe (boolean?) A quest resumes (Journal de quêtes 11, events version 33): tried again after a failure (the log's Try again button, reessayer auto, quetes.reessayer, or given again when it does not start over), or started again by an "Also fails if" row of the quest set to recommence. etape is the step it resumes at (from 1; 0: none). The steps before it stay done; marks stay set and the world is not put back as it was: a Trigger rule on the step's annonce_debut does that. groupe: true for a quest of the whole group. inventaire.ajouter objet (text), quantite (number), joueur (id?), fiche (number?) Ask the inventory to add items, such as a reward. Answered by inventaire.change, or inventaire.plein. With several players, joueur says whose bag; without it, the player whose action is being handled, or every player. inventaire.retirer objet (text), quantite (number), fiche (number?) Ask the inventory to remove items, such as a payment. Answered by inventaire.change, or inventaire.manque if there are not enough. For a kind with unique copies (version 15): fiche removes that copy, otherwise the first ones; their records are destroyed. dialogue.marquer marque (text), retirer (boolean?) Ask the dialogue system to set a mark, from a script or another system; with retirer true, to remove it. Dialogue conditions then see it.

items.title: What it listens to
items.text: Event Fields Description quetes.demarrer quete (text) Ask the quest log to give a quest to the player, by its title: from a script, a dialogue or a trigger. Nothing happens if it was already given. quetes.creer modele (text), valeurs (table?), titre (text?), graine (number?) Ask the quest log to make a real quest from a template (Journal de quêtes 15, events version 34): modele is the template's title (a quest ticked modele). Its holes {name} are filled from valeurs ({lieu = id, n = 3}), or from a field of the event with the hole's name (cible, from a Trigger rule), otherwise by the template's draw rows (an object with a tag at a distance from the player, a number); a value given comes before the draw. titre: its title, holes allowed (empty: the template's title and the next number, "Livraison 3"). graine: the seed of the draw (the same seed gives the same result; empty: drawn from the game). The quest starts at once; quetes.creee follows, or quetes.creation_impossible. quetes.echouer quete (text) Ask the quest log to make a quest in progress fail, by its title: from a script or a trigger. Nothing happens if it is not in progress. quetes.abandonner quete (text) Ask the quest log to abandon a quest in progress, by its title, as the player does from the log. Nothing happens if it is not in progress. quetes.reessayer quete (text) Ask the quest log to try a failed quest again, by its title (Journal de quêtes 11, events version 33): the same as its Try again button in the log. It resumes from where its setting reprise says (the start, the failed step or the last checkpoint). Nothing happens if it has not failed or cannot be taken up again (reprendre). joueur.reapparu joueur (id), cible (id), position (vector) A dead player stands up again (death and respawn module): respawned, or brought back by sante.ranimer. inventaire.change objet (text), quantite (number), total (number), chargement (boolean?), fiche (number?), jete (boolean?) The quantity of an item changed. total is the new quantity. chargement is true when a saved game gives the items back (game.load): nothing was picked up. For a unique copy (version 15), objet is its kind, fiche its record's number, total how many of that kind. With several stacks of a kind (version 21), total counts all of them; jete is true when a slot was dropped on the ground. dialogue.marque marque (text) A dialogue set a mark: a word the game remembers (a line shown, an answer chosen). Every dialogue's conditions can use it. zone.entree cible (id), qui (id), joueur (id?) Something entered a zone (an object carrying the zone system): a player, a character or a moving object, depending on what the zone detects (joueur: every player). joueur is set when qui is a player. Announced by the engine. vehicule.monte cible (id), qui (id), joueur (id?) A player got into a vehicle (an object carrying the vehicule system) and now drives it: qui and joueur are their character (the host's, or a guest's). Announced by the engine. vehicule.descendu cible (id), qui (id), joueur (id?) A player got out of a vehicle. Announced by the engine. jour_nuit.lever jour (number) The sun rose: day jour begins. Lamps tagged for the night went out. progression.niveau joueur (id?), cle (text), piste (text), niveau (number), ancien (number) Sent by the engine for each level a player reached on a track (several levels at once: several events), also when an admin sets a level. The Progression module gives the rewards of that level; a Trigger rule can play a sound or open a door.

items.title: Points a script can replace (game.override)
items.text:
The descriptions come from the code.

  • quetes.texte: function(default, key) -> the text the quest log shows for that key: titre, aucune, en_cours, terminees, fermer, fait, nouvelle, etape, finie, recompense, echouee, abandonnee, ratees, echouee_court, abandonnee_court, abandonner, confirmer, reste, manque, ou, facultatif, manquee, etape_ratee, reprise, reessayer, demain, disponible, recompense_xp, a_venir. It may hold {quete}, {etape}, {objet}, {n}, {total} and {liste}, replaced afterwards (in the player's language). The default is the game's translation of the text in the original language (translations_get lists them as built-in texts of the quest log); without one, French or English, after the player's language.
  • quetes.compte: function(default, e, quete, etape) -> how much the event e counts for a step that ends on an event (0: not at all), once its fin_cible matched. quete is the quest's title, etape the step's row (its settings, plus numero, its rank from 1), or the row of one of its other ways to end it (plus issue, its rank among them from 1). The default applies fin_objet (the kind of item of e.objet or e.ressource), fin_par_joueur (e.source, e.joueur or e.qui is the player or the vehicle they drive) and fin_compter (e.quantite, otherwise 1). To add a condition without touching the system: only at night, only with a given weapon.

items.title: What the agent knows about this system
items.text: The text the agent reads before using this system.

items.title: Quest log (quetes)
items.text: The game's quests and their steps, written in its settings and moved on by events, without code. Notifications announce each new quest, step done, failure and resume; the current steps show on the right of the screen; a log window opens with the control journal (J, or → on a gamepad). Add it once with modules_add; it is for the whole game, not placed on objects. Use it whenever the user talks about quests, missions, objectives or tasks: set its list with modules_set, never write a quest in a script, never copy a quest into a script, never edit the system (override its hooks with game.override).

items.title: The list quetes
items.text:
Its game setting quetes is a list of rows, in order. Its kinds (sorte):

sorte What it is Under quete Starts a quest; the rows after it belong to it. — etape A step: texte (what to do, as the log writes it) and fin (what ends it). its quest issue Another way to end the step right above it ("Other way to end the step"), with its own texte, end fields and suite. right under its step test An instant switch on a mark or an item carried. its quest echec "Also fails if": one more failure reason, for the quest (right under the quete row) or for one step (right under it). its quest or step condition "Only if": a prerequisite of the quest; without it, the quest is not given. its quest tirage "Random draw": fills a hole of a template (modele) when a quest is made from it. its template recompense "Reward": one more reward, given at the end of the row above it. right under its quest, step or issue

Step numbers (in events, saves and the map's quete_etape) are the rank among the etape rows of the quest, from 1; issue, test and echec rows are not counted.

quete: titre (shown, and names the quest in events), description, depart (when the player gets it): debut (game start), evenement (the event depart_evenement: a dialogue answer's annonce, a declencheur rule), marque (the Dialogue mark depart_marque, at once if set), quete (when the quest titled depart_quete ends: a chain). Also dans_l_ordre (on: one step after the other; off: all at once), recompense and recompense_quantite (items given at the end; needs inventaire), abandon (an Abandonner button in the log, pressed twice), reprendre (on: what gives it gives it again after a failure or an abandon; a quest starting with the game is given again by quetes.demarrer), marque_echec and annonce_echec (a mark and an event when it fails or is abandoned). donneur (a scene object, optional): the character above whom the carte shows a "!" while the quest can be given; empty, every character whose dialogue sends depart_evenement or sets depart_marque gets it. Set it when a declencheur rule gives the quest near someone.

Step ends (fin), on etape and issue:

  • evenement: the event fin_evenement happens fin_fois times while the step is active. Filters: fin_cible (only about an object of that name: "Loup" counts "Loup 2"), fin_objet (only that kind of item, from the event's objet or ressource, any case: boutique.achat + "Pomme"), fin_compter (each event counts its quantite; fin_fois is the total), fin_par_joueur (only if the player caused it, its source, or the vehicle they drive; with several players, only the author's copy counts, or any player with groupe). "Defeat", "talk", "buy" are evenement steps (sante.mort, dialogue.fin, boutique.achat): never ask for another kind.
  • marque: the Dialogue mark fin_marque is set (at once if it already is).
  • objet: the player carries fin_quantite of fin_objet (from the inventory).
  • remettre: on fin_evenement (for fin_cible, such as dialogue.fin with "Meunier"), if the player carries fin_quantite of fin_objet, the inventory takes them and the step is done; otherwise an announcement says how many are missing. "Bring 3 pelts to the miller".
  • lieu: the player reaches the scene object fin_lieu: within fin_rayon metres, measured flat (it may move: a character, a car), or, if it carries the zone system, when they enter the zone. Write this rather than evenement + zone.entree. An object missing from the scene: the step waits (one line in the game log).
  • tenir: hold on fin_duree seconds of play while the step is active; with fin_lieu, time only passes within fin_rayon of it. "Survive 90 s", "Defend the farm 60 s". Time waits during a pause; the tracker and the log show what is left ("Reste 0:42").

For any other condition ("only at night"), a game script overrides quetes.compte, which says how much an event counts for a step (0: nothing): game.override("quetes.compte", function(default, e, quete, etape) if quete == "Chasse nocturne" and not shared.nuit then return 0 end return default(e, quete, etape) end) (etape is the step's row, with numero; shared.nuit stands for your game's condition).

On every step and issue: marque (a mark set when it ends, seen by every dialogue) and annonce (an event sent when it ends, for a declencheur rule: a bridge appears). Also on the quest itself (at its end): reputation (a reputation track of the progression system, such as bandits) and reputation_valeur (added to it, negative to lower it: "the bandits like the player less after this branch"); with groupe, every player present. Never a script for it. A step also has annonce_debut: an event sent when it starts (and again when it starts over or the quest resumes at it), for a declencheur rule that makes what this step needs appear (copier, montrer): the wolves of this step only, the parcel again.

items.title: Rewards
items.text:
The quest's recompense/recompense_quantite (and xp/piste_xp) stay its first reward. For more, add recompense rows right under the quest (given when it ends), a step (when the step itself is done, optional ones too) or an issue (when that way is taken). Each row gives one thing, chosen by donne: objet (recompense and recompense_quantite, into the inventory; with groupe, as recompense_groupe says), xp (donne_xp on the Progression track donne_piste, empty: the main one; with groupe, every player present), butin (the butin table donne_table, rolled and dropped near the player) or marque (the mark donne_marque). Each is given once: never again on a load, a resume after a failure or a step done again after a branch back; only a repetable quest that starts over gives them again. The log shows the items and XP to come ("Reward: Gold x50, 100 XP"); the end announcement names them. Never a script or a declencheur rule for a quest's reward.

Recipe, a quest with three rewards: {"sorte": "quete", "titre": "The mill", "recompense": "Or", "recompense_quantite": 50}, {"sorte": "recompense", "donne": "xp", "donne_xp": 100}, {"sorte": "recompense", "donne": "butin", "donne_table": "<a table of the user's butin>"}, {"sorte": "etape", "texte": "Find the miller", "fin": "marque", "fin_marque": "meunier_vu"}, {"sorte": "recompense", "donne": "objet", "recompense": "Pain", "recompense_quantite": 2} (the bread comes when this step is done). Use only items, tables and tracks the game has.

items.title: Branches (quests with dans_l_ordre on), the same keys as the dialogue
items.text:
• etiquette on a step or a test names it. suite on a step or an issue says where the quest goes once it is done: a label (backwards too: the steps gone back to are to do again, counts and times from zero), fin (the quest succeeds), echec (it fails), or empty: the next row. A missing label: the quest waits there, and the game log says so (quetes: step 3 of 'X' leads to no label 'Y').
  • issue rows: the step and its other ways are active together; the first one done wins, the others close. A player's choice in a Dialogue: each answer sets a mark or sends an event, each issue waits for one. Never invent an event to jump to a label: send the event an issue waits for.
  • test rows: when the quest reaches one, it looks at once at test marque (test_marque set?) or objet (carrying test_quantite of test_objet?) and goes to si_oui or si_non (label, fin, echec, empty: the next row). For a mark set elsewhere (the player betrayed the king). Tests leading to each other stop after 100 jumps (game log).
  • With dans_l_ordre off, suite and tests are ignored (game log); issue rows still work.
  • The editor's quest map ("Show the map", editable like the dialogue's) changes these same rows: dragging an arrow sets its suite (or si_oui, si_non, alors_suite) to the target's etiquette, giving the target one from its text if it has none; an added step goes at the end of its quest with its own etiquette (the last step's empty suite becomes fin, so nothing else changes); removing a step sets what named it to fin. To link or add yourself, write the same rows: an etiquette on the target, the label in suite, a new etape row before the next quete row. Its "All quests" view draws the chains (depart: quete, depart_quete): nothing to write for it.
  • facultative on a step: optional (a bonus, a hidden chest). It becomes active and the quest moves on at once; it stays doable until the quest ends, which does not wait for it. Its marque and annonce are its reward. An echec row under it makes it missed ("find the chest within 2 minutes"), never the quest failed.

items.title: Prerequisites and repeatable quests
items.text:
• condition rows (any number, under the quest): condition niveau (the player's level on the Progression track condition_piste, empty: the main level, at least condition_niveau; with groupe, any player's), objet / sans_objet (carrying at least condition_quantite of condition_objet, or not), marque / sans_marque (condition_marque set, or not), quete (the quest condition_quete is at condition_etat, finie by default). The same keys as a dialogue answer's condition. While one is missing, whatever gives the quest (its event, mark, quetes.demarrer) is ignored (one line in the game log: quetes: 'X' is not available yet) and the carte shows its giver's "!" in grey (icone_indisponible_couleur); a quest given at the start, by a mark or by another quest is given as soon as everything is met. "Only from level 5" is a condition row, never a script or a mark.
  • repetable on the quest: non (default: once), toujours (what gives it gives it again as soon as it is done), chaque_jour (given again on another day than its last end; a quest given at the start, by a mark or by another quest comes back by itself that day). The day is set by the game setting jour_repetition: jeu (default: a day of the game starts at the jour_nuit sunrise, jour_nuit.lever; without that system the day never changes) or reel (the computer's date, game.today()). Saves keep the day of the last end. The log writes a repeatable quest already done "(available)" or "(again tomorrow)". A daily delivery: {"sorte": "quete", "titre": "Delivery", "depart": "evenement", "depart_evenement": "delivery.accepted", "repetable": "chaque_jour"}.
  • A character who offers it only when it can be given: a dialogue test quete with test_etat disponible.

items.title: Templates: quests made during the game
items.text:
• A quest with modele on is a template: it never starts by itself and is not in the log. Its texts and its object fields (fin_lieu, echec_lieu, reprise_lieu, donneur) and fin_cible have holes {name} ({cible}, {lieu}, {objet}, {n}, any name). game.emit("quetes.creer", {modele = "Delivery", valeurs = {lieu = id}, titre = "...", graine = 7}) (or the template's own depart evenement) makes a real quest from it: its rows copied, holes filled, its own title (titre, holes allowed; empty: the template's title and the next number, "Delivery 3"), then it starts. Saves keep it (same title, values, progress); quetes.creee (quete, modele, valeurs) announces it.
  • Values, first found wins: the event's valeurs; a field of the event with the hole's name (a declencheur rule envoyer sends cible, its object: {cible}); then the template's tirage rows. A tirage row (under the template): tirage_trou (the hole's name, no braces), tirage objet (a scene object carrying the tag tirage_etiquette, between tirage_distance_min and tirage_distance_max metres from the player, flat; two holes of one quest never get the same object) or nombre (a whole number from tirage_nombre_min to tirage_nombre_max). The draw uses graine (same seed, same result). In an object field a hole gets the object's id, in a text its name. {n} in a step's texte also sets its number to reach (fin_quantite, fin_fois, fin_duree).
  • A town's shops are tagged commerce and commerce:<kind> (city_get, building): they are draw candidates with nothing more. Never place objects or tag them for a template unless the user asks.
  • Nothing to draw, a hole with no value, an unknown template, unmet condition rows: nothing is created, quetes.creation_impossible (modele, motif: modele_inconnu, pas_un_modele, aucun_candidat, valeur_manquante, conditions, titre_pris; raison, also in the game log). A declencheur rule "When the event" on it can tell the player.
  • Recipe, a generated delivery (write the template; never write the deliveries themselves): {"sorte": "quete", "titre": "Delivery", "modele": true, "depart": "evenement", "depart_evenement": "delivery.ask", "description": "A parcel for {lieu}."}, {"sorte": "tirage", "tirage_trou": "depart", "tirage_etiquette": "commerce:boulangerie", "tirage_distance_max": 200}, {"sorte": "tirage", "tirage_trou": "lieu", "tirage_etiquette": "commerce:superette", "tirage_distance_min": 150, "tirage_distance_max": 600}, {"sorte": "etape", "texte": "Pick up the parcel at {depart}", "fin": "lieu", "fin_lieu": "{depart}"}, {"sorte": "etape", "texte": "Deliver it to {lieu}", "fin": "lieu", "fin_lieu": "{lieu}"}; a dialogue answer annonce: "delivery.ask" (or a declencheur rule envoyer) gives one more each time. The carte shows the drawn place's marker like any lieu step.
  • Daily quests: a template with repetable chaque_jour makes par_jour quests (default 1) per day (the day of jour_repetition: the game's sunrise or the real date), each from a new draw, so a different mission every day. When depends on its depart: debut (or a mark, or another quest finished): all of them at the start of the game and at each new day; evenement (a quest giver's dialogue answer annonce, a declencheur rule): one each time, up to par_jour, then nothing before the next day (the giver's "!" turns grey; one line in the game log). hier: garder (default: yesterday's unfinished quest stays) or retirer (abandoned on the new day, not a failure: quetes.abandon). Saves keep the last day and its count: loading on the same day makes nothing again. A quest made by it is not repeatable itself.
  • Recipe, the delivery of the day (write the template; never the deliveries): {"sorte": "quete", "titre": "Delivery of the day", "modele": true, "repetable": "chaque_jour", "par_jour": 1, "hier": "retirer", "description": "A parcel for {lieu}."}, {"sorte": "tirage", "tirage_trou": "lieu", "tirage_etiquette": "commerce:superette", "tirage_distance_min": 100, "tirage_distance_max": 500}, {"sorte": "etape", "texte": "Deliver the parcel to {lieu}", "fin": "lieu", "fin_lieu": "{lieu}"}. Given by a character instead: "depart": "evenement", "depart_evenement": "delivery.ask", "donneur": "<the character's id>" and his dialogue answer annonce: "delivery.ask".

items.title: Failures
items.text:
The quest's own echec field is its main reason; echec rows add more, with the same keys. Reasons (echec):

  • aucun: never (the default; an echec row left on it does nothing);
  • evenement: echec_evenement happens, about echec_cible if given (sante.mort with "Marchand": the escorted merchant died); echec_par_joueur: only if the player caused it (sante.mort with "Passant");
  • marque: the mark echec_marque is set (a mark already set counts at once only with alors echoue);
  • temps: echec_delai seconds of play since the quest started, or, on a row under a step, since the step started ("Deliver within 60 s"); shown as "Reste 0:42";
  • objet: the player carries fewer than echec_quantite of echec_objet, once they carried enough: it does not fail before they took the parcel; handing it over with remettre is not losing it;
  • eloigne: the player is more than echec_rayon metres (flat) from the scene object echec_lieu, once they were close enough (escort); with groupe, when all the players are.

alors on an echec row says what happens: echoue (default: the quest fails; under an optional step, the step is missed), recommence (the step starts again from zero: counts, time, other ways, its annonce_debut again, announcement "Étape ratée : …"; under the quest: it resumes as reprise says, without failing), etiquette (the quest goes to the label alors_suite: a plan B, "spotted: flee").

items.title: Resuming and trying again
items.text:
Only with reprendre on. reprise on the quest: debut (default: from the start), etape (at the failed step) or point (at the last step ticked point_de_reprise that it reached; none: the start). The steps before stay done; the quest's time limit starts again in full; the step's annonce_debut is sent again. Marks stay set and the world is not put back: a declencheur rule on that annonce_debut brings the enemies or the parcel back. A checkpoint step's reprise_lieu (a scene object): the player is put there (dead: when the mort module respawns them; with groupe, every player).

reessayer on the quest: non (default: what gives the quest gives it again), bouton (a "Try again" button under it in the log), auto (by itself after reessai_delai seconds of play). A script or a rule sends quetes.reessayer (quete) for the same effect.

items.title: Recipes
items.text:
• A branch by a Dialogue answer: step {"texte": "Get through the gate", "fin": "lieu", "fin_lieu": "Gate"}, under it {"sorte": "issue", "texte": "Pay the guard", "fin": "evenement", "fin_evenement": "guard.paid", "suite": "paid"} and {"sorte": "issue", "texte": "Anger the guard", "fin": "marque", "fin_marque": "guard_angry", "suite": "alarm"}; the guard's answers send guard.paid (annonce) or set guard_angry (marque); then a step labelled paid with "suite": "fin" and a step labelled alarm.
  • Deliver within 60 s without losing the parcel, to A or B: step {"texte": "Take the parcel", "fin": "objet", "fin_objet": "Parcel"}; step {"texte": "Deliver it to Anne", "fin": "lieu", "fin_lieu": "Anne", "suite": "fin", "point_de_reprise": true, "reprise_lieu": "Depot", "annonce_debut": "parcel.again"}, under it {"sorte": "issue", "texte": "Deliver it to Bruno", "fin": "lieu", "fin_lieu": "Bruno", "suite": "fin"}, {"sorte": "echec", "echec": "temps", "echec_delai": 60} and {"sorte": "echec", "echec": "objet", "echec_objet": "Parcel"}; on the quest "reprise": "point", "reessayer": "auto"; a declencheur rule on parcel.again gives the parcel back.
  • Defend the farm 60 s, start again at the checkpoint: step {"texte": "Defend the farm", "fin": "tenir", "fin_duree": 60, "fin_lieu": "Farm", "fin_rayon": 15, "point_de_reprise": true, "reprise_lieu": "Farm", "annonce_debut": "farm.wave"}, under it {"sorte": "echec", "echec": "evenement", "echec_evenement": "sante.mort", "echec_cible": "Farmer"}; on the quest "echec": "evenement", "echec_evenement": "joueur.mort", "reprise": "point", "reessayer": "bouton"; a declencheur rule on farm.wave brings the enemies.
  • Escort a character to a place: the character carries the accompagner system (read its notes: teleportation off, destination the place). Step {"texte": "Escort the merchant", "fin": "evenement", "fin_evenement": "accompagner.arrive", "fin_cible": "Merchant", "annonce_debut": "accompagner.suivre"}, under it {"sorte": "echec", "echec": "eloigne", "echec_lieu": "<merchant id>", "echec_rayon": 25} and {"sorte": "echec", "echec": "evenement", "echec_evenement": "sante.mort", "echec_cible": "Merchant"}. Never script the walking.
  • A miller's wolves: his dialogue answer "I'll do it" with annonce: "loups.accepte"; then {"sorte": "quete", "titre": "Les loups du moulin", "depart": "evenement", "depart_evenement": "loups.accepte", "recompense": "Or", "recompense_quantite": 50}, {"sorte": "etape", "texte": "Vaincre 3 loups", "fin": "evenement", "fin_evenement": "sante.mort", "fin_cible": "Loup", "fin_fois": 3, "fin_par_joueur": true, "marque": "loups_chasses"}, {"sorte": "etape", "texte": "Revenir voir le meunier", "fin": "evenement", "fin_evenement": "dialogue.fin", "fin_cible": "Meunier"}.

Write titles and steps in the user's language, short.

items.title: Events, scripts, saves
items.text:
• Sent: quetes.debut (quete), quetes.etape_debut (quete, etape, texte), quetes.etape (quete, etape, texte; issue: rank of the other way that did it; suite: the label taken), quetes.etape_echec (quete, etape, alors; manquee for an optional step), quetes.fin (quete, facultatives {faites, total}), quetes.echec, quetes.abandon, quetes.reprise (quete, etape: where it resumes). For one quest, prefer its annonce or annonce_echec.
  • Listened: game.emit("quetes.demarrer", {quete = "..."}) (without quete: the first quest not started), quetes.echouer, quetes.abandonner, quetes.reessayer (quete), quetes.creer (modele, valeurs, titre, graine: a quest from a template, above). Sent too: quetes.creee, quetes.creation_impossible.
  • Another system needing the quests in progress reads shared.quetes_en_cours[player](): {title -> {faites, actives, chemin, issues, manquees, cibles, lieux, place, suivie, rendre}} (suivie: the tracked quest; rendre: lower-case names to talk to or hand something to for an active step). The givers: shared.quetes_donneurs[player]() -> {{id, titre, disponible}}. Where one quest is: shared.quetes_etat(player, title) -> etat (pas_commencee, en_cours, finie, echouee, abandonnee; nil: no quest of that title), etape (the step to do now), actives ({number -> true, label -> true}), disponible (it can be given now: prerequisites met, not done today); the dialogue test and answer condition quete and the declencheur condition quete read it (the log answers declencheur.condition itself). A character who speaks according to a quest, or a rule that only acts during it: use those, never marks that copy the quest's state. The carte reads both (its on-screen marker and "! / ?" icons): never compute what is active elsewhere.
  • Saves: game.save keeps every quest's state, the branch taken, counts, times and marks; game.load gives them back without announcing, with the day a repeatable quest was last done. Nothing to write.

items.title: Screens, texts, tests
items.text:
• Game settings: fenetre (the log with J), pause_fenetre, notifications, duree_notification, suivi (the current steps on the right, with progress such as 2/5). They hide during a pause.
  • The log and the tracker show the path taken (done steps in grey), missed optional steps ("(missed)"), the active steps ("(optional)") with their other ways under them ("or: Pay the guard"); branches not taken never show.
  • Three screens delivered by the system (modules/quetes/ecrans/): « Journal de quêtes » (Fenêtre, Titre, Liste with row Ligne in shapes Rubrique, Quête, Description, Étape, Reste, Quête passée, Abandonner, Réessayer, Vide; Fermer), « Suivi des quêtes » (Fond, Titre, Étapes row Étape, Reste), « Annonces des quêtes » (Fond, Lignes row Annonce). Restyle them with screens_set; never redraw them with game.hud_*. B or Escape closes the log.
  • Texts follow the player's language. The log's own texts are built-in (French and English), listed by translations_get: translate them there for other languages. Titles and steps are translated with the game's tables; events keep the original title. To change a word: game.override("quetes.texte", function(default, key) if key == "titre" then return "Missions" end return default(key) end) (keys in modules_info).
  • Testing: in game_run, do what each step asks (walk to the place, wait out a time limit), then read the report's hud: Suivi des quêtes/Étape#1, Suivi des quêtes/Reste, Annonces des quêtes/Annonce#1, and, with journal pressed, Journal de quêtes/Quête#2, Journal de quêtes/Étape#3. A script that game.logs the quetes.* events shows the order (step taken, issue, failure, resume).

items.title: Several players
items.text:
By default each player has their own quests, steps, log and rewards. For a cooperative game, tick groupe (« Quêtes du groupe »; never copy quests between players in a script): any player moves a step on, everyone sees the same state, an event that names no player counts once, a newcomer finds where the group is. recompense_groupe: groupe (once, into the Inventory's shared bag with sac_commun, else the finisher's bag) or chacun (every player present). quetes.* events are then sent once with groupe: true and joueur the player who moved it on. Pair it with sac_commun and chests in mode groupe (coffres).

items.title: Health
items.text:
Health and armor for the objects that carry it: the player, a group of skeletons, a boss, each with its own values. Shows nothing: add "Health bar" to see it.

Identifier sante Version 9 Placed on objects yes

items.title: Settings for the whole game
items.text:
In the Systems panel (Developer mode), by opening the system's card.

Setting What it does Name in code Type Default Limits or choices Armor calculation How armor reduces damage, in the whole game. Simple: an armor of 25 stops 25 % of each hit (90 % at most). Curve: armor is counted in points, each one counting a little less than the one before, for a role-playing game with a long progression. calcul Choice in a list Simple: armor is a percentage pourcentage: Simple: armor is a percentagecourbe: Curve: armor / (armor + K), like Diablo or WoW Curve: the armor that stops half the damage (K) With the curve calculation: the armor that stops half the damage. With 100, an armor of 100 stops half, 300 stops three quarters. constante Number 100 from 1 to 1 000 000 Touching lava What lava does to what touches it, in the whole game: damage every second while you stay in it (each one's "Lava damage" setting), or death as soon as you enter. Armor and invulnerability change nothing. lave Choice in a list Damage per second degats: Damage per secondmort: Instant death

items.title: Settings on each object
items.text:
In the Properties of an object or folder that carries the system, Systems section. A folder passes its values on to what it contains; an object can change a value for itself only.

Setting What it does Name in code Type Default Limits or choices Health points Its health at the start of the game, which is also its maximum health. At zero, it dies. With Progression, it is the base of the value "sante_max", to which its bonuses add. points_de_vie Number 100 from 1 to 1 000 000 Armor (in % or in points, depending on the game's calculation) What reduces each hit taken. With the simple calculation, a percentage: 25 stops 25 %. With the curve calculation, points: see the game setting. armure Number 0 from 0 to 1 000 000 Invulnerability after a hit (s) After a hit, it loses no health for this many seconds: hits too close together count only once. 0: every hit counts. invulnerabilite Number 0.5 from 0 to 60 Lava damage per second The health it loses each second spent in lava (with damage per second). 0: lava does nothing to it, for a fire creature. lave_degats Number 25 from 0 to 1 000 000 Remove the object when it dies (not the player) Ticked: the object leaves the game when it dies. Unticked: it stays there. The player is never removed. detruire_a_la_mort Yes or no no

items.title: Events
items.text: The descriptions come from the code.

items.title: What it announces
items.text: Event Fields Description sante.change cible (id), vie (number), max (number) An object's health changed, or is announced once when the game starts. sante.mort cible (id), source (id?) An object's health reached zero. What happens next belongs to the game: the health module does nothing else, unless its setting says to destroy the object. sante.pare cible (id), source (id?), montant (number) A hit was blocked by a guard: montant is the damage it stopped. For a clang, sparks, a stamina cost.

items.title: What it listens to
items.text: Event Fields Description scene.change depuis (text), vers (text) Sent by the engine once the player has arrived in another scene of the game (game.go_to, or a passage). Scripts keep running across scenes: this is when a module looks at the objects of the new scene. sante.blesser cible (id), montant (number), source (id?) Ask the health module to remove health from an object. sante.soigner cible (id), montant (number) Ask the health module to give health back, up to its maximum. sante.ranimer cible (id), part (number?), montant (number?), invulnerabilite (number?) Ask the health module to bring an object back to life, even dead: part (0 to 1 of its maximum, all by default) or montant (points), then invulnerabilite seconds without losing health. Sent by the death and respawn module. sante.garde cible (id), part (number), angle (number) An object protects itself, or stops (part 0): hits coming from in front of it, within angle degrees, lose part of their damage (0 to 1) before its armor. A hit without a source cannot be blocked. lave.contact cible (id), secondes (number), lave (id?), joueur (id?) Something touches lava (a water body of the terrain whose liquid is lava): a player, a character by the feet, or a moving object by the bottom of its box. Announced once when it enters, then every secondes (0.5) while it stays. lave is the lava object; joueur is set when cible is a player. The health module turns it into damage per second or instant death (its settings). Announced by the engine.

items.title: Points a script can replace (game.override)
items.text:
The descriptions come from the code.

  • sante.degats: function(default, cible, brut, source, retenue) -> the health removed. brut: the raw damage sent; retenue: the share stopped by the target's armor (0 to 1). The default returns brut * (1 - retenue). For critical hits, weaknesses, a boss that only takes fire.
  • sante.lave: function(default, cible, montant, lave) -> the health removed by one lava contact (lave.contact, every half second). montant: the setting's damage for that half second, or all the remaining health with instant death. Return 0 for a creature that does not fear lava.

items.text: The text the agent reads before using this system.

items.title: Health (sante)
items.text:
Health and armor for the objects that carry this system: place it on the player, on an enemy, or on a group so that all its children have it. Each object or group has its own values: an early skeleton and a final boss do not have the same health. It decides nothing for the game: it removes and gives back health, and announces changes and deaths.

  • Place it with systems_attach, and set each group's values with systems_set: points_de_vie, armure, invulnerabilite, detruire_a_la_mort. A child can change one value for itself; the rest comes from its group.
  • For the whole game (modules_set): calcul is pourcentage (armor 25 stops 25 % of each hit, at most 90 %) or courbe (armor in points, stopping armor / (armor + K): with K = constante = 100, 100 armor stops half, 300 stops 75 %). Choose courbe for an RPG with a long progression; tell the user.
  • Hurt something: game.emit("sante.blesser", {cible = id, montant = 10, source = attacker}). montant is the raw damage: the target's armor is applied here.
  • Heal: game.emit("sante.soigner", {cible = id, montant = 10}). For potions, food and springs, use the module soins.
  • Guard: game.emit("sante.garde", {cible = id, part = 0.7, angle = 120}) makes hits from in front lose 70 % before armor, until sent again with part = 0. The player's blocking comes from combat.basique: use this only for a guard of your own, such as a shielded enemy. Announced by sante.pare.
  • This module shows nothing on screen. For the player's health bar, add barre_de_vie; for anything else, listen to sante.change (cible, vie, max). It is announced once for everyone on the first step, then on each change.
  • React to a death: listen to sante.mort (cible, source). For the player's death (fall, death screen, respawn or game over), add the module mort rather than a script. Anything else a death means (loot, a door that opens) belongs to the game, and only if the user asked for it.
  • Bring back to life, even dead: game.emit("sante.ranimer", {cible = id, part = 0.5, invulnerabilite = 3}) (part 0 to 1 of the maximum, all by default, or montant in points). sante.soigner never heals the dead.
  • Lava (a water body of the terrain whose liquid is lava, set with water_set, liquid lava): the engine announces lave.contact (cible, secondes, lave) when something enters it, then every half second. This module turns it into damage: lave (whole game, modules_set) is degats (each one's lave_degats per second, 25 by default; 0 for a fire creature) or mort (instant death). Armor and invulnerability do not count. A game can change it with game.override("sante.lave", function(default, cible, montant, lave) ... end). Without this module, lava hurts nobody: add it to make lava dangerous, with the module mort for the player's death and respawn.
  • Objects cloned during the game from an object carrying it have its values.

items.title: Several players
items.text:
One for the whole game: every object carrying it has its own health, each player's character included. A player is never destroyed at death.

items.title: Knowledge
items.text:
What the player knows how to do, and how they learn it: knowledges that unlock Crafting recipes, Building pieces or whatever the game wants. Each is learned in one or several ways: known from the start, by obtaining an item, by studying an item at a research table, with points in a tree, by reading a plan, from a character or a quest, by analysing objects of the world, or by crafting again and again. A window (K) shows what is known, what can be learned and how.

Identifier savoir Version 5 Placed on objects yes Also activates Inventory, Interaction Also needs, on the same object Interaction
