items.title: Events
items.text: The descriptions come from the code.

items.title: What it announces
items.text: Event Fields Description savoir.appris connaissance (text), moyen (text), categorie (text), etiquettes (text) The player learned a knowledge (version 26): connaissance is its name (original language), moyen how (depart, objet, etude, points, plan, evenement, marque, analyse, fabrication, apprendre), categorie its category, etiquettes the tags it unlocks, separated by commas. Each tag is also set as a Dialogue mark of the same word. savoir.points points (number), gain (number) The player's knowledge points changed (version 26): points is the new total, gain what was added (negative when spent in the tree). savoir.analyse connaissance (text), compte (number), besoin (number), cible (id) The player analysed an object of the world (version 26): cible, which counts for the knowledge connaissance; compte analyses done, besoin needed. savoir.refus connaissance (text), raison (text) A knowledge could not be learned (version 26): raison says why, in the player's language (what is needed first, missing points or items, a game script's refusal). dialogue.marquer marque (text), retirer (boolean?) Ask the dialogue system to set a mark, from a script or another system; with retirer true, to remove it. Dialogue conditions then see it. inventaire.retirer objet (text), quantite (number), fiche (number?) Ask the inventory to remove items, such as a payment. Answered by inventaire.change, or inventaire.manque if there are not enough. For a kind with unique copies (version 15): fiche removes that copy, otherwise the first ones; their records are destroyed. inventaire.ajouter objet (text), quantite (number), joueur (id?), fiche (number?) Ask the inventory to add items, such as a reward. Answered by inventaire.change, or inventaire.plein. With several players, joueur says whose bag; without it, the player whose action is being handled, or every player.

items.title: What it listens to
items.text: Event Fields Description savoir.apprendre connaissance (text), joueur (id?) Ask the knowledge system to teach connaissance to the player (version 26), even without what it needs first: a Trigger rule, a master in a Dialogue, a quest's reward. A game script can still refuse it (savoir.permise). savoir.donner_points points (number), joueur (id?) Ask the knowledge system to give points to the player (version 26), to spend in the knowledge window: a level gained, a book read. savoir.ouvrir table (text?) Ask the knowledge system to open its window (version 26); with table, the study of that research table's items. savoir.etudier objet (text), table (text?) Ask the knowledge system to study objet as at the research table named table (empty or missing: any table), as its button would (version 26). Refused, with savoir.refus, if something is missing. inventaire.change objet (text), quantite (number), total (number), chargement (boolean?), fiche (number?), jete (boolean?) The quantity of an item changed. total is the new quantity. chargement is true when a saved game gives the items back (game.load): nothing was picked up. For a unique copy (version 15), objet is its kind, fiche its record's number, total how many of that kind. With several stacks of a kind (version 21), total counts all of them; jete is true when a slot was dropped on the ground. inventaire.choisi objet (text), total (number), fiche (number?), double (boolean?), case (text?) The player clicked a slot of the inventory window: objet is the kind of item, total how many they carry. What it does belongs to the game: eat, equip, read. case (version 21) is the slot's key ("Wood~2" for a second stack). inventaire.manque objet (text), quantite (number), fiche (number?) Items could not be removed: there are not enough. inventaire.plein objet (text), fiche (number?), reste (number?) An item could not be added: every slot holds another kind of item (or another unique copy), or (version 21) every stack of its kind is full. reste: picked up in part, how many stayed on the ground. fabrication.fabrique objet (text), quantite (number), etabli (text), cible (text?), xp (number?), piste (text?) The player crafted a recipe: its ingredients left the inventory and objet (quantite of it) came in, at once or at the end of its time in the queue. etabli is the kind of station where it was made (empty bare-handed), cible the station object (missing bare-handed). interaction.utiliser cible (id), joueur (id) The player used the object in reach: a door, a merchant, an item to pick up. Whoever owns that object decides what it does. dialogue.marque marque (text) A dialogue set a mark: a word the game remembers (a line shown, an answer chosen). Every dialogue's conditions can use it. langue.change langue (text) Sent by the engine when the player changes the game's language (game.set_language, the Menu options). A module redraws what it already shows: its texts go through game.t and game.language.

items.title: Points a script can replace (game.override)
items.text:
The descriptions come from the code.

  • savoir.permise: function(default, connaissance, moyen) -> true, or false and the reason shown (text): whether this knowledge can be learned now. connaissance is its name (original language), moyen the way (depart, objet, etude, points, plan, evenement, marque, analyse, fabrication, apprendre). The default is true. To ask for a level, a place, a time of day.
  • savoir.texte: function(default, key) -> the text the knowledge window shows for that key: titre, titre_table, points, aucune, fermer, tout, connu, a_apprendre, verrouille, il_faut, apprendre, etudier, appris, deja, pas_assez, manque, refus, etude_rien, analyse, comment, moyen_depart, moyen_objet, moyen_etude, moyen_etude_table, moyen_cout, moyen_points, moyen_plan, moyen_evenement, moyen_marque, moyen_analyse, moyen_fabrication, moyen_autre, a_apprendre_raison, invite_table, invite_analyse. It may hold {connaissance}, {objet}, {n}, {total}, {table}, {liste} and {raison}, replaced afterwards (in the player's language). The default is the game's translation of the text in the original language; without one, French or English, after the player's language.

items.title: Knowledge (savoir)
items.text:
What the player knows how to do, and how they learn it: the research / tech tree / blueprint / recipe-discovery system of survival games, in user data. Activating it activates inventory and interaction; placing it on an object places interaction there too.

  • Knowledges: the game setting connaissances, a list of rows. A connaissance row (nom, description, categorie: a tab of the window, icone: an image, secrete: hidden until learned) is followed by its own rows:
  • prerequis (prerequis: another knowledge's name): needed first, whatever the way. Several rows: all needed. The window draws them as a tree.
  • debloque (debloque: recette | piece | etiquette, debloque_nom): a Crafting recipe (the name of what it gives) or a Building piece (its name) that stays closed until the knowledge is learned (game setting verrouiller, on); or a free tag, which the Trigger condition, scripts and Dialogue tests can look at (learning it also sets a Dialogue mark of the same word).
  • moyen (moyen, then its fields): one way to learn it. Add several rows for several ways; the first met is enough.
    • depart: known from the start.
    • objet + objet: when the player obtains that kind of item (picked up, crafted, given). Learned later if what it needs first is missing then.
    • etude + objet, nombre (used up), cout and cout_nombre (optional extra cost, used up too), table (a research table's name, empty: any): studied at a research table.
    • points + nombre: bought with points in the window (K).
    • plan + objet: reading a plan; a click on its slot in the inventory window uses one up (not if already known).
    • evenement + evenement: an event name; send it from a Dialogue answer (annonce), a quest's end (annonce), a Trigger rule (envoyer) or a script.
    • marque + marque: a Dialogue or quest mark.
    • analyse + nombre: analysing that many objects of the world (see below).
    • fabrication + objet, nombre: crafting that recipe that many times (learning by doing).
  • Research table: any object (an imported model) with this system (systems_attach), object setting role table (the default), nom_table (empty: its name without number). Using it (E) opens the study of what can be learned there.
  • Objects to analyse: object setting role analyse, analyse = the knowledge's name, analyse_retirer to remove it once analysed. Each object counts once. Tag many objects (wrecks, plants) the same way.
  • Points: points_depart; the list gains (evenement, cible: only for the object named, points), e.g. fabrication.fabrique 1, sante.mort with Wolf 2, quetes.fin 5; the Trigger action donner_points; the event savoir.donner_points.
  • Trigger: actions apprendre (connaissance; ignores what is needed first) and donner_points (points); every rule has condition (aucune, connait, ignore) and condition_valeur (a knowledge or a tag): a door only an initiate opens.
  • Events: it announces savoir.appris (connaissance, moyen, categorie, etiquettes), savoir.points, savoir.analyse, savoir.refus; it listens to savoir.apprendre (without connaissance, since version 4: the first one the player does not know yet), savoir.donner_points, savoir.ouvrir (table optional), savoir.etudier.
  • Hooks: savoir.permise (refuse learning now: a level, a place), savoir.texte (every text of the window). It answers fabrication.permise, construction.permise, declencheur.condition and interaction.texte itself: do not override those to lock recipes, write a knowledge instead.
  • A recipe of Crafting can also name its own knowledge (passed to fabrication.permise as an extra argument): it is closed until that knowledge or tag is known.
  • Window: control knowledge (K) (fenetre), pause_fenetre. largeur (old) is no longer used: widen the window by its screen.
  • Its window and its announcement are two screens delivered by the system (modules/savoir/ecrans/), which its script shows and fills:
  • « Savoir »: Fenêtre, Titre, Points, the list Onglets (row Onglet: Tout, then each category; the system's action onglet), the list Liste (it scrolls past the height given in its file), whose row Ligne holds Retrait (one step of the tree per level: its width in the file), Icône, Nom (the knowledge, its state, how to learn it), Apprendre (a button, the action apprendre: with points, or Étudier at a research table) and Vide (nothing to learn, alone on its row); then Message and Fermer (action fermer).
  • « Annonce du savoir » (top centre): Annonce (« Appris : Arc », an analysis). Change their look, places and sizes with screens_set (styles, not hand-made values): the rows' text takes what the window's width leaves, so widen Fenêtre and the rows follow. Never draw them again with game.hud_*, and never edit the system.
  • Gamepad and keyboard: B or Escape closes the window (Savoir/Fermer is its back button), like A or Enter on Close; the tabs and the Apprendre buttons are reached like any other button.
  • Testing: in game_run, press knowledge and read the report's hud: Savoir/Titre, Savoir/Points, the rows Savoir/Nom#<row> and Savoir/Apprendre#<row>, the tabs Savoir/Onglet#<n>, Savoir/Message; the announcement Annonce du savoir/Annonce.
  • Saved games keep what is learned, the points, the analyses and the counters.

items.title: Recipes
items.text:
Write names in the user's language. Recipes and pieces must already exist in fabrication / construction.

  • The default (a new game, the logic Khalil chose for survival): the default rows match the default recipes of fabrication: « Outils de pierre » (Hache, Pioche, Lance) and « Cuisine au feu » (Viande cuite, Poisson grillé, Baies grillées) known from the start (moyen depart); « Travail du fer » (Fer, Hache de fer, Pioche de fer) learned by obtaining « Minerai de fer » (moyen objet); « Boulangerie » (Pain, Ragoût) by obtaining « Farine », after « Cuisine au feu »; « Arc » studied at a research table (moyen etude, objet « Arc », the bow found is used up). So for « un jeu de survie », keep this logic (learn by obtaining an ingredient, study at a research table, a few known from the start), rename it in the user's words, and place one research table (any model, role table) near the workbench. Switch to points (ARK) or another style below only if the user asks.
  • Like Rust (research table + scrap, then a tech tree): a research table (any bench model, role table, nom_table "Research table"). Each weapon or tool: a knowledge debloque recette, with moyen etude (objet the item itself, cout "Scrap", cout_nombre 75). The tree: knowledges with prerequis and moyen points; gains give points for collecte.recolte or crafting. Shared tech for a team: commun on.
  • Like Valheim (discover by holding an ingredient; station level): each recipe's knowledge with moyen objet = its key ingredient ("Copper" teaches "Bronze axe"); chain them with prerequis (bronze needs copper smelting). The station level belongs to Crafting (its workbench name/level); the knowledge just opens the recipe. No window needed: fenetre can stay on as a codex.
  • Like Enshrouded (craftsmen unlock recipes): a character with a Dialogue whose answer sends an event (annonce "blacksmith.rescued"); knowledges with moyen evenement on it; or a quest's end (annonce); or a Trigger rule apprendre on the rescued NPC. Categories per craftsman ("Blacksmith", "Alchemist").
  • Like ARK (engrams with level points): every knowledge moyen points (nombre = its cost) and prerequis; gains on the level-up event of the game (or quetes.fin, sante.mort with cible); points_depart for the first ones.
  • Like Subnautica (scan fragments): fragments are objects with role analyse and analyse_retirer; the knowledge moyen analyse nombre 3.
  • Blueprints: an item "Forge blueprint" to pick up (inventaire), and a knowledge moyen plan objet "Forge blueprint".
  • Learning by doing: moyen fabrication objet "Arrow" nombre 20 teaches "Iron arrows".

items.title: Several players
items.text:
One copy per player: each learns for themselves, with their own points (their copy answers the recipe and piece locks for them only), and sees their own window and announcements. The game setting commun ("One knowledge for the whole group") shares what is learned and the points; the host's save keeps it.

items.title: Healing
items.text:
What carries this system gives health back to the player: a spring to touch, or a potion picked up into the inventory and drunk with a key, each with what it gives.

Identifier soins Version 5 Placed on objects yes Also activates Health

items.title: Settings for the whole game
items.text:
In the Systems panel (Developer mode), by opening the system's card.

Setting What it does Name in code Type Default Limits or choices Heal by walking over (what does not go to the inventory) Ticked: an object that heals on the spot, without going to the inventory (a spring, a heart), heals as soon as the player walks over it. Unticked: it must be used, if it also carries the Interaction system. au_contact Yes or no yes Reach to touch (m) The distance, in meters, at which the player touches an object that heals by walking over it. distance_contact Number 1.2 from 0.1 to 10 Action to drink a potion from the inventory The game's control action that drinks a potion carried ("heal": R by default, ↑ on a gamepad). The player drinks the first kind of potion they have. action Text heal Time between two potions (s) The minimum time, in seconds, between two potions drunk: longer, the player cannot drink them all at once in the middle of a fight. recharge Number 1 from 0 to 60 Use nothing up when health is full Ticked: when the player's health is full, no potion is drunk and no object disappears for nothing. vie_pleine Yes or no yes

items.title: Settings on each object
items.text:
In the Properties of an object or folder that carries the system, Systems section. A folder passes its values on to what it contains; an object can change a value for itself only.

Setting What it does Name in code Type Default Limits or choices Health given The health points this object gives back to the player, without going past their maximum health. montant Number 30 from 0 to 1 000 000 Effects given too (Status effects module) The identifiers of status effects this object gives on top of the health, separated by commas: "regeneration, rapidite". Empty: none. A potion that gives an effect can be drunk even at full health. effets Text (empty) Comes back after (s, 0: never) For an object that heals on the spot: it comes back after this many seconds. 0: it is gone for good. An arena whose healing comes back keeps a long fight playable. reapparition Number 0 from 0 to 3600

items.title: Controls added to the game
items.text:
They appear in the Game controls panel (Developer mode), where you can change their key.

Control Name for scripts Key Gamepad Drink a potion heal R ↑

items.title: Events
items.text: The descriptions come from the code.

items.title: What it announces
items.text: Event Fields Description soins.soin cible (id), montant (number), objet (text) The healing module gave health back: a potion drunk, a spring touched. objet is the kind of potion or the name of what healed. sante.soigner cible (id), montant (number) Ask the health module to give health back, up to its maximum. inventaire.retirer objet (text), quantite (number), fiche (number?) Ask the inventory to remove items, such as a payment. Answered by inventaire.change, or inventaire.manque if there are not enough. For a kind with unique copies (version 15): fiche removes that copy, otherwise the first ones; their records are destroyed.

items.title: What it listens to
items.text: Event Fields Description scene.change depuis (text), vers (text) Sent by the engine once the player has arrived in another scene of the game (game.go_to, or a passage). Scripts keep running across scenes: this is when a module looks at the objects of the new scene. sante.change cible (id), vie (number), max (number) An object's health changed, or is announced once when the game starts. interaction.utiliser cible (id), joueur (id) The player used the object in reach: a door, a merchant, an item to pick up. Whoever owns that object decides what it does. inventaire.change objet (text), quantite (number), total (number), chargement (boolean?), fiche (number?), jete (boolean?) The quantity of an item changed. total is the new quantity. chargement is true when a saved game gives the items back (game.load): nothing was picked up. For a unique copy (version 15), objet is its kind, fiche its record's number, total how many of that kind. With several stacks of a kind (version 21), total counts all of them; jete is true when a slot was dropped on the ground. action.prise action (text), prise (boolean), par (text), joueur (id?) A system takes a control action for itself, or gives it back (prise false) (version 24): gathering takes attack while the player aims at a resource that needs a tool, so the press chops instead of swinging a weapon. par names who says it ("collecte"). Fighting modules do not strike (nor block) with that action while any system holds it; tir takes attack, block and heal while a ranged weapon is held, so the right button aims and R reloads without drinking.

items.text: The text the agent reads before using this system.

items.title: Healing (soins)
items.text:
Objects carrying this system give health back to the player, each with its own montant (systems_set). Activating it activates the health module. Use it whenever the player can be hurt and fights last: without a way to heal, a long fight is lost in advance.

  • Picked up and drunk later (potions, food): place inventaire on the object too. It is picked up like any item, under its kind (the inventory's nom, or its name without a trailing number; a kind renamed by overriding inventaire.sorte is not seen here, so set nom instead). The action heal (R by default, ↑ on a gamepad) drinks the first kind carried and gives that kind's montant. recharge is the time between two. While a ranged weapon of tir is held, R reloads and does not drink (the event action.prise, as for any system that takes the key for itself); with another item or empty hands, R drinks again.
  • Used on the spot (a spring, a heart, a campfire): no inventory. It heals when the player walks over it (game setting au_contact, on by default), or when used if it also carries interaction. Then it is removed, or comes back after reapparition seconds: an arena whose healing comes back keeps a long fight possible.
  • With vie_pleine on (the default), nothing is used up while the player's health is full.
  • Each heal is announced by soins.soin (cible, montant, objet): listen to it for a sound or an effect. Health bars follow on their own (sante.change).
  • Name potions and food in the user's language. Do not heal from your own script with sante.soigner when this module fits.

items.title: Several players
items.text:
One copy per player: what a player touches or drinks heals that player.

This page is generated automatically from the WorldMint code (modules/soins/module.json, modules/soins/AGENT.md, modules/events.json): it always matches the editor.

items.title: Sounds
items.text:
The game's noises, placed on what makes them: footsteps of characters (timed by their animation, and by the ground), hits given and taken, deaths, doors and chests being used, ambience of a fire or a river, an enemy's alert cry. Plus, for the whole game: music, fight music, pickups. Several files separated by commas: a random one each time.

Identifier sons Version 8 Placed on objects yes

items.title: Settings for the whole game
items.text:
In the Systems panel (Developer mode), by opening the system's card.

Setting What it does Name in code Type Default Limits or choices Background music (loops from the start) The music looping from the start of the game. Several files separated by commas: a random one. musique Text (empty) Fight music (while an enemy chases the player) The music that replaces the background music while an enemy chases the player; the background music then fades back in. Empty: the background music keeps playing. musique_combat Text (empty) Music volume The music volume: 0 silent, 1 loudest. 0.5 keeps it under the game's noises. volume_musique Number 0.5 from 0 to 1 Item picked up (Inventory module) The sound played when the player picks something up (Inventory system). Several files separated by commas: a random one. ramassage Text (empty) Inventory full The sound played when the player can no longer pick up a new kind of item: their inventory is full. inventaire_plein Text (empty) Healing (potion drunk, spring touched: Healing module) The sound played at each heal of the Healing system: a potion drunk, a spring touched. soin Text (empty) Player exhausted (Stamina module) The sound played when the player runs out of stamina (Stamina system). essoufflement Text (empty) Sound mixer group: noises (steps, hits, deaths, doors, gathering, healing) The sound mixer group (Game tab, Sound mixer section) the game's noises go to: steps, hits, blocks, deaths, alerts, doors, gathering, healing, exhaustion. Its volume sets them all at once. groupe_bruits Group of the sound mixer effects Sound mixer group: looping ambiences (fire, river) The sound mixer group the looping ambiences placed on objects go to: a fire, a river, a forge. Lower it to push them into the background. groupe_ambiance Group of the sound mixer ambience Sound mixer group: cues (item picked up, inventory full) The sound mixer group the small cues that come from nowhere in particular go to: an item picked up, the inventory full. groupe_interface Group of the sound mixer ui Pitch variation for each sound (0: always the same) Slightly changes the pitch of each sound, so that twenty identical steps do not sound mechanical. 0: always the same; 0.08: barely; 0.3: very varied. variation Number 0.08 from 0 to 0.5

items.title: Settings on each object
items.text:
In the Properties of an object or folder that carries the system, Systems section. A folder passes its values on to what it contains; an object can change a value for itself only.

Setting What it does Name in code Type Default Limits or choices Footsteps (timed by the walk and run animation) This character's footsteps. With a walk or run animation, each step falls when a foot touches the ground. Give two to four files separated by commas for variety. pas Text (empty) Steps on this object (a floor, a bridge: replaces those of whoever walks on it) To place on a floor, a bridge, a carpet: whoever walks on it makes these steps instead of their own. The floor needs a collider. surface Text (empty) Without animation: distance between two steps when walking (m) For what moves without animation: one step every so many meters walked. When running, the stride gets longer, up to double. foulee Number 0.8 from 0.2 to 5 Footstep volume The footstep volume, compared with the other sounds of this object: 0 silent, 1 just as loud. volume_pas Number 0.6 from 0 to 1 Jump (the player) The sound played when the player jumps. Only used on the player. saut Text (empty) Landing after a jump or a fall (the player) The sound played when the player lands after a jump or a fall. atterrissage Text (empty) Strike, hit or miss (the weapon's swing) The sound of its weapon, played at each strike, whether it hits or not (Combat system). attaque Text (empty) Hit taken The sound played when it takes a hit, from the player or an enemy. coup_recu Text (empty) Hit blocked (the shield or blade sound) The sound played when it blocks a hit: the shield or blade stopping it. parade Text (empty) Death The sound played when it dies (Health system). mort Text (empty) Alert (an enemy starts chasing) The sound played when this enemy spots the player and starts chasing them. alerte Text (empty) When used (door, chest, lever: Interaction module) The sound played when the player uses it: a door, a chest, a lever (Interaction system). utiliser Text (empty) Gathering: each hit (axe in wood, pick in stone: Gathering module) The sound of each hit on this resource: the axe in wood, the pick in stone (Gathering system). recolte_coup Text (empty) Gathering: when used up (a tree falling, a rock bursting) The sound played when this resource is used up: a tree falling, a rock bursting. It stays where the resource was, even if it disappears. recolte_fin Text (empty) Looping ambience (fire, river, forge) A looping sound coming from this object: a fire, a river, a forge. Only the eight ambiences nearest the player play at the same time. ambiance Text (empty) Group of its sounds in the sound mixer (Automatic: by kind of sound) The sound mixer group all this object's sounds go to: Voice for a talking character, Ambience for a radio. Automatic: its noises go with the noises, its ambience with the ambiences. groupe Group of the sound mixer (empty) Volume of its sounds The volume of all this object's sounds: 0 silent, 1 loudest. They also get quieter with distance. volume Number 1 from 0 to 1 Range: beyond it, it is not heard (m) The distance, in meters, beyond which its sounds are no longer heard: 25 m for a character, more for a waterfall, less for a small fire. portee Number 25 from 2 to 300

items.title: Events
items.text: The descriptions come from the code.

items.title: What it listens to
items.text: Event Fields Description scene.change depuis (text), vers (text) Sent by the engine once the player has arrived in another scene of the game (game.go_to, or a passage). Scripts keep running across scenes: this is when a module looks at the objects of the new scene. combat.attaque source (id) Someone struck, whether it hit or not: the stamina module counts it. combat.coup cible (id), source (id), montant (number) An attack hit something. The health module, if present, has been asked to remove the damage. sante.mort cible (id), source (id?) An object's health reached zero. What happens next belongs to the game: the health module does nothing else, unless its setting says to destroy the object. interaction.utiliser cible (id), joueur (id) The player used the object in reach: a door, a merchant, an item to pick up. Whoever owns that object decides what it does. collecte.coup cible (id), coups (number), restants (number) The player hit a resource (a use of something carrying collecte). restants is how many hits are left before it is used up. collecte.epuise cible (id) A resource is used up and is about to disappear (destroyed, or hidden until it grows back): it still exists while this is sent. inventaire.change objet (text), quantite (number), total (number), chargement (boolean?), fiche (number?), jete (boolean?) The quantity of an item changed. total is the new quantity. chargement is true when a saved game gives the items back (game.load): nothing was picked up. For a unique copy (version 15), objet is its kind, fiche its record's number, total how many of that kind. With several stacks of a kind (version 21), total counts all of them; jete is true when a slot was dropped on the ground. inventaire.plein objet (text), fiche (number?), reste (number?) An item could not be added: every slot holds another kind of item (or another unique copy), or (version 21) every stack of its kind is full. reste: picked up in part, how many stayed on the ground. ennemi.etat cible (id), etat (text) An enemy changed state: patrouille (patrols), poursuite (chases the player), visee (a shooter aims before its first shot: the moment for a warning sound), attaque (hits in reach, or shoots), attente (waits its turn near the player, when enough others are already attacking), retour (goes back to its spot), mort (dead, does nothing more). endurance.change valeur (number), max (number), epuise (boolean) The player's stamina changed. epuise is true from zero until they regain a share of it: meanwhile they cannot run, jump or strike. sante.pare cible (id), source (id?), montant (number) A hit was blocked by a guard: montant is the damage it stopped. For a clang, sparks, a stamina cost. soins.soin cible (id), montant (number), objet (text) The healing module gave health back: a potion drunk, a spring touched. objet is the kind of potion or the name of what healed.

items.title: Points a script can replace (game.override)
items.text:
The descriptions come from the code.

  • sons.pas: function(default, id, sol, fichiers) -> the files of this footstep (text, commas allowed), or "" for silence. sol: the object under the feet or nil; fichiers: what the module would play (the ground's surface, or the walker's steps).

items.title: What the agent knows about this system
items.text: The text the agent reads before using this system.

items.title: Sounds (sons)
items.text:
The game's noises, placed on what makes them, like the other systems: on the player, on a folder of skeletons, on a door, on a campfire. Each object or folder has its own sounds. Only with sound files the user has: find them with assets_search and kind sound.

  • Placed on objects (systems_attach, then systems_set): pas (footsteps: for animated characters, each one falls when a foot touches the ground in the walk or run animation, at any speed; foulee in metres only serves objects without animation), surface (placed on a floor, a bridge, a carpet: whoever walks on it makes these steps instead of their own), saut and atterrissage (the player's jump and landing), attaque (the swing of its weapon, hit or miss), coup_recu, parade (a hit it blocked), mort, alerte (an enemy starts chasing), utiliser (a door, a chest, a lever used through the interaction module), ambiance (a loop coming from it: fire, river, forge; only the nearest play), plus volume, portee (beyond it, not heard), foulee, volume_pas.
  • For the whole game (modules_set): musique, musique_combat (while an enemy chases the player), volume_musique, ramassage, inventaire_plein, soin (a heal from the module soins), essoufflement, variation (a slightly different pitch each time, so twenty identical sounds do not sound mechanical).
  • Sound mixer groups: its noises (steps, hits, deaths, doors, gathering, heals) go to groupe_bruits (effects), the looping ambiences to groupe_ambiance (ambience), pickups and a full inventory to groupe_interface (ui), the music to music. On an object, groupe sends all its sounds to one group (voice for a talking character, ambience for a radio); empty: by kind of sound. Balance whole groups with mixer_set, not each object's volume.
  • Several files separated by commas give a random one each time: give footsteps and hits two to four files when the pack has them.
  • Shipped melee sounds (cite "sons/<pack>/<file>", copied into the project with their licence): attaque of a swordsman sons/armes-blanches/epee_coup_1.wav, sons/armes-blanches/epee_coup_2.wav, sons/armes-blanches/epee_coup_3.wav (a dagger dague_coup_1, an axe hache_coup_1), parade sons/armes-blanches/parade_1.wav, sons/armes-blanches/parade_2.wav, sons/armes-blanches/parade_3.wav, sons/armes-blanches/parade_4.wav (an axe parade_hache_1), coup_recu sons/explosions-magie/coup_lourd_1.wav, sons/explosions-magie/coup_lourd_2.wav. Drawing and sheathing a blade (epee_degainer_1..2, dague_degainer_1..2, epee_rengainer_1..2) are for a script (game.sound), for instance when a weapon is taken in hand.
  • It only listens to what the other modules announce: hits and swings come from combat.basique and ennemis, deaths from sante, uses from interaction, pickups from inventaire. A sound the game needs elsewhere (a lever in a puzzle, a cutscene) is a game.sound in that script.
  • Different grounds: place the module on each kind of floor (or its folder) with surface: grass, stone, wood. The floor needs a collider. A character still needs the module on itself to make steps at all.
  • In game_run nothing is heard: the report's sounds lists what played.

items.title: Several players
items.text: One for the whole game, what the host hears: sounds placed somewhere (steps, hits, jumps of every player) are heard from everyone; sounds with no place (picking up, running out of breath) are the host's only. Guests do not hear the game's sounds yet.

items.title: Several players
items.text:
Its sounds reach the guests: the sounds placed somewhere (steps, hits, jumps of every player) and the music are heard by everyone, each from their own place; a sound without a place for one player (picking up, getting out of breath) is heard by that player only.

This page is generated automatically from the WorldMint code (modules/sons/module.json, modules/sons/AGENT.md, modules/events.json): it always matches the editor.

items.title: Ranged weapons
items.text:
Pistols, rifles, bows, crossbows and grenades: the player aims (right click), shoots (left click) and reloads (R). Each weapon is a row of settings: damage, head, fire rate, spread, recoil, magazine, ammunition. It hits what carries Health.

Identifier tir Version 11 Placed on objects no Also activates Health

items.title: Settings for the whole game
items.text:
In the Systems panel (Developer mode), by opening the system's card.

Setting What it does Name in code Type Default Limits or choices Weapons given at the start (names, separated by commas) The weapons each player has from the start, by their name in the "Weapons" list, such as "Pistol, Bow". With the Inventory, they go into their bag with their starting ammunition and are chosen in the bar; without it, the mouse wheel goes from one to the next. Empty: the player picks up their weapons. armes_depart Text (empty) Several players: players can hurt each other In a game with several players: ticked, a shot also hurts the other players (and a grenade its thrower). Unticked (the default), friends do not hurt each other. Like the setting of the same name in Basic combat. blesser_joueurs Yes or no no Reload by itself when the magazine is empty Ticked: shooting with an empty magazine reloads the weapon, if ammunition is left. Unticked: the player has to press Reload (R). recharge_auto Yes or no yes Show the crosshair and the ammunition Shows on screen, while a ranged weapon is held: the crosshair, the marker when a shot hits, the ammunition and the reloading. Untick it if your game draws its own: shooting works the same. afficher Yes or no yes Crosshair in the centre (opens up with the spread) Four lines around the place aimed at, as far apart as shots can stray: tight when aiming still, wide when running or after a burst. reticule Yes or no yes Marker when a shot hits A brief cross in the centre when a shot hits what carries Health; bigger and in the "head" colour for a head shot. marqueur Yes or no yes Crosshair colour The colour of the crosshair's lines and of the hit marker. A dark outline sets them apart from any background. couleur_reticule Color #ffffff Colour of a head shot The colour of the marker when the shot hits the head: red by default, so it is recognised at a glance. couleur_tete Color #ff4d3a Flashes, trails, impacts and bullet holes Each shot shows the flash at the muzzle and the bullet's trail (if the weapon has them), an impact where it hits and a hole on walls. Untick it for a game without particles. effets Yes or no yes Shoulder to aim over Over which shoulder the camera goes when the player aims, in third-person view. epaule Choice in a list Right droite: Rightgauche: Left View speed while aiming How fast the view turns while the player aims. It is already divided by the weapon's zoom, so a scope stays as easy to hold as a pistol: 1 usually suits, less for a steadier aim. sensibilite Number 1 from 0.05 to 4 Aim assist with a gamepad (0: none) With a gamepad only: the view slows down near a target carrying Health and moves a little toward it. 0.3 helps without aiming for the player; 0 turns it off. aide Number 0.3 from 0 to 1 Action to shoot The game's control action that shoots ("attack": the left mouse button by default). While a ranged weapon is held, Basic combat does not strike with it. action Text attack Action to aim The action to hold to aim ("aim": the right mouse button, or the left trigger on a gamepad). The camera moves to the shoulder, comes closer by the weapon's zoom, and shots tighten. action_visee Text aim Action to reload The action that reloads the weapon held ("reload": R, or X on a gamepad). action_recharge Text reload Block action replaced by aiming Basic combat's block action ("block"), on the same key as aiming: while a ranged weapon is held, that key aims instead of blocking. action_parade Text block Healing action replaced by reloading The Healing module's "drink a potion" action ("heal"), on the same key as reloading (R): while a ranged weapon is held, R reloads and does not drink. Empty: both work together. action_soin Text heal Arms clip at rest, weapon in hand Played on the upper body while a firearm is in hand without aiming, while the legs walk or run. A clip of the player's character (Pistol_Idle_Loop of the UAL1 pack by default). Empty, or missing from its model: it keeps its animation. clip_repos Player animation Pistol_Idle_Loop Arms clip while aiming Played on the upper body while aiming with a firearm; the weapon is fitted on this clip's pose (the grip in its fist). Pistol_Aim_Neutral of the UAL1 pack by default. clip_visee Player animation Pistol_Aim_Neutral Aiming up clip The same pose aiming straight up (90°): blended with the aiming clip by where the player looks. Empty: the back leans. clip_visee_haut Player animation Pistol_Aim_Up Aiming down clip The same pose aiming straight down (90°): blended with the aiming clip by where the player looks. Empty: the back leans. clip_visee_bas Player animation Pistol_Aim_Down Shot clip Played once on the upper body at each firearm shot, then the aiming or rest clip takes over again. clip_tir Player animation Pistol_Shoot Reload clip Played on the upper body during the reload, sped up or slowed down to last the weapon's reload time. clip_recharge Player animation Pistol_Reload Throw clip (grenade) Played once on the upper body when a thrown weapon leaves (a grenade). OverhandThrow of the UAL2 pack by default. clip_lancer Player animation OverhandThrow Fingers clip The fingers taken from this clip (at its middle) during the weapon's gestures, and to fit the weapon in the fist. For clips of a pack whose hands have no fingers (KayKit: Ranged_2H_Aiming, Ranged_Bow_Aiming_Idle...): Pistol_Aim_Neutral or Idle_Torch_Loop close the fist. Empty: the fingers of the clip played. clip_mains Player animation (empty) Arms clip with a bow, aiming Played on the upper body while aiming with a bow: the left arm stretched toward the target, the string drawn to the corner of the mouth; the bow is fitted in its left fist. Bow_Aim_Loop of the worldmint-armes pack by default; without it on the character, Idle_Torch_Loop of UAL1. clip_arc Player animation Bow_Aim_Loop Arms clip with a bow, at rest Played on the upper body with a bow in hand, not aiming: the bow low and forward in the left hand. Empty: the bow's aiming clip. clip_arc_repos Player animation Bow_Idle_Loop Bow release clip Played once on the upper body when the arrow leaves: the right hand opens and moves back a little. clip_arc_tir Player animation Bow_Release Support hand on the weapon With a shoulder weapon, the left hand is put on the real weapon after the clip: on each weapon's measured handguard (or, out of the arm's reach, the most forward point it reaches under the weapon, never the magazine), and on the magazine during a reload. Unticked: the hand stays where the clip puts it. main_soutien Yes or no yes Arms clip at rest, shoulder weapon Played on the upper body while a shoulder weapon (rifle, shotgun, sniper rifle, submachine gun, crossbow) is in hand without aiming: low ready, the muzzle down, the stock at the shoulder. Rifle_Idle_Loop of the worldmint-armes pack by default; missing from the character, the pistol clips are used. clip_fusil_repos Player animation Rifle_Idle_Loop Aiming clip, shoulder weapon Played while aiming with a shoulder weapon: the stock in the shoulder pocket, the cheek on the stock, the left hand under the handguard; the weapon is fitted on this clip's right fist. clip_fusil_visee Player animation Rifle_Aim_Neutral Aiming up clip, shoulder weapon A shoulder weapon aiming up (75°), blended by where the player looks. clip_fusil_visee_haut Player animation Rifle_Aim_Up Aiming down clip, shoulder weapon A shoulder weapon aiming down (75°), blended by where the player looks. clip_fusil_visee_bas Player animation Rifle_Aim_Down Shot clip, shoulder weapon Played once at each shot of a shoulder weapon: the recoil into the shoulder (0.25 s). clip_fusil_tir Player animation Rifle_Shoot Reload clip, shoulder weapon Played during a shoulder weapon's reload, stretched to the reload time: the left hand goes to the magazine, down, back up, back to the handguard. clip_fusil_recharge Player animation Rifle_Reload Arms clip at rest, shotgun Played on the upper body while a weapon with the “shotgun” gestures is in hand without aiming: the right hand on the wrist of the stock, the left hand on the pump. Shotgun_Idle_Loop of the worldmint-armes pack; missing from the character, the rifle clips are used. clip_pompe_repos Player animation Shotgun_Idle_Loop Aiming clip, shotgun Played while aiming with a shotgun; the weapon is fitted on this clip's right fist (on the wrist of the stock). clip_pompe_visee Player animation Shotgun_Aim_Neutral Aiming up clip, shotgun A shotgun aiming up (75°), blended by where the player looks. clip_pompe_visee_haut Player animation Shotgun_Aim_Up Aiming down clip, shotgun A shotgun aiming down (75°), blended by where the player looks. clip_pompe_visee_bas Player animation Shotgun_Aim_Down Shot clip, shotgun Played once at each shotgun shot: the recoil into the shoulder (0.3 s). clip_pompe_tir Player animation Shotgun_Shoot Pump clip, shotgun Played after the shot clip: the left hand pulls the pump back then pushes it forward (0.5 s). Empty: no pump gesture. clip_pompe_pompe Player animation Shotgun_Pump Reload clip, shotgun Played during a shotgun's reload, stretched to the reload time: three shells taken from the belt and slid in one by one from below. clip_pompe_recharge Player animation Shotgun_Reload Arms clip at rest, sniper rifle Played on the upper body while a weapon with the “sniper rifle” gestures is in hand without aiming: low ready, the muzzle down, the head upright. Sniper_Idle_Loop of the worldmint-armes pack; missing from the character, the rifle clips are used. clip_precision_repos Player animation Sniper_Idle_Loop Aiming clip, sniper rifle Played while aiming with a weapon with the “sniper rifle” gestures: the scope at the eye, the head barely lowered; the weapon is fitted on this clip's right fist. clip_precision_visee Player animation Sniper_Aim_Neutral Aiming up clip, sniper rifle Aiming up (75°), blended by where the player looks. clip_precision_visee_haut Player animation Sniper_Aim_Up Aiming down clip, sniper rifle Aiming down (75°), blended by where the player looks. clip_precision_visee_bas Player animation Sniper_Aim_Down Shot clip, sniper rifle Played once at each shot: the recoil into the shoulder (0.25 s), a slight overshoot. clip_precision_tir Player animation Sniper_Shoot Reload clip, sniper rifle Played during the reload, stretched to its time: the left hand goes to the magazine, takes it out, puts one in, comes back under the weapon. clip_precision_recharge Player animation Sniper_Reload Arms clip at rest, crossbow Played on the upper body while a weapon with the “crossbow” gestures is in hand without aiming: low ready, the muzzle down, the head upright. Crossbow_Idle_Loop of the worldmint-armes pack; missing from the character, the rifle clips are used. clip_arbalete_repos Player animation Crossbow_Idle_Loop Aiming clip, crossbow Played while aiming with a weapon with the “crossbow” gestures: the stock in the shoulder pocket, the left hand under the fore-end; the weapon is fitted on this clip's right fist. clip_arbalete_visee Player animation Crossbow_Aim_Neutral Aiming up clip, crossbow Aiming up (75°), blended by where the player looks. clip_arbalete_visee_haut Player animation Crossbow_Aim_Up Aiming down clip, crossbow Aiming down (75°), blended by where the player looks. clip_arbalete_visee_bas Player animation Crossbow_Aim_Down Shot clip, crossbow Played once at each shot: the recoil into the shoulder (0.25 s), a slight overshoot. clip_arbalete_tir Player animation Crossbow_Shoot Reload clip, crossbow Played during the reload, stretched to its time: the left hand takes a bolt at the hip, lays it on the rail, draws the string back to the latch, comes back under the fore-end. clip_arbalete_recharge Player animation Crossbow_Reload Bow draw clip Played once when starting to aim with a bow: the bow rises toward the target, the right hand takes the string and draws it to the corner of the mouth (0.6 s); then the bow's aiming clip loops. Empty: no gesture. clip_arc_bander Player animation Bow_Draw Weapons One row per weapon, all of them editable: pistol, revolver, assault rifle, submachine gun, shotgun, sniper rifle, bow, crossbow and grenade are ready, with their shipped model.
