items.title: The fields of each “Weapon”
items.text:
In the Properties, each “Weapon” has its own numbered frame; Add: Weapon adds one, the cross removes it. A field only appears when it is useful: under its name, the table says when.

Setting What it does Name in code Type Default Limits or choices Name (the kind of item held in hand) The weapon's name, which is also the Inventory's kind of item: holding a "Pistol" in the bar puts this weapon in hand. nom Text Arme Kind of shot A bullet hits at once what is on the aiming line (firearms). A projectile flies, falls with gravity and can be seen: an arrow, a bolt, a grenade. sorte Choice in a list Bullet (hits at once, in a straight line) balle: Bullet (hits at once, in a straight line)projectile: Projectile that flies and falls (arrow, bolt, grenade) Damage of a shot The health points a shot removes, before the target's armor; for a shotgun, those of each pellet. 20 against 100 health points: five shots. degats Number 20 from 0 to 1 000 000 Head multiplier Damage is multiplied by this number when the shot hits the head: 2 counts double, 1 like anywhere else. The head is found on each model's skeleton. tete Number 2 from 0 to 100 Full damage up to (m) Up to this distance, in metres, the shot does all its damage. Beyond it, damage drops until the next distance. chute_debut Number 25 from 0 to 10 000 Weakest damage from (m) From this distance, in metres, the shot only does the share of damage below: a shotgun loses quickly, a sniper rifle hardly at all. chute_fin Number 60 from 0 to 10 000 Share of damage kept far away (%) The share of damage left at the longest range, as a percentage: 100, the weapon loses nothing with distance; 20, a fifth is left. degats_loin Number 60 from 0 to 100 Range (m) How far, in metres, a bullet can hit; for a projectile, how far the point aimed at is looked for. portee Number 150 from 1 to 5000 Most shots per second How many shots the weapon can make in one second: 5 for a pistol, 10 for an assault rifle, less than 1 for a sniper rifle. cadence Number 5 from 0.05 to 30 Firing mode Single shot: one shot per press. Burst: a few shots in a row per press. Automatic: the weapon fires as long as the key is held, at its rate. mode Choice in a list Single shot (one shot per press) coup_par_coup: Single shot (one shot per press)rafale: Burst (a few shots per press)automatique: Automatic (fires while held) Shots per burstshown only if Firing mode is “Burst (a few shots per press)” How many shots each press fires, at the weapon's rate. rafale Number 3 from 2 to 20, as a whole number Pellets per shot How many bullets each shot fires, each with its own spread: 1 for most weapons, 8 for a shotgun. plombs Number 1 from 1 to 32, as a whole number Spread without aiming (°) By how many degrees at most a shot strays from the centre when the player shoots without aiming. 0: always in the centre. dispersion_hanche Number 2 from 0 to 45 Spread while aiming (°) The same while the player aims: smaller, aiming pays off. A shotgun keeps a wide spray. dispersion_visee Number 0.4 from 0 to 45 Extra spread while moving (°) The degrees added while the player walks or runs: shooting while still is more precise. dispersion_marche Number 1.5 from 0 to 45 Extra spread at each shot (°) The degrees added by each shot, which then fade away: a long burst widens, measured shots stay precise. dispersion_tir Number 1 from 0 to 45 Spread recovery (° per second) How fast the spread added by shots comes back to zero, in degrees per second. dispersion_retour Number 8 from 0 to 200 Recoil upward (°) By how many degrees the view jumps up at each shot, before coming back by itself: 2 to 4 for a pistol, 6 to 10 for a shotgun. recul Number 2.5 from 0 to 45 Sideways recoil, at random (°) At most how many degrees the view moves left or right at each shot, at random: a little makes the weapon feel alive. recul_cote Number 0.8 from 0 to 45 Shots per magazine (0: no magazine) How many shots before reloading. 0: no magazine, each shot takes one piece of ammunition directly (a bow, grenades). chargeur Number 12 from 0 to 1000, as a whole number Ammunition (empty: endless) The kind of item the weapon uses up, such as "Bullets" or "Arrows": with the Inventory, it is picked up and counted in the bag. Empty: endless ammunition. For a grenade, its own name: each throw takes one. munitions Text (empty) Starting ammunition The ammunition the player gets with the weapon when it is given at the start (on top of a full magazine). Without the Inventory, it is the reserve the weapon keeps itself. reserve Number 48 from 0 to 100 000, as a whole number Reload time (s) How many seconds a reload lasts; the player cannot shoot meanwhile. Switching weapons interrupts it. rechargement Number 1.4 from 0 to 30 Zoom while aiming How much closer the view comes when the player aims: 1.5 for most weapons, 4 or more for a sniper scope. zoom Number 1.5 from 1 to 8 Projectile speed (m/s)shown only if Kind of shot is “Projectile that flies and falls (arrow, bolt, grenade)” The speed at launch, in metres per second: about 55 for an arrow, 80 for a bolt, 15 for a thrown grenade. vitesse Number 60 from 1 to 2000 Projectile gravity (1: normal)shown only if Kind of shot is “Projectile that flies and falls (arrow, bolt, grenade)” How the projectile falls: 1 like a stone, 0 straight on (a magic ball), in between for an arrow that carries far. gravite Number 1 from 0 to 10 Flight time, or fuse (s)shown only if Kind of shot is “Projectile that flies and falls (arrow, bolt, grenade)” After this many seconds, the projectile goes. For a grenade that bounces, it is its fuse: it explodes at the end. duree Number 6 from 0.1 to 60 Projectile model (a hidden object)shown only if Kind of shot is “Projectile that flies and falls (arrow, bolt, grenade)” An object of the scene, usually hidden, a copy of which flies: an arrow, a grenade. Its longest side follows the path. Empty: the projectile cannot be seen. modele_projectile Object of the scene (empty) Sticks in what it hitsshown only if Kind of shot is “Projectile that flies and falls (arrow, bolt, grenade)” Ticked: the arrow stays stuck in what it hits and follows it (a walking enemy), then goes after a few seconds. plante Yes or no no Bounce (0: stops at the first hit)shown only if Kind of shot is “Projectile that flies and falls (arrow, bolt, grenade)” The share of its speed the projectile keeps when bouncing: 0.35 for a grenade that rolls a little. 0: it stops where it hits. rebond Number 0 from 0 to 1 Explosion radius (m, 0: no explosion) The shot explodes where it ends: everything carrying Health within this radius, with no wall in between, loses damage that drops with distance, and what moves is blown away. 5 for a grenade. explosion Number 0 from 0 to 100 Push on what is hit (m/s) How hard a shot pushes what it hits, from the point hit: a crate that spins, an enemy that steps back. 0: nothing moves. poussee Number 3 from 0 to 100 Flash at the muzzle A firearm makes a brief flash of light and a little smoke at the muzzle. Untick it for a bow or a silenced weapon. eclair Yes or no yes Bright trail of the bulletshown only if Kind of shot is “Bullet (hits at once, in a straight line)” A bright streak flies from the muzzle to the point hit, to see where the bullet goes. trainee Yes or no yes Model held (a hidden object of the scene) Without the Inventory system, the object of the scene shown in the hand (put it in the character's hand in the editor, then hide it). With the Inventory, its "Models in hand" list shows it. modele Object of the scene (empty) Weapon model (a file) The file of the model held in hand when no object of the scene is chosen above and the Inventory shows none. The ready weapons have a model shipped with WorldMint (copied into the project with its licence when the game starts). The grip goes into the palm and the barrel follows the aim, measured on the model. modele_fichier model (empty) Real length of the weapon (m, 0: the object's) The weapon's real length, for a 1.8 m character: the model in hand (the row's file, or the Inventory's) is brought to this length, measured along the barrel (a bow's height), then scaled to the character's height measured on its model. Reference lengths: pistol 0.20 m, revolver 0.28, submachine gun 0.6, assault rifle 0.9, shotgun 1.0, sniper rifle 1.15, crossbow 0.8, bow 1.45 (sword 0.95, dagger 0.3). 0: the object's size is kept. An object placed by hand in the editor keeps its own. longueur Number 0 from 0 to 5 Front of the model (the muzzle) The side of the model where the muzzle is: where the shot starts, turned toward the aim. Found by itself, it is the thinnest end of its longest axis (the stock and the grip are at the back). Choose an axis if a weapon is held backwards. avant_modele Choice in a list Found by itself (the thinnest end) auto: Found by itself (the thinnest end)+x: +X-x: −X+y: +Y-y: −Y+z: +Z-z: −Z Way to hold A firearm or a crossbow: the grip in the palm, the barrel forward. A bow: upright in the fist, its length along the thumb, its wood forward. prise Choice in a list Like a firearm (the barrel along the fingers) arme: Like a firearm (the barrel along the fingers)debout: Upright, like a bow (across the fist) Hand that holds The hand the weapon goes in, found by measuring the character's skeleton: usually the right one, the left one for a bow. main Choice in a list Right hand droite: Right handgauche: Left hand Size (1: real size) The weapon in hand takes its real length ("Length", for a 1.8 m character), scaled to the character's height measured on its model. This number makes it bigger or smaller: 1 usually, 1.5 for a cartoon weapon. taille Number 1 from 0.1 to 5 Hold How the character holds the weapon. Two-handed: the butt against the shoulder, one hand on the grip, the other under the barrel, the weapon pointed along the aim (low across the body at rest). Like a bow: in the left hand, the arm stretched and the string drawn while aiming. Found by itself: a bow if it is held upright, two hands if the weapon is longer than three quarters of the arm, otherwise one hand. tenue Choice in a list Found by itself (from the weapon's length) auto: Found by itself (from the weapon's length)une_main: One-handed (a pistol)deux_mains: Two-handed (a rifle: butt against the shoulder)arc: Like a bow (the string drawn while aiming) Grip (where the hand holds, -1: found by itself) Where the hand holds the weapon, along its length: 0 at the back (the stock), 1 at the muzzle. -1: the grip is measured on the model (the rear-most part hanging under the weapon, behind the magazine). Only set it for a model the measure gets wrong: the hand held the magazine or the stock. position_prise Number -1 from -1 to 1 Handguard (where the other hand holds, -1: found by itself) Two-handed, where the other hand supports the weapon, along its length: 0 at the back, 1 at the muzzle. -1: measured (under the barrel, in front of the magazine). position_garde_main Number -1 from -1 to 1 Projectile model (a file)shown only if Kind of shot is “Projectile that flies and falls (arrow, bolt, grenade)” The file of the model that flies, when no hidden object is chosen above: an arrow, a bolt. Its longest side follows the path. modele_projectile_fichier model (empty) Size of the flash The flash already follows the weapon's length (bigger for a rifle than for a pistol); this number makes it bigger or smaller: 1 usually, 0.5 for a discreet weapon. taille_eclair Number 1 from 0.1 to 5 Shot sound (optional) The sound played at each shot, from the player. Several files separated by commas: one at random at each shot, so a burst does not repeat the same bang. The ready-made weapons have the sounds shipped with the editor. son_tir Sound from the library (empty) Empty sound (optional) The little click played when the player shoots without ammunition. Several files separated by commas: one at random. son_vide Sound from the library (empty) Reload sound (optional) The sound played at the start of each reload. Several files separated by commas: one at random. son_recharge Sound from the library (empty) Sound when aiming (optional) The sound played when the player starts aiming: the string of a bow being drawn. Empty for a firearm. Several files separated by commas: one at random. son_visee Sound from the library (empty) Impact sound (optional) The sound played where the shot lands: an arrow sticking in, a bolt. Once per thing hit. Several files separated by commas: one at random. son_impact Sound from the library (empty) Explosion sound (optional) The sound played where the weapon explodes (a grenade, with an explosion radius). Several files separated by commas: one at random. son_explosion Sound from the library (empty) Character's gestures Which upper-body clips this weapon plays: one family per kind of weapon, each with rest, aim, shot and reload clips made for it (handgun, rifle, shotgun, sniper rifle, crossbow), the bow (draw, aim, release), a grenade throw, or none. Found by themselves: a bow if held upright, a throw if it has no model, a shoulder weapon if held two-handed (or at least 45 cm long), otherwise a firearm. gestes Choice in a list Found by themselves auto: Found by themselvesarme_courte: Handgun (the pistol clips)fusil: Assault rifle, submachine gun (the rifle clips)fusil_pompe: Shotgun (wrist of the stock, pump)precision: Sniper rifle (the scope at the eye)arbalete: Crossbowarme: Firearm (old name of “Handgun”)arc: Bow (the bow clip)lancer: Throw (a grenade)aucun: None Aiming clip, instead of the setting (optional) A clip of the player's character played on the upper body while aiming with this weapon, instead of the « Arms clip while aiming ». Empty: the setting's. animation_tenue Player animation (empty) Shot clip, instead of the setting (optional) A clip of the player's character played once on the upper body at each shot of this weapon. Empty: the « Shot clip » (or the throw clip). animation_tir Player animation (empty) Reload clip, instead of the setting (optional) A clip of the player's character played on the upper body during this weapon's reload, lasting the reload time. Empty: the « Reload clip ». animation_recharge Player animation (empty)

items.title: Controls added to the game
items.text:
They appear in the Game controls panel (Developer mode), where you can change their key.

Control Name for scripts Key Gamepad Aim aim Right-click LT Reload reload R X Next weapon (without inventory) weapon_next Wheel down —

items.title: Events
items.text: The descriptions come from the code.

items.title: What it announces
items.text: Event Fields Description tir.arme arme (text), joueur (id?) The ranged weapon in the player's hand changed (version 25): arme is its name in the tir module's list, "" when no ranged weapon is held (another item, empty hands). tir.tir source (id), arme (text), origine (vector), direction (vector) The player fired a ranged weapon (version 25), whether it hits or not: origine is the muzzle, direction the aim before spread. For a sound, a noise that alerts enemies, a counter. tir.touche cible (id), source (id), arme (text), montant (number), partie (text?), point (vector), tete (boolean) A shot of the player hit something carrying Health (version 25); the health module has been asked to remove montant (before armor). partie is tete, torse, bras or jambes (missing for an object or an explosion); tete is true for a head shot. All the pellets of one shotgun shot on the same target make one tir.touche. tir.recharge source (id), arme (text), etat (text), chargeur (number), reserve (number) A reload of the weapon in hand (version 25): etat is debut (it starts), fin (the magazine is filled) or annule (the weapon was put away meanwhile). chargeur is what the magazine holds, reserve the ammunition left (-1: endless). tir.vide source (id), arme (text) The player pulled the trigger with nothing to shoot (version 25): an empty magazine or no ammunition left. For a click sound or a message. tir.explosion source (id), arme (text), point (vector), rayon (number) A shot of the player exploded (version 25): a grenade at the end of its fuse or a rocket on impact. Health was removed within rayon metres, with no wall in between. sante.blesser cible (id), montant (number), source (id?) Ask the health module to remove health from an object. action.prise action (text), prise (boolean), par (text), joueur (id?) A system takes a control action for itself, or gives it back (prise false) (version 24): gathering takes attack while the player aims at a resource that needs a tool, so the press chops instead of swinging a weapon. par names who says it ("collecte"). Fighting modules do not strike (nor block) with that action while any system holds it; tir takes attack, block and heal while a ranged weapon is held, so the right button aims and R reloads without drinking. inventaire.ajouter objet (text), quantite (number), joueur (id?), fiche (number?) Ask the inventory to add items, such as a reward. Answered by inventaire.change, or inventaire.plein. With several players, joueur says whose bag; without it, the player whose action is being handled, or every player. inventaire.retirer objet (text), quantite (number), fiche (number?) Ask the inventory to remove items, such as a payment. Answered by inventaire.change, or inventaire.manque if there are not enough. For a kind with unique copies (version 15): fiche removes that copy, otherwise the first ones; their records are destroyed.

items.title: What it listens to
items.text: Event Fields Description inventaire.en_main objet (text), avant (text), place (number), chargement (boolean?), joueur (id?), fiche (number?), source (text?) What the player holds in hand changed (version 24): the slot chosen in the inventory's bar (keys 1 to 9, wheel), an item used up, a load (chargement true). objet is the kind held, "" for empty hands; avant the one held before; place the bar slot (0: nothing). Gathering checks the tool held; a game script equips a sword with it. inventaire.change objet (text), quantite (number), total (number), chargement (boolean?), fiche (number?), jete (boolean?) The quantity of an item changed. total is the new quantity. chargement is true when a saved game gives the items back (game.load): nothing was picked up. For a unique copy (version 15), objet is its kind, fiche its record's number, total how many of that kind. With several stacks of a kind (version 21), total counts all of them; jete is true when a slot was dropped on the ground. action.prise action (text), prise (boolean), par (text), joueur (id?) A system takes a control action for itself, or gives it back (prise false) (version 24): gathering takes attack while the player aims at a resource that needs a tool, so the press chops instead of swinging a weapon. par names who says it ("collecte"). Fighting modules do not strike (nor block) with that action while any system holds it; tir takes attack, block and heal while a ranged weapon is held, so the right button aims and R reloads without drinking. joueur.occupe occupe (boolean), par (text) The player's hands are taken by something else than fighting (version 23): a building mode where the click places a piece, a tool being aimed. occupe true when it starts, false when it ends; par names who says it ("construction"), so several can overlap. Fighting modules do not strike nor block while any of them keeps the player busy. projectile.touche projectile (number), owner (id?), cible (id?), point (vector), normale (vector), partie (text?), os (text?), vitesse (vector), eau (boolean?), data (table?) A projectile launched by game.projectile hit something: cible is the object hit (nil for the terrain and for water), partie the part of a character's body (tete, torse, bras, jambes; missing for an object), os the bone, vitesse its velocity on arrival (m/s), data the table given at launch. eau = true when it entered water (point on the surface): it goes on, strongly slowed, and sinks (put a splash there, game.effect("eclaboussure", e.point), or stop it with game.stop_projectile). Announced by the engine; a projectile that bounces announces each hit. projectile.fin projectile (number), owner (id?), raison (text), point (vector), data (table?) A projectile launched by game.projectile is gone: raison is touche (it hit and stopped), duree (its life ran out: a grenade explodes here), plantee (stuck, its delay is over), cible_partie (what it was stuck in disappeared), eau (a projectile without gravity stopped by water) or arrete (game.stop_projectile). point is where it ended. Announced by the engine. tir.tenir arme (text), joueur (id?) Without the Inventory, give a ranged weapon to the player (if they do not have it yet, with its starting ammunition) and put it in hand (version 25); arme "" puts it away. With the Inventory, use inventaire.ajouter and inventaire.tenir instead.

items.title: Points a script can replace (game.override)
items.text:
The descriptions come from the code.

  • tir.degats: function(default, joueur, cible, degats, partie, arme) -> the raw damage of one shot of the player on this target. degats: what the weapon row gives at that distance, head multiplier included (all the pellets of a shotgun shot that hit this target, added up; for a grenade, the share at that distance); partie: tete, torse, bras, jambes or nil; arme: the weapon's name. The default returns degats. For a weak spot, a critical hit, a boss hurt only by arrows.

items.title: What the agent knows about this system
items.text: The text the agent reads before using this system.

items.title: Ranged weapons (tir)
items.text:
Pistols, rifles, shotguns, sniper rifles, bows, crossbows and grenades for the player: aim (aim, right mouse button / left trigger), shoot (attack), reload (reload, R / X). Activating it activates the health module. Add it only if the user asked for weapons that shoot or throw; melee stays with combat.basique.

Each weapon is a row of the game setting armes (modules_set), never code. Nine rows are ready and playable, each with a model shipped with the editor: Pistolet, Revolver, Fusil d'assaut, Mitraillette, Fusil à pompe, Fusil de précision, Arc, Arbalète, Grenade (no model). Keep the rows the game uses, change their values, rename them in the user's language, add one for a new weapon (a row given with a few fields takes the defaults for the others). Never write a shooting script.

items.title: How the player gets a weapon
items.text:
• With the inventory (best): a weapon is a kind of item. Its row's nom is the inventory kind: an object carrying inventaire with nom "Pistolet" is picked up, goes in the bar, and holding it puts the weapon in hand (inventaire.en_main). Its model in the hand is the inventory's job (en_main rows, set with attach_bone and a capture). Ammunition is another kind of item (munitions: "Balles", "Flèches"...): boxes of bullets carry inventaire with that nom and a quantite.
  • Given at the start: the game setting armes_depart ("Pistolet, Arc"): with the inventory, they go into each player's bag with reserve ammunition; without it, the module keeps them and the wheel (weapon_next) switches. Without the inventory, modele is the hidden model shown in the hand. A script gives one later with game.emit("tir.tenir", {arme = "Arc"}) (no inventory only; with it, inventaire.ajouter).
  • A weapon arrives loaded the first time it is held.

items.title: The model in hand
items.text:
• Ready-made: each row's modele_fichier names a model shipped with the editor (armes/quaternius-armes/Pistol_1.fbx, armes/avramania-armes/mdvl_weapons_shortbow_01.glb...). It is copied into the project with its licence when the game starts. The bow and the crossbow also fly an arrow and a bolt (modele_projectile_fichier).
  • Change it: weapon_library_list gives every shipped weapon (40 firearms and accessories by Quaternius; bows, crossbows, swords, axes, shields by Avramania); put another "armes/<pack>/<file>", or a model file of the project, in modele_fichier.
  • Real size: longueur is the weapon's real length in metres for a 1.8 m character (along the barrel; a bow's height). The model in hand (the row's file or the Inventory's copy) is brought to it, then scaled to the character's height measured on its model, whatever the file's own scale. Reference lengths: pistol 0.20, revolver 0.28, submachine gun 0.6, assault rifle 0.9, shotgun 1.0, sniper rifle 1.15, crossbow 0.8, bow 1.45; for scripts holding melee weapons (game.attach {weapon = true, length = ...}): sword 0.95, dagger 0.3. taille multiplies it (1: real size, 1.5 for a cartoon look). 0 keeps the object's size. An object of the scene in modele wins over the file (placed in the hand in the editor, its exact place is reused).
  • How it is held, measured on the model, never guessed: the barrel is the longest side; its front (the muzzle) is found by measuring (the thinnest end, the lighter half, the barrel at the top); the grip (what goes down under the barrel at the back) goes into the palm of the hand found by the skeleton's bone roles, the barrel along the fingers, the top on the thumb side. If a weapon is held backwards, set avant_modele to the axis of its front (+x, -z...), like the front of a vehicle. prise debout holds it upright across the fist (a bow), main gauche puts it in the left hand (a bow).
  • One hand, two hands or like a bow (tenue): auto (default) finds it from the model: a bow if held upright, two hands if the weapon is longer than 60 % of the character's arm or has a stock (rifles, submachine guns, shotguns, crossbows), one hand otherwise (pistols, revolvers). The arms come from the shipped clips, played on the upper body only (game.play_upper) while the legs keep walking or running: never write a pose script for this (see « Gestures » below).
  • Where the hands hold (position_prise, position_garde_main): -1 (default) measures them on the model's side silhouette: the grip is the rear-most part hanging under the weapon that slants back, behind the magazine (a stock is skipped; a pistol's slanted grip can reach the back end); the handguard is in front of the magazine. For a model the measure gets wrong (the hand on the magazine or in the stock), give a fraction of the length: 0 at the back, 1 at the muzzle. Check it with game.weapon(id).grip_at.
  • Fitted to the hand: after longueur, the weapon is made smaller if its grip is more than a tenth taller than the character's palm is wide, or its magazine longer than the hand (stocky low-poly models). taille multiplies the result. game.hold_check(player) measures the weapon in the body and the palms against the weapon.
  • With the inventory: its model in hand (its en_main row or the item picked up) is held the same way, its offsets and rotation kept on top; a model placed in the hand by hand in the editor keeps its place. A weapon given at the start with no model in the inventory shows the row's file.
  • Shots start at the muzzle measured on the model held, and the muzzle flash grows with the weapon's length (taille_eclair scales it).
  • Shoulder weapons and bows (version 7): gestes fusil (auto for a weapon held two-handed or at least 45 cm long: rifles, shotguns, sniper rifles, submachine guns, crossbows) plays clip_fusil_repos / clip_fusil_visee / clip_fusil_visee_haut / clip_fusil_visee_bas / clip_fusil_tir / clip_fusil_recharge (Rifle_Idle_Loop, Rifle_Aim_Neutral, Rifle_Aim_Up, Rifle_Aim_Down, Rifle_Shoot, Rifle_Reload of the animations/worldmint-armes pack: stock at the shoulder); the bow plays clip_arc_repos (Bow_Idle_Loop), clip_arc (Bow_Aim_Loop) and clip_arc_tir (Bow_Release). The player's model needs the pack file WorldMint_Armes.glb among its animations (animation_library_give); without it the pistol clips (and Idle_Torch_Loop for a bow) are used as before. Version 8: main_soutien (on by default) puts the left hand on each weapon's measured handguard after the clip (two-bone IK of the arm; out of reach, the most forward point under the weapon it reaches, never the magazine) and on the magazine during a reload; untick it to keep the clip's hand.
  • Gestures (clips on the upper body, version 5; clip_mains since version 6): game settings clip_repos (Pistol_Idle_Loop: weapon in hand, not aiming), clip_visee (Pistol_Aim_Neutral: aiming; the weapon is fitted on this clip's fist with game.attach {pose}), clip_visee_haut / clip_visee_bas (Pistol_Aim_Up / Pistol_Aim_Down: blended by the aim pitch instead of leaning the back), clip_tir (Pistol_Shoot, once per shot), clip_recharge (Pistol_Reload, stretched to the reload time), clip_lancer (OverhandThrow, a grenade), clip_arc (Idle_Torch_Loop: the shipped packs have no bow clip, this left fist held out is the closest). All on the upper body: the legs keep walking or running. Each row's gestes picks them: auto (a bow if held upright, a throw if it has no model, else a firearm), arme, arc, lancer, aucun; its animation_tenue, animation_tir, animation_recharge replace the setting's clip for that weapon. For another skeleton or pack, give its clip names (read with animation_clips); a missing clip is skipped. The UAL1 pistol clips hold the weapon two-handed at arm's length: long guns (rifle, shotgun, sniper, crossbow) are held the same way, pistol-style, until a pack with rifle clips is added (give its clips in these settings). The KayKit pack (animations/kaykit-animations, version 6) has rifle and bow clips (Ranged_2H_Aiming, Ranged_2H_Shoot, Ranged_2H_Reload, Ranged_Bow_Idle, Ranged_Bow_Aiming_Idle, Running_HoldingRifle), but they are made for a big-headed character: on a realistic human the rifle is held along the flank, 30 cm from the shoulder, and the left hand 35 to 45 cm from the weapon (measured with game.hold_check). Keep the UAL defaults for realistic characters; use the KayKit clips only for a character with KayKit proportions, with clip_mains (Fingers clip: Pistol_Aim_Neutral, Idle_Torch_Loop for a bow) when the character has finger bones, since KayKit hands have none and would stay open.

items.title: The values of a weapon row (what to change for which game)
items.text:
• sorte: balle (instant ray, firearms) or projectile (flies and falls: arrows, bolts, grenades, rockets).
  • Damage: degats per shot (per pellet for a shotgun), tete the head multiplier (found on any skeleton), and the drop with distance: full up to chute_debut m, down to degats_loin % at chute_fin m. All pellets of one shot on a target add up into one hit.
  • Rhythm: cadence (shots per second), mode (coup_par_coup, rafale with rafale shots, automatique while held), plombs per shot.
  • Precision: dispersion_hanche (hip fire), dispersion_visee (aiming), dispersion_marche (added while moving), dispersion_tir (added per shot, fading at dispersion_retour °/s). The crosshair opens with it.
  • Feel: recul (view kick up, degrees) and recul_cote (random sideways), zoom while aiming (1.5 usual, 4 for a scope), poussee (push on what is hit, from the point hit: a crate spins).
  • Ammunition: chargeur (0: none, each shot takes from the reserve: a bow, grenades), munitions (an item kind; empty: endless), reserve (given with armes_depart, or kept by the module without inventory), rechargement seconds.
  • Projectiles: vitesse (m/s), gravite (1 falls like a stone, 0 straight), duree (life, the fuse of a grenade), modele_projectile (a hidden object of the scene: an arrow, a grenade; its longest side follows the path), plante (sticks in what it hits and follows it), rebond (0 to 1).
  • explosion: radius in m (0: none). The shot explodes where it ends (at the end of its fuse if it bounces, on impact otherwise): everything carrying sante in the radius with no wall in between loses degats times a share falling to 0 at the edge, and what moves is pushed by poussee.
  • Look and sound: eclair (muzzle flash, firearms), trainee (bullet trail), son_tir (each shot), son_vide (shot with no ammunition), son_recharge (start of a reload), son_visee (when aiming starts: a bow being drawn), son_impact (where the shot lands, once per thing hit: an arrow sticking in), son_explosion (where it explodes). Each takes one file or several separated by commas: one at random each time (a burst does not repeat the same bang).
  • Shipped sounds already set on the nine ready weapons (cited "sons/<pack>/<file>", copied into the project with their licence when the game starts or is exported): Pistolet armes-a-feu/pistolet_1..3, empty rechargements/clic_vide_1..2, reload rechargements/chargeur_pistolet; Revolver revolver_1..2, clic_vide_3, recharge_arme; Fusil d'assaut fusil_assaut_1..3, clic_vide_1..2, chargeur_fusil; Mitraillette mitraillette_1..3, clic_vide_1..2, recharge_arme; Fusil à pompe fusil_pompe_1..3, clic_vide_3, pompe_armer; Fusil de précision fusil_precision_1..3, clic_vide_3, chargeur_fusil; Arc: shot arc-arbalete/arc_tir_1..3, aim arc_bander_1..2, impact explosions-magie/fleche_impact_1..3; Arbalète: shot arbalete_tir_1..3, reload arbalete_recharge_1..2, impact fleche_impact_1..3; Grenade: throw armes-blanches/dague_coup_1 (a whoosh), explosion explosions-magie/explosion_1..3. A row the user adds starts silent: give it the family that fits (list in the main guide, « Ready-made sounds shipped with the editor »), or the user's own files. Empty a sound to silence it. The _loin gunshots are for distant enemies, not the player.
  • Gestures: gestes (auto, arme, arc, lancer, aucun) and, optional, clips of the player's model read with animation_clips, never guessed, replacing the game settings for this weapon on the upper body: animation_tenue (while aiming), animation_tir (each shot), animation_recharge (stretched to the reload time).
  • The muzzle is measured on the model held (game.weapon), whatever the model: never set it by hand; if it is at the wrong end, set avant_modele.

Starting points by kind of game: an arcade shooter keeps the presets; a tactical game raises tete (3), lowers dispersion_visee and cadence, and gives few reserve; a survival game sets munitions on every weapon and places ammunition boxes to find; a fantasy game keeps Arc and Arbalète only; a party game sets munitions empty (endless) and recharge_auto.

items.title: Game settings
items.text: armes_depart, blesser_joueurs, recharge_auto (reload by itself when empty), afficher (the HUD: crosshair, hit marker, ammunition, reload bar; the weapon's name and ammunition, bottom right, are the screen « Arme et munitions » delivered by the system, shapes Nom and Munitions, HUD keys Arme et munitions/Nom and Arme et munitions/Munitions, which the user restyles in the screen editor; the crosshair, hit marker and reload bar follow the aimed point and stay drawn by the script, keys tir.reticule.*, tir.marque.*, tir.recharge), reticule, marqueur, couleur_reticule, couleur_tete (hit marker on a head shot), effets (flashes, trails, impacts, holes), epaule (droite/gauche), sensibilite (view speed while aiming, already divided by the zoom), aide (gamepad aim assist, 0 to 1), and the control names action, action_visee, action_recharge, and those it takes from other systems while a weapon is held: action_parade (block, Basic combat) and action_soin (heal, Healing).

items.title: With other systems
items.text:
• Targets: anything carrying sante. Its invulnerabilite (0.5 s by default) swallows hits that come faster: for an automatic weapon, set it to 0 (or 0.05) on the enemies.
  • combat.basique on the same player: while a ranged weapon is held, the module takes attack and block (event action.prise): the left click shoots, the right click aims instead of blocking. With another item or empty hands, the player strikes and blocks as before.
  • soins uses R too (heal): while a ranged weapon is held, the module takes heal too (action.prise, game setting action_soin), so R reloads and does not drink a potion; with another item or empty hands, R drinks. No need to move a key.
  • While the cursor is shown or the player is busy (joueur.occupe), nothing shoots.
  • Enemies that shoot back are the ennemis module, not this one.

items.title: Events and override
items.text:
• tir.arme (arme, "" for none), tir.tir (source, arme, origine, direction), tir.touche (cible, source, arme, montant, partie, point, tete), tir.recharge (arme, etat debut/fin/annule, chargeur, reserve), tir.vide (arme), tir.explosion (arme, point, rayon). For a sound of your own, a score for head shots, a noise that alerts enemies: game.on, or a declencheur rule on the event.
  • game.override("tir.degats", function(default, joueur, cible, degats, partie, arme) ... end): a weak spot, a boss only arrows hurt, a critical hit. Return the damage.

items.title: Several players
items.text: One copy per player: each has their own magazines, reload, aim, crosshair and ammunition (their own bag). Players do not hurt each other (nor themselves with a grenade) unless blesser_joueurs is ticked.

items.title: Check it
items.text:
game_run with captures: aim (hold aim), shoot (attack), reload (reload). Its report counts shooting (rays, projectiles, hits), particles, decals and tracers; the events above are in its logs if a script logs them. - Shotgun (version 9): gestures fusil_pompe (the Shotgun preset's gestes; give it to any weapon without a separate pistol grip): settings clip_pompe_repos, clip_pompe_visee, clip_pompe_visee_haut, clip_pompe_visee_bas, clip_pompe_tir, clip_pompe_pompe (played after each shot clip: the left hand pulls the pump back and pushes it forward; the model's pump does not move), clip_pompe_recharge (shells slid in one by one from below). Shotgun_* clips of the worldmint-armes pack: the right fist on the measured wrist of the stock, the left hand on the pump. The support hand is the clip's during the pump and the reload, on the measured pump otherwise. Without the Shotgun_* clips on the character, the rifle clips are used. Rifle and shotgun clips: the weapon rises to the eye (the stock higher in the shoulder pocket, up to 6 cm), the head only tilts a little (10° at most); at rest the head stays as in the UAL source clip.

  • One clip set per weapon family (version 10): gestes is arme_courte (pistols, revolvers: the UAL1 Pistol_* clips; arme is its old name), fusil (assault rifle, submachine gun: Rifle_), fusil_pompe (Shotgun_), precision (sniper rifle: Sniper_, the scope at the eye), arbalete (Crossbow_), arc (Bow_*: Bow_Draw is played when aiming starts, then Bow_Aim_Loop loops, Bow_Release at the shot), lancer, aucun. The presets have theirs. Each family's clips are game settings (clip_precision_repos, clip_precision_visee, _visee_haut, _visee_bas, _tir, _recharge, the same for clip_arbalete_..., and clip_arc_bander); a family clip missing from the character falls back to the rifle clip, then to the pistol clips. The clip makes the pose (left elbow bent, stock at the shoulder, sights at the eye); after it, the engine only corrects the support hand and the weapon by 2 cm at most (game.hold_check gives correction and correction_wanted: more than 0.02 means the clip does not fit this weapon or character: give its row another family or its own clips in animation_tenue...). During a reload or a pump the support hand is the clip's.

items.title: Vehicle
items.text:
Turns a model into a car, a motorbike or a boat you drive. A car: its wheels (chosen among its children, found by their name, or taken out of a one-piece model) spin, steer and follow the suspension. A motorbike: it stays upright, leans into turns and can fall over. A boat: its hull floats, measured on its model, an engine pushes it and a rudder turns it; it runs aground on land. The player gets in and out with the Use control, drives with the game's controls, on the keyboard or the gamepad, and the camera follows.

Identifier vehicule Version 5 Placed on objects yes Run by the engine yes: the engine runs it itself, without a script

items.title: Settings for the whole game
items.text:
In the Systems panel (Developer mode), by opening the system's card.

Setting What it does Name in code Type Default Limits or choices Distance to get in (m) How far from the vehicle's edge, in meters, the player can get in with the Use control (E, or Y on a gamepad). distance Number 2.5 from 0.5 to 20

items.title: Settings on each object
items.text:
In the Properties of an object or folder that carries the system, Systems section. A folder passes its values on to what it contains; an object can change a value for itself only.

Setting What it does Name in code Type Default Limits or choices Kind of vehicle A car rolls on its wheels. A motorbike rolls on two wheels: it stays upright by itself, leans into turns and falls over if knocked down. A boat floats on its hull, measured on its model: an engine at the back pushes it, a rudder turns it, it rocks with the waves and runs aground on land. Place the boat on the water of a lake or the sea. sorte Choice in a list Car: wheels on land voiture: Car: wheels on landmoto: Motorbike: two wheels, one behind the otherbateau: Boat: a hull on water Wheels (empty: found by their name)shown only if Kind of vehicle is “Car: wheels on land” or “Motorbike: two wheels, one behind the other” The objects inside the vehicle that are its wheels. Empty: those whose name contains "roue", "wheel", "tire", "tyre" or "pneu". With no wheel found, the model's own wheels if it is made in one piece (see "Wheels of the model"), otherwise invisible wheels under the model (four at a car's corners, two in the middle of a motorbike). Their size comes from their model. roues List of “Wheel” (empty) one line per “Wheel”: its fields Wheels of a one-piece modelshown only if Kind of vehicle is “Car: wheels on land” or “Motorbike: two wheels, one behind the other” When no wheel is placed apart, looks for the wheels inside the model itself: the round pieces at its bottom, seen from the side. In the game, they come off and turn like real wheels. Unchecked: invisible wheels carry it, and the model's own wheels stay still. roues_du_modele Yes or no yes Lean in turns (degrees)shown only if Kind of vehicle is “Motorbike: two wheels, one behind the other” How far the motorbike leans at most in a turn: 45 for a road bike, 55 for a racing bike, 25 for a scooter. The more it leans, the tighter it turns at high speed. inclinaison Number 45 from 0 to 70 Balance (1: ordinary)shown only if Kind of vehicle is “Motorbike: two wheels, one behind the other” The strength that keeps the motorbike upright and straightens it after a turn: 1 ordinary, 2 very steady, 0.5 wobbly. equilibre Number 1 from 0.1 to 5 Handling (1: ordinary)shown only if Kind of vehicle is “Motorbike: two wheels, one behind the other” How fast the handlebars turn when steering: 1 ordinary (a quarter of a second from one end to the other), 2 quick, 0.5 heavy. Too quick, a sharp turn can knock it down. maniabilite Number 1 from 0.1 to 5 Hit that unbalances it (m/s)shown only if Kind of vehicle is “Motorbike: two wheels, one behind the other” Hit from the side (a rock, a car), the motorbike loses its balance for a moment if its sideways speed changes at once by more than this, in meters per second: the momentum knocks it down, or it recovers. 4 ordinary, 8 sturdy, 0: never. choc Number 4 from 0 to 50 Can fall overshown only if Kind of vehicle is “Motorbike: two wheels, one behind the other” Checked: knocked over (a crash, a turn too tight), the motorbike falls on its side and the rider is thrown off; getting back on with the Use control sets it upright. Unchecked: it never leans further than its lean setting, as in an arcade game. chute Yes or no yes Front of the model The side of the model that is the front of the vehicle. A car's or a motorbike's wheels on that side steer; a boat's propeller is on the opposite side. An arrow shows it in the 3D view when the vehicle is selected. avant Choice in a list +Z (most models) +z: +Z (most models)-z: −Z+x: +X-x: −X Mass (kg) Its weight, in kilograms: a car 1,200, a kart 150, a truck 8,000, a motorbike 200, a scooter 110; a motorboat 1,200, a rowing boat 150. The heavier, the more it pushes what it hits and the more power it needs; a heavy boat sits deeper. masse Number 1200 from 10 to 100 000 Engine power (N·m)shown only if Kind of vehicle is “Car: wheels on land” or “Motorbike: two wheels, one behind the other” The engine's torque, in newton-meters: it makes it accelerate. 600 for a car, 150 for a kart or a motorbike, 3,000 for a truck. puissance Number 600 from 10 to 100 000 Top speed (km/h) Beyond it, it no longer speeds up, forwards or backwards, in kilometers per hour. vitesse_max Number 80 from 1 to 500 Grip (1: dry road)shown only if Kind of vehicle is “Car: wheels on land” or “Motorbike: two wheels, one behind the other” How much the tires grip: 1 on a dry road, 0.4 slides as on snow, 1.5 sticks like a race car. adherence Number 1 from 0.1 to 3 Suspension travel (m)shown only if Kind of vehicle is “Car: wheels on land” or “Motorbike: two wheels, one behind the other” How much each wheel moves up and down, in meters: 0.3 for a car, 0.6 for an off-roader. suspension Number 0.3 from 0.02 to 2 Suspension stiffnessshown only if Kind of vehicle is “Car: wheels on land” or “Motorbike: two wheels, one behind the other” 1.5 is soft like an everyday car, 3 is firm like a sports car; lower, it sways. raideur Number 1.5 from 0.2 to 10 Front wheel steering (degrees)shown only if Kind of vehicle is “Car: wheels on land” or “Motorbike: two wheels, one behind the other” How far the front wheels turn at full lock: 30 for a car; more, it turns tighter. braquage Number 30 from 0 to 70 Brake strength (N·m per wheel)shown only if Kind of vehicle is “Car: wheels on land” or “Motorbike: two wheels, one behind the other” The brake strength of each wheel. The hand brake (Jump: Space, or A on a gamepad) locks the rear wheels. freins Number 1500 from 0 to 100 000 Driving assist (1: arcade)shown only if Kind of vehicle is “Car: wheels on land” or “Motorbike: two wheels, one behind the other” 1, as in an arcade game: at speed it steers less, the wheel turns smoothly even on the keyboard, and it follows the road without spinning out or sliding sideways (the hand brake still makes it drift). 0: physics alone, like a simulation; 0.5 in between. aide Number 1 from 0 to 1 Visible drivershown only if Kind of vehicle is “Car: wheels on land” or “Motorbike: two wheels, one behind the other” Checked: the player's character stays on screen while driving, seated on the motorbike (astride, hands on the handlebars, leaning with it) or in the car (in the driver's seat, hands on the wheel). Unchecked: they disappear while driving, as in a car with tinted windows. conducteur Yes or no yes Driving animation (optional)shown only if Kind of vehicle is “Car: wheels on land” or “Motorbike: two wheels, one behind the other” An animation of the player's character, looped while driving. Empty: an animation whose name is about driving or sitting (drive, ride, sit, seat…), if their model has one; otherwise a seated pose made from their own. animation_conduite Player animation (empty) Seat: forwards (m)shown only if Kind of vehicle is “Car: wheels on land” or “Motorbike: two wheels, one behind the other” Moves the driver forwards (or backwards, negative), in meters, from the place measured on the model: a motorbike's saddle, a car's driver seat. siege_avant Number 0 from -5 to 5 Seat: upwards (m)shown only if Kind of vehicle is “Car: wheels on land” or “Motorbike: two wheels, one behind the other” Raises (or lowers, negative) the driver, in meters: when they sink into the saddle or float above it. siege_hauteur Number 0 from -3 to 3 Seat: to the right (m)shown only if Kind of vehicle is “Car: wheels on land” or “Motorbike: two wheels, one behind the other” Moves the driver to the right (or to the left, negative), in meters: a British car's wheel is on the right. siege_cote Number 0 from -3 to 3 Passenger seatsshown only if Kind of vehicle is “Car: wheels on land” How many characters (a companion, a passenger set by a script) can sit in the car besides the driver: the first seat on their right, the next ones at the back, from right to left. A passenger is shown seated only if its model has a sitting animation; otherwise it rides hidden. 0: none is shown. A motorbike has one seat, behind the rider. passagers Number 3 from 0 to 16 Passengers: forwards (m)shown only if Kind of vehicle is “Car: wheels on land” or “Motorbike: two wheels, one behind the other” Moves the passenger seats forwards (or backwards, negative), in meters, from the ones measured on the model: beside the driver and at the back of a car, behind the rider on a motorbike. passager_avant Number 0 from -5 to 5 Passengers: upwards (m)shown only if Kind of vehicle is “Car: wheels on land” or “Motorbike: two wheels, one behind the other” Raises (or lowers, negative) the passengers, in meters: when they sink into the seat or float above it. passager_hauteur Number 0 from -3 to 3 Passengers: to the right (m)shown only if Kind of vehicle is “Car: wheels on land” or “Motorbike: two wheels, one behind the other” Moves the passenger seats to the right (or to the left, negative), in meters. passager_cote Number 0 from -3 to 3 Engine thrust (N)shown only if Kind of vehicle is “Boat: a hull on water” The engine's force, in newtons: it makes it speed up. 4,000 for a 1,200 kg motorboat, 800 for a rowing boat, 40,000 for a fishing boat. The engine only pushes in water. poussee Number 4000 from 1 to 1 000 000 Turn at full rudder (degrees per second)shown only if Kind of vehicle is “Boat: a hull on water” How far the boat turns in one second at full rudder, once moving: 40 for a motorboat, 15 for a big boat. The rudder turns better the faster the boat moves. virage Number 40 from 0 to 180

items.title: What it announces
items.text: Event Fields Description vehicule.monte cible (id), qui (id), joueur (id?) A player got into a vehicle (an object carrying the vehicule system) and now drives it: qui and joueur are their character (the host's, or a guest's). Announced by the engine. vehicule.descendu cible (id), qui (id), joueur (id?) A player got out of a vehicle. Announced by the engine. vehicule.tombe cible (id), qui (id?) A motorbike fell over on its side (a crash, a turn too tight, a push). Its rider, if any, is thrown off. Announced by the engine.

items.title: What the agent knows about this system
items.text: The text the agent reads before using this system.

items.title: Vehicle (vehicule)
items.text:
Turns a model into a car, a motorbike or a boat the player drives: wheels with suspension, engine, brakes and steering. The engine runs it, without a script. The player gets in and out with the interact control (E, Y on a gamepad) next to it, drives with the movement controls (forward and back accelerate or brake then reverse, left and right steer), jump is the hand brake; the camera follows behind it.

  • systems_attach it on the car object itself (or on the folder that holds the body and the wheels), placed on the ground, not on each part.
  • Wheels: the car's children (any depth) whose name contains roue, wheel, tire, tyre or pneu are found by themselves; otherwise list them in roues ([{"objet": "<wheel id>"}, ...]). Their size and place come from their models. Never assume a pack's names: look at the children (entities_list) and list them if their names say nothing.
  • A model made in one piece (no wheel among its children): with « roues_du_modele » on (the default), the engine looks for the wheels inside the model itself, the round pieces at its bottom seen from the side; in the game they come off the body and turn like real wheels. The editor circles them when the vehicle is selected. When none is found (the wheels are welded to the body), invisible wheels carry it: four at a car's corners, two in the middle of a motorbike, and the model's own wheels do not turn.
  • avant: which side of the model is the front (+z most models, -z, +x, -x): the wheels on that side steer. Check it in a screenshot: an arrow shows it when the vehicle is selected.
  • Per object: masse (kg, car 1200, kart 150, motorbike 200), puissance (engine torque N·m: car 600, kart or motorbike 150, truck 3000), vitesse_max (km/h), adherence (1 dry road, 0.4 snow), suspension (travel in m), raideur (1.5 soft, 3 firm), braquage (degrees), freins. Game-wide: distance to get in.
  • A motorbike: set « sorte » to « moto ». Two wheels one behind the other (found or listed like a car's, the front one steers, the rear one drives). It stands upright by itself, parked or ridden, and leans into turns. Per object: « inclinaison » (the most it leans in a turn, degrees: 45 road bike, 55 racing, 25 scooter), « equilibre » (how hard it straightens, 1 ordinary), « maniabilite » (how fast the handlebars turn, 1 ordinary), « choc » (a sideways hit faster than this, in m/s, unbalances it for a moment: 4 ordinary, 0 never), « chute » (can fall over, on by default). Knocked over (a crash, a hard hit), it falls on its side and its rider is thrown off (a rider with the chiffon system falls limp); getting back on with interact or game.drive sets it upright. Set « masse » and « puissance » for a bike: the defaults are a car's.
  • Driving feel: « aide » (driving assist, 0 to 1, default 1) makes a car or a motorbike arcade-friendly, as in GTA or Forza Horizon: it steers less at speed (full lock standing, a third at 80 km/h), the steering moves smoothly even on the keyboard, and the vehicle follows where its wheels point, within its grip, instead of spinning out or sliding sideways (the hand brake still drifts). 0 is physics alone, like a simulation. When the user says a vehicle is hard to drive, check « aide » is 1 before touching anything else; a car that turns too little at speed: raise « braquage »; a motorbike that leans too little: raise « inclinaison ».
  • The driver stays visible (« conducteur », on by default): seated astride the motorbike, hands on the handlebars, leaning with it, or in the car's driver seat (left side), hands on the wheel, seen through the windows. The seat is measured on the model (a motorbike: the top of the model between the wheels; a car: driver side, a bit over a third of its height); « siege_avant », « siege_hauteur », « siege_cote » (meters) move it when the rider sinks into the saddle or floats above it: check a screenshot while driving. « animation_conduite »: a clip of the player's character looped while driving; empty, a clip whose name says drive, ride, sit or seat is used if the model has one (read animation_clips), otherwise a seated pose is made from the character's own. « conducteur » off hides the driver while driving (tinted windows). A boat's driver stays hidden.
  • Passengers: game.seat(id, vehicle, {clip}) seats a character (a companion of the accompagner system does it by itself) at a passenger seat, playing a sitting clip of its own model (never a made-up pose; without one it stays as it is, and accompagner hides it). A car: « passagers » seats (3 by default: beside the driver on the right, then the back seats right to left); a motorbike: one, behind the rider; a boat or « conducteur » off: none shown. « passager_avant », « passager_hauteur », « passager_cote » (meters) move them all: check a screenshot. game.seat(id, nil) gets it up.
  • Copies: game.clone(id, pos) of a vehicle gives another vehicle you can drive, with its wheels; a vehicle hidden then shown again (game.set_visible) is a vehicle again.
  • Scripts: game.drive(id) puts the player in, game.leave_vehicle(), game.driving() (the vehicle driven or nil), game.vehicle(id) (speed in km/h, driven, flipped, motorbike, fallen, lean in degrees). Events vehicule.monte and vehicule.descendu (cible, qui): a race starts when the player gets in; vehicule.tombe (cible, qui if someone rode it) when a motorbike falls over.
  • A zone detects the driven vehicle as the player: a finish line works as for a runner.
  • Check with game_run and inputs: press interact next to it, then hold move_forward; vehicles reports « kind » (car, motorbike, boat), top_speed_kmh, travelled_m, flipped (it turned over during the run) and driven_s, wheels, invisible_wheels and « model_wheels » (taken out of a one-piece model). A motorbike adds « max_lean_deg » (how far it leaned), « falls » and « fallen_now ». A vehicle that does not move: check its wheels are found and that it stands on the ground. A motorbike that falls at once: lower « maniabilite » or raise « equilibre ».
  • A boat: set « sorte » to « bateau » and place it on the water (a lake or the sea, its bottom at the surface). No wheels: its hull is measured on its model (length, width slice by slice, bottom), how deep it sits comes from masse, its center of gravity is at the waterline so a mast does not capsize it. Per object: masse (motorboat 1200, rowing boat 150), « poussee » (engine thrust in N: 4000 for a 1200 kg motorboat, 800 for a rowing boat), « vitesse_max » (km/h, it levels off there at full thrust), « virage » (degrees per second at full rudder, once moving: 40 motorboat, 15 big boat). Driven like a car; the engine only pushes in water, so it runs aground on land and stays there. It rocks with the waves and drifts with moving water.
  • For a boat, game_run's vehicles adds « kind » « boat », « afloat_s », « aground_now », « aground_s », « draft_m » (how deep its hull sits) and « float_points » (where the water carries it, measured on the model; 4 or more). game.vehicle(id) has boat and aground. A boat that does not move: check it is on the water (« afloat_s » above 0) and not « aground_now ».

items.title: Several players
items.text:
The engine runs it once for the whole game: any player gets in and out with interact, drives with their own controls, and nobody gets into a vehicle another player drives (vehicule.monte and vehicule.descendu carry joueur). Every player sees the others seated on the vehicles they drive.

This page is generated automatically from the WorldMint code (modules/vehicule/module.json, modules/vehicule/AGENT.md, modules/events.json): it always matches the editor.

items.title: Zone
items.text:
A zone that announces who enters and who leaves it: a pressure plate, a trap, a finish line, a goal. Place it on an invisible box, of the size you want. The game decides what happens.

Identifier zone Version 1 Placed on objects yes Run by the engine yes: the engine runs it itself, without a script

items.title: Settings for the whole game
items.text:

items.title: Zone (zone)
items.text:
An object carrying this system announces zone.entree and zone.sortie when something enters or leaves its box: the box of its model, at its place, rotation and scale. The system has no script: the engine detects, the game decides what happens.

  • Make a zone: create a box (builtin:cube) with visible: false, no collider, scaled to the area (a plate 2 × 0.2 × 2, a finish line 10 × 4 × 1), then systems_attach this system on it. A zone works hidden; the editor still shows it.
  • Per object (systems_set): detecte, who counts: joueur (default), personnages (the player and characters), objets (moving objects of the physique system), tout.
  • React in a script of the game: game.on("zone.entree", function(e) if e.cible == plate then ... end end). e.qui is who entered: game.player(), a character, or a moving object. A ball in a goal: the zone detects objets, and the script checks e.qui.
  • Something already inside when the game starts enters on the first step. game.set_solid(zone, false) switches a zone off; true switches it back on.

items.title: Several players
items.text:
The engine runs it once for the whole game: detecte = joueur sees every player, and zone.entree / zone.sortie carry joueur when a player enters or leaves.
